source_views.view: Long life, uncharitable, sickly, sudden gains, eye complaints, sores in the head, poor and uneventful, obscure.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. II, 'Planets in the Eighth House'
source_views.view: Exalted: long life, charming, eloquent; afflicted: sores, weak eyes, penury, uneventful life; with 8th or 11th lord sudden speculative gains; few, mostly male, children.

source_views.source: PanchangBodh, Sun in the 12 houses
source_views.view: Depth, research, inheritance, in-laws; recognition late but lasting; written clarity on shared property; aspect on 2nd puts family wealth under scrutiny.

source_views.source: VedicFeed, Effects of the Sun in 12 Houses
source_views.view: Perfectionist, handles crises, firm; difficult marriage, emotionally reserved, takes offence.

planet_in_house/sun/8.disagreements: On longevity Phaladeepika reads it as reduced, while Raman HPA lists long life; Raman's How to Judge a Horoscope reconciles this by giving long life when the Sun is exalted. Jataka Parijata is milder (charming, argumentative) than the other classics.
planet_in_house/sun/8.phrasing_guidance: Frame this as a research-minded, private placement where recognition comes slowly. Never speak of lifespan or death; keep eye or health notes general and suggest ordinary check-ups at most.

planet_in_house/sun/9.summary: The Sun in the 9th brings devotion, fortune and children in some texts, but strain or loss around the father and elders in others. It is the most disputed of the Sun's house placements.
common_outcomes: Devoted to gods and the learned; godly and charitable (Phaladeepika 8.4, Raman HPA)
Children, wealth and happiness (Brihat Jataka 20.3); children and relatives (Phaladeepika 8.4)
Strained relations with the father or elders (Phaladeepika 8.4, Jataka Parijata 8.86, Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope)
Little patrimony, self-made property (Raman)
rare_outcomes: Turns to a faith different from the parents' (Jataka Parijata 8.86; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope when afflicted)
Learned in esoteric or occult subjects; successful farmer; glandular disease (Raman HPA)

by_area.personality: Ambitious and enterprising, a man of action and thought (Raman).
by_area.finance: Self-acquired property and lands, little patrimony (Raman HPA).
by_area.health: Ordinary health (Raman).
by_area.family: Loss of or distance from the father (Phaladeepika 8.4); antipathy to parents and teachers (Jataka Parijata 8.86); dutiful sons (Raman HPA); the father is strongly felt (PanchangBodh).
by_area.spirituality: Devotion to gods and the learned (Phaladeepika 8.4); godly, philosophical (Raman HPA); may change faith if the Sun is afflicted (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope).

strengtheners: Unafflicted Sun: a dutiful son with regard for spiritual pursuits (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Afflicted Sun: change of faith and hostility to the father and teachers (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope)
Moon with the Sun here: eye trouble; Venus with the Sun: sickness (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope)
Raman calls the presence of the father-significator Sun in the 9th 'not at all desirable' in a father-related case study (How to Judge a Horoscope, Ninth House)

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 8.4
source_views.view: Loses the father; has children and relatives; reveres gods and Brahmins.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 20.3 with notes
source_views.view: Children, wealth and happiness. Note: some astrologers hold the Sun bad in the 9th.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.86 and notes
source_views.view: Antipathy to parents and spiritual teachers; takes up a religion different from theirs. The translator's note says Varahamihira, unlike some astrologers, gives good results here.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXI
source_views.view: Well read, charitable, godly, lucky and successful, ordinary health, little patrimony, dutiful sons, self-acquired property, philosophical, occult learning, ambitious.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. II, 'Planets in the Ninth House'
source_views.view: If afflicted, may change faith and be hostile to father and teachers; if not, a dutiful son with spiritual regard; Moon or Venus with the Sun bring eye trouble or sickness; little patrimony; ambitious.

source_views.source: PanchangBodh, Sun in the 12 houses
source_views.view: Principled outlook and a strongly felt father; calls the 'karako bhava nashaya' maxim debated.

source_views.source: VedicFeed, Effects of the Sun in 12 Houses
source_views.view: Spiritual, generous, charitable; can be self-righteous about moral views.

planet_in_house/sun/9.disagreements: Brihat Jataka and Raman HPA read it as fortunate; Phaladeepika gives loss of the father with otherwise good results; Jataka Parijata gives antipathy to parents and a change of religion. Both Sastri's Brihat Jataka note and Jataka Parijata's note record that 'some astrologers' hold the Sun bad here. Raman makes the outcome depend on affliction.
planet_in_house/sun/9.phrasing_guidance: Speak of strong personal convictions and a meaningful, sometimes complex, bond with the father or mentors. Never predict a parent's death or a religious break.

planet_in_house/sun/10.summary: The Sun is strongest in the 10th: power, fame, high position, often in government, with wealth and children. All sources agree it is one of its best placements.
common_outcomes: Power, fame and high or royal standing (Phaladeepika 8.4, Brihat Jataka 20.3, Jataka Parijata 8.89, Raman)
Sons, vehicles, intelligence and wealth (Phaladeepika 8.4; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope)
Success in what he undertakes (Raman)
Hereditary or ancestral wealth (Jataka Parijata 8.89; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope)
rare_outcomes: Founder of institutions; successful military or political career (Raman HPA)
Fond of music; personal magnetism (Raman)

by_area.personality: Bold, quick to decide, strong personal influence (Raman HPA).
by_area.career: Government service, high position, military or political success (Raman); office, government and public work (PanchangBodh).
by_area.finance: Wealth and ancestral property (Phaladeepika 8.4, Jataka Parijata 8.89); Sastri's note to Brihat Jataka says the 10th-house Sun gives much labour and less income.
by_area.health: Healthy (Raman HPA).
by_area.family: Sons (Phaladeepika 8.4); dutiful sons (Raman HPA).
by_area.spirituality: Virtue (Jataka Parijata 8.89).

strengtheners: Directional strength (digbala) in the 10th (PanchangBodh)
Mercury with the Sun: deep scientific knowledge (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope)
Venus with the Sun: a wealthy spouse (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mars with the Sun: tendency to vices such as drinking (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope)
Saturn with the Sun: sorrow and dejection (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope)
Rahu with the Sun in the 10th, aspected by Saturn, is tied to a chequered, embattled political career in one of Raman's case studies (How to Judge a Horoscope, Tenth House, Chart 197)

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 8.4
source_views.view: Sons, vehicles, praise, intelligence, wealth, strength, fame; becomes a king.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 20.3 with notes
source_views.view: Happy and powerful. Note: much labour and little income, because the Sun is square the lagna, which is why 'wealth' is not named here.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.89
source_views.view: Hereditary wealth, virtue, learning, fame and strength; a king's equal.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXI
source_views.view: Bold, famous, clever at acquiring wealth, healthy, learned, quick decisions, fond of music, founder of institutions, high position, dutiful sons, military or political success.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. II, 'Planets in the Tenth House'
source_views.view: Success in all undertakings, sons, vehicles, fame, money, power; government service; ancestral wealth; conjunction notes for Mars, Mercury, Venus, Saturn.

source_views.source: PanchangBodh, Sun in the 12 houses
source_views.view: Strongest house with digbala; office, government, public work; aspects the 4th. Notes Parashara gives the 10th house to Mercury as karaka, so the Sun's claim is later tradition.

source_views.source: VedicFeed, Effects of the Sun in 12 Houses
source_views.view: Executive success and fast rise; ego and anxiety about image.

planet_in_house/sun/10.disagreements: Agreement on status and power. On money, Phaladeepika, Jataka Parijata and Raman give wealth, while Sastri's note to Brihat Jataka argues the placement gives more labour than income.
planet_in_house/sun/10.phrasing_guidance: Speak confidently about leadership, visibility and success in public or official work, with ego and work-life balance as the caution.

planet_in_house/sun/11.summary: The Sun in the 11th is a strong gain placement: wealth, long life, influence and success with little strain, with favour from authorities.
common_outcomes: Wealthy (Phaladeepika 8.4, Brihat Jataka 20.3, Jataka Parijata 8.94, Raman)
Long life and freedom from sorrow (Phaladeepika 8.4; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope)
Success without much effort; royal or government favour (Raman)
Wife, children and servants (Jataka Parijata 8.94; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope)
rare_outcomes: Many enemies, including political enemies (Raman HPA)
Becomes a king or ruler (Phaladeepika 8.4)

by_area.personality: Learned, persevering, principled and sagacious (Raman).
by_area.career: Government favour and great position (Raman).
by_area.finance: Wealth through fair means (Raman HPA); income through position and recognition (PanchangBodh).
by_area.relationships: Capacity to make friends (Raman HPA).
by_area.family: Wife, children and servants (Jataka Parijata 8.94); elder siblings or mentors matter (PanchangBodh).

strengtheners: Sastri's note: the Sun is good in the 11th because it is in sextile to the lagna (Brihat Jataka 20.3 notes)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Afflicted: expectations can outrun income (PanchangBodh)

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 8.4
source_views.view: Very wealthy, long-lived, becomes a king, free of sorrow.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 20.3 with notes
source_views.view: Wealthy; good because sextile to the lagna.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.94
source_views.view: Extensive wealth, wife, children and servants; happy.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXI
source_views.view: Learned, wealthy, stately, success without effort, famous, many enemies, fair means, good reputation, insight, principled, great position.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. II, 'Planets in the Eleventh House'
source_views.view: Long life and wealth, wife, children and servants, royal and government favour, effortless success, sagacious and principled.

source_views.source: PanchangBodh, Sun in the 12 houses
source_views.view: Upachaya; income through position and recognition; elder siblings and mentors; lesson is less need for centrality.

source_views.source: VedicFeed, Effects of the Sun in 12 Houses
source_views.view: Kind, humanitarian, wide circle, organised; group conflicts possible.

planet_in_house/sun/11.disagreements: Little disagreement; Raman HPA alone adds many (political) enemies.
planet_in_house/sun/11.phrasing_guidance: Speak of steady gains, useful connections and recognition. Present any 'ruler' language as influence within one's field.

planet_in_house/sun/12.summary: The Sun in the 12th is classically weak: loss of standing, strained ties with the father, weak eyes and little wealth. Some texts still give energy and sons, and modern writers stress retreat, foreign work and spiritual life.
common_outcomes: Fall in standing or feeling neglected (Brihat Jataka 20.3; Raman)
Weak eyesight (Phaladeepika 8.4; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope)
Little wealth or lack of success (Phaladeepika 8.4, Raman)
Energetic and has sons (Jataka Parijata 8.97; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope)
rare_outcomes: Hostility toward the father (Phaladeepika 8.4)
Becomes an apostate and a wanderer (Jataka Parijata 8.97)
Loss of a limb, or a 'maimed' body (Jataka Parijata 8.97; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope)
Love of esoteric and occult knowledge, ritual-minded (Raman HPA)

by_area.personality: Energetic (Jataka Parijata 8.97); Raman HPA lists sinful or adulterous tendencies.
by_area.career: Works out of the spotlight: research, hospitals, ashrams, foreign postings (PanchangBodh).
by_area.finance: Poor (Phaladeepika 8.4, Raman HPA).
by_area.health: Weak eyes (Phaladeepika 8.4, Raman).
by_area.family: Hostile to father (Phaladeepika 8.4); has sons (Jataka Parijata 8.97) though Phaladeepika gives no sons and Raman HPA no happiness from children.
by_area.spirituality: Esoteric and occult interest (Raman HPA); read as release, retreat and moksha (PanchangBodh).

strengtheners: Satyacharya: malefics in the 12th favour fortune; Bhattotpala: benefics there reduce expenditure (Brihat Jataka 20.10 notes)
A strong Jupiter aspect on the Sun in the 12th made the native spiritual in one of Raman's case studies (How to Judge a Horoscope, Twelfth House, Chart 247)

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 8.4
source_views.view: Hostile to father, poor eyesight, without wealth and children.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 20.3 with notes
source_views.view: Degradation or fall in status; the note calls the Sun bad in the 12th.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.97
source_views.view: Has sons, is maimed, very energetic, an apostate and a vagrant.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXI
source_views.view: Sinful, poor, fallen, unsuccessful, neglected, long limbs, ritual-minded, lover of occult knowledge, no happiness from children.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. II, 'Planets in the Twelfth House'
source_views.view: May take to an immoral life or low work, not very successful, feels neglected, loss of a limb, weak eyes; energetic and has sons.

source_views.source: PanchangBodh, Sun in the 12 houses
source_views.view: Works out of the spotlight: research, hospitals, ashrams, foreign postings, long apprenticeships; read as release rather than mere loss.

source_views.source: VedicFeed, Effects of the Sun in 12 Houses
source_views.view: Positive: career and financial growth; malefic: losses, strained relations with authority, restless sleep.

planet_in_house/sun/12.disagreements: On children Phaladeepika says none, Jataka Parijata and Raman's How to Judge a Horoscope say sons. Classical texts are negative about status and wealth; PanchangBodh and VedicFeed read it as a placement of quiet, foreign or spiritual work and even growth.
planet_in_house/sun/12.phrasing_guidance: Describe a person who may shine behind the scenes, abroad or in service and spiritual settings. Avoid moral judgements, and do not predict loss of limbs, poverty or a broken bond with the father.

planet_in_house/venus/1.summary: Venus in the lagna is read as beauty, charm, happiness and long life, with attraction to and from the opposite sex and a love of art and comfort.
common_outcomes: Attractive body, beautiful eyes and face (Phaladeepika 8.17; Saravali 30.62; Jataka Parijata 8.58)
Happy (Phaladeepika 8.17; Saravali 30.62; Brihat Jataka 20.8)
Long-lived (Phaladeepika 8.17; Saravali 30.62; Bhrigu Sutras 1-13)
Attractive to the opposite sex; skilled in love (Saravali 30.62; Brihat Jataka 20.8; Raman)
rare_outcomes: Proficient in mathematics (Bhrigu Sutras 1-13)
Timid (Saravali 30.62)
Two marriages and fluctuating fortune if Venus is weak or rules the 12th (Bhrigu Sutras 11, as qualified by the commentator)
Early marriage (Raman)

by_area.personality: Amiable, cheerful, emotionally responsive, craves pleasure (Raman); well-groomed, pleasant speech (PanchangBodh); fond of ornaments and good dress (Bhrigu Sutras 1-13).
by_area.finance: Wealthy (Bhrigu Sutras 1-13); with a benefic in the 4th, high prosperity (Bhrigu Sutras 1-13).
by_area.health: Healthy body (Phaladeepika 8.17); with malefics or debilitated, rheumatic and phlegmatic complaints (Bhrigu Sutras 1-13).
by_area.relationships: Loved by the spouse (Bhrigu Sutras 1-13); fond of spouse, early marriage, discord if afflicted (Raman); 7th aspect keeps partnership in view (PanchangBodh).
by_area.family: Blessed with wife and children (Jataka Parijata 8.58).
by_area.spirituality: Performs pious deeds (Chamatkar Chintamani, via summary).

strengtheners: Exalted (Pisces) or own sign (Taurus, Libra): Brihat Jataka 20.11 scales a benefic's good results from full in exaltation to half in own sign; Bhrigu Sutras repeatedly makes the best results depend on dignity or benefic company
In a kendra in Taurus, Libra or Pisces it forms Malavya Yoga (PanchangBodh; Bhrigu Sutras commentary)
Own sign: 'Maharaja yoga' of name, fame and wealth (Bhrigu Sutras 10)
Benefic conjunction: lustrous body and many ornaments (Bhrigu Sutras 1-13)
A benefic in the 4th: high prosperity (Bhrigu Sutras 1-13)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Debilitation in Virgo or malefic association turns results adverse (Bhrigu Sutras, e.g. sutras 4, 32, 40)
Combustion: Brihat Jataka 20.11 gives a benefic no good result when combust; PanchangBodh gives the orb as 10 deg (8 deg retrograde)
Afflicted: discord in married life (Raman)
As lord of the 12th, or weak: unsteady fortune and a hard heart (Bhrigu Sutras 11 and commentary)
planet_in_house/venus/1.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman: more fortunate when the lagna is Capricorn or Aquarius. Bhrigu Sutras commentary: Venus is a yogakaraka for Virgo (2nd and 9th lord), Capricorn (5th and 10th lord) and Aquarius (4th and 9th lord) lagnas, so Venus here is very beneficial for them.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 8.17 (Mantreswara; English rendering on siva.sh)
source_views.view: Healthy, beautiful body, happy, long-lived.

source_views.source: Saravali 30.62 (Kalyana Varma; English translation PDF, translator not named in file)
source_views.view: Beautiful eyes, face and physique, happy, long-lived, timid, attractive to women.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 20.8 (Varahamihira; tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed.)
source_views.view: Venus in the lagna makes the person skilled in amorous sport and happy.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.58 (Vaidyanatha; tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, Vol. I)
source_views.view: Libidinous, lovely in looks, blessed with wife and children, learned.

source_views.source: Bhrigu Sutras ch. VII ('Effects of Venus in the Twelve Houses') sutras 1-13, with the English commentator's notes (commentator not named in file)
source_views.view: Mathematical, long-lived, loved by spouse, fond of ornaments, wealthy, learned; malefic or debilitated brings dishonesty and phlegmatic ailments; own sign gives great fortune; commentator: all authorities agree it is good; Malavya Yoga.

source_views.source: Chamatkar Chintamani, as quoted under 'Other Views' in the Bhrigu Sutras commentary (via summary)
source_views.view: Attractive, keeps noble company, pious, high comforts.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope, Vol. I ch. IV 'Planets in the First House' p.29
source_views.view: Fortunate, especially for Capricorn or Aquarius lagna; amiable, cheerful, artistic, pleasure-loving, musical; admired; fond of spouse; early marriage; afflicted discord.

source_views.source: PanchangBodh, 'Venus in houses' (modern practitioner site)
source_views.view: Attractive presence, pleasant speech, taste for comfort; aspects the 7th; Malavya in kendra; risks vanity and ease.

source_views.source: VedicFeed (Mona), 'Positive and Negative Effects of Venus in 12 Houses' (generic modern article, no classical citations)
source_views.view: Self-improvement, courtesy, happiness; downside conceit.

planet_in_house/venus/1.disagreements: Agreement on beauty, happiness and long life. Saravali 30.62 alone adds 'timid'. Jataka Parijata 8.58 and Brihat Jataka 20.8 stress sensuality more than the others.
planet_in_house/venus/1.phrasing_guidance: Lead with charm, taste and warmth. Keep attraction and pleasure language light and non-judgemental; do not predict multiple marriages.

planet_in_house/venus/2.summary: Venus in the 2nd is unanimously good: wealth from many sources, fine food and drink, sweet speech and poetic or artistic gifts.
common_outcomes: Wealthy, often very wealthy (Phaladeepika 8.17; Saravali 30.63; Jataka Parijata 8.63; Bhrigu Sutras 14-19)
Good food and drink (Saravali 30.63; Bhrigu Sutras 14-19; Raman)
Sweet or good speech (Saravali 30.63; Brihat Jataka 20.8 read with 20.7)
Poet (Phaladeepika 8.17)
rare_outcomes: Beautiful spouse around the 32nd year (Bhrigu Sutras 14-19); text detail only
Money comes readily through the favour of others (Raman)
Eye trouble if the 2nd lord is weak or in a dusthana (Bhrigu Sutras 14-19)

by_area.personality: Humble, kind, helpful (Bhrigu Sutras 14-19); skilful and pleasant (Raman); learning, gallantry, personal graces (Jataka Parijata 8.63).
by_area.career: Earnings from art, beauty, luxury or food; singing (PanchangBodh).
by_area.finance: Wealth from many sources (Phaladeepika 8.17); amasses great wealth (Saravali 30.63); overspending on pleasure is the cost (PanchangBodh).
by_area.health: Eyes are the weak point if the 2nd lord is afflicted (Bhrigu Sutras 14-19); rich eating is a caution (PanchangBodh).
by_area.relationships: Marries a good spouse (Raman; Bhrigu Sutras 14-19).
by_area.family: Large family (Raman); family life valued for comfort (PanchangBodh).

strengtheners: Exalted (Pisces) or own sign (Taurus, Libra): Brihat Jataka 20.11 scales a benefic's good results from full in exaltation to half in own sign; Bhrigu Sutras repeatedly makes the best results depend on dignity or benefic company
In a kendra in Taurus, Libra or Pisces it forms Malavya Yoga (PanchangBodh; Bhrigu Sutras commentary)
Own sign or exaltation improves results further (Bhrigu Sutras commentary)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Debilitation in Virgo or malefic association turns results adverse (Bhrigu Sutras, e.g. sutras 4, 32, 40)
Combustion: Brihat Jataka 20.11 gives a benefic no good result when combust; PanchangBodh gives the orb as 10 deg (8 deg retrograde)
Weak 2nd lord or 2nd lord in the 6th, 8th or 12th: eye trouble; with the Moon as well, wealth squandered (Bhrigu Sutras 16-19)
planet_in_house/venus/2.lagna_or_context_notes: Bhrigu Sutras commentary: Dhana yogas for Aries lagna (Venus in Taurus as 2nd and 7th lord), Virgo lagna (Libra, 2nd and 9th lord) and Aquarius lagna (exalted in Pisces as 4th and 9th lord).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 8.17 (Mantreswara; English rendering on siva.sh)
source_views.view: A poet with many kinds of wealth.

source_views.source: Saravali 30.63 (Kalyana Varma; English translation PDF, translator not named in file)
source_views.view: Abundant food, drink and wealth, excellent pleasures, good speech, great wealth.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 20.8 read with 20.7 (Venus in houses not named in 20.8 gives Jupiter's results; tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Venus in the 2nd, like Jupiter there, makes the person eloquent or sweet-tongued.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.63 (Vaidyanatha; tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, Vol. I)
source_views.view: Learning, gallantry, personal graces and much wealth.

source_views.source: Bhrigu Sutras ch. VII ('Effects of Venus in the Twelve Houses') sutras 14-19, with the English commentator's notes (commentator not named in file)
source_views.view: Wealthy, family, good food, attractive eyes, humble and kind; weak 2nd lord gives eye trouble; commentator: consensus that it is very beneficial; Dhana-yoga lagnas listed.

source_views.source: Chamatkar Chintamani, as quoted under 'Other Views' in the Bhrigu Sutras commentary (via summary)
source_views.view: Sweet-tongued, intelligent, good looks and dress, fond of beauty.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope, Vol. I ch. V 'Planets in the Second House' p.55
source_views.view: Large family, money through favours, good food, conveyances, handsome, skilful, good spouse, health and wealth.

source_views.source: PanchangBodh, 'Venus in houses' (modern practitioner site)
source_views.view: Sweet speech and singing; income from art, beauty, luxury, food; aspects the 8th; overspending and rich food.

source_views.source: VedicFeed (Mona), 'Positive and Negative Effects of Venus in 12 Houses' (generic modern article, no classical citations)
source_views.view: Comfort and wealth, artistic income; downside waste and over-expectation.

planet_in_house/venus/2.disagreements: No real disagreement; Bhrigu Sutras adds conditions (2nd lord's state) under which the eyes or savings suffer.
planet_in_house/venus/2.phrasing_guidance: Speak of a pleasant voice, taste and earning through beauty or art. Frame spending on pleasure as the thing to balance.

planet_in_house/venus/3.summary: Venus in the 3rd is widely read as a weak placement: stinginess, lack of luck or courage and domination by the spouse are common themes, though Saravali still calls the person happy and rich and modern writers stress charm and artistic expression.
common_outcomes: Stingy or miserly (Phaladeepika 8.17; Brihat Jataka 20.8 read with 20.7; Bhrigu Sutras 20-22)
Dominated by or 'conquered by' women or the spouse (Saravali 30.64; Jataka Parijata 8.66)
Unhappy, poor or unfortunate (Phaladeepika 8.17; Saravali 30.64)
Delight in music, singing, dance and fine arts (Raman)
rare_outcomes: Without a wife (Phaladeepika 8.17)
Happy and rich, though unlucky and unenthusiastic (Saravali 30.64)
Sorrow, disease and danger, unless Venus is an evening star ahead of the Sun (Jataka Parijata 8.67)
Success through determined effort; brothers decrease over time (Bhrigu Sutras 20-22)

by_area.personality: Fretful in speech (Jataka Parijata 8.66); not courageous (Saravali 30.64; Chamatkar Chintamani, via summary); likeable negotiator (PanchangBodh).
by_area.career: Writing, music, performance, media, photography, decoration (PanchangBodh).
by_area.finance: Financially not very successful (Raman); poor (Phaladeepika 8.17); Saravali instead says rich.
by_area.health: Health poor, lacking vitality, though the mind is good (Raman).
by_area.relationships: Unpopular (Phaladeepika 8.17); spouse dominates (Saravali 30.64).
by_area.family: Good brothers (Raman); affectionate siblings, especially sisters (PanchangBodh); strong 3rd lord increases brothers, afflicted 3rd lord loses them (Bhrigu Sutras 20-22); little happiness from children (Raman).

planet_in_house/venus/3.phrasing_guidance: Present as artistic, diplomatic expression and warm sibling ties, with advice to build courage and follow-through. Avoid 'no spouse' or 'poor' predictions.

planet_in_house/venus/4.summary: Venus in the 4th is a strong placement with directional strength: a beautiful home, vehicles, ornaments, fragrance, friends and happiness; Jataka Parijata adds being overruled by the spouse.

by_area.finance: Rich (Saravali 30.65); gold and conveyances with a strong 4th lord (Bhrigu Sutras 23-28).
by_area.relationships: Many friends (Raman); risk of extra-marital ties if the 4th lord is afflicted (Bhrigu Sutras 28).

by_area.spirituality: Religiously inclined (Raman).

planet_in_house/venus/4.phrasing_guidance: Describe a beautiful, comfortable home and close bond with the mother. Treat property and vehicles as traditional indications, not promises.

planet_in_house/venus/5.summary: Venus in the 5th is read as happiness, wealth, wisdom and children, often with a high or advisory position; only Chamatkar Chintamani doubts happiness from children.

by_area.health: Afflicted: health lost through over-indulgence (Raman).

planet_in_house/venus/6.summary: Venus in the 6th is mixed and contested: Brihat Jataka, Phaladeepika and Bhrigu Sutras say no enemies, but Saravali says many enemies; most texts add grief, little wealth or friction with the spouse.
common_outcomes: No enemies, or enemies destroyed (Phaladeepika 8.18; Brihat Jataka 20.8 read with 20.7; Bhrigu Sutras 34-36; Raman)
Little wealth or poverty (Phaladeepika 8.18; Saravali 30.67)
Grief, sorrow or distress (Phaladeepika 8.18; Saravali 30.67; Jataka Parijata 8.77)
Involvement with young women (Phaladeepika 8.18; Raman)
rare_outcomes: Many enemies (Saravali 30.67; Chamatkar Chintamani, via summary)
Dislikes the spouse (Saravali 30.67)
Calumny (Jataka Parijata 8.77)
Gives the same wealth-yoga as in the 12th (Bhavartha Ratnakara, as quoted in the Bhrigu Sutras commentary; via summary)

by_area.personality: Mean, startled (Saravali 30.67); deceitful, wasteful (Bhrigu Sutras 34-36); wins through charm and negotiation (PanchangBodh).
by_area.career: Medicine, nursing, beauty, wellness, food, hospitality, tailoring, service (PanchangBodh); nursing, films or drama when well placed (Raman).
by_area.finance: Little wealth (Phaladeepika 8.18); wasteful expenditure (Bhrigu Sutras 34-36); spending can become borrowing (PanchangBodh).
by_area.health: Diseases (Bhrigu Sutras 34-36); afflicted, urinary and sexual troubles (Raman); reproductive system and kidneys deserve ordinary care (PanchangBodh).
by_area.relationships: Bitterness toward the spouse (Saravali 30.67); favours from women (Raman); workplace relationships need discretion (PanchangBodh).
by_area.family: Many relations, children and grandchildren (Bhrigu Sutras 34-36), which its commentator doubts.

planet_in_house/venus/6.phrasing_guidance: Describe a person who smooths conflict with charm and suits caring, beauty or hospitality work. Keep health remarks general and avoid predicting marital bitterness or affairs.

planet_in_house/venus/7.summary: Venus in the 7th, its own significator house, gives a good, attractive spouse and wealth in most texts, but Phaladeepika, Brihat Jataka and Bhrigu Sutras add strong passion, quarrels or straying, and Saravali alone is wholly harmonious.

Wealthy (Phaladeepika 8.18; Saravali 30.68; Bhrigu Sutras 37-44)
Strong passions, fond of sexual union (Brihat Jataka 20.8; Bhrigu Sutras 37-44; Raman)
Charming, magnetic personality (Saravali 30.68; Raman)
rare_outcomes: Secret affairs and loss of the spouse (Phaladeepika 8.18)
Promotes quarrels (Brihat Jataka 20.8); fond of quarrelling (Raman)
Favourite with courtesans, lovely but lame (Jataka Parijata 8.80)
Wealth through in-laws when dignified (Bhrigu Sutras 43)

by_area.career: Success in partnership with the opposite sex (Raman); efficient in work (Bhrigu Sutras 37-44).
by_area.finance: Great riches (Saravali 30.68); wealth through in-laws (Bhrigu Sutras 43).
by_area.health: Risk of lost vigour from excess (Raman).
by_area.relationships: Happy marriage and devoted spouse (Raman); good spouse but possible straying (Phaladeepika 8.18); malefic or debilitated Venus may bring loss of spouse and remarriage (Bhrigu Sutras 41-42).
by_area.family: A fine son (Chamatkar Chintamani, via summary).

In a kendra in Taurus, Libra or Pisces it forms Malavya Yoga (PanchangBodh; Bhrigu Sutras commentary)

With malefics, in a malefic's sign or debilitated: loss of spouse and remarriage (Bhrigu Sutras 41-42)
Afflicted by the Sun: lack of physical attraction (Raman)

planet_in_house/venus/7.disagreements: Main disagreement among Venus placements. Saravali 30.68 is wholly favourable (free of quarrels); Phaladeepika 8.18 gives a good wife but affairs and possible loss; Brihat Jataka 20.8 gives quarrels and passion; Jataka Parijata 8.80 is negative. PanchangBodh reports BPHS as cautionary (not verified in BPHS here). The Bhrigu Sutras commentator says Saravali alone omits extra-marital themes.
planet_in_house/venus/7.phrasing_guidance: Lead with affection, charm and the value placed on partnership. Never predict infidelity or loss of a spouse; at most note that the texts link strong desire here with a need for loyalty and balance.

planet_in_house/venus/8.summary: Venus in the 8th is surprisingly well rated by Phaladeepika, Saravali and Jataka Parijata (long life, wealth, comforts, land), against Brihat Jataka ('base') and Bhrigu Sutras (sickly, shorter life).

Rich, very rich (Phaladeepika 8.18; Saravali 30.69; Jataka Parijata 8.84; Raman)
All comforts (Jataka Parijata 8.84; Raman)
Rules over land; equal to a king (Phaladeepika 8.18; Saravali 30.69)

Venus: comforts of home, dress and spouse, but timid. Saturn: untidy, miserly, sharp, famous, no lasting children or friendship.

planet_in_sign/jupiter/aries.phrasing_guidance: Present as principled, energetic leadership and effort-based success. Mention rivals and expenses as things to manage, not as threats. No injury predictions.

Comfortable means, good clothes, many friends

planet_in_sign/jupiter/cancer.summary: Jupiter in Cancer (Karka) is exalted, deepest at 5 degrees: wisdom, generosity and good fortune are at their fullest. Texts describe a learned, kind, truthful and prosperous person with good children and wide respect, and Hamsa Yoga if in a kendra.

Wealth and abundant resources
Respected widely; truthful and disciplined
Children who do well; loyal friendships

source_views.view: Sun: attendants, tall, learned, a minister. Moon: very rich and calm. Mars: attractive, brave, high birth. Mercury: learned and virtuous. Venus: very attractive and affluent. Saturn: learned and wealthy but untidy and without a spouse.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.12 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Jupiter in a Venus sign: strong body, children, friends, wealth, generous, well-loved.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.12 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed., p. 350)
source_views.view: Jupiter in a Venus sign: a sound body, wealthy, friends and sons, liberal, liked by all.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (general rules: combustion, navamsa, house placements, dignities)
source_views.view: A planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and spoiled; a vargottama planet gives own-sign results, while a fallen planet that is vargottama is only worse off and a planet exalted in the birth chart but fallen in the navamsa gives very mixed results; a fallen planet is badly weakened unless well aspected; planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled.

planet_in_sign/jupiter/libra.disagreements: As with Taurus, the enemy-sign status is not reflected in the favourable classical sign verses; Sastri notes that Jupiter is good in Venus' signs.
planet_in_sign/jupiter/libra.phrasing_guidance: Describe a cultured, diplomatic and commercially capable person. Avoid predicting foreign residence; say opportunities away from home are indicated.

planet_in_sign/jupiter/scorpio.summary: Jupiter in Scorpio (Vrischika), the water sign of its friend Mars, gives deep, scriptural and intense wisdom: an expert in texts, a commentator or builder of institutions, but with a fierce streak, hardships and, classically, few children.
common_outcomes: Expert in scripture or specialised knowledge
Skilled; may build temples, towns or institutions
Intense, sometimes fierce or showy conduct
Periods of difficulty alongside achievement
rare_outcomes: Saravali 27.15-16: may become a ruler or write commentaries on many works
Saravali mentions many partners but few children (low weight)
Brihat Jataka 18.12 (Mars sign): army leader, famous

by_area.personality: Saravali 27.15-16: very fierce and ostentatious, yet virtuous; may commit contemptuous acts.
by_area.career: Saravali 27.15-16: expert in Sastras, writes commentaries, builds temples and towns. Brihat Jataka 18.12: head of an army.
by_area.finance: Brihat Jataka grants great wealth; Saravali notes hardships.
by_area.health: Saravali mentions illness among hardships; do not convert into a prediction.
by_area.relationships: Saravali mentions many partners (a period marker of status).
by_area.family: Saravali: few children; treat as low weight.
by_area.spirituality: Saravali 27.15-16: expert in sacred texts and their commentaries.

strengtheners: Friendly sign (Phaladeepika 3.18)

Saravali 27.25-30 (Aries/Scorpio group): Sun's aspect gives charity, truthfulness and famous children; Moon's aspect gives learning and writing; Mars' aspect gives valour and political knowledge; Venus' aspect gives comforts
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a vargottama planet gives results like a planet in its own sign
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saravali 27.25-30: Mercury's aspect makes crafty; Saturn's aspect brings miserliness and no lasting children or friendship
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (rules of interpretation): planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled

source_views.source: Saravali 27.15-16 (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Expert in scripture, may become a ruler or commentator, skilled, builds temples and towns, many partners but few sons, illness and hardship, fierce, showy, fundamentally virtuous though may do disdainful acts.

source_views.source: Saravali 27.25-30, aspects on Jupiter in Aries/Scorpio (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Sun: charitable, truthful, famous children. Moon: writer of history and poetry, learned. Mars: valorous, political knowledge, disobedient servants. Mercury: crafty, fault-finding. Venus: comforts. Saturn: miserly, no lasting children or friendship.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.12 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Jupiter in a Mars sign: army leader, wealthy, generous, forgiving, sharp-witted, famous.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.12 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed., p. 350)
source_views.view: Jupiter in a Mars sign: head of an army, very wealthy, many wives and children, liberal, forgiving, brave, generous, famous.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (general rules: combustion, navamsa, house placements, dignities)
source_views.view: A planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and spoiled; a vargottama planet gives own-sign results, while a fallen planet that is vargottama is only worse off and a planet exalted in the birth chart but fallen in the navamsa gives very mixed results; a fallen planet is badly weakened unless well aspected; planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled.

planet_in_sign/jupiter/scorpio.disagreements: Brihat Jataka treats Aries and Scorpio alike and is favourable; Saravali gives Scorpio a more mixed picture (scriptural mastery but hardship, fierceness and few children).
planet_in_sign/jupiter/scorpio.phrasing_guidance: Present as profound knowledge and the ability to build lasting institutions. Do not predict childlessness or illness; mention intensity as something to channel well.

planet_in_sign/jupiter/sagittarius.summary: Jupiter in Sagittarius (Dhanu) is in its moolatrikona (0-10 degrees) and own sign (10-30 degrees): a strong, dharmic Jupiter that gives a teacher, priest or adviser, charitable, learned, well-travelled and drawn to solitude and pilgrimage. Hamsa Yoga if in a kendra.
common_outcomes: Teacher, preceptor or guide; conducts rites or ceremonies
Charitable, helpful and loyal to one's own
Learned in scripture or philosophy
Travels widely; visits sacred places
rare_outcomes: Saravali 27.17-18: may lead a region or serve as a minister
Brihat Jataka 18.13 (own sign): provincial ruler, minister, army commander or wealthy
Hamsa Yoga in a kendra

by_area.personality: Saravali 27.17-18: charitable, helpful, friendly to his own people, prefers solitude. Foss (name 52): Sagittarius is Jupiter's male sign, the priest or educator; its challenge is appreciating other people's opinions.
by_area.career: Saravali 27.17-18: a preceptor, head of a region or a minister. Brihat Jataka 18.13 (own sign): a king, minister, commander or very wealthy.
by_area.finance: Saravali: lasting wealth.
by_area.relationships: Saravali: friendly to his own people.
by_area.spirituality: Strong: rites, vows, initiations and pilgrimage (Saravali 27.17-18).

strengtheners: Moolatrikona 0-10 degrees (BPHS 3.53); Foss (name 45) calls Sagittarius the moolatrikona and 'most favoured' of Jupiter's signs. Phaladeepika 3.18 calls a planet in moolatrikona 'happy' and in own sign 'confident'
Hamsa Yoga if in a kendra (Phaladeepika 6.1, 6.3; Raman no. 19)

Saravali 27.55-60 (Sagittarius/Pisces group): Moon's aspect gives many kinds of happiness, a fortunate marriage and wealth; Mercury's aspect gives a minister's or ruler's standing with wealth and children; Venus' aspect gives learning, long life and Lakshmi's blessing
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a vargottama planet gives results like a planet in its own sign
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saravali 27.55-60: Sun's aspect brings enmity with authority and loss of wealth and relatives; Mars' aspect, injury in conflict, cruelty and loss of children; Saturn's aspect, fear and neglect by others
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (rules of interpretation): planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled
planet_in_sign/jupiter/sagittarius.lagna_or_context_notes: Hamsa Yoga needs Sagittarius to be a kendra from the lagna: Sagittarius, Gemini, Virgo and Pisces lagnas (Phaladeepika 6.1, 6.3). Raman (no. 19) says that when Hamsa is present Jupiter's kendra ownership ceases to matter, though an own-sign Hamsa keeps a trace of that defect; his own-sign example (Jupiter in the 10th) gave a self-made, respected public figure rather than a ruler.

source_views.source: Saravali 27.17-18 (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: A preceptor who conducts rites, vows and initiations, lasting wealth, charitable, loyal, helpful, learned in scripture, may lead a region or be a minister, travels widely, prefers solitude, visits shrines.

source_views.source: Saravali 27.55-60, aspects on Jupiter in Sagittarius/Pisces (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Sun: hostile to the ruler, without wealth and relatives. Moon: many kinds of happiness, fortunate marriage, honour and wealth. Mars: injured in war, cruel, loses children. Mercury: minister or ruler, wealth, children, delights. Venus: happy, learned, long-lived, blessed by Lakshmi. Saturn: untidy, fearful, neglected, unhappy.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.13 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Jupiter in own sign: provincial ruler, minister, army commander or wealthy.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 3.53
source_views.view: Jupiter's moolatrikona is the first 10 degrees of Sagittarius; the rest is own sign.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.1, 6.3
source_views.view: Hamsa Yoga definition and results.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.13 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed., p. 352)
source_views.view: Jupiter in his own sign: a king, his minister, a commander of forces, or immensely wealthy.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 19 Hamsa Yoga (pp. 43-47)
source_views.view: Jupiter in a kendra in its own or exaltation sign: handsome, liked by others, righteous and pure-minded. Possible only for movable and common lagnas; the 10th is the strongest kendra; Jupiter's kendra ownership is normally undesirable but loses significance when Hamsa is present, and an exaltation-sign Hamsa is preferable to an own-sign one. Malefic aspects restrict the results.

source_views.source: Andrew Foss, The Yoga of the Planets: Jupiter, Brihaspati, names 45 and 52
source_views.view: Sagittarius is the moolatrikona, 'most favoured' of Jupiter's signs, a place of the battle of good and evil. It is the priest or educator working for the people; feeling naturally correct, its challenge is appreciating others' opinions.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (general rules: combustion, navamsa, house placements, dignities)
source_views.view: A planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and spoiled; a vargottama planet gives own-sign results, while a fallen planet that is vargottama is only worse off and a planet exalted in the birth chart but fallen in the navamsa gives very mixed results; a fallen planet is badly weakened unless well aspected; planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled.

planet_in_sign/jupiter/sagittarius.disagreements: Strong agreement. Saravali emphasises the teacher or priest role, Brihat Jataka the worldly rank of an own-sign Jupiter, Foss the risk of being sure of one's own opinions.
planet_in_sign/jupiter/sagittarius.phrasing_guidance: Describe a principled, generous, knowledge-sharing nature. Keep worldly rank conditional on the rest of the chart.

planet_in_sign/jupiter/capricorn.summary: Jupiter in Capricorn (Makara) is debilitated, deepest at 5 degrees: faith, optimism and generosity are restricted by Saturn's sign. Classical texts describe low vigour, hardship and lack of means, but neecha bhanga is common and modern authors read it as practical, earned wisdom.
common_outcomes: Practical, structured worldview; convictions earned through experience (astromedha)
Periods of hardship, low spirits or limited resources (Saravali, Brihat Jataka)
Serves others or works in demanding roles (Saravali)
Interest in ritual and in the practical application of knowledge (Foss)
rare_outcomes: Saravali 27.19-20: wish to live abroad
Saravali 27.61-66: with Saturn's aspect, a learned ruler; with Mars' aspect, valour and command (these aspect results apply to Capricorn/Aquarius)
With neecha bhanga, rise to prominence after early struggle (Phaladeepika 7.26-30)

by_area.personality: Saravali 27.19-20: timid and low in spirits. Foss (name 7): can show as concern for status or ego, which may arise from a fear of being deficient.
by_area.career: Saravali 27.19-20: serves others.
by_area.finance: Saravali: penury; Brihat Jataka 18.13: poor. Disciplined saving is relevant.
by_area.family: Saravali 27.19-20: lacking affection toward relatives.
by_area.spirituality: Saravali: lacking religious feeling. Foss: a strong interest in ritual, against the more philosophical Jupiter in Cancer; the knowledge one needs will come when one is ready. astromedha: risk of spiritual emptiness.

strengtheners: Neecha bhanga (Phaladeepika 7.26-30): Saturn (lord of Capricorn) or the Moon (lord of Jupiter's exaltation sign Cancer) in a kendra from the lagna or Moon; the two lords in mutual kendras; or Jupiter aspected by Saturn (7.28). Phaladeepika's commentary allows the planet exalted in Capricorn (Mars) as an alternative reading
Raman (no. 250) prefers that alternative: Mars, exalted in Capricorn, in a kendra from the lagna or Moon cancels the debility

Saravali 27.61-66 (Capricorn/Aquarius group): Sun's aspect gives learning, royal standing and courage; Moon's aspect, devotion to parents, learning and charity; Mars' aspect, an army chief who is famous and honoured; Venus' aspect, comforts, wealth and a fine spouse; Saturn's aspect, incomparable learning and rule over a country
Foss: many great people have a debilitated Jupiter; it helps the practical application of Jupiter's gifts, so it need not cause concern
weakeners_or_cancellations: Phaladeepika 3.19: a debilitated planet is 'greatly afraid'; Braha: a planet in its fallen sign is badly weakened unless well aspected
Deepest debility near 5 degrees Capricorn (BPHS 3.50)
Saravali 27.61-66: Mercury's aspect gives fame, wealth and friends but strong desires
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a debilitated planet that is also vargottama is only worse off
planet_in_sign/jupiter/capricorn.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman (Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 250) reckons neecha bhanga from both the lagna and the Moon, so check kendras from both before giving a weak reading.

source_views.source: Saravali 27.19-20 (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Less vigorous, much grief and hardship, mean, dull, often poor, serves others, lacks virtue and religious feeling, thin, timid, wishes to live abroad, low spirits.

source_views.source: Saravali 27.61-66, aspects on Jupiter in Capricorn/Aquarius (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Sun: learned, courageous. Moon: devoted to parents. Mars: valorous army chief. Mercury: famous, strong desires. Venus: comforts. Saturn: a learned ruler.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.13 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Jupiter in Capricorn: base, little wealth, unhappy.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 3.49-50
source_views.view: Debilitation is the seventh sign from exaltation at the same degree: 5 degrees Capricorn.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 7.26-30
source_views.view: Neecha bhanga raja yoga conditions and results.

source_views.source: astromedha.in, Jupiter in Capricorn (practitioner, no classical citation)
source_views.view: Practical, structured worldview, earned convictions; risks of rigidity and spiritual emptiness; cancellation if Saturn is in a kendra or Jupiter itself is in a kendra.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.13 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed., p. 352)
source_views.view: Jupiter in Makara: base, poor and unhappy.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 250 Neechabhanga Raja Yoga (pp. 242-244)
source_views.view: The lord of the debilitation sign, or the planet exalted there, in a kendra from the lagna or Moon cancels debility and gives elevation. Raman follows B. Suryanarain Rao in reading 'thaduchchanatha' as the planet exalted in that sign (Mars, for Jupiter in Capricorn) and notes the reading is disputed.

source_views.source: Andrew Foss, The Yoga of the Planets: Jupiter, Brihaspati, name 7
source_views.view: Jupiter's maximum debilitation is in Capricorn, a sign concerned with status: like a teacher who thinks himself special and lacks the humility of pure knowledge, an ego that may come from fear of being deficient. It shows as strong interest in ritual. Many great people have it; it helps the practical application of Jupiter's tendencies, so one should not be concerned.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (general rules: combustion, navamsa, house placements, dignities)
source_views.view: A planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and spoiled; a vargottama planet gives own-sign results, while a fallen planet that is vargottama is only worse off and a planet exalted in the birth chart but fallen in the navamsa gives very mixed results; a fallen planet is badly weakened unless well aspected; planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled.

planet_in_sign/jupiter/capricorn.disagreements: Classical sign verses are uniformly adverse; Foss and astromedha stress practical wisdom and frequent cancellation. Practitioners differ on whether Mars (exalted in Capricorn) counts as a cancelling planet: Phaladeepika 7.26's commentary gives it as an alternative reading, and Raman adopts it while saying the point is still disputed.
planet_in_sign/jupiter/capricorn.phrasing_guidance: Never say 'bad Jupiter' or predict poverty. Describe a grounded, practical wisdom that grows through experience, and always check for neecha bhanga, aspects and D9 before giving a weak reading.

planet_in_sign/jupiter/aquarius.summary: Jupiter in Aquarius (Kumbha), Saturn's air sign and neutral for Jupiter, is described very differently by the two main texts: Saravali gives a harsh picture (gossip, low company, loss through one's own words), while Brihat Jataka, in both Sastri's and the word-by-word translation, says the results equal those of Jupiter in Cancer (gems, wealth, family happiness).
common_outcomes: Speech has strong consequences: Saravali says wealth is lost through one's own words
Mixed fortune depending on aspects and house, because the main texts conflict
Saravali: may be chief among his own people despite its other warnings
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 18.13: results like Jupiter in Cancer (gems, wealth, spouse, children, comforts)
Saravali 27.21-22: association with low company and disreputable work
Saravali 27.61-66: Saturn's aspect gives a learned ruler

by_area.personality: Saravali warns of malicious or careless talk and ill disposition.
by_area.career: Saravali 27.21-22: interested in disreputable work, yet chief among his own people.
by_area.finance: Saravali: loses wealth through own speech; Brihat Jataka: prosperous (like Cancer).
by_area.health: Saravali mentions frequent illness; do not convert into a prediction.

strengtheners: Brihat Jataka 18.13 (Sastri and the wisdomlib word-by-word gloss): results equal to Jupiter in Cancer; Sastri's note to 18.12: Jupiter is good in all signs except Capricorn

Saravali 27.61-66 (Capricorn/Aquarius group): Sun's aspect gives learning and courage; Moon's aspect, learning and charity; Mars' aspect, command; Venus' aspect, comforts; Saturn's aspect, a learned ruler
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a vargottama planet gives results like a planet in its own sign
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saravali 27.21-22: the sign verse itself is strongly adverse
Saravali 27.61-66: Mercury's aspect gives fame with strong desires
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (rules of interpretation): planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled

source_views.source: Saravali 27.21-22 (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Tale-bearer, ill-disposed, interested in evil work, yet chief among his own people; keeps low company, malicious, miserly, often ill, loses wealth through his own words, lacks intelligence and virtue.

source_views.source: Saravali 27.61-66, aspects on Jupiter in Capricorn/Aquarius (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Sun: learned, courageous. Moon: devoted to parents. Mars: army chief. Venus: comforts. Saturn: learned ruler.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.13 (tr. M. D. Neely, word-by-word gloss; the English rendering omits this line)
source_views.view: Jupiter in Aquarius: results similar to Jupiter in Cancer.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.13 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed., p. 352)
source_views.view: The effect of a birth with Jupiter in Aquarius will be similar to that described for Jupiter in Cancer (gems, sons, wealth, wives, influence, good intellect, comforts). Sastri's note to 18.12: Jupiter is good in all signs except Makara.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (general rules: combustion, navamsa, house placements, dignities)
source_views.view: A planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and spoiled; a vargottama planet gives own-sign results, while a fallen planet that is vargottama is only worse off and a planet exalted in the birth chart but fallen in the navamsa gives very mixed results; a fallen planet is badly weakened unless well aspected; planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled.

planet_in_sign/jupiter/aquarius.disagreements: Major disagreement: Brihat Jataka equates Aquarius with Cancer (favourable), while Saravali's verse is strongly adverse. The Brihat Jataka line is now verified: Sastri's translation of 18.13 (p. 352) states it explicitly, matching the word-by-word gloss on wisdomlib (Neely's English rendering omits it).
planet_in_sign/jupiter/aquarius.phrasing_guidance: Because classical sources conflict, keep the reading neutral: wisdom whose results depend on aspects and house, with mindful speech as a practical point. No illness predictions.

planet_in_sign/jupiter/pisces.summary: Jupiter in Pisces (Meena), its own water sign, gives a spiritually learned, honoured, prosperous and steady person with skill in strategy and conduct; Hamsa Yoga if in a kendra.
common_outcomes: Expert in sacred or philosophical knowledge
Honoured by friends and good people
Rich, steadfast and composed
Skilled in planning, conduct and strategy
rare_outcomes: Saravali 27.23-24: royal official or ruler; unconquerable in contests
Brihat Jataka 18.13 (own sign): provincial ruler, minister, army commander
Hamsa Yoga in a kendra

by_area.personality: Saravali 27.23-24: fearless, proud, firm in undertakings, calm in conduct. Foss (name 52): Pisces is vast like the ocean; its challenge is controlling the ego.
by_area.career: Saravali 27.23-24: a headman in the ruler's employ, skilled in policy, training, conduct and war tactics. Brihat Jataka 18.13: a king, minister, commander or very wealthy.
by_area.finance: Favourable: rich (Saravali).
by_area.relationships: Saravali: honoured by friends and virtuous people.
by_area.spirituality: Strong: expert in the meaning of the Vedas and Sastras (Saravali).

strengtheners: Own sign (Phaladeepika 3.18: 'confident')
Hamsa Yoga in a kendra (Phaladeepika 6.1, 6.3; Raman no. 19)

James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a vargottama planet gives results like a planet in its own sign

source_views.source: Andrew Foss, The Yoga of the Planets: Jupiter, Brihaspati, name 52
source_views.view: Pisces is the ocean, vast like Jupiter, receiving everything; it is the sign closest to Brahman, giving a sense of greatness that is often deserved; its challenge is controlling the ego, and it may take in things not ideal for health.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (general rules: combustion, navamsa, house placements, dignities)
source_views.view: A planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and spoiled; a vargottama planet gives own-sign results, while a fallen planet that is vargottama is only worse off and a planet exalted in the birth chart but fallen in the navamsa gives very mixed results; a fallen planet is badly weakened unless well aspected; planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled.

planet_in_sign/jupiter/pisces.disagreements: None substantial; both main texts are favourable. Foss adds an ego caution that the classical verses do not raise.
planet_in_sign/jupiter/pisces.phrasing_guidance: Describe a wise, composed and spiritually inclined person with good standing. Keep 'ruler' language as respect and influence, conditional on the wider chart.

planet_in_sign/ketu/aries.summary: Ketu in Aries sits in Mars's sign, and Ketu is widely said to act like Mars (Frawley, Foss), so modern readers see a natural fit; BPHS names Aries among signs where Ketu brings wealth even in a weak avastha. Raman's dasa note, however, is harsh, warning of family friction, losses and travel.
common_outcomes: Mars-like energy and courage (Frawley p.103; Foss, name 5)

planet_in_sign/mars/aries.summary: Aries is Mars's own sign; 0-12° is its moolatrikona and 12-30° own sign. It gives courage, drive, truthfulness and leadership, with a fondness for adventure and competition, and some exposure to injury.

Leadership in teams, groups or organisations
Love of adventure, sport and competition
Honoured for action and initiative

by_area.personality: Splendid, truthful, brave, fierce and adventurous (Saravali 25.1-2); organising capacity, commanding, pioneering, frank and generous but combative (Raman HPA ch. XXII).

Kendra placement; Braha (p. 50) says planets in kendras are powerful and prominent
Placement in the 10th, where Mars has directional strength (Braha pp. 23, 60; Foss, Mars name 12)
Jupiter's aspect (Saravali 25.25-30: learning, fortune, wealth, kingly results for Mars in its own signs)

Exalted or own sign in the navamsa, or vargottama (Braha pp. 13-14, 59-60)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Venus's aspect (Saravali 25.25-30: loss and trouble through relationships)
Mercury's aspect (Saravali 25.25-30: deceit)
Saturn's aspect (Saravali 25.25-30: loss of followers)
Combustion (within about 8 degrees of the Sun), which Braha (pp. 17, 61) says spoils a planet
planet_in_sign/mars/aries.lagna_or_context_notes: Mars in Aries in a kendra forms Ruchaka yoga (Phaladeepika 6.1-2): Aries (1st), Capricorn (4th), Libra (7th), Cancer (10th) lagnas; Phaladeepika 6.4 also counts kendras from the Moon. Braha ('Planets in the Houses', pp. 79 ff.) reads the own-sign Mars house by house: Aries lagna (1st) success, respect, courage; Capricorn lagna (4th) land and houses, a strong but discordant bond with the mother; Libra lagna (7th) marriage still strained but a better-quality spouse; Cancer lagna (10th) a great career with wealth and fame; Gemini lagna (11th) ambitions realised. Braha (p. 67) counts Mars in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th as Kujadosha unless it is in that house's exception sign; with Mars in Aries this applies to Capricorn (4th), Libra (7th), Virgo (8th), Taurus (12th) lagnas, while Aries lagna (1st) is exempt. He notes some astrologers use the 2nd house instead of the 1st. For Cancer lagna Mars alone forms rajayoga as lord of the 5th and 10th (Braha p. 53).

planet_in_sign/mars/cancer.summary: Mars is debilitated in Cancer (deepest fall at 28°), though Cancer's lord, the Moon, is a friend. The fiery planet in a watery sign gives emotional reactivity, indirect assertion and unsettled living conditions, yet texts also give prosperity through water-related work; neecha bhanga is frequently present.

planet_in_sign/mars/cancer.lagna_or_context_notes: Braha ('Planets in the Houses', pp. 79 ff.) reads the fallen Mars harshly house by house: Cancer lagna (1st) health and self-respect suffer, though Mars as 5th and 10th lord still gives some benefits there; Aries lagna (4th) strain around home and mother; Capricorn lagna (7th) a difficult marriage; Libra lagna (10th) career difficulties and changes. Frawley (p. 126) instead says debility is much reduced in an angle, especially the 10th, so the 1st, 4th, 7th and 10th cases above are where the two authors pull in opposite directions. Braha (p. 67) counts Mars in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th as Kujadosha unless it is in that house's exception sign; with Mars in Cancer this applies to Cancer (1st), Aries (4th), Capricorn (7th), Leo (12th) lagnas, while Sagittarius lagna (8th) is exempt. He notes some astrologers use the 2nd house instead of the 1st. For Cancer lagna Mars alone forms rajayoga as lord of the 5th and 10th (Braha p. 53).

planet_in_sign/mars/scorpio.summary: Scorpio is Mars's own sign (its second, watery sign). It gives tenacity, strategic courage and land or property, but classical texts link it to intrigue, hidden conflicts and exposure to danger from fire, weapons or poison.

by_area.career: Trade and Vedic learning (Saravali 25.15-16); command or trade (Brihat Jataka 18.5); Raman: great strides in life.

by_area.family: Lands, sons and a wife (Saravali 25.15-16).
by_area.spirituality: Interested in Vedic knowledge (Saravali 25.15-16).

planet_in_sign/mars/scorpio.lagna_or_context_notes: Mars in Scorpio in a kendra forms Ruchaka yoga (Phaladeepika 6.1-2): Scorpio (1st), Leo (4th), Taurus (7th), Aquarius (10th) lagnas; Phaladeepika 6.4 also counts kendras from the Moon. Braha ('Planets in the Houses', pp. 79 ff.) reads the own-sign Mars house by house: Scorpio lagna (1st) success, respect, courage; Leo lagna (4th) land and houses; Taurus lagna (7th) marriage still strained but a better-quality spouse; Aquarius lagna (10th) a great career with wealth and fame; Capricorn lagna (11th) ambitions realised. Braha (p. 67) counts Mars in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th as Kujadosha unless it is in that house's exception sign; with Mars in Scorpio this applies to Scorpio (1st), Taurus (7th), Aries (8th), Sagittarius (12th) lagnas, while Leo lagna (4th) is exempt. He notes some astrologers use the 2nd house instead of the 1st. For Cancer lagna Mars alone forms rajayoga as lord of the 5th and 10th (Braha p. 53).

planet_in_sign/mars/capricorn.summary: Mars is exalted in Capricorn (deepest exaltation at 28°), in Saturn's sign. It gives disciplined, effective courage: wealth, fame, leadership and success in competition, with a good spouse and family.

planet_in_sign/mars/capricorn.lagna_or_context_notes: Mars in Capricorn in a kendra forms Ruchaka yoga (Phaladeepika 6.1-2): Capricorn (1st), Libra (4th), Cancer (7th), Aries (10th) lagnas; Phaladeepika 6.4 also counts kendras from the Moon. Braha ('Planets in the Houses', pp. 79 ff.) reads the exalted Mars house by house: Capricorn lagna (1st) success, respect, courage; Libra lagna (4th) land and houses; Cancer lagna (7th) a better-quality spouse and more domestic peace because Capricorn cancels Kujadosha; Aries lagna (10th) a great career with wealth and fame; Pisces lagna (11th) ambitions realised. Braha (p. 67) counts Mars in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th as Kujadosha unless it is in that house's exception sign; with Mars in Capricorn this applies to Capricorn (1st), Libra (4th), Gemini (8th), Aquarius (12th) lagnas, while Cancer lagna (7th) is exempt. He notes some astrologers use the 2nd house instead of the 1st. For Cancer lagna Mars alone forms rajayoga as lord of the 5th and 10th (Braha p. 53).

source_views.view: Troubles in love affairs, few children, passionate, restless, antagonistic, faithful, colic, indolent, wilful.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), 'Mars' p. 23, 'House Rulerships' pp. 50-53, 'Shad Bala' pp. 59-61 and 'Kujadosha' p. 67
source_views.view: Mars does well in the upachaya houses and best in the 10th (directional strength); kendras are powerful, trikonas flourish, dusthanas spoil; combustion within about 8 degrees spoils a planet; dignity in the navamsa strengthens; Mars in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th gives Kujadosha unless in the exception sign; for Cancer lagna Mars alone forms rajayoga.

planet_in_sign/mars/pisces.disagreements: Brihat Jataka is mostly favourable (fame, ministerial post); Saravali is mostly unfavourable (loss of wealth through the native's own cunning, family friction) but still says famous; Raman is mixed. The friend's-sign dignity (BPHS 3.55) supports the milder view.
planet_in_sign/mars/pisces.phrasing_guidance: Present as recognition-seeking, service-capable energy; advise care with trust in money matters. Avoid disease or family-conflict predictions.

planet_in_sign/mercury/aries.summary: Mercury in Aries (Mesha), a Mars-ruled fire sign that is neutral for Mercury, gives a quick, combative and impatient intellect: sharp in debate and fond of the arts, but classical texts warn of hasty speech, loose finances and a tendency to bend the truth.
common_outcomes: Fast thinker and speaker who enjoys argument and competition of ideas
Learned or well-read, with an interest in music, dance or the performing arts
Restless mind that alternates between fickle and firm
Money earned with effort can slip away through haste or overspending
rare_outcomes: Saravali 26.1-2 adds a writer who produces fiction or invented material
Saravali also mentions repeated debts and even confinement (read today as legal or contractual trouble from rash commitments)
Brihat Jataka 18.8 (Mercury in a Mars sign) lists gambling, debt, fondness for drink, scepticism and deceitful dealings

by_area.personality: Saravali 26.1-2: fond of fights, very learned, interested in music and dance, sometimes fickle and sometimes firm. Brihat Jataka 18.8 adds a tendency to falsehood.
by_area.career: Saravali 26.1-2: a writer who produces invented or fictional material.
by_area.finance: Saravali 26.1-2: loses hard-earned money and incurs debts; Brihat Jataka 18.8: poor. Careful contracts and budgeting matter.
by_area.health: Saravali describes a lean build; no further health claims should be made.
by_area.relationships: Saravali 26.1-2 mentions strong attachment to sexual pleasure; Brihat Jataka 18.8 (Sastri) mentions a difficult spouse.
by_area.spirituality: Brihat Jataka 18.8 calls the native unbelieving (Neely) or an atheist (Sastri): a sceptical, questioning mind.

strengtheners: Saravali 26.25-30: Mercury in Aries/Scorpio aspected by the Sun gives truthfulness, happiness and honour from the ruler; aspected by Jupiter gives happiness, great wealth and command (though also called sinful); aspected by Venus gives royal service, trustworthiness and a spouse
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a vargottama planet gives results like a planet in its own sign
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (rules of interpretation): planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saravali 26.25-30: Saturn's aspect gives misery, fierceness and loss of one's own people; the Moon's aspect makes the native serve others and lack virtues
Mars' aspect gives learning, wealth and courage but adds lying and quarrelling (Saravali 26.25-30)

James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (Sun and 'Combustion' sections): a planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and its significations and the houses it rules are spoiled; Raman (Budha-Aditya Yoga) suggests Mercury may partly escape this

source_views.source: Saravali 26.1-2 (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Combative, learned but crafty, lean, fond of music and dance, untruthful, sensual, a writer of fiction, heavy eater, loses earned money, debts and confinement, mind alternately fickle and firm.

source_views.source: Saravali 26.25-30, aspects on Mercury in Aries/Scorpio (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Sun: truthful, happy, honoured by the ruler. Moon: attracts women, serves others. Mars: learned, wealthy, brave but untruthful. Jupiter: happy, rich, commanding. Venus: royal service, trustworthy. Saturn: miserable, harsh, without his own people.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.8 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Mercury in a sign of Mars: gambler, debtor, fond of drink, unbelieving, thieving and poor, given to falsehood and fraud.

source_views.source: AstroSage, Mercury in Aries (via summary)
source_views.view: Restates the Saravali description: combative, learned, writer, debts.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra ch. 3 (natural relationships)
source_views.view: Mercury treats Mars as neutral, so Aries is a neutral sign for Mercury.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.8 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed., p. 345)
source_views.view: Mercury in a Mars sign: addicted to gambling, takes others' wealth, [a drunkard], an atheist, steals, poor, has a wicked wife, a cheat, speaks falsehood. Sastri's note to 18.10: Mercury is good in signs owned by benefics and bad in signs owned by malefics and in its debilitation sign.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer ('Budha-Mercury' section)
source_views.view: Mars, Jupiter and Saturn are neutral to Mercury. Mercury is best in the first half of Virgo and worst in Pisces.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (general rules: combustion, navamsa, house placements, dignities)
source_views.view: A planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and spoiled; a vargottama planet gives own-sign results, while a fallen planet that is vargottama is only worse off and a planet exalted in the birth chart but fallen in the navamsa gives very mixed results; a fallen planet is badly weakened unless well aspected; planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 24 Budha-Aditya Yoga (p. 54)
source_views.view: Mercury with the Sun: highly intelligent, skilful, good reputation, comforts. Planets with the Sun usually become combust and lose power, but Mercury may be an exception; the yoga should not be assumed regardless of the distance between them.

planet_in_sign/mercury/aries.disagreements: Saravali and Brihat Jataka agree on the negative tone (rashness, untruth, debt), but Saravali also grants real learning and artistic talent, while Brihat Jataka's verse is almost wholly unfavourable (Sastri and Neely agree on this). Brihat Jataka treats Aries and Scorpio together as Mars signs; Saravali separates them, and its Scorpio verse is harsher than its Aries verse.
planet_in_sign/mercury/aries.phrasing_guidance: Frame as a quick, competitive mind that does best when it slows down before speaking, signing or spending. Do not call the person dishonest, a gambler or headed for jail; present those classical lines as cautions about haste. Weigh aspects and the condition of Mars before concluding.

planet_in_sign/mercury/taurus.summary: Mercury in Taurus (Vrishabha), the earth sign of its friend Venus, gives a steady, practical and pleasant intellect: sweet in speech, skilled, learned and good at earning honestly. Classical texts rate it favourably.
common_outcomes: Skilful, generous and well regarded
Learned in traditional or technical knowledge
Pleasant, persuasive speech
Wealth earned by fair means; enjoys good clothes, ornaments and comfort
rare_outcomes: Saravali mentions fondness for physical exercise
Brihat Jataka 18.8 (Mercury in a Venus sign) describes a teacher who is devoted to his guru and generous
Saravali 26.31-36: with Jupiter's aspect the person rises to leadership and fame

by_area.personality: Saravali 26.3-4: firm in disposition, a soft and sweet speaker, skilful and very liberal.
by_area.career: Brihat Jataka 18.8: a teacher (Sastri and Neely agree).
by_area.finance: Saravali 26.3-4: sincerely earned wealth. Brihat Jataka 18.8 (Sastri): keen on amassing a large property.
by_area.relationships: Saravali 26.3-4: a chaste spouse and a sensual nature.
by_area.family: Brihat Jataka 18.8 (Sastri): wife and children; respects parents and elders.
by_area.spirituality: Saravali 26.3-4: knowledge of Vedas and Sastras. Brihat Jataka 18.8 (Neely): devoted to the guru.

strengtheners: Saravali 26.31-36: Moon's aspect gives trust, wealth, piety, health, lasting family ties and a ministerial role; Jupiter's aspect gives great learning, kept promises, leadership and fame; Venus' aspect gives fortune, gentleness and charm
Friend's sign: Braha says Mercury is 'welcomed' in the signs of its friends the Sun and Venus; Phaladeepika 3.18 calls a planet in a friend's house 'delighted'
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a vargottama planet gives results like a planet in its own sign
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saravali 26.31-36 (Taurus/Libra group): Sun's aspect is described as bringing poverty, grief, a sickly body and censure; Mars' aspect brings disease, enemies, royal insult and loss of possessions; Saturn's aspect brings unhappiness, disease and grief over relatives

James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (Sun and 'Combustion' sections): a planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and its significations and the houses it rules are spoiled; Raman (Budha-Aditya Yoga) suggests Mercury may partly escape this

source_views.source: Saravali 26.3-4 (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Skilful, very generous, famous, versed in scripture and learning, fond of good clothes, ornaments and exercise, honest wealth, faithful wife, sweet speech, sensual.

source_views.source: Saravali 26.31-36, aspects on Mercury in Taurus/Libra (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Sun: poor and censured. Moon: trusted, wealthy, a minister. Mars: loss of goods. Jupiter: learned leader, famous. Venus: fortunate, gentle. Saturn: unhappy, grieving over kin.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.8 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Mercury in a Venus sign: a teacher, wanting many children and wealth, generous, devoted to the guru.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra ch. 3 (natural relationships)
source_views.view: Venus is Mercury's natural friend, so Taurus is a friendly sign.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.8 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed., p. 345)
source_views.view: Mercury in a Venus sign: a teacher, endowed with wife and children, keen on amassing a large property, liberal in gifts, respects parents and elders.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer ('Budha-Mercury' section)
source_views.view: The Sun and Venus are Mercury's friends, and Mercury is welcomed in their signs.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (general rules: combustion, navamsa, house placements, dignities)
