source_views.view: Mercury with the Sun: highly intelligent, skilful, good reputation, comforts. Planets with the Sun usually become combust and lose power, but Mercury may be an exception; the yoga should not be assumed regardless of the distance between them.

planet_in_sign/mercury/taurus.disagreements: Little disagreement on the core: Saravali and Brihat Jataka are both favourable. They differ in emphasis (Saravali on refinement and honest wealth, Brihat Jataka on teaching and respect for elders or the guru). Saravali's Sun-aspect line cannot apply literally: Mercury never moves more than about 28 degrees from the Sun, so the Sun's 7th-house aspect on it does not occur.
planet_in_sign/mercury/taurus.phrasing_guidance: Present as a grounded, pleasant communicator with good earning sense. Avoid promising wealth; describe it as a supportive tendency that depends on the rest of the chart.

planet_in_sign/mercury/gemini.summary: Mercury in Gemini (Mithuna), its own air sign, is at home: eloquent, curious, witty and skilled at teaching and the arts. Own-sign dignity makes Mercury 'confident' and gives its results freely.
common_outcomes: Articulate, charming and quick-learning
Skilled at teaching arts, languages or crafts
Many friends and contacts; enjoys debate
Comfortable means and personal independence
rare_outcomes: Saravali mentions two marriages or reduced marital intimacy
Brihat Jataka 18.9 adds a tendency to boast
Forms Bhadra Mahapurusha Yoga if Gemini is a kendra from the lagna (Phaladeepika 6.1-2)

by_area.personality: Saravali 26.5-6: sweet and able speaker, fond of arguments, independent. Brihat Jataka 18.9 (Sastri): talkative, affable, intent on pleasure.
by_area.career: Brihat Jataka 18.9: learned in the sciences and arts and skilled at teaching them. Saravali 26.5-6: proficient in work, a poet.
by_area.finance: Saravali calls the native very affluent and munificent.
by_area.relationships: Saravali 26.5-6 mentions reduced marital intimacy and two wives; best read as a need for mental companionship.
by_area.family: Saravali speaks of many sons and friends.
by_area.spirituality: Saravali 26.5-6: learned in Vedas and Sastras.

strengtheners: Own sign (Phaladeepika 3.18: a planet in its own house is 'confident'); Braha: Mercury produces very good results in Gemini or Virgo
In a kendra from the lagna it forms Bhadra Yoga (Phaladeepika 6.1-2; Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 23)

Saravali 26.37-42 (Gemini/Virgo group): Sun's aspect gives truthfulness, fortune and favour from the ruler; Jupiter's aspect gives a minister's post, beauty, charity, wealth and courage; Saturn's aspect gives progress, modesty, success and wealth
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a vargottama planet gives results like a planet in its own sign
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saravali 26.37-42: Mars' aspect gives genius and royal service but an injured body; Venus' aspect gives learning and royal employment but low company

James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (Sun and 'Combustion' sections): a planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and its significations and the houses it rules are spoiled; Raman (Budha-Aditya Yoga) suggests Mercury may partly escape this
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (rules of interpretation): planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled
planet_in_sign/mercury/gemini.lagna_or_context_notes: Bhadra Yoga arises when Gemini is a kendra from the lagna, i.e. for Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius and Pisces lagnas (Phaladeepika 6.1-2). Raman (Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 23) adds that Mercury must be very powerful, otherwise the yoga is present only on paper.

source_views.source: Saravali 26.5-6 (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Attractive, eloquent, affluent, honourable and independent; argumentative, a learned poet, generous, with many children and friends; marital intimacy reduced, two wives mentioned.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.9 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Mercury in Gemini: boastful, skilled in teaching the arts, kind-spoken, pleasure-loving.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.1-2 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Bhadra Yoga (Mercury in own or exaltation sign in a kendra): long life, sharp intellect, spotless fame praised by scholars, wealth, eloquence in assemblies.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 3.18
source_views.view: A planet in its own house is described as 'confident'.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.9 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed., p. 346)
source_views.view: Mercury in Gemini: talkative, learned in the sciences and arts, affable, always intent on pleasure.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 23 Bhadra Yoga (p. 53)
source_views.view: Mercury in a kendra in its own or exaltation sign: strong, well-built, taciturn, helps relatives, long-lived. Mercury must be very powerful or the yoga exists only on paper.

source_views.source: Andrew Foss, The Yoga of the Planets: Mercury, Budha, name 106 'Fond of Virgo'
source_views.view: Virgo is where Mercury is happiest: own sign, moolatrikona and exaltation at once. Virgo, an earth sign, helps Mercury express stability; Gemini is excellent for intellectual pursuits.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer ('Budha-Mercury' section)
source_views.view: Mercury owns Gemini and Virgo and produces very good results in either sign.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (general rules: combustion, navamsa, house placements, dignities)

planet_in_sign/mercury/gemini.disagreements: Saravali's mention of two wives and less intimacy is not echoed in Brihat Jataka. On Brihat Jataka 18.9 the translations differ in tone: Neely has 'boastful', Sastri 'talkative'. All agree on eloquence and skill in the arts.
planet_in_sign/mercury/gemini.phrasing_guidance: Describe a naturally strong communicator and learner. Present the marriage lines from Saravali only as a possible need for mental rapport, never as a prediction of divorce or remarriage.

planet_in_sign/mercury/cancer.summary: Mercury in Cancer (Karka), the Moon's water sign, which Mercury treats as an enemy's sign, gives an imaginative, emotional and changeable intellect: talented with words and music but restless, talkative and prone to friction with relatives.
common_outcomes: Learned and poetic, with a feeling-led way of thinking
Restless and changeable; may take up many occupations
Inclination to live or work away from the birthplace
Fond of music; talkative
rare_outcomes: Saravali says popularity may come through the reputation of ancestors
Brihat Jataka 18.9: income from water or water-related trades, together with enmity from one's own people
Saravali mentions loss of wealth through romantic involvements

by_area.personality: Saravali 26.7-8: fickle-minded, prattling, fond of arguments.
by_area.career: Saravali 26.7-8: interested in many jobs, a good poet. Brihat Jataka 18.9: earns through water.
by_area.finance: Brihat Jataka links gains to water; Saravali warns of money lost through enmity with women.
by_area.relationships: Saravali 26.7-8: fond of the company of women, but loses wealth through enmity with them.
by_area.family: Both main texts mention hostility with relatives (Brihat Jataka 18.9 Sastri: hated by his relations), even as the ancestors' fame brings popularity (Saravali).

strengtheners: Saravali 26.43-48: Jupiter's aspect makes the native a great scholar, dear to all and to the ruler, who goes beyond the usual bounds of learning; Venus' aspect gives beauty, skill in singing and instruments, and fortune
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a vargottama planet gives results like a planet in its own sign
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saravali 26.43-48: Moon's aspect brings loss of wealth or vigour and misery through women; Mars' aspect brings little learning, lying and invention of falsehoods; Saturn's aspect brings vanity, imprisonment and hostility to siblings and elders
Enemy's sign: Braha and BPHS both list the Moon as Mercury's enemy; Phaladeepika 3.19: a planet in an enemy's house is 'distressed'

James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (Sun and 'Combustion' sections): a planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and its significations and the houses it rules are spoiled; Raman (Budha-Aditya Yoga) suggests Mercury may partly escape this

source_views.source: Saravali 26.7-8 (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Learned but restless, prefers living abroad, enjoys music and pleasure, talkative and inconstant, quarrels with relatives, loses wealth through women, takes up many jobs, a good poet whose popularity rests on ancestral fame.

source_views.source: Saravali 26.43-48, aspects on Mercury in Cancer (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Sun: craftsman's trades. Moon: loses wealth and vigour through women. Mars: untruthful, weak in learning. Jupiter: great scholar, favoured by the ruler. Venus: handsome, musical, fortunate. Saturn: vain, hostile to kin, confinement.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.9 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Mercury in the Moon's sign: gains wealth from water, becomes hostile to his own people.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 3.19
source_views.view: A planet in an enemy's house is 'exceedingly distressed'.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.9 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed., p. 347)
source_views.view: Mercury in Cancer: earns wealth through water, hated by his relations.

source_views.view: The Moon is an enemy to Mercury.

planet_in_sign/mercury/cancer.disagreements: The texts agree on family friction. Saravali stresses poetic talent and restlessness; Brihat Jataka stresses water-related income. Mercury regards the Moon as an enemy (BPHS ch. 3; Braha), though the Moon regards Mercury as a friend; five-fold (panchadha) friendship can change the relationship in an individual chart.
planet_in_sign/mercury/cancer.phrasing_guidance: Present as an imaginative, emotionally attuned mind that benefits from structure and from not taking family disagreements to heart. Avoid predicting estrangement or financial loss; mention them only as areas to handle with care.

planet_in_sign/mercury/leo.summary: Mercury in Leo (Simha), the Sun's fire sign and a friend's sign for Mercury, gives a proud, authoritative way of speaking and thinking, yet both Saravali and Brihat Jataka describe it unfavourably, warning of weak memory or judgement, restlessness and strained family ties.
common_outcomes: Speech and thinking take on a confident, commanding tone
Can gain some name or wealth (Saravali)
Tension with siblings or kin while being kind to outsiders
Restless or wandering tendencies
rare_outcomes: Saravali mentions working in service of others and difficulty with children
Brihat Jataka 18.10 adds loss of comfort and self-inflicted embarrassment

by_area.personality: Saravali 26.9-10: weak memory, not truthful, independent. Brihat Jataka 18.10 (Sastri): ignorant and always wandering.
by_area.career: Saravali 26.9-10: may work as a servant (in service of others).
by_area.finance: Saravali grants wealth and fame; Brihat Jataka 18.10 calls the native penniless (Sastri).
by_area.health: Saravali mentions a weak constitution; do not convert this into a health prediction.
by_area.relationships: Saravali: unfortunate in respect of the spouse; Brihat Jataka 18.10: hated (Sastri) or disliked (Neely) by women. Best read as a need to listen more in relationships.
by_area.family: Saravali 26.9-10: conflict with brothers, few or no children, against one's own people but kind to others. Brihat Jataka 18.10 (Sastri): insulted by his own people.

strengtheners: Saravali 26.49-54: Moon's aspect gives beauty, skill, wealth and talent in poetry, music and dance; Jupiter's aspect gives beauty, learning, eloquence, fame and conveyances; Venus' aspect gives beauty, courage, conveyances and a minister's post
Mercury with the Sun forms Budha-Aditya Yoga (intelligence, skill, reputation), but Raman warns it should not be assumed regardless of their distance (Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 24)
Sastri's note to Brihat Jataka 18.10: in Leo Mercury 'improves a little', being in a friend's house
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a vargottama planet gives results like a planet in its own sign
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saravali 26.49-54: Sun's aspect gives wealth and virtue but jealousy, cruelty and fickleness; Mars' aspect gives baseness, misery, injury and lack of skill; Saturn's aspect gives a lacklustre appearance and misery

James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (Sun and 'Combustion' sections): a planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and its significations and the houses it rules are spoiled; Raman (Budha-Aditya Yoga) suggests Mercury may partly escape this

source_views.view: Lacks wisdom and memory though may be wealthy and famous; untruthful, physically weak, quarrels with brothers, unlucky in marriage, few or no children, works for others, hostile to kin but kind to outsiders.

source_views.source: Saravali 26.49-54, aspects on Mercury in Leo (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Sun: jealous, harsh, yet rich. Moon: beautiful, skilled, wealthy, artistic. Mars: base, injured. Jupiter: eloquent, famous. Venus: very beautiful, a minister. Saturn: miserable.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.10 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Mercury in Leo: disliked by women, loses wealth, comfort and children, wanders, lacks learning, driven by desire, brings humiliation on himself.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.10 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed., p. 347)
source_views.view: Mercury in Leo: hated by women, penniless, without happiness or sons, always wandering, ignorant, fond of young women, insulted by his own people. Sastri's note: in Leo Mercury improves a little, being a friendly house.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 24 Budha-Aditya Yoga (p. 54)

planet_in_sign/mercury/leo.disagreements: Dignity rules (friend's sign, per BPHS and Braha) and the classical sign verses (largely adverse) point in different directions; Sastri's note softens the verse only slightly. Saravali allows wealth and fame alongside the negatives; Brihat Jataka is uniformly negative in both translations.
planet_in_sign/mercury/leo.phrasing_guidance: Describe a confident, authoritative communicator who benefits from humility and careful listening. Do not tell the user they lack intelligence, will be childless or unlucky in marriage; these classical statements should be treated as low-weight unless the rest of the chart confirms them.

planet_in_sign/mercury/virgo.summary: Mercury in Virgo (Kanya) is in its exaltation, moolatrikona and own sign at once: the strongest possible sign for Mercury, giving a precise, discerning, articulate and skilful mind with gifts for writing, analysis and the arts.
common_outcomes: Sharp, analytical and well-organised mind
Eloquent and skilled in writing, poetry, crafts or technical arts
Generous, wise and patient; reasons well
Respected by learned or good people
rare_outcomes: Saravali notes the native may be the eldest child and is attractive to others but of modest vigour
Forms Bhadra Mahapurusha Yoga in a kendra from the lagna
Saravali also calls the native argumentative despite being modest

by_area.personality: Saravali 26.11-12: virtuous, eloquent, sweet, modest and argumentative. Brihat Jataka 18.10 (Sastri): liberal, forgiving, inventive and fearless.
by_area.career: Saravali 26.11-12: skilled in writing, poetry and fine or mechanical arts; disposed to serve others.
by_area.finance: Saravali calls the native charitable; Brihat Jataka 18.10 (Sastri): lives in comfort.
by_area.relationships: Saravali 26.11-12: liked by women.
by_area.family: Saravali: often the eldest child.
by_area.spirituality: Saravali: honoured by the virtuous.

strengtheners: Exaltation: deepest at 15 degrees Virgo (BPHS 3.49-50); moolatrikona after the exaltation portion, own sign for the rest (BPHS 3.53). Braha: Mercury functions best in the first half of Virgo
Phaladeepika 3.18: an exalted planet is 'blazing', in moolatrikona 'happy'
Bhadra Yoga if in a kendra from the lagna (Phaladeepika 6.1-2; Raman no. 23)

Saravali 26.37-42 (Gemini/Virgo group): Sun's aspect gives truthfulness and royal favour; Jupiter's aspect a minister's post and wealth; Saturn's aspect success and wealth; Moon's aspect study of the Sastras and success in all undertakings
Foss: Virgo is where Mercury is happiest (own, moolatrikona and exaltation together)
weakeners_or_cancellations: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (Sun and 'Combustion' sections): a planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and its significations and the houses it rules are spoiled; Raman (Budha-Aditya Yoga) suggests Mercury may partly escape this

planet_in_sign/mercury/virgo.lagna_or_context_notes: Bhadra Yoga arises when Virgo is a kendra from the lagna, i.e. for Virgo, Gemini, Sagittarius and Pisces lagnas (Phaladeepika 6.1-2). Raman (no. 23) adds that Mercury must be very powerful for the yoga to deliver.

planet_in_sign/mercury/virgo.disagreements: Sources agree this is Mercury's best sign. BPHS 3.53 gives only the length of the moolatrikona portion (5 degrees after the exaltation portion), so the exact boundary at 15 or 16 degrees depends on interpretation; Braha simply says the first half of Virgo is best. Saravali's 'less virile' and 'argumentative' remarks are not found in Brihat Jataka.
planet_in_sign/mercury/virgo.phrasing_guidance: Describe a strong, precise and capable mind. Avoid overpromising: an exalted Mercury still depends on its house, combustion and the rest of the chart. Do not repeat Saravali's remark on virility.

planet_in_sign/mercury/libra.summary: Mercury in Libra (Tula), the air sign of its friend Venus, gives a diplomatic, artistic and trade-minded intellect: fond of discussion and the arts, generous in spending and respectful of teachers, though Saravali also warns of fickleness and calculated charm.
common_outcomes: Knowledgeable in arts and enjoys debate
Runs varied business interests; spends freely
Respectful toward teachers, guests and the sacred
Amiable and sociable
rare_outcomes: Saravali says the native may appear to serve others for advantage, and swings between short temper and calm
Brihat Jataka 18.8 (Mercury in a Venus sign) describes a teacher devoted to the guru

by_area.personality: Saravali 26.13-14: amiable, fond of arguments, fickle, sometimes short-tempered and sometimes peaceful.
by_area.career: Saravali 26.13-14: business in various directions, knowledge of arts, an able speaker. Brihat Jataka 18.8: a teacher.
by_area.finance: Saravali notes lavish spending; Brihat Jataka 18.8 (Sastri): keen on amassing a large property.
by_area.family: Brihat Jataka 18.8 (Sastri): wife and children; respects parents and elders.
by_area.spirituality: Saravali 26.13-14: honours the wise, guests, gods and preceptors; devoted to the gods.

planet_in_sign/mercury/libra.phrasing_guidance: Present as a diplomatic, artistic and commercially minded communicator. Mention consistency and sincerity as growth areas rather than calling the person deceitful.

planet_in_sign/mercury/scorpio.summary: Mercury in Scorpio (Vrischika), Mars' fixed water sign and neutral for Mercury, is rated among its worst placements by the classical texts, which warn of grief, harsh conduct, bad company and debt.

Periods of trouble or worry tied to speech and dealings
Tendency toward debts or financial strain if unchecked
Can be guarded or stingy

Brihat Jataka 18.8 (Mercury in a Mars sign): gambling, drink, scepticism, fraud

planet_in_sign/mercury/sagittarius.summary: Mercury in Sagittarius (Dhanu), Jupiter's fire sign and neutral for Mercury, gives a learned, eloquent and principled intellect; classical texts rate it well, describing scholarship, fame, generosity and advisory roles.

Skilful, persuasive speaker; respected by authorities
Generous and charitable
Good at writing and the arts
rare_outcomes: Saravali mentions ministerial roles or service as family priest
Saravali adds bravery and a meditative disposition

by_area.spirituality: Strong: performs sacrifices, meditates, learned in sacred texts (Saravali 26.17-18).

planet_in_sign/mercury/capricorn.summary: Mercury in Capricorn (Makara), Saturn's earth sign and neutral for Mercury, gives a practical, cautious and work-focused intellect; classical texts are largely unfavourable, describing work for others, hardship, debt and timidity.

Brihat Jataka 18.11 (Mercury in a Saturn sign) adds forced labour or obligations

source_views.view: A planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and spoiled; a vargottama planet gives own-sign results, while a fallen planet that is vargottama is only worse off and a planet exalted in the birth chart but fallen in the navamsa gives very mixed results; a fallen planet is badly weakened unless well aspected; planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 24 Budha-Aditya Yoga (p. 54)
source_views.view: Mercury with the Sun: highly intelligent, skilful, good reputation, comforts. Planets with the Sun usually become combust and lose power, but Mercury may be an exception; the yoga should not be assumed regardless of the distance between them.

planet_in_sign/mercury/aquarius.disagreements: Saravali and Brihat Jataka (both translations) are adverse. The 'innovative, humanitarian' reading common online draws on Western sign symbolism and has no classical or cited modern source here.
planet_in_sign/mercury/aquarius.phrasing_guidance: Present as an independent, unconventional thinker. Avoid predicting marital conflict or poverty; mention only that warmth in communication and financial planning are useful focus areas.

planet_in_sign/mercury/pisces.summary: Mercury in Pisces (Meena) is debilitated, deepest at 15 degrees: logical, detailed thinking is weakened and intuition, imagination and feeling take over. Classical texts give a mixed picture (good conduct and a faithful spouse, but limited formal learning and money), and the debility can be cancelled by neecha bhanga.
common_outcomes: Intuitive, imaginative and empathic thinking; less comfortable with detail and contracts
Serves others or works in support roles
Modest artistic or craft skill
May live or work away from home
rare_outcomes: Saravali says the native is skilled at sewing or fine handwork
Saravali has a paradoxical line: skilled at taking others' wealth yet remaining poor
With neecha bhanga, creative and spiritual gifts as a communicator (astromedha.in)

by_area.personality: Saravali 26.23-24: fond of good conduct and purity; virtuous and fortunate.
by_area.career: Saravali 26.23-24: skilled in stitching or fine handwork. Brihat Jataka 18.11: serves others (Neely) or wins over servants and is skilled in humble handicrafts (Sastri).
by_area.finance: Saravali mentions poverty; written agreements and careful reading of terms help.
by_area.relationships: Saravali 26.23-24: a chaste spouse.
by_area.family: Saravali mentions few or no children; treat as low weight.
by_area.spirituality: Saravali: fond of purity yet without formal religion. Foss: the debilitation is a challenge to accept Jupiter's wisdom without trying to reinvent it; letting go of Mercury's agenda can make it very auspicious.

strengtheners: Neecha bhanga (Phaladeepika 7.26-30): Jupiter (lord of Pisces) or Mercury's exaltation-sign lord (Mercury itself, lord of Virgo) in a kendra from the lagna or Moon; or the two lords in mutual kendras; or Mercury aspected by Jupiter (7.28)
Raman (no. 250) reads the cancelling planet as the one exalted in Pisces, i.e. Venus in a kendra from the lagna or Moon
astromedha.in: cancellation if Jupiter or Mercury is in a kendra

Saravali 26.55-60 (Sagittarius/Pisces group): Jupiter's aspect gives wealth, intelligence, nobility and a minister's or treasurer's role; Moon's aspect makes a wealthy, happy writer; Venus' aspect gives a teacher, wealth and courage
weakeners_or_cancellations: Phaladeepika 3.19: a debilitated planet is 'greatly afraid'; Braha: Pisces is Mercury's worst sign
Closest to 15 degrees Pisces the debility is deepest (BPHS 3.50)
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a debilitated planet that is also vargottama is only worse off

James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (Sun and 'Combustion' sections): a planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and its significations and the houses it rules are spoiled; Raman (Budha-Aditya Yoga) suggests Mercury may partly escape this
Saturn's aspect (Saravali 26.55-60): life in remote places and lack of success
planet_in_sign/mercury/pisces.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman (Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 250) reckons neecha bhanga from both the lagna and the Moon, so check kendras from both before giving a weak reading.

source_views.source: Saravali 26.23-24 (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Fond of good conduct and purity, lives abroad, few children and limited money, but a chaste spouse; virtuous and fortunate yet irreligious; skilled in sewing; lacks formal learning; skilled at taking others' wealth while staying poor.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.11 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Mercury in Pisces: serves others, modest artistic skill.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 3.49-50
source_views.view: Debilitation is the seventh sign from exaltation at the same degree: 15 degrees Pisces for Mercury.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 7.26-30
source_views.view: Neecha bhanga raja yoga conditions: the debilitation-sign lord or exaltation-sign lord in a kendra from the lagna or Moon; the two in mutual kendras; or the debilitated planet aspected by its sign lord.

source_views.source: astromedha.in, Mercury in Pisces (practitioner, no classical citation)
source_views.view: Empathic, creative and spiritual communicators when supported; indecision and vague agreements as challenges; cancellation if Jupiter or Mercury is in a kendra.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.11 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed., p. 349)
source_views.view: Mercury in Pisces: wins over his servants and is skilled in the handicrafts of low-caste people.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 250 Neechabhanga Raja Yoga (pp. 242-244)
source_views.view: The lord of the debilitation sign, or the planet exalted there, in a kendra from the lagna or Moon cancels debility. Raman follows B. Suryanarain Rao in reading 'thaduchchanatha' as the planet exalted in that sign, and notes the reading is disputed.

source_views.source: Andrew Foss, The Yoga of the Planets: Mercury, Budha, name 10 'Speaking truth'
source_views.view: Mercury, unless retrograde, is debilitated in Pisces. The debilitation is the challenge to accept Jupiter's wisdom without trying to reinvent it; any planet in Pisces can gently let go of its agenda, which can make it very auspicious.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer ('Budha-Mercury' section)
source_views.view: Mercury functions worst in Pisces, its fallen sign.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (general rules: combustion, navamsa, house placements, dignities)
source_views.view: A planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and spoiled; a vargottama planet gives own-sign results, while a fallen planet that is vargottama is only worse off and a planet exalted in the birth chart but fallen in the navamsa gives very mixed results; a fallen planet is badly weakened unless well aspected; planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 24 Budha-Aditya Yoga (p. 54)
source_views.view: Mercury with the Sun: highly intelligent, skilful, good reputation, comforts. Planets with the Sun usually become combust and lose power, but Mercury may be an exception; the yoga should not be assumed regardless of the distance between them.

planet_in_sign/mercury/pisces.disagreements: Saravali's verse mixes favourable (virtuous, fortunate, faithful spouse) and unfavourable lines. On Brihat Jataka 18.11 the translations differ: Neely has the native serving others, Sastri has him winning over his servants. Practitioners disagree on whether Jupiter's aspect alone cancels the debility or whether a kendra placement is needed; Phaladeepika 7.28 supports the aspect route, and Raman notes the meaning of 'thaduchchanatha' is disputed. Foss alone exempts a retrograde Mercury from debilitation. In BPHS Mercury treats Jupiter as neutral (Braha agrees); it is Jupiter that treats Mercury as an enemy.
planet_in_sign/mercury/pisces.phrasing_guidance: Never call the person unintelligent. Describe a mind that thinks in images and feelings, and suggest structure, checklists and careful contracts as practical supports. Always check neecha bhanga before giving any 'weak Mercury' reading, and avoid stating that someone will be poor or childless.

planet_in_sign/moon/aries.summary: The Moon in Aries (Mars's sign, neutral for the Moon) gives a quick, restless, courageous and proud mind. Texts describe a lively, impulsive person, popular with others, whose finances can be unsteady.
common_outcomes: Quick-thinking, decisive, impatient
Restless, fond of travel and movement
Brave and self-respecting; values honour over money
Changeable moods
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 17.1: eldest among siblings; marks or scars on the head; fear of water
Saravali 23.1: no siblings (contrasting with BJ's 'eldest'); many sons; easily won over by women
Phaladeepika 9.1 (Aries rising/Moon): eats little, always on the move, tends to bend the truth

by_area.personality: Quick to understand, restless and heroic (Brihat Jataka 17.1); valorous, self-respecting and fickle (Saravali 23.1); impulsive, irritable, enterprising, haughty and restless (Raman HPA ch. XXII).
by_area.career: Raman HPA ch. XXII: enterprising and dexterous but subordinate in position.
by_area.finance: Brihat Jataka 17.1: unstable wealth; Saravali 23.1: lasting wealth.
by_area.health: Texts mention weak knees or legs and head wounds (Brihat Jataka 17.1; Saravali 23.1) as traditional bodily markers; do not use as predictions.
by_area.relationships: Won over by women (Saravali 23.1); popular and fond of women (Raman).
by_area.family: Brihat Jataka 17.1 makes the native the eldest sibling while Saravali 23.1 says without co-born; Saravali adds more sons.

strengtheners: Bright (waxing, well-lit) Moon, which Braha (pp. 19-20) treats as benefic and stronger
Jupiter's aspect (Saravali 23.2-7: servants and high status for Moon in Aries)
Venus's aspect (Saravali 23.2-7: luck and sons)
Mercury's aspect (Saravali 23.2-7: teaching and poetic fame)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saturn's aspect (Saravali 23.2-7: poverty, dishonesty)
Mars's aspect (Saravali 23.2-7: eye/teeth trouble and wounds)
Waning or dim Moon, which Braha (pp. 19-20) treats as malefic and weaker
Placement in a dusthana (6th, 8th, 12th); Braha (pp. 51-52) says a planet there is spoiled, the 6th being the mildest
planet_in_sign/moon/aries.lagna_or_context_notes: Phaladeepika 9.13 and Brihat Jataka 18.20 say the results given for a rising sign also apply when the Moon occupies that sign, and Braha (p. 20) reads the whole chart from the Moon as a second ascendant (Chandra lagna).

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 17.1 (tr. M. D. Neely, 2007)
source_views.view: Round reddish eyes, eats pungent food sparingly, quick to understand, restless wanderer, lustful, weak knees, fragile nails, head scars, unstable wealth, heroic, popular with women, good at service, proud, eldest sibling, timid around water.

source_views.source: Saravali 23.1, Moon in Aries (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Golden complexion, lasting wealth, no siblings, brave, proud, lustful, weak legs, thin hair, fickle, values honour over wealth, many sons, friendly, fears deep water, head wounds.

source_views.source: Saravali 23.2-7, aspects on the Moon in Aries (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Sun: irritability with royal honour; Mars: eye/teeth trouble and wounds; Mercury: teaching, poetic fame; Jupiter: servants and high status; Venus: luck and sons; Saturn: poverty and dishonesty.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 9.1 and 9.13 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Aries: round eyes, weak knees, fierce, fears water, eats little, always moving, ticklish, prone to lying; 9.13 says the same applies when the Moon is in the sign.

source_views.source: Saravali 23.88, when the results mature (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: The Moon-sign effects come to pass fully only when the Moon, the Moon's sign and that sign's lord are strong; they vary with the dignity of the dispositor and of aspecting planets.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 3.55, naisargika maitri (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1 pp. 40-41)
source_views.view: Same moolatrikona rule; Santhanam's table and his note on the Chaukhamba reading give the Moon's friends as Sun and Mercury, with Mars, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn neutral and no enemies.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 2.21-22 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: The Moon's friends are the Sun and Mercury; all the rest are neutral to it.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXII 'Planets in Different Rasis or Signs' (Moon, pp. 205-209)
source_views.view: Round eyes, impulsive, fond of travel, irritable, quick to decide and act, haughty, enterprising, subordinate in position, self-respecting, ambitious, popular, restless, versatile.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), '1st House' (pp. 79-90) and 'Yogas', Miscellaneous Notes no. 1
source_views.view: The scriptures call the Moon in Aries a fine or beneficial placement; Braha finds this odd since the Moon falls in Scorpio, the other Mars sign, and suggests the reason is Aries' closeness to the exaltation point at 3 degrees Taurus.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), 'The Moon' pp. 19-21, 'House Rulerships' pp. 50-52 and 'Shad Bala' pp. 59-61
source_views.view: A waxing, bright Moon is benefic and stronger and a waning, dim one malefic; the chart is also read from the Moon (Chandra lagna); the Moon has directional strength in the 4th; planets in kendras are powerful and in dusthanas spoiled.

planet_in_sign/moon/aries.disagreements: Brihat Jataka says unstable wealth and eldest sibling; Saravali says lasting wealth and no siblings. Treat both sibling and wealth claims as low-confidence. Braha notes that the scriptures call Aries a fine place for the Moon, possibly because it is close to the exaltation point at 3 degrees Taurus.
planet_in_sign/moon/aries.phrasing_guidance: Describe an energetic, brave, quick-reacting mind that benefits from patience. Avoid bodily-mark or water-fear claims unless asked about classical texts.

planet_in_sign/moon/taurus.summary: The Moon is exalted in Taurus (deepest exaltation at 3°), and per BPHS the rest of Taurus (about 4-30°) is its moolatrikona. It gives a calm, patient, generous and attractive temperament with growing happiness in middle and later life.
common_outcomes: Steady, patient, forbearing mind
Attractive appearance and graceful manner
Generous and charitable; loyal friend
Happiness and stability increase in middle and later life
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 17.2 and Saravali 23.8: more daughters
Brihat Jataka 17.2: some separation from early relatives or family wealth
Phaladeepika 9.2: work connected with agriculture or cattle

by_area.personality: Self-denying, enduring and authoritative (Brihat Jataka 17.2); large-hearted, charitable, discerning and forbearing (Saravali 23.8); liberal, intelligent, of sound judgment but a wavering mind (Raman HPA ch. XXII).
by_area.career: Agriculture and cattle (Phaladeepika 9.2); Raman: ability to command, influential.
by_area.finance: Raman HPA ch. XXII: rich and lucky; Phaladeepika 9.14 (any exalted planet): wealth and treasures.
by_area.health: Brihat Jataka 17.2 mentions strong digestion and a kapha constitution; present only as a temperament note.
by_area.relationships: Raman HPA ch. XXII: popular, fond of the opposite sex, influenced by women, love intrigues.
by_area.family: Classical texts mention more daughters (Brihat Jataka 17.2; Saravali 23.8); confirm from the 5th house before saying so.
by_area.spirituality: Brihat Jataka 17.2 calls the native self-denying.

strengtheners: Within 0-3° (exaltation) per BPHS 3.49-51
Bright (waxing, well-lit) Moon, which Braha (pp. 19-20) treats as benefic and stronger
Jupiter's aspect (Saravali 23.9-14: fame and virtue)
Venus's aspect (Saravali 23.9-14: comforts and luxuries)
Mercury's aspect (Saravali 23.9-14: learning)
Kendra placement (Braha p. 50), especially the 4th, where the Moon has directional strength (Braha p. 60)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Waning or dim Moon, which Braha (pp. 19-20) treats as malefic and weaker
Saturn's aspect (Saravali 23.9-14: poverty, though children)
Mars's aspect (Saravali 23.9-14: strong desires, strain in marriage)
Placement in a dusthana (6th, 8th, 12th); Braha (pp. 51-52) says a planet there is spoiled, the 6th being the mildest
planet_in_sign/moon/taurus.lagna_or_context_notes: Phaladeepika 9.13 and Brihat Jataka 18.20 say the results given for a rising sign also apply when the Moon occupies that sign, and Braha (p. 20) reads the whole chart from the Moon as a second ascendant (Chandra lagna). Braha ('Planets in the Houses', pp. 79 ff.) reads the exalted Moon house by house: Taurus lagna (1st) attractive, respected, happy marriage; Aquarius lagna (4th) fine homes and comforts, a happy bond with the mother; Capricorn lagna (5th) intelligence and faith; Scorpio lagna (7th) a blissful marriage; Leo lagna (10th) public fame; Cancer lagna (11th) large gains and goals realised. He says results are smaller but still good if the Moon is waning.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 3.49-51
source_views.view: Moon exalted in Taurus at 3°; the first 3° are exaltation and the remainder of Taurus is moolatrikona.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 17.2 (tr. M. D. Neely, 2007)
source_views.view: Attractive, lively gait, broad face and thighs, marks on back/face/sides, self-denying, enduring, authoritative, strong digestion, kapha nature, daughters, liked by women, loyal friend, happy in middle and later life.

source_views.source: Saravali 23.8, Moon in Taurus (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Big-hearted, charitable, famous, bright, more daughters, discerning, happy in middle and later life, graceful, forbearing.

source_views.source: Saravali 23.9-14, aspects on the Moon in Taurus (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Sun: farming or lending; Mars: strong desire, strain in marriage; Mercury: learning; Jupiter: fame and virtue; Venus: comforts; Saturn: poverty but children.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 9.2, 9.13, 9.14 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Taurus: big face, agriculture, happy in middle/later life, generous, forgiving, enduring, owns cattle; exalted planet gives fame, wealth and virtues.

source_views.source: Saravali 23.88, when the results mature (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: The Moon-sign effects come to pass fully only when the Moon, the Moon's sign and that sign's lord are strong; they vary with the dignity of the dispositor and of aspecting planets.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXII 'Planets in Different Rasis or Signs' (Moon, pp. 205-209)
source_views.view: Liberal, powerful, happy, able to command, intelligent, handsome, influential, happy in middle and later life, patient, respected, sound judgment but a wavering mind, lucky, popular.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, ch. 'The Signs: How Planets Transmit Influences of the Stars', pp. 125-127
source_views.view: Moon's exaltation point is 3 degrees Taurus; its moolatrikona is given as 4-20 degrees Taurus.

source_views.source: Andrew Foss, The Yoga of the Planets: Chandra, the Moon, name 20
source_views.view: The Moon is exalted in Taurus, where it is most fertile; the exaltation falls in Krittika, followed by Rohini, the Moon's favourite nakshatra.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), 'Planetary Powers' p. 47 and 'Planets in the Houses' pp. 79 ff.
source_views.view: A planet past its deepest exaltation degree is technically no longer exalted; gives house-by-house results for the Moon in Taurus or Cancer.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), 'The Moon' pp. 19-21, 'House Rulerships' pp. 50-52 and 'Shad Bala' pp. 59-61
source_views.view: A waxing, bright Moon is benefic and stronger and a waning, dim one malefic; the chart is also read from the Moon (Chandra lagna); the Moon has directional strength in the 4th; planets in kendras are powerful and in dusthanas spoiled.

planet_in_sign/moon/taurus.disagreements: Moolatrikona range: BPHS 3.51-54 makes all of Taurus after the first 3 degrees moolatrikona, while Frawley (p. 127) gives 4-20 degrees. Braha (p. 47) says a planet past its deepest exaltation degree is technically no longer exalted, while BPHS treats the whole sign as exaltation. The core meaning is consistent across texts.
planet_in_sign/moon/taurus.phrasing_guidance: Present as emotional steadiness and contentment that deepens with age. Do not predict the gender of children.

planet_in_sign/moon/gemini.summary: The Moon in Gemini is in Mercury's sign, a friend of the Moon. It gives a quick, witty, communicative and artistic mind, fond of music, games and social play.
common_outcomes: Sharp, clever, curious mind
Gentle, agreeable speech; eloquent
Love of music, dance, poetry and games
Strong social and romantic interests
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 17.3: works as a messenger or go-between
Saravali 23.16: 'two mothers' (e.g. a foster or step-mother figure)
Phaladeepika 9.3: able to read others' thoughts; likes to stay at home

by_area.personality: Sharp-minded and gentle-spoken (Brihat Jataka 17.3); intelligent, jocular and eloquent (Saravali 23.16); well read, witty, persuasive and subtle (Raman HPA ch. XXII).
by_area.career: Messenger or go-between (Brihat Jataka 17.3); Raman: powerful speaker, learned in scriptures, fond of music.
by_area.relationships: Skilled in the arts of love (Brihat Jataka 17.3; Saravali 23.16); won over by women (Saravali 23.16); fond of women (Raman).
by_area.family: Saravali 23.16: 'two mothers', a rare, text-specific note.
by_area.spirituality: Learned in scriptures (Raman HPA ch. XXII).

strengtheners: Strong sign lord (Mercury): Saravali 23.88 says the Moon-sign results come to pass fully only when the Moon, its sign and that sign's lord are strong
Mars's aspect (Saravali 23.17-22: valour and wealth)
Jupiter's aspect (Saravali 23.17-22: teaching, eloquence)
Venus's aspect (Saravali 23.17-22: luxury)
Bright (waxing, well-lit) Moon, which Braha (pp. 19-20) treats as benefic and stronger
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saturn's aspect (Saravali 23.17-22: isolation and loss)
Sun's aspect (Saravali 23.17-22: learning with hardship)
Waning or dim Moon, which Braha (pp. 19-20) treats as malefic and weaker

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 17.3 (tr. M. D. Neely, 2007)
source_views.view: Drawn to romance and skilled in intimacy, coppery eyes, learned, messenger/go-between, curly hair, sharp mind, knows games and gestures, graceful, gentle speech, hearty appetite, loves music and dance, prominent nose.

source_views.source: Saravali 23.16, Moon in Gemini (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Prominent nose, dark eyes, skilled in love arts and poetry, intelligent, radiant, jovial, eloquent, influenced by partners, tall, two mothers.

source_views.source: Saravali 23.17-22, aspects on the Moon in Gemini (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Sun: learning with hardship; Mars: valour and wealth; Mercury: skill in earning; Jupiter: teaching, eloquence; Venus: luxury; Saturn: isolation and loss.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 9.3, 9.13 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Gemini: dark eyes, curly hair, playful with partners, reads others' thoughts, raised nose, loves music and dance, stays home.

source_views.source: Saravali 23.88, when the results mature (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: The Moon-sign effects come to pass fully only when the Moon, the Moon's sign and that sign's lord are strong; they vary with the dignity of the dispositor and of aspecting planets.

source_views.view: The Moon's friends are the Sun and Mercury; all the rest are neutral to it.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXII 'Planets in Different Rasis or Signs' (Moon, pp. 205-209)
source_views.view: Well read, creative, learned in scriptures, persuasive, a powerful speaker, witty, fond of music, a thought reader, subtle.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), 'The Moon' pp. 19-21, 'House Rulerships' pp. 50-52 and 'Shad Bala' pp. 59-61
source_views.view: A waxing, bright Moon is benefic and stronger and a waning, dim one malefic; the chart is also read from the Moon (Chandra lagna); the Moon has directional strength in the 4th; planets in kendras are powerful and in dusthanas spoiled.

planet_in_sign/moon/gemini.disagreements: Sources agree closely on intellect, music and romance.
planet_in_sign/moon/gemini.phrasing_guidance: Highlight wit, communication and artistic sense. Keep sexual or romantic notes general and respectful.

planet_in_sign/moon/cancer.summary: Cancer is the Moon's own sign. It gives a caring, home-loving, intuitive and loyal nature, attached to friends and water, but Brihat Jataka notes the waxing-waning pattern of the Moon shows as ups and downs in wealth and mood.
common_outcomes: Caring, protective, emotionally deep
Many friends and attachment to home
Love of water, gardens and flowers
Fluctuating moods and finances
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 17.4 and Saravali 23.23: skill in astrology
Saravali 23.23: minister or trusted adviser; builds houses and wells; lives abroad
Phaladeepika 9.4: many houses, wealthy, few sons, walks fast

by_area.personality: Loyal to friends and influenced by the partner (Brihat Jataka 17.4); fortunate, valorous, grateful and truthful (Saravali 23.23); wise, kind, sensitive, meditative, prudent and frugal (Raman HPA ch. XXII).
by_area.career: Astrology (Brihat Jataka 17.4; Saravali 23.23); minister or adviser, builder of houses and wells (Saravali 23.23); Raman: scientist.
by_area.finance: Brihat Jataka 17.4: loss of wealth in waxing-waning cycles; Saravali 23.23 and Phaladeepika 9.4: wealthy, many houses; Raman: much immovable property.

planet_in_sign/moon/scorpio.summary: The Moon is debilitated in Scorpio (deepest fall at 3°), the sign of Mars. It gives intense, private, guarded emotions and resilience under pressure; classical texts are harsh, while modern practitioners stress depth, investigative skill and transformation, and note that cancellation is common.
common_outcomes: Intense, private emotions; slow to trust
Strong will and endurance under pressure
Industrious and skilled
Early-life challenges or separations

by_area.personality: Classical texts list harshness and concealed faults (Brihat Jataka 17.8; Saravali 23.51); Raman HPA ch. XXII: straightforward, frank and open-minded yet obstinate and impetuous. Frawley (p. 126): with the debility cancelled it can give a very deep understanding of the psyche. Read the harsh items as shadow tendencies, not verdicts.
by_area.career: Industrious and skilful (Saravali 23.51); Frawley (p. 126) says a cancelled Moon in Scorpio is common among spiritual teachers, occultists and psychologists.
by_area.finance: Saravali 23.51: losses through the wrath of authorities; Phaladeepika 9.8: honoured by rulers; Raman: wealthy.
by_area.health: Texts mention illness in early life (Brihat Jataka 17.8; Saravali 23.51); present only as a traditional note, never as a prediction.
by_area.relationships: Saravali 23.51 lists attraction to others' partners and Raman agitation and unhappiness; handle gently.

by_area.spirituality: Frawley (p. 126): common in spiritual teachers and occultists when the debility is cancelled.

planet_in_sign/moon/scorpio.lagna_or_context_notes: Phaladeepika 9.13 and Brihat Jataka 18.20 say the results given for a rising sign also apply when the Moon occupies that sign, and Braha (p. 20) reads the whole chart from the Moon as a second ascendant (Chandra lagna). Braha ('Planets in the Houses', pp. 79 ff.) reads the fallen Moon harshly house by house: Scorpio lagna (1st) unsteady mind and weak health; Leo lagna (4th) strain around home and mother; Cancer lagna (5th) feelings overrule reason; Taurus lagna (7th) a rough married life; Aquarius lagna (10th) frequent career changes. Frawley (p. 126) instead says debility is much reduced in an angle from the lagna or Moon, especially the 10th, which covers the Scorpio, Leo, Taurus and Aquarius lagna cases.

source_views.view: Debility is cancelled by an angle from lagna or Moon, an exalted sign lord (Mars in Capricorn), or an exalted planet in a sign the fallen planet rules; a strong or own-sign Mars also reduces it. A cancelled Moon in Scorpio gives deep psychological insight and is common in spiritual teachers, occultists and psychologists.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), 'Planetary Powers' p. 47, 'Planets in the Houses' pp. 79 ff. and 'Yogas' no. 13 (neechabhanga)
source_views.view: The fallen Moon harms the overall tenor of the chart and is read harshly in every house; neechabhanga arises when an exalted planet joins it, its sign lord is exalted or in a kendra from lagna or Moon.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), 'The Moon' pp. 19-21, 'House Rulerships' pp. 50-52 and 'Shad Bala' pp. 59-61
source_views.view: A waxing, bright Moon is benefic and stronger and a waning, dim one malefic; the chart is also read from the Moon (Chandra lagna); the Moon has directional strength in the 4th; planets in kendras are powerful and in dusthanas spoiled.

planet_in_sign/moon/scorpio.disagreements: Classical verses are mostly unfavourable, yet Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika also mention a respected family or royal honour. Modern practitioners give a more psychological, growth-oriented reading. Commentators differ on whether the 'exaltation lord' for cancellation is Venus (lord of Taurus) or the planet exalted in Scorpio (none in the standard scheme). Braha reads the fallen Moon harshly in every house, while Frawley says cancellation is possible and a cancelled Moon in Scorpio gives psychological depth; Frawley's angle rule and Braha's angle readings conflict directly for the 1st, 4th, 7th and 10th houses. BPHS treats all of Scorpio as debilitation, while Braha (p. 47) says that past 3 degrees the Moon is technically no longer fallen.
planet_in_sign/moon/scorpio.phrasing_guidance: Never call the person cruel or secretive. Say the emotional nature is deep and protective, and that supports in the chart (cancellation, Jupiter) matter a lot. No health or parental-loss predictions.

Mars is listed as Rahu's enemy in several schemes.

planet_in_sign/saturn/aries.summary: Saturn in Aries is debilitated (deepest at 20 degrees) in the sign of an enemy, Mars. Patience and structure meet impulse and haste, so the classical picture is friction, restlessness and strained relationships, which later authors say can be transformed when the debilitation is cancelled.
common_outcomes: Hardship through hard labour and one's own habits; ill temper; friction with relatives and one's own people (Saravali 29.1-2; Raman HPA ch.22)
Restless, wandering and friendless tendencies (Brihat Jataka 18.17; Raman HPA ch.22)
Limited means and loss of position or dependence during the planet's dasa (Saravali 29.1-2; Phaladeepika 9.18 on debilitated planets)
Raman describes Saturn's dasa from Aries as a period of losses, disappointments and strained relations (HPA ch.24)
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 18.17 lists foolishness, wandering and deceit as Aries-specific traits
Saravali 29.29: a Jupiter aspect on Saturn in a Mars sign gives happiness, wealth and a minister's or chief's position; 29.25: a Sun aspect gives farming and livestock wealth
Frawley: Saturn in Aries with its debility cancelled can give strong leadership and strength of will

by_area.personality: Classical and modern sign lists describe temper, impatience and resentment (Saravali 29.1-2; Raman HPA ch.22); with cancelled debility, strength of will (Frawley p.126).
by_area.career: Hard labour and work under others (Saravali 29.1-2); Braha describes Saturn in Aries in the 10th house as an uphill professional struggle.
by_area.finance: Limited means in classical texts (Saravali 29.1-2); a Jupiter aspect reverses this (Saravali 29.29).
by_area.relationships: Friction with one's own people and relatives (Saravali 29.1-2; Raman HPA ch.24).
by_area.family: Saravali 29.1-2 says inimical to relatives; Raman's dasa note adds misunderstandings with relatives and friends (HPA ch.24).

strengtheners: Cancelled debility (neecha bhanga): Saturn in an angle from the lagna or Moon, Mars (lord of Aries) exalted or strong, or a planet exalted in Saturn's own signs (e.g. Mars in Capricorn); Frawley says at least two such factors are needed (Astrology of the Seers pp.126-127)
Jupiter aspecting Saturn in a Mars sign (Saravali 29.29)
Sun aspect gives agricultural and livestock wealth (Saravali 29.25)
Retrograde Saturn: Phaladeepika 9.20 says a retrograde planet gives results like exaltation; Frawley counts retrogression only a minor cancelling factor
weakeners_or_cancellations: Moon, Mars, Mercury or Venus aspect on Saturn in a Mars sign is described negatively (Saravali 29.26-28, 29.30)
Combustion weakens a planet in its dasa (Phaladeepika 9.19)
If Mars is exalted in Capricorn while Saturn is debilitated in Aries, each rules the other's sign and their effects tend to neutralise, the stronger one prevailing (Frawley p.127)
planet_in_sign/saturn/aries.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman (HPA ch.17) names Saturn the sole rajayoga planet for Taurus and Libra lagnas, so its sign results tend to be felt more favourably there; Raman (HPA ch.17) lists Saturn as ill-disposed for Aries, Leo and Pisces lagnas. Braha describes Saturn in Aries rising as a hard start in life and in the 10th house as professional struggle; these lagna-specific readings still depend on cancellation factors.

planet_in_sign/saturn/aries.disagreements: Classical texts (Saravali, Brihat Jataka) and Raman's sign list are uniformly harsh. Frawley and the neecha bhanga rules allow a cancelled debility to give leadership and will; Phaladeepika 9.20 treats a retrograde planet as exalted, while Frawley counts retrogression only a minor factor. Authors differ on how many cancelling factors are needed.
planet_in_sign/saturn/aries.phrasing_guidance: Present as a placement where patience is learned through friction, not as a curse. Always check for cancellation before describing it as weak. Avoid words like 'foolish' or 'deceitful' for the person; say 'may be tested around impatience or trust'. No health or longevity predictions.

Classical texts describe a serving or dependent position, modest means and attraction to pleasure, while Raman's modern list adds success, cleverness and self-restraint, and his dasa note speaks of good income.

by_area.personality: Raman: clever, persuasive, likes solitude, self-restrained but a worrier (HPA ch.22).
by_area.career: Service and many assignments (Saravali 29.3-4); agriculture and land gains in Saturn's dasa (Raman HPA ch.24).
by_area.finance: Saravali 29.3-4 says bereft of wealth; Raman's dasa note gives great income (HPA ch.24); benefic aspects improve wealth (Saravali 29.32, 29.36).
by_area.relationships: Classical texts flag attraction to women and several unions (Saravali 29.3-4; Brihat Jataka 18.18).

strengtheners: Venus is Saturn's friend (Braha; Bhavartha Ratnakara 15.7 lists Taurus as friendly for Saturn)
Moon, Jupiter or Venus aspecting Saturn (Saravali 29.32, 29.35, 29.36)
Phaladeepika 9.16: a planet in a friend's sign brings success through friends and support
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mercury aspect is described as weakening and base (Saravali 29.34)
Sun aspect costs wealth (Saravali 29.31)
planet_in_sign/saturn/taurus.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman (HPA ch.17) names Saturn the sole rajayoga planet for Taurus and Libra lagnas, so its sign results tend to be felt more favourably there. For Taurus lagna this places the yogakaraka in the lagna itself.

planet_in_sign/saturn/taurus.disagreements: Saravali calls the native poor; Raman's sign list calls him successful and powerful and his dasa note promises income. The friendly-sign rule (Phaladeepika, Bhavartha Ratnakara, Braha) supports the more favourable reading.
planet_in_sign/saturn/taurus.phrasing_guidance: Emphasise patient building of security and the need for discipline with comfort. Do not predict infidelity or multiple marriages; say relationships benefit from clear commitments.

planet_in_sign/saturn/gemini.summary: Saturn in Gemini is in the sign of its friend Mercury. Classical verses warn of debts, toil and restraint, while Raman's modern list adds an original, strategic and scientific mind, and his dasa note speaks of recognition and trade profits.
common_outcomes: Debts, confinement and toil (Saravali 29.5-6)
Wandering nature (Saravali 29.5-6; Raman HPA ch.22)
Original, subtle, strategic and logical mind with a taste for chemical and mechanical sciences (Raman HPA ch.22)
Raman's dasa note: recognition of services, trade profits and respect from rulers (HPA ch.24)
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 18.17: in Mercury's signs, lacking modesty, comfort or wealth and uneven in writing or painting

Saravali 29.40: Mercury aspect gives wealth and skill in dance, music and arts; 29.41: Jupiter aspect makes one trusted in the king's circle; 29.38: Moon aspect gives king-like standing and honour through women
Saravali 29.5-6 also mentions devotion through hymns and prayers

by_area.personality: Raman: original, subtle, ingenious, strategic, logical, sometimes narrow-minded (HPA ch.22).
by_area.career: Chemical and mechanical sciences (Raman HPA ch.22); recognition and trade profits in Saturn's dasa (Raman HPA ch.24).
by_area.finance: Saravali 29.5-6 warns of debts; Raman's dasa note gives profits in trade and speculation (HPA ch.24).
by_area.family: Raman lists few children (HPA ch.22).
by_area.spirituality: Saravali 29.5-6 mentions consecration through hymns and prayers.

strengtheners: Mercury is Saturn's friend (Braha; Bhavartha Ratnakara 15.7)
Mercury or Jupiter aspecting Saturn (Saravali 29.40-41)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mars aspect: heavy loads and dullness (Saravali 29.39)
Sun aspect: virtuous and enduring but without happiness or wealth (Saravali 29.37)
planet_in_sign/saturn/gemini.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman (HPA ch.17) says that for Gemini lagna Venus joined with Saturn in good signs gives an excellent career; Raman (HPA ch.17) names Saturn the sole rajayoga planet for Taurus and Libra lagnas, so its sign results tend to be felt more favourably there.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.17 (tr. M. D. Neely)

source_views.view: For Saturn, Gemini is a friendly sign.

source_views.view: Saturn in Gemini: wandering, untidy, original, subtle, ingenious, strategic, few children, taste for chemical and mechanical sciences, logical, speculative.

source_views.view: Saturn's dasa from Gemini: recognition of services, humanitarian work, profits in trade and speculation, respect from rulers, reputation.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer, chapter on Saturn and Saturn-in-houses dignity notes (archive.org scan)
source_views.view: Mercury is one of Saturn's friends.

planet_in_sign/saturn/gemini.disagreements: Saravali and Brihat Jataka are negative; Raman's modern sign list and dasa note are mixed to favourable. Brihat Jataka treats Gemini and Virgo together; Saravali gives them separate verses but shared aspect verses.
planet_in_sign/saturn/gemini.phrasing_guidance: Describe as a careful, serious mind that does well with structure; mention obligations or debts only as areas to manage. Avoid predicting legal trouble.

planet_in_sign/saturn/cancer.summary: Saturn in Cancer is in the sign of the Moon, a natural enemy. Classical texts link it with poverty in youth, distance from the mother and quarrels with kin, but Saravali adds learning, soft speech and a king-like position in mid-life; Foss sees Cancer's caring nature as improving Saturn.
common_outcomes: Lack of wealth in boyhood with improvement and a king-like position in mid-life (Saravali 29.7-8)
Distance from the mother or lack of motherly care (Saravali 29.7-8; Brihat Jataka 18.18; Raman HPA ch.22)
Friction with relatives (Saravali 29.7-8; Raman HPA ch.24)
Learned and soft-spoken (Saravali 29.7-8)
rare_outcomes: Saravali 29.7-8 also gives a beloved wife
Saravali 29.47: Jupiter aspect gives lands, houses, friends, sons, wealth and gems; 29.45: Mars aspect gives royal wealth but a difficult circle; 29.43: Sun aspect is the hardest
Brihat Jataka 18.18 adds childlessness and poverty

by_area.personality: Soft-spoken and learned (Saravali 29.7-8); Raman lists slow, stubborn and selfish traits (HPA ch.22).
by_area.career: Distinguished in action and king-like in mid-life (Saravali 29.7-8).
by_area.finance: Poor in youth, improving later (Saravali 29.7-8); Jupiter aspect brings property and wealth (Saravali 29.47).
by_area.relationships: Saravali 29.7-8 gives a beloved wife.
by_area.family: Distance from mother and quarrels with kin are classical themes (Saravali 29.7-8; Brihat Jataka 18.18); Raman's dasa note adds family strife (HPA ch.24).

strengtheners: Jupiter aspect (Saravali 29.47)
Mercury aspect: conquers enemies and does noble acts (Saravali 29.46)
Retrograde Saturn (Phaladeepika 9.20)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Sun aspect (Saravali 29.43) is described as the most difficult
Phaladeepika 9.17: a planet in an enemy's sign brings dependence and opposition in its dasa
Frawley: non-watery planets such as Saturn in water signs tend to negate the water element, and can be overpowered by it if weak (p.115)
planet_in_sign/saturn/cancer.lagna_or_context_notes: Foss notes that Saturn in Cancer in the 1st house (examples: Indira Gandhi, G.W. Bush) is generally improved by Cancer's sattvic, caring nature. Raman (HPA ch.17) names Saturn the sole rajayoga planet for Taurus and Libra lagnas, so its sign results tend to be felt more favourably there.

planet_in_sign/saturn/cancer.disagreements: Brihat Jataka says lacking learning; Saravali says learned and king-like in mid-life. Raman's dasa note is harsh, while Foss reads Cancer as improving Saturn. All agree on early domestic hardship and the mother theme.
planet_in_sign/saturn/cancer.phrasing_guidance: Speak of emotional responsibility and a slow-building sense of security. Never predict a parent's death or childlessness; say 'the relationship with mother or home may carry responsibility or distance'.

planet_in_sign/saturn/leo.summary: Saturn in Leo is in the sign of its chief enemy, the Sun. Texts describe toil, servitude and strained close relationships, alongside skill and interest in writing and reading; Raman calls it a hard-working, good writer.
common_outcomes: Heavy work and toil before recognition (Saravali 29.9-10; Brihat Jataka 18.18; Raman HPA ch.22)
Interest and skill in writing and reading (Saravali 29.9-10; Raman HPA ch.22: good writer)
Strained ties with spouse, children or one's own people (Saravali 29.9-10; Brihat Jataka 18.18)
Raman's dasa note: uneasiness, distrust and disappointment (HPA ch.24)
rare_outcomes: Saravali 29.53: Jupiter aspect makes one chief and rich in his town or among his people, with children; 29.50: Moon aspect gives wealth, fame and royal favour; 29.54: Venus aspect gives splendour, wealth and a good end; 29.49 (Sun) and 29.51 (Mars) aspects give hardship
Brihat Jataka 18.18: coarse conduct and trouble through offspring

by_area.personality: Raman: severe, obstinate, hard-working (HPA ch.22); Saravali 29.9-10 adds ill temper and strong desires.
by_area.career: Service and heavy labour (Saravali 29.9-10); writing and reading (Saravali 29.9-10; Raman HPA ch.22).
by_area.finance: Improves with Moon, Jupiter or Venus aspect (Saravali 29.50, 29.53, 29.54).
by_area.relationships: Saravali 29.9-10 says devoid of wife or of one's own people; present only as strain to work on.
by_area.family: Few sons (Raman HPA ch.22); trouble through children (Brihat Jataka 18.18).

strengtheners: Jupiter, Moon or Venus aspect on Saturn (Saravali 29.50, 29.53, 29.54)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Sun aspect (Saravali 29.49), Mars aspect (29.51) and Mercury aspect (29.52)
Phaladeepika 9.17 on enemy-sign placement
planet_in_sign/saturn/leo.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman (HPA ch.17) lists Saturn as ill-disposed for Aries, Leo and Pisces lagnas; for Leo lagna Saturn rising here combines both. Braha says that for Taurus lagna (Saturn in the 4th, i.e. Leo) Saturn gives happiness and fixed assets, especially real estate.

planet_in_sign/saturn/leo.disagreements: Sources agree on difficulty. Saravali and Raman see writing and reading as a compensating gift; Brihat Jataka does not mention it. Braha's lagna-based note for Taurus ascendant is more favourable than the sign verses.
planet_in_sign/saturn/leo.phrasing_guidance: Frame as recognition that arrives through persistence and humility. Avoid predicting estrangement; say relationships benefit from softening pride.

planet_in_sign/saturn/virgo.summary: Saturn in Virgo, the sign of its friend Mercury, gets mixed verdicts. Saravali lists dependence, few friends and low conduct, but also sons, wealth, helpfulness and caution; Raman's sign list is harsh, yet his dasa note promises elevation and fame. Foss says Virgo has a particular problem with Saturn.
common_outcomes: Cautious in action and helpful to others (Saravali 29.11-12)
Sons and wealth, with some dependence on others and few friends (Saravali 29.11-12)
Raman lists poverty, quarrelsomeness and conservatism but also a taste for public life (HPA ch.22)
Raman's dasa note: elevation, royal favour, business success and fame (HPA ch.24)
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 18.17 (Mercury's signs): uneven in writing or painting, lacking comfort
Saravali 29.40: Mercury aspect gives wealth and skill in arts; 29.42: Venus aspect, a teacher of yoga or saint

by_area.personality: Cautious and helpful (Saravali 29.11-12); Raman lists narrow-minded, erratic and conservative traits (HPA ch.22).
by_area.career: Taste for public life (Raman HPA ch.22); elevation and business success in Saturn's dasa (Raman HPA ch.24).
by_area.finance: Saravali 29.11-12 gives wealth; Raman's sign list says poor (HPA ch.22).
by_area.family: Saravali 29.11-12 gives sons and wealth.
by_area.spirituality: Foss recommends worship of the Sun (Gayatri) to meet Saturn's difficulty in Virgo (name 34).

strengtheners: Mercury is Saturn's friend (Braha; Bhavartha Ratnakara 15.7 lists Virgo as friendly)
Mercury or Jupiter aspect on Saturn (Saravali 29.40-41)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mars aspect (Saravali 29.39)
Foss: Saturn's air opposes the earth of Mercury's Virgo, giving Virgo a particular problem with Saturn (name 34)
planet_in_sign/saturn/virgo.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman (HPA ch.17) names Saturn the sole rajayoga planet for Taurus and Libra lagnas, so its sign results tend to be felt more favourably there.

source_views.view: Saturn in Virgo: crafty, dependent on others for food, few friends, unacquainted with arts, indolent, yet possesses sons and wealth, helpful to others and cautious in actions.

planet_in_sign/saturn/virgo.disagreements: Friendly by dignity tables, but Foss calls Virgo problematic for Saturn. Brihat Jataka denies children and wealth for Mercury's signs while Saravali gives sons and wealth for Virgo. Raman's sign list is harsh but his dasa note is favourable.
planet_in_sign/saturn/virgo.phrasing_guidance: Highlight diligence, craft and service. Do not make moral judgements about the person.

planet_in_sign/saturn/libra.summary: Saturn is exalted in Libra (deepest at 20 degrees), in the sign of its friend Venus. It is one of Saturn's best placements: classical and modern texts agree on wealth, standing, sound judgment and leadership of groups or institutions.
common_outcomes: Respect and leadership within groups, towns and institutions (Brihat Jataka 18.18; Saravali 29.13-14: senior in his circle)
Wealth and honour, including from abroad (Saravali 29.13-14; Brihat Jataka 18.18)
Raman: famous, founder of institutions, tactful, respected, sound judgment, charitable (HPA ch.22)
Sasa yoga (a Pancha Mahapurusha yoga) when Saturn is in an angle in its exaltation or own sign (Saravali 37.2)
rare_outcomes: Saravali 29.13-14 adds association with dancers and courtesans
Saravali 29.32: Moon aspect gives wealth and ministers' honour; 29.36: Venus aspect gives gems and royal favour; 29.34: Mercury aspect weakens
Phaladeepika 9.14: an exalted planet gives rulership, fame and courage
Raman's dasa note: foreign travel, opening new business branches, public speaking and honour (HPA ch.24)

by_area.personality: Raman: tactful, powerful, independent, proud, sound in judgment (HPA ch.22); Saravali 29.13-14: soft-spoken and good.
by_area.career: King or scholar, high status through gracious speech in assemblies (Saravali 29.13-14); founder of institutions (Raman HPA ch.22); Braha describes Saturn in Libra in the 10th as great career success growing with age.
by_area.finance: Rich, earning money from abroad, wealth protected by relatives (Saravali 29.13-14).
by_area.relationships: Saravali 29.13-14 and Raman (subservient to women, HPA ch.22) note strong attachments.
by_area.family: Wealth protected by relatives (Saravali 29.13-14); domestic happiness in Saturn's dasa (Raman HPA ch.24).

strengtheners: Saturn in an angle (Sasa yoga, Saravali 37.2, 37.8-10)
Moon, Jupiter or Venus aspect (Saravali 29.32, 29.35, 29.36)
Close to 20 degrees, the exaltation point (BPHS 3.49-50; Frawley p.125)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mercury aspect (Saravali 29.34) and Sun aspect (29.31)
Frawley: an exaltation can be cancelled by malefic aspect, difficult houses or rulership of malefics, and an exalted but neutralised planet gives poor results (p.127)
planet_in_sign/saturn/libra.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman (HPA ch.17) names Saturn the sole rajayoga planet for Taurus and Libra lagnas, so its sign results tend to be felt more favourably there, so for Libra lagna this is the yogakaraka exalted in the lagna. Braha: Saturn in Libra in the ascendant gives leadership and high status; Foss cites Margaret Thatcher (Libra rising, exalted Saturn) as an example of leadership and a well-presented style.

source_views.view: Saturn exalted in Libra at 20 degrees.

source_views.source: BPHS 3.59
source_views.view: A planet in exaltation gives full auspicious results.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.18 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Saturn in Libra: respected by groups, towns, armies and villages; wealthy.

source_views.source: Saravali 29.13-14 (English e-text on archive.org whose chapter captions and wording match R. Santhanam's translation; translator not named in the file)

source_views.source: Saravali 37.2, 37.8-10 (English e-text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Saturn in its own or exaltation sign in an angle forms Sasa yoga: famous, an army chief, skilful in all assignments.

source_views.view: For Saturn, Libra is the sign of exaltation.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 9.14
source_views.view: An exalted planet gives rulership, praise and fame.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch.22 'Planets in Different Rasis', Saturn (pp.132-134)
source_views.view: Saturn in Libra: famous, founder of institutions, rich, tactful, powerful, respected, sound judgment, independent, proud, charitable.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch.24, Saturn's dasa by sign (pp.158-159)
source_views.view: Saturn's dasa from Libra: foreign travel, new business branches, public lectures, honour and domestic happiness.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer, chapter on Saturn and Saturn-in-houses dignity notes (archive.org scan)
source_views.view: Saturn functions best in Libra; in Libra, Capricorn or Aquarius in the 1st or 10th it gives leadership, high status and career success.

source_views.view: Commentary on names 19 and 57: Thatcher, with exalted Saturn rising in Libra, rose to leadership; the Venus sign showed in her careful presentation.

planet_in_sign/saturn/libra.disagreements: Little disagreement on strength. Saravali and Raman add indulgent or proud traits that Brihat Jataka omits. Frawley warns that exaltation can be neutralised by affliction.
planet_in_sign/saturn/libra.phrasing_guidance: Describe as earned authority and fairness. Avoid promising fame or wealth outright; say the placement supports steady rise through responsibility.

planet_in_sign/saturn/scorpio.summary: Saturn in Scorpio is in the sign of its enemy Mars. Classical and modern texts describe a hostile, harsh and miserly temperament, wealth gained through others and a risk-prone life; it is a placement of endurance under pressure.
common_outcomes: Hostile, ill-tempered or harsh temperament (Saravali 29.15-16; Brihat Jataka 18.17; Raman HPA ch.22)
Wealth, including through others' money, alongside losses and misery (Saravali 29.15-16)
Reserved, adventurous and hard-hearted (Raman HPA ch.22)
Raman's dasa note: displeasure of superiors and loss of prestige (HPA ch.24)
rare_outcomes: Saravali 29.15-16 and Raman (HPA ch.22) list risks from poison, fire or weapons (a risk theme, never a prediction)
Saravali 29.15-16 says averse to festive music
Saravali 29.29: Jupiter aspect in a Mars sign gives wealth, fortune and a minister's or chief's position

by_area.personality: Hostile, crooked, egoistic in Saravali 29.15-16; Raman: reserved, adventurous, hard-hearted, rash (HPA ch.22).
by_area.career: Raman's dasa note warns of friction with superiors and loss of prestige (HPA ch.24).
by_area.finance: Rich and miserly, gaining others' money, yet facing loss (Saravali 29.15-16); Raman adds wastefulness (HPA ch.22).

Sun aspect gives agricultural wealth (Saravali 29.25)
Retrograde Saturn (Phaladeepika 9.20)

Phaladeepika 9.17 enemy-sign effects in dasa

source_views.view: Saturn's dasa from Scorpio: displeasure of superiors, loss of prestige, damage to property.

planet_in_sign/saturn/scorpio.disagreements: Texts agree on difficulty. Saravali says rich (through others' money) while Raman says wasteful. The earlier reading of a 'connection with music' was a mistranslation; Saravali says averse to festive music.
planet_in_sign/saturn/scorpio.phrasing_guidance: Speak of depth, endurance and handling shared resources carefully. Never mention injury, poison or violence as predictions.

planet_in_sign/saturn/sagittarius.summary: Saturn in Sagittarius is in Jupiter's sign, neutral to Saturn. Classical texts are favourable: skill in teaching and sacred learning, fame through good children and family, few words, and wealth in old age. Foss and Braha both say Saturn does especially well in Jupiter's signs.
common_outcomes: Trusted position with authorities; good children, spouse and wealth (Brihat Jataka 18.19)
Skill in conduct, teaching and the meaning of sacred texts (Saravali 29.17-18)
Fame through virtuous children, family profession and own virtues; affluence in old age (Saravali 29.17-18)
Raman's dasa note: philosophical and religious study and peace (HPA ch.24)
rare_outcomes: Saravali 29.17-18 says speaks little and has many names
Saravali 29.59: Jupiter aspect makes one a king, minister or army chief; 29.58: Mercury aspect a respected preceptor; 29.57: Mars aspect is unfavourable
Brihat Jataka 18.19: leadership of a town, army or village

by_area.personality: Speaks little, soft in disposition (Saravali 29.17-18); Raman: peaceful, faithful, courteous, sometimes pretentious (HPA ch.22).
by_area.career: Teaching and sacred learning (Saravali 29.17-18); leading a town or group (Brihat Jataka 18.19).
by_area.finance: Excellent affluence in old age (Saravali 29.17-18).
by_area.relationships: Brihat Jataka 18.19 gives a good spouse; Raman notes troubles with wife (HPA ch.22).
by_area.family: Fame through virtuous children and family profession (Saravali 29.17-18); dutiful children (Raman HPA ch.22).
by_area.spirituality: Study of philosophy and religion (Raman HPA ch.24).

strengtheners: Jupiter or Mercury aspect (Saravali 29.58-59)
Foss and Braha: Saturn is most auspicious in Jupiter's signs despite Jupiter being only neutral to it
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mars aspect (Saravali 29.57)
Phaladeepika 9.19: a neutral sign gives no marked change by itself
