source_views.view: Scriptures commonly say Saturn gives excellent results in Sagittarius and Pisces even though Jupiter is technically neutral to it.

planet_in_sign/saturn/sagittarius.disagreements: Classical verses and modern authors (Foss, Braha) are positive although the dignity is only neutral. Raman notes marital trouble that Brihat Jataka does not.
planet_in_sign/saturn/sagittarius.phrasing_guidance: Describe as earned trust and principled leadership that matures over time. Avoid guaranteeing children or wealth.

planet_in_sign/saturn/capricorn.summary: Saturn in Capricorn is in its own sign. Saravali gives learning, many arts, honour among one's people, courage and residence abroad; Brihat Jataka gives leadership of a town or group; Raman adds intelligence and domestic harmony, and Foss calls Capricorn steady and suited to big business.
common_outcomes: Learning, virtues and knowledge of many fine arts; excellent among his people, honourable and famous (Saravali 29.19-20)
Leadership of a town, group or unit (Brihat Jataka 18.19)
Living in foreign places; courageous and polite (Saravali 29.19-20)
Sasa yoga when in an angle (Saravali 37.2)
rare_outcomes: Saravali 29.19-20 says he lords over lands of others' women and likes bathing and decoration
Brihat Jataka 18.19: wealth connected with another's spouse, unkempt appearance
Saravali 29.65: Jupiter aspect gives fame, royal status, long life and good health; 29.63: Mars aspect gives valour and fame; 29.61 (Sun) and 29.62 (Moon) aspects give hardship
Raman: inheritance through the spouse's family (HPA ch.22)

by_area.personality: Courageous and polite (Saravali 29.19-20); Raman: intelligent, prudent, reflective but suspicious and melancholy (HPA ch.22); Foss: steady and unflinching.
by_area.career: Leadership of a group (Brihat Jataka 18.19); Foss links Capricorn with big business; Braha: in the 10th house, great career success growing with age.
by_area.finance: Raman's dasa note: increase in lands, wealth and business (HPA ch.24).
by_area.relationships: Raman: harmony in domestic life (HPA ch.22).
by_area.spirituality: Saravali 29.19-20 gives Vedic knowledge.

strengtheners: Angle placement (Sasa yoga, Saravali 37.2)
Jupiter, Mars or Venus aspect (Saravali 29.63, 29.65, 29.66)
Phaladeepika 9.15: own-sign planet brings settled position, property and honour in its dasa
weakeners_or_cancellations: Sun or Moon aspect (Saravali 29.61-62)
Combustion (Phaladeepika 9.19)
Foss: Capricorn Saturn can cause divisions in the pursuit of dominance (name 35)
planet_in_sign/saturn/capricorn.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman (HPA ch.17) names Saturn the sole rajayoga planet for Taurus and Libra lagnas, so its sign results tend to be felt more favourably there. Braha: Saturn in Capricorn in the ascendant gives leadership and high status, and in the 4th (Libra lagna) homes and real estate.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.19 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Saturn in own sign: leads a town, army or village, steady wealth; some unflattering traits.

source_views.view: Saturn in Capricorn: intelligent, domestic harmony, learned, reflective, prudent, but selfish, suspicious and melancholy; inheritance from the spouse's family.

source_views.view: Saturn's dasa from Capricorn: increase in lands, wealth and business; friendship with eminent people.

source_views.view: Commentary on names 25-26 and 35: Capricorn is moveable yet Saturn there is steady; it represents big business and can divide in gaining dominance.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer, chapter on Saturn and Saturn-in-houses dignity notes (archive.org scan)
source_views.view: Saturn rules Capricorn and gives very good results there; in the 1st or 10th it gives leadership and career success.

planet_in_sign/saturn/capricorn.disagreements: Strength is agreed. The earlier file put untruthful and indulgent traits under Capricorn; in the Saravali text those belong to Aquarius (29.21-22). Brihat Jataka still gives some unflattering traits for Saturn's own signs.
planet_in_sign/saturn/capricorn.phrasing_guidance: Emphasise reliability, organisation and earned authority. Avoid character labels like 'untruthful'.

planet_in_sign/saturn/aquarius.summary: Saturn in Aquarius is in its moolatrikona (0-20 degrees) and own sign beyond, and Foss calls it Saturn's strongest sign. Classical verses are nevertheless harsh (untruthful, harsh speech, many undertakings), while Raman's modern list is favourable: practical, able, diplomatic and philosophical.
common_outcomes: Attempts many undertakings (Saravali 29.21-22)
Eminent standing (Saravali 29.21-22); leadership of a group with steady means (Brihat Jataka 18.19)
Raman: practical, able, diplomatic, ingenious, prudent, reflective, philosophical (HPA ch.22)
Sasa yoga when in an angle (Saravali 37.2)
rare_outcomes: Saravali 29.21-22 lists untruthfulness, harsh speech, indulgence and aversion to tradition
Raman: can be overcome by enemies (HPA ch.22); his dasa note gives travel westward, success in litigation and wealth (HPA ch.24)
BPHS 3.59: moolatrikona gives three-quarters of full benefic results

by_area.personality: Raman: practical, diplomatic, reflective (HPA ch.22); Saravali 29.21-22: harsh in speech.
by_area.career: Many undertakings (Saravali 29.21-22); Braha: in the 10th, a powerful leader with a vision for organisations; Foss: Saturn rising in Aquarius gives influence over the masses (Karl Marx example).
by_area.finance: Raman's dasa note: acquisition of wealth (HPA ch.24).
by_area.spirituality: Raman lists a philosophical turn (HPA ch.22).

strengtheners: Angle placement (Sasa yoga, Saravali 37.2)
Jupiter, Mars or Venus aspect (Saravali 29.63, 29.65, 29.66)
Degree within 0-20, the moolatrikona (BPHS 3.54; Raman HPA ch.6; Frawley p.127)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Sun or Moon aspect (Saravali 29.61-62)
Combustion (Phaladeepika 9.19)

Braha: Saturn in Aquarius in the ascendant gives leadership and high status. Foss notes the tamas of both Saturn and Aquarius when Saturn rises there.

planet_in_sign/saturn/aquarius.disagreements: Saravali's Aquarius verse is harsh, whereas dignity (moolatrikona) and modern authors (Raman, Braha, Foss) are favourable. The earlier file attached Saravali's gem-testing and calm-leadership lines to Aquarius; those are in the Pisces verse (29.23-24). BPHS 3.54, Raman and Frawley agree on Aquarius 0-20 as moolatrikona.
planet_in_sign/saturn/aquarius.phrasing_guidance: Emphasise strength, collective purpose and independence; mention bluntness as a style to soften. Do not mention addiction or illicit relationships as predictions.

planet_in_sign/saturn/pisces.summary: Saturn in Pisces is in Jupiter's sign, neutral to Saturn. Saravali is kind: fond of sacrifices and arts, chief among relatives and friends, calm, skilled in policy and in judging gems, virtuous and modest, with growing wealth and authority later in life. Foss and Braha both rate Jupiter's signs highly for Saturn.
common_outcomes: Chief among relatives and friends; calm, virtuous and modest (Saravali 29.23-24)
Increasing wealth and an authoritative position later in life (Saravali 29.23-24)
Trusted role, good family, leadership (Brihat Jataka 18.19)
Raman: clever, gifted, polite, helpful and wealthy (HPA ch.22)
rare_outcomes: Saravali 29.23-24: skill at testing diamonds and in policy-making
Saravali 29.60: Venus aspect, living in forests or hills, unsteady; 29.56: Moon aspect, two names with wife, children and wealth
Raman's dasa note: pilgrimages and indifference to sectarian rules, with some sorrow and unrest (HPA ch.24)

by_area.personality: Calm, virtuous, modest (Saravali 29.23-24); Raman: clever, polite, helpful, sometimes scheming (HPA ch.22).
by_area.career: Skill in policy-making; authority later in life (Saravali 29.23-24).
by_area.finance: Increasing wealth (Saravali 29.23-24); wealthy (Raman HPA ch.22).
by_area.family: Chief among relatives and friends (Saravali 29.23-24).
by_area.spirituality: Fond of sacrifices (Saravali 29.23-24); pilgrimage in Saturn's dasa (Raman HPA ch.24).

strengtheners: Jupiter or Mercury aspect (Saravali 29.58-59)
Foss and Braha: Saturn is most auspicious in Jupiter's signs
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mars aspect (Saravali 29.57)
Neutral dignity alone does not raise results (Phaladeepika 9.19)
Frawley: Saturn in a water sign tends to negate the water element (p.115)

Raman (HPA ch.17) names Saturn the sole rajayoga planet for Taurus and Libra lagnas, so its sign results tend to be felt more favourably there.

planet_in_sign/saturn/pisces.disagreements: Sources broadly agree this is benign; the gem-testing line, earlier uncertain between Aquarius and Pisces, belongs to Pisces in the English Saravali (29.23-24). Raman's dasa note is more mixed than his sign list.
planet_in_sign/saturn/pisces.phrasing_guidance: Describe quiet virtue, service and respect that matures with time. Avoid promising specific status.

planet_in_sign/sun/aries.summary: The Sun is exalted in Aries (deepest exaltation at 10°), which gives strong self-confidence, initiative and a drive to lead. Classical texts describe a famous, energetic, combative person who rises through their own effort.
common_outcomes: Strong will, self-reliance and willingness to take the lead
Recognition or fame for skill or bold action
Restless, active temperament; likes travel and movement
Attraction to competitive, military, sporting or command roles
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka says the native is famous and clever but wanders and gains little, and bears weapons when the Sun is not in its exact exaltation degree
Saravali 22.2-3 describes a commentator on scriptures, famous in the arts, who becomes a king or ruler-like figure
Saravali 22.2-3 associates the placement with a 'bilious' (pitta) constitution and strong bones

by_area.personality: Bold, fierce, fond of war and roaming, attached to duty (Saravali 22.2-3); active, ambitious, impulsive, irritable and pioneering (Raman HPA ch. XXII).
by_area.career: Saravali 22.2-3 says the native may rise to kingly status; Raman lists warrior and traveller; Brihat Jataka 18.1 says the native bears weapons when the Sun is short of its exact exaltation degree.
by_area.finance: Brihat Jataka 18.1: fame with little gain; Raman: wealthy but of variable fortune; Phaladeepika 9.14 (any exalted planet): wealth and treasures.
by_area.health: Saravali 22.2-3 links the placement to bilious and blood disorders and strong bones; treat as a temperament note only, never as a medical prediction.
by_area.spirituality: Saravali 22.2-3: comments on the meaning of the shastras.

strengtheners: Near 10° Aries (exact exaltation); Brihat Jataka 18.1 specifically distinguishes results at the exaltation degree
Kendra placement; Braha (p. 50) says planets in kendras are powerful and prominent
Placement in the 10th, where the Sun has directional strength (Braha pp. 17, 60)
Jupiter's aspect (Saravali 22.4-9: wealth and high office) or Mars's aspect (courage in battle)
Exalted or own sign in the navamsa, or vargottama (Braha pp. 13-14, 59-60)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saturn's aspect (Saravali 22.4-9: grief, dullness for the Sun in Mars's signs)
Venus's aspect (Saravali lists an unhappy marriage among results for Sun in Mars's signs)
Placement in a dusthana (6th, 8th, 12th); Braha (pp. 51-52) says a planet there is spoiled, the 6th being the mildest
Mercury's aspect: Saravali gives servitude and poverty for the Sun in Mars's signs
planet_in_sign/sun/aries.lagna_or_context_notes: Braha ('Planets in the Houses', pp. 79 ff.) reads the exalted or own-sign Sun house by house. With the Sun in Aries: Aries lagna (1st) respect, learning and a good start in life; Cancer lagna (10th) fame and a high position; Leo lagna (9th) fortune, faith and a prosperous father; Capricorn lagna (4th) homes, property and power but less happiness from the mother; Gemini lagna (11th) wealth from many sources; Libra lagna (7th) a capable spouse while the Sun's usual 7th-house strains remain.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 3.49-50
source_views.view: Sun's exaltation sign is Aries at 10°; the 7th sign (Libra) at the same degree is its debilitation.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.1 (tr. M. D. Neely, 2007)
source_views.view: Sun in Aries: famous, clever, wandering, with little gain; bears arms when not at the exaltation degree.

source_views.source: Saravali 22.4-9, aspects on the Sun in Mars's signs (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Moon's aspect gives generosity and servants; Mars courage in battle; Mercury servitude; Jupiter wealth and high office; Venus a difficult marriage; Saturn grief and dullness.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 9.14 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: A planet in exaltation gives rule over land, royal praise, wealth, fame, valour, generosity and cleverness.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXII 'Planets in Different Rasis or Signs' (Sun, pp. 204-205)
source_views.view: Active, intelligent, famous, a traveller, wealthy, warrior-like, variable fortune, ambitious, powerful, impulsive, irritable, pioneering.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), 'Planetary Powers' p. 47 and '1st House' (pp. 79-90)
source_views.view: Sun is exalted in Aries; a planet before its deepest degree keeps the state less intensely and one past it is technically no longer exalted; the exalted Sun in the 1st gives respect, learning and a good start in life.

source_views.source: Andrew Foss, The Yoga of the Planets: Surya, the Sun, name 70 ('The victor')
source_views.view: Exaltation in Aries gives a sense of being naturally victorious, peaking at 10 degrees Aries.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), 'The Sun' p. 17, 'Navamsa' pp. 13-14, 'House Rulerships' pp. 50-52 and 'Shad Bala' pp. 59-61
source_views.view: The Sun does best in the upachaya houses and in the 10th (directional strength); planets in kendras are powerful and in trikonas flourish, while a planet in a dusthana is spoiled; dignity in the navamsa or vargottama strengthens a planet, but not a fallen one.

planet_in_sign/sun/aries.disagreements: Brihat Jataka gives fame with limited gain and a wandering, weapon-bearing life unless the Sun is at its exact exaltation degree; Saravali is more uniformly positive (kingly), and Raman lists wealth with variable fortune. BPHS 3.49-50 treats all of Aries as exaltation with the peak at 10 degrees, while Braha (p. 47) says a planet past its deepest degree is technically no longer exalted.
planet_in_sign/sun/aries.phrasing_guidance: Describe as strong confidence and leadership potential that grows with effort. Avoid promising fame or power; note that impatience or pride is the main thing to manage. No health or longevity predictions.

planet_in_sign/sun/taurus.summary: The Sun in Taurus sits in the sign of Venus, a natural enemy, so its fiery assertiveness becomes steadier and more pleasure- and resource-oriented. Texts link it to arts, music, trade in fine goods and enjoyment of comforts.
common_outcomes: Clever and reflective; slow to act but self-confident (Raman HPA ch. XXII)
Interest or skill in singing, music, dance or aesthetic trades
Livelihood through trade in cloth, perfumes or other fine goods
Enjoys food, garments, scents and comforts
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka says the native dislikes women or is at odds with them
Saravali 22.10-11 lists a slim build, endurance of hardship and few sons
Saravali 22.10-11 mentions risk connected with water

by_area.personality: Wise, decorous and good-looking, fond of food, garlands, robes and scents (Saravali 22.10-11); clever, reflective, slow to act, self-confident, tactful and sociable (Raman HPA ch. XXII).
by_area.career: Trade in cloth and perfumes (Brihat Jataka 18.1; Raman: dealer in perfumes); singing, instruments and dance (Saravali 22.10-11; Raman: musician).
by_area.health: Saravali 22.10-11 mentions face and eye complaints, a lean body and risk from water; treat as traditional notes, not predictions.
by_area.relationships: Brihat Jataka 18.1 and Raman say the native is at odds with or disliked by women; present only as a tradition, never as a forecast.
by_area.family: Saravali 22.10-11 gives few sons; confirm from the 5th house before mentioning.

strengtheners: Jupiter's aspect (Saravali 22.12-17: royal minister, splendour, many friends as well as foes)
Upachaya placement (3rd, 6th, 10th, 11th), where Braha (pp. 17, 51) says malefics such as the Sun give excellent results
Exalted or own sign in the navamsa, or vargottama (Braha pp. 13-14, 59-60)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saturn's aspect (Saravali 22.12-17: meanness, liaisons with older women for the Sun in Venus's signs)
Placement in a dusthana (6th, 8th, 12th); Braha (pp. 51-52) says a planet there is spoiled, the 6th being the mildest

source_views.view: A planet in an enemy sign tends toward dependence on others, petty-mindedness and trouble from enemies.

source_views.view: Clever, reflective, deals in perfumes, disliked by women, slow to act, musician, self-confident, tactful, sociable.

source_views.source: Andrew Foss, The Yoga of the Planets: Surya, the Sun, name 9 ('The imperishable')
source_views.view: The Sun is uncomfortable in Libra, a movable Venus sign, but not afflicted in Taurus because that fixed sign helps it stay steady.

planet_in_sign/sun/taurus.disagreements: Both texts agree on music, arts and enjoyment; Saravali adds bodily hardship and few sons that Brihat Jataka does not mention. Foss treats Taurus as relatively steadying for the Sun because it is a fixed sign, unlike Libra.
planet_in_sign/sun/taurus.phrasing_guidance: Frame as artistic, steady and comfort-loving with possible friction between pride and pleasure. Do not predict problems with women, children or eyes; mention them only as traditional notes if asked.

planet_in_sign/sun/gemini.summary: The Sun in Gemini sits in Mercury's sign, which is neutral for the Sun. Both major texts describe a learned, articulate and well-off person, skilled in calculation or astrology.
common_outcomes: Intellectual, sweet-spoken, well-mannered
Learning in both worldly and sacred subjects
Skill with numbers, writing or astrology
Comfortable finances
rare_outcomes: Saravali 22.18-19 mentions 'two mothers' (e.g. a foster or step-mother figure)
Saravali 22.18-19 notes special affection for children

by_area.personality: Sweet-spoken, well-mannered, modest and affectionate (Saravali 22.18-19); polite, critical, a good conversationalist, shy and reserved (Raman HPA ch. XXII).
by_area.career: Astrology and learning (Brihat Jataka 18.2; Saravali 22.18-19); Raman adds astronomer, scholar and grammarian.
by_area.finance: Wealthy (Brihat Jataka 18.2; Raman); Saravali 22.18-19 adds very affluent and liberal.
by_area.relationships: Saravali 22.18-19: affectionate, especially toward children.
by_area.family: Saravali 22.18-19: 'two mothers' (for example a foster or step-mother figure), a rare text-specific note.
by_area.spirituality: Saravali 22.18-19: expert in the shastras as well as worldly knowledge.

Venus's aspect (Saravali 22.20-25: wealth)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mars's aspect (Saravali 22.20-25: loss, poverty, quarrels for the Sun in Mercury's signs)
Moon's aspect (Saravali 22.20-25: trouble from kin or enemies)
Saturn's aspect (Saravali 22.20-25: craftiness, though many servants)

planet_in_sign/sun/gemini.phrasing_guidance: Present as a bright, articulate, learning-oriented placement. Avoid promising wealth; say it supports earning through knowledge and communication.

planet_in_sign/sun/cancer.summary: The Sun in Cancer is in the Moon's sign, a friend, but the watery, emotional sign tempers the Sun's steadiness. Texts give mixed results: honour and good qualities alongside unsteady undertakings, hard work for others and tension with relatives.
common_outcomes: Unsteady in undertakings (Saravali 22.26-27)
Works hard, often on behalf of others
Fluctuating projects or plans
Recognition for virtue, eloquence or public service
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka describes a hot-tempered, poor person who faces hardship and an austere path
Saravali 22.26-27 describes royal qualities and fame, but strain with paternal relatives and an unattractive spouse
Saravali 22.26-27 mentions study of geography or atmospheric sciences and a liking for intoxicants

by_area.personality: Unsteady in undertakings yet honourable and eloquent (Saravali 22.26-27); hot-tempered (Brihat Jataka 18.2); Raman HPA ch. XXII lists indolence, sorrow and a servile mentality.
by_area.career: Works for others (Brihat Jataka 18.2); famed for royal qualities, studies geography and the sky (Saravali 22.26-27); Raman: travelling.
by_area.finance: Brihat Jataka 18.2 and Raman say poor; Saravali 22.26-27 does not stress poverty.
by_area.health: Saravali 22.26-27 links the placement to phlegm-bile imbalance and fatigue from hard labour, and Raman lists sickliness; mention only as a traditional tendency.
by_area.relationships: Saravali 22.26-27 notes an unattractive or difficult spouse; treat cautiously and confirm from the 7th.
by_area.family: Saravali 22.26-27: hates his own people and those on the paternal side.
by_area.spirituality: Brihat Jataka 18.2 speaks of hardship on an austere path; Saravali 22.26-27: follows virtuous principles.

Venus's aspect (Saravali 22.28-33: wealth through spouse)

Saturn's aspect (Saravali 22.28-33: phlegm and wind disorders)

planet_in_sign/sun/cancer.phrasing_guidance: Say this placement mixes sensitivity and service with pride; results depend strongly on the Moon. Avoid stating poverty or a bad marriage as fact.

planet_in_sign/sun/leo.summary: Leo is the Sun's own sign; 0-20° is its moolatrikona and 20-30° own sign. It gives authority, courage, self-respect and a love of open, wild places, with a quick temper.
common_outcomes: Natural authority and leadership, strong self-respect
Courage and decisive action; defeats rivals
Love of nature, forests, hills and open spaces
Quick to anger; proud
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka says the native is vigorous but lacks knowledge
Saravali 22.34-35 says the native becomes a wealthy, famous ruler
Saravali 22.34-35 mentions fondness for meat

by_area.personality: Quick to anger, enthusiastic, valorous, talkative and restless (Saravali 22.34-35); vigorous (Brihat Jataka 18.2); stubborn, strong, independent and generous (Raman HPA ch. XXII).
by_area.career: Notable deeds and kingly status (Saravali 22.34-35); Raman: organising capacity and talent for propaganda; Braha ('Planets in the Houses') gives fame and high position when the own-sign Sun is in the 10th.
by_area.finance: Saravali 22.34-35: plentiful wealth and fame; Raman: poor. The texts disagree.

strengtheners: Within 0-20° (moolatrikona) per BPHS 3.51
Jupiter's aspect (Saravali 22.36-41: builds temples, gardens and tanks; highly intelligent) or Mars's aspect (courage, leadership)

weakeners_or_cancellations: Venus's aspect (Saravali 22.36-41: bad repute)
Saturn's aspect (Saravali 22.36-41: obstruction)
Mercury's aspect gives learning but Saravali also notes gambling or a mean streak
Placement in a dusthana (6th, 8th, 12th); Braha (pp. 51-52) says a planet there is spoiled, the 6th being the mildest

With the Sun in Leo: Leo lagna (1st) respect, learning and a good start in life; Scorpio lagna (10th) fame and a high position; Aries lagna (5th) intelligence, faith and possible leadership; Gemini lagna (3rd) courage and a strong personality; Libra lagna (11th) wealth from many sources; Taurus lagna (4th) homes and property but less happiness from the mother.

planet_in_sign/sun/leo.phrasing_guidance: Present as strong leadership and self-belief; suggest channelling pride and temper constructively. Do not promise status.

planet_in_sign/sun/virgo.summary: The Sun in Virgo sits in Mercury's sign (neutral). Texts agree on skill in writing, painting, poetry, mathematics and music, with a gentle manner and a slighter build.

Gentle, soft-spoken manner
Service to elders, teachers or the divine
Analytical, detail-oriented approach

Saravali 22.42-43 names skill in repairing vehicles and in Vedic study

by_area.career: Writing, painting, poetry and mathematics (Brihat Jataka 18.2); expert writer, repairer of vehicles, Vedas, song and instruments (Saravali 22.42-43); linguist, poet and mathematician (Raman).
by_area.health: Saravali 22.42-43 notes a slight build and some weakness; treat as a traditional note, not a prediction.
by_area.spirituality: Serves gods and elders (Saravali 22.42-43); learned in religious lore (Raman).

strengtheners: Mercury's or Jupiter's aspect (Saravali 22.20-25: knowledge of many shastras, royal messenger, foreign travel; also a fierce, bewildered temper)
Upachaya placement (3rd, 6th, 10th, 11th), where Braha (pp. 17, 51) says malefics such as the Sun give excellent results
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mars's aspect (Saravali 22.20-25: loss and quarrels)
Moon's aspect (Saravali 22.20-25: trouble from kin or enemies)

planet_in_sign/sun/libra.summary: The Sun is debilitated in Libra (deepest fall at 10°), the sign of Venus, its enemy. Classical texts describe frustration, expenses, dependence on others and trade in metals or liquor; modern practice stresses that cancellation of debility is common and that the placement teaches cooperation over ego.
common_outcomes: Fluctuating confidence; difficulty asserting oneself
Tendency to work for or through others
Travel or residence away from home
Expenses and setbacks that require persistence
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 18.3: livelihood in distilling or selling liquor, or as a goldsmith; fond of travel; lowly work
Saravali 22.44-45: dealing in gold and metals, living abroad out of distress, displeasure of authorities
Phaladeepika 9.18 (general debility): fall from position, debts, menial work, distant travel

by_area.personality: Classical verses list harsh traits (Saravali 22.44-45); Raman HPA ch. XXII gives popular, frank and submissive yet arrogant and pompous. Braha ('1st House') says a fallen Sun in the 1st undermines confidence and self-esteem, while Frawley (p. 126) says a Sun in Libra whose debility is cancelled can give a strong, self-confident, expressive character.
by_area.career: Selling liquor or working as a goldsmith (Brihat Jataka 18.3); trade in gold and metals and doing others' work (Saravali 22.44-45); Raman: manufacturer of liquors.
by_area.finance: Saravali 22.44-45: frustration, losses and heavy expenditure.

Placement in the 10th, where the Sun has directional strength (Braha pp. 17, 60)

Saturn's aspect without other relief (Saravali 22.12-17: meanness, indolence, illness)

planet_in_sign/sun/libra.lagna_or_context_notes: Braha ('Planets in the Houses', pp. 79 ff.) reads the fallen Sun house by house. With the Sun in Libra: Libra lagna (1st) weak confidence and recognition; Leo lagna (3rd) strong but often unfulfilled desires; Cancer lagna (4th) unease and an unsettled home; Capricorn lagna (10th) a slow-to-settle career with many changes; Virgo lagna (2nd) money and family strain. Frawley (p. 126) adds that debility is much reduced in an angle from the lagna or Moon, the 10th most of all, so the Cancer, Aries, Capricorn and Libra lagna cases (4th, 7th, 10th, 1st) also carry that relief.

source_views.view: Debility can be cancelled (planet in an angle from lagna or Moon, sign lord exalted, an exalted planet in a sign the fallen planet rules); a Sun in Libra with debility cancelled can give a strong, self-confident, expressive character. Usually at least two cancelling factors are needed.

source_views.view: The fallen Sun in the 1st harms confidence and recognition; neechabhanga occurs when an exalted planet joins the fallen one, the sign lord is exalted, the sign lord is in a kendra from lagna or Moon, or the planet exalted in that sign is in such a kendra.

source_views.source: Andrew Foss, The Yoga of the Planets: Surya, the Sun, name 9 ('The imperishable')

planet_in_sign/sun/libra.disagreements: Classical sign verses are uniformly unfavourable, but Phaladeepika ch. 7, Braha and Frawley all say the debility can be cancelled, and Frawley says a cancelled Sun in Libra can be strong and self-confident. Commentators differ on whether 'lord of the exaltation sign' means Mars (lord of Aries) or Saturn (the planet exalted in Libra) (Phaladeepika 7.26 footnote); Braha lists both kinds of condition. BPHS treats all of Libra as debilitation, while Braha (p. 47) says that past 10 degrees the Sun is technically no longer fallen.
planet_in_sign/sun/libra.phrasing_guidance: Never call this 'bad' outright. Explain that debility is often cancelled and that the theme is building self-worth and learning cooperation. Do not repeat the texts' moral judgements or predict loss of father.

planet_in_sign/sun/scorpio.summary: The Sun in Scorpio is in Mars's sign, a friend. It gives intensity, boldness and a combative streak; classical texts lean harsh, describing a fierce, quarrelsome nature, skill with weapons and exposure to danger.

Can be combative or quick to quarrel
Skill with tools, weapons, chemicals or crisis work
Secretive or private approach

planet_in_sign/sun/scorpio.phrasing_guidance: Describe as courage and intensity best channelled into demanding, high-stakes work. Do not predict accidents, poisoning, or family loss; avoid moral labels.

planet_in_sign/sun/sagittarius.summary: The Sun in Sagittarius is in Jupiter's sign, a friend. Texts agree it gives respect from the wise, prosperity, learning and skill, with an honourable, dharmic outlook.

planet_in_sign/sun/capricorn.summary: The Sun in Capricorn is in Saturn's sign, an enemy. Texts are unfavourable: modest means, hard or menial work, family conflict and dependence on others. Modern readings emphasise slow, disciplined rise through effort.

by_area.relationships: The central area: classical texts warn of scandal and infidelity (Saravali 28.1-2; Brihat Jataka 18.14); loyalty and patience are growth areas.
by_area.family: Brihat Jataka warns of bringing disrepute on the family.

strengtheners: Saravali 28.25-30 (Aries/Scorpio group): Jupiter's aspect gives beautiful eyes, a charitable spouse, a handsome build and many children; Sun's aspect gives royal standing and learning despite losses through relationships
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a vargottama planet gives results like a planet in its own sign
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saravali 28.25-30: Moon's aspect gives fickleness, confinement, an unsuitable match and no children; Mars' aspect, loss of wealth, honour and happiness and menial work; Mercury's aspect, foolishness, profligacy and estrangement from relatives; Saturn's aspect, laziness, wandering and service to others
Sastri's note to Brihat Jataka 18.16: Venus is bad in the signs of malefics

James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (Sun and 'Combustion' sections): a planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and its significations and the houses it rules are spoiled

source_views.source: Saravali 28.1-2 (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Poor night vision, many faults, hostile, drawn to others' partners, wanders forests and hills, risk of confinement through relationships, harsh and unreliable, yet may lead an army or group.

source_views.source: Saravali 28.25-30, aspects on Venus in Aries/Scorpio (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Sun: losses and misery through women, yet royal standing and learning. Moon: confinement, fickle, unsuitable match, no children. Mars: without wealth, honour and happiness, menial work. Mercury: foolish, profligate, estranged, thievish. Jupiter: beautiful eyes, charitable spouse, handsome, many sons. Saturn: untidy, lazy, wandering, serves others.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.14 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Venus in a Mars sign: interest in others' spouses, loses wealth through flattery, brings disgrace on the family.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra ch. 3 (natural relationships)
source_views.view: Venus treats Mars as neutral, so Aries is a neutral sign.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.14 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed., p. 353)
source_views.view: Venus in a Mars sign: intrigues with others' wives, loses all wealth pleading on their behalf, a disgrace to the family. Sastri's note to 18.16: Venus is good for finance and material welfare in signs ruled by benefics and bad in signs of malefics and in its debilitation sign; it is good in Jupiter's signs; Venus in Makara or Kumbha may give handsomeness but not fortune.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer ('Sukra-Venus' section)
source_views.view: Mars and Jupiter are neutral to Venus.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (general rules: combustion, navamsa, house placements, dignities)
source_views.view: A planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and spoiled; a vargottama planet gives own-sign results, while a fallen planet that is vargottama is only worse off and a planet exalted in the birth chart but fallen in the navamsa gives very mixed results; a fallen planet is badly weakened unless well aspected; planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled.

planet_in_sign/venus/aries.disagreements: Both texts are largely adverse about relationships. Saravali uniquely allows leadership of a group or army. The two Brihat Jataka translations differ on how wealth is lost (flattery in Neely, pleading for others in Sastri).
planet_in_sign/venus/aries.phrasing_guidance: Describe passionate, spontaneous affection and a need for excitement. Never predict infidelity or scandal; frame classical warnings as the value of patience and loyalty. Avoid medical claims about eyesight.

planet_in_sign/venus/taurus.summary: Venus in Taurus (Vrishabha), its own earth sign, gives comfort, beauty, sensual refinement and prosperity: fine clothes, perfumes, land or livestock, generosity toward relatives and respected leadership. Malavya Yoga if in a kendra.
common_outcomes: Good looks, refined taste and enjoyment of comfort
Prosperity through land, agriculture, cattle, perfumes or fine goods
Generous; supports relatives
Learned in many fields and respected
rare_outcomes: Saravali 28.3-4: many partners and jewels (read as a rich social and romantic life)
Brihat Jataka 18.14 (own sign): wealth through own strength and intelligence, honoured by rulers, community leader, famous and fearless
Malavya Mahapurusha Yoga in a kendra (Phaladeepika 6.1, 6.3)

by_area.personality: Saravali 28.3-4: charitable, helps living beings, good appearance.
by_area.career: Saravali 28.3-4: agriculture and livelihood through cattle; a principal person. Brihat Jataka 18.14: powerful among his people, honoured by the ruler.
by_area.finance: Brihat Jataka 18.14: money by own exertion and intelligence. Saravali: gems, perfumes, garlands and fine clothes.
by_area.relationships: Saravali's 'many wives' is a period marker of wealth; Raman (Malavya) promises happiness from spouse and children when the yoga forms.
by_area.family: Supports relatives (Saravali).
by_area.spirituality: Raman (Malavya Yoga remarks): Malavya inclines to pleasure, with spiritual advancement in inverse ratio to comforts.

strengtheners: Own sign (Phaladeepika 3.18: 'confident'); Braha: Venus gives very good results in Taurus and Libra
Malavya Yoga in a kendra: strong body, resolute mind, wealth, good spouse and children, comforts, vehicles, fame, learning (Phaladeepika 6.1, 6.3; Raman no. 20)

Saravali 28.31-36 (Taurus/Libra group): Moon's aspect gives a good mother, wealth, respect and sons; Mercury's aspect gives charm, luck, wisdom and strength; Jupiter's aspect gives spouse, children, home and vehicles

James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a vargottama planet gives results like a planet in its own sign

James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (Sun and 'Combustion' sections): a planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and its significations and the houses it rules are spoiled
planet_in_sign/venus/taurus.lagna_or_context_notes: Malavya Yoga forms where Taurus is a kendra from the lagna (Phaladeepika 6.1, 6.3). Raman's table (Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 20) places it in the 1st for Taurus lagna, the 7th for Scorpio, the 10th for Leo and the 4th for Aquarius; he adds that unblemished Malavya is exceptional.

source_views.source: Saravali 28.3-4 (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Many partners and jewels, farming, perfumes, garlands and fine clothes, livelihood through cattle, generous, supports relatives, good-looking, learned in many fields, respected leader.

source_views.source: Saravali 28.31-36, aspects on Venus in Taurus/Libra (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Sun: excellent spouse and wealth, but dominated. Moon: good mother, wealth, respect. Mars: difficult spouse, loss through relationships. Mercury: splendid, lucky, wise. Jupiter: spouse, children, home, vehicles. Saturn: little happiness.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.14 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Venus in own sign: wealth by own strength and intelligence, honoured by rulers, leader of the community, famous, fearless.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.1, 6.3
source_views.view: Malavya Yoga definition and results.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.14 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed., p. 354)
source_views.view: Venus in own sign: earns money by own exertion and intelligence, honoured by the king, powerful among his people, famous and brave.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 20 Malavya Yoga (pp. 48-49)
source_views.view: Venus in a kendra in its own or exaltation sign: well-developed physique, strong-minded, wealthy, happy with spouse and children, vehicles, clean senses, renowned and learned. It inclines to pleasure and a materialistic outlook, spiritual advancement being in inverse ratio to comforts. Lagna table: Taurus, Libra, Pisces lagnas in the 1st; Aries, Scorpio, Virgo in the 7th; Gemini, Leo, Capricorn in the 10th; Sagittarius, Aquarius, Cancer in the 4th. Unblemished cases are exceptional.

source_views.source: Andrew Foss, The Yoga of the Planets: Venus, Shukra, name 9
source_views.view: Exalted Venus is not about being a great artist, as it can be when Venus is in its own sign, nor about wealth.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer ('Sukra-Venus' section)
source_views.view: Venus owns Taurus and Libra and gives very good results in those signs.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (general rules: combustion, navamsa, house placements, dignities)
source_views.view: A planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and spoiled; a vargottama planet gives own-sign results, while a fallen planet that is vargottama is only worse off and a planet exalted in the birth chart but fallen in the navamsa gives very mixed results; a fallen planet is badly weakened unless well aspected; planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled.

planet_in_sign/venus/taurus.disagreements: None substantial. Saravali's 'many wives' is a period-specific marker of wealth and is not echoed by Brihat Jataka.
planet_in_sign/venus/taurus.phrasing_guidance: Describe comfort, beauty and steady prosperity as supported tendencies. Do not suggest multiple marriages; Saravali's line reflects its era.

planet_in_sign/venus/gemini.summary: Venus in Gemini (Mithuna), the air sign of its friend Mercury, gives charm through words and arts: attractive, witty, skilled in writing, poetry, music and dance, with many friends and earnings through creative or communicative skills.
common_outcomes: Attractive and socially engaging
Skilled in writing, poetry or performing arts
Earns through music, dance or creative work
Many friends; loyal in friendship
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 18.15: performs official or administrative duties, wealthy and purposeful, skilled in the arts
Saravali 28.5-6: known for learning and scripture; honours the learned

by_area.personality: Saravali 28.5-6: beautiful, sensual, firm in friendship.
by_area.career: Saravali 28.5-6: skilful in writing and poetry, earns through music and dance. Brihat Jataka 18.15: does the work of a king (Sastri's example: a lawyer), skilled in the arts.
by_area.finance: Saravali: wealth through music and dance; Brihat Jataka 18.15: wealthy.
by_area.relationships: Saravali: dear to good people, many friends.
by_area.spirituality: Honours gods and learned people (Saravali).

strengtheners: Friendly sign (Phaladeepika 3.18; Braha lists Mercury as Venus' friend)

Saravali 28.37-42 (Gemini/Virgo group): Sun's aspect gives goodwill toward ruler, mother and spouse, learning and wealth; Moon's aspect gives beauty, comforts and luck; Mercury's aspect gives learning, wealth and leadership; Jupiter's aspect gives happiness, courage and a teaching role
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a vargottama planet gives results like a planet in its own sign
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saravali 28.37-42: Mars' aspect gives sensuality and loss of wealth through relationships; Saturn's aspect brings misery, insult, fickleness and envy

James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (Sun and 'Combustion' sections): a planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and its significations and the houses it rules are spoiled

source_views.view: Known for learning, attractive, sensual, skilled in writing and poetry, earns through music and dance, many friends, honours gods and the learned, steadfast friend.

source_views.source: Saravali 28.37-42, aspects on Venus in Gemini/Virgo (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Sun: favour from authority, learned, rich. Moon: beauty, luck, comforts. Mars: sensual, spends on relationships. Mercury: learned, wealthy, leader. Jupiter: happy, teacher. Saturn: unhappy, envious.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.15 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed., p. 355)
source_views.view: Venus in Gemini: does the work of a king (a lawyer, for instance), wealthy, skilled in the arts.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer ('Sukra-Venus' section)
source_views.view: The friends of Venus are Mercury and Saturn.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (general rules: combustion, navamsa, house placements, dignities)

planet_in_sign/venus/gemini.disagreements: Both texts agree on artistic skill. Brihat Jataka adds an official or administrative role that Saravali does not mention.
planet_in_sign/venus/gemini.phrasing_guidance: Describe a charming, artistic communicator. Avoid implying inconstancy in love; mention a need for mental connection instead.

planet_in_sign/venus/cancer.summary: Venus in Cancer (Karka), the Moon's water sign and an enemy's sign for Venus, gives emotional, gentle and nurturing affection with comfort and good character, but classical texts warn of emotional turbulence, indulgence and recurring domestic difficulties.
common_outcomes: Gentle, wise, virtuous and good-looking
Gets the comforts desired
Strong emotional needs in relationships
Recurring family or domestic difficulties
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 18.16: two marriages, timidity and sorrow through desire
Saravali mentions trouble through relationships and drink

by_area.personality: Saravali 28.7-8: wise, virtuous, soft and just. Brihat Jataka 18.16 (Sastri): timid but very arrogant.
by_area.career: Saravali 28.7-8: chief among men.
by_area.finance: Saravali: desired happiness and wealth. Brihat Jataka 18.16 (Sastri): seeks monetary help from others.
by_area.relationships: Classical texts warn of turbulence: troubles through women (Saravali) and, in Brihat Jataka, two marriages.
by_area.family: Recurring family difficulties (Saravali).

strengtheners: Saravali 28.43-48: Sun's aspect gives a dutiful spouse of good family and wealth; Moon's aspect gives happiness, children and beauty; Mars' aspect gives artistic skill, wealth and fortune; Jupiter's aspect gives servants, children, friends and favour from authorities
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a vargottama planet gives results like a planet in its own sign
weakeners_or_cancellations: Enemy's sign (Phaladeepika 3.19: 'distressed'); Braha: the Moon is Venus' enemy and Venus is not welcomed in its sign
Saravali 28.43-48: Saturn's aspect brings domination by partner, poverty and unhappiness; Mercury's aspect, troubles through relatives and wandering

James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (Sun and 'Combustion' sections): a planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and its significations and the houses it rules are spoiled

source_views.view: Wise, virtuous, learned, strong and gentle, gets desired comforts, handsome and just, troubled by relationships and drink, recurring family difficulties.

source_views.source: Saravali 28.43-48, aspects on Venus in Cancer (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Sun: devoted spouse, wealthy. Moon: happy, children. Mars: artistic, fortunate. Mercury: learned spouse, family troubles. Jupiter: servants, children, friends, favour. Saturn: dominated by partner, poor, unhappy.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.16 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Venus in the Moon's sign: two spouses, desirous, timid, intense desire and sorrow.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.16 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed., p. 356)
source_views.view: Venus in Cancer: two wives, solicits monetary help from others, timid but very arrogant, suffers great misery.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer ('Sukra-Venus' section)
source_views.view: The Sun and Moon are Venus' enemies and it is not welcomed in their signs.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (general rules: combustion, navamsa, house placements, dignities)
source_views.view: A planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and spoiled; a vargottama planet gives own-sign results, while a fallen planet that is vargottama is only worse off and a planet exalted in the birth chart but fallen in the navamsa gives very mixed results; a fallen planet is badly weakened unless well aspected; planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled.

planet_in_sign/venus/cancer.disagreements: Saravali gives a fairly positive character picture with domestic difficulties; Brihat Jataka is more negative in both translations, focusing on two marriages, timidity and misery.
planet_in_sign/venus/cancer.phrasing_guidance: Describe a warm, nurturing heart with strong emotional needs. Never predict divorce or remarriage; frame as the importance of emotional security. Avoid any statement about drinking.

planet_in_sign/venus/leo.summary: Venus in Leo (Simha), the Sun's fire sign and an enemy's sign for Venus, gives proud, generous and dramatic affection: comfortable means, respect for elders and gains through partners, but classical texts note inner dissatisfaction and few children.
common_outcomes: Comfortable means; gains through spouse or women
Loved by relatives; helps others
Respectful toward teachers and elders
Some dissatisfaction despite comforts
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 18.16: a distinguished young spouse and few children
Saravali mentions reduced vigour and lack of fine judgement

by_area.personality: Saravali 28.9-10: helps others; lacks fine judgement; unhappy despite comforts.
by_area.finance: Comfortable; money through women or the spouse (Brihat Jataka 18.16).
by_area.relationships: Saravali: respects women. Brihat Jataka 18.16: a beautiful (Sastri) or distinguished young (Neely) spouse.
by_area.family: Loved by relatives (Saravali); Brihat Jataka mentions few children (low weight).
by_area.spirituality: Honours Brahmins, elders and teachers (Saravali).

strengtheners: Saravali 28.49-54: Mars' aspect gives royal standing, fame and prosperity; Jupiter's aspect gives vehicles, wealth, servants and a minister's post; Saturn's aspect gives fame and wealth (with an unconventional marriage)
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a vargottama planet gives results like a planet in its own sign
weakeners_or_cancellations: Enemy's sign (Phaladeepika 3.19); Braha: Venus is not welcomed in the Sun's sign
Saravali 28.49-54: Moon's aspect gives emotional unsteadiness and misery through women; Mercury's aspect gives stinginess and cunning

James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (Sun and 'Combustion' sections): a planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and its significations and the houses it rules are spoiled

planet_in_sign/venus/leo.disagreements: Both texts mention gains through partners and comfort; Saravali adds inner dissatisfaction, Brihat Jataka adds few children. The translations differ on the spouse: 'beautiful' (Sastri) versus 'distinguished young' (Neely).
planet_in_sign/venus/leo.phrasing_guidance: Describe generous, dignified affection and the value of finding contentment beyond status. Do not predict few children.

planet_in_sign/venus/virgo.summary: Venus in Virgo (Kanya) is debilitated, deepest at 27 degrees: pleasure, romance and aesthetic ease are filtered through analysis and criticism. Classical texts describe a gentle, skilled, helpful person with modest or service-oriented work and mixed relationship results; neecha bhanga is frequent.
common_outcomes: Gentle, skilled, helpful and sweet-spoken (Saravali)
Love shown through service and practical care (astromedha)
Earnings from several sources (Saravali)
Exacting standards in relationships (astromedha)
rare_outcomes: Saravali 28.11-12: more daughters than sons; visits shrines; speaks well in assemblies
Brihat Jataka 18.15: very lowly work (Neely) or base acts (Sastri)
With cancellation, powerful results (Foss)

by_area.personality: Saravali 28.11-12: soft, skilful, helpful, sweet-spoken, not very discriminating. astromedha: tension between enjoying and critiquing.
by_area.career: Saravali 28.11-12: a scholar in an assembly; earns from several sources. Brihat Jataka 18.15: modest or lowly work.
by_area.finance: Saravali: earns money through several sources.
by_area.relationships: Saravali 28.11-12: low company, little happiness and pleasure. Braha: Venus in Virgo often brings overindulgence in sensual pleasures. Foss: desire may be held back by a search for purity. astromedha: risk of over-criticising partners.
by_area.family: Saravali mentions more daughters (low weight).
by_area.spirituality: Pilgrimage and practical devotion (Saravali). Foss: Virgo seeks the sacred and the pure within the impure.

strengtheners: Neecha bhanga (Phaladeepika 7.26-30): Mercury (lord of Virgo) or Jupiter (lord of Pisces, Venus' exaltation sign) in a kendra from the lagna or Moon; the two in mutual kendras; or Venus aspected by Mercury (7.28)
Raman (no. 250) reads the cancelling planet as the one exalted in Virgo, i.e. Mercury, in a kendra from the lagna or Moon
Foss: Venus in Virgo is not defiled and can give powerful results if well placed, certainly if with Mercury or if Mercury or Jupiter is strongly placed in an angle

Saravali 28.37-42 (Gemini/Virgo group): Sun's aspect gives favour from authority and wealth; Moon's aspect gives beauty and luck; Mercury's aspect gives learning, wealth and leadership; Jupiter's aspect gives happiness and a teaching role
weakeners_or_cancellations: Phaladeepika 3.19: a debilitated planet is 'greatly afraid'; Braha: Virgo is Venus' worst sign
Deepest debility at 27 degrees Virgo (BPHS 3.50)
James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (navamsa section): a debilitated planet that is also vargottama is only worse off
Saravali 28.37-42: Saturn's aspect brings misery and envy; Mars' aspect, loss of wealth through relationships

James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (Sun and 'Combustion' sections): a planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and its significations and the houses it rules are spoiled
planet_in_sign/venus/virgo.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman (Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 250) reckons neecha bhanga from both the lagna and the Moon, so check kendras from both before giving a weak reading.

source_views.source: Saravali 28.11-12 (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Not very discerning but gentle, skilled, helpful and sweet-spoken, earns from several sources, questionable company, stingy, more daughters than sons, visits shrines, speaks well in assemblies.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.15 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Venus in Virgo: takes on very lowly work.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 3.49-50
source_views.view: Venus is exalted in Pisces and debilitated in the seventh sign, Virgo, at the same degree. The degree word-code is commonly read as 27.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 7.26-30
source_views.view: Neecha bhanga raja yoga conditions.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.15 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed., p. 355)
source_views.view: Venus in Virgo: the person will do base acts.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 250 Neechabhanga Raja Yoga (pp. 242-244)
source_views.view: The lord of the debilitation sign, or the planet exalted there, in a kendra from the lagna or Moon cancels debility. Raman reads 'thaduchchanatha' as the planet exalted in that sign (Mercury, for Venus in Virgo) and notes the reading is disputed.

source_views.source: Andrew Foss, The Yoga of the Planets: Venus, Shukra, name 2
source_views.view: Venus is debilitated in Virgo, whose agenda is to seek the sacred and the pure within the impure; desire may be rejected as unsuited to that quest, so Venus can seem weak, but it is not defiled and can give powerful results if well placed, certainly if with Mercury or if Mercury or Jupiter is strong in an angle.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer ('Sukra-Venus' section)
source_views.view: Venus operates worst in Virgo, its fallen sign; in Virgo it often brings overindulgence in sex or sensual pleasures.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (general rules: combustion, navamsa, house placements, dignities)
source_views.view: A planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and spoiled; a vargottama planet gives own-sign results, while a fallen planet that is vargottama is only worse off and a planet exalted in the birth chart but fallen in the navamsa gives very mixed results; a fallen planet is badly weakened unless well aspected; planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled.

planet_in_sign/venus/virgo.disagreements: Saravali's verse is mixed (gentle and skilled but stingy); Brihat Jataka gives only a terse negative line. Modern authors read the debility in opposite ways: Braha says Virgo Venus tends to overindulgence, while Foss and astromedha describe desire held back by purity or criticism. On cancellation, Phaladeepika uses kendra placement from lagna/Moon or aspect; Foss names Mercury conjunct Venus. BPHS and Braha make Mercury and Venus mutual friends.
planet_in_sign/venus/virgo.phrasing_guidance: Never say the person will be unhappy in love or do menial work. Describe a caring, practical and discerning way of loving, and suggest self-acceptance and balance as growth areas. Always check neecha bhanga before giving a weak reading.

planet_in_sign/venus/libra.summary: Venus in Libra (Tula) is in its moolatrikona (0-15 degrees) and own sign (15-30 degrees): a strong, balanced Venus giving refinement, fairness, wealth earned through effort, good dress, travel and respect; Malavya Yoga if in a kendra.
common_outcomes: Well dressed, refined and socially graceful
