source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer ('Sukra-Venus' section)
source_views.view: Venus operates best in Pisces, its exaltation sign.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (general rules: combustion, navamsa, house placements, dignities)
source_views.view: A planet within about 8 degrees of the Sun is combust and spoiled; a vargottama planet gives own-sign results, while a fallen planet that is vargottama is only worse off and a planet exalted in the birth chart but fallen in the navamsa gives very mixed results; a fallen planet is badly weakened unless well aspected; planets in kendras are powerful, in trikonas enhanced, in the 6th, 8th or 12th spoiled.

planet_in_sign/venus/pisces.disagreements: None on dignity. Emphasis differs: Saravali and Brihat Jataka stress wealth, honour and learning, while Foss says exalted Venus is not about wealth or artistry but devotion. The 27-degree exaltation point rests on reading the BPHS word-code 'bhamita' as 27. Saravali 28.55-60 in Santhanam's translation gives only five aspect results (Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Saturn); it has no statement for Jupiter's aspect on Venus in Sagittarius or Pisces.
planet_in_sign/venus/pisces.phrasing_guidance: Describe refined, generous and devotional love and good fortune as supported tendencies, still dependent on house, aspects and dasha. Avoid absolute promises of wealth or fame.

lord_in_house/1/1.summary: The lagna lord in its own house (always its own sign) makes the self strong and self-directed: good physical vitality, cleverness and independence, with a restless or changeable streak.
common_outcomes: strong sense of identity and personal initiative
good bodily comfort and resilience
clever, capable of shaping own circumstances
some fickleness or restlessness of mind
rare_outcomes: BPHS (traditional view) mentions more than one marriage or relationships outside marriage; this is a text-specific line, not a general rule

by_area.personality: Self-reliant and independent; lives by own exertion; clever and vigorous but changeable (BPHS 24.1; Raman HTJH I; Rath 4.4.1: strong, brave, intelligent, fickle-minded).
by_area.career: Rises by own effort; when the lagna lord is well placed the person becomes known in own community and country (Raman HTJH I).
by_area.finance: Charak lists ownership of, and benefit from, landed property.
by_area.health: Sound health and long life (Charak); a strong lagna lord in a kendra supports bodily well-being (BPHS 12.1). Do not make medical claims.
by_area.relationships: BPHS 24.1, Raman ('one married and another illegal'), Charak and Rath all repeat a traditional line about two marriages or outside ties; treat it as a sign of an independent streak to be checked against the 7th house and Venus.

strengtheners: lagna lord is automatically in own sign here; for Virgo lagna Mercury is also exalted; strong shadbala and good navamsa (own/exalted/friendly D9) amplify results
benefic aspects or conjunctions on the lagna (BPHS 12.4)
lagna lord a natural benefic (Mercury, Jupiter, Venus) in a kendra: BPHS 12.5 promises long life, wealth, intelligence and royal favour
lagna lord in a movable sign aspected by benefics: fame and comforts (BPHS 12.6)
lords of the 1st, 2nd and 11th each in their own house form a dhana yoga (Bhavartha Ratnakara II, Dhana yogas st. 7)
well disposed in the lagna: fame in own community and country (Raman HTJH I)
weakeners_or_cancellations: combustion by the Sun or association with malefics/dusthana lords reduces the good effect (BPHS 12.1-2)
papakartari (hemmed between malefics) around the lagna (Phaladeepika 15.6)
debilitated or weak in navamsa
lord_in_house/1/1.lagna_or_context_notes: The lagna lord is treated as auspicious for its lagna even when a natural malefic (Phaladeepika 15.10; BPHS 34; Laghu Parashari sloka 6 commentary: the lagna lord is auspicious under all conditions). For Aries and Libra lagna the lagna lord also owns the 8th; Laghu Parashari sloka 9 says the 8th-lord blemish is removed when that planet is also the lagna lord, and O.P. Verma's commentary adds that this holds when it sits in the lagna or the 8th, which is the case here. Lagna lord placed in its own house gives that house's well-being (Phaladeepika 15.9).

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.1 (Sanskrit with English, enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Bodily comfort, strength, intelligence, but fickle; two wives or relations with others possible.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.1 (English, Santhanam-based text on archive.org)
source_views.view: Physical well-being and prowess; clever but inconstant; two wives or affairs.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 12.1, 12.5-6 (Tanu Bhava)
source_views.view: Lagna lord in kendra/kona gives bodily happiness; benefic lagna lord in kendra gives long life, wealth, intellect, royal favour.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 15.9-10 (Mantreswara)
source_views.view: The bhava occupied by the lagna lord flourishes; even a malefic lagna lord promotes the house it occupies.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. IV 'Results of Lord of First House Occupying Different Houses' (pp. 21-22)
source_views.view: Lives by own exertion, independent spirit; two wives or one married and another illicit. Well disposed: famous in own community and country. Results must be weighed by the lord's strength and aspects.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Lagna lord (pp. 230-231)
source_views.view: Sound health, long-lived, valorous, thoughtful, very fickle; two wives, adulterous; owns and benefits from landed property.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 4.4 'Placement of Ascendant Lord' 4.4.1 (p. 34)
source_views.view: Strong, fickle-minded, brave, intelligent; two or more wives; a mahapurusha (great person).

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara of Ramanujacharya (tr. B.V. Raman), ch. II Dhana yogas st. 7
source_views.view: Dhana yoga if the lords of the 11th, 1st and 2nd are in their respective houses.

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari (Jataka Chandrika), tr. with commentary by O.P. Verma, slokas 6 and 9 with notes
source_views.view: Trikona lords (lagna included per Sita Ram Jha) are auspicious and the lagna lord is auspicious under all conditions; an 8th lord who also owns the lagna is auspicious, especially when placed in the lagna or the 8th.

lord_in_house/1/1.disagreements: All sources agree on strength and independence. BPHS, Raman, Charak and Rath all repeat the two-marriages line; it is not echoed in the general bhava rules, and Raman stresses that such combinations are general and must be weighed by the lord's strength and aspects.
lord_in_house/1/1.phrasing_guidance: Emphasise self-reliance, vitality and initiative; mention restlessness as something to channel. Do not predict multiple marriages or infidelity; at most say traditional texts link this to a strong independent streak in relationships.

lord_in_house/1/2.summary: The self is invested in wealth, family and speech: the person works to build resources and values, and tends to be cultured, principled and contented.
common_outcomes: gains wealth through own effort
learned, well-spoken and principled
close identification with family and its values
contentment and good conduct
rare_outcomes: youthful appearance (ELS rendering of BPHS 24.2)
BPHS traditional line mentioning more than one wife or many spouses
Raman: teased or worried by enemies; prominent eyes
Rath 4.4.2: happiness from children hard to obtain (traditional view)

by_area.personality: Cultured, dutiful, content and honourable (BPHS 24.2); good character, generous-hearted, ambitious and far-sighted when well placed (Raman HTJH I); sober and self-respecting (Charak).
by_area.finance: More gains (Raman HTJH I); learned and prosperous (Charak; Rath 4.4.2: scholarly, wealthy); the lagna lord nourishes the house of wealth (Phaladeepika 15.9).
by_area.relationships: BPHS 24.2 (Santhanam rendering) and Charak mention several spouses; treat as text-specific.
by_area.family: Gladly discharges duties to kith and kin when the lord is well disposed (Raman HTJH I).
by_area.spirituality: Religious-minded (BPHS 24.2 Santhanam rendering; Charak; Rath 4.4.2).

strengtheners: lagna lord in own sign in the 2nd (Capricorn lagna: Saturn in Aquarius) or a friendly sign
Jupiter or Venus aspecting or joining
link with the 11th lord (BPHS 13.4 wealth yoga logic)
weakeners_or_cancellations: malefic affliction to the 2nd house can sharpen speech (BPHS 13.13 for afflicted 2nd)
debilitation (Sagittarius lagna: Jupiter in Capricorn) or combustion
lord_in_house/1/2.lagna_or_context_notes: For Capricorn lagna Saturn owns both the 1st and 2nd and sits in its own sign Aquarius; Bhavartha Ratnakara (II, Dhana st. 7) counts lords of the 1st, 2nd and 11th in their own houses as a dhana yoga, which this placement partly meets.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.2 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Youthful look, gains, learned, content, good conduct, honourable, good spouses.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.2 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Earns well, learned, religious, honourable; many wives.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 15.9 (Mantreswara)
source_views.view: The house the lagna lord occupies prospers.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. IV 'Results of Lord of First House Occupying Different Houses' (pp. 21-22)
source_views.view: More gains, worried by enemies, good character, respectable and generous. Well disposed: discharges duties to kith and kin, ambitious, prominent eyes, forethought.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Lagna lord (pp. 230-231)
source_views.view: Learned, prosperous, religious, long-lived, sober, self-respecting; several wives; many virtues; earns from land and horses.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 4.4 'Placement of Ascendant Lord' 4.4.2 (p. 34)
source_views.view: Scholarly, wealthy, happy, religious, honourable and passionate; progenic bliss hard to obtain.

lord_in_house/1/2.disagreements: Renderings differ slightly ('good spouses' vs 'many wives'; Charak also 'several wives'). Rath adds that children are hard to obtain, a line not in BPHS 24.2 as rendered here or in Raman.
lord_in_house/1/2.phrasing_guidance: Frame as an orientation toward building resources and living by family values. Avoid any claims about number of marriages.

lord_in_house/1/3.summary: The self expresses itself through courage, initiative and communication: brave, enterprising and self-made, with siblings and short ventures prominent.
common_outcomes: lion-like courage and willingness to take risks
prosperity and honour won by personal effort
intelligent and content
help from, and rise through, siblings (Raman, Charak, Rath)
rare_outcomes: BPHS traditional line: two wives
Raman: fame as a musician or mathematician when well disposed

by_area.personality: Bold and enterprising with lion-like courage (BPHS 24.3; Charak); Rath 6.5: dynamic, enterprising, bold and fortunate, as the lord aspects the 9th from here.
by_area.career: When the lagna lord is well disposed, rise in life comes through brothers, and the person may become known as a musician or mathematician depending on the sign and planets involved (Raman HTJH I).
by_area.finance: Prosperous (BPHS 24.3; Charak; Rath 4.4.3: wealthy, fortunate).
by_area.health: Rath 6.5: the Martian influence of the 3rd gives a robust physique.
by_area.relationships: BPHS 24.3, Raman and Charak repeat a two-marriages line; check the 7th house before saying anything.
by_area.family: Brothers are helpful (Rath 4.4.3); blessed with brothers and relatives (Charak); rise through brothers (Raman).

strengtheners: Mars connection or strong lagna lord: upachaya placements improve with malefic strength (Phaladeepika 15.7: strong malefics in 3/6/11 support)
exaltation: Scorpio lagna, Mars in Capricorn
benefic aspect on the 3rd; good D9 dignity
weakeners_or_cancellations: debilitation: Leo lagna (Sun in Libra) and Aquarius lagna (Saturn in Aries)
the 3rd is a mildly malefic (trishadaya) house; association with the 3rd lord's malefic role may bring restlessness
affliction can make courage turn into rashness or conflicts with siblings
lord_in_house/1/3.lagna_or_context_notes: Rath (Crux 6.5) reads the Martian influence of the 3rd as good for the lagna lord: robust physique and success in contests, plus fortune through its aspect on the 9th. Phaladeepika 15.7 adds that strong malefics in the 3rd, 6th or 11th from a bhava support it.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.3 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Brave as a lion, prosperous, honoured, intelligent, content; two wives.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.3 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Lion-like courage, wealth, honour, intelligence, happiness; two wives.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 15.7 (Mantreswara)
source_views.view: Strong malefics in the 3rd, 6th or 11th from a bhava support it during their periods.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. IV 'Results of Lord of First House Occupying Different Houses' (pp. 21-22)
source_views.view: Highly courageous, fortunate, respectable, two wives, intelligent, happy. Well disposed: rise through brothers; may become famous as a musician or mathematician.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Lagna lord (pp. 230-231)
source_views.view: Very courageous like a lion, prosperous, wise, self-respecting, two wives, blessed with brothers and relatives.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 4.4 'Placement of Ascendant Lord' 4.4.3 (p. 34)
source_views.view: Courageous, wealthy, honourable, fortunate, intelligent, happy, passionate; brothers helpful.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 6.4-6.5 (third lord; lords in the third) (pp. 65-66)
source_views.view: With the lagna lord in the 3rd the native is dynamic, enterprising, bold and fortunate (it aspects the 9th); the Martian influence gives a robust physique and success in battles.

lord_in_house/1/3.disagreements: Classical and modern sources agree on courage and self-effort. The two-marriages line appears in BPHS, Raman and Charak but not in Rath.
lord_in_house/1/3.phrasing_guidance: Present as courage and self-made success. Mention the 'two wives' line only as an old textual statement if asked, never as a prediction.

lord_in_house/1/4.summary: The self is rooted in home, mother and inner contentment: the person enjoys parental support, comforts and an attractive, pleasant nature.
common_outcomes: happiness from parents, especially mother
comforts of home, property or vehicles
pleasant, attractive, good-natured
property gained through the mother's side when well placed (Raman)
rare_outcomes: BPHS: many siblings (brothers)
BPHS: a pleasure-loving or sensual temperament

by_area.personality: Gentle, appealing, virtuous but fond of pleasures (BPHS 24.4); materialistic, well built, fair-looking and well-behaved (Raman HTJH I).
by_area.finance: If well disposed, considerable landed property, especially through maternal sources; rich, happy, famous, with many conveyances (Raman HTJH I).
by_area.health: Kendra placement of the lagna lord supports bodily comfort (BPHS 12.1); Charak adds long life and a small appetite.
by_area.family: Happiness from parents and many brothers (BPHS 24.4; Raman); devoted to mother and father (Charak); parental happiness assured (Rath 4.4.4).

strengtheners: lagna lord in own sign in the 4th (Gemini lagna: Mercury in Virgo, also exalted; Sagittarius lagna: Jupiter in Pisces)
lagna lord in the 4th aspected by benefics gives complete domestic happiness (BPHS 15.2)
strong Moon (karaka for mother)
exchange of the 1st and 4th lords gives Bhagyavahana yoga: general fortune and vehicles (Bhavartha Ratnakara IV st. 13)
weakeners_or_cancellations: malefic affliction to the 4th or Moon reduces domestic peace
debilitation: Aries lagna (Mars in Cancer) and Capricorn lagna (Saturn in Aries); neecha-bhanga rules may modify
combustion
lord_in_house/1/4.lagna_or_context_notes: For Aries lagna (Mars in Cancer) and Capricorn lagna (Saturn in Aries) the lagna lord is debilitated in the 4th, so results are mixed unless cancellation applies. For Gemini and Sagittarius lagna, the lagna lord also owns the 4th, giving a strong own-sign placement.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.4 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Parental comforts, many siblings, sensual, virtuous, charming.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.4 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Paternal and maternal happiness, several brothers, lustful yet virtuous and charming.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 15.2 (Bandhu Bhava)
source_views.view: Lagna lord (or 4th lord) in the 4th with benefic aspect gives full domestic happiness.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. IV 'Results of Lord of First House Occupying Different Houses' (pp. 21-22)
source_views.view: Happiness from parents, many brothers, materialistic, well built, fair, well behaved. Favourably disposed: considerable landed property especially through maternal sources, rich, famous, many conveyances.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Lagna lord (pp. 230-231)
source_views.view: Comforts from mother, several brothers, sensuous, virtuous, good-looking, long-lived, devoted to parents, small appetite.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 4.4 'Placement of Ascendant Lord' 4.4.4 (p. 34)
source_views.view: Parental happiness assured; siblings, properties, virtues and charm; works with missionary zeal.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara of Ramanujacharya (tr. B.V. Raman), ch. IV st. 13
source_views.view: Bhagyavahana yoga (fortune and conveyances) when the lords of the lagna and the 4th exchange houses.

lord_in_house/1/4.disagreements: Sources agree. The 'many siblings' line (BPHS, Raman, Charak) is not explained by house logic and is treated as text-specific.
lord_in_house/1/4.phrasing_guidance: Describe a home-centred, comfort-seeking, family-supported nature. Avoid predicting number of siblings.

lord_in_house/1/5.summary: A kendra-trikona link: the self joins intelligence, creativity and merit. The person is respected and favoured by authorities but can be proud or quick-tempered; children are a focus with some traditional cautions.
common_outcomes: respected and honoured
favour of superiors, rulers or government
service to or work under others (Raman, Rath)
pride and a quick temper
rare_outcomes: BPHS traditional line: moderate happiness from children and difficulty concerning the first child; state only as a traditional view

by_area.personality: Honourable, proud, short-tempered (BPHS 24.5; Charak; Rath 4.4.5); Raman adds subservient, serving others.
by_area.career: If fortified, in the good graces of rulers or political parties and likely to enter trade or diplomatic service (Raman HTJH I); Rath: a favourite of rulers who still tends to serve others.
by_area.family: BPHS 24.5, Raman, Charak and Rath all carry a traditional caution about the first child and modest happiness from children; state only as an old view.
by_area.spirituality: If fortified, propitiates deities suited to the 5th lord (Raman HTJH I); given to virtuous deeds (Charak).

strengtheners: exaltation: Pisces lagna, Jupiter in Cancer
Phaladeepika 15.10 example: Mars as lagna lord in the 5th (Leo for Aries, Pisces for Scorpio) aspected by a benefic brings children soon
Jupiter (karaka of children) strong; benefic aspect on the 5th
weakeners_or_cancellations: malefic affliction to the 5th or Jupiter is where the BPHS child caution becomes relevant
debilitation: Cancer lagna (Moon in Scorpio) and Taurus lagna (Venus in Virgo); combustion
lord_in_house/1/5.lagna_or_context_notes: Phaladeepika 15.10 gives a direct example: Mars as lagna lord in the 5th (Leo for Aries, Pisces for Scorpio) with benefic aspect promises children early, which softens the BPHS caution. The lagna lord in a kona falls under BPHS 12.1 (bodily happiness).

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.5 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Moderate happiness from children, first child lost; honourable, angry, dear to rulers.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.5 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Mediocre progenic happiness, loses first child; honoured, given to anger, dear to the king.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 15.10 (Mantreswara)
source_views.view: A malefic lagna lord still promotes the house it occupies; Mars as lagna lord in the 5th aspected by a benefic gives sons quickly.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. IV 'Results of Lord of First House Occupying Different Houses' (pp. 21-22)
source_views.view: First child does not survive, little happiness from children, short-tempered, subservient, serving others. Fortified: favour of rulers or political parties, trade or diplomatic service, worship suited to the 5th lord.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Lagna lord (pp. 230-231)
source_views.view: Easily angered, proud, honoured by the ruler; ordinary comfort from children, first-born may not survive; long-lived, virtuous deeds.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 4.4 'Placement of Ascendant Lord' 4.4.5 (p. 34)
source_views.view: Progenic bliss not assured, first child could be lost; honourable, friendly, short-tempered, favourite of rulers but tends to serve others.

lord_in_house/1/5.disagreements: BPHS, Raman, Charak and Rath all give a caution about the first child; Phaladeepika's rule that the lagna lord promotes the house it occupies (with its 5th-house example) points the other way. Read the 5th house, its lord and Jupiter before saying anything about children.
lord_in_house/1/5.phrasing_guidance: Stress intelligence, creativity and recognition. Never predict loss of a child; if asked about the classical line, say older texts gave a caution about children which modern practice checks against many other factors.

lord_in_house/1/6.summary: The self is placed in the house of obstacles, service and competition: life involves effort against rivals, work and health routines; outcomes depend heavily on whether benefics support the lord.
common_outcomes: life shaped by work, duty and overcoming opponents
less physical ease; needs good routines
competitive strength if the lord is strong
military, medical or health-service careers when fortified (Raman)
debts that clear in time (Raman)
rare_outcomes: BPHS: trouble from enemies when the lord is with malefics and lacks benefic aspect
Rath 4.4.6: traditional line about early loss of spouse; never predict

by_area.personality: Intelligent and courageous (Rath 4.4.6).
by_area.career: When fortified the person may join the army and rise to command, or head medical or health services, or become an expert physician or surgeon (Raman HTJH I).
by_area.finance: Debts that are cleared in the lagna lord's dasa (Raman HTJH I); frugal and rich, earns from lands (Charak); Rath: debts, but with benefic aspect or in the lagna lord's period destroys enemies and gains wealth and status.
by_area.health: Classical texts say bodily comfort is reduced (BPHS 24.6, 12.1); Charak gives good health unless afflicted. Do not predict illness.

strengtheners: lagna lord in own sign in the 6th (Taurus lagna: Venus in Libra; Scorpio lagna: Mars in Aries) - the lord owns the 6th too, so results are much better
exaltation: Libra lagna, Venus in Pisces
benefic aspect on the lord or the 6th (BPHS 24.6 conditions harm on its absence)
strong lagna lord: Phaladeepika 15.9 says the injury is slight when the lord is strong
weakeners_or_cancellations: malefic conjunction with no benefic aspect (BPHS 24.6)
debilitation, combustion or weak navamsa
Phaladeepika 15.5: a bhava lord in a dusthana harms the bhava
lord_in_house/1/6.lagna_or_context_notes: For Taurus and Scorpio lagna the lagna lord owns the 6th and sits in its own sign, and lagna ownership predominates (Phaladeepika 15.10).

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.6 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Lack of bodily comfort; if malefics afflict without benefic aspect, enemies trouble the native.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 12.1 (Tanu Bhava)
source_views.view: Lagna lord with malefics in the 6th, 8th or 12th reduces bodily happiness.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 15.5, 15.9 (Mantreswara)
source_views.view: A lord in a dusthana injures its house; harm is slight if the lord is strong, severe if weak.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. IV 'Results of Lord of First House Occupying Different Houses' (pp. 21-22)
source_views.view: As for the 3rd plus debts, liquidated in the lagna lord's dasa. Fortified: army commander, or head of medical/health services, or expert physician or surgeon.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Lagna lord (pp. 230-231)
source_views.view: Good health, destroys opponents, frugal and rich, earns from lands; if afflicted, poor health and trouble from enemies.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 4.4 'Placement of Ascendant Lord' 4.4.6 (p. 34)
source_views.view: Debts and ill health, troubled by enemies; intelligent and courageous; with benefic aspect or in the lagna lord's period destroys enemies and gains wealth and royal status; early loss of spouse indicated.

lord_in_house/1/6.disagreements: BPHS is cautionary (reduced bodily comfort, enemies). Charak gives good health and victory over opponents unless afflicted, and Raman and Rath give strong positive results when the lord is fortified or benefic-aspected. All views depend on strength.
lord_in_house/1/6.phrasing_guidance: Speak of challenges, service and resilience rather than illness or enmity as fate. Suggest healthy routines without making medical predictions.

lord_in_house/1/7.summary: The self faces the partner and the public: relationships, partnerships and dealings with others define life. BPHS gives sharply split results depending on whether the lord is malefic or benefic.
common_outcomes: life strongly oriented toward spouse, partners and the public
much travel or time spent abroad (Raman, Charak)
results swing sharply with the lagna lord's strength (Rath, Raman)
rare_outcomes: BPHS (malefic lagna lord): a traditional line about the spouse's longevity; state only as an old view, never predict
BPHS (benefic lagna lord): wandering, poverty or detachment, or alternatively becoming a ruler
Raman: if well disposed, a licentious life abroad, or being 'a puppet in the hands of' parents-in-law

by_area.career: Much travelling; if well disposed, spends most of the time in foreign countries (Raman HTJH I); Charak (malefic lagna lord): wanders in foreign lands.
by_area.finance: Rich or poor depending on other factors (Raman HTJH I); Rath 4.4.7: if the lord is strong, great wealth and prosperity.
by_area.relationships: Marriage is central and sensitive. BPHS, Raman and Rath carry traditional lines about the spouse's longevity or more than one marriage; Charak instead gives a brilliant, good-looking, good-natured spouse, with loss of spouse only for a malefic lagna lord; Raman adds possible dependence on parents-in-law. Never predict these.
by_area.spirituality: Detachment or ascetic leanings later in life (Raman HTJH I; BPHS 24.7 'virakta'); Rath: may become an ascetic or nomad unless the lord is strong.

strengtheners: lagna lord a strong natural benefic with good D9 (no lagna lord is exalted in the 7th)
benefic aspects on the 7th
BPHS 24.7: a benefic lord can even make one a ruler
Rath 4.4.7: a strong lagna lord here gives great wealth and prosperity
Rath (Crux, chart 15): neecha-bhanga in the lagna lord's company in the 7th cancelled the wandering result and gave a rise after marriage
weakeners_or_cancellations: malefic lagna lord afflicted in the 7th (BPHS 24.7 caution)
debilitation: Virgo lagna, Mercury in Pisces
lagna lord in an enemy sign: Leo lagna (Sun in Aquarius), Capricorn lagna (Saturn in Cancer)
lord_in_house/1/7.lagna_or_context_notes: Which lords count as 'malefic' here is debated: BPHS 24.7 and Charak split results by the lord's natural nature, but in opposite directions. Rath's chart 15 (Jupiter as lagna lord in the 7th with neecha-bhanga Venus) shows strength overriding the negative lines. Mercury in the 7th for Gemini/Virgo lagna is in a Jupiter sign; Jupiter in the 7th for Sagittarius/Pisces lagna is in a Mercury sign.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.7 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com, with word-by-word)
source_views.view: If malefic, the wife does not live (traditional); if benefic, the native may wander, be poor or detached, or even be a king.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.7 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Malefic: wife short-lived. Benefic: aimless, poor, dejected, though a strong benefic may make one a king.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 15.9 (Mantreswara)
source_views.view: Lagna lord's occupation of a bhava assures its well-being.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. IV 'Results of Lord of First House Occupying Different Houses' (pp. 21-22)
source_views.view: Wife does not live or more than one marriage; later detachment and ascetic life; rich or poor by other factors; much travel. Well disposed: much time abroad, licentious, or dependent on parents-in-law.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Lagna lord (pp. 230-231)
source_views.view: Brilliant, good-looking, good-natured wife. If the lagna lord is a natural malefic: bereft of wife, detached, poor or a king, wandering in foreign lands.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 4.4 'Placement of Ascendant Lord' 4.4.7 (p. 34) and chart 15
source_views.view: Wife short-lived, more than one marriage, misfortunes; unless strong could become ascetic or nomad; if strong, great wealth and prosperity. In chart 15 neecha-bhanga cancelled the wandering result and a rise came after marriage.

lord_in_house/1/7.disagreements: Sources agree that the placement makes partnership, travel and detachment central and that strength decides, but split the details differently. BPHS: malefic lord harms the spouse, benefic lord gives wandering, poverty or detachment (or kingship). Charak reverses this: a good spouse in general, loss of spouse and wandering for a malefic lord. Raman gives the harsh lines unconditionally but adds travel and wealth-or-poverty. Rath makes the outcome depend on strength. Phaladeepika 15.9's rule (the lagna lord helps the house it occupies) is the most positive view.
lord_in_house/1/7.phrasing_guidance: Talk about partnership focus and growth through relationships. Never mention spouse longevity or death. If asked, say BPHS has a cautionary verse that modern practice does not apply literally.

lord_in_house/1/8.summary: The self is drawn into hidden matters, research, transformation and the occult; classical texts warn of hardships and a volatile temperament, especially if the lord is weak.
common_outcomes: interest in occult, astrology, research or hidden knowledge
life marked by sudden changes and reinventions
intense, private nature
periods of stress or setbacks that test resilience
rare_outcomes: BPHS traditional list: sickliness, theft, strong anger, gambling, illicit relationships

by_area.personality: Learned, with gambling tendencies and interest in occultism (Raman HTJH I; BPHS 24.8); Rath 4.4.8: learned, short-tempered.
by_area.finance: Sources split: Charak says accumulates wealth; Rath says wealth nil; BPHS mentions gambling. Bhavartha Ratnakara (II, Nirdhana st. 1) gives poverty from birth when the lords of the lagna, 4th and 9th are all in the 8th (less if only two).
by_area.health: Raman: a weak constitution unless favourable aspects exist (HTJH I, 'Other Important Combinations'); Charak: long-lived but with ill-health. Do not make medical predictions.
by_area.relationships: Traditional lines on illicit ties (BPHS 24.8, Charak) and an unhappy married life (Rath 4.4.8); do not predict.
by_area.spirituality: Interest in occultism (Raman); good for spiritual pursuits (Charak); a strong lord makes one religiously inclined and keen to help others (Raman).

strengtheners: lagna lord in own sign in the 8th (Aries lagna: Mars in Scorpio; Libra lagna: Venus in Taurus) - lagna ownership predominates and results improve
exaltation: Sagittarius lagna, Jupiter in Cancer
benefic aspect (Phaladeepika 15.3 makes benefic aspect the saving factor)
strong shadbala and good D9
strong lord: takes pride in helping others, many friends, religiously inclined (Raman HTJH I)
weakeners_or_cancellations: combust, debilitated or in an enemy sign without benefic aspect: Phaladeepika 15.3 calls this destruction of the bhava's results
malefic conjunction (BPHS 12.1)
lagna lord in the 8th together with the 4th and 9th lords: poverty yoga (Bhavartha Ratnakara II, Nirdhana st. 1)
lagna lord in the 8th without favourable aspects: weak constitution (Raman HTJH I)
lord_in_house/1/8.lagna_or_context_notes: For Aries and Libra lagna the lagna lord also owns the 8th and sits in its own sign here. Laghu Parashari sloka 9 says the 8th-lord blemish is removed when that planet also owns the lagna, and O.P. Verma's commentary specifies that this applies when it occupies the lagna or the 8th, so these two lagnas get a much milder reading.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.8 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Skilled in occult learning, but sickly, thievish, very angry, a gambler, with illicit ties.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.8 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Scholarly, but sickly, thievish, quick-tempered, gambling, consorting with others' wives.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 15.3, 15.9 (Mantreswara)
source_views.view: A bhava lord in the 8th that is combust/debilitated/in enemy sign without benefic aspect ruins the bhava; a strong lord limits the injury.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. IV 'Results of Lord of First House Occupying Different Houses' (pp. 21-22)
source_views.view: Learned, gambling tendencies, interest in occultism, mean character. Strong lord: helps others, many friends, religious, peaceful end. Also: lagna lord in the 8th gives a weak constitution unless favourable aspects exist.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Lagna lord (pp. 230-231)
source_views.view: Long-lived, accumulates wealth, ill-health, adulterous, thievish, gambler, easily angered; good for spiritual pursuits.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 4.4 'Placement of Ascendant Lord' 4.4.8 (p. 34)
source_views.view: Learned, diseased, short-tempered, unfortunate, gambler, profligate; married life miserable and wealth nil.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara of Ramanujacharya (tr. B.V. Raman), ch. II Nirdhana yogas st. 1 with Raman's note
source_views.view: Lords of the lagna, 4th and 9th in the 8th give poverty from birth; if only two of them are there, the poverty is less.

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari (Jataka Chandrika), tr. with commentary by O.P. Verma, sloka 9 with notes
source_views.view: The 8th lord is inauspicious unless it also owns the lagna; per the commentary, the lagna-cum-8th lord is auspicious when in the lagna or the 8th.

lord_in_house/1/8.disagreements: Classical texts and Rath are mostly negative; Charak gives long life and wealth alongside the negatives; Raman gives a positive picture when the lord is strong. Rath says wealth is nil while Charak says wealth accumulates.
lord_in_house/1/8.phrasing_guidance: Lead with depth, research ability and resilience through change. Never label the person as a thief, gambler or unfaithful; present BPHS's list as an old, severe text that modern practice softens. No health or longevity predictions.

lord_in_house/1/9.summary: One of the best placements: the self joins fortune, dharma and the guru. The person is lucky, well-liked, devout, eloquent and blessed with family and wealth.
common_outcomes: good fortune and support from elders, teachers and father
religious or philosophical nature
eloquence and skill
happiness through spouse, children and wealth
rare_outcomes: BPHS specifically: devotion to Vishnu

by_area.personality: Fortunate, principled, beloved by people (BPHS 24.9); protector of others and a good orator (Raman HTJH I).
by_area.finance: Rich (Raman; BPHS 24.9; Rath 4.4.9); if well disposed, inherits good ancestral and paternal property (Raman).
by_area.relationships: Happiness through spouse and children (BPHS 24.9; Raman).
by_area.family: If well disposed, the father is famous, philanthropic and god-fearing (Raman); happy family (Rath 4.4.9).
by_area.spirituality: Religious; traditional mention of devotion to Vishnu (BPHS 24.9; Raman; Charak; Rath).

strengtheners: exaltation: Leo lagna (Sun in Aries) and Aquarius lagna (Saturn in Libra)
Jupiter aspect, strong 9th lord
lagna lord and 9th lord connected (classical raja yoga)
weakeners_or_cancellations: debilitation: Scorpio lagna, Mars in Cancer
combustion, malefic affliction, papakartari on the 9th
lord_in_house/1/9.lagna_or_context_notes: For Leo lagna (Sun in Aries) and Aquarius lagna (Saturn in Libra) the lagna lord is exalted here.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.9 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Fortunate, dear to people, devotee of Vishnu, skilled in speech, with spouse, sons and wealth.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.9 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Fortunate, beloved, devoted to Vishnu, skilful, eloquent; wife, sons, wealth.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 12.1, 12.5
source_views.view: Lagna lord in a kona gives bodily happiness; benefic lagna lord in kona gives long life, wealth, favour.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. IV 'Results of Lord of First House Occupying Different Houses' (pp. 21-22)
source_views.view: Fortunate, protector of others, religious, Vishnu-worshipper, good orator, happiness from wife and children, rich. Well disposed: good ancestral and paternal property; father famous and philanthropic.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Lagna lord (pp. 230-231)
source_views.view: Fortunate, learned, beloved, worships Vishnu, benevolent talker, wife, sons, wealth, very famous.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 4.4 'Placement of Ascendant Lord' 4.4.9 (pp. 34-35)
source_views.view: Fortunate, popular, skilled, eloquent, happy family, wealth, blessed by Jupiter (Vishnu).

lord_in_house/1/9.disagreements: None significant; all classical and modern sources agree.
lord_in_house/1/9.phrasing_guidance: Describe as a fortunate, principled placement. Phrase devotion generally (spiritual or philosophical leaning) rather than naming a deity unless the user's tradition calls for it.

lord_in_house/1/10.summary: The self is expressed through career, reputation and public action: the person is self-made, recognised by authorities and well known, with support from the father.
common_outcomes: career and public standing central to identity
recognition from government or superiors
fame and self-earned income
support or happiness through father

by_area.personality: Honourable, famous, self-made and ambitious (Rath 4.4.10).
by_area.career: Professional success, honoured by eminent people; may become a research scholar or specialist in the field shown by the lagna and 10th lords (Raman HTJH I); royal honour and fame (BPHS 24.10).
by_area.finance: Self-earned wealth (BPHS 24.10; Charak: fame and wealth through own prowess; Rath: prosperous).
by_area.health: Kendra placement supports vitality (BPHS 12.1).
by_area.family: Happiness from the father (BPHS 24.10; Charak: all comforts from father; Rath: blessed by parents).

strengtheners: directional strength (dig bala): Sun or Mars in the 10th
exaltation: Aries lagna (Mars in Capricorn) and Capricorn lagna (Saturn in Libra)
own sign: Virgo lagna (Mercury in Gemini) and Pisces lagna (Jupiter in Sagittarius)
lagna lord connected with the 9th or 5th lord; benefic aspects
lords of the lagna, 4th and 9th in the 10th, lagna or 7th together with the 10th lord: very fortunate in their dasas (Bhavartha Ratnakara VIII st. 9-10)
weakeners_or_cancellations: debilitation: Gemini lagna, Mercury in Pisces
combustion and malefic aspect
lord_in_house/1/10.lagna_or_context_notes: Exalted for Aries and Capricorn lagna; own sign for Virgo and Pisces lagna (the lagna lord also owns the 10th). Debilitated for Gemini lagna, where neecha-bhanga should be checked.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.10 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Happiness from father, royal honour, fame, self-earned wealth.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.10 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Paternal happiness, royal honour, fame, self-earned wealth.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 15.9
source_views.view: The house the lagna lord occupies flourishes.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. IV 'Results of Lord of First House Occupying Different Houses' (pp. 21-22)
source_views.view: Results of the 4th plus professional success, honoured by eminent men, a research scholar or specialist in the field of the lagna and 10th lords.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Lagna lord (pp. 230-231)
source_views.view: Learned, honoured by the ruler, comforts from father, fame and wealth through own prowess.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 4.4 'Placement of Ascendant Lord' 4.4.10 (p. 35)
source_views.view: Honourable, famous, self-made, blessed by parents, ambitious and prosperous.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara of Ramanujacharya (tr. B.V. Raman), ch. VIII (Bhagya yogas) st. 9-10
source_views.view: If the lords of the lagna, 9th and 4th are in the 10th, lagna or 7th with the 10th lord, the native becomes very fortunate in the dasas of those lords.

lord_in_house/1/10.phrasing_guidance: Speak of ambition and public achievement; avoid guaranteeing fame or office.

lord_in_house/1/11.summary: The self is aimed at gains, goals and networks: steady income, good qualities and wide reputation.
common_outcomes: regular gains and fulfilment of desires
good character and wide reputation
large social or professional network
rare_outcomes: BPHS traditional line: many wives (Santhanam) or many good qualities (ELS reading)

by_area.personality: Good qualities and fame (BPHS 24.11; Charak); excellent qualities of head and heart (Rath 4.4.11).
by_area.career: Constant gains in business for a businessman (Raman HTJH I).
by_area.finance: Never in financial straits; large business profits (Raman); constant gains (BPHS 24.11); good income (Rath).
by_area.relationships: BPHS (Santhanam rendering), Charak and Rath carry a line about several spouses or love affairs; do not use.
by_area.family: Owes prosperity to an elder brother (Raman); long-lived sons (Charak).

strengtheners: connection with the 2nd lord (wealth yoga logic, BPHS 13.4)
exaltation: Cancer lagna (Moon in Taurus) and Taurus lagna (Venus in Pisces)
strong malefic lagna lords do well in upachayas (Phaladeepika 15.7)
weakeners_or_cancellations: 11th is also a trishadaya house; desires can multiply
debilitation: Pisces lagna, Jupiter in Capricorn

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.11 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Always gaining, good character, famous, multiple spouses or good qualities.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.11 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Constant gains, good qualities, fame, many wives.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. IV 'Results of Lord of First House Occupying Different Houses' (pp. 21-22)
source_views.view: Results of the 2nd plus constant business gains; never in financial straits. Prosperity owed to elder brother; enormous profits consistent with other planets.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Lagna lord (pp. 230-231)
source_views.view: Manifold benefits, good qualities, multiple wives, famous, long-lived sons, lives in comfort.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 4.4 'Placement of Ascendant Lord' 4.4.11 (p. 35)
source_views.view: Good income, reputation, love affairs or wives, excellent qualities of head and heart.

lord_in_house/1/11.disagreements: The two BPHS renderings differ on whether the verse speaks of many wives or many good qualities; Charak and Rath side with the spouse reading.
lord_in_house/1/11.phrasing_guidance: Focus on gains, networks and fulfilment of goals. Do not mention multiple marriages.

lord_in_house/1/12.summary: The self is drawn toward expenditure, distance and withdrawal: classical texts warn of reduced comfort, heavy spending and anger unless benefics help; modern readers add foreign residence and spiritual inclination.
common_outcomes: high or uncontrolled expenses
living in a foreign land (Charak)
visits to holy places and charitable spending (Raman)
less physical ease unless benefics support
rare_outcomes: BPHS: wasteful spending and anger when no benefic aspect or conjunction

by_area.personality: Can be quick-tempered (BPHS 24.12); Rath 4.4.12: the cause of own misfortunes, short temper, a spendthrift.
by_area.career: Losses and little success in business enterprises unless fortified (Raman HTJH I); Charak: lives in a foreign land.
by_area.finance: Many losses (Raman); spending patterns follow the nature of the lagna and 12th lords (Rath 4.4.12); when strong, inherited riches are spent on charity (Raman).
by_area.health: Classical texts reduce bodily comfort (BPHS 12.1, 24.12; Charak); no medical predictions.
by_area.spirituality: Visits holy places; when well placed, emotionally balanced and dedicated to public welfare (Raman HTJH I).

strengtheners: benefic aspect or conjunction (BPHS 24.12 conditions the bad results on their absence)
lagna lord in own sign in the 12th (Aquarius lagna: Saturn in Capricorn) - lagna ownership predominates
Jupiter's aspect or a spiritually oriented D9 supports the moksha side
weakeners_or_cancellations: malefic association without benefic aspect (BPHS 12.1, 24.12)
weak lord: Phaladeepika 15.9 says harm is severe when the lord is weak
debilitation: Libra lagna, Venus in Virgo
lord_in_house/1/12.lagna_or_context_notes: For Aquarius lagna Saturn owns the 12th too and sits in own sign Capricorn; lagna ownership predominates (Phaladeepika 15.10; BPHS 34), so the placement is far milder. For Libra lagna Venus is debilitated in Virgo in the 12th, which increases the classical caution unless neecha-bhanga applies.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.12 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Without benefic help: lack of bodily comfort, wasteful spending, quick temper.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.12 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Devoid of physical happiness, spends unfruitfully, given to anger, if without benefic aspect/conjunction.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 15.5, 15.9
source_views.view: Lord in a dusthana harms its bhava; strong lord limits the harm; benefic aspect restores prosperity.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. IV 'Results of Lord of First House Occupying Different Houses' (pp. 21-22)
source_views.view: Same as the 8th, plus many losses, visits to holy places, no success in business. Well placed: spends inherited riches on charity, emotionally balanced, dedicated to public welfare.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Lagna lord (pp. 230-231)
source_views.view: Bereft of bodily comforts, unworthy pursuits, lives in a foreign land; without benefic influence, futile expenditure and anger.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 4.4 'Placement of Ascendant Lord' 4.4.12 (p. 35)
source_views.view: Cause of own misfortunes, little physical felicity, short temper, spendthrift; expenses depend on the ascendant and 12th lords.

lord_in_house/1/12.disagreements: Classical texts and Rath treat this as unfavourable; Raman gives a charitable, public-service expression when the lord is well placed; Charak names living in a foreign land, which BPHS 24.12 does not state.
lord_in_house/1/12.phrasing_guidance: Describe as a placement of giving, distance and inner life; suggest mindful spending. Avoid predicting isolation, loss or illness.

lord_in_house/2/1.summary: Wealth, speech and family values are tied to the self: the person earns and has children and resources, but can be blunt or abrasive within the family and busy with others' affairs.
common_outcomes: personal identity built around earning and resources
forceful or outspoken speech
some friction or distance with family members
involvement in others' work or affairs
rare_outcomes: BPHS traditional view: lustful and harsh temperament
Santhanam rendering: works for others (service) rather than for self

by_area.personality: Strong-willed and sometimes harsh (BPHS 24.13); passionate, short on polite manners and time-serving (Raman HTJH I); tight-fisted with money (Rath 5.3.1); thrifty yet ready to help others (Charak).
by_area.career: Earns by own effort, intelligence and learning (Raman; Rath 5.3.1); the Santhanam rendering of BPHS adds working for others.
by_area.finance: Wealth indicated by every source (BPHS 24.13; Raman; Charak; Rath). Inherited wealth if the 9th lord or the Sun joins the combination (Raman). With the 11th lord also in the lagna, a strong dhana yoga (Bhavartha Ratnakara II st. 8).
by_area.family: Has children but can be at odds with family (BPHS 24.13; Raman: 'hates his own family'; Charak: 'a thorn in the flesh of his own family'); Rath 5.3.2 explains this as the 4th from the 2nd lord (here the 4th house of family happiness) turning hostile.

strengtheners: own sign: Capricorn lagna, where Saturn owns both 1st and 2nd (strong for wealth and self)
benefic aspects on the lagna or connection with the 11th lord (BPHS 13.4)
2nd lord a natural benefic softens speech
2nd and 11th lords both in the lagna: powerful dhana yoga (Bhavartha Ratnakara II st. 8)
9th lord or the Sun connected: inherited wealth (Raman HTJH I)
weakeners_or_cancellations: debilitation: Virgo lagna, Venus in Virgo
2nd lord with malefics and malefics in the 2nd: harsh or untruthful speech (BPHS 13.13)
lord_in_house/2/1.lagna_or_context_notes: For Leo lagna Mercury owns both the 2nd and 11th, so Mercury in the lagna meets Bhavartha Ratnakara's '2nd and 11th lords in the lagna' dhana yoga (II st. 8; Raman's chart 17 is this case). For Aries and Libra lagna the 2nd lord also owns the 7th; for Virgo lagna Venus (2nd and 9th lord) is debilitated here. Laghu Parashari sloka 8: the 2nd lord gives results by its associations and the house it occupies rather than by its ownership.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.13 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Has sons and wealth, but a thorn in the family; lustful, harsh, busy with others' affairs.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.13 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Sons and wealth, but inimical to family, lustful, harsh, does others' work.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 13.1, 13.4 (Dhana Bhava)
source_views.view: 2nd lord in a kendra or kona supports wealth; link with the 11th lord in kendra/kona makes one wealthy.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. V 'Results of Lord of Second being Situated in Different Houses' (pp. 52-53)
source_views.view: Wealthy but hates own family, lacks polite manners, passionate, subservient, time-serving. Earns by own effort, intelligence and learning, or inherits if the 9th lord or the Sun is involved.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Second lord (pp. 231-232)
source_views.view: Wealthy, thrifty, cruel, many comforts, sons; ever ready to help others but a thorn in the flesh of own family.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 5.3 'Placement of Lord of Second House' (p. 48)
source_views.view: Tight-fisted and wealthy; money by own effort and intelligence; passionate and subservient. The 4th from the 2nd lord is weakened, so the 4th house (family) becomes hostile.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara of Ramanujacharya (tr. B.V. Raman), ch. II Dhana yogas st. 8 with chart 17
source_views.view: Dhana yoga when both the 2nd and 11th lords are in the lagna; Raman's example is a single planet owning both, placed in the lagna.

lord_in_house/2/1.disagreements: BPHS renderings differ on 'meddles in others' affairs' vs 'works for others'. Raman, Charak and Rath all confirm the family friction, and Raman and Rath stress self-earned wealth.
lord_in_house/2/1.phrasing_guidance: Frame as self-made resources and strong speech; suggest tact in family dealings. Avoid labelling the person lustful or harsh.

lord_in_house/2/2.summary: The 2nd lord in its own house strengthens wealth, family and speech: the person is wealthy and self-respecting, though BPHS adds traditional cautions about marriage and children.
common_outcomes: stable accumulation of wealth
strong family ties and traditions
confident, authoritative speech
pride or a sense of self-worth
rare_outcomes: BPHS traditional view: two or more marriages, or no children

by_area.personality: Self-respecting and proud (BPHS 24.14; Raman; Charak, who adds 'inclined to oppose others').
by_area.career: If exalted or otherwise fortified, the 2nd lord acts almost as a yogakaraka and gives a considerable fortune through business or work suited to the 2nd lord and house (Raman HTJH I).
by_area.finance: Wealth strongly supported (BPHS 13.3; Charak: wealthy, earns well; Rath: rich). Malefic aspects bring losses, and an afflicted lord can show as poor food or family illness (Raman). With evil planets in or aspecting the 2nd, poverty (Raman, 'Other Important Combinations').
by_area.relationships: BPHS 24.14, Raman ('twice or thrice depending on the 7th house'), Charak and Rath all carry a line about more than one marriage; Raman also links affliction to a lack of cordiality with the partner. Traditional only; check the 7th and 5th houses.
by_area.family: Family resources strong; traditional caution about children (BPHS 24.14; Raman: may be childless; Charak: son-less; Rath 5.3.2: the 5th, being 4th from the 2nd lord, is damaged).

strengtheners: always own sign here; Leo lagna Mercury is also exalted (Virgo)
conjunction with Mars or Jupiter in the 2nd (BPHS 13.3)
own/exalted sign: benefactor and renowned (BPHS 13.10)
good D9 or vaisheshikamsha dignity: prosperity without effort (BPHS 13.11)
lords of the 1st, 2nd and 11th each in own house: dhana yoga (Bhavartha Ratnakara II st. 7)
2nd lord in the 2nd and 5th lord in the 5th: rajayoga (Bhavartha Ratnakara IX, Raman's notes and chart 42)
2nd lord in a nakshatra other than the 3rd, 5th or 7th from the birth star, joined or aspected by benefics (Raman HTJH I)
weakeners_or_cancellations: combustion or malefic conjunction
malefic occupants of the 2nd spoil speech (BPHS 13.13)
evil planets in or aspecting the 2nd with its lord: poverty (Raman HTJH I)
lord_in_house/2/2.lagna_or_context_notes: For Capricorn lagna Saturn here also owns the 1st; for Taurus and Scorpio lagna the 2nd lord also owns the 5th, which with the 5th lord's own placement is the rajayoga of Bhavartha Ratnakara IX (chart 42); for Aries and Libra lagna it also owns the 7th.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.14 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 13.3, 13.10-11
source_views.view: 2nd lord in the 2nd, own or exalted sign, or with good vargas gives wealth and renown.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. V 'Results of Lord of Second being Situated in Different Houses' (pp. 52-53)
source_views.view: Proud; may marry twice or thrice depending on the 7th; may be childless. Fortified (exalted, or in 1/4/5/7/9/10): near-yogakaraka, fortune through business. Afflicted: losses, poor food, family illness, poor relations with partner.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Second lord (pp. 231-232)
source_views.view: Wealthy, earns well, enjoys comforts, proud, two or three wives, son-less, inclined to oppose others.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 5.3 'Placement of Lord of Second House' (p. 48)
source_views.view: The 2nd lord in the 2nd makes the native rich and increases the possibility of a second marriage; it tends to damage offspring (the 5th is 4th from it).

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara of Ramanujacharya (tr. B.V. Raman), ch. II Dhana yogas st. 7; ch. IX notes with chart 42 (p. 78; the stanza page itself is missing from the scan read)
source_views.view: Lords of the 11th, 1st and 2nd in their own houses give dhana yoga; Raman's note to ch. IX shows the 2nd lord in the 2nd with the 5th lord in the 5th giving rajayoga.

lord_in_house/2/2.disagreements: BPHS ch. 13 is wholly positive about wealth; ch. 24, Raman, Charak and Rath add the marriage and children lines. The ELS rendering frames childlessness as an alternative ('or'), the Santhanam text, Raman and Charak as an additional effect. Raman notes that afflictions reverse the wealth result.
lord_in_house/2/2.phrasing_guidance: Lead with wealth and family strength. Never predict childlessness or multiple marriages.

lord_in_house/2/3.summary: Wealth flows through effort, courage, communication and siblings: brave, intelligent and virtuous, but texts warn of strong desires and tightness with money; the influence on the lord decides which side dominates.
common_outcomes: brave and intelligent, with strong appetites
tight with money, especially later in life (BPHS, Raman)
siblings involved in gains or in friction (Raman, Charak)
success over rivals (Rath 5.3.2)
rare_outcomes: BPHS: lustful and greedy or miserly
BPHS: with malefic influence, scornful of the gods (heterodox)
Raman: propitiation of minor spirits (kshudra devatas) when fortified
Charak: a natural-benefic 2nd lord here opposes the ruler; Mars as 2nd lord here, a thief (traditional)

by_area.personality: Brave and clever with strong appetites (BPHS 24.15; Charak: virtuous, wise, valorous, greedy, sensuous); Raman adds a taste for luxuries and miserliness later in life.
by_area.career: If fortified, benefits from learning fine arts such as music and dancing (Raman HTJH I).
by_area.finance: Greedy or miserly (BPHS renderings; Raman: a miser later in life). If the 3rd lord also joins, generous; with Saturn added to the 2nd and 3rd lords, a miser (Bhavartha Ratnakara III st. 8-9).
by_area.family: If fortified, benefits through sisters (Raman); a natural-malefic 2nd lord brings differences with siblings (Charak).
by_area.spirituality: Benefic influence supports good conduct; malefic influence inclines toward irreverence (BPHS 24.15; Raman: atheistic tendencies; Charak: speaks ill of the gods with malefics).

strengtheners: own sign: Sagittarius lagna, Saturn in Aquarius
benefic conjunction or aspect (BPHS 24.15)
weakeners_or_cancellations: debilitation: Scorpio lagna, Jupiter in Capricorn
malefic association (BPHS 24.15)
lord_in_house/2/3.lagna_or_context_notes: For Sagittarius lagna Saturn owns both the 2nd and 3rd and sits in own sign. Bhavartha Ratnakara III st. 9 links Saturn with the 2nd and 3rd lords to miserliness; it does not say whether this applies when Saturn is itself both lords.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.15 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Brave, intelligent, virtuous, lustful and greedy; benefic influence improves, malefic makes one scorn the gods.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.15 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Valorous, wise, virtuous, lustful, miserly; heterodox if malefic-linked.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. V 'Results of Lord of Second being Situated in Different Houses' (pp. 52-53)
source_views.view: Brave, intelligent, good-natured but depraved character; atheistic tendencies, addicted to luxuries, later a miser. Fortified: benefits through sisters, learns fine arts (music, dancing), propitiates minor spirits.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Second lord (pp. 231-232)
source_views.view: Virtuous, wise, valorous, greedy, sensuous. Malefic 2nd lord: differences with siblings; benefic 2nd lord: opposed to the ruler; Mars as 2nd lord: a thief; with malefics: speaks ill of the gods.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 5.3 'Placement of Lord of Second House' (p. 48)
source_views.view: In the 3rd house the 2nd lord destroys enemies (the 6th, being 4th from it, is weakened).

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara of Ramanujacharya (tr. B.V. Raman), ch. III Brothers st. 8-9
source_views.view: Generous instincts if the 3rd lord is combined with the 2nd lord; a miser if Saturn joins the 2nd and 3rd lords.

lord_in_house/2/3.disagreements: Translations differ between 'greedy' and 'miserly'; Raman includes both (luxuries, later a miser). Rath's view (destroys enemies) is more positive than BPHS, Raman and Charak.
lord_in_house/2/3.phrasing_guidance: Speak of earning through effort and communication; mention strong desires only as something to balance. Do not call the person irreligious.

lord_in_house/2/4.summary: Wealth joins home, property and comforts: a broadly prosperous placement; exaltation plus Jupiter's company is said to give near-royal status.
common_outcomes: gains of all kinds, often through land, home or vehicles
comfortable domestic life
family wealth connected with the mother
rare_outcomes: BPHS: if exalted and with Jupiter, king-like status

by_area.personality: Truthful (Charak); spends on own comfort yet frugal with money (Raman HTJH I).
by_area.career: If fortified: earnings as a vehicle dealer or agent, agriculturist, landlord or commission agent (Raman HTJH I).
by_area.finance: Prosperous in every way (BPHS 24.16); kendra placement supports wealth (BPHS 13.1); king-like if exalted with Jupiter (BPHS 24.16; Charak adds Venus).
by_area.family: Benefits from maternal relations, with losses through them if the 4th lord is afflicted (Raman); benefits from father (Charak).

strengtheners: exaltation: Libra lagna, Mars in Capricorn
conjunction with Jupiter while exalted (BPHS 24.16)
connection with the 11th lord (BPHS 13.4)
2nd lord with Jupiter in a kendra or trikona: learned and publicly honoured (Bhavartha Ratnakara II, Education st. 8)
weakeners_or_cancellations: debilitation: Cancer lagna (Sun in Libra) and Capricorn lagna (Saturn in Aries)
malefic affliction to the 4th or Moon
lord_in_house/2/4.lagna_or_context_notes: For Libra lagna, Mars (2nd and 7th lord) is exalted in the 4th; BPHS's 'exalted with Jupiter' condition is most directly met here when Jupiter joins.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.16 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Prosperous in every way; exalted and with Jupiter, equal to a king.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.16 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Gains wealth in many forms; king-like if exalted and with Jupiter.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Second lord (pp. 231-232)
source_views.view: Wealthy, truthful, long-lived, benefits from father; if exalted or with Jupiter or Venus, equal to a king.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara of Ramanujacharya (tr. B.V. Raman), ch. II Education st. 8

lord_in_house/2/4.disagreements: Raman's fortified results (vehicles, land, agriculture) and Charak's 'benefits from father' extend BPHS without conflicting with it.
lord_in_house/2/4.phrasing_guidance: Present as comfort and property-linked prosperity; avoid promising royal status.

lord_in_house/2/5.summary: Wealth links to intelligence, children and past merit: the person is wealthy, and children too are capable of earning.

children who are financially capable
family values passed to children

by_area.finance: Wealthy (BPHS 24.17; Charak). If fortified, sudden gains through lotteries, prize contests or the favour of rulers (Raman HTJH I). Exchange of the 2nd and 5th lords gives much wealth (Bhavartha Ratnakara II st. 1).
by_area.family: Children able to earn (BPHS 24.17; Charak: several sons).

strengtheners: own sign and exaltation: Taurus lagna (Mercury in Virgo, own and exalted, also 5th lord)
own sign: Scorpio lagna (Jupiter in Pisces, also 5th lord)
Jupiter influence
exchange with the 5th lord (2nd lord in 5th, 5th lord in 2nd): much wealth (Bhavartha Ratnakara II st. 1)
2nd lord with Jupiter in a kendra or trikona: learned and publicly honoured (Bhavartha Ratnakara II, Education st. 8)
weakeners_or_cancellations: debilitation: Sagittarius lagna (Saturn in Aries) and Pisces lagna (Mars in Cancer)
malefic affliction to the 5th
lord_in_house/2/5.lagna_or_context_notes: For Taurus and Scorpio lagna the 2nd lord also owns the 5th and occupies it; Bhavartha Ratnakara (ch. IX notes, chart 42) treats the 2nd and 5th lords in their own houses as a rajayoga.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Second lord (pp. 231-232)
source_views.view: Wealthy, famous for efficiency, several sons, capable of earning wealth, sickly.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara of Ramanujacharya (tr. B.V. Raman), ch. II Dhana yogas st. 1

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara of Ramanujacharya (tr. B.V. Raman), ch. II Education st. 8
source_views.view: If the 2nd lord and Jupiter are placed in a kendra or trikona, the native is learned in different branches of knowledge and publicly honoured.

lord_in_house/2/5.disagreements: BPHS and Charak are positive. Raman's unfortified reading (family friction, stinginess) is more negative, while his fortified reading adds windfall gains.
lord_in_house/2/5.phrasing_guidance: Positive; keep speculation advice cautious and avoid promising investment gains.

lord_in_house/2/6.summary: Wealth meets the house of enemies, debt and service: with benefic influence money can come through opponents, competition or service; with malefic influence money can be lost through disputes.
common_outcomes: income through competition or through opponents (BPHS, Charak, Rath)
expenses also arising through rivals or disputes (Raman, Rath)
outcome swings with benefic or malefic influence (BPHS 24.18)
rare_outcomes: BPHS: with malefic influence, a defect or injury to a limb (traditional view)
BPHS 13.6: 2nd and 11th lords both in the 6th indicates poverty
Raman: a fortified lord here can show gains through questionable dealings, and an afflicted one legal trouble over breach of trust or forgery (traditional)

by_area.career: Wealth and status through success in contests or competition (Rath 5.3.1).
by_area.finance: Depends on benefic or malefic influence (BPHS 24.18). Income and expenditure both come through enemies (Raman HTJH I); earns through and over enemies (Charak); Rath: gains through competition, but losses through enemies because the lord here aspects the 12th.
by_area.health: BPHS (limb or shank), Raman and Charak (anal region, thighs) carry traditional body-part lines; do not make medical predictions.
by_area.family: With Mercury also in the 6th, money through cousins (Bhavartha Ratnakara VIII st. 20).

strengtheners: benefic conjunction or aspect: gains from enemies (BPHS 24.18)
exaltation: Aquarius lagna, Jupiter in Cancer
strong lord limits harm (Phaladeepika 15.9)

weakeners_or_cancellations: malefic association (BPHS 24.18)
debilitation: Aries lagna (Venus in Virgo) and Gemini lagna (Moon in Scorpio)
11th lord also in the 6th (BPHS 13.6)
Phaladeepika 15.5: a bhava lord in a dusthana harms its bhava
lord_in_house/2/6.lagna_or_context_notes: For Aquarius lagna Jupiter (2nd and 11th lord) is exalted in the 6th.

source_views.view: Income and expenditure from enemies; diseases of anus and thighs. Fortified: wealth through questionable and deceitful dealings; afflicted: involved in such troubles and punished for breach of trust, forgery or perjury.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Second lord (pp. 231-232)
source_views.view: Accumulates wealth, destroys enemies, earns through enemies; with malefics, loss of wealth and disease of anal region and breast.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 5.3 'Placement of Lord of Second House' (p. 48)
source_views.view: The 2nd lord in the 6th gives wealth and status through success in war or competition; as it aspects the 12th, it also shows losses through enemies.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara of Ramanujacharya (tr. B.V. Raman), ch. VIII st. 20
source_views.view: Money through cousins if Mercury and the 2nd lord occupy the 6th (or Mercury alone).

lord_in_house/2/6.disagreements: BPHS splits by benefic/malefic influence; Charak and Rath lean positive (victory, earning through enemies), Raman stresses both income and expenditure through enemies and an ethical risk. The renderings differ on the body part (limb, leg/shank, anal region).
lord_in_house/2/6.phrasing_guidance: Talk about service-based income and careful handling of debts and disputes. Do not predict injury or poverty.

lord_in_house/2/7.summary: Wealth and family link with spouse, partnerships and the public: money through partners or trade; BPHS adds an interest in healing work and cautionary lines about fidelity.
common_outcomes: income through partners, spouse or trade, sometimes from abroad (Raman, Charak)
spouse contributes to family finances (Charak)
an interest in healing work (BPHS, Raman, Charak)
rare_outcomes: BPHS: may practise medicine (physician)
BPHS traditional view: attraction to others' spouses; with malefics, doubt about spouse's fidelity

by_area.personality: Pleasure-seeking (BPHS 24.19; Raman; Charak).
by_area.career: Healing or medical work (BPHS 24.19; Raman: likely to become a healer; Charak: a physician if afflicted by malefics). A strong 2nd lord with the 7th lord: business and travel abroad (Raman HTJH I).
by_area.finance: Wealth from foreign sources when the 2nd lord is strong and joined by the 7th lord, and benefit through women if its sign, navamsa or nakshatra is feminine (Raman); a money-earning spouse (Charak); Raman warns of spending on the senses.
by_area.relationships: BPHS, Raman and Charak all have cautionary lines about fidelity; these are traditional and must not be predicted.

exaltation: Virgo lagna, Venus in Pisces (also 9th lord)
benefic aspects on the 7th
strong 2nd lord joined by the 7th lord: wealth from foreign sources and business abroad (Raman HTJH I)
2nd lord with Jupiter in a kendra or trikona: learned and publicly honoured (Bhavartha Ratnakara II, Education st. 8)
weakeners_or_cancellations: malefic conjunction (BPHS 24.19 fidelity caution)
combustion
lord_in_house/2/7.lagna_or_context_notes: For Aries and Libra lagna the 2nd lord also owns the 7th and sits in its own sign.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.19 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Drawn to others' spouses, may be a physician; with malefics, spouse unfaithful.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.19 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Addicted to others' wives, a doctor; if malefic-linked, wife of doubtful conduct.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 13.1
source_views.view: 2nd lord in a kendra supports wealth.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. V 'Results of Lord of Second being Situated in Different Houses' (pp. 52-53)
source_views.view: Likely to become a healer; laxity of morals in both partners; money wasted on the senses. Strong with the 7th lord: wealth through foreign sources, business abroad; feminine sign/navamsa/nakshatra: benefit through women.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Second lord (pp. 231-232)
source_views.view: Sensuous; money-earning wife; if afflicted by malefics, becomes a physician; adultery by both.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara of Ramanujacharya (tr. B.V. Raman), ch. II Education st. 8
source_views.view: If the 2nd lord and Jupiter are placed in a kendra or trikona, the native is learned in different branches of knowledge and publicly honoured.

lord_in_house/2/7.disagreements: BPHS ch. 13 (kendra = wealth) and ch. 24 (moral cautions) emphasise different things. Raman and Charak repeat the healing and fidelity lines; Raman adds foreign income when the lord is strong.
lord_in_house/2/7.phrasing_guidance: Discuss partnership-linked income and possible healing vocations. Never suggest infidelity of the person or spouse.

lord_in_house/2/8.summary: Wealth enters the house of hidden and inherited matters: BPHS gives much land and wealth, but less marital happiness and little support from an elder sibling.
common_outcomes: gains of land or property (BPHS, Raman, Charak)
wealth that comes and goes; savings hard to hold (Raman, Rath)
spouse-linked money, gained or lost depending on strength (Rath)
less ease in marriage and with an elder sibling (traditional; BPHS, Raman, Charak)
rare_outcomes: BPHS: limited marital happiness and no happiness from elder brother
Charak: lives on alms and charities (traditional)

by_area.finance: Sources split. BPHS 24.20 and Charak give income from land and property, and Raman also says land is gained; but Raman's own observation is that hardly anything is earned and inherited or accumulated wealth disappears, with both influx and loss when the lord is strong. Rath: a large dowry or a loss through alimony, depending on strength. BPHS 13.8 warns that wealth lords in 6/8/12 bring loss.
by_area.relationships: Little happiness from the spouse (BPHS 24.20; Raman; Charak); traditional only, do not predict.
by_area.family: Misunderstandings with, or no comfort from, an elder sibling (BPHS 24.20; Raman; Charak).

strengtheners: strong lord with benefic aspect (Phaladeepika 15.3, 15.9)
connection with the 11th lord in a good house
weakeners_or_cancellations: debilitation: Leo lagna, Mercury in Pisces
combust, debilitated or in an enemy sign without benefic aspect: the 2nd house's results are spoiled (Phaladeepika 15.3)
11th lord also in a dusthana (BPHS 13.8)

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.20 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Much land and wealth, little marital happiness, no happiness from elder sibling.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.20 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 15.3

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. V 'Results of Lord of Second being Situated in Different Houses' (pp. 52-53)
source_views.view: Very little happiness from spouse; misunderstandings with elder brothers; gets landed property. Strong: influx and loss of wealth; observation shows hardly any earnings and the loss of inherited or accumulated wealth.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Second lord (pp. 231-232)
source_views.view: Income from lands and property; diminished comfort from wife and from elder brother; harmful to others; lives on alms.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 5.3 'Placement of Lord of Second House' (p. 48)
source_views.view: A 2nd lord in the 8th can bring a huge dowry or a loss through alimony, depending on its strength.

lord_in_house/2/8.disagreements: On wealth the sources conflict: BPHS 24.20 and Charak are positive (land and wealth), Raman's observation and BPHS 13.8 are negative, and Rath makes it depend on strength. On marriage and the elder sibling, BPHS, Raman and Charak agree.
lord_in_house/2/8.phrasing_guidance: Speak of inherited, shared or hidden resources and fluctuating savings. Do not predict marital unhappiness or family estrangement.

lord_in_house/2/9.summary: Wealth joins fortune and dharma: the person becomes wealthy, diligent and skilful; early life may be harder, with later life happier, and religious observances and pilgrimage feature.
common_outcomes: wealth through fortune, teachers, father or dharmic work
hard-working and skilled
religious practices, vows, pilgrimages
life improves with age
