source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. VI 'Results of the Lord of the Third House Being Posited in Different Houses' (pp. 73-74)
source_views.view: Happy on the whole, rich and learned, but a cruel-hearted spouse. Well fortified with weak lagna and 9th lords: brothers survive the native; step-brothers if the 9th lord is strong; weak Mars: loss of lands.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Third lord (pp. 232-233)
source_views.view: Enjoys comforts, wealthy, wise, opposed to his mother, has a cruel wife.

lord_in_house/3/4.disagreements: The spouse line appears in BPHS, Raman and Charak; it has no evident house logic. Charak's friction with the mother is not in BPHS 24.28.
lord_in_house/3/4.phrasing_guidance: Emphasise home comforts and wealth gained through effort. Do not characterise the spouse.

lord_in_house/3/5.summary: Courage and skill flow into intelligence, creativity and children: the person has children and good qualities; BPHS adds a caution about the spouse when malefics influence the lord.
common_outcomes: children and good qualities
help and gains through siblings (Raman, Rath)
comfort in finances (Raman)
rare_outcomes: BPHS traditional view: with malefic influence, a cruel or formidable spouse
Raman: adoption into a rich family

by_area.personality: Virtuous and capable (BPHS 24.29); helpful to others (Charak).
by_area.career: If well disposed, success in government service or large-scale agriculture (Raman HTJH I).
by_area.finance: Financially well off (Raman). Rath: from the 5th the 3rd lord aspects the 11th and has argala on the 2nd, supporting gains and wealth, provided the 5th lord (its dispositor) is well placed.
by_area.relationships: With malefic influence, a traditional line about a harsh spouse (BPHS 24.29; Charak); Raman notes friction in domestic life. Rath adds argala on the 7th, benefit through the spouse.
by_area.family: Children indicated (BPHS 24.29; Charak), though Raman says little pleasure from them; benefit from brothers when well disposed (Raman; Rath: help from siblings and sons' friends).

strengtheners: exaltation: Virgo lagna, Mars in Capricorn
benefic aspects; strong Jupiter
5th lord (the dispositor) well placed (Rath, Crux 6.4)
weakeners_or_cancellations: malefic conjunction or aspect (BPHS 24.29)
debilitation: Gemini lagna (Sun in Libra) and Sagittarius lagna (Saturn in Aries)
dispositor (5th lord) in the 12th: little gain from siblings or children (Rath, Crux 6.4)
lord_in_house/3/5.lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS 34, Laghu Parashari sloka 6 and Bhavartha Ratnakara XII st. 2 class the 3rd lord as a functional malefic, so its placement in a trikona is not counted as a raja-yoga link.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.29 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Sons and good qualities; with malefic conjunction/aspect, a cruel spouse.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.29 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Sons, virtuous; if malefic-linked, a formidable wife.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. VI 'Results of the Lord of the Third House Being Posited in Different Houses' (pp. 73-74)
source_views.view: Little pleasure from children, financially well off, friction in domestic life. Well disposed: much benefit from brothers, large-scale agriculture, adoption by a rich family, or success in government service.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Third lord (pp. 232-233)
source_views.view: Virtuous, blessed with sons, long-lived, ever helping others; with malefic conjunction or aspect, a cruel wife.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 6.4-6.5 (third lord; lords in the third) (pp. 65-66)
source_views.view: A 3rd lord in the 5th aspects the 11th (gains from brothers, sons' friends) and has argala on the 2nd (wealth, family), 4th (happiness) and 7th (benefit from spouse); results depend on the dispositor (5th lord).

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari (Jataka Chandrika), tr. with commentary by O.P. Verma, sloka 6 with notes (and notes to sloka 22)
source_views.view: Lords of the 3rd, 6th and 11th produce evil even when natural benefics; the commentary ranks the 3rd lord as the least inauspicious of these, and quotes the Sajjanaranjani view that 3rd/6th/11th lords placed in their own houses do good.

lord_in_house/3/5.disagreements: Raman's 'little pleasure from children' differs from BPHS and Charak, which give children. Rath is the most positive (gains, wealth, happiness through argala).
lord_in_house/3/5.phrasing_guidance: Speak of creative skills, children and good qualities. Do not characterise the spouse.

lord_in_house/3/6.summary: The lord of siblings and effort in the house of conflict: friction with siblings and maternal uncles, yet considerable wealth and competitive drive.
common_outcomes: disagreements or rivalry with siblings
strong competitive or fighting spirit
wealth through service, competition or litigation
rare_outcomes: BPHS: enmity with maternal uncle, but affection from maternal aunt (ELS rendering)
Raman: accepting illegal gratification (traditional)

by_area.personality: Determined in conflict (BPHS 24.30); Rath 6.4: the 3rd lord in a dusthana keeps impulses under control.
by_area.career: With the 6th lord in the 3rd at the same time (exchange), sport, physical culture or athletics (Raman HTJH I).
by_area.finance: Very wealthy (BPHS 24.30; Raman: becomes rich; Charak: very rich); Rath: sudden gains through conquest or competition.
by_area.health: Charak lists eye trouble and sickliness, and Raman disease when both houses are afflicted (traditional); no medical claims.
by_area.family: Sibling and maternal-relative tensions (BPHS 24.30; Raman; Charak). If well disposed, a younger sibling may join the army or a sibling become a physician (Raman). Bhavartha Ratnakara III st. 6 and 10 carry a traditional line about loss of brothers (late in life if benefics are there); never predict.

strengtheners: own sign: Aries lagna (Mercury in Virgo, also exalted and 6th lord) and Libra lagna (Jupiter in Pisces, also 6th lord)
strong malefic in the 6th fights obstacles well (Phaladeepika 15.7)
3rd lord joined by other dusthana lords here: viparita rajayoga (Rath, Crux 6.4)
6th lord in the 3rd at the same time: sportsman or athlete (Raman HTJH I)
weakeners_or_cancellations: debilitation: Scorpio lagna (Saturn in Aries) and Aquarius lagna (Mars in Cancer)
malefic affliction increases conflict
3rd and 6th both afflicted: illness, enemies and deceit (Raman HTJH I)
lord_in_house/3/6.lagna_or_context_notes: Phaladeepika 15.7 says strong malefics in the 3rd/6th/11th from a bhava support it, consistent with BPHS giving wealth alongside sibling friction.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.30 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Enmity with siblings, very wealthy, enmity with maternal uncle, liked by maternal aunt.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.30 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Inimical to co-born, affluent, inimical to maternal uncle.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 15.5
source_views.view: A bhava lord in a dusthana harms its bhava (here siblings/courage).

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. VI 'Results of the Lord of the Third House Being Posited in Different Houses' (pp. 73-74)
source_views.view: Hates brothers and relatives, rich, maternal relatives suffer, accepts illegal gratification. Well disposed: a younger brother joins the army, a brother becomes a physician; with the 6th lord in the 3rd, a sportsman or athlete; both afflicted: disease, enemies, deceit.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Third lord (pp. 232-233)
source_views.view: Enmity with brothers, very rich, little comfort from maternal uncle, desires maternal aunt, eye diseases, sickly.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 6.4-6.5 (third lord; lords in the third) (pp. 65-66)
source_views.view: The 3rd lord in a dusthana (6th, 8th or 12th) is considered auspicious, as the native's sexual urge and animal instincts are under control; with other dusthana lords it forms viparita rajayoga; involvement of the 6th shows sudden gains through conquest, of the 8th legacy or inheritance.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara of Ramanujacharya (tr. B.V. Raman), ch. III Brothers st. 6 and 10
source_views.view: If the 3rd lord is in the 6th, 8th or 12th, brothers die; if benefics are in those houses, this happens late in life.

lord_in_house/3/6.disagreements: BPHS, Raman, Charak and Bhavartha Ratnakara stress friction with or loss of siblings; Rath reads the 3rd lord in a dusthana as auspicious. All agree on wealth. The ELS rendering includes the maternal-aunt line, as does Charak.
lord_in_house/3/6.phrasing_guidance: Mention possible sibling disagreements as something to manage and highlight competitive strength and earnings. Avoid predicting estrangement.

lord_in_house/3/7.summary: Effort is directed to partnerships and public service: the person works for government or authorities, with a harder childhood and a more contented later life.
common_outcomes: employment with government or large institutions (BPHS, Charak)
difficulties early in life, improving later (BPHS, Raman, Charak)
many ups and downs (Raman)
rare_outcomes: Raman: danger while travelling (traditional)

by_area.personality: Matures with time: a harder childhood and an easier later life (BPHS 24.31; Raman; Charak).
by_area.career: Service under government or a ruler (BPHS 24.31; Charak: follower of a king); Raman instead warns of the displeasure of authorities.
by_area.relationships: Charak gives a good-natured spouse; Raman calls the union unfortunate. Traditional views; check the 7th house.
by_area.family: If fortified, cordial relations among siblings; with the 7th lord in the lagna, a sibling settles abroad and helps the native (Raman HTJH I).

strengtheners: exaltation: Capricorn lagna, Jupiter in Cancer
benefic aspects on the 7th
weakeners_or_cancellations: debilitation: Taurus lagna (Moon in Scorpio) and Pisces lagna (Venus in Virgo)
malefic affliction

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.31 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Government service; unhappy in childhood, content later.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.31 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Serves the king; unhappy in boyhood, happy later.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. VI 'Results of the Lord of the Third House Being Posited in Different Houses' (pp. 73-74)
source_views.view: May incur the displeasure of rulers; many vicissitudes; suffering in childhood; unfortunate union; danger while travelling. Fortified: cordial feelings between brothers; with the 7th lord in the lagna, a brother settles abroad and helps.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Third lord (pp. 232-233)
source_views.view: Troubled in childhood, comfortable later; follower of a king; good-natured wife.

lord_in_house/3/7.disagreements: BPHS and Charak are favourable (service, a contented later life, a good spouse); Raman is cautionary (trouble with authorities, ups and downs, unfortunate union, travel risk). All agree on a harder childhood.
lord_in_house/3/7.phrasing_guidance: Frame as steady service and a life that improves with time.

lord_in_house/3/8.summary: Effort and courage fall into the house of hidden and difficult matters. BPHS gives some of its harshest lines here (dishonesty, servitude, trouble with authorities); modern readers emphasise struggle, research and hidden work, and the outcome depends heavily on dignity.
common_outcomes: periods where effort feels blocked or unrewarded (Raman: 'victim of misfortune')
subordinate roles (BPHS, Charak)
need for caution with authorities and legal matters (Raman, Charak)
possible legacy or inheritance (Rath 6.4)
rare_outcomes: BPHS traditional view: inclination to theft and living by servitude
BPHS traditional view: a severe end connected with the state; never predict this
Raman: false accusations, a legal case, or trouble over bequests

by_area.career: Career may not run smoothly (Raman HTJH I); BPHS and Charak speak of servitude.
by_area.finance: Rath: with the 8th house involved, the 3rd lord can show legacy or inheritance.
by_area.health: Raman has a traditional line about a serious illness; no medical predictions.
by_area.relationships: Raman: marriage unfortunate (traditional; do not predict).
by_area.family: Sibling matters weakened (Phaladeepika 15.5). Raman and Bhavartha Ratnakara III st. 6 and 10 carry a traditional line about losing a younger brother (late in life if benefics are there); never predict.

strengtheners: own sign: Virgo lagna (Mars in Aries, also 8th lord) and Pisces lagna (Venus in Libra, also 8th lord)
exaltation: Leo lagna, Venus in Pisces
benefic aspect (Phaladeepika 15.3)
3rd lord joined by other dusthana lords here: viparita rajayoga (Rath, Crux 6.4)
weakeners_or_cancellations: combust, debilitated or in an enemy sign without benefic aspect (Phaladeepika 15.3)
malefic conjunctions
lord_in_house/3/8.lagna_or_context_notes: For Virgo and Pisces lagna the 3rd lord also owns the 8th and sits in its own sign. O.P. Verma's commentary on Laghu Parashari treats an 8th lord that also owns a trishadaya house as particularly inauspicious, but adds that the 8th lord placed in the 8th removes the evil of 8th lordship, which is this case.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.32 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com, with word-by-word)
source_views.view: Becomes a thief, lives by servitude, may die at the king's gate (traditional).

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.32 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Thief, serves others, dies at the palace gate.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 15.3, 15.5
source_views.view: A lord in the 8th without benefic help harms its bhava; benefic aspect restores it.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. VI 'Results of the Lord of the Third House Being Posited in Different Houses' (pp. 73-74)
source_views.view: Involvement in a criminal case or false accusations; trouble over death or bequests; unfortunate marriage; career not smooth; victim of misfortune; serious illness and loss of a younger brother.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Third lord (pp. 232-233)
source_views.view: A thief, servile, capital punishment from the ruler, adverse for siblings.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 6.4-6.5 (third lord; lords in the third) (pp. 65-66)
source_views.view: The 3rd lord in a dusthana (6th, 8th or 12th) is considered auspicious, as the native's sexual urge and animal instincts are under control; with other dusthana lords it forms viparita rajayoga; involvement of the 6th shows sudden gains through conquest, of the 8th legacy or inheritance.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara of Ramanujacharya (tr. B.V. Raman), ch. III Brothers st. 6 and 10
source_views.view: If the 3rd lord is in the 6th, 8th or 12th, brothers die; if benefics are in those houses, this happens late in life.

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari (Jataka Chandrika), tr. with commentary by O.P. Verma, notes to slokas 7 and 9
source_views.view: An 8th lord that is also a trishadaya lord is particularly inauspicious; the 8th lord in the 8th eradicates the evils of 8th lordship.

lord_in_house/3/8.disagreements: BPHS, Raman, Charak and Bhavartha Ratnakara agree on a difficult placement (legal trouble, servitude, harm to siblings). Rath dissents: the 3rd lord in any dusthana is auspicious, and the 8th adds legacy. BPHS's harshest lines are not repeated in the general bhava rules and are not applied literally.
lord_in_house/3/8.phrasing_guidance: Never call the person dishonest and never mention manner of death. Say effort may meet obstacles and advise care with authorities, contracts and legal matters; highlight research ability.

lord_in_house/3/9.summary: Effort meets fortune and the father: BPHS says less happiness from the father, but fortune rising through women or the spouse, and happiness through children.
common_outcomes: fortune helped by women or the spouse
long journeys (Raman)
less closeness or support from father

by_area.personality: Learned (Charak); life marked by sudden and unexpected changes (Raman HTJH I).
by_area.career: Long journeys (Raman).
by_area.finance: Fortune through women or after marriage (BPHS 24.33; Raman; Charak).
by_area.relationships: Fortune improves after marriage (Raman).
by_area.family: Less closeness with the father (BPHS 24.33; Raman: father untrustworthy; Charak: no comfort from father), sharper if afflicted (Raman); help from children (Charak); if well disposed, a brother inherits ancestral property and the native benefits through him (Raman).

strengtheners: benefic aspects, strong 9th house
weakeners_or_cancellations: debilitation: Cancer lagna, Mercury in Pisces
malefic affliction to the 9th or Sun
lord_in_house/3/9.lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS 34, Laghu Parashari sloka 6 and Bhavartha Ratnakara XII st. 2 class the 3rd lord as a functional malefic, consistent with the mixed result for father and fortune.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.33 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Lacks father's happiness; fortune rises through women; family happiness.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.33 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Lacks paternal bliss; fortunate through wife; enjoys children.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. VI 'Results of the Lord of the Third House Being Posited in Different Houses' (pp. 73-74)
source_views.view: Fortune improves after marriage; father untrustworthy; long journeys; sudden changes. Favourably disposed: brother inherits ancestral property and helps the native; afflicted: misunderstandings with father.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Third lord (pp. 232-233)
source_views.view: Acquires fortune through women; no comfort from father; help from children; learned.

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari (Jataka Chandrika), tr. with commentary by O.P. Verma, sloka 6 with notes (and notes to sloka 22)
source_views.view: Lords of the 3rd, 6th and 11th produce evil even when natural benefics; the commentary ranks the 3rd lord as the least inauspicious of these, and quotes the Sajjanaranjani view that 3rd/6th/11th lords placed in their own houses do good.

lord_in_house/3/9.disagreements: BPHS renderings differ on 'women' vs 'wife' as the source of fortune; Raman specifies 'after marriage'. All sources agree on less support from the father.
lord_in_house/3/9.phrasing_guidance: Highlight fortune through partner and personal initiative. Mention father matters gently, as possible distance rather than loss.

lord_in_house/3/10.summary: Effort and enterprise shape the career: all comforts and self-earned wealth, with a traditional caution about supporting unworthy people.
common_outcomes: career built through effort and skill
self-earned wealth and comforts
gain from work-related travel (Raman)
support from siblings (Raman)
rare_outcomes: BPHS traditional view: supporting or associating with difficult or wicked women

by_area.personality: Happy and intelligent (Raman HTJH I).
by_area.career: Strong career through initiative (BPHS 24.34); gains from journeys connected with the profession (Raman); honoured by the ruler (Charak).
by_area.finance: Self-made wealth (BPHS 24.34; Raman: becomes rich; Charak: earns through own efforts).
by_area.relationships: BPHS and Charak (supporting a wicked woman) and Raman (a quarrelsome, unfaithful spouse) carry harsh traditional lines; do not predict.
by_area.family: Siblings do well and help the native in every way (Raman).

strengtheners: own sign: Leo lagna (Venus in Taurus, also 10th lord) and Aquarius lagna (Mars in Scorpio, also 10th lord)
exaltation: Libra lagna, Jupiter in Cancer
Mars with dig bala in the 10th
if the 3rd and 10th lords are conjoined or aspect each other, the 3rd lord's dasa gives fortune while the 10th lord's does not (Bhavartha Ratnakara XI st. 4)
weakeners_or_cancellations: malefic affliction or combustion
lord_in_house/3/10.lagna_or_context_notes: For Leo and Aquarius lagna the 3rd lord also owns the 10th and sits in own sign.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.34 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: All comforts, self-earned wealth, supports difficult women.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.34 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: All kinds of happiness, self-made wealth, nourishes wicked women.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. VI 'Results of the Lord of the Third House Being Posited in Different Houses' (pp. 73-74)
source_views.view: Quarrelsome and faithless wife; becomes rich, happy, intelligent; gain from journeys connected with profession. All brothers shine and help the native.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Third lord (pp. 232-233)
source_views.view: Earns wealth through own efforts, varied comforts, looks after a wicked woman, honoured by the ruler.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara of Ramanujacharya (tr. B.V. Raman), ch. XI Results of dasas st. 4 with Raman's note
source_views.view: If the 10th and 3rd lords are conjoined or in mutual aspect, the native lacks fortune in the 10th lord's dasa and enjoys fortunate results in the 3rd lord's dasa.

lord_in_house/3/10.disagreements: All sources agree on self-made wealth; the spouse/association line takes a different form in each (BPHS and Charak: supporting a wicked woman; Raman: a quarrelsome spouse).
lord_in_house/3/10.phrasing_guidance: Positive about self-made career. Omit the line about women or present it only as an archaic textual statement if asked.

lord_in_house/3/11.summary: Effort turns into gains: profits in business, intelligence and courage, often in service roles and without needing much formal education.
common_outcomes: gains through business, earned with effort (BPHS, Raman, Charak)
brave and clever
service to or dependence on others (BPHS, Raman, Charak)

by_area.personality: Bold and resourceful (BPHS 24.35); Raman and Charak add vindictiveness or foolishness and dependence on others.
by_area.career: Business, trade and service roles (BPHS 24.35); dependent on or subservient to others (Raman; Charak: servile).
by_area.finance: Gains in business (BPHS 24.35), earned with effort (Raman; Charak: earns through own efforts).
by_area.health: Raman and Charak give a weak or sickly constitution (traditional); no medical claims.

strengtheners: exaltation: Gemini lagna (Sun in Aries) and Sagittarius lagna (Saturn in Libra)
strong malefics in upachayas do well (Phaladeepika 15.7)
weakeners_or_cancellations: debilitation: Virgo lagna, Mars in Cancer
malefic affliction

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.35 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Always profitable in business; intelligent, brave, serves others even with little education.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.35 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Gains in trade, intelligent though not learned, adventurous, serves others.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 15.7
source_views.view: Strong malefics in 3/6/11 from a bhava support it.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. VI 'Results of the Lord of the Third House Being Posited in Different Houses' (pp. 73-74)
source_views.view: Not a very good combination: earnings with effort, vindictive, unattractive and emaciated body, subservient or dependent, frequent illness.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Third lord (pp. 232-233)
source_views.view: Foolish, weak, sickly, servile, courageous; earns wealth through own efforts; indulges in physical pleasures.

lord_in_house/3/11.disagreements: BPHS is favourable (constant business gains); Raman calls it 'not a very good combination' and Charak is similarly negative on health and character. All agree that gains come through effort.
lord_in_house/3/11.phrasing_guidance: Positive: gains through effort and enterprise. Avoid implying lack of education.

lord_in_house/3/12.summary: Effort and courage are spent in the house of loss: BPHS warns of spending on improper ends and a harsh father, but says fortune comes through a woman.
common_outcomes: travel or wandering abroad (Charak)
expenses on pleasures or improper ends (BPHS, Charak)
fortune helped by a woman or spouse (BPHS, Raman, Charak)
rare_outcomes: BPHS traditional view: spending on wrongful ends; a harsh or cruel father

by_area.personality: Seclusion and great ups and downs (Raman HTJH I).
by_area.career: Wanders in foreign countries (Charak).
by_area.finance: Spending on improper ends needs discipline (BPHS 24.36; Charak: wastes money in wicked pursuits); Raman: the native may become poor on account of a younger sibling.
by_area.relationships: Fortune through a woman or through marriage (BPHS 24.36; Raman; Charak).
by_area.family: Strained relationship with the father (BPHS; Raman: unscrupulous father; Charak: cruel father) and sorrow through relatives (Raman; Charak: opposed to relatives and friends). Bhavartha Ratnakara III st. 10 carries a traditional line about loss of brothers; never predict.
by_area.spirituality: Inclination to seclusion (Raman).

strengtheners: own sign: Cancer lagna (Mercury in Gemini, also 12th lord) and Capricorn lagna (Jupiter in Sagittarius, also 12th lord)
exaltation: Scorpio lagna (Saturn in Libra) and Aquarius lagna (Mars in Capricorn)
benefic aspects
3rd lord joined by other dusthana lords here: viparita rajayoga (Rath, Crux 6.4)
weakeners_or_cancellations: debilitation: Aries lagna, Mercury in Pisces
malefic affliction (Phaladeepika 15.5)
lord_in_house/3/12.lagna_or_context_notes: For Cancer and Capricorn lagna one planet owns both the 3rd and 12th and sits in own sign.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.36 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: Spends on improper ends, harsh father, fortune through women.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.36 (Santhanam-based text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Spends on vice, wicked father, fortunate through a woman.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 15.5
source_views.view: Lord in a dusthana harms its bhava; benefic aspect restores it.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. VI 'Results of the Lord of the Third House Being Posited in Different Houses' (pp. 73-74)
source_views.view: Sorrow through relatives, fortune from marriage, seclusion, great ups and downs, unscrupulous father; the youngest brother may be a tyrant and impoverish the native.

source_views.source: K.S. Charak, Elements of Vedic Astrology, ch. 'Placement of Lords of Houses': Third lord (pp. 232-233)
source_views.view: Wastes money in wicked pursuits, cruel father, fortunate through women, opposed to relatives and friends, wanders in foreign countries.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 6.4-6.5 (third lord; lords in the third) (pp. 65-66)
source_views.view: The 3rd lord in a dusthana (6th, 8th or 12th) is considered auspicious, as the native's sexual urge and animal instincts are under control; with other dusthana lords it forms viparita rajayoga; involvement of the 6th shows sudden gains through conquest, of the 8th legacy or inheritance.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara of Ramanujacharya (tr. B.V. Raman), ch. III Brothers st. 6 and 10

lord_in_house/3/12.disagreements: BPHS, Raman and Charak are negative on spending, relatives and the father but positive on fortune through a woman; Rath reads the 3rd lord in a dusthana as auspicious. Charak's foreign wandering is not in BPHS 24.36.
lord_in_house/3/12.phrasing_guidance: Suggest channelling energy and spending mindfully. Do not characterise the father negatively as a prediction.

lord_in_house/4/1.summary: Home, mother and inner happiness merge with the self: the person is learned and virtuous, enjoys land and vehicles, and has happiness through the mother.

ownership of land, home or vehicles
close, supportive bond with mother
emotional security forms part of identity

by_area.finance: Land and vehicles (BPHS 24.37; Charak). Raman: may lose inherited wealth; whether the 4th lord here is strong, middling or weak shows birth into a rich, middling or poor family.
by_area.family: Mother's happiness and support (BPHS 24.37; Charak). Rath 7.3.1: being in trine to the 9th, good relations with the father and gains from his position.

exaltation: Libra lagna (Saturn in Libra, yogakaraka) and Capricorn lagna (Mars in Capricorn)
benefic aspects; strong Moon

Verma's notes to Laghu Parashari sloka 7 count as auspicious for Libra; here it is also exalted in the lagna. For Gemini and Sagittarius lagna one planet owns the 1st and 4th. Raman ('Important Combinations') says the 4th lord in the lagna or the 7th gives a house without difficulty.

lord_in_house/4/1.disagreements: Textual: the enjoylearningsanskrit edition reads verse 37 as 4th lord in the 2nd (two verses for the 2nd, none for the 1st), likely a transcription issue; the Santhanam-based text and Charak assign the learning/lands/vehicles/mother result to the lagna. Raman's text for this placement (learned but shy in assemblies, loses inherited wealth) matches what BPHS 24.43 and Charak give for the 4th lord in the 7th, so Raman appears to follow a different verse order here.
lord_in_house/4/1.phrasing_guidance: Positive: learning, home comforts and maternal support. Avoid promising property.

lord_in_house/4/4.lagna_or_context_notes: For Leo (Mars), Libra (Saturn) and Aquarius (Venus) lagna the 4th lord also owns a trikona, which Laghu Parashari (sloka 7 notes) treats as auspicious. For Virgo lagna Bhavartha Ratnakara (I, Kanya st. 5) gives yoga when Jupiter (4th lord) and Venus (9th lord) are in the 4th, though Raman notes Venus's dasa works better because Jupiter suffers as a kendra lord. BPHS 15.9 has a specific traditional line about speech when the 4th lord is in a movable sign in the 4th with Mars in the 6th or 12th; treat as text-specific.

lord_in_house/4/7.phrasing_guidance: Emphasise learning and partnership-based home life. Present the inheritance line as a tendency to rely on own earnings rather than family assets.

inherited or ancestral property (jagannathhora.com, practitioner site)

by_area.family: Parental happiness limited (BPHS 24.44; Raman; Charak: little help from father and mother); Raman lists friction with the mother when the 4th lord is 8th from the lagna or its lord.

lord_in_house/4/8.phrasing_guidance: Speak of home changes and the need to build inner security. Never mention sexual capacity; avoid predictions about parents' health.

It is a yogakaraka for Cancer (Mars 5+10), Libra (Saturn 4+5) and Capricorn (Venus 5+10). Where it co-owns a difficult house the sources differ: Venus (5+12) is the only benefic for Gemini (BPHS 34.25, Raman) and gives mainly 5th-house results (Frawley); Mars (5+12) for Sagittarius is auspicious (BPHS 34.37, Raman); Jupiter (5+8) for Leo is auspicious in BPHS 34.29 but neutral in Raman; Mercury (5+8) for Aquarius gives mixed effects (BPHS 34.41) and is neutral in Raman; Saturn (5+6) for Virgo is neutral in Raman and less auspicious in Frawley because its mulatrikona sign rules the 6th; Mercury (2+5) for Taurus is 'somewhat inauspicious' in BPHS 34.23 but a benefic in Raman. The lagna is both a kendra and a trikona (BPHS 34.2-7), so a trikona lord here is a classic auspicious link.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.49 (tr. G.C. Sharma; cross-check translation)
source_views.view: Scholarly, happy through children, but a miser, crooked, and one who takes others' wealth (same sense as the other translation).

source_views.view: If the 5th lord occupies or aspects the lagna and the lagna lord is similarly linked to the 5th, the child is obedient; the 5th lord in the 1st, 2nd or 3rd gives a male first child.

source_views.view: Fifth lord in the ascendant: very intelligent, kind-hearted and knowledgeable, with knowledge of politics; effects of the 5th lord in any house depend on its natural nature, the houses it aspects and its argala.

lord_in_house/5/1.disagreements: BPHS 24.49 mixes praise with moral criticism (miser, crooked, takes others' wealth). Braha and Rath give only positive traits. Raman resolves it by condition: the authority and grace results when well associated, the deceitful results when afflicted. Raman also says 'few children' where BPHS and Braha give happiness from children.
lord_in_house/5/1.phrasing_guidance: Lead with intelligence, kindness and closeness to children. Present the 'miserly or calculating' line only as a traditional caution about self-interest, never as a character verdict.

lord_in_house/5/2.summary: The lord of intelligence and children in the house of wealth, speech and family links learning to earning. BPHS, Raman and Braha agree on wealth, learning and family support; Raman adds that a weak, afflicted lord reverses this.

Learned, a good speaker; Raman and Braha both name astrology, and Braha mathematics and teaching
Children who add to family standing (BPHS 24.50; Raman: well-behaved children)
rare_outcomes: Raman: gains from government; a beautiful spouse
Braha: income through temples or teaching religious techniques; enjoys good food
Rath: love of money and a good voice, possibly a singer; if the 5th lord is a natural malefic it can be adverse for wealth
Raman, when weak and afflicted: poverty, loss through government displeasure, family misunderstandings, becoming a temple priest

by_area.personality: Learned and articulate (BPHS 24.50; Braha: great intelligence, good imagination).
by_area.career: Braha: education, astrology or mathematics; Raman: learned, a good astrologer, gains from government.
by_area.finance: Wealth (BPHS 24.50; Braha; Rath: good finances). Raman: poverty and loss through government displeasure if weak and afflicted.
by_area.relationships: BPHS 24.50: attached to the spouse (Sharma) or fond of women (other translation); Raman: a beautiful spouse.
by_area.family: Supports and heads the family, honoured (BPHS 24.50); happy, large or prosperous family (Braha).
by_area.spirituality: Braha: may earn through temples or by teaching religious techniques.

Absorbed in one's own work (BPHS 24.51)
Talent in music, dance, drama or writing (Braha)

Raman, unfavourable: concerns for children, misunderstandings with brothers and continuing occupational troubles

lord_in_house/5/3.phrasing_guidance: Emphasise sibling bonds, effort and creative or communicative talent. Present the 'miserly or tale-bearer' line as a traditional caution, not a description.

Adviser, minister or preceptor to those in power (BPHS 24.52; Raman)

lord_in_house/5/4.phrasing_guidance: Lead with a happy home, a supportive mother and an advisory gift. Do not predict the number or sex of children.

lord_in_house/5/5.summary: The 5th lord in its own house strengthens intelligence, merit and the house of children. BPHS and Phaladeepika make the children result depend on benefic influence; Raman and Braha add mantra, mathematics and leadership of religious bodies.
common_outcomes: Highly intelligent, virtuous and dear to friends (BPHS 24.53; Braha)
Children when benefics influence the lord (BPHS 24.53; Phaladeepika 12.9); Raman: a number of sons when favourable
Great in one's own field; expertise in mantra, mathematics or scripture (Raman; Braha)
rare_outcomes: Raman and Braha: may head a religious or spiritual institution
Braha: interest in politics or rulership; successful investments and speculation
Bhavartha Ratnakara 4.16 and 9.19: the 5th lord in the 5th together with the 4th lord in the 4th gives fortune and vehicles, and with the 10th lord in the 10th gives power and fame
Bhavartha Ratnakara (ch. XI st. 5): 5th, 7th and 9th lords in their own houses give holy dips during their periods
Raman, afflicted: concerns for children, not keeping one's word, wavering mind, cruelty (traditional view)

by_area.personality: Virtuous and dear to friends (BPHS 24.53); integrity and merit (Braha). Raman: wavering and unreliable if afflicted.
by_area.career: Raman: becomes great in his own line; expert in mantra shastra or mathematics; befriends the powerful. Braha: may be a ruler or politician.
by_area.finance: Braha: successful investments and a liking for speculation.
by_area.relationships: Braha: happy love affairs.
by_area.family: Children if benefics are involved, none or grief if malefics (BPHS 24.53; Phaladeepika 12.9); Raman: a number of sons when favourable.
by_area.spirituality: Knowledge of mantras or scriptures, religious-minded, strong past merit (Braha); expert in mantra shastra, may head a religious institution (Raman).

strengtheners: Benefic aspect or conjunction on the lord (BPHS 24.53; Phaladeepika 12.9)
The 4th lord in the 4th or the 10th lord in the 10th at the same time (Bhavartha Ratnakara 4.16, 9.19)
Jupiter joining or aspecting the 5th lord (Bhavartha Ratnakara 4.19: birth of children is indicated)
The 5th lord a benefic and aspected by a benefic or placed in a benefic sign (Raman, 300 Combinations no. 231 Buddhimaturya: intelligence and good character)
The 5th lord well placed and in a vaiseshikamsa (Phaladeepika 16.15: intelligent and open-hearted)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Malefic aspect or conjunction with no benefic aspect (BPHS 24.53; Phaladeepika 12.9: loss of children)
Raman: an afflicted lord gives contrary results
When Jupiter, the natural significator of children, is itself the 5th lord in the 5th, the 'karaka in its own bhava harms it' dictum is sometimes applied; see disagreements
lord_in_house/5/5.lagna_or_context_notes: Functional role (BPHS 34.2-7; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope pp. 13-15): the 5th lord is a trikona lord and auspicious, and BPHS names the 5th a house 'specially for wealth'. It is a yogakaraka for Cancer (Mars 5+10), Libra (Saturn 4+5) and Capricorn (Venus 5+10). Where it co-owns a difficult house the sources differ: Venus (5+12) is the only benefic for Gemini (BPHS 34.25, Raman) and gives mainly 5th-house results (Frawley); Mars (5+12) for Sagittarius is auspicious (BPHS 34.37, Raman); Jupiter (5+8) for Leo is auspicious in BPHS 34.29 but neutral in Raman; Mercury (5+8) for Aquarius gives mixed effects (BPHS 34.41) and is neutral in Raman; Saturn (5+6) for Virgo is neutral in Raman and less auspicious in Frawley because its mulatrikona sign rules the 6th; Mercury (2+5) for Taurus is 'somewhat inauspicious' in BPHS 34.23 but a benefic in Raman. Jupiter is the 5th lord in the 5th for Leo (Sagittarius) and Scorpio (Pisces); see the karaka debate under disagreements.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.53
source_views.view: Fifth lord in the 5th: there will be children if a benefic aspects or joins it; with malefic influence, childlessness. The native is virtuous and dear to friends.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.53 (tr. G.C. Sharma; cross-check translation)
source_views.view: Progeny if a benefic is related to the lord; no issue if a malefic is related; the native is virtuous and dear to friends.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. VIII 'Results of the Lord of the Fifth House being placed in Different Houses' (pp. 113-114)
source_views.view: Favourable: a number of sons, great in his own line; otherwise an expert in mantra shastra who befriends the powerful, possibly an expert in mathematics or head of a religious institution. Afflicted: contrary results, children at risk, not keeping his word, wavering and cruel.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer (1986), 'The ruler of the 5th house placed in the...' (archive.org file 'Ancient Hindu astrology_James Braha')
source_views.view: Own sign: happiness from and prosperity of children, highly intelligent, religious, good deeds, successful investments, happy love affairs, knowledge of mantras or scriptures, strong integrity, may head a religious organisation, very strong past merit, interest in politics.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 12.9 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Loss of children is predicted when the 5th lord is debilitated, in an enemy sign, combust or with the 12th, 6th or 8th lords; likewise when the 5th lord is in the 5th without benefic aspect.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara (tr. B.V. Raman, 2nd ed. 1947), ch. IV st. 16; ch. IX st. 19
source_views.view: 4th and 5th lords in their own houses give Bhagyavahana yoga (fortune and vehicles); 10th and 5th lords in the 10th and 5th give power and fame.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara (tr. B.V. Raman, 2nd ed. 1947), ch. VII st. 10 with Raman's notes
source_views.view: The text repeats the dictum that a karaka in its own bhava destroys it (Jupiter in the 5th harms sons); Raman writes that his own long experience contradicts this: Jupiter in the 5th gives a long-lived first son, and only affliction by Mars, Saturn or Rahu spoils it.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 34.2-7, 19-44 (tr. G.C. Sharma)
source_views.view: Lords of trikonas give auspicious results; the 5th and 9th are 'specially for wealth'; lagna-by-lagna lists of auspicious and inauspicious planets (e.g. Mars a full yogakaraka for Cancer, Venus the only auspicious planet for Gemini, Mercury mixed for Aquarius).

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. I, ch. II 'Benefics and Malefics for each Lagna' and 'Yoga Karakas' (pp. 13-15)
source_views.view: Lists benefic, malefic and neutral planets for each lagna; trikona lords are benefic, the 9th more so than the 5th; Mars, Saturn and Venus become yogakarakas when one planet owns a kendra and a trikona (Cancer, Leo, Libra, Taurus, Capricorn, Aquarius).

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, 'Laws of House Rulership' and 'House Lords as Specific Significators' (pp. 157-161)
source_views.view: Lords of trines (1, 5, 9) are always auspicious; a planet ruling a good and a bad house gives mixed results, the house of its mulatrikona sign predominating; Venus (5+12) for Gemini is very auspicious and gives mainly 5th-house results; Saturn (5+6) for Virgo is less auspicious because its mulatrikona rules the 6th.

lord_in_house/5/5.disagreements: Karaka debate: Bhavartha Ratnakara repeats the dictum that Jupiter in the 5th harms children (relevant when Jupiter is the 5th lord for Leo or Scorpio), but its translator Raman disagrees from experience and limits the harm to affliction by Mars, Saturn or Rahu. On the core placement, BPHS, Phaladeepika, Raman and Braha agree that benefic or malefic influence decides the children result.
lord_in_house/5/5.phrasing_guidance: Lead with intelligence, integrity and creative or spiritual gifts. Say children prospects depend on other factors in the chart; never predict childlessness.

lord_in_house/5/6.summary: The lord of children and intelligence in the house of conflict, debt and illness. BPHS, Phaladeepika, Raman and Braha all read difficulty around children and mental ease, with some gain through maternal relatives, service and competition.
common_outcomes: Strain, delay or friction connected with children (BPHS 24.54; Phaladeepika 6.62; Raman; Braha)
A disturbed mind or difficulty with exams (Braha)
Benefits through the maternal uncle (Raman; Braha); good jobs and health (Braha)
rare_outcomes: BPHS 24.54 (both translations read): a son who becomes hostile, losing children, or an adopted child (traditional view)
Raman: enmity with one's own son; if afflicted, adoption from the maternal uncle's line
Phaladeepika 6.62 Pamara yoga (5th lord in 6, 8 or 12): a harsh classical description including loss or lack of children
Braha: knowledge of medicine or healing carried over from a past life

by_area.career: Braha: gets good jobs; knowledge of medicine or healing arts.
by_area.health: Braha: good health.
by_area.relationships: Braha: hardships in love affairs.
by_area.family: Children are the main concern (BPHS 24.54; Raman; Braha). Raman: the maternal uncle may be famous.

strengtheners: Raman: a favourably disposed lord gives a famous maternal uncle rather than the harsher results
Benefic aspect on the 5th house (Phaladeepika 15.5)
Jupiter joining or aspecting the 5th lord (Bhavartha Ratnakara 4.19: birth of children is indicated)
Jupiter, the 5th lord and the lagna lord all in kendras or trikonas (Bhavartha Ratnakara 4.20: happiness from children)
weakeners_or_cancellations: The 5th lord debilitated, in an enemy sign, combust, or joined by the 6th, 8th or 12th lords (Phaladeepika 12.9: loss or grief concerning children)

Raman, 300 Combinations no. 224 Aputra yoga (5th lord in a dusthana: no issue), which Raman calls very general and not to be applied literally (pp. 213-214)
Raman: an afflicted lord here is read for difficulty in having children

It is a yogakaraka for Cancer (Mars 5+10), Libra (Saturn 4+5) and Capricorn (Venus 5+10). lord_in_house/5/6.disagreements: All sources agree on difficulty for children; they differ on severity. Phaladeepika (Pamara) and Raman's Aputra yoga state it absolutely, while Raman himself warns Aputra must not be applied literally, and Braha adds compensations (good health, good jobs).
lord_in_house/5/6.phrasing_guidance: Say children and peace of mind are areas that need care, and that the rest of the chart decides. Never predict childlessness or loss.

lord_in_house/5/7.summary: A trikona lord in a kendra, linking intelligence and children with marriage and partnership. BPHS, Raman and Braha read honour, learning and happiness through children and spouse, but Phaladeepika and Raman's marriage combinations give a sharply opposite traditional rule.
common_outcomes: Respected, righteous and helpful (BPHS 24.55); renowned, learned and prosperous (Raman)
Happiness from children; a child may live abroad and do well (BPHS 24.55; Raman; Braha)
A beautiful, intelligent or devoted spouse and a happy marriage (Braha)
rare_outcomes: Raman: greatly devoted to one's master or employer; charming personality
Braha: good for health, name and fame, because the 5th lord in the 7th aspects the lagna

Phaladeepika 10.2 (traditional): the 5th lord in the 7th is listed for loss of the wife; Raman's 7th-house combinations say the 7th lord in the 5th or 5th lord in the 7th may deny marriage or children
Exchange with the 7th lord forms a Maha (parivartana) yoga (Phaladeepika 6.32)

by_area.career: Raman: devoted to his master; prosperous.
by_area.finance: Raman: prosperous; a son abroad attains wealth and fame.
by_area.health: Braha: fortunate for health and fame (the lord aspects the lagna).
by_area.relationships: Braha: happy marriage with a beautiful, intelligent or devoted spouse; strong passions. Phaladeepika 10.2 gives an opposite traditional rule (see disagreements).
by_area.family: Happiness from children (BPHS 24.55; Braha); a child may live abroad (Raman; Braha).
by_area.spirituality: Devoted to dharma (BPHS 24.55).

weakeners_or_cancellations: Raman: afflicted, loss concerning children, one dying abroad after attaining fame (traditional view)

Phaladeepika 10.2 and Raman's combination on the 5th-7th link (see disagreements)

lord_in_house/5/7.disagreements: Direct conflict: BPHS 24.55, Raman's lord-placement list and Braha are favourable for marriage and children, while Phaladeepika 10.2 and the combination Raman quotes in his 7th-house chapter make the 5th-7th link a rule for loss of spouse or no marriage or children. Raman presents both without reconciling them.
lord_in_house/5/7.phrasing_guidance: Warm about honour, learning and partnership. Never mention loss of a spouse or childlessness; say marriage and children are judged from several factors together.

lord_in_house/5/8.summary: The lord of intelligence and children in the house of hidden matters and sudden change. BPHS, Phaladeepika, Raman and Braha agree on limited happiness from children and an irritable or troubled mind; BPHS and Raman both mention chest or lung complaints.
common_outcomes: Little happiness from children, or strain with a child (BPHS 24.56; Braha; Phaladeepika 6.62)
Irritable, peevish or unhappy temperament (BPHS 24.56; Raman)

It is a yogakaraka for Cancer (Mars 5+10), Libra (Saturn 4+5) and Capricorn (Venus 5+10). Where it co-owns a difficult house the sources differ: Venus (5+12) is the only benefic for Gemini (BPHS 34.25, Raman) and gives mainly 5th-house results (Frawley); Mars (5+12) for Sagittarius is auspicious (BPHS 34.37, Raman); Jupiter (5+8) for Leo is auspicious in BPHS 34.29 but neutral in Raman; Mercury (5+8) for Aquarius gives mixed effects (BPHS 34.41) and is neutral in Raman; Saturn (5+6) for Virgo is neutral in Raman and less auspicious in Frawley because its mulatrikona sign rules the 6th; Mercury (2+5) for Taurus is 'somewhat inauspicious' in BPHS 34.23 but a benefic in Raman. lord_in_house/5/12.phrasing_guidance: Lead with the spiritual and contemplative orientation. Say children matters are judged from several factors; never predict childlessness.

lord_in_house/6/1.summary: The lord of conflict, service and illness joins the self. BPHS gives a sickly but famous, wealthy and courageous person who is at odds with his own people; Raman and Bhavartha Ratnakara add trouble from cousins, while Raman also names military or penal careers when the lord is well aspected.

Friction with one's own people or cousins (BPHS 24.61; Bhavartha Ratnakara 5.1 with Raman's note)
Hard-working; drawn to army, prisons, medicine or healing (Raman; Braha)

by_area.finance: Rich (BPHS 24.61).
by_area.health: BPHS 24.61 and Bhavartha Ratnakara 5.1: sickly (traditional); Braha: poor health; Rath gives the opposite (good health to self).
by_area.relationships: Bhavartha Ratnakara 5.1: troubled by cousins; Raman's note adds worry from relatives' machinations.
by_area.family: Raman: lives in the maternal uncle's house; Braha: close to the maternal uncle, born to a common family.

lord_in_house/6/1.lagna_or_context_notes: Functional role (BPHS 34.2-7; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope pp. 13-15; Frawley): lords of the 3rd, 6th and 11th give evil effects, and Raman ranks the 6th lord less malefic than the 11th but more than the 3rd. By lagna: Mercury (3+6) is the greatest malefic for Aries and Mars (6+11) the most malefic for Gemini (Raman); Saturn (6+7) for Leo, Jupiter (3+6) for Libra, the Moon for Aquarius and the Sun for Pisces are malefics (BPHS 34.29-44); Venus (6+11) is the only inauspicious planet for Sagittarius (BPHS 34.37). Exceptions: Jupiter (6+9) for Cancer and Mercury (6+9) for Capricorn are auspicious (BPHS 34.27, 34.39; Raman); Mars (1+6) is neutral for Scorpio (BPHS 34.35; Raman); for Taurus, Venus (1+6) is listed as a malefic in BPHS 34.23 but neutral in Raman, and Frawley says a lagna lord stays generally auspicious though tainted by the 6th; Saturn (5+6) for Virgo is neutral in Raman. For Taurus (Venus) and Scorpio (Mars) the 6th lord is the lagna lord itself; Bhavartha Ratnakara 5.8 says that when a weak lagna lord who also owns the 6th is joined by benefics, enemies turn friends.

lord_in_house/6/8.disagreements: Direct conflict: BPHS 24.68, Raman (both books) and Braha are unfavourable; Phaladeepika 6.63 (Harsha) and Rath's Vipareeta principle are favourable. Raman explicitly argues against the favourable reading from practice.
lord_in_house/6/8.phrasing_guidance: Present as 'obstacles can turn around with discipline'. State BPHS's harsh line only as a traditional view if needed; no health, morality or longevity predictions.

lord_in_house/6/9.summary: The lord of conflict and service in the house of fortune, father and dharma. BPHS and Raman both name trade or work in wood and stone with fluctuating fortunes; Raman and Braha agree on friction with the father and benefits from the maternal uncle or cousins.
common_outcomes: Work in wood, stone or building materials; fluctuating professional fortunes (BPHS 24.69; Raman: mason, timber merchant or stone cutter)
Friction or misunderstanding with the father (Raman; Braha)
Benefits from the maternal uncle or cousins (Raman; Braha)
rare_outcomes: Raman: well fortified, the father may be a judge; afflicted, poverty, misfortune through relatives, ingratitude to teachers (traditional view)
Braha: good health, good jobs, honest workers and tenants; but bad luck, little faith and no gains from gurus
BPHS 24.69 (Sharma's note): 'pashana' can also mean poison

by_area.career: Trade in wood and stone with fluctuating fortunes (BPHS 24.69); mason, timber merchant or stone cutter when moderately placed (Raman); good jobs (Braha).
by_area.finance: Raman: poverty if afflicted. Braha: bad luck.
by_area.health: Braha: good health.
by_area.relationships: Benefits from cousins (Raman); powerful or religious maternal uncle (Braha).
by_area.family: Friction with the father (Raman; Braha); Braha: sickly father or a father in medicine.
by_area.spirituality: Braha: little enjoyment of religion, no faith, no gains from gurus; Raman: ungrateful toward preceptors if afflicted (traditional view).

strengtheners: Raman: the lord well fortified gives a judge father and a fortunate maternal uncle
The lagna lord stronger than the 6th lord, in a benefic's sign or amsa and aspected by a benefic (Phaladeepika 16.17: health and comfort)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Raman: afflicted gives poverty and unrighteous deeds (traditional view)

lord_in_house/6/9.lagna_or_context_notes: Functional role (BPHS 34.2-7; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope pp. 13-15; Frawley): lords of the 3rd, 6th and 11th give evil effects, and Raman ranks the 6th lord less malefic than the 11th but more than the 3rd. By lagna: Mercury (3+6) is the greatest malefic for Aries and Mars (6+11) the most malefic for Gemini (Raman); Saturn (6+7) for Leo, Jupiter (3+6) for Libra, the Moon for Aquarius and the Sun for Pisces are malefics (BPHS 34.29-44); Venus (6+11) is the only inauspicious planet for Sagittarius (BPHS 34.37). Exceptions: Jupiter (6+9) for Cancer and Mercury (6+9) for Capricorn are auspicious (BPHS 34.27, 34.39; Raman); Mars (1+6) is neutral for Scorpio (BPHS 34.35; Raman); for Taurus, Venus (1+6) is listed as a malefic in BPHS 34.23 but neutral in Raman, and Frawley says a lagna lord stays generally auspicious though tainted by the 6th; Saturn (5+6) for Virgo is neutral in Raman. For Cancer (Jupiter 6+9) and Capricorn (Mercury 6+9) the 6th lord also owns the 9th and is in its own sign here; BPHS 34 calls both auspicious for those lagnas.

lord_in_house/6/10.summary: The lord of service and competition in the house of career. BPHS is favourable (well known, a gifted speaker, happy abroad, but critical of the father); Raman and Braha are not (enemies blocking career, changes, hypocrisy or dismissal in Raman's harsh lines).

Losses through subordinates or dishonest workers (Braha)
Possible reversal: enemies suffer loss and the native gains, especially with the 12th lord involved (Rath; Phaladeepika 6.63)
rare_outcomes: BPHS 24.72 (both translations): spends on vices, hostile to the learned, cruel to living beings (traditional view); Raman's 300 Combinations quotes this against Harsha yoga
Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope: even well disposed, sorrow through a destructive nature; afflicted, a hard existence (traditional view)

By lagna: Mercury (3+6) is the greatest malefic for Aries and Mars (6+11) the most malefic for Gemini (Raman); Saturn (6+7) for Leo, Jupiter (3+6) for Libra, the Moon for Aquarius and the Sun for Pisces are malefics (BPHS 34.29-44); Venus (6+11) is the only inauspicious planet for Sagittarius (BPHS 34.37). Exceptions: Jupiter (6+9) for Cancer and Mercury (6+9) for Capricorn are auspicious (BPHS 34.27, 34.39; Raman); Mars (1+6) is neutral for Scorpio (BPHS 34.35; Raman); for Taurus, Venus (1+6) is listed as a malefic in BPHS 34.23 but neutral in Raman, and Frawley says a lagna lord stays generally auspicious though tainted by the 6th; Saturn (5+6) for Virgo is neutral in Raman.

lord_in_house/6/12.disagreements: Direct conflict: BPHS 24.72, Raman (both books) and Braha are unfavourable; Phaladeepika 6.63 and Rath's Vipareeta principle are favourable. Raman argues from practice that the favourable reading rarely holds in full.

lord_in_house/7/1.summary: The lord of marriage and partnership joins the self, so partners shape the person's identity. Raman and Braha read a spouse known from childhood and a stable partnership; Rath adds a dominating streak; BPHS is critical, describing restlessness and wandering affections.

Good-looking and fortunate but dominating with spouse and partners (Rath)
rare_outcomes: BPHS 24.73 (both translations): goes after others' spouses, clever but of crooked conduct, lacking courage, prone to wind (vata) complaints (traditional view)

Braha: healthy, powerful, respected; 7th-house matters especially fruitful because the lord aspects its own house

by_area.personality: Intelligent and able to weigh pros and cons (Raman); healthy, powerful, respected (Braha); dominating (Rath). BPHS 24.73: clever but unsteady (traditional view).
by_area.career: Braha: successful partnerships.
by_area.finance: Braha: a beautiful or wealthy spouse.
by_area.health: BPHS 24.73: wind-type complaints (traditional note only).

Raman adds that a natural benefic owning a kendra stops acting as a malefic when it occupies that same kendra. The 7th lord is also a maraka (Raman's notes to Bhavartha Ratnakara ch. X), used only for timing and never stated to users. lord_in_house/7/12.lagna_or_context_notes: Functional role (BPHS 34.2-7, 34.14; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope pp. 13-15; Frawley): the 7th is a kendra; natural benefics owning kendras lose their benefic quality and natural malefics owning them stop being inauspicious, and BPHS names the 7th and 10th 'specially for happiness'. Raman adds that a natural benefic owning a kendra stops acting as a malefic when it occupies that same kendra. The 7th lord is also a maraka (Raman's notes to Bhavartha Ratnakara ch. X), used only for timing and never stated to users. By lagna: Venus (2+7) for Aries is a 'direct killer' and Mars (7+12) for Taurus a killer (BPHS 34.19-24); Jupiter (7+10) for Gemini and (4+7) for Virgo is malefic (BPHS 34.25, 34.31; Raman); Saturn (7+8) for Cancer and Mars (2+7) for Libra are killers (BPHS 34.27, 34.33); Saturn (6+7) for Leo and Venus (7+12) for Scorpio are malefic (BPHS 34.29, 34.35); Mercury (7+10) for Sagittarius can confer a yoga with the Sun (BPHS 34.37) though Raman counts it evil; the Moon for Capricorn and Mercury (4+7) for Pisces are malefic (BPHS 34.39, 34.43); the Sun for Aquarius is a killer in BPHS 34.41 but a benefic in Raman. For Taurus (Mars 7+12) and Scorpio (Venus 7+12) the 7th lord also owns the 12th and is in its own sign here.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.84 (tr. G.C. Sharma; cross-check translation)
source_views.view: Incurs penury, a miser, livelihood related to clothes; the wife is a spendthrift.

source_views.view: Planets in the 12th show losses to the houses they own: the 7th lord in the 12th gives a spouse from a poor family; for Virgo or Gemini lagna the badhaka 7th lord Jupiter in the 12th gives excellent results, its dasa marked by joy and prosperity.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events (1998), ch. X 10.3.1-10.3.3 (pp. 149-150) (archive.org file 'Crux Of Vedic Astrology - Timing Of Events - Sanjay Rath')
source_views.view: The 7th lord behaves like Venus; its house position shows the native's attitude to the spouse (dominating in the 1st, loving spouse and family in the 4th, harmony and respect in the 7th, obsessed with the spouse in the 10th); in the 6th, 8th or 12th the spouse is of a different status and a culture gap is seen.

Hardships, debts or trouble from superiors and authorities (Raman; Braha)
Interest in spiritual, ascetic or occult subjects (Braha)

Raman: with the lagna lord in the lagna, penury and debts; severely afflicted, disfigurement and government trouble (traditional view)

Braha: accident-prone; court cases; a difficult start in life

lord_in_house/8/1.lagna_or_context_notes: Functional role (BPHS 34.2-7; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope pp. 13-15; Frawley; Braha): BPHS says the 8th lord is not auspicious, being 12th from the 9th; co-owning the 3rd, 7th or 11th makes it specifically harmful, co-owning a trikona makes it auspicious, and the Sun or Moon as 8th lord is not evil (Raman: neutral). Frawley calls the 2nd, 8th and 12th lords functionally neutral but the stain of the 8th the greatest; Braha warns that despite the sages' neutral rating a dusthana lord carries the most malefic energy. By lagna: Mars (1+8) is helpful for Aries (BPHS 34.19; Raman: benefic) and Venus (1+8) neutral for Libra (BPHS 34.33), and as lagna lords both stay generally auspicious (Frawley). Specifically harmful: Jupiter (8+11) for Taurus, Saturn (7+8) for Cancer, Mars (3+8) for Virgo, Mercury (8+11) for Scorpio, Venus (3+8) for Pisces. With a trikona: Saturn (8+9) for Gemini gives more good than bad because its mulatrikona rules the 9th (Frawley); Jupiter (5+8) for Leo is auspicious in BPHS 34.29, neutral in Raman; Mercury (5+8) for Aquarius is mixed (BPHS 34.41). The Moon (Sagittarius) and Sun (Capricorn) as 8th lords are neutral (BPHS 34.7, 34.39; Raman).

Frawley calls the 2nd, 8th and 12th lords functionally neutral but the stain of the 8th the greatest; Braha warns that despite the sages' neutral rating a dusthana lord carries the most malefic energy. By lagna: Mars (1+8) is helpful for Aries (BPHS 34.19; Raman: benefic) and Venus (1+8) neutral for Libra (BPHS 34.33), and as lagna lords both stay generally auspicious (Frawley). Specifically harmful: Jupiter (8+11) for Taurus, Saturn (7+8) for Cancer, Mars (3+8) for Virgo, Mercury (8+11) for Scorpio, Venus (3+8) for Pisces. With a trikona: Saturn (8+9) for Gemini gives more good than bad because its mulatrikona rules the 9th (Frawley); Jupiter (5+8) for Leo is auspicious in BPHS 34.29, neutral in Raman; Mercury (5+8) for Aquarius is mixed (BPHS 34.41). The Moon (Sagittarius) and Sun (Capricorn) as 8th lords are neutral (BPHS 34.7, 34.39; Raman).

lord_in_house/8/11.summary: The lord of hidden matters in the house of gains, friends and elder siblings. BPHS makes the result hinge on benefic or malefic influence with a hard early life and better later life; Raman and Braha agree on trouble for friends and the elder sibling and on uneven gains, with Braha adding legacies and insurance.
common_outcomes: Trouble for, or strain with, close friends and the elder sibling (Raman; Braha)
Uneven gains, business losses or few opportunities (Raman; Braha); with malefics, lack of wealth (BPHS 24.95)

by_area.family: The elder sibling passes through a difficult time; strained relations (Raman; Braha).

lord_in_house/8/11.lagna_or_context_notes: Functional role (BPHS 34.2-7; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope pp. 13-15; Frawley; Braha): BPHS says the 8th lord is not auspicious, being 12th from the 9th; co-owning the 3rd, 7th or 11th makes it specifically harmful, co-owning a trikona makes it auspicious, and the Sun or Moon as 8th lord is not evil (Raman: neutral). Frawley calls the 2nd, 8th and 12th lords functionally neutral but the stain of the 8th the greatest; Braha warns that despite the sages' neutral rating a dusthana lord carries the most malefic energy. By lagna: Mars (1+8) is helpful for Aries (BPHS 34.19; Raman: benefic) and Venus (1+8) neutral for Libra (BPHS 34.33), and as lagna lords both stay generally auspicious (Frawley). Specifically harmful: Jupiter (8+11) for Taurus, Saturn (7+8) for Cancer, Mars (3+8) for Virgo, Mercury (8+11) for Scorpio, Venus (3+8) for Pisces. With a trikona: Saturn (8+9) for Gemini gives more good than bad because its mulatrikona rules the 9th (Frawley); Jupiter (5+8) for Leo is auspicious in BPHS 34.29, neutral in Raman; Mercury (5+8) for Aquarius is mixed (BPHS 34.41). The Moon (Sagittarius) and Sun (Capricorn) as 8th lords are neutral (BPHS 34.7, 34.39; Raman). For Taurus (Jupiter 8+11) and Scorpio (Mercury 8+11) the 8th lord also owns the 11th and is in its own sign here; BPHS 34.7 calls this combination of lordships specifically harmful.

lord_in_house/8/12.summary: A dusthana lord in the house of loss: Sarala yoga in Phaladeepika and Raman's definition. Raman (with the 12th lord) calls it a Raja yoga that can bring religious learning and authority, Bhavartha Ratnakara says diseases are destroyed under certain conditions, and Braha calls it a 'moksha lord in a moksha house'; BPHS and Braha also read heavy expenses and a traditional longevity caution.
common_outcomes: A strong spiritual nature; meditation and renunciation (Braha); religious learning and piety when the 12th lord is well placed (Raman)
Unexpected expenditure, debts and losses (Raman; Braha; BPHS 24.96)
Difficulties tend to be absorbed: Raman's Raja yoga, Phaladeepika's Sarala yoga

Raman, afflicted: secret vices (traditional view); Braha: troubles in foreign countries

by_area.finance: Unexpected expenditure and pecuniary losses (Raman); many expenses and debts (Braha); spending on evil deeds (BPHS 24.96).
by_area.health: Bhavartha Ratnakara 5.7: under the stated conditions diseases are destroyed; Braha lists left ear, left eye and anal complaints (traditional notes only).
by_area.relationships: Raman: treachery of friends when benefics join; Braha: no money from the marriage partner, little sexual strength.
by_area.spirituality: A moksha lord in a moksha house: strong spiritual nature, meditation, asceticism (Braha); religious learning and piety (Raman).

strengtheners: The 12th lord well placed in a kendra or trikona (Raman: religious learning, piety and authority)
Debilitated or inimical planets with the 8th lord here and a strong lagna lord (Bhavartha Ratnakara 5.7)
8th and 12th lords associating in a dusthana without benefics (Rath, Crux 2.3)

Malefic affliction (Raman: secret vices; BPHS 24.96: worse with a malefic in the 12th)
Raman, 300 Combinations no. 106: the evil of dusthana lordship is only modified

lord_in_house/8/12.disagreements: Direct conflict on longevity: BPHS 24.96 and Braha read a short life, Phaladeepika 6.65 (Sarala) a long one; Bhavartha Ratnakara 5.7 reads freedom from disease under stated conditions. Raman agrees with Rath that benefics spoil this combination, and doubts Sarala's full results in practice.
lord_in_house/8/12.phrasing_guidance: Never discuss lifespan. Frame as difficulties tending to pass, a spiritual or foreign orientation, and a need for mindful spending.

lord_in_house/9/1.summary: The lord of fortune and dharma sits on the lagna, so luck, guidance and principled conduct become part of the person's own identity and body. Classically one of the most fortunate placements of any house lord.
common_outcomes: born fortunate: 'born with luck' (Braha); very fortunate (BPHS 24.97)
honour from rulers or people in authority (BPHS 24.97); drawn to public service (Rath Crux 12.9)
self-made: earns much through own efforts (Raman HTJH; Braha)
virtuous, learned and handsome, with a religious or principled nature (BPHS 24.97; Braha)
close, happy relationship with the father and a good start in life (Braha)
rare_outcomes: common in charts of saints and religious leaders; may head a religious organisation (Braha)
with the lagna lord also in the 1st and a benefic aspect: riches and happiness (Raman HTJH)
exalted 9th lord in the lagna, as in the chart of Sri Rama (Cancer lagna, Jupiter), forms a Lakshmi yoga in the lagna (Rath Crux 12.9; Frawley, Example Charts: Lord Rama)

by_area.personality: Virtuous, handsome, learned (BPHS 24.97); intelligent and well-bred (Rath Crux 12.9); born with wisdom and a strong life purpose (Braha).
by_area.career: Self-made, earns through own effort (Raman HTJH; Braha); interest in public service, since the 9th lord also stands for the ruler or government (Rath Crux 12.9).
by_area.finance: Earns much money through own efforts; fortunate with riches when joined by the lagna lord and aspected by a benefic (Raman HTJH).
by_area.health: Braha lists 'healthy' among the results; a general indication only.
by_area.family: Happy, close bond with the father (Braha). Rath notes that planets joining the 9th lord bring their own houses into the fortune story, e.g. the Moon joining it in Sri Rama's chart tied his fortune to his mothers (Crux 12.9).
by_area.spirituality: Religious, of great merit and faith; may head a religious organisation (Braha).

strengtheners: 9th lord strong in the lagna (a kendra) with the lagna aspected by its own lord: fortunes come in a crowd (JP 14.97)
lagna lord joined with it and a benefic aspect (Raman HTJH); lagna lord with the 9th lord and Jupiter in the 7th gives wealth and vehicles (BPHS 20.29)
exaltation, as in Sri Rama's chart (Rath Crux 12.9; Frawley, Example Charts)
weakeners_or_cancellations: debilitation with combustion of the 9th lord (BPHS 20.12 treats it as very weak for fortune)
Rath: planets conjoining the 9th lord draw their own houses into its results, and those houses should not be afflicted by malefics (Crux 12.9)
if the 9th lord also owns a dusthana (e.g. Saturn 8th+9th for Gemini, Jupiter 9th+12th for Aries, Mercury 9th+12th for Libra), both lordships act (BPHS 24.146-147)
lord_in_house/9/1.lagna_or_context_notes: Results scale with the lord's strength: full, half or a quarter (BPHS 24.145-148). Dual lordship: Frawley (pp. 159-160) weights a planet by its mulatrikona house, so Saturn as 8th+9th lord for Gemini is mainly positive, and a 12th lordship mainly gives the results of the other house ruled. Frawley's Aurobindo chart (Cancer lagna) has the 9th lord Jupiter and 10th lord Mars rising together as a potential Raja yoga.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 12.9 'Placement of the ninth lord'
source_views.view: 9th lord in the lagna: intelligent, well-bred, interested in public service; Sri Rama's chart (exalted Jupiter in Cancer lagna with the Moon) shows a Lakshmi yoga in the lagna, with planets joining the 9th lord shaping the fortune.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Example Charts: Lord Rama; Sri Aurobindo

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata (Vaidyanatha; tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, Vol. II) XIV.97
source_views.view: If the 9th lord is in a kendra or trikona in great strength and the lagna is aspected by its own lord, good fortunes come in a crowd.

lord_in_house/9/1.disagreements: Little disagreement: BPHS, Raman, Braha and Rath are all favourable. Raman and Braha stress fortune that is self-made through effort, while BPHS stresses royal honour; Rath adds that the result depends on which planets join the 9th lord.
lord_in_house/9/1.phrasing_guidance: Describe as a supportive, blessed placement that shows good fortune through principled living and mentors. Avoid promising wealth or fame outright; note that the lord's dignity and the rest of the chart decide the scale.

scholarly, liked by people and wealthy (BPHS 24.98)
good speech and imagination; a good orator (Braha)
happiness with spouse and children (BPHS 24.98); happy family life (Braha)

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. II, ch. XIII 'Results of the Lord of the Ninth House being situated in Different Houses'
source_views.view: Beneficially placed: the father is rich and influential and the native acquires wealth from him; malefic influence ruins paternal property.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer, '9th House' chapter, 'The ruler of the 9th house placed in the' houses
source_views.view: Wealthy, good speech and imagination, an orator, happy family life, learned, popular, wealth from the father.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Example Charts: Nelson Rockefeller
source_views.view: Venus as ruler of the 2nd and 9th houses of wealth (Virgo lagna) is given prominence by its placement.

lord_in_house/9/2.disagreements: Sources agree on wealth and learning. Raman and Braha tie the wealth to the father; BPHS speaks of the native's own scholarship and popularity. The age-32 timing applies only to the exchange case in BPHS 20.10.
lord_in_house/9/2.phrasing_guidance: Frame as good potential for savings, family support and a respected voice. Do not cite the maraka label or any death timing. Give the age-32 note only as a traditional timing hint for the exchange case.

lord_in_house/9/3.summary: Fortune works through effort, communication, siblings and travel. BPHS and Braha see happiness from siblings; Raman says fortune is made through writing and speaking.
common_outcomes: happiness from siblings (BPHS 24.99; Braha)
fortune made through writing, speeches and oratory (Raman HTJH)
advances fortune with the help of siblings (Raman HTJH)
many short and long journeys (Braha)
talent in music, dance, drama or literature (Braha)
rare_outcomes: Rath reads the 9th lord in the 3rd harshly for the father's conduct and calls the native passionate (Crux 6.5, 12.9); a derived-house view, never to be used as a judgement of a parent
afflicted: trouble through one's writings, possibly forcing a sale of paternal property (Raman HTJH)

by_area.personality: Good character and virtuous (BPHS 24.99); courageous and adventurous (Braha).
by_area.career: Writing, speaking and oratory (Raman HTJH); literary talent, efforts succeed with ease (Braha).
by_area.finance: Wealthy (BPHS 24.99); Raman says the father is of moderate means and the native advances his own fortune.
by_area.family: Siblings bring happiness and help fortune (BPHS 24.99; Raman HTJH); a sibling may be close to the father (Braha).
by_area.spirituality: Lucky, religious and spiritual, as the 9th lord aspects its own house from here (Braha).

strengtheners: the 9th lord aspects its own 9th house from the 3rd, so 9th-house matters flourish (Braha)
strength scales the result (BPHS 24.145-148)
weakeners_or_cancellations: malefic affliction: trouble through irrational or offensive writing and loss of paternal property (Raman HTJH)

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.99
source_views.view: Blessed with siblings' happiness, wealthy, virtuous and of good character.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. II, ch. XIII 'Results of the Lord of the Ninth House being situated in Different Houses'
source_views.view: Fortune through writing, speeches and oratory; the father of moderate means; fortune advanced through siblings. Afflicted: trouble through one's writings and sale of paternal property.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer, '9th House' chapter, 'The ruler of the 9th house placed in the' houses
source_views.view: Happiness from siblings, talent in music, drama or literature, efforts succeed, many journeys; the 9th lord aspects its own house so 9th-house matters flourish; lucky and religious; wealthy, long-lived father.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, 6.5 and 12.9
source_views.view: With the 9th lord in the 3rd (the house of passion) the native is passionate and the father is judged untrustworthy; a harsh derived-house reading.

lord_in_house/9/3.disagreements: BPHS, Raman and Braha are favourable on siblings, communication and effort. On the father they conflict: Braha calls him wealthy and long-lived, Raman of moderate means, and Rath reads his character negatively. Do not use the father lines.
lord_in_house/9/3.phrasing_guidance: Say fortune is activated by initiative, communication and siblings; avoid suggesting luck is 'lost'. Keep it encouraging about effort paying off.

lord_in_house/9/4.summary: A trikona lord in a kendra (a kendra-trikona raja yoga link): fortune shows up as home, property, vehicles, comforts and a close bond with the mother.
common_outcomes: comfort in home and vehicles, abundant wealth (BPHS 24.100)
vast landed property and fine homes; may earn through land or estates (Raman HTJH; Braha)
devoted to and benefiting from the mother, who is fortunate or of good character (BPHS 24.100; Raman HTJH; Braha)
inherits the father's immovable property (Raman HTJH)
good education, a high degree (Braha)
rare_outcomes: BPHS 20.6: 9th lord in a kendra aspected by Jupiter gives the father conveyances and high status
JP 12.86: with Venus and predominant strength, long-lasting pleasure and opulence
the 9th lord aspects the 10th from here, adding career success and status (Braha)

by_area.career: Earnings through estate and land dealings (Raman HTJH); a successful career, as the 9th lord aspects the 10th (Braha).
by_area.finance: Abundant wealth (BPHS 24.100); landed property and the father's immovables (Raman HTJH).
by_area.family: Devoted to the mother (BPHS 24.100), who is rich and fortunate (Raman HTJH). If afflicted, early life may be marked by a hard father or parental discord (Raman HTJH).
by_area.spirituality: Visits holy sites; religion is dear to the heart (Braha).

strengtheners: Jupiter's aspect (BPHS 20.6 for the father's prosperity)
conjunction with Venus in great strength (JP 12.86)
strong in a kendra with the lagna aspected by its own lord (JP 14.97)
weakeners_or_cancellations: affliction: domestic unhappiness and parental discord; with Rahu, the parents may live apart (Raman HTJH)
dual dusthana lordship dilutes (BPHS 24.146-147)
lord_in_house/9/4.lagna_or_context_notes: Where the 9th lord also owns the 4th (Mars for Leo, Venus for Aquarius) it occupies its own sign here. Results scale with strength (BPHS 24.145-148).

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 24.100
source_views.view: Comfort in home and vehicles, abundant wealth, devoted to mother.

source_views.source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra 20.6
source_views.view: 9th lord in a kendra and aspected by Jupiter: the father has vehicles and high status.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope Vol. II, ch. XIII 'Results of the Lord of the Ninth House being situated in Different Houses'
source_views.view: Vast landed property and fine homes, or earnings through estates; a rich, fortunate mother; inherits the father's immovables. Afflicted: domestic unhappiness, a hard father or parental discord; with Rahu the parents may live apart.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer, '9th House' chapter, 'The ruler of the 9th house placed in the' houses
source_views.view: Benefits from a religious mother, ancestral property, many comforts and fixed assets, good education, visits holy sites; the 9th lord aspects the 10th, giving career success and status.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata (Vaidyanatha; tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, Vol. II) XII.86
