dasha_principle/functional_nature_by_lag.summary: Whether a dasha is good or bad depends first on which houses the planet rules for that lagna: lords of the trikonas (1, 5, 9) give good periods, lords of 3, 6 and 11 give troubled ones, kendra lords depend on whether the planet is a natural benefic or malefic, and a planet ruling both a kendra and a trikona is the best of all (yogakaraka).
common_outcomes: Before reading any dasha, classify each planet for the lagna: trikona lord (good), 3/6/11 lord (bad), kendra lord (natural benefics lose goodness, natural malefics lose harm), 2nd/12th lord (neutral, act by association), 8th lord (bad unless it also rules the lagna).
Expect the dashas of trikona lords and of yogakarakas to be the productive periods of life, and the dashas of 3/6/11 and 8th lords to be the testing ones, other factors equal.
When a planet rules two houses, the one holding its moolatrikona sign weighs more; a good lordship can override a weaker bad one (e.g. 9th lordship over 8th).
rare_outcomes: Uttara Kalamrita calls the periods of 2nd, 3rd and 11th lords medium rather than bad.
strengtheners: A trikona lord in a kendra or a kendra lord in a trikona makes its dasha very favourable (BPHS 48.13; Phaladeepika 20.42).
Exchange or conjunction of the 9th and lagna lords, or of the 10th and lagna lords, makes both dashas very good (BPHS 48.14-17).
weakeners_or_cancellations: A kendra or trikona lord that also rules a bad house does not produce raja yoga by mere connection (BPHS 34.15).
Lords of 6, 8 or 12 become favourable in dasha if associated with a trikona lord (BPHS 48.14).
dasha_principle/functional_nature_by_lag.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman lists the good and bad planets for each lagna (e.g. Saturn best for Taurus, Mars yogakaraka for Cancer and Leo, Venus for Capricorn and Aquarius); Verma gives a similar table under Laghu Parashari 37-38.

source_views.source: BPHS 34.2-7, 34.13-15 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1)
source_views.view: Benefics owning kendras do not give good results and malefics owning kendras lose their harm; trikona lords are auspicious, the lagna lord especially; lords of 3, 6 and 11 are evil; 12th and 2nd lords act by association; the 8th lord is not good, but the Sun and Moon are not spoiled by 8th lordship; a planet ruling both a kendra and a trikona is a yogakaraka.

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari 6-12 (with Jataka Chandrika, tr. O.P. Verma)
source_views.view: Trikona lords are auspicious and 3/6/11 lords inauspicious even if benefic (6); kendra lords' results depend on nature (7); 2nd and 12th lords follow association and their other house (8); the 8th lord is bad unless it is also the lagna lord (9); kendra rulership spoils Jupiter and Venus most, Mercury less, the Moon least (10); 8th lordship does not harm the Sun or Moon (11); Mars as mere 10th lord is neutral and must also rule a trikona to do good (12).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.41-42, 20.50-51 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Restates Parashara: trikona lords give auspicious dashas, lords of 3, 6 and 11 only harm even if benefic, the lagna lord who also rules the 8th is good, and the Sun or Moon as 8th lord gives good results; Jupiter and Venus ruling kendras become harmful, Mercury less so, then the Moon, while malefic kendra lords grow more auspicious. (Part of 20.41 is garbled in the OCR.)

source_views.source: BPHS 48.9-20 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
source_views.view: Dashas of kendra and trikona lords and planets related to them are favourable; dashas of 3/6/11 lords, planets in those houses and planets joining them are unfavourable, as are planets joined with maraka lords and planets in the 8th.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita 6.22-23 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
source_views.view: Periods of kendra and kona lords are auspicious, those of 2nd, 3rd and 11th lords medium, those of 6th, 8th and 12th lords always adverse.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XVII and ch. XXIV rules 3 and 11
source_views.view: Gives the good and evil planets for each lagna; dashas of 6th and 8th lords harm unless they gain goodness otherwise; periods of 5th and 9th lords and of planets related to them are good.

source_views.source: R. Santhanam, notes to BPHS 48 (vol. 2)
source_views.view: From experience, the 3rd, 6th and 11th lords do not give bad results if they sit in their own signs in those houses; a well-placed 2nd lord gives wealth and a well-placed 7th lord celebrations despite their maraka role.

dasha_principle/functional_nature_by_lag.disagreements: Uttara Kalamrita rates 2nd, 3rd and 11th lords' periods as medium, while BPHS 34 and Laghu Parashari treat 3/11 lords as evil and the 2nd lord as neutral. Santhanam's notes soften the 3/6/11 rule when these lords occupy their own signs.
dasha_principle/functional_nature_by_lag.phrasing_guidance: Say 'this period tends to be supportive / demanding for this rising sign' rather than calling a planet good or evil in itself.

dasha_principle/dignity_and_strength.summary: The same dasha gives more or less of its promise according to the lord's strength: exalted, moolatrikona, own or friendly sign raise the good results; debilitation, enemy sign or combustion reduce or spoil them. A planet moving toward its exaltation gives a better period than one moving toward its fall.
common_outcomes: Scale the good results of a dasha by the lord's dignity: full when exalted, about three-quarters in moolatrikona, half in own sign, a quarter in a friend's sign, little or none when debilitated (Phaladeepika's scale).
Treat a combust lord like a debilitated one.
A strong lord in a good house gives the full positive results of its houses; the same lord weak and in a dusthana gives their negative side.
Phaladeepika also classifies dashas as descending (falling from exaltation), middling (friend's or exalted sign), ascending (rising from debilitation) and worst (debilitated or enemy sign).
rare_outcomes: Uttara Kalamrita: a planet with more than 10 rupas of shadbala moving toward exaltation gives an exceedingly favourable dasha; under 5 rupas it brings misery.
Raman: planets on a bhava sandhi (house junction) cannot give their full results in their dashas.
strengtheners: Retrograde planets are listed among those that give the good effects (Phaladeepika 20.14).
Benefic aspect on a weak lord brings some relief (BPHS 47.12-15).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Combustion or planetary war ('eclipsed') counts as weakness (Phaladeepika 20.14, 20.30).
Malefic aspect keeps a weak lord's results adverse (BPHS 47.12-15).
dasha_principle/dignity_and_strength.lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS 48.1: a planet that is naturally inauspicious still gives good results when exalted and in a good house, while a benefic that is debilitated and in a bad house gives bad ones; dignity and house placement work together.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.3, 47.7-33 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
source_views.view: Dasha effects follow the planet's strength; for each planet the good results come when it is exalted, in own or moolatrikona sign, in a kendra or good house, and the bad ones when it is debilitated, weak or in 6, 8 or 12.

source_views.source: BPHS 48.1 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
source_views.view: The 10th lord in exaltation in a good house gives a favourable dasha, debilitated in a bad house an adverse one; this shows a natural malefic exalted in a good house will not harm and a benefic debilitated in a bad house will.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.14, 20.27, 20.30, 20.56-57 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Planets in own, exalted or friendly signs, retrograde, or outside 6/8/12 give the good results; enemy-sign, debilitated, combust or dusthana planets give the bad ones (20.14); benefics debilitated or in 6/12 give only bad results and malefics so placed cause severe suffering (20.27); good results are full, three-quarters, half, quarter or nil from exaltation, moolatrikona, own, friend and debilitation, the reverse for malefics, and a combust planet is like a debilitated one (20.30); dashas are graded descending, middling, ascending and worst (20.56); a debilitated or enemy-sign planet in an auspicious sign or amsa gives mixed results with the good in the latter half (20.57).

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita 2.21-22 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
source_views.view: A planet of full strength (over 10 rupas) moving toward exaltation gives an excellent dasha; medium strength moving toward exaltation still prospers; moving toward debilitation the dasha is unfavourable; under 5 rupas it brings misery.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV (intro and rule 4)
source_views.view: Results vary with the strength and weakness of the dasha lord and must not be applied word for word; the lord's quality is modified by house, sign, aspects and navamsa; planets in bhava sandhis cannot give full results.

dasha_principle/dignity_and_strength.disagreements: Phaladeepika 20.30 says the dignity scale is reversed for malefics (their harm, not their good, is fullest in debilitation), while BPHS 48.1 says an exalted natural malefic in a good house gives good results.
dasha_principle/dignity_and_strength.phrasing_guidance: Speak of 'how fully' a period delivers rather than whether it delivers at all; a weak lord means more effort for the same result.

dasha_principle/navamsa_strength.summary: The dasha lord's condition in the navamsa (D9) modifies its period: vargottama or an own/exalted or benefic navamsa improves results, a bad navamsa limits them even when the D1 position looks strong.
common_outcomes: After judging the D1 position, check the lord's navamsa: vargottama or own/exalted navamsa supports the good results.
Do not promise the full results of a strong D1 position if the navamsa position is weak or afflicted.
A weak D1 planet in a good navamsa still gives mixed results, improving in the second half.
strengtheners: Vargottama (Phaladeepika 20.22; Uttara Kalamrita 6.28).
Own or exalted navamsa (BPHS 47.45-48).
Benefic navamsa (BPHS 47.27-32).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Unfavourable navamsa position (Raman, HPA ch. XXIV).

source_views.view: Among the conditions for a good dasha: the Sun strong in its vargas; Mars in a benefic navamsa; Jupiter in its own or exalted navamsa.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.22, 20.57 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: A planet in vargottama gives a favourable dasha; a weak planet in an auspicious sign or amsa gives mixed results, good in the latter half.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV (intro)
source_views.view: Success in a dasha is at its maximum only if the lord is equally strong in the navamsa; the lord's favourable or unfavourable navamsa position modifies its results.

dasha_principle/navamsa_strength.disagreements: Uttara Kalamrita 6.28 makes an exception: when Venus and Saturn are both very strong (exalted, own or vargottama), their mutual periods are bad (see dasha_principle/venus_saturn_mutual_periods).
dasha_principle/navamsa_strength.phrasing_guidance: Present D9 as a refinement ('the deeper strength of the planet'), not as overriding the main chart.

dasha_principle/navamsa_strength.phases: Phaladeepika 20.57: good results come in the latter half when a weak planet sits in an auspicious amsa.

dasha_principle/rahu_ketu_results.summary: Rahu and Ketu own no houses of their own, so in their dashas they give the results of the house they occupy and of the planets they join (and, per some, the lord of their sign and planets aspecting them). In a kendra or trikona linked with a kendra or trikona lord they act as yogakarakas; in the 8th or 12th, with maraka lords or debilitated, they trouble.
common_outcomes: Judge a node's dasha from: the house it occupies, the planets conjoined with it (taking on their lordships), the lord of its sign and its strength.
Rahu or Ketu in a kendra or trikona connected with a kendra or trikona lord gives a raja-yoga-like period.
A node in the 3rd, 6th or 11th generally gives good results (Santhanam's note); in the 8th or 12th, troubled periods.
A node joined with a maraka planet or sitting in a maraka relationship can act as maraka in its period.
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika: a benefic joined with Rahu causes harm, especially at the end of the dasha.
Phaladeepika: Rahu in Virgo, Pisces or Scorpio gives honour and property in its dasha, which may be lost at the end.
Uttara Kalamrita: nodes in a trikona aspected by or with the 2nd or 7th lord can cause death; in the 2nd or 7th with the 5th or 9th lord they give wealth and long life.
strengtheners: Exaltation (Taurus for Rahu per BPHS 47; Scorpio for Ketu in BPHS and Uttara Kalamrita).
Association or aspect of benefics and placement in a benefic sign (BPHS 47.34-39; Phaladeepika 19.15).
Link with a kendra or trikona lord (BPHS 34.17; Laghu Parashari 36; Phaladeepika 20.53).
weakeners_or_cancellations: 8th or 12th house, malefic or maraka association, debilitation (BPHS 47.40-43).
Association with 6th, 8th or 12th lords (Uttara Kalamrita 6.15-17).
dasha_principle/rahu_ketu_results.lagna_or_context_notes: Verma (on Laghu Parashari 36) adds that a node alone in the 8th or with the 8th lord acts like the 8th lord; with a benefic kendra lord it takes on kendradhipati dosha; with a benefic 7th lord it becomes maraka.

source_views.source: BPHS 34.16-17 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1)
source_views.view: Rahu and Ketu mainly give the results of the house lord they are conjoined with or of the house they occupy; a node in a kendra related to a trikona lord, or in a trikona related to a kendra lord, becomes a yogakaraka.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.34-43 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
source_views.view: Rahu exalted, or with benefics in a benefic sign in houses 1, 3, 4, 7, 10 or 11, gives wealth, property and honour; in the 8th or 12th, with a malefic or maraka planet, or debilitated, it brings loss of position, home troubles and distress, with loss at the start, some relief in the middle and anxiety at the end.

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari 13, 36 (with Jataka Chandrika, tr. O.P. Verma)
source_views.view: The nodes strongly give the results of the houses they occupy and of the planets they are conjoined with (13); placed in a kendra or trikona they give good results in their own dasha and in yogakaraka sub-periods even without a link to other planets (36). Verma adds from practice that they also partly give the results of planets aspecting them.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 19.15-16, 20.39, 20.53 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Rahu with a benefic and outside 6/8/12 gives a prosperous dasha (19.15); in Virgo, Pisces or Scorpio it gives honour that may be lost at the end (19.16); Rahu gives results according to the planet it associates with, and a benefic joined with Rahu harms, especially at the end of the dasha (20.39); nodes in a kendra or trikona linked to a kendra or trikona lord become yogakarakas, and in benefic-owned houses they give good sub-periods in the dasha of the planet they are linked to (20.53, numbering uncertain in OCR).

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita 6.14-21 and 8.82-88 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
source_views.view: Nodes in a trikona with or aspected by the 2nd or 7th lord can kill in their dasha; in dual signs with kendra or kona lords they give wealth and power; in the 6th, 8th or 12th with dusthana lords they harm; with strong yogakarakas in 1, 3, 4, 7 or 10 they give prosperity; when strong they take the strength of the lord of the house they occupy (6.20-21). In kendra or trikona, or with the lord of that house, they are auspicious (8.83) and give good bhuktis in benefics' dashas when conjoined with them (8.87).

source_views.source: BPHS 44.22-24 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1)
source_views.view: A node in the lagna, 7th, 8th or 12th, or in the 7th from or with a maraka lord, gains power to kill in its periods; Rahu in 6, 8 or 12 gives difficulties unless aspected or joined by benefics.

source_views.source: R. Santhanam, notes to BPHS 48.18-20 (vol. 2)
source_views.view: Rahu and Ketu give favourable results in the upachaya houses 3, 6 and 11.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV (Rahu's dasa)
source_views.view: Gives Rahu's dasha results sign by sign (e.g. troubled in Scorpio, its debilitation) and says they must be adjusted for the node's house, friendly or enemy sign and strength.

dasha_principle/rahu_ketu_results.disagreements: Own and moolatrikona signs of the nodes differ: BPHS 47 gives Rahu moolatrikona Gemini and own sign Aquarius (others say Virgo); Uttara Kalamrita 6.19-20 gives moolatrikona Gemini and Virgo and own signs Aquarius and Scorpio. Laghu Parashari stresses the house and conjoined planet; Verma adds aspects from practice; Uttara Kalamrita stresses the lord of the occupied house. Santhanam calls 3/6/11 good for nodes, while BPHS 48.18-20 calls planets in 3/6/11 unfavourable. The nakshatra-lord view of node results was not found in the sources read.
dasha_principle/rahu_ketu_results.phrasing_guidance: Explain that node periods 'borrow' their tone from the house and companions; avoid sensational language about Rahu.

BPHS 47.3-4: node results come in reverse drekkana order because they are always retrograde. Phaladeepika 20.39: harm from a benefic joined with Rahu peaks at the end of the dasha.

dasha_principle/antardasha_position_from.summary: An antardasha is judged partly by where its lord sits counted from the mahadasha lord: in a kendra, trikona, 3rd or 11th from it the sub-period cooperates and is good; in the 6th, 8th or 12th from it the sub-period is hostile and troubled. The dasha lord's sign is treated like a temporary lagna.
common_outcomes: Count from the mahadasha lord's sign to the antardasha lord's sign; 6, 8 or 12 marks a strained sub-period even if both planets are otherwise good.
Also check the antardasha lord's own house from the lagna and its dignity; BPHS judges both.
Treat the mahadasha lord's sign as a lagna and read the antardasha lord's placement from it.
strengtheners: Antardasha lord strong and in a kendra, trikona, 3rd or 11th from the dasha lord (BPHS 52-59 throughout).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Antardasha lord weak, or in 6/8/12 from the dasha lord (BPHS 52.13-14, 52.19-20).
dasha_principle/antardasha_position_from.lagna_or_context_notes: Sanjay Rath describes the Satyacharya principle of treating the dasha planet like a lagna when judging sub-periods.

source_views.view: Throughout the antardasha chapters, a sub-lord in a kendra, trikona, 3rd, 11th (sometimes 2nd) from the dasha lord and strong gives gains; in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the dasha lord, or weak, it gives troubles.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.29 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Results depend on the house from the dasha lord occupied by the bhukti lord: 6th, 8th or 12th unhappy, other houses good.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita 6.21-24 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
source_views.view: Treat the dasha lord's house as lagna and see where the bhukti lord falls; in the 12th, 6th or 8th from the dasha lord it is hostile; in the 11th, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 9th or 10th it is very beneficial; the 7th and a planet conjoined with the dasha lord are also favourable. Mutual 6/8 placement gives evil according to strength.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV rules 12 and 14
source_views.view: The bhukti lord modifies the dasha and both must be compounded; sub-lord and major lord in 6/8 or 12/2 from each other give unfavourable results.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, sec. 8.6.2
source_views.view: Uses the Satyacharya principle of treating the dasha planet like the lagna, and requires the antardasha planet to relate to the matter's lord or sit in trines, 7th or 12th from it.

dasha_principle/antardasha_position_from.disagreements: Uttara Kalamrita counts the 2nd from the dasha lord as very beneficial, while Raman counts a mutual 2/12 placement as unfavourable. Phaladeepika treats every position except 6/8/12 as good.
dasha_principle/antardasha_position_from.phrasing_guidance: Describe a 6/8/12 sub-period as a time of friction between the two planets' agendas, not as a disaster.

effects: unhappy sub-period; the sub-lord works against the dasha lord

dasha_principle/antardasha_position_from.phases: BPHS 53.49: even a well-placed Ketu antardasha in the Moon's dasha may bring loss at its end.

dasha_principle/mahadasha_antardasha_rel.summary: A mahadasha lord shows its results mainly in the sub-periods of planets that are related to it (by conjunction, aspect, exchange or mutual kendra/trikona) or that share its functional character; unrelated or opposite-natured sub-lords give reduced or mixed results, and enemies of the dasha lord bring opposition.
common_outcomes: Find which sub-lords are related to the dasha lord; those are the windows in which the dasha's main promise (good or bad) actually shows.
A sub-lord of the same functional type (e.g. both yogakarakas, or both marakas) intensifies the dasha's theme; an opposite type dilutes it.
A sub-lord who is a natural enemy of the dasha lord or of the lagna lord tends to bring rivals and loss of standing.
dasha_principle/mahadasha_antardasha_rel.lagna_or_context_notes: Phaladeepika 15.30 (cross-referenced in 20.44) defines relationship; Verma quotes five kinds: exchange, same sign, mutual aspect, mutual kendra, mutual trikona.

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari 30-31 (with Jataka Chandrika, tr. O.P. Verma)
source_views.view: Planets show their own results in the sub-periods of planets related to them or similar in character (30); in sub-periods of unrelated planets of contrary character, results must be worked out by their natures (31). Verma tabulates: related and same character gives the dasha lord's full results; related but contrary character gives very few; unrelated gives mixed.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.28, 20.44 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: The dasha's effects appear in bhuktis of planets related to the dasha lord (20.44); the bhukti of an enemy of the dasha lord, of a planet in the 6th, or of an enemy of the lagna lord brings danger from enemies, loss of position and hostility from friends (20.28).

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita 8.85-86 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
source_views.view: All planets show in their own bhuktis effects natural to them or to planets they associate with; bhuktis of planets inimical to the dasha lord follow the bhukti lord's own nature.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV rule 12
source_views.view: The dasha's general effects are modified by the bhukti lord; the influences of both planets and their mutual relation must be compounded.

dasha_principle/mahadasha_antardasha_rel.phrasing_guidance: Frame related sub-periods as 'when this period's main story plays out'.

dasha_principle/own_antardasha.summary: The first sub-period of every mahadasha is the lord's own; it does not deliver the full good or bad promise of the dasha, which comes later in related sub-periods. It is judged by the lord's dignity and house, and by maraka lordship.
common_outcomes: Do not predict the peak events of a mahadasha in its opening sub-period; expect a partial or preparatory taste.
Judge the own sub-period by the lord's natal dignity and house: exalted, own, kendra, trikona or 11th good; debilitated or in a bad house adverse; otherwise medium.
rare_outcomes: Uttara Kalamrita 6.24-25: a dasha lord able to give both yoga and death gives the yoga first, in its own bhukti.
Uttara Kalamrita 8.89: in Saturn's dasha its own bhukti gives Mars-like results and Mars's bhukti gives Saturn's own, and the same applies in Mars's dasha.

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari 29 (with Jataka Chandrika, tr. O.P. Verma)
source_views.view: Planets do not give their full auspicious, inauspicious or maraka results in their own sub-period within their dasha, only an ordinary share of them.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.43-44 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Restates that planets do not fully give the results of their houses in their own bhukti; the effects show in the bhuktis of related planets. (The printed wording of 20.43 is ambiguous.)

source_views.source: BPHS 52.1-3 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
source_views.view: The Sun's own sub-period in its dasha is good when exalted, in own sign, 11th, kendra or trikona; adverse when debilitated or in a bad house; medium elsewhere; as 2nd or 7th lord it threatens life.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita 6.24-25, 8.85, 8.89 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
source_views.view: A lord that can give both yoga and death gives the yoga first in its own bhukti; planets show their natural effects in their own bhuktis; Saturn and Mars swap results in their own and each other's bhuktis.

dasha_principle/own_antardasha.disagreements: Laghu Parashari and Phaladeepika say the own sub-period does not give the full results, while Uttara Kalamrita 6.24-25 places the yoga first in the lord's own bhukti.
dasha_principle/own_antardasha.phrasing_guidance: Call it a 'settling-in' phase of the new period.

dasha_principle/yogakaraka_periods.summary: Raja yoga results come in the dashas and sub-periods of the related kendra and trikona lords (yogakarakas). Within a yogakaraka's dasha, sub-periods of related planets deliver the most; related malefic or maraka sub-lords still deliver some yoga; unrelated benefic sub-lords between yoga sub-periods keep the good going.
common_outcomes: Identify the related kendra-trikona pairs; their mutual dasha/bhukti is the peak of the yoga.

In a yogakaraka's dasha, grade sub-periods: related yogakaraka best, related benefic next, related inauspicious planet less, related maraka least; unrelated benefic mildly good; unrelated malefic mixed.
A raja yoga that begins in a maraka sub-period brings recognition first; the material benefits come in a following related inauspicious sub-period.
rare_outcomes: Uttara Kalamrita 8.82-83: the yoga is destroyed if the 9th lord also rules the 8th or 12th, or if the 9th and 10th lords join the 8th or 12th lords.
strengtheners: Both lords unblemished (not also ruling bad houses) and free of combustion or debilitation (Verma on Laghu Parashari 32).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Kendra or trikona lord also ruling a dusthana or 3/11 reduces the yoga (BPHS 34.15; Laghu Parashari 15, 32).

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari 18-19, 32-35 (with Jataka Chandrika, tr. O.P. Verma)
source_views.view: Yoga results come in the dasha and bhukti of the two related yogakarakas and also in sub-periods of unrelated benefics falling between them (18); inauspicious planets related to yogakarakas give good results by strength in their bhuktis within the yogakaraka's dasha (19); a kendra lord's dasha with a related trikona lord's bhukti is good and vice versa, weak if both are blemished, bad if blemished and unrelated (32); raja yoga starting in a maraka bhukti gives fame, its comforts coming in a related inauspicious bhukti, and related benefic bhuktis give large results while unrelated ones give ordinary results (33-34); in a benefic's dasha the bhukti of a related yogakaraka seldom gives full yoga (35).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.42, 20.45-49, 20.54 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Kendra and trikona lords help each other in each other's bhuktis; related kendra and trikona lords become yogakarakas; planets related to a yogakaraka give good bhuktis even if malefic; unrelated planets do no harm; raja yoga begins in the bhuktis of karaka planets in the yogakaraka's dasha and grows in following malefic bhuktis.

source_views.source: BPHS 34.11-13 (vol. 1) and 48.9-17 (vol. 2) (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Exchange, conjunction, mutual aspect or kendra/trikona placement between a kendra and a trikona lord forms raja yoga; dashas of the 9th and 10th lords joined with the 5th lord, of 10th and 4th lords joined with the 9th lord, of planets aspected by kendra or trikona lords, and of lagna-9th or lagna-10th exchange lords are favourable.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita 8.86-87 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
source_views.view: In a kona lord's dasha a kendra lord's bhukti is good only if that kendra lord is linked with benefics; malefic bhuktis turn good through relation with a yogakaraka; a yogakaraka does good in its dasha even in the bhukti of an unrelated planet.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV rules 11 and 15
source_views.view: Periods of 5th and 9th lords and of planets related to them are good; the 5th lord's sub-period in the 9th lord's dasha, or vice versa, is good.

dasha_principle/yogakaraka_periods.disagreements: Uttara Kalamrita 8.87 says a yogakaraka does good even in an unrelated planet's bhukti, but 6.24-25 says an unrelated yogakaraka bhukti in an inauspicious dasha becomes distressing. Verma notes Susloka Sataka gives related maraka and related inauspicious bhuktis the same yoga strength, unlike Laghu Parashari.
dasha_principle/yogakaraka_periods.phrasing_guidance: Present yoga periods as windows of opportunity that still need effort; avoid promising status or wealth outright.

dasha_principle/yogakaraka_periods.phases: Verma on Laghu Parashari 33-34: when a planet is both yogakaraka and maraka, yoga results come first in benefic sub-periods and maraka results later; within a maraka sub-period, the start is good and the later part brings the maraka results.

dasha_principle/inauspicious_dasha_subpe.summary: In the dasha of a functionally inauspicious planet (8th lord, 3/6/11 lords), even good sub-lords struggle: an unrelated benefic or yogakaraka sub-period turns out badly, a related one gives mixed results, and another malefic sub-period is very hard.
common_outcomes: Do not expect a benefic sub-period to rescue a malefic mahadasha unless the sub-lord is linked to the dasha lord.
Related good sub-lords soften the period into mixed results; unrelated ones are overridden.
Two malefic lords in 6/8/12 from each other make the worst sub-periods.
dasha_principle/inauspicious_dasha_subpe.lagna_or_context_notes: Verma quotes the commentator Vinayaka Sastri: the dasha lord is like a king and the bhukti lord a courtier who must carry out the king's orders unless they are in contact.

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari 37-38 (with Jataka Chandrika, tr. O.P. Verma)
source_views.view: In an inauspicious planet's dasha, the bhukti of an unrelated benefic is evil, of a related benefic mixed, of a related yogakaraka mixed, and of an unrelated yogakaraka extremely bad.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita 6.24-25 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
source_views.view: When the dasha lord is inauspicious and the bhukti lord auspicious but not associated, the result is adverse; associated, mixed; an unassociated yogakaraka bhukti becomes even more distressing.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.22 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: When dasha and sub-period lords both own or occupy the 6th, 8th or 12th, results are unfavourable.

dasha_principle/inauspicious_dasha_subpe.phrasing_guidance: Describe these as periods needing patience, where help comes mainly through connected people or planets.

dasha_principle/maraka_periods.summary: The 2nd and 7th houses are the maraka (death-inflicting) houses. Their lords, malefics placed in them and malefics joined with their lords are marakas, and their periods are the classical windows for danger to life when the lifespan indicated by other methods is ending; otherwise they bring illness and hardship. Saturn linked to marakas becomes the chief maraka.
common_outcomes: Flag dashas and sub-periods of 2nd and 7th lords and of malefics in or with them as periods of health caution; texts tie actual danger to life to the longevity span worked out separately.
In a maraka dasha, a related benefic sub-lord does not bring the worst; an unrelated malefic sub-lord does.
Also note the 2nd lord's period can bring wealth and the 7th lord's marriage when well placed (Santhanam).
rare_outcomes: BPHS 44.15-21: lords of the 2nd and 12th from the Moon sign can act as marakas (if malefic; if benefic, only illness).
Laghu Parashari 24-25: if death does not come in the marakas' periods, it may come in the 12th lord's or other malefics' periods.
weakeners_or_cancellations: A malefic dasha does not kill in a benefic's sub-period even if they are related (BPHS 44.8).
Raman lists planets that do not kill for certain lagnas even with maraka powers (e.g. the Sun for Cancer, Saturn for Leo, Jupiter for Scorpio).
dasha_principle/maraka_periods.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman, HPA ch. XVII gives, per lagna, which planets kill and which do not despite maraka lordship.

source_views.source: BPHS 44.2-9, 44.15-24 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1)
source_views.view: The 2nd and 7th (12th from the 3rd and 8th) are maraka houses, the 2nd stronger; their lords, malefics in them and malefics with their lords are marakas whose major and sub-periods bring death according to short, medium or long life; a benefic related to the 12th lord, the 8th lord or a strong malefic may also kill; a malefic dasha does not kill in a benefic sub-period; an ill-disposed Saturn related to a maraka kills first; nodes in 1, 7, 8 or 12 or with marakas become marakas; when the indicated life span does not match, there are illnesses instead of death.

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari 23-28, 39 (with Jataka Chandrika, tr. O.P. Verma)
source_views.view: The 8th and 3rd are houses of life and the 12th from each (7th and 2nd) are maraka houses (23); death comes in their lords' dashas, in malefics conjoined with them, or else in the 12th lord's periods (24-27); Saturn related to marakas becomes the prime maraka (28); in a maraka dasha a related benefic sub-period does not kill while an unrelated inauspicious one does (39).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.40, 20.50 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Strong lords or occupants of the 2nd and 7th cause death in their dashas; if the 8th or 12th lord is very weak, death may come in a maraka lord's bhukti; Jupiter and Venus ruling kendras and maraka houses can cause death.

source_views.source: BPHS 48.2-8 and notes (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
source_views.view: The 2nd lord's dasha brings distress and possible death and the 7th lord's distress to the spouse and possible death; Santhanam notes the well-placed 2nd lord also gives wealth and the 7th lord marriage.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita 8.84-85 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
source_views.view: The 2nd and 7th are maraka houses; Saturn alone can kill even in a benefic's bhukti when linked with the 8th or 12th lord or a maraka.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XVII
source_views.view: For each lagna names the planets that inflict death when they gain maraka powers and those that do not.

dasha_principle/maraka_periods.disagreements: Laghu Parashari's commentators differ on which maraka house is stronger: BPHS 44 and one reading make the 2nd stronger, Verma's preferred reading makes the 7th stronger (counted from the 8th).
dasha_principle/maraka_periods.phrasing_guidance: Never predict death. Rephrase maraka periods as times to look after health and avoid risks, and say lifespan cannot be judged from one factor.

dasha_principle/venus_saturn_mutual_peri.summary: Venus and Saturn give each other's results in their mutual periods: in Venus dasha and Saturn sub-period Saturn's results come, and the reverse. If both are very strong, their mutual periods can bring a sharp fall; if one is strong and one weak, the strong one gives good results.
common_outcomes: In Venus-Saturn or Saturn-Venus periods, read the sub-lord's promise rather than the dasha lord's.
Be cautious when both Venus and Saturn are exalted, in own sign or vargottama: the classics predict reversal of fortune in their mutual periods.
If both are weak and in 6/8/12 from each other, the texts paradoxically predict good results.
rare_outcomes: Uttara Kalamrita gives similar pair rules for Jupiter-Venus, Saturn-Sun, Mars-Jupiter and Jupiter-Mercury mutual periods when strong and well placed.
dasha_principle/venus_saturn_mutual_peri.lagna_or_context_notes: Verma notes Venus is yogakaraka for Saturn's lagnas (Capricorn, Aquarius) and Saturn for Venus's (Taurus, Libra).

source_views.view: Whatever results Venus and Saturn are to give, each gives them in the other's sub-period.

source_views.view: Venus and Saturn both exalted, own or vargottama and equally strong make even a king a beggar in their mutual periods; one strong and one weak, the strong gives yoga; both weak and in 6/8/12 from each other they grant wealth. Also gives mutual-period rules for Jupiter-Venus, Saturn-Sun, Mars-Jupiter and Jupiter-Mercury when strong and well placed.

dasha_principle/phases_within_dasha.summary: When a planet's results arrive inside its dasha depends on its decanate (drekkana): first decanate at the start, second in the middle, third at the end; a retrograde planet, and always Rahu and Ketu, give them in reverse order.
common_outcomes: Use the lord's drekkana (0-10, 10-20, 20-30 degrees of the sign) to place its main effects in the first, middle or last third of the period, reversed if retrograde or a node.
Weak planets in good signs or amsas improve in the second half (Phaladeepika).
Some planets' periods carry specific end-of-period warnings (Mars, afflicted Rahu, Rahu with a benefic).
rare_outcomes: BPHS 47.27-32: even a strong Mars dasha may bring some unfavourable effects at the end.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.3-4 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
source_views.view: A planet in the first drekkana gives its effects at the start of the dasha, the second in the middle, the third at the end; for a retrograde planet the order reverses, and Rahu and Ketu, always retrograde, always give results in reverse order.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.27-32, 47.40-43 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
source_views.view: Mars's good dasha may turn somewhat unfavourable at its end; afflicted Rahu brings loss at the start, relief in the middle and distress at the end.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 19.16, 20.39, 20.57 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Rahu's gains in Virgo, Pisces or Scorpio may be lost at the end; harm from a benefic joined with Rahu peaks at the end; a weak planet in an auspicious sign or amsa gives good effects in the latter half.

dasha_principle/phases_within_dasha.phrasing_guidance: Give phases as tendencies ('more likely early in the period'), not dates.

dasha_principle/transits_during_dasha.summary: Transits time and modify what the dasha promises. The dasha lord's position in the sky when the dasha begins, and its later transits through good or bad houses and signs, raise or lower the results; the Moon's transit relative to the dasha lord does the same day to day. Modern practice (K.N. Rao) times major events by the Jupiter-Saturn double transit within a supporting dasha.
common_outcomes: Check where the dasha lord is transiting when its dasha starts: in the lagna, its exaltation, own or friend's sign is good; in 6, 8 or 12, debilitation or enemy sign is bad. Combine this with the natal position.
Within a dasha, the lord's transit through its own, exalted or friendly sign boosts its houses; transit through debilitation or enemy sign hurts them.
Use transits to time events the dasha already indicates, not to create events the dasha does not support.
For major events, look for Jupiter and Saturn both influencing the relevant house by transit while a related dasha runs.
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika: an auspicious bhukti gives results when the Sun transits the bhukti lord's exaltation sign; an inauspicious one when the Sun passes its debilitation or enemy sign.
strengtheners: Dasha lord transiting the lagna or the 3rd, 6th, 10th or 11th from it (Phaladeepika 20.59).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Natally weak dasha lord transiting anywhere spoils the bhava it signifies (Phaladeepika 20.35).
dasha_principle/transits_during_dasha.lagna_or_context_notes: Phaladeepika 20.60 judges the dasha lord's transit house counted from the Moon; it does not say natal or transit Moon explicitly.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.5-6 and 48.8 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
source_views.view: Results are favourable if at the start of the dasha the lord is in the lagna, exaltation, own or friend's sign, and unfavourable if then in 6, 8 or 12, debilitation or an enemy sign; a planet in a trikona at the dasha's start gives good results, in 6/8/12 bad, so both the birth position and the position at the start must be weighed.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.34-38, 20.59-61 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: A strong dasha lord transiting its own, exalted or friendly sign boosts its bhava; a natally weak one transiting anywhere harms it; the Moon transiting the dasha lord's exaltation or friend's sign, or the 3rd, 6th, 10th, 11th, trines or 7th from it, gives happy results; a bhukti lord transiting debilitation or enemy sign brings misery and own or exaltation sign good; the Sun's transit triggers bhukti results; a dasha lord transiting the lagna or the 3rd, 6th, 10th or 11th from it is auspicious; results also depend on the house from the Moon the dasha lord transits.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV rule 6
source_views.view: Dasha results are modified by transits (gochara).

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events, p. 53 (dasha-start charts)
source_views.view: Standard texts prescribe casting a chart for the start of a dasha, though the exact start moment of a Vimshottari dasha is hard to fix.

dasha_principle/yogas_fructify_in_dashas.summary: A yoga in the birth chart gives its results mainly in the dashas and sub-periods of the planets that form it; Nabhasa yogas are an exception, felt throughout life.
common_outcomes: For each major yoga, note the planets forming it and expect its results when their dashas or sub-periods run.
If none of a yoga's planets rules a dasha during the useful years of life, its results stay limited.
Treat Nabhasa (pattern) yogas as lifelong background rather than period-specific.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Uttara Kalamrita 8.98 notes yogas are also influenced by other forces.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita 8.98 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
source_views.view: Beings born under a yoga experience its effects during the dashas of the planets responsible for it, though other forces also shape it.

source_views.source: BPHS 33.94-99, 35.50 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1)
source_views.view: The effects of yogas come in the dashas of the signs or planets concerned (33.99, said of Kemadruma-type yogas); the results of Nabhasa yogas are felt throughout, in all dashas (35.50).

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari 18 (with Jataka Chandrika, tr. O.P. Verma)
source_views.view: Raja yoga results come in the dasha and bhukti of the yoga-forming planets.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.54 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Raja yoga begins in the bhuktis of karaka planets in the yogakaraka's dasha.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV (intro)
source_views.view: Dashas are the periods in which planets' indications are realised; to time an event, find when the planet that promises it takes control.

dasha_principle/yogas_fructify_in_dashas.phrasing_guidance: Link yoga promises to their periods so the reader sees when potential is most likely to show.

dasha_principle/tara_subperiods.summary: In the dasha of a malefic, sub-periods of the lords of the 3rd, 5th and 7th nakshatras from the birth star (Vipat, Pratyak, Vadha) bring trouble; the same stars' dashas are classical danger windows for short, medium and long life.
common_outcomes: Count from the birth nakshatra: the lords of the 3rd, 5th and 7th stars are the trouble sub-lords inside a malefic's dasha.
Expect setbacks from rivals, theft or misfortune in those sub-periods.
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika adds the bhukti of the Moon-sign lord or the 8th lord from it in a malefic dasha.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.23 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: In a malefic's dasha, the bhukti of the lord of the 3rd, 5th or 7th star from the birth star, or of the Moon-sign lord or the 8th lord from it, brings thieves, enemies and misery.

source_views.source: BPHS 44.15-21 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1)
source_views.view: Short-lived natives may die in the dasha of the Vipat (3rd) star, medium-lived in the Pratyak (5th), long-lived in the Vadha (7th) star from the birth star.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV rule 13
source_views.view: In a malefic's dasha, the sub-period of the planet ruling the 3rd, 5th or 7th star from the natal star is a time of trial.

dasha_principle/tara_subperiods.phrasing_guidance: Describe as periods for extra caution; never predict death.

dasha_principle/dasha_sequence_number.summary: Certain dashas are flagged as difficult by their position in the native's sequence of dashas: Saturn as the 4th dasha, Jupiter as the 6th, and Mars or Rahu as the 5th. A planet at the very end of a sign also gives a dangerous dasha.
common_outcomes: Number the dashas from the one running at birth; if Saturn's is the 4th, Jupiter's the 6th, or Mars's or Rahu's the 5th, read that period cautiously.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.24 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)

dasha_md/jupiter.summary: Jupiter's 16-year mahadasha is described in every source as one of the best periods when Jupiter is strong: honour and high position, wealth, vehicles, marriage and children, learning and religious life. When Jupiter is debilitated, combust, joined with malefics or in the 6th or 8th, the texts predict loss of home and position, worry and trouble to children, but BPHS limits the bad results to the opening years and makes the later part good.
common_outcomes: high position or authority, recognition from the government, vehicles and clothes, devotion to gods and Brahmins, happiness from spouse and children, success in religious rites (BPHS 47.45-48, when strong)
virtuous deeds, birth of children, honour from the ruler and praise from great men, fulfilment of desires (Phaladeepika 19.11)
new clothes, attendants, respect, children, wealth and friends, praise for one's sound speech (Phaladeepika 19.22)
rank, wealth, vehicles, clothes, royal goodwill, purity of heart, knowledge and its practice, wife and children (Jataka Parijata 18.110)
plenty of clothes, wealth, grain, status, house, relatives, success and the things one wants, when Jupiter is strong and well placed (Uttara Kalamrita, Results of the Major Periods)
rare_outcomes: separation from elders or teachers, ear disease, phlegm (kapha) disorders (Phaladeepika 19.22)
displeasure of rulers, illness, loss of courage, shortage of food and money, trouble from Brahmins, the father's anger, consumption, when Jupiter is a malefic for the chart (Uttara Kalamrita)
as the sixth dasa in the sequence from birth, Jupiter's period is called dangerous (Phaladeepika 20.24; Raman, HPA ch. XXIV rule 2)
loss of residence, distress to children, loss of cattle, and pilgrimage, when afflicted (BPHS 47.49-50)

by_area.personality: Purity of heart, diligence, sound speech and learning (Jataka Parijata 18.110; Phaladeepika 19.22). Raman ties the tone to Jupiter's sign: calm and spiritual in Scorpio, dissolute and selfish in Libra, mean motives in Capricorn (HPA pp. 255-257).
by_area.career: Attainment of high office, recognition from the government, success in ventures (BPHS 47.45-48); rank and royal goodwill (Jataka Parijata 18.110). Loss of position when Jupiter is afflicted (BPHS 47.49-50, Sanskrit gloss). Raman: promotion and public success in Cancer, trustee or responsible office in Aries, firm business in Taurus.
by_area.finance: Wealth, vehicles, clothes, grain and property when strong (BPHS 47.45-48; Uttara Kalamrita); loss of cattle and wealth when afflicted (BPHS 47.49-50, gloss); lack of money when Jupiter is a malefic (Uttara Kalamrita). Raman: unexpected wealth in Cancer, loss of wealth in Virgo and Aquarius.
by_area.health: Generally good when strong. Ear disease and phlegm disorders (Phaladeepika 19.22); illness and consumption when Jupiter is a malefic (Uttara Kalamrita); nervous trouble in Virgo, consumption in Aquarius (Raman).
by_area.relationships: Happiness from wife and children (BPHS 47.47; Jataka Parijata 18.110). Raman reverses this for Gemini, Virgo and Capricorn, where he predicts loss of or illness to the wife.
by_area.family: Birth of children and their welfare (Phaladeepika 19.11; BPHS 47.49); distress to children when Jupiter is afflicted (BPHS 47.50). Separation from elders (Phaladeepika 19.22); the father's anger when Jupiter is a malefic (Uttara Kalamrita).
by_area.spirituality: Devotion to gods and Brahmins, success in Vedic rites and study of Vedanta (BPHS 47.46-47); pilgrimages even in the afflicted case (BPHS 47.50). Raman: religious worship and philosophical discourse when Jupiter is in Scorpio. Rath: an atmakaraka Jupiter's period turns one to spiritual life, with little sorrow if Jupiter is exalted (Crux p. 312).

strengtheners: Jupiter exalted, in its own sign or moolatrikona (BPHS 47.45)
Jupiter in the 5th, 9th or 10th from the lagna (BPHS 47.45, Santhanam); in a kendra, the 11th or a trikona (Sanskrit gloss)
Jupiter in its own or exaltation navamsa (BPHS 47.45)

Jupiter ruling the 5th or 9th (Raman, HPA ch. XXIV rule 11), or a kendra or trikona (Uttara Kalamrita, p. 155)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Jupiter debilitated, or in the 6th or 8th (BPHS 47.49; Santhanam); in the 8th or 12th (Sanskrit gloss)
Jupiter combust or joined with malefics (BPHS 47.49)
Jupiter in an enemy sign, debilitated, combust or in a dusthana (BPHS 47.6; Phaladeepika 20.14, 20.27)
Jupiter ruling kendras (Phaladeepika 20.50), or the 6th, 8th or 12th (Phaladeepika 20.22, 20.24; Uttara Kalamrita p. 155)
planets placed in the 6th from Jupiter (Rath, Crux p. 330, citing Sarvartha Chintamani)
Jupiter in Gemini, Virgo, Libra, Capricorn or Aquarius, by Raman's sign list (HPA pp. 255-257)
dasha_md/jupiter.lagna_or_context_notes: Functional role matters: P.S. Sastri notes that Jupiter becomes a functional malefic for some lagnas (he names Taurus, Cancer and Libra) and that a benefic in the 6th, 8th or 12th or owning kendras can turn harmful (Uttara Kalamrita, notes p. 147). Phaladeepika 20.50 makes Jupiter as a kendra owner capable of harm and, if it also owns or occupies the 2nd or 7th, of causing death. None of the sources read gives a natal rule for Jupiter's mahadasha by house from the Moon; Phaladeepika 20.60-62 judge from the Moon by transit. PVR Narasimha Rao (after Sanjay Rath) takes the Sun as the reference for mahadasha results (Integrated Approach 16.5.3).

source_views.source: BPHS 47.3-6, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 576-577
source_views.view: General rules for all dashas: results follow the lord's strength; a lord in the first, second or third decanate gives its results at the start, middle or end, reversed if retrograde. Good if the lord is in the lagna, exalted, own or friendly sign; bad in the 6th, 8th or 12th, debilitated or in an enemy sign.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.44-51, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 583-584
source_views.view: Strong Jupiter (exalted, own sign, moolatrikona, in the 10th, 5th or 9th, own or exalted navamsa): high position, government recognition, vehicles, clothes, devotion, happiness from wife and children, success in sacrifices. Debilitated, combust with malefics, or in the 6th or 8th: loss of residence, anxiety, distress to children, loss of cattle, pilgrimage; the bad results come only at the start and the later part brings wealth and honours.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.44-51, Sanskrit with English gloss, enjoylearningsanskrit.com
source_views.view: Strength listed as exalted, own sign, kendra, 11th or trikona, moolatrikona, exalted or own navamsa: kingdom, courage, fame, palanquins, children and spouse, generosity with food. Adverse if linked with debilitated or combust malefics in the 8th or 12th: loss of position, mental distress, harm to children, fear, loss of livestock and wealth, pilgrimage. Early part hard, middle and end good.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 19.11 and 19.22 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: 19.11: virtuous deeds, children, honour from the sovereign, praise from great men, vehicles, reunion with family and friends, fulfilled desires. 19.22: new clothes, attendants, respect, children, wealth, friends, admired speech; also separation from elders, ear disease and phlegm troubles.

Retrograde, own, exalted or friendly planets outside the dusthanas give good results; combust, debilitated or enemy-sign planets or those in dusthanas give bad ones (20.14, 20.27). Vargottama gives good results, combust or debilitated mixed (20.22). Jupiter's dasa as the sixth dasa is dangerous (20.24). Combustion equals debilitation (20.30). Strong 2nd and 7th lords or occupants cause death in their dashas (20.40). Jupiter owning kendras becomes harmful and, owning or occupying the 2nd or 7th, death-causing (20.50). A combust, debilitated or enemy-sign planet in a good sign or amsa gives mixed results, good in the latter part (20.57).

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.110 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, vol. II)
source_views.view: Rank, wealth, vehicles, apparel, royal goodwill, purity of heart, power, knowledge and its practice, wife and children.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita, ch. 'Results of the Major Periods of Planets', tr. P.S. Sastri, pp. 145, 147, 154-155 (verse numbers not legible in the scan)
source_views.view: Strong, well-placed Guru: clothes, endless wealth, grain, status, house, relatives, success, luxuries. As a malefic: royal displeasure, worry, disease, loss of courage, want of food and money, trouble from Brahmins, father's anger, consumption. Periods of kendra and kona lords are highly beneficial, of 2nd, 3rd and 11th lords average, of 6th, 8th and 12th lords troublesome. Translator's note: Jupiter is a functional malefic for some lagnas.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XXIV, pp. 230-233 and 255-257
source_views.view: Results vary with the dasa lord's strength, sign, aspects and navamsa and must not be applied verbatim. Jupiter's dasa is unfavourable if it is the sixth dasa; periods of 5th and 9th lords are good. Sign-wise: Aries, Taurus, Cancer, Leo, Scorpio, Sagittarius and Pisces give property, success, fame and harmony; Gemini, Virgo, Libra, Capricorn and Aquarius give loss of wife, children or property, ill health, enemies or disgrace.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events (1998), pp. 312, 330-331
source_views.view: Planets in the 6th house from Jupiter are very inimical throughout Jupiter's dasa and their harm comes out in their own sub-periods (citing Sarvartha Chintamani 1.125-126). Treat the dasa planet as a temporary lagna. The dasa of the atmakaraka can be hard and spiritual, but an exalted Jupiter keeps sorrow minimal (Osho example).

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 16.5, pp. 213-215
source_views.view: A planet gives the results promised by its positions in the divisional charts. By Rath's 'tripod of life', the Sun is the reference point for judging a mahadasha, the Moon for an antardasha and the lagna for a pratyantardasha.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, ch. on planetary periods, pp. 202-203
source_views.view: The major lord gives the results of the houses it rules and aspects. The start of a benefic's major period sows seeds rather than giving fruit at once. The start of a period is the time for remedies: strengthen a weak benefic with its gem, propitiate a malefic with mantra or worship.

dasha_md/jupiter.disagreements: BPHS (Santhanam) lists the 10th, 5th and 9th as good houses; the Sanskrit gloss lists any kendra, the 11th or a trikona. Santhanam's bad case is the 6th or 8th; the gloss has the 8th or 12th and links the affliction to debilitated or combust malefics. Phaladeepika 20.24 and Raman call Jupiter's dasa dangerous if it is the sixth in sequence, which BPHS does not mention. Raman's sign list makes Jupiter bad in Gemini, Virgo, Libra, Capricorn and Aquarius regardless of house, while BPHS judges by dignity and house only. Phaladeepika 20.14 treats retrogression as a strength; BPHS 47.4 uses it only to reverse the timing.
dasha_md/jupiter.phrasing_guidance: Describe this as a growth period for learning, family, status and faith, scaled by Jupiter's strength. Where the chart shows affliction, say the opening years may be slower or more worrying and that the period improves later, as BPHS says. Do not predict the death of a spouse or children or the native's death; Raman's harsh sign results are best given as areas needing care.

dasha_md/jupiter.phases: BPHS 47.49-51: when Jupiter is afflicted the bad results fall at the start of the dasha only and the later part brings wealth and recognition (the Sanskrit gloss: early part hard with some gain through animals, middle and end happy). BPHS 47.3-4: Jupiter in the first, second or third decanate of its sign gives its results at the start, middle or end of the dasha, reversed if retrograde. Phaladeepika 20.57: a combust, debilitated or enemy-sign Jupiter in a good sign or amsa gives its good effects in the latter part. Frawley: the opening of a benefic's major period sows seeds; the fruit comes later.

dasha_md/ketu.summary: Ketu's seven-year period is described by most texts as unsettled: quarrels, trouble from enemies, thieves or authorities, wounds, fevers, scandal, losses and living away from home. BPHS makes it good, even giving high position, land and family happiness, when Ketu is in a kendra, trikona or the 11th, in a benefic or own/exaltation sign, or in an upachaya house; bad in the 2nd, 8th or 12th or under malefic influence. Because Ketu owns no sign here, much depends on the sign it sits in, its sign lord and the planets joined with it.
themes: exile or living away from home
results borrowed from sign lord and associates
common_outcomes: trouble from enemies, thieves and the ruler, wounds from weapons, diseases from heat, false accusation and a stain on the family name, danger from fire, living away from home (Phaladeepika 19.17)
grief and confusion connected with women, trouble from powerful people, loss of wealth, improper conduct, exile, toothache, leg pain and phlegm disorders (Phaladeepika 19.25)
distress, failing judgement, various illnesses and growing physical trouble, a life of much misery with only slight comforts (Jataka Parijata 18.145)
when well placed: favour of rulers, headship of a village or region, vehicles, children, gains from abroad, happiness from the spouse and cattle (BPHS 47.72-74)
rare_outcomes: imprisonment, destruction of kinsmen and of the home, company of low people (BPHS 47.77, when badly placed)
attainment of a kingdom or high government position and opportunities to acquire elephants (BPHS 47.74-75, Ketu in the 3rd, 6th or 11th)
Raman (by sign): founding of sacred institutions (Gemini); misappropriation of funds and prosecution (Capricorn); travel by water to distant countries and respect there (Pisces)

by_area.personality: Failing judgement and distress (Jataka Parijata 18.145); anxiety and fear in the middle of the period (BPHS 47.75); in Raman's sign list, religious study, moral elevation and tolerance in Sagittarius or Pisces, pessimism and dependence in Aquarius.
by_area.career: Favour of rulers, headship of a place and high position when Ketu is in a kendra, trikona, the 11th or an upachaya (BPHS 47.72-75); trouble from the ruler, false accusation and scandal (Phaladeepika 19.17); trouble from powerful people (Phaladeepika 19.25); Raman: promotion and favour of superiors in Pisces, displeasure of superiors in Aquarius.
by_area.finance: Loss of wealth (Phaladeepika 19.25); gains of land, vehicles and cattle when well placed (BPHS 47.72-74); money comes in during the middle of the period (Jataka Parijata 18.157); abundant wealth if Ketu is aspected by a benefic (Jataka Parijata 18.155); waste of wealth through illness if joined with malefics (Jataka Parijata 18.156).
by_area.health: Wounds from weapons, heat diseases, danger from fire (Phaladeepika 19.17); toothache, leg pain, phlegm disorders (Phaladeepika 19.25); various diseases and physical torment (Jataka Parijata 18.145); illness in the last part of the period (BPHS 47.76); disease when Ketu is in the 2nd, 8th or 12th (BPHS 47.77).
by_area.relationships: Happiness from the spouse when well placed (BPHS 47.73-74); grief and confusion linked to women (Phaladeepika 19.25); Raman lists sickness or loss of the wife under several signs (Aries, Taurus, Cancer, Capricorn).
by_area.family: Children and growth of the household when well placed (BPHS 47.73-74); elders and relatives fall ill at the start (Jataka Parijata 18.157); loss of kinsmen and of the home when badly placed (BPHS 47.77); stain on the family name (Phaladeepika 19.17).
by_area.spirituality: Raman's sign list stresses pilgrimage and religious study (Taurus), philosophical initiation (Cancer), philosophical debate (Leo), religious discussion (Sagittarius) and religious devotion (Pisces). Raman's list of Ketu's general significations includes religion, astrology and moksha (ch. XXIII). Rath calls Ketu the mokshakaraka.

dasha_md/ketu.lagna_or_context_notes: Ketu owns no sign in this library, so the texts route its results through other factors: Raman (ch. XXIII) says the nodes give the results of the lord of the sign they occupy; Rele (p. 64) and Jataka Parijata 18.155-156 say they act through the planets they join; Phaladeepika 20.52-53 makes them yogakarakas when tied to kendra or trikona lords. BPHS 47.3-4 says the nodes, being always retrograde, deliver the drekkana-based phase results in reverse order. P.V.R. Narasimha Rao (citing Sanjay Rath's 'tripod of life') judges a mahadasha mainly from the Sun's position, antardashas from the Moon and smaller periods from the lagna. No source read gives Ketu-mahadasha results counted from the Moon.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.71-77, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2
source_views.view: Ketu, the headless trunk. In a kendra, trikona or the 11th, in a benefic sign, or in its exaltation or own sign: good relations with the ruler, headship of a country or village, vehicles, children, gains from abroad, happiness from the wife, cattle. In the 3rd, 6th or 11th: a kingdom or high position, good friends, elephants. Raja yoga at the start, fear in the middle, illness and distant travel at the end. In the 2nd, 8th or 12th, or aspected by a malefic: imprisonment, loss of kinsmen and home, anxiety, company of low people, disease.

dasha_md/ketu.disagreements: Sign rulership and dignity: BPHS 47.35-36 gives Ketu exaltation in Scorpio, moolatrikona in Sagittarius and own sign Scorpio (Pisces by some); Rath and Narasimha Rao treat Ketu as co-lord of Scorpio and Rath calls it debilitated in Taurus; Rele (p. 64) and this library say the nodes own no houses, and the library's node dignity (exalted Taurus, debilitated Scorpio) is the reverse of BPHS for Ketu, so sign conditions are written by sign name here. BPHS 47.76-77: Santhanam reads the bad case as the 2nd, 8th or 12th OR malefic aspect; the Sanskrit gloss reads the houses together with malefic influence. Phases: BPHS puts raja yoga at the start, fear in the middle and illness and travel at the end; Jataka Parijata puts illness of elders at the start, money in the middle and happiness at the end. Tone: BPHS and Jataka Parijata 18.155 allow strongly good results, while Phaladeepika 19 and Jataka Parijata 18.145 give only troubles. Raman's 3rd/6th/11th rule (good) contrasts with Frawley's general view that the 3rd, 6th and 8th weaken Ketu.
dasha_md/ketu.phrasing_guidance: Describe the period as one of withdrawal, sudden changes and tests, with real gains possible when the chart shows the listed good placements. Lead with what the chart supports (sign, house, sign lord, companions) rather than the generic list of troubles. Avoid predicting imprisonment, the death of relatives or specific diseases; frame health items as reasons for care. Remedies can be offered as traditional practices, not as guarantees.

dasha_md/mars.summary: Mars's seven-year mahadasha is a period of energy, effort and conflict: income through land, courage, authority, fighting, medicine or fire, alongside quarrels with siblings and family and illness from heat, bile and blood. BPHS makes it strongly favourable (high position, land, wealth, victory over enemies) when Mars is exalted, in its own or moolatrikona sign, or strong in a kendra, the 2nd, 3rd or 11th, and troubled when Mars is debilitated, in the 6th, 8th or 12th, or afflicted by malefics.
common_outcomes: money made through land, litigation and dealings with rulers; more land and cattle (Phaladeepika 19.20)
wealth through fire, rulers, fighting and the like, and also through medicine, deceit and harsh dealings (Phaladeepika 19.9; Jataka Parijata 18.84)
quarrels with brothers, sons, wife, relatives and elders (Phaladeepika 19.9, 19.20; Jataka Parijata 18.84)
illness from bile, blood, fever and heat (Phaladeepika 19.9, 19.20; Jataka Parijata 18.84)
when well placed: land, fulfilled wishes, clarity of mind, courage, money, defeat of enemies, support of younger siblings (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI, p. 144-145)
when strong: high position, recognition from government, wealth and land, gains from abroad, vehicles and ornaments, harmony with siblings (BPHS 47.27-30)
rare_outcomes: rise to a kingdom or command at the head of a large army, when exalted Mars is in the 10th or 11th or in an upward-facing sign (Phaladeepika 20.25)
loss of eyesight or injury to the eye, cuts from weapons, when Mars is unfavourable (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI, p. 145)
mortgaging of landed property and loss of spouse and children for Mars in Libra (Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XXIV, p. 245)
having to eat poor, unwholesome food (Jataka Parijata 18.84)

by_area.personality: Courage, effort and clarity of mind when Mars is favourable (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI); a harsher, scheming streak and envy of others' fortune when it is not (Phaladeepika 19.9).
by_area.career: High administrative or political position and government recognition when Mars is strong (BPHS 47.27-30); income through rulers, fighting, the military, medicine or fire (Phaladeepika 19.9, 19.20); military success and respect for skill for Mars in Capricorn (Raman). Trouble with rulers and superiors when Mars is afflicted (Uttara Kalamrita; Raman for Cancer and Aquarius).
by_area.finance: Wealth through valour, land and property, gains from abroad (BPHS 47.27-31); money through land and litigation, but also loss of wealth (Phaladeepika 19.20); loss of wealth and distress when Mars is debilitated or in a dusthana (BPHS 47.33).
by_area.health: Fevers and illness from bile, blood and heat (Phaladeepika 19.9, 19.20; Jataka Parijata 18.84); wounds, cuts from weapons and eye trouble when Mars is unfavourable (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI).
by_area.relationships: Happiness from spouse and children when Mars is strong in a kendra or the 3rd (BPHS 47.31-32); quarrels with wife and children and liaisons with low company otherwise (Phaladeepika 19.9; Jataka Parijata 18.84).
by_area.family: Siblings are central: happiness and good relations with co-borns when Mars is strong (BPHS 47.30; Uttara Kalamrita), quarrels with brothers and relatives when it is not (Phaladeepika 19.20; Raman for Cancer, Libra).

dasha_md/mars.lagna_or_context_notes: Functional role matters as much as sign: Santhanam (note to BPHS 47.33) says Mars, ruling a kendra and a trikona, is yogakaraka for Cancer (5th and 10th) and Leo (4th and 9th) lagnas, and as 2nd and 9th lord is very good for Pisces lagna, so its dasha is very beneficial there if Mars is unafflicted. Laghu Parashari (v. 12, tr. O.P. Verma) adds that a malefic like Mars becomes auspicious by kendra lordship only when it also rules a trikona; for Aquarius lagna (3rd and 10th lord) it is called evil. Frawley (p. 245) lists Mars as generally benefic for Cancer, Leo, Sagittarius and Pisces lagnas and usually good for Aries and Scorpio. Uttara Kalamrita (p. 251) says that in Mars's mahadasha Saturn's sub-period gives Mars's own results and vice versa. No source read gives Mars-dasha results by house counted from the Moon.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.27-33, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 580-581
source_views.view: Exalted, moolatrikona or own-sign Mars, or Mars strong in a kendra, the 11th or 2nd, in a benefic navamsa and with a benefic: high position, wealth and land, government recognition, gains from abroad, vehicles, ornaments, happiness with siblings. Strong in a kendra or the 3rd: wealth through valour, victory over enemies, happiness from spouse and children, but some unfavourable effects at the end of the dasha. Debilitated, in the 6th, 8th or 12th, or with or aspected by malefics: loss of wealth and distress. Santhanam's note: yogakaraka for Cancer and Leo, very good for Pisces lagna, if unafflicted.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.3-6 and 47.27-33, Sanskrit with English gloss, enjoylearningsanskrit.com
source_views.view: The gloss adds trikona to the favourable houses (v. 28), reads the benefic as aspecting (v. 29), and gives happiness at the start of the dasha and trouble at its end (v. 32). Verses 3-4 time results by the planet's decanate (first decanate early, second middle, third late; reversed when retrograde); verses 5-6 make a dasha good if its lord is in the lagna, exalted, own or friendly sign, and bad if in the 6th, 8th or 12th, debilitated, combust or in an enemy sign.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 19.9 and 19.20 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: 19.9: wealth through fire, rulers and fighting, and also by medicine, falsehood and cruel acts; constant bile, blood and fever trouble; low company; quarrels with wife, children, relatives and elders; enjoying others' fortune. 19.20: money through land, litigation and the ruler; more cattle and land; quarrels with brothers and sons; wicked company; diseases of bile, blood and fire; loss of wealth.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.22, 20.24, 20.25, 20.27, 20.40, 20.57 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: 20.25: Mars in an upward-facing sign, or exalted in the 10th or 11th, gives a kingdom, victory over enemies, vehicles and an army. 20.24: the fifth dasha from birth belonging to Mars is dangerous. 20.22: a vargottama dasha lord gives good results, an eclipsed or debilitated one mixed results. 20.27: malefics in depression, enemy signs, 6th or 12th give intense misery. 20.40: powerful lords of or planets in the 2nd and 7th can cause death in their dashas. 20.57: a debilitated or combust planet in an auspicious sign or navamsa gives mixed results, good in the latter half.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.84 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, vol. II p. 1042)
source_views.view: Money through arms, wars between kings and other means, also through medicine, trickery, fraud and cruel acts; fever from bile and blood; low company; hatred from sons, wife, relatives and elders, and as a result poor food. Nearly identical to Phaladeepika 19.9.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI (tr. P.S. Sastri, pp. 144-145, 251)
source_views.view: Highly beneficial Mars: land, desired objects, wisdom, clarity, valour, money, defeat of enemies, younger siblings. Unfavourable Mars: distress to younger siblings, quarrels, trouble over land and fire, wounds, eye trouble, trouble from government, anger of the learned, weapon cuts, disease. Page 251: in Mars's mahadasha Saturn's sub-period gives Mars's results, and Mars's results come in Saturn's sub-period.

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari v. 12 (tr. O.P. Verma, pp. 47-48)
source_views.view: Mars does not become auspicious merely by owning the 10th; only with a trikona lordship as well (Cancer lagna, 5th and 10th) is it a yogakaraka. For Aquarius lagna (3rd and 10th) it is evil.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XXIV, pp. 244-245
source_views.view: Results by Mars's sign. Good: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Leo, Virgo, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Pisces (wealth, fame, success, land, victory, learning). Bad: Cancer (enemies, litigation, ill health, family discord), Libra (misery, family losses, mortgaged property), Aquarius (hardship, friction with superiors, trouble to mother and servants). He also warns that results vary with the dasha lord's strength, aspects and navamsa.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, pp. 202-203, 245-247
source_views.view: General: the major lord gives the results of the houses it rules and aspects; the start of a period is the time to balance it with gems, mantras or worship. For Mars: benefic for Cancer, Leo, Sagittarius and Pisces lagnas; red coral (avoid if Mars is a malefic lord, esp. Gemini and Virgo lagna, or in the 7th); mantras OM KUJAYA NAMAHA, OM KUM, OM ANGARAKAYA NAMAHA; deity Skanda. His dasha chapter gives no Mars-specific period results.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach ch. 16.5
source_views.view: General only: a planet gives in its dasha what its positions in the divisional charts promise; judge the mahadasha mainly from the Sun, antardashas from the Moon, with the dasha lord as a further reference. No Mars-specific results.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events (1998), pp. 21-22, 162
source_views.view: Examples only: for P.V. Narasimha Rao, Mars as 3rd and 8th lord with the 12th lord Sun in the 10th (a vipareeta raja yoga) brought him to Prime Minister in Mars dasha; another native's Mars dasha took him away from home to finish his education.

dasha_md/mars.disagreements: Phaladeepika and Jataka Parijata describe the dasha mostly in mixed or harsh terms (gains through land and fighting, but quarrels and bile/blood illness), while BPHS makes it strongly good or bad depending on dignity and house. Santhanam's BPHS 47.32 says the strong-Mars dasha has some unfavourable effects at its end; the Sanskrit gloss reads it as happiness at the start and trouble at the end. Santhanam lists the favourable houses as kendra, 11th and 2nd; the gloss adds trikona. Raman makes Cancer (debilitation) and also Libra and Aquarius bad signs, but Santhanam's note makes Mars a yogakaraka for Cancer lagna, so sign and functional role can pull in opposite directions.
dasha_md/mars.phrasing_guidance: Frame this as a high-energy, effort-driven period: good for property, initiative, competition and courage, with a need to manage temper, disputes (especially with siblings and family) and heat-related health. Stress the favourable version only when the chart shows a strong or yogakaraka Mars. Do not predict deaths, accidents or surgery; at most suggest care with health, safety and conflict.
