dasha_md/mars.phases: BPHS 47.32: when Mars is strong in a kendra or the 3rd, some unfavourable effects come at the end of the dasha (the Sanskrit gloss: happiness at the start, trouble at the end). BPHS 47.3-4: a planet in the first decanate of its sign gives its results at the start of the dasha, the second in the middle, the third at the end; the order reverses if the planet is retrograde. Phaladeepika 20.57: a weak Mars in an auspicious sign or navamsa gives its good results in the latter half.

dasha_md/mercury.summary: Mercury's 17-year mahadasha is described in every source as a period of learning, speech, trade, friends and family happiness, with honour from rulers or superiors when Mercury is strong. When Mercury is joined with malefics, debilitated, combust or in the 6th, 8th or 12th, the same period brings quarrels with relatives, losses, nervous or wind ailments and trouble from authorities. BPHS adds that the start is good, the middle brings recognition and the last part is troubled.
themes: wind and nervous ailments when afflicted
common_outcomes: gain of wealth, reputation and knowledge, royal favour, auspicious functions, happiness from wife and children, profit in business, when Mercury is well placed (BPHS 47.62-65)
meeting friends, personal comforts, fame through the praise of learned people, favour from elders, skill in speech, doing good to others, an elevated position (Phaladeepika 19.10)
money through seniors, relatives and friends, fame and happiness, going on an embassy or errand, income from dealing in gold, some wind ailment (Jataka Parijata 18.133)
garments, large wealth, grain, position, a mansion, fulfilment of wishes when Mercury is auspicious (Uttara Kalamrita, 'Dasas and their effects' sl. 8-9)
rare_outcomes: gain of new lands, cows and horses; money through Brahmins; worship of great men and gods; illness from wind, heat and phlegm (Phaladeepika 19.24, a second verse on Mercury's dasa)
journey to a foreign country and dependence on others when Mercury is with malefics (BPHS 47.66)
loss of wealth through lascivious habits, rheumatism and jaundice when Mercury is in the 6th, 8th or 12th (BPHS 47.67-68)
book writing and fame as a communicator when Mercury is linked to the houses of writing and fame (P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, example 52)

by_area.personality: Clear speech, cleverness and a helpful nature (Phaladeepika 19.10); growth of intelligence (BPHS 47.63). When Mercury is afflicted: short temper and weakened intellect (Uttara Kalamrita sl. 8-9).
by_area.career: Favour from government and superiors, good standing, profit in trade (BPHS 47.62-65); an elevated position (Phaladeepika 19.10); errands or embassies (Jataka Parijata 18.133). Punishment or displeasure from government when Mercury is with malefics or in a dusthana (BPHS 47.66-68); trouble from the trading class (Uttara Kalamrita sl. 8-9).
by_area.finance: Wealth through business, seniors, relatives and friends (BPHS 47.64; Jataka Parijata 18.133); dealing in gold (Jataka Parijata 18.133). Loss of wealth, land and cattle when Mercury is in the 6th, 8th or 12th (BPHS 47.67-68).
by_area.health: Good health when Mercury is strong (BPHS 47.64). Wind ailments (Jataka Parijata 18.133); wind, heat and phlegm disorders (Phaladeepika 19.24); urinary trouble when Mercury is with malefics; rheumatism and jaundice when in a dusthana (BPHS 47.66-68).
by_area.relationships: Happiness from wife and children (BPHS 47.64; Phaladeepika 19.10). Marriage is mentioned for Mercury in Aries, Gemini, Leo and Virgo (Raman, HPA pp. 264-265); loss of wife and children for Mercury in Scorpio (Raman).
by_area.family: Birth of children in the early part (BPHS 47.69); enmity with relatives when Mercury is with malefics (BPHS 47.66); loss of relations when Mercury is malefic (Uttara Kalamrita sl. 8-9).
by_area.spirituality: Worship of gods and great men, benefit from spiritual teachers (Phaladeepika 19.24); religious and charitable work for Mercury in Aries, Virgo and Sagittarius; recitation of scriptures for Gemini and Capricorn (Raman, HPA pp. 264-265).

strengtheners: Mercury exalted, in its own sign or a friendly sign (BPHS 47.62)
Mercury in the 5th, 9th or 11th (Santhanam's reading) or in a kendra, the 11th or a trikona (Sanskrit gloss) (BPHS 47.62)
aspect of a benefic, placement in the 9th, or Mercury ruling the 10th, which gives the good results in full (BPHS 47.65)
Mercury retrograde, or vargottama (Phaladeepika 20.14, 20.22)
Mercury in an upachaya house from the lagna (Jataka Parijata 18.14, 18.16)
weakeners_or_cancellations: association with a malefic (BPHS 47.66)
placement in the 6th, 8th or 12th (BPHS 47.67-68)
debilitation, an enemy's sign, or the 6th or 12th: a benefic then gives only untoward results (Phaladeepika 20.27)
combustion ('eclipsed' by the Sun): adverse results (Phaladeepika 20.14)
dasha_md/mercury.lagna_or_context_notes: Phaladeepika 20.50-51 says benefics that own kendras turn harmful, but Mercury does less harm as a kendra lord than Jupiter or Venus do. This matters for Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius and Pisces lagnas, where Mercury rules two kendras. BPHS 47.65 names Mercury as lord of the 10th as a strengthening condition. Raman (HPA ch. XXIV, rules 3, 5, 10-11) says the dasa gives results by the houses Mercury rules, occupies and aspects, and that lords of the 6th and 8th give harm unless otherwise redeemed. P.V.R. Narasimha Rao (ch. 16.5.3, following Sanjay Rath) judges a mahadasha mainly from the Sun's position, so Mercury in the 2nd from the Sun, which forms Vesi yoga, gives that yoga's results in its dasa.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.61-70, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 585-586
source_views.view: Mercury exalted, in its own or a friendly sign, or in the 11th, 5th or 9th: wealth, reputation, knowledge, government favour, auspicious functions, happiness from wife and children, health, sweet food, business profits. Aspected by a benefic, in the 9th, or lord of the 10th: these results in full. With a malefic: punishment by government, enmity with kin, foreign travel, dependence on others, urinary trouble. In the 6th, 8th or 12th: losses through lust, rheumatism, jaundice, theft, government hostility, loss of land and cattle. The start brings wealth, education, children and happiness; the middle, recognition from government; the last part is distressing.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.61-70, Sanskrit with English gloss, enjoylearningsanskrit.com
source_views.view: Verse 62 asks for Mercury exalted, in its own or a friendly sign and also in a kendra, the 11th or a trikona. Verse 66 counts conjunction or aspect by malefics: royal displeasure, mental distress, conflict with kin, foreign travel. Verse 67 for the 6th, 8th or 12th: dependence, quarrels, fear of illness, loss of wealth. Verse 70: honour from the ruler in the middle, suffering at the end.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 19.10 and 19.24 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: 19.10: friends, comforts, fame from the learned, favour of elders, clever speech, helping others, happiness to family, a high position. 19.24: help from spiritual teachers, money through Brahmins, new lands, cows and horses, worship of the great and of gods, great wealth, but also wind, heat and phlegm diseases.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.14, 20.22, 20.27, 20.50-51 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: General rules that apply to Mercury: retrograde planets and those in own, exalted or friendly signs give the good results, while eclipsed (combust), debilitated, inimical or 6/8/12 planets give adverse ones (20.14); a vargottama planet gives good results (20.22); a benefic debilitated, in an enemy's sign or in the 6th or 12th gives only untoward results (20.27); Mercury as a kendra lord does less harm than Jupiter or Venus (20.51).

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.133, with 18.14 and 18.16 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, vol. II)
source_views.view: 18.133: money through seniors, relatives and friends; fame and happiness; going on an embassy; income from gold; wind ailments. General rules: a dasa lord in an upachaya from the lagna, or in its own, exalted or friendly sign, or aspected by a benefic or friend, gives a good dasa (18.14, 18.16); the dasa is happy when the Moon's sign is the dasa lord's exaltation sign or a friendly sign, or is an upachaya, trikona or the 7th from the dasa lord (18.14).

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita, 'The Dasas and their effects', sl. 8-9 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
source_views.view: Auspicious Mercury: garments, great wealth, grain, position, prosperity, a mansion, relatives, success, wishes fulfilled. Malefic Mercury: going abroad, short temper, loss of relations, weakened intellect, trouble from traders, disputes, loss of land and money.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XXIV, pp. 230-233 and 263-266
source_views.view: Results of Mercury's dasa by sign. Aries: marriage, religious and social work, charity, favour of rulers, gains from land and cattle. Taurus: great happiness, titles, authority, music. Gemini: great learning, completion of studies, fame, wealth, marriage. Cancer: disgrace, change of residence, fines or confinement, loss of land, enmity. Leo: courage, travel in hills, wealth from abroad, marriage, fame. Virgo: the best period of life, royal favour, health, unexpected gains. Libra: works published in one's name, favour of the wealthy and educated, leadership. Scorpio: loss of wife, children and riches, mental trouble, business losses, loss of reputation. Sagittarius: success in education, learned company, travel east. Capricorn: success in trade, new business, patronage, victory over foes. Aquarius: wealth, pleasure, good name. Pisces: theft, dysentery, litigation, quarrels with relatives, nervous breakdown, failure. General rules: the dasa lord gives results by ownership, association, placement and aspect, modified by navamsa and transits, and is never to be read verbatim.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 16.5-16.6 (examples 52, 54)
source_views.view: A planet gives in its dasa what its placements in the divisional charts promise. Rath's 'tripod' rule: judge the mahadasha from the Sun, the antardasha from the Moon. Examples: a Mercury dasa that brought book writing, with Mercury as significator of writing linked to the arudha of the 3rd and forming Vesi yoga from the Sun; a Mercury dasa in which the native became a chief minister, with Mercury well placed from the Sun and the Moon.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, ch. 6 (planetary periods) pp. 202-203, and example charts pp. 284-285 (a novelist) and 308-309 (Roosevelt)
source_views.view: The major lord gives the results of the houses it rules and aspects. Examples: a Mercury period that brought out a writer's best work; a Mercury period of steadily rising political power, because Mercury as dispositor of a strong Mars carried Mars's power to the ascendant. Remedies at the start of a period: strengthen a weak benefic lord with its gem, propitiate a malefic one with mantra or worship.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events (1998), pp. 389-390, 456-458
source_views.view: Examples only. An exalted Mercury in the 6th from the arudha lagna led gradually to renunciation, which came at the start of the Mercury dasa (sannyasa in Mercury-Venus). In Akbar's chart the Mercury dasa saw the founding of a synthetic faith, with Moon and Mercury in close aspect.

dasha_md/mercury.disagreements: BPHS 47.62: Santhanam lists the 11th, 5th or 9th as an alternative to good dignity, while the Sanskrit gloss requires good dignity and also a kendra, the 11th or a trikona. BPHS gives the end of the dasa as distressing; Phaladeepika and Jataka Parijata do not divide the period. Phaladeepika 19.10 is wholly favourable, while 19.24 adds wind, heat and phlegm diseases. Raman makes Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces bad signs for this dasa even though Pisces is only Mercury's debilitation sign and Cancer and Scorpio are not named by the classical dasa verses. Phaladeepika 20.14 treats retrogression as favourable; other sources here are silent.
dasha_md/mercury.phrasing_guidance: Frame this as a long period for study, communication, trade and networks, whose tone depends on Mercury's dignity, house and associations. Mention the troubled version only when the chart shows the listed conditions, and keep health notes general (nerves, digestion), with no diagnosis. Present the BPHS start-middle-end pattern as a tendency, not a certainty.

dasha_md/mercury.phases: BPHS 47.69-70: the start brings wealth, progress in education, birth of children and happiness; the middle brings recognition from government; the last part is distressing. Phaladeepika 20.57: a combust or debilitated Mercury in an auspicious sign or navamsa gives its good effects in the later part. Frawley (p. 203): the opening sub-period of a benefic's dasa plants seeds rather than fruit, and is a good time to set goals.

dasha_md/moon.summary: The Moon's ten-year mahadasha is described as a generally pleasant period: peace of mind, comfort, good food, gains of clothes, ornaments, land and cattle, marriage or children, and favour from those in authority. All sources make the outcome depend on the Moon's strength. A strong, waxing or well-placed Moon gives the full good results. A debilitated, waning, afflicted or 6th/8th/12th-house Moon brings loss of money, worry, trouble to the mother and friction with authorities.
themes: strength depends on the Moon's phase
common_outcomes: opulence, good fortune, gain of wealth, auspicious functions at home, high position, vehicles, clothes, children and cattle when the Moon is strong and well placed (BPHS 47.16-22)
tranquillity of mind, success in all business, good food, wife and children, ornaments, clothes, gems, cows and lands; honouring Brahmins (Phaladeepika 19.7)
money through sacred prayers, deities, Brahmins and royal favour; women, wealth and lands; flowers, clothes, ornaments and perfumes (Phaladeepika 19.19; Jataka Parijata 18.73)
misunderstandings with wicked people, some loss of money, wind-related illness (Phaladeepika 19.19)
loss of wealth when the Moon is debilitated or waning (BPHS 47.23-26)
rare_outcomes: extraordinary wealth and luxuries when the strong Moon is in the 2nd house (BPHS 47.16-22)
gain of a deposit or hidden treasure and acquisition of learning, with the Moon in the 2nd (BPHS 47.21-22, Sanskrit gloss)
digging tanks and building gardens or public works (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI, tr. P.S. Sastri, p. 144)
unexpected finding of treasure (Raman, Moon in Cancer)
death of the mother (Raman, Moon in Virgo)

by_area.personality: Calm and contented mind when the Moon is strong (Phaladeepika 19.7). With malefics: dullness, mental tension (BPHS 47.23-26); irritability (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI). Waning or descending Moon: mental worry and derangement (Raman).
by_area.career: High position in government, recognition from rulers, success in undertakings (BPHS 47.16-22); success in all business (Phaladeepika 19.7); taking charge of a new office (Raman, Moon in Pisces). Inimical relations with government when a waning Moon is in the 6th, 8th or 12th or with malefics (BPHS 47.23-26); trouble from employees (BPHS 47.23-26).
by_area.finance: Gain of wealth, vehicles, clothes, cattle and land (BPHS 47.16-22; Phaladeepika 19.7, 19.19); wealth that keeps increasing when the Moon is strong (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI). Loss of wealth if the Moon is debilitated, waning or with malefics (BPHS 47.23-26); want of food and loss of money if the Moon is malefic (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI); poverty if anything checks the Moon's strength (Jataka Parijata 18.73).
by_area.health: Good health when the Moon is strong. Wind-related disease (Phaladeepika 19.19; Jataka Parijata 18.73); ill health and fevers when the Moon is malefic (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI); bodily sluggishness with a weak Moon joined by malefics (BPHS 47.24, Sanskrit gloss).
by_area.relationships: Acquisition of a wife, children and the company of women (Phaladeepika 19.7, 19.19); births of children (BPHS 47.16-22). Troubles to the wife when the Moon is descending from exaltation (Raman).
by_area.family: Auspicious functions at home (BPHS 47.16-22); well-being of the mother when the Moon is strong (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI). Distress to the mother when the Moon is waning, weak or with malefics (BPHS 47.23-26). Quarrels with relatives when the Moon is weak (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI); domestic happiness with the Moon in Sagittarius (Raman).
by_area.spirituality: Devotion to deities and Brahmins, sacred prayers and recitation (Phaladeepika 19.7, 19.19; Jataka Parijata 18.73); visits to holy places with the Moon in Libra or Capricorn and reciting religious texts with the Moon in Pisces (Raman).

dasha_md/moon.lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS judges the period from the Moon's dignity, phase, house from the lagna, associations and the lords it joins. Phaladeepika 19.8 says everything in this period must be judged from the Moon's strength by phase: moderate in the first ten days of the lunar month, full in the middle ten, declining in the last ten. Functional role: Phaladeepika 20.41 (Parashara's view) exempts the Moon from the 8th-lord blemish, while 20.50-51 says a natural benefic owning a kendra turns less helpful, the Moon less so than Jupiter, Venus or Mercury. Raman gives separate results for the Moon in each sign, in the lagna, debilitated, in moolatrikona and when moving from exaltation towards debilitation.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.16-26, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 579-580
source_views.view: Throughout the period: opulence, good fortune, wealth, auspicious functions at home, a high position, vehicles, clothes, children and cattle, if the Moon is exalted, in its own sign, in a kendra, in the 11th, 9th or 5th, joined or aspected by benefics, fully powerful and associated with the 10th, 9th or 4th lord. Extraordinary wealth if such a Moon is in the 2nd. Debilitated or waning: loss of wealth. In the 3rd: happiness off and on. With malefics: dullness, mental tension, trouble from employees and the mother, loss of wealth. Waning in the 6th, 8th or 12th or with malefics: enmity with government, loss of wealth, distress to the mother. Strong in the 6th, 8th or 12th: troubles alternating with good spells.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.16-26, Sanskrit with English gloss, enjoylearningsanskrit.com
source_views.view: Verse 17 lists exaltation, own sign, a kendra, the 11th or a trine, benefic conjunction, fullness and strength. Verse 18 adds the 10th and 9th lords and the lord of vehicles (4th). Verse 19 reads the Moon 'in the house' (taken as the 4th): vehicles, audience with rulers, Lakshmi at home. Verses 21-22: in the 2nd, exalted or own: sons, cattle, treasure, learning. Verse 23: debilitated or waning, loss of wealth; strong in the 3rd, wealth and happiness come intermittently. Verse 26: a strong but badly placed Moon gives the mother's distress and mental anguish mixed with gains; shanti is advised.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 19.7, 19.8, 19.19 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: 19.7: tranquillity of mind, success in all undertakings, good food, wife, children, ornaments, clothes, gems, cows and lands, honouring Brahmins. 19.8: everything is to be stated after weighing the Moon's strength. It is moderate in the first ten days of the lunar month, full and very auspicious in the middle ten, and declining in the last ten. 19.19: money through prayers, gods, Brahmins and royal favour; women, wealth, lands, flowers, clothes, ornaments and perfumes; also disputes with the wicked, loss of money and wind disease.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.27, 20.33, 20.41, 20.50-51 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: General rules that bear on the Moon. 20.27: benefics in debilitation, an enemy's sign, the 6th or the 12th give only untoward results. 20.33: planets in prishtodaya signs give results at the end of their period, ubhayodaya in the middle, shirshodaya at the beginning. 20.41: the Sun or the Moon give good effects even as 8th lords. 20.50-51: kendra lordship makes Jupiter and Venus most harmful, then Mercury, then the Moon.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.73, 18.83 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, vol. II)
source_views.view: 18.73: sacred prayers, scripture and Brahmins; charm over women; women, wealth and lands; flowers, clothes, ornaments and perfumes. If anything checks the Moon's strength, poverty and wind disease. 18.83: the house the Moon presides over gives results at the start of the period; the nature of that sign and the Moon's position show in the middle; the aspects on the Moon and the body part of that house show at the end.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI 'Results of the Major Periods of Planets' (tr. P.S. Sastri), p. 144; verse number not legible in the scan
source_views.view: A highly beneficial, powerful Moon gives the mother's well-being, digging of tanks, lands, gardens, a house, blessings of the twice-born, wealth, auspicious events and palanquins. A malefic Moon gives want of food, misery, loss of pleasure and money, ill health, lack of learning, irritability, being disliked, and malarial fevers.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XXIV, pp. 238-240
source_views.view: Results by sign: Aries, physical and mental happiness, contentment. Taurus, fame and great wealth. Gemini, education and property. Cancer, wealth, success in litigation, treasure, travel. Leo, education, unexpected gains. Virgo, death of the mother, enemies, restlessness. Libra, wealth, friends, pilgrimage, success. Scorpio, fear of rulers, loss of relatives, wealth, liberty and honour. Sagittarius, domestic happiness. Capricorn, lands, houses, new ventures, pilgrimage. Aquarius, loss of property, fear of authorities, family misunderstandings. Pisces, new office, religious texts, easy gains. In the lagna, charity and good friends. Descending from exaltation: losses, trouble to the wife, mental derangement, fear of rulers and poison. Debilitated: losses and worry. Moolatrikona: respect from rulers, money, land, happiness.

source_views.source: V.G. Rele, Directional Astrology of the Hindus, pp. 67-71
source_views.view: Gives no separate result for the Moon's major period as a whole. His general rules: a planet is in dignity when exalted, own, friendly, with benefics, with the 1st, 9th or 10th lord, or in a kendra, trikona or 11th from the lagna; a benefic owning a kendra is weakened. Planets in the 2nd or 7th cause illness even if not debilitated.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers ch. 6, pp. 202-203
source_views.view: General rule only: the major lord gives the results of the houses it rules and aspects. A benefic major period gives seeds of good results at its start rather than immediate fruit. The start of a period is the time for remedies: strengthen a weak benefic with its gem, propitiate a malefic with mantra or worship.

dasha_md/moon.disagreements: BPHS and Uttara Kalamrita make the whole period good or bad by the Moon's strength and placement. Phaladeepika 19.19 and Jataka Parijata 18.73 give fixed mixed results: comforts together with some loss of money and wind disease. Santhanam reads BPHS 47 as one long list of favourable conditions; the Sanskrit gloss splits it and reads verse 19 as the Moon in the 4th, a placement Santhanam does not mention. In BPHS 47.23 Santhanam gives the Moon in the 3rd 'happiness off and on'; the gloss says a strong Moon there brings wealth and happiness intermittently. Raman's sign results (bad in Virgo and Aquarius, good in Libra and Capricorn) are not found in the BPHS or Phaladeepika chapters read. Phaladeepika 20.41 exempts the Moon from the 8th-lord blemish but 20.50-51 still counts its kendra lordship as a mild blemish.
dasha_md/moon.phrasing_guidance: Describe this as a period whose tone follows the Moon's condition: comfort, home life and emotional steadiness when the Moon is strong; worry, money strain and concern for the mother when it is weak. Say waxing or waning plainly, as a matter of strength. Do not predict the mother's death or any illness as certain; frame health points as times to rest and look after the body.

dasha_md/moon.phases: Jataka Parijata 18.83: at the start of the Moon's period come the results of the house the Moon rules over; in the middle, results from the nature of that sign and the Moon's own position; towards the end, results from the planets aspecting the Moon and to the part of the body that house governs. Phaladeepika 20.33 (general rule): a planet in a shirshodaya sign gives its results early in its period, in an ubhayodaya sign in the middle, and in a prishtodaya sign at the end. Frawley (pp. 202-203, general): a benefic period gives seeds at its start and fruit later.

dasha_md/rahu.summary: Rahu's 18-year mahadasha is described by the classical texts as an unsettling period of sudden rises and losses, foreign or unconventional contacts, trouble from authorities, hidden illness and family strain, unless Rahu is well placed (exalted, in a favourable sign, in an upachaya or good house, or joined with benefics or a yogakaraka), when it can give power, wealth, property and recognition, often through foreigners or the state. Gains made in it are repeatedly said to be unstable and liable to be lost toward the end.
common_outcomes: trouble or displeasure from rulers and officials, removal from office or loss of status (Phaladeepika 19.14, 19.21)
danger from thieves, poison, fire and weapons (Phaladeepika 19.14, 19.21)
mental unrest and anxiety (Phaladeepika 19.14; BPHS 47.40-43 when afflicted)
illness or trouble to spouse and children, loss of or separation from relatives (Phaladeepika 19.14, 19.21; BPHS 47.40-43; Jataka Parijata 18.96)
an obscure, hard-to-diagnose illness; eye and head complaints (Phaladeepika 19.21)
living or wandering in a foreign or distant place (Jataka Parijata 18.96)
when Rahu is well placed: wealth, property, vehicles and recognition through friends, the state or a foreign government (BPHS 47.34-39)
rare_outcomes: rise to near-royal affluence and wide fame when Rahu is with a benefic and outside the 6th, 8th and 12th (Phaladeepika 19.15)
command of an army, kingly status (Jataka Parijata 18.108, sign list corrupt in the scan)
insults from lowly people, scandal, leg injury, failure of undertakings (Phaladeepika 19.14)
imprisonment for fraud or political offences when Rahu is in Leo; miscarriage or loss of a child when Rahu is in Scorpio (B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XXIV)
political rise, often after the fall of a mentor or leader, when Rahu is tied to the Amatyakaraka or the lagna lord (Sanjay Rath, srath.com)

by_area.personality: Restless, anxious or ill-natured moods are named (Phaladeepika 19.14, 19.21); irritability with Rahu in Gemini, mean tendencies in Aquarius (Raman). Frawley describes the period as dispersing energy and drawing attention toward what is foreign or distant.
by_area.career: Removal from office, failed undertakings and trouble from rulers are the default (Phaladeepika 19.14, 19.21). Well placed, Rahu gives comforts and wealth through government favour or a foreign government (BPHS 47.34-39), sudden promotion and state recognition in Capricorn, high position in Virgo (Raman). Loss of position when afflicted (BPHS 47.40-43).
by_area.finance: Loss of wealth at the start of an afflicted period (BPHS 47.40-43); wealth, crops and new house when exalted (BPHS 47.34-39); landholdings, vehicles and servants in Virgo, Pisces or Scorpio, liable to be lost at the end (Phaladeepika 19.16). Raman lists effortless gains in Sagittarius and sudden riches in Virgo, losses and litigation in Libra.
by_area.health: Obscure, hard-to-diagnose illness, poisoning, eye and head ailments (Phaladeepika 19.21); severe illness (Jataka Parijata 18.96); leg injury (Phaladeepika 19.14).
by_area.relationships: Trouble to spouse and children when Rahu is afflicted (BPHS 47.40-43); loss of or separation from wife and children (Phaladeepika 19.21; Jataka Parijata 18.96); disputes with friends (Phaladeepika 19.21). Domestic and marital happiness when Rahu is in Virgo or Aries (Raman).
by_area.family: Loss of relatives (Phaladeepika 19.14); illness to children (Phaladeepika 19.14); bereavement of parents at the end of the period (Jataka Parijata 18.109); sons and domestic happiness when well placed (BPHS 47.34-39).
by_area.spirituality: Religious inclination when Rahu is exalted (BPHS 47.34-39); pilgrimages and philosophical study with Rahu in Taurus, humanitarian service in Cancer, household recitation of sacred texts in Aries (Raman).

dasha_md/rahu.lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS judges Rahu's dasha by Rahu's own sign, dignity, house from the lagna and associations. Santhanam's text gives Taurus as exaltation, Gemini as moolatrikona and Aquarius as own sign (noting others give Virgo). Phaladeepika 20.52-53 and Raman tie the results to the planets Rahu joins and to the lord of its sign, so the dispositor's house rulership for the lagna matters. No consulted source gives results by Rahu's house from the Moon.

source_views.source: BPHS ch. 47 (Effects of Dasas) vv. 34-43, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2
source_views.view: Exalted Rahu gives wealth, crops, vehicles through friends and the state, a new house, sons, religious leaning and recognition. With or aspected by benefics, in a benefic sign and in the 1st, 3rd, 4th, 7th, 10th or 11th: comforts by royal favour, wealth through a foreign ruler, domestic happiness. In the 8th or 12th: distress. With a malefic or maraka planet, or debilitated: loss of position and residence, mental agony, trouble to spouse and children, poor food; wealth lost at the start, some relief and gain in one's own country in the middle, anxiety at the end. Translator's note: association with a yogakaraka makes Rahu a yogakaraka.

source_views.source: BPHS ch. 47 vv. 3-6, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2
source_views.view: A dasha lord in the 1st, 2nd or 3rd drekkana shows its results at the start, middle or end of the period, reversed for retrograde planets; the translator applies the reversal to the always-retrograde nodes. A dasha lord in the 6th, 8th or 12th, debilitated or in an enemy sign at birth gives unfavourable results.

source_views.source: BPHS ch. 48, closing translator's note, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2
source_views.view: Rahu and Ketu give favourable results in the 3rd, 6th and 11th.

source_views.source: BPHS ch. 57 (Antardasas in the Mahadasa of Rahu), tr. G.C. Sharma vol. 2 (via summary)
source_views.view: Only the publisher's summary was available: the antardasha results depend on the sub-lord's strength and position from the lagna and from Rahu, with remedies for adverse periods.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 19.14-16, 19.21 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: 19.14: trouble from the ruler, thieves, poison, fire and weapons, illness of children, mental unrest, loss of relatives, insult from low people, scandal, removal from office, leg injury, failure of ventures. 19.15: with a benefic and outside the 6th, 8th and 12th the period is highly auspicious: near-royal affluence, desires met, domestic comfort, wealth, fame. 19.16: in Virgo, Pisces or Scorpio, honour, land, vehicles and servants, all liable to be lost at the end. 19.21: ill nature or an obscure illness, loss of wife and children, poison, enemies, eye and head ailments, disputes with friends and farmers, the ruler's displeasure.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.31, 20.39, 20.52-53 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: 20.39: Rahu's results follow the planet it is joined with; a benefic joined to Rahu can do harm near the end of its period. 20.52: a node in a kendra or trikona connected with a kendra or trikona lord becomes a yogakaraka. 20.53: a node in a benefic's sign and connected with a planet acts well in that planet's sub-periods. 20.31: Rahu is among the planets whose dasha can prove fatal when it is the weakest of them, timed by Saturn's transit of the 6th, 8th or 12th.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.96, 18.106-109 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, vol. II)
source_views.view: General: loss of comfort, wealth and status, separation from wife, children and kin, severe illness, life abroad, quarrelsomeness. In Cancer, Taurus or Aries: wealth, grain, learning, honour from the ruler. In Virgo, (probably) Gemini or Sagittarius: wife, children, lands, a carriage, liable to be lost at the end. In Leo, Virgo or Cancer (as printed; the list is likely corrupt): kingly status, army command, wealth. Phases: distress at the start, enjoyment in the middle, bereavement of parents and loss of status at the end. OCR verse numbers are irregular.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV, pp. 249-251; ch. XXII p. 220
source_views.view: Gives Rahu dasha results sign by sign: good in Aries, Taurus, Cancer, Virgo and Capricorn; bad in Gemini, Leo, Libra, Scorpio (debilitated) and Aquarius; mixed in Sagittarius and Pisces. Results must be adjusted to Rahu's exact position and strength. The nodes give the results of the lords of the houses they occupy (p. 220).

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, ch. 6 (Planetary Periods), pp. 197-204
source_views.view: Rahu's 18-year period disperses energy and draws attention toward what is foreign or distant; Rahu is separative and can remove one from what it influences. Results follow the houses ruled, occupied and aspected; no special dispositor rule is given.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, 'Rahu is PM Maker', srath.com
source_views.view: Rahu is the key planet for political power. Rahu as or with the Amatyakaraka, or aspecting or joined with the lagna lord, gives political rise in its periods. Rahu in its maranakaraka sthana (the 9th) brings power only after the death, removal or fall of a leader or mentor. Illustrated by Indian prime ministers' charts; anecdotal.

source_views.source: Komilla Sutton (via summary)
source_views.view: A secondary summary cites Sutton (2001) advising preparation for Rahu's periods and describing the first and last years of the 18 years as the hardest. Her text itself was not read.

dasha_md/rahu.disagreements: Signs: Phaladeepika 19.16 counts Scorpio among Rahu's good signs, while Santhanam's BPHS 47 and Raman treat Scorpio as Rahu's debilitation with harmful results. Aquarius is Rahu's own sign in Santhanam's BPHS, yet Raman lists it among the worst placements. Jataka Parijata names Cancer in two different sign groups, and its lists do not match Raman's. Phases: BPHS (afflicted case) gives loss at the start, some relief in the middle and distress at the end; Jataka Parijata gives distress at the start, enjoyment in the middle, and bereavement and loss of status at the end; Phaladeepika 19.16 says gains are lost at the end. Sutton is reported as calling the first and last years the hardest. Lordship: Raman says the nodes give the results of the lord of the house they occupy; Phaladeepika 20.39 stresses the planet joined with Rahu instead; BPHS 47 judges Rahu by its own sign and associations.
dasha_md/rahu.phrasing_guidance: Describe Rahu's period as one of ambition, change and unusual opportunities, with the warning that gains can be unstable, and that health, family and dealings with authority need care. Say which conditions in the chart point toward the favourable or the difficult version. Never predict death, poisoning or loss of family members as certain; rephrase maraka lines as a time to take extra care of health. Offer remedies only as traditional practices.

dasha_md/rahu.phases: BPHS 47.40-43 (Santhanam), for an afflicted Rahu: wealth is lost at the start, there is some relief and gain in one's own country in the middle, and anxiety and distress come at the end. Jataka Parijata 18.109: distress at the start, considerable enjoyment in the middle, bereavement of parents and loss of status at the end. Phaladeepika 19.16 and Jataka Parijata 18.107: gains made under a well-placed Rahu may be lost when the period ends. BPHS 47.3-4: the period's results are timed by the drekkana Rahu occupies (1st, 2nd or 3rd drekkana gives results at the start, middle or end); Santhanam's note reverses this order for the always-retrograde nodes.

dasha_md/saturn.summary: Saturn's 19-year mahadasha is described in the general texts as a slow, burdensome period: illness in the family, losses in farming and property, absence from home, servants leaving and sudden losses. Every classical source makes it strongly conditional: in its own, exalted or friendly sign, in the 3rd or 11th, in a kendra or trikona, in Sagittarius or Pisces, with benefics or as a yogakaraka it gives high position, property, wealth and children; in the 6th, 8th or 12th, debilitated or combust it brings danger, imprisonment, separation from parents and trouble to spouse and children.
common_outcomes: wind ailments such as gout or rheumatism in the family, losses in farming, gossip and slander, servants leaving, long stays away from home, sudden losses of relatives, land, comfort and wealth (Phaladeepika 19.13)

gains of servants, elderly women and cattle, sometimes through unrest in the country, alongside trouble to spouse and children, wind and phlegm disorders, piles and burning in the limbs (Phaladeepika 19.23)
possession of livestock and coarse grain, earnings from running a guild, trade body or village community (Jataka Parijata 18.121)
when well placed: recognition from government, wealth, conveyances, a high post such as command of an army, gain of property and birth of children (BPHS 47.53-56)
when badly placed: danger from poison and weapons, separation from father, distress to wife and children, trouble from government displeasure, imprisonment (BPHS 47.57-58)
rare_outcomes: rule over a low tribe or a village, or headship of a village or small town (Jataka Parijata 18.121; Uttara Kalamrita sec. 6, sl. 11.5-12.5)
acquisition of a kingdom or very high office (BPHS 47.56, 47.60)
a vipareeta-type rajayoga when a yogakaraka Saturn sits in a dusthana (Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, example of K. Karunakaran)
travel to Western or foreign countries (Raman p. 260, Saturn in Libra or Aquarius)

by_area.personality: Laziness, wrongdoing and bad company in the general texts (Phaladeepika 19.13); when well disposed, intelligence, enthusiasm and many undertakings (Uttara Kalamrita sec. 6, sl. 11.5-12.5). Raman's sign results range from philosophical study and mental peace (Sagittarius) to distrust and unrest (Leo).
by_area.career: Recognition from government, command or high office, success in learning when Saturn is strong or in the 3rd/11th (BPHS 47.53-56); headship of a village, trade or a guild (Jataka Parijata 18.121; Uttara Kalamrita); loss of position and government displeasure when in a dusthana, debilitated or combust (BPHS 47.57-58).
by_area.finance: Gain of wealth, land and property when well placed (BPHS 47.53-56; Uttara Kalamrita); farming losses and sudden loss of land and wealth in the general description (Phaladeepika 19.13); loss of wealth when Saturn is malefic (Uttara Kalamrita).
by_area.health: Wind ailments such as gout or rheumatism, phlegm disorders, piles, burning in the limbs (Phaladeepika 19.13, 19.23); injury from poison or weapons when Saturn is in a dusthana, debilitated or combust (BPHS 47.57); disease and becoming crippled when Saturn is malefic (Uttara Kalamrita).
by_area.relationships: Trouble and illness for spouse and children (Phaladeepika 19.13, 19.23; BPHS 47.58); happiness from spouse and birth of children when well placed (BPHS 47.56).
by_area.family: Separation from father, and in the Sanskrit gloss from mother too (BPHS 47.58); misunderstandings among relatives in some signs (Raman p. 259); sudden loss of relatives (Phaladeepika 19.13).
by_area.spirituality: Performance of sacrifices and rituals when Saturn is well disposed (Uttara Kalamrita sec. 6, sl. 11.5-12.5); pilgrimage and religious study with Saturn in Sagittarius or Pisces (Raman p. 260).

dasha_md/saturn.lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS ch. 34 (tr. Santhanam vol. 1) gives Saturn's functional role by lagna. It is auspicious and gives rajayoga for Taurus (34.23-24) and is auspicious for Libra (34.33-34) and Aquarius (34.41-42). It is a malefic or killer for Aries, mainly when related to Venus (34.19-22), and for Cancer (34.27-28), Leo (34.29-30), Scorpio (34.35-36), Sagittarius (34.37-38) and Pisces (34.43-44). For Capricorn it does not kill on its own (34.39-40). Phaladeepika 20.60 judges a dasa lord's effect at any time by the house it is transiting from the Moon. Rath (Crux p. 330) treats Saturn's sign as a temporary lagna during the dasa: malefics in houses Saturn signifies (e.g. the 8th from it) spoil those matters, and benefics there improve them. PVR Narasimha Rao uses the Sun as the main reference point for judging a mahadasha.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.52-60, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 584-585
source_views.view: Calls Saturn the lowest of the planets. Exalted, in own, moolatrikona or friendly sign, in own or exalted navamsa, and in the 3rd or 11th: recognition from government, opulence, fame, success in education, conveyances, wealth, command of an army, a kingdom, Lakshmi's favour, property and children. In the 6th, 8th or 12th, debilitated or combust: poison, weapon injuries, separation from father, distress to wife and children, disaster from government displeasure, imprisonment. With or aspected by a benefic, in a kendra or trikona, in Sagittarius or Pisces: kingdom or high office, conveyances and clothes. Translator's note: as kendra-trikona lord Saturn is yogakaraka for Taurus and Libra lagnas and does very well if unafflicted.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.52-60, Sanskrit with English gloss, enjoylearningsanskrit.com

source_views.source: BPHS 34.19-44, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 1
source_views.view: Saturn's functional role by lagna: rajayoga-giver for Taurus; auspicious for Libra and Aquarius; malefic or killer for Aries (if related to Venus), Cancer, Leo, Scorpio, Sagittarius and Pisces; not a killer on its own for Capricorn.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 19.13 and 19.23 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: 19.13: wind ailments such as gout in wife and children, farming losses, gossip, bad company, servants leaving, long absence from home, sudden loss of relatives, land, comfort and wealth. 19.23: gains of servants, elderly women and cattle through national unrest; trouble to children and wife; wind and phlegm disorders, piles, burning in the limbs.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.24, 20.27, 20.31, 20.57 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri; siva.sh)
source_views.view: 20.24: Saturn's dasa falling fourth in the sequence is dangerous. 20.27: malefics in debilitation, an enemy sign, the 6th or 12th cause severe suffering in their dasas. 20.31: among Saturn, Mandi, Rahu, the 22nd-drekkana lord and the 8th lord, only the weakest gives a fatal dasa, with death when Saturn transits the 6th, 8th or 12th from the lagna. 20.57: a combust, debilitated or enemy-sign planet in an auspicious sign or navamsa gives a mixed dasa that improves in its second half.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.121 and 18.132 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri vol. 2)
source_views.view: 18.121: goats, asses, camels, old women, birds and coarse grain; wealth from running a guild, trade body or village community; may rule a low tribe. 18.132: Saturn in its debilitation navamsa while in its exaltation sign gives happiness at the start and misery at the end; in its exaltation navamsa while in its debilitation sign, trouble from robbers and enemies, misery and roaming abroad at the start, happiness at the end.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita Kanda I sec. 6, sl. 11.5-12.5 (English edition on archive.org; P.S. Sastri's translation, ch. VI, agrees)
source_views.view: A well-disposed Saturn gives prosperity, intelligence, sacrifices and rituals, lands, headship of a village or town, success as a merchant and in many activities. A malefic Saturn gives poisoning, loss of wealth, bodily trouble, the ruler's anger, forbidden acts, being crippled and disease.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XXIV, pp. 230-232 and 259-260
source_views.view: General rule: Saturn's dasa as the 4th dasa is unfavourable. By sign: Aries the worst period, with losses, failures and more enemies; Taurus agricultural gains and much income; Gemini recognition, profits in trade and speculation, political success; Cancer miseries, family strife, illness; Leo unease, distrust, misappropriation of money and prosecution if badly afflicted, hated by all and longing for death as relief; Virgo high position and business success; Libra foreign travel, new business branches, honour and domestic happiness; Scorpio odium of superiors, loss of prestige and property; Sagittarius philosophical study, marriages at home, peace; Capricorn more land, wealth and great friends; Aquarius travel in Western countries, success in litigation, wealth; Pisces pilgrimage and indifference to sectarian rules, but also sorrow and unrest.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events (1998), pp. 330-331 and the Karunakaran example
source_views.view: In Saturn's dasa, planets in the 6th from Saturn are very hostile throughout and show their harm in their own sub-periods (citing Sarvartha Chintamani). Houses Saturn signifies, counted from it, should hold benefics: e.g. Mars 8th from Saturn spoils spouse's health and debts in Saturn's dasa. Example: for a Taurus lagna, yogakaraka Saturn in the 3rd (a dusthana) gave a strong rajayoga through its dasa.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, ch. on planetary periods, pp. 199-204
source_views.view: The major lord gives the results of the houses it rules and aspects. A functionally benefic Saturn can still bring out its natural malefic nature when the other period lords are difficult. Advises remedial balancing at the start of a period, propitiating a malefic lord through mantra, ritual or worship.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, sec. 16.5-16.6
source_views.view: General method only, no Saturn-specific list: a planet gives in its dasa what its divisional-chart positions promise, and the Sun is the key reference point for a mahadasha. Ayur-dasa example: Saturn as 7th lord and Maheswara was a strong maraka, and J.F. Kennedy Jr. died in Saturn-Mercury.

dasha_md/saturn.disagreements: Phaladeepika 19.13 and Jataka Parijata 18.121 give mostly mixed or low-grade results without conditions, while BPHS and Uttara Kalamrita make the period strongly conditional and potentially excellent. Santhanam reads BPHS 47.53-56 as dignity together with the 3rd/11th placement. The Sanskrit gloss treats the dignities, the 9th house and the 3rd/11th as separate good conditions and adds the 11th to verse 59. Raman judges the dasa by Saturn's sign, rating Aries the worst and Libra or Capricorn favourable, which broadly follows dignity. He also rates Pisces mixed although BPHS lists Pisces as good. Phaladeepika 20.24 and Raman agree that Saturn's dasa is dangerous when it is the fourth dasa.
dasha_md/saturn.phrasing_guidance: Describe this as a long period of steady effort, responsibility and slow results, not as a disaster. Lead with the chart's actual conditions (dignity, house, functional role) and give the favourable version when they apply. Mention health in terms of joints, chronic or wind-type complaints and general care, never as a diagnosis. Do not predict death, imprisonment or the loss of a parent; at most suggest extra care for family elders and legal matters.

dasha_md/saturn.phases: Jataka Parijata 18.132 is the only text that gives phases specific to Saturn: exalted in the rasi but in its debilitation navamsa, the dasa starts happily and ends in misery; debilitated in the rasi but in its exaltation navamsa, it starts with trouble, enemies and wandering abroad and ends happily. dasha_md/sun.summary: The Sun's six-year period turns on the Sun's strength. A strong, well-placed Sun brings wealth, honour from government and people in power, rank, children, fame and steady effort. A weak or afflicted Sun brings loss of money, displeasure of authorities, quarrels with relatives, worry about the father, fevers and moves away from home.
themes: travel and moves away from home
common_outcomes: when strong: wealth, happiness and honours from the government; gains of clothes, conveyances and produce (BPHS 47.7-11)
when strong: sons, intelligence, wisdom, status, knowledge, wealth, fame, valour and divine blessings (Uttara Kalamrita 6.5-6)
when strong: courage, effort, intelligence, fame and valour grow; gains through fire, medicines, forests and royal contact (Saravali 41.25-26)
when well placed: wealth earned through hard work, travel, dealings with rulers, fame, steady devotion to duty (Phaladeepika 19.6)
when weak or afflicted: loss of wealth, anger of rulers, quarrels with kinsmen, distress to the father, trouble at home (BPHS 47.12-15; Uttara Kalamrita 6.5-6)
when badly placed: quarrels, sudden anger of the ruler, illness among relatives, wandering, anxiety, fire danger to wealth, children and wife (Phaladeepika 19.5)
rare_outcomes: a high post such as army command through the ruler's favour (BPHS 47.7-11)
kingdom or royal insignia when the Sun is exalted or in the lagna (Saravali 41.54-59)
exile or banishment, punishment from government (BPHS 47.12-15)
[maraka: text predicts danger to life / death] when the Sun is debilitated in the sign but exalted in the navamsa, at the end of the period (Jataka Parijata 18.72)
[maraka: text predicts danger to life / death] in the period of any planet placed in the 8th house (Saravali 41.66-68)

by_area.personality: Courage, effort, intelligence and firmness grow when the Sun is strong (Saravali 41.25-26; Phaladeepika 19.6). When weak: anxiety, harsh temper and a turn to wrong acts (Phaladeepika 19.5; Saravali 41.27-28).
by_area.career: The main theme. Strong Sun: honours and a high post from government, even army command (BPHS 47.7-11); kingdom or leadership of large areas in exaltation, own sign or moolatrikona (Saravali 41.54-59). Weak Sun: punishment or displeasure from authorities, loss of position, humiliation (BPHS 47.12-15; Uttara Kalamrita 6.5-6; Saravali 41.70).
by_area.finance: Wealth, produce, clothes and conveyances when strong (BPHS 47.7-11; Uttara Kalamrita 6.5-6). Loss of wealth when weak (BPHS 47.12-15); efforts go to waste (Uttara Kalamrita 6.5-6). Raman by sign: losses in Virgo, Libra, Capricorn and Aquarius; gains in most other signs (HPA ch. XXIV).
by_area.health: Weak Sun: fever, heart and bile problems, hunger and thirst (Saravali 41.27-28); eye, head and fever trouble when debilitated, eye and face trouble in an enemy sign (Saravali 41.54-59); the whole body suffers when the Sun is in the 8th (Saravali 41.54-59). Ill-health with enemies when weak (Uttara Kalamrita 6.5-6).
by_area.relationships: Weak Sun: trouble through wife, children and relatives (Saravali 41.27-28); fire danger to wife and children (Phaladeepika 19.5). Raman: death of the wife with the Sun in Aquarius; enjoyment and friendships in Aries (HPA ch. XXIV).
by_area.family: Distress to the father and to paternal and maternal uncles, opposition from kinsmen, trouble at home when the Sun is weak (BPHS 47.12-15). A son when the Sun is joined with the 5th lord (BPHS 47.9). Jataka Parijata: the father falls ill at the start of the period (18.71).
by_area.spirituality: Righteous conduct with the Sun in Leo; reverence for holy people with the Sun in Taurus; pilgrimages with positional strength (Raman, HPA ch. XXIV). Divine blessings when strong (Uttara Kalamrita 6.5-6).

dasha_md/sun.lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS judges this period from the lagna and by the Sun's dignity and associations; it gives no separate rule counted from the Moon. The Moon rules found (Phaladeepika 20.60-61, Jataka Parijata 18.7 and 18.14, Saravali 41.17-18) use the Moon's transit position when the period starts, counted from the dasha lord, so they need transit data rather than birth-chart facts. The Sun rules one sign (Leo), so its functional role depends on the lagna: Phaladeepika 20.41 says the Sun gives good results even as 8th lord (Capricorn lagna). Uttara Kalamrita 6.22 gives the general rule that kendra and trikona lords' periods are good and 6th, 8th and 12th lords' periods are hard.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.3-6 and 47.7-15, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2
source_views.view: Results come at the start, middle or end of a period by the planet's drekkana (first, second, third), reversed if retrograde. Good if the dasha lord is in the lagna, exalted, own or friendly sign; bad in the 6th, 8th or 12th, debilitated or in an enemy sign. Sun in own sign, exaltation, a kendra or the 11th, with the 9th or 10th lord and strong in varga: wealth, happiness, government honours. With the 5th lord a son; with the 2nd lord wealth; with the 4th lord conveyances; a high post like army chief. Debilitated, weak in 6/8/12, with malefics or the 6/8/12 lord: loss of wealth, punishment from government, exile, opposition of kinsmen, distress to the father and to uncles, trouble at home, needless enmity. Benefic aspect gives some good at times; malefic aspect keeps it bad.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.1-15, Sanskrit with English gloss, enjoylearningsanskrit.com
source_views.view: Same structure. Verse 12 adds a Sun joined with Rahu or Ketu among the afflictions. Verse 15 says a benefic aspect brings some happiness in the middle of the period.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 19.5-6 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Badly placed Sun: quarrels, sudden anger of the ruler, illness of relatives, wandering, great anxiety, fire danger to wealth, grain, sons and wife. Well placed: wealth through harsh effort, journeys, dealings with kings and disputes, travel through forests and hills, fame, success in business, steady devotion to duty. Ch. 20 adds general rules: exalted, own or friendly sign good, debilitated, inimical or 6/8/12 bad (20.14); the Sun as 8th lord still good (20.41); planets in shirshodaya signs act early in a period, prishtodaya late (20.33).

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.71-72 and 18.58 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri vol. 2)
source_views.view: Start of the Sun's period: the father falls ill and expenses are heavy; middle: trouble to everyone in the household, people and animals; end: ease and comfort. Sun exalted but in its debilitation navamsa: blame, danger, death of a son, wife or paternal relative, loss in farming. Sun debilitated but in its exaltation navamsa: regal prosperity and happiness, though loss of wealth or the native's own death may come near the end. For any malefic planet, its dignity shows at the start of its period, its house matters in the middle and aspects on it at the end (18.58).

source_views.source: Saravali 41.25-28, 41.53-59, 41.66-75 (English text, lakshminarayanlenasia.com PDF; translator not named)
source_views.view: Favourable Sun: gains from forests, medicines, travel, fire and royal contact; courage, diligence, intelligence and fame grow; kingship. Adverse Sun: grief through servants, theft, eyes, weapons, fire, water and the king; trouble from children, wife and relatives; fever, heart and bile disorders. By placement: lagna gives kingdom; other kendras in an enemy's sign give hip, throat and eye trouble; debilitated gives eye, fever and head trouble and confinement; exalted gives kingdom and insignia; moolatrikona ends miseries and gives leadership of large areas; enemy sign gives eye and face trouble and disgrace; 8th house afflicts the whole body and causes wandering. General rules: planets in the 6th give misfortune, in the 8th death; planets in shirshodaya signs act at the start of their period, prishtodaya and debilitated ones at the end.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita 6.5-6 (tr. S.S. Sareen; also P.S. Sastri ed.)
source_views.view: Auspiciously placed Sun: sons, intelligence, wisdom, status and power, knowledge, wealth, fame, valour, happiness and divine favour. Inauspiciously placed: hardship, wasted effort, loss of money and position, disease and enemies, royal displeasure, ill-health of the father.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XXIV, pp. 231-234
source_views.view: Results by the Sun's sign: Aries (deep exaltation) sudden gains, travel east, foreign residence, quarrels with friends, pleasures; moolatrikona children, respect, power and political success; Taurus land and reverence for saints; Gemini wealth, learning, music; Cancer political success and property; Leo respect from the great, righteous conduct, children; Virgo serious illness and losses; Libra poverty, enemies, failures, death of brothers and friends; Scorpio new enterprises, hill travel; Sagittarius success and health; Capricorn wandering, loss of patrimony and good name; Aquarius worry, death of wife, loss of property; Pisces wealth and celebrations. Also lists results by the six strengths (sthana, dig, kala, naisargika, chesta).

source_views.source: V.G. Rele, Directional Astrology of the Hindus, pp. 67-72
source_views.view: General method: a planet in dignity (exalted, own or friendly sign, with benefics, with the lagna, 9th or 10th lord, in angles, trines or the 11th) gives good results in its period; in debility (fall, enemy sign, with malefics, ruling 3/6/8/11) gives evil. Gives graded results for the nine avasthas, including Kopita, a planet joined with the Sun: sinful conduct, disgrace, eye trouble, danger from fire, king and thieves.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, pp. 202-203
source_views.view: The major lord gives the results of the houses it rules and aspects; the major lord sets the general nature of the time. A good period does not always give its fruit at once: the seeds show at the start. The beginning of a period is the time for remedies: strengthen a weak benefic lord with its gem, propitiate a malefic one by mantra, ritual or worship.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 16.5.1
source_views.view: A planet gives in its period the results promised by its positions in the divisional charts (for example the D-10 for career), not only the rasi chart.

dasha_md/sun.disagreements: Phases: Jataka Parijata 18.71 gives a fixed pattern for the Sun's period (father ill and expenses at the start, household trouble in the middle, ease at the end); BPHS 47.3-4 instead times results by the Sun's drekkana; Saravali 41.75 and Phaladeepika 20.33 by whether the sign rises head-first or hind-first. Santhanam's BPHS 47.15 says a benefic aspect gives good 'at times'; the Sanskrit gloss puts that relief in the middle of the period. Raman's sign list makes the Sun in Virgo, Capricorn and Aquarius (signs that are neither enemy nor debilitation for the Sun in BPHS) quite bad, which the BPHS dignity rules do not predict.
dasha_md/sun.phrasing_guidance: Frame this as a period about authority, recognition and self-reliance whose tone depends on the Sun's strength. For a weak Sun, advise patience with superiors and government matters, care of health (fever, eyes, heart) and attention to the father's wellbeing. Do not state that a parent, spouse or the native will die; turn maraka lines into advice about caution and health checks.

dasha_md/sun.phases: Jataka Parijata 18.71: at the start the father falls ill and expenses are heavy; in the middle everyone in the household, people and animals, has trouble; at the end there is ease and comfort. BPHS 47.3-4: if the Sun is in the first drekkana (0-10 degrees) of its sign its results come at the start of the period, in the second drekkana in the middle, in the third at the end (reversed if retrograde, which the Sun never is). Saravali 41.75 and Phaladeepika 20.33: a planet in a shirshodaya (head-rising) sign gives its results early, in a prishtodaya (hind-rising) sign or debilitated late, in Pisces (both) throughout or in the middle. Jataka Parijata 18.58: for a malefic such as the Sun, its dignity shows at the start, its house in the middle and the aspects on it at the end.

dasha_md/venus.summary: Venus's 20-year mahadasha, the longest in the Vimshottari cycle, is described as a period of comfort, marriage and family celebration, vehicles, fine clothes, ornaments, wealth, the arts and royal favour when Venus is well placed. BPHS turns it toward quarrels with kin, trouble to the wife, business loss and separation from relatives when Venus is in the 6th, 8th or 12th, and toward bodily trouble when Venus rules the 2nd or 7th.
common_outcomes: fine clothes, ornaments, conveyances, cattle and land; sweet food daily; recognition from the ruler; music and dance at home by the grace of Lakshmi (BPHS 47.79-82, when Venus is exalted, in its own sign or in a kendra or trikona)
a wife, children, wealth, great comfort, garlands and perfumes, clothes, ornaments, vehicles, and fortune and fame like a king's (Jataka Parijata 18.158)

materials for pleasure and comfort, good vehicles, cows, gems, ornaments and treasure, enjoyment with young women, intellectual work, voyages, auspicious acts and gifts from the ruler (Phaladeepika 19.12)
a wife, jewels, clothes, treasure, horses and the comforts of bed and seat; wealth from trade, farming and voyages (Phaladeepika 19.26)
quarrels with kinsmen, distress to the wife, business losses, loss of cattle and separation from relatives when Venus is in the 6th, 8th or 12th (BPHS 47.83-84)
rare_outcomes: a kingdom or high government post, command of an army, marriages and births in the family, recovery of a lost position or property (BPHS 47.81-83, Venus in its moolatrikona)
rulership of a region or village, building temples and reservoirs, giving food in charity (BPHS 47.85-87, Venus in the 4th as 9th or 10th lord)
anxiety, mental distress, separation from or loss of parents and elders, and hardship to relatives (Phaladeepika 19.26)
gems, sharper intellect, great wealth and public praise (Phaladeepika 20.26, Venus strong in own or exaltation sign in the 10th, 11th or 12th)
[maraka: text predicts danger to life / death] when Venus owns kendras and also owns or occupies the 2nd or 7th (Phaladeepika 20.50)

by_area.personality: Pleasure-seeking, intellectual and artistic pursuits (Phaladeepika 19.12); enthusiasm and vigour in work (BPHS 47.87); a period of strong sensuality when Venus is in Libra (Raman p. 276).
by_area.career: Recognition from the ruler, high government post, command of an army when Venus is strong (BPHS 47.79-83); rulership of a region or village as 9th or 10th lord in the 4th (BPHS 47.85-86); business losses when Venus is in the 6th, 8th or 12th (BPHS 47.84); promotion to responsible office with Venus in Pisces (Raman p. 277).
by_area.finance: Vehicles, clothes, ornaments, cattle and land (BPHS 47.79-80); wealth, treasure and gems (Jataka Parijata 18.158; Phaladeepika 19.12); income from trade, farming and voyages (Phaladeepika 19.26); loss of wealth and status if Venus is exalted in the rasi but debilitated in the navamsa (Jataka Parijata 18.168).
by_area.health: Bodily pain and trouble when Venus rules the 2nd or 7th (BPHS 47.88); Raman notes venereal trouble with Venus in Taurus and generative-organ trouble, arthritis and nervous strain with Venus in Virgo (pp. 275-276).
by_area.relationships: Marriage and a wife are central (Jataka Parijata 18.158; Phaladeepika 19.26; BPHS 47.82); distress to and harassment from the wife when Venus is in the 6th, 8th or 12th (BPHS 47.84-85); quarrels and separation with Venus in Virgo (Raman p. 276).
by_area.family: Births and marriages in the family, visits of friends (BPHS 47.81-82); happiness from wife and children (BPHS 47.87); enmity with kinsmen and separation from relatives when Venus is in a dusthana (BPHS 47.84-85); anxiety about parents and elders (Phaladeepika 19.26).
by_area.spirituality: Pious works such as building temples and reservoirs and giving grain in charity (BPHS 47.86-87); religious and philosophical study with Venus in Sagittarius (Raman p. 277).

Venus in its moolatrikona (BPHS 47.81)

Venus debilitated in the rasi but exalted in the navamsa (Jataka Parijata 18.169)
Venus yogakaraka for Capricorn and Aquarius lagnas, and lord of the 2nd and 9th for Virgo lagna (Santhanam's note to BPHS 47.89)

Venus lord of the 2nd or 7th (BPHS 47.88)

dasha_md/venus.lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS judges the dasha from the lagna: the house Venus occupies, its dignity, and its lordship of the 2nd/7th (maraka) or 9th/10th. Santhanam notes Venus is yogakaraka for Capricorn and Aquarius lagnas and very auspicious for Virgo lagna. Phaladeepika 20.50 says Venus, like Jupiter, is harmed by kendra lordship and becomes a strong maraka if it also owns or occupies the 2nd or 7th. BPHS 47.88 says the same results appear in Venus's own sub-period, and in the other sub-periods according to the sub-lords' strength. Raman reads results by Venus's sign (pp. 275-277). Modern method notes: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao uses the Sun as a reference point for a mahadasha, the Moon for an antardasha and the dasha lord as a temporary lagna for its sub-periods; Frawley stresses the dasha lord's lordship and aspects. No source read gives a Venus-specific rule counted from the Moon.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.78-89, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 588-589
source_views.view: Venus exalted, own sign, kendra or trikona: clothes, ornaments, conveyances, cattle and land, daily sweets, royal recognition, songs and dances by Lakshmi's grace. In moolatrikona: kingdom or high post, a house, children and grandchildren, marriages, army command, friends' visits, recovery of lost position. In the 6th, 8th or 12th: enmity of kinsmen, distress to wife, business loss, cattle destroyed, separation from relations. In the 4th as lord of the 9th or 10th: rulership of a region or village, pious works, charity, fame, happiness from wife and children. Same results in its own sub-period. Lord of the 2nd or 7th: bodily pain; remedy Shatarudriya or Mrityunjaya japa and the gift of a cow or female buffalo.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.78-89, Sanskrit with English gloss, enjoylearningsanskrit.com
source_views.view: Verse 79 adds deep exaltation and coronation. Verse 83 lists the 6th, 8th or 12th, or debilitated, or in the sign of loss. Verse 85 reads 'in the lagna or the 4th sign, by lordship of the 9th and 10th'. Verse 88: in its own bhukti these results, in other bhuktis according to their strength; as 2nd/7th lord bodily trouble. Verse 89: recite the Rudra or Tryambaka mantra and give a white cow or a buffalo, after which health returns.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 19.12 and 19.26 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib; 19.26 marked not proofread)
source_views.view: 19.12: things for pleasure and comfort, good vehicles, cows, gems, ornaments, treasure, enjoyment with young women, intellectual pursuits, voyages, auspicious acts, gifts from the ruler. 19.26: a wife, jewels, clothes, treasure, horses, comforts; wealth from trade, farming and voyages; but anxiety, mental distress, separation from or loss of parents and elders, and hardship to relatives.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.26 and 20.50 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri; siva.sh)
source_views.view: 20.26: Venus in its own or exaltation sign, not combust, not with a malefic, in the 10th, 11th or 12th gives gems, sharp intellect, great wealth and public praise. 20.50: Jupiter and Venus are harmful as kendra lords and become powerful death-inflicting planets if they also own or occupy the 2nd or 7th.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.158, 18.168-169 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri vol. 2, pp. 1071, 1075; 18.168 is printed as a second 169)
source_views.view: Venus's dasa gives a wife, children, wealth, great comfort, garlands, clothes, ornaments, vehicles, and fortune and fame like a king's. Venus exalted but in its debilitation navamsa: loss of wealth and status. Venus debilitated but in its exaltation navamsa: success in farming and trade and more wealth as the dasa ripens.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XXIV, pp. 230-233, 275-277
source_views.view: Gives results by Venus's sign: Aries palatial living, fame, a child; Taurus great ease and pleasure, sea travel, debts cleared, venereal trouble; Gemini gain of territory, vehicles, marital harmony; Cancer grief, loss of property and wealth, quarrels with relatives; Leo mental sorrow, danger from fire and poison, exile, illness of spouse or child; Virgo marital quarrels and separation, mortgaged property, genital and nervous troubles; Libra fame, royal patronage, luxury; Scorpio hatred, risks, loss of wealth; Sagittarius fame, religious study, success; Capricorn foreign travel, learning, success; Aquarius new property, books, honours, domestic harmony; Pisces political power, promotion, charity, domestic happiness. General rules: results vary with the dasa lord's strength, house, sign, aspects and navamsa, and are modified by transits.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers ch. 6, pp. 199-203
source_views.view: Lists the sub-periods of Venus's 20-year dasa. General method only: the major lord gives the results of the houses it rules and aspects; the relationship between major and minor lords is magnified, with 6/8/12 placements from each other working badly, trines and quadrants well, and friendship or enmity adjusting the outcome.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, sec. 16.5, pp. 214-215
source_views.view: General method only: each planet gives what it indicates in the divisional charts in its dasas; the Sun is the key reference for a mahadasha, the Moon for an antardasha, the lagna for a pratyantardasha, and the dasa lord can serve as a temporary lagna for its antardashas.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events (1998)
source_views.view: Case studies only, no general rules for Venus's dasa: Rath reads Venus-period events through house lordship in divisional charts (vehicles from D-16, education from D-24, parents from D-12) and prescribes the mantra of the planet's deity as a remedy.

dasha_md/venus.disagreements: BPHS 47.85: Santhanam has Venus 'in the 4th' as 9th or 10th lord, while the Sanskrit reads 'in the lagna or the 4th'. BPHS 47.83: the Sanskrit adds debilitation to the 6/8/12 condition, Santhanam omits it. BPHS 47.89 remedy: Santhanam gives Shatarudriya or Mrityunjaya japa, the Sanskrit gloss gives the Rudra or Tryambaka mantra. Both prescribe giving a (white) cow or a buffalo. Phaladeepika 19.26 adds anxiety and loss of parents and elders, which the other classical texts do not mention. Raman's sign-by-sign results make Cancer, Leo, Virgo and Scorpio bad, which follows no dignity rule in BPHS (Cancer and Leo are not Venus's debilitation).
dasha_md/venus.phrasing_guidance: Frame the Venus period as a long chapter centred on comfort, relationships, family events, possessions and the arts. Its tone depends on Venus's house, dignity and lordship. Where the chart shows the weak conditions, speak of strain in close relationships and money, and of keeping balance in pleasures. Never predict death, the loss of a parent or a specific illness; for the maraka rule, speak only of a time to look after health.

dasha_ad/jupiter/jupiter.summary: Jupiter's own sub-period at the start of its mahadasha (about 2 years 1 month 18 days) is good in every source when Jupiter is strong: high position, wealth, a new house, success, honour and happiness from spouse and children. BPHS turns it bad if Jupiter is debilitated, in a debilitated navamsa or in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the lagna, and warns of danger to life in that case.
common_outcomes: good fortune, prestige, a good son, royal honour, meeting one's teacher and good people, wishes fulfilled (Phaladeepika 21.39)
royal favour, great diligence, success in whatever is attempted, learning and science (Jataka Parijata 18.111)
more property, domestic happiness, gain from work, birth of children, reputation, good food, health, travel, pilgrimage and holy baths (Raman, p. 257)
rare_outcomes: building of a new house or mansion (BPHS 56.1-3)
slander by co-heirs and the employer's anger (BPHS 56.4-5, afflicted)
honour at stake if Jupiter is afflicted (Raman, p. 257)

by_area.personality: Great diligence and learning (Jataka Parijata 18.111; Raman).
by_area.career: High position, success in ventures, unusual profit from the employer, meetings with rulers (BPHS 56.1-3); the employer's anger when afflicted (BPHS 56.4-5).
by_area.finance: Wealth, cattle, clothes, ornaments, vehicles, a new house (BPHS 56.1-3); loss of wealth and grain when afflicted (BPHS 56.4-5).
by_area.health: Good health (Raman); bodily pain if Jupiter rules the 7th or 2nd (BPHS 56.6, Santhanam).
by_area.relationships: Happiness from wife and children (BPHS 56.3); separation from them when afflicted (BPHS 56.4-5).
by_area.family: Birth of a son or children (Phaladeepika 21.39; Raman); slander by co-heirs when afflicted (BPHS 56.4-5).
by_area.spirituality: Meeting the teacher and good people (Phaladeepika 21.39); pilgrimage and holy baths (Raman).

dasha_ad/jupiter/jupiter.lagna_or_context_notes: Here the dasha and sub-period lord are the same planet, so its position from the dasha lord is always the 1st; BPHS judges it from the lagna and by dignity only. P.S. Sastri's note on Uttara Kalamrita (p. 155) says a dasha lord is not usually expected to give good results in its own sub-period, and if it does the later sub-periods may be less fruitful; this is the translator's reading.

source_views.source: BPHS 56.1-7, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 678-679
source_views.view: Exalted, own sign, or in a kendra or trikona from the lagna: rule over many, wealth, honour from the king, cattle, clothes, ornaments, vehicles, a new house, fortune, success, meetings with Brahmins and the king, profit from the employer, happiness from wife and children. Debilitated, in a debilitated navamsa or in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the lagna: low company, distress, slander by co-heirs, the employer's anger, danger of premature death, separation from wife and children, loss of wealth and grain. Pain in the body if Jupiter rules the 7th (or 2nd). Remedy: Rudra japa and Shiva Sahasranama.

source_views.source: BPHS 56.1-7, Sanskrit with English gloss, enjoylearningsanskrit.com
source_views.view: Same good conditions. The bad case adds association with low people and thoughtless quarrels with kin and superiors that can bring untimely death; verse 6 blames 'a fault of the 7th lord' for trouble from deities. Remedy: Shiva Sahasranama, Rudra japa and the gift of a cow.

The Uttara Kalamrita translator's note doubts that the dasha lord gives good results in its own sub-period at all.

dasha_ad/jupiter/saturn.summary: Saturn's sub-period in Jupiter's dasha (about 2 years 6 months 12 days) is mixed. BPHS gives high position, property and travel west when Saturn is strong and well placed from the lagna or from Jupiter, but loss, fever, family trouble and estrangement when it is in a dusthana, combust or in an enemy sign; the other classics and Raman stress aversion, mental anguish, waste of money through sons and business failure.
common_outcomes: aversion, mental anguish, waste of wealth through sons, business failure (Jataka Parijata 18.112)
bad company and intoxicants, yet rise to eminence; illness in family and cattle, heavy expense, fear, eye trouble, children's illness (Phaladeepika 21.40)

aversion, anguish, waste through sons, business failure, bodily and rheumatic pain, trouble through spouse or partners, enmity of friends, family quarrels, court testimony, depression, funeral rites for others; also some rise in wealth (Raman, p. 257)
rare_outcomes: gain of a blue horse; journey west and an audience with the ruler (BPHS 56.8-11)
riches gained through an enemy (BPHS 56.15)
adultery (Raman, p. 257)

by_area.career: High position when Saturn is strong (BPHS 56.8-11); loss of employment, obstacles in ventures and business failure when weak (BPHS 56.12-17; Jataka Parijata 18.112).
by_area.finance: Wealth, grain, land, house and vehicles when strong (BPHS 56.9-15); loss of wealth and heavy expense when weak (BPHS 56.12-17; Phaladeepika 21.40).
by_area.health: Fever and mental illness (BPHS 56.13); eye trouble (Phaladeepika 21.40); rheumatic pains (Raman).
by_area.relationships: Joy from the wife when strong (BPHS 56.9, gloss); wounds or distress to wife and children when weak (BPHS 56.13); trouble through partners (Raman).
by_area.family: Happiness from sons and friends when strong (BPHS 56.10); antagonism with kin, danger from family members, illness of children (BPHS 56.14-17; Phaladeepika 21.40).

strengtheners: Saturn exalted or in its own sign, in a kendra or trikona, strong (BPHS 56.8)
Saturn in a kendra, trikona, the 11th or the 2nd from Jupiter (BPHS 56.15)

Saturn in the 6th, 8th or 12th from Jupiter or with a malefic (BPHS 56.16)
Saturn ruling the 2nd or 7th (BPHS 56.18)
dasha_ad/jupiter/saturn.lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS judges Saturn both from the lagna (verses 8-14) and from Jupiter (15-17). Frawley's general example uses exactly this pair: a negative Saturn sub-period inside a positive Jupiter dasha.

source_views.source: BPHS 56.8-19, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 679-681
source_views.view: Exalted, own sign, kendra or trikona with strength: high position, clothes, ornaments, wealth, grain, vehicles, cattle, happiness from son and friends, a blue horse, travel west and wealth from the king. In the 6th, 8th or 12th from the lagna, combust or in an enemy sign: loss of wealth, fever, mental agony, wounds to wife and children, bad events at home, loss of cattle and job, enmity of kin. In a kendra, trikona, 11th or 2nd from Jupiter: land, house, son, cattle, riches through the enemy. In the 6th, 8th or 12th from Jupiter or with a malefic: loss of wealth, enmity of kin, obstacles in industry, bodily pain, danger from family members. Lord of the 2nd or 7th: fear of premature death. Remedy: Vishnu Sahasranama and gift of a black cow or female buffalo.
