dasha_ad/sun/venus.summary: Venus's sub-period closes the Sun's mahadasha (1 year). BPHS makes it rich in marriage, comforts, jewels, vehicles, travel and high position when Venus is in a kendra or trikona or dignified, with a moderate start, gains in the middle and some loss of standing at the end. Other classical texts, reflecting the Sun-Venus enmity, stress head, throat and stomach ailments, illness of spouse and children, and losses.
common_outcomes: marriage, property, travel, meeting officials, high position, sweets, pearls and jewels, clothes, vehicles, good reputation (BPHS 52.65-68)
headache, stomach pain, anal trouble, loss of house, wealth and grain, illness of children, serious illness of the wife (Phaladeepika 21.11)
pearls or products of the sea, fatigue, addiction to bad women, profitless discussion (Jataka Parijata 18.70)
head and throat disease, fever and gout, defeat by enemies, leaving one's country (Saravali 42.16)
gain of money, respect from rulers, vehicles, likely marriage, more property, illness, good works, pearls, fatigue (Raman p. 238)
rare_outcomes: royal insignia, rulership (BPHS 52.65-66 gloss)
[maraka: text predicts danger to life / death] when Venus is joined with the lord of the 6th or 8th (BPHS 52.72)

by_area.personality: Enthusiasm, magnanimity (BPHS 52.67-68); mental agony when Venus is 6/8/12 from the Sun (BPHS 52.69).
by_area.career: High position and meetings with officials (BPHS 52.65-66); loss of position or fame at the end (BPHS 52.70); displeasure of the ruler when badly placed (BPHS 52.69).
by_area.finance: Riches, pearls, jewels, cattle, grain and vehicles (BPHS 52.67-68); loss of house, wealth and grain (Phaladeepika 21.11).
by_area.health: Headache, stomach and anal trouble (Phaladeepika 21.11); head, throat, fever and gout (Saravali 42.16); body pain and disease when Venus rules the 7th (BPHS 52.71).
by_area.relationships: Marriage and happiness with the wife (BPHS 52.65); serious illness of the wife (Phaladeepika 21.11); distress to wife and children when 6/8/12 from the Sun (BPHS 52.69); illicit connections (Jataka Parijata 18.70; Rele).
by_area.family: Auspicious functions at home (BPHS 52.67); enmity with kin and loss of comforts at the end (BPHS 52.70-71); illness of children (Phaladeepika 21.11).
by_area.spirituality: Meeting Brahmins (BPHS 52.66).

strengtheners: Venus in a kendra or trikona (BPHS 52.65)
Venus exalted, in its own sign, own varga or a friendly sign (BPHS 52.65)
Venus in Cancer (Rele p. 76)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Venus in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the Sun (BPHS 52.69)

Venus joined with the lord of the 6th or 8th (BPHS 52.72)
dasha_ad/sun/venus.lagna_or_context_notes: Venus is a natural enemy of the Sun (Rele p. 120). From the Sun, Venus can only be within two signs either side, so 'from the dasha lord' it can be 12th but not 6th or 8th. BPHS counts the good kendra/trikona from the lagna.

source_views.source: BPHS 52.65-73, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2
source_views.view: Venus in a kendra or trikona, exalted, own sign, own varga or a friendly sign: marriage and happiness with the wife, property, travel, meeting Brahmins and officials, high position, riches, magnanimity, auspicious functions, sweets, pearls and jewels, clothes, cattle, grain, vehicles, enthusiasm, good name. In 6/8/12 from the dasha lord: displeasure of the ruler, mental agony, distress to wife and children. Moderate at the start, good in the middle, disrepute, loss of position, enmity with kin and loss of comforts at the end. Lord of the 7th (and 2nd): body pain and disease. Joined with the lord of the 6th or 8th: premature death. Remedy: Mrityunjaya japa, Rudra japa, gift of a tawny cow or female buffalo.

source_views.source: BPHS 52.65-73, Sanskrit with English gloss, enjoylearningsanskrit.com
source_views.view: Adds royal insignia and conveyances carried by men; verse 69 reads Venus in 6/8/12 and weak under the dasha lord; verse 72 links the 8th and 12th houses with untimely death; remedy names a white cow and buffalo with Rudra japa.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 21.11 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Headache, stomach pain, trouble in the anus, farm work, loss of house, wealth and grain, illness of children, serious illness of the wife.

source_views.source: V.G. Rele, Directional Astrology of the Hindus, pp. 76-77
source_views.view: Exalted, own house, trines or Cancer: a wife of choice and desired children, distant travel, music, luxury, wealth. In 6/8/12 from the lagna or significator: displeasure of superiors, worry, illicit connection, loss of wife, son and wealth. With the 7th lord: mental disease and sloth; with the 8th and 12th lords: accidental death.

dasha_ad/sun/venus.disagreements: BPHS, Raman and Rele (for a well-placed Venus) are favourable; Phaladeepika and Saravali give only illness and loss; Jataka Parijata is mixed. The BPHS remedy cow is tawny in Santhanam and white in the gloss. Santhanam places the death danger with the 6th or 8th lord, the gloss with the 8th and 12th houses, Rele with the 8th and 12th lords.
dasha_ad/sun/venus.phrasing_guidance: Present as a comfortable, social closing phase of the Sun period when Venus is well placed, while advising moderation in pleasures, attention to the spouse's health and care of reputation toward the end. Do not predict death or infidelity as fact.

dasha_ad/venus/venus.summary: Venus's own sub-period at the start of its mahadasha (3 years 4 months) is one of the most consistently favourable in the texts: wealth, vehicles, clothes and ornaments, a new house, celebrations for children, comforts and royal favour. BPHS turns it bad when Venus is in the 6th, 8th or 12th with malefics, and gives fear of death when Venus rules the 2nd or 7th.
common_outcomes: clothes, ornaments, vehicles and perfumes in plenty, bodily lustre, comforts of the bed, wealth from the ruler (Phaladeepika 21.75)
conches, women, wealth and clothes, good work, enemies disappear, fame (Jataka Parijata 18.159)
success, good servants, many pleasures, plenty of money, enemies vanish, fame, birth of children (Raman p. 277-278)
wealth and cattle through Brahmins, celebrations for a son's birth, a new house, daily sweets, happiness of wife and children, gains of clothes, vehicles and ornaments (BPHS 60.1-6)
rare_outcomes: a kingdom or high government post (BPHS 60.2, 60.7-8)
travel westward bringing clothes and conveyances (BPHS 60.6)
[maraka: text predicts danger to life / death] when Venus rules the 2nd or 7th (BPHS 60.11)

by_area.personality: Enthusiasm and good spirits (BPHS 60.8).
by_area.career: Royal favour, high position, success in business (BPHS 60.2-8); success and fame (Raman); friction with officials and public hostility when Venus is in a dusthana with malefics (BPHS 60.9-10).
by_area.finance: Wealth, cattle, clothes, vehicles and ornaments (BPHS 60.2-6; Phaladeepika 21.75); plentiful money (Raman).
by_area.health: Bodily lustre (Phaladeepika 21.75); wounds and danger from thieves when Venus is in the 6th, 8th or 12th with malefics (BPHS 60.9).
by_area.relationships: Happiness of wife and children (BPHS 60.4); distress to wife and children when badly placed (BPHS 60.10); Rele adds marriage when well placed.
by_area.family: Celebrations for the birth of a son, prosperity at home (BPHS 60.2, 60.8); loss of friends and kinsmen when badly placed (BPHS 60.10).
by_area.spirituality: Giving food and grain in charity (BPHS 60.5).

Venus exalted, in its own sign, or in an exalted or own navamsa (BPHS 60.3-6)
Venus in an upachaya from the lagna with benefic association or aspect and in a friendly navamsa (BPHS 60.7)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Venus in the 6th, 8th or 12th with or aspected by a malefic (BPHS 60.9-10)
Venus lord of the 2nd or 7th (BPHS 60.11)
dasha_ad/venus/venus.lagna_or_context_notes: In its own sub-period Venus is both dasha and sub-period lord, so its position from the dasha lord is always the 1st; BPHS judges it from the lagna, by dignity and by navamsa. BPHS 47.88 adds that the mahadasha's results show most fully in this sub-period.

source_views.source: BPHS 60.1-11, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 730-731
source_views.view: Kendra, trikona or 11th from the lagna and strong: wealth and cattle through Brahmins, a son's birth, royal recognition, high position. Exalted, own sign or exalted/own navamsa: a new house, sweets, happiness of wife and children, charity, royal favour, clothes, vehicles, business success, westward journeys. Upachaya with benefics in a friendly navamsa: high position, enthusiasm, family growth. In the 6th, 8th or 12th with a malefic: thieves, friction with officials, loss of friends and kin, distress to wife and children. Lord of the 2nd or 7th: fear of death; remedy Durga Path and the gift of a cow.

source_views.source: BPHS 60.1-11, Sanskrit with English gloss, enjoylearningsanskrit.com
source_views.view: Verse 7 adds association with an exalted planet, the 11th lord and a yogakaraka. Verse 11: if the 2nd/7th lord is so placed, death may occur; recite Durga japa and give 'dhanu', glossed as a bow.

source_views.view: Clothes, ornaments, vehicles and perfumes in plenty, bodily lustre, comforts of the bed, wealth from the ruler.

source_views.view: Venus exalted, in own sign, in the 9th or 10th, in angles, trines or the 11th, or with the lagna lord: great wealth, princely comforts and pleasures, marriage or a son's birth, honours, travel west. In the 6th, 8th or 12th or with or aspected by a malefic: robbers, weapons, quarrels with superiors, loss of a brother, trouble to wife and children. In the 2nd or 7th: illness; with the lords of these houses: possible death.

dasha_ad/venus/venus.disagreements: BPHS 60.11 remedy: Santhanam reads the gift of a cow (dhenu), the enjoylearningsanskrit gloss reads 'dhanu' as a bow. Santhanam says the fear of death applies if Venus is lord of the 2nd or 7th; the gloss reads it as the planet ruling both the 2nd and 7th being adversely placed. Rele places the danger on Venus in the 2nd or 7th (illness) or joined with their lords (death). Phaladeepika, Jataka Parijata and Raman give only good results with no conditions.
dasha_ad/venus/venus.phrasing_guidance: Describe this as the sub-period where the Venus themes come through most clearly: comfort, home, relationships, family events and possessions. Mention the difficult version only when the chart shows Venus in the 6th, 8th or 12th with malefics. For the 2nd/7th-lord rule, speak only of looking after health; never predict death.

dasha_ad/venus/sun.summary: The Sun's sub-period in Venus's mahadasha (1 year) is described mostly as troubled: friction with authorities, quarrels with elders and co-sharers, ailments of the eyes, head and belly, and damage to farming and property. BPHS makes it good, with high position, wealth and family happiness, when the Sun is exalted, in its own sign, or in a kendra, trikona, 2nd or 11th from the lagna or from Venus.
common_outcomes: ailments of the eyes, belly and cheeks, danger from rulers, trouble from elders, family and relatives (Phaladeepika 21.76)
diseases of the head, belly and eyes, damage to farming, cattle and property, displeasure of rulers (Jataka Parijata 18.160)
anxiety, prosperity collapsing, troubles with wife, children and family, quarrels, head, belly and eye diseases, damage to farming (Raman p. 278)
agony, wrath of the government, quarrels with co-sharers (BPHS 60.12)
rare_outcomes: high government post, wealth, marriage, birth of a son, happiness from parents and employer (BPHS 60.13-15 when the Sun is strong)
snakes, danger at home, destruction of crops or property (BPHS 60.18)

by_area.personality: Agony and mental distress (BPHS 60.12, 60.16); anxiety about everything (Raman).
by_area.career: Wrath of the government (BPHS 60.12, 60.17; Jataka Parijata 18.160; Phaladeepika 21.76); high position and happiness from the employer when the Sun is strong (BPHS 60.13-15).
by_area.finance: Damage to farming, cattle and property (Jataka Parijata 18.160; Raman); gains of wealth when strong (BPHS 60.13-14).
by_area.health: Eyes, head, belly and cheeks (Phaladeepika 21.76; Jataka Parijata 18.160; Raman); many diseases when the Sun is in a dusthana or weak (BPHS 60.16-18).
by_area.relationships: Troubles with wife and children (Raman); marriage and happiness from wife and children when the Sun is strong (BPHS 60.13-15).
by_area.family: Quarrels with co-sharers (BPHS 60.12); distress to father and loss of kinsmen (BPHS 60.17); trouble from elders (Phaladeepika 21.76).

strengtheners: Sun exalted, in its own sign, or in a kendra, trikona, 2nd or 11th from the lagna or from Venus (BPHS 60.13-15)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Sun in the 6th, 8th or 12th, debilitated or in an enemy sign (BPHS 60.16-18)
Sun lord of the 2nd or 7th (BPHS 60.19)
dasha_ad/venus/sun.lagna_or_context_notes: The Sun and Venus are natural enemies; BPHS 60.13-15 counts the good positions both from the lagna and from Venus, the dasha lord. Santhanam flags verse 12 as faulty, since a Sun in an ordinary sign need not give bad results. The Sun rules only Leo, so it is lord of the 2nd for Cancer lagna and of the 7th for Aquarius lagna.

source_views.source: BPHS 60.12-20, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 732-733

Sun in the 6th, 8th or 12th, debilitated or in an enemy sign: distress, harsh speech, distress to father, loss of kin, wrath of the government, danger at home, many diseases, crop loss. Lord of the 2nd or 7th: evil from the planets; remedy worship of the Sun.

dasha_ad/venus/sun.phrasing_guidance: Present this as a short sub-period that asks for care with authority figures, elders and family harmony, and for attention to eyes and digestion. Give the favourable version when the Sun is strong as listed. Do not predict harm to the father.

dasha_ad/venus/moon.summary: The Moon's sub-period in Venus's mahadasha (1 year 8 months) is mixed. BPHS gives royal favour, wealth, vehicles, music and learned company, cattle and business profit when the Moon is strong or well placed from the lagna or from Venus, and loss of wealth, fear, journeys and separation from kin when it is debilitated, combust or in a dusthana. Phaladeepika, Jataka Parijata and Raman stress nervous, bilious and lustful complaints.
common_outcomes: inflammation of nails, head or teeth, wind and bile disorders, loss of wealth, diarrhoea, spleen trouble or wasting (Phaladeepika 21.77)
much pain from inflammation of the nerves and from lust and passions, with little ease (Jataka Parijata 18.161)
gains of women, learning, money, children and vehicles, worship, desires fulfilled, trouble through the wife then domestic happiness, nervous inflammation and passions (Raman p. 278)
wealth, conveyances and clothes by royal favour, devotion, music and learned company, cattle and business profit when the Moon is strong (BPHS 60.21-23)
rare_outcomes: rule over a province or village, building a reservoir (BPHS 60.27-28)
elephants and great opulence, merit from bathing in great rivers (BPHS 60.22, Sanskrit gloss)

by_area.personality: Agony and fear when the Moon is weak (BPHS 60.24-26); passions and lust (Jataka Parijata 18.161).
by_area.career: Royal favour and rule over a province or village (BPHS 60.21-28); wrath of the government when weak (BPHS 60.26); Rele: an administrative post and fame through writing.
by_area.finance: Wealth, vehicles, clothes, cattle, business profits (BPHS 60.21-23); loss of wealth (BPHS 60.24-25; Phaladeepika 21.77).
by_area.health: Nails, head, teeth, wind and bile, diarrhoea, spleen, wasting (Phaladeepika 21.77); nervous inflammation (Jataka Parijata 18.161; Raman); physical fitness at the start and distress at the end (BPHS 60.29).
by_area.relationships: Trouble through the wife, then domestic happiness (Raman); distress to wife and children when weak (BPHS 60.26-27).
by_area.family: Happiness in the family and dining with relatives (BPHS 60.21-24); separation from kinsmen when weak (BPHS 60.26-27).
by_area.spirituality: Devotion to deities and Brahmins (BPHS 60.21-22); pilgrimage (BPHS 60.26).

strengtheners: Moon exalted, in its own sign, with the 9th lord, the 10th lord or benefics, or in a kendra, trikona or the 11th (BPHS 60.21-23)
Moon in a kendra, trikona, 3rd or 11th from Venus (BPHS 60.27-28)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Moon debilitated or combust, or in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the lagna or from Venus (BPHS 60.24-26)
dasha_ad/venus/moon.lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS keeps two reference points: verses 21-26 count from the lagna (and Santhanam adds 'or the lord of the Dasa' for the bad positions), verses 27-29 from Venus. Santhanam notes that the 2nd/7th-lord rule given for the other planets is not stated for the Moon here.

source_views.source: BPHS 60.20-29, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 733-734
source_views.view: Moon exalted, own sign, with the 9th lord, benefics or the 10th lord, or in a kendra, trikona or 11th: wealth, conveyances and clothes by royal favour, family happiness, opulence, devotion; music and learned company, cattle, business profits, dining with brothers. Debilitated, combust, or in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the lagna or Venus: loss of wealth, fears, physical distress, wrath of the government, foreign journeys or pilgrimage, distress to wife and children, separation from kinsmen. Kendra, trikona, 3rd or 11th from Venus: rule over a province or village, clothes, a reservoir, more wealth; fitness at the start and distress at the end.

source_views.view: Moon exalted, own sign, with a benefic or the 9th or 10th lords, in angles, trines, 11th or 12th from the lagna or significator: gain and fame through writing, favours, business prosperity, singing and dancing, a larger family, possibly an administrative post. Debilitated or in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the lagna or significator: loss by speculation, quarrels, foreign travel, family trouble, separation of brothers, some mental and physical trouble.

Rele lists the 12th as a good house for the Moon, which BPHS does not. The Sanskrit verse 21 requires a full Moon; Santhanam does not.
dasha_ad/venus/moon.phrasing_guidance: Present this as a sub-period whose tone follows the Moon's strength: creative, social and financially active when strong, emotionally and physically draining when weak. Suggest moderation and rest; avoid naming specific diseases.

dasha_ad/venus/mars.summary: Mars's sub-period in Venus's mahadasha (1 year 2 months) brings income, land, gold and marriage or romance alongside bile and blood disorders, eye trouble and heavy exertion. BPHS gives position, property and desired objects when Mars is in a kendra, trikona or the 11th, exalted or in its own sign, and fevers, quarrels, loss of position and overspending when Mars is in the 6th, 8th or 12th.
common_outcomes: bleeding and bile disorders, gain of gold and copper, land, involvement with a young woman, loss of position (Phaladeepika 21.78)
flow of bile, eye disease, great exertion, money coming in, acquisition of wives and lands (Jataka Parijata 18.162)
bile, eye disease, exertion, much income, marriage, lands, venereal disease, danger from weapons, exile, pleasure-seeking, property through women (Raman p. 278)
high position, property, clothes, ornaments, land and desired objects when Mars is well placed (BPHS 60.30-31)
rare_outcomes: raja-yoga-like prosperity when Mars joins the lagna, 9th or 10th lord (BPHS 60.31)
atheistic leanings and neglect of duty (Raman p. 278)

by_area.personality: Bent on pleasure and passion (Raman); mental distress when badly placed (BPHS 60.33).
by_area.career: High position (BPHS 60.30-31); loss of position, antagonism with government officials (BPHS 60.32-34; Phaladeepika 21.78); losses in profession as 2nd/7th lord (BPHS 60.35).
by_area.finance: Gold, copper, land and income (Phaladeepika 21.78; Jataka Parijata 18.162); extravagant spending (BPHS 60.34); loss of village or land as 2nd/7th lord (BPHS 60.35).
by_area.health: Bile, bleeding, eye disease (Phaladeepika 21.78; Jataka Parijata 18.162; Raman); cold fevers when badly placed (BPHS 60.33); venereal disease and danger from weapons (Raman).
by_area.relationships: Acquisition of wives, marriage, a young woman (Jataka Parijata 18.162; Raman; Phaladeepika 21.78).
by_area.family: Fevers to parents, quarrels, loss of kinsmen when badly placed (BPHS 60.33-34).

strengtheners: Mars in a kendra, trikona or 11th from the lagna, exalted or in its own sign (BPHS 60.30)
Mars with the lagna lord, 9th lord or 10th lord (BPHS 60.31)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mars in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the lagna or from Venus (BPHS 60.32-34)
Mars lord of the 2nd or 7th (BPHS 60.35)
dasha_ad/venus/mars.lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS counts the bad positions both from the lagna and from Venus (verse 32 'or from the dasa lord'). Mars and Venus together are linked by all four classical texts to passion, marriage and property. Mars rules the 2nd for Pisces and Libra lagnas and the 7th for Libra and Taurus lagnas.

source_views.source: BPHS 60.30-35, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, p. 735
source_views.view: Mars in a kendra, trikona or 11th from the lagna, exalted or in its own sign, or with the lagna, 9th or 10th lord: high position, property, clothes, ornaments, land, desired objects. In the 6th, 8th or 12th from the lagna or Venus: cold fevers, fever to parents, loss of position, quarrels, antagonism with government and officials, extravagance. Lord of the 2nd or 7th: physical distress, losses in profession, loss of village or land. Santhanam adds his own note that giving a bull in charity should bring relief, though the text gives no remedy.

dasha_ad/venus/rahu.summary: Rahu's sub-period in Venus's mahadasha (3 years) is mixed: BPHS gives enjoyment, wealth, land, successful journeys and victory over enemies when Rahu is in a kendra, trikona, 11th or upachaya, exalted or aspected by benefics, with fever or indigestion at one end of the period. Phaladeepika adds hidden treasure and a son but danger from fire, thieves or poison; Jataka Parijata and Raman stress dislike of relatives, trouble from friends and fire.
common_outcomes: discovery of treasure, birth of a son, good news, honour from kin, enemies defeated, harm from fire, thieves or poison (Phaladeepika 21.79)
acquisition of 'black' valuables, dislike of relatives, evil from friends, injury by fire (Jataka Parijata 18.163)
seclusion and meditation, quarrels among relatives, complete change of surroundings, deception, miserliness, recovery of lost property, evil from friends, fire (Raman p. 279)
great enjoyment, wealth, friends' visits, successful journeys, cattle and land when Rahu is well placed (BPHS 60.36-38)
rare_outcomes: kingly enjoyments and success through foreign journeys with safe return home (BPHS 60.40-41)
blessings from Brahmins and merit from holy places (BPHS 60.41-42)

by_area.personality: Worries and obstacles (BPHS 60.40); seclusion, meditation, deception and miserliness (Raman).
by_area.career: Success in ventures, royal favour, enemies destroyed (BPHS 60.38-39); antagonism with people when badly placed (BPHS 60.42-43).
by_area.finance: Wealth, cattle, land (BPHS 60.37-38); hidden treasure (Phaladeepika 21.79); 'black' valuables (Jataka Parijata 18.163); recovery of lost property (Raman).
by_area.health: Fever and indigestion at one end of the sub-period (BPHS 60.39); physical distress or lethargy with Rahu in the 2nd or 7th (BPHS 60.44); injury by fire or poison (Phaladeepika 21.79; Jataka Parijata 18.163).
by_area.relationships: Evil from friends (Jataka Parijata 18.163; Raman).
by_area.family: Birth of a son and honour from kin (Phaladeepika 21.79); dislike of and quarrels among relatives (Jataka Parijata 18.163; Raman); inauspicious for parents when badly placed (BPHS 60.43).
by_area.spirituality: Pilgrimage and blessings from Brahmins (BPHS 60.41-42); meditation and seclusion (Raman).

strengtheners: Rahu in a kendra, trikona or 11th, exalted, aspected by benefics or joined with a yogakaraka (BPHS 60.36)
Rahu in an upachaya from the lagna (BPHS 60.38)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Rahu with a malefic in the 8th or 12th from Venus (BPHS 60.42-43)
Rahu in (Santhanam: lord of) the 2nd or 7th (BPHS 60.44)
dasha_ad/venus/rahu.lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS gives the good positions from the lagna and the bad ones from Venus, the dasha lord. Rahu owns no sign in this library, so Santhanam's '2nd or 7th lord' rule is checked as placement, following the Sanskrit gloss.

source_views.source: BPHS 60.36-44, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 736-737
source_views.view: Rahu in a kendra, trikona or 11th, exalted or in own sign, or with or aspected by benefics: great enjoyment, wealth, friends' visits, successful journeys, cattle and land. In an upachaya from the lagna: enjoyment, destruction of enemies, enthusiasm, royal favour; good for five months from the start, fever and indigestion at the end. Apart from obstacles and worries on journeys, kingly enjoyments; foreign journeys succeed with safe return; Brahmins' blessings, holy places. With a malefic in the 8th or 12th from Venus: inauspicious for self and parents, antagonism with people. Lord of the 2nd or 7th: physical distress. Remedy Mrityunjaya japa.

Verse 42 reads the 8th or 12th from the dasa lord, or with malefics. Verse 44: in the 2nd or 7th, bodily lethargy; Mrityunjaya japa.

dasha_ad/venus/jupiter.summary: Jupiter's sub-period in Venus's mahadasha (2 years 8 months) is generally described as good: wealth, clothes and ornaments, religious duties, family life with wife and children, reputation, learning and recovery of a lost position. The texts warn of illness to wife and children, and BPHS of trouble from rulers and thieves, quarrels and loss of position when Jupiter is in the 6th, 8th or 12th from Venus with a malefic.
common_outcomes: religious duties, worship of the gods, happy home life with wife and children, pleasures of authority (Phaladeepika 21.80)
wealth, clothes and ornaments, religious duties leading to happiness; wife and children may fall ill (Jataka Parijata 18.164)
settled livelihood, gains from profession, help from superiors, fame, gain of knowledge, end of dependence, marriage, wealth, good deeds; wife and children suffer in the end (Raman p. 279)
recovery of a lost position, grains, clothes, property, reputation, conveyances, learned company, study of the shastras, a son's birth, happiness to parents (BPHS 60.45-48)
rare_outcomes: anxiety and quarrels with religious men (Raman p. 279)
going away to foreign lands, many kinds of disease (BPHS 60.50, when badly placed)

by_area.personality: Satisfaction (BPHS 60.48); mental agony from quarrels when badly placed (BPHS 60.50).
by_area.career: Reinstatement in a high position, recognition from the ruler, association with the employer (BPHS 60.46-47); settled livelihood and help from superiors (Raman); loss of position when badly placed (BPHS 60.50).
by_area.finance: Wealth, grain, clothes, property and conveyances (BPHS 60.46-47; Jataka Parijata 18.164).
by_area.health: Physical distress when Jupiter is badly placed or rules the 2nd/7th (BPHS 60.49-51).
by_area.relationships: Happy home life with the wife (Phaladeepika 21.80); illness of wife and children (Jataka Parijata 18.164; Raman); marriage (Raman).
by_area.family: Birth of a son, visits of close friends, happiness to parents and son (BPHS 60.48); distress to kinsmen when badly placed (BPHS 60.50).
by_area.spirituality: Religious duties and worship (Phaladeepika 21.80; Jataka Parijata 18.164); study of the shastras (BPHS 60.47).

strengtheners: Jupiter exalted, in its own sign, or in a kendra or trikona from the lagna or from Venus (BPHS 60.45-48)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Jupiter in the 6th, 8th or 12th from Venus and with a malefic (BPHS 60.49-50)
Jupiter lord of the 2nd or 7th (BPHS 60.51)
dasha_ad/venus/jupiter.lagna_or_context_notes: Jupiter and Venus are both benefics but natural enemies. BPHS gives the good positions from the lagna or from Venus and the bad ones from Venus only. Jupiter is lord of the 2nd for Scorpio and Aquarius lagnas and of the 7th for Gemini and Virgo lagnas.

In the 6th, 8th or 12th from Venus with a malefic: danger from rulers and thieves, distress to self and kin, quarrels, agony, loss of position, going abroad, many diseases. Lord of the 2nd and 7th: physical distress; remedy Mrityunjaya japa.

dasha_ad/venus/saturn.summary: Saturn's sub-period in Venus's mahadasha (3 years 2 months) is generally productive: houses, lands and wealth, honour from authorities, enemies removed, and for BPHS the birth of a daughter and pilgrimages when Saturn is strong. Weak or badly placed, Saturn brings lethargy, spending above income, trouble to parents, spouse and children, and business losses; Raman adds chronic ailments and bad habits.
common_outcomes: honour from civic leaders, the army, police or the ruler, a desirable spouse, more wealth and goods, comforts (Phaladeepika 21.81)
liaison with older women, houses, lands and wealth, enemies disappear (Jataka Parijata 18.165)
relations with older women, lands and wealth, enemies vanish, piles, rheumatic pains, eye trouble, poor appetite, money loss, wandering, servitude, gambling or drink, poor memory (Raman pp. 279-280)
great enjoyment, friends and kin, recognition from the government, birth of a daughter, pilgrimages, authority conferred (BPHS 60.52-54)
rare_outcomes: wandering in foreign lands (BPHS 60.56)
impotence and addiction (Raman p. 280)

by_area.career: Authority conferred by the ruler, position from one's master (BPHS 60.53-54); honour from the army, police or rulers (Phaladeepika 21.81); servitude (Raman); losses in profession when badly placed (BPHS 60.57).
by_area.finance: Houses, lands and wealth (Jataka Parijata 18.165; Phaladeepika 21.81); expenditure above income when Saturn is debilitated (BPHS 60.55); loss of money and gambling (Raman).
by_area.health: Physical distress as 2nd/7th lord (BPHS 60.57); piles, rheumatic pains, eyesight, poor appetite (Raman).
by_area.relationships: A desirable spouse (Phaladeepika 21.81); liaison with older women (Jataka Parijata 18.165; Raman); distress to wife and children when badly placed (BPHS 60.56).
by_area.family: Birth of a daughter, reunion with relatives (BPHS 60.53); distress to parents at the start when badly placed (BPHS 60.56).
by_area.spirituality: Pilgrimage, charity and virtuous acts (BPHS 60.54).

strengtheners: Saturn exalted (deep exaltation), in its own sign, in a kendra or trikona, or in its own or exalted navamsa (BPHS 60.52)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saturn debilitated (BPHS 60.54-55)

BPHS counts the bad positions from the lagna or from Venus. Saturn rules the 2nd for Sagittarius and Capricorn lagnas and the 7th for Cancer and Leo lagnas.

dasha_ad/venus/mercury.summary: Mercury's sub-period in Venus's mahadasha (2 years 10 months) is among the most favourable: comfort from children and friends, wealth, royal favour, learning, the arts and sound health. BPHS gives the good results when Mercury is in a kendra, trikona or 11th, exalted or in its own sign, with the pattern good at the start, middling in the middle and fever at the end; badly placed from Venus it brings loss in business and living away from home.
common_outcomes: comfort from sons, happiness, power and fame, defeat of enemies, but wind and bile illness (Phaladeepika 21.82)
comfort from sons and friends, wealth, royal favour, happiness on a large scale, prosperity and sound health (Jataka Parijata 18.166)
pleasures with courtesans, knowledge and mathematics, success in litigation, music, piles and hot ailments, joy from wife and children, wealth, royal favour, prosperity, sound health (Raman p. 280)
dawn of fortune, birth of a son, wealth through a court judgement, listening to the Puranas, company of poets, friends, happiness from the employer, sweets (BPHS 60.60-62)
rare_outcomes: living in other people's houses and loss in all ventures when badly placed (BPHS 60.63-64)

by_area.finance: Wealth through just means or a court ruling (BPHS 60.61); increase of wealth (Jataka Parijata 18.166; Raman); loss of cattle when badly placed (BPHS 60.63).
by_area.health: Sound health (Jataka Parijata 18.166); wind and bile (Phaladeepika 21.82); piles and hot ailments (Raman); fever and colds at the end of the sub-period (BPHS 60.65).
by_area.relationships: Pleasure through wife and children (Raman); association with amorous company (BPHS 60.61 gloss; Raman).
by_area.family: Birth of a son, a house full of relatives and friends (BPHS 60.60-62); comfort from sons (Phaladeepika 21.82; Jataka Parijata 18.166).
by_area.spirituality: Listening to the Puranas (BPHS 60.61).

strengtheners: Mercury in a kendra, trikona or 11th, exalted or in its own sign (BPHS 60.60)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mercury in the 6th, 8th or 12th from Venus, weak, or with or aspected by a malefic (BPHS 60.63-64)
Mercury lord of the 2nd or 7th (BPHS 60.66)

Mercury rules the 2nd for Taurus and Leo lagnas and the 7th for Sagittarius and Pisces lagnas.

dasha_ad/venus/ketu.summary: Ketu's sub-period closing Venus's mahadasha (1 year 2 months) is described mostly as difficult: discord, loss of relatives, injury from enemies, anxiety, loss of wealth, fire, and friction with spouse and children. BPHS makes it good, with gains, cattle and victory, when Ketu is exalted, in its own sign, linked to a yogakaraka or strong, and bad when Ketu is in the 8th or 12th from Venus or with a malefic.
common_outcomes: loss of children and happiness, danger from fire, injury or disease to a limb, association with courtesans (Phaladeepika 21.83)
discord, death of relatives, injury from enemies, misgivings in the heart, loss of wealth (Jataka Parijata 18.167)

discord, death of relatives, injury from enemies, loss of wealth, troubles through the wife, danger from animals, illness of partner or family, weakness of body and mind, seclusion, but happiness at the end (Raman p. 280)
snakes, thieves, wounds, poor thinking, headache, causeless quarrels, diabetes, heavy expenses, antagonism with wife and children, foreign travel, failed ventures when badly placed (BPHS 60.70-72)
rare_outcomes: sweets, abnormal gains and more cattle, victory in war (BPHS 60.67-69 when Ketu is strong)
accidental blood poisoning and delirious fits (Raman p. 280)

by_area.relationships: Antagonism with wife and children (BPHS 60.72); troubles through the wife and illness of the partner (Raman); association with courtesans (Phaladeepika 21.83).

transit/saturn/1.summary: Saturn over the natal Moon's own sign (janma Shani) is one of its hardest transits in the classical texts: illness, losses, separation from family, humiliation and tiring travel. It is the middle, peak phase of Sade Sati.
common_outcomes: illness or low vitality
loss of money and of comforts
separation from relatives or living away from home
loss of standing or humiliation
tiring, unwanted journeys
rare_outcomes: a death in the family for which the native performs the last rites [maraka: text predicts death of a relative]
danger from poison or fire, confinement or harassment (Brihat Samhita)
[maraka: text predicts danger to life] when Saturn is in the 1st from the Moon (Phaladeepika 26.33)

by_area.personality: Mind under pressure; humiliation and loss of confidence (Brihat Samhita 104.39). Popular modern accounts call this the most intense part of Sade Sati.
by_area.career: Loss of position is listed among the dangers of Saturn in the 1st from the Moon (Phaladeepika 26.33).
by_area.finance: Loss of wealth (Brihat Samhita 104.39; Phaladeepika 26.33).
by_area.health: Disease (Phaladeepika 26.22); fatigue from journeys on foot (Brihat Samhita 104.39).
by_area.relationships: Separation from kinsmen; living among friends in a foreign place (Brihat Samhita 104.39).
by_area.family: Loss of sons and a bereavement requiring the native to perform funeral rites (Phaladeepika 26.22; Brihat Samhita 104.39).

transit/saturn/5.summary: Saturn in the 5th from the Moon is unfavourable: worry over children, decline of money, a confused mind and quarrels.
common_outcomes: concern for or separation from children

quarrels

weakeners_or_cancellations: (intensifying) Saturn debilitated (Aries) or in an enemy's sign (Phaladeepika 26.32)

(intensifying) no or few bindus in Saturn's ashtakavarga for the sign (Raman)
transit/saturn/5.lagna_or_context_notes: Classical gochara is counted from the natal Moon's sign; Phaladeepika 26.1 says only the Moon's lagna counts for transits. P.S. Sastri's note to Uttara Kalamrita ch. 6 (verse on annual results) records other views: count from the lagna up to age 33, from the Moon for the next 33 years and from the Sun after that, or from the stronger of lagna and Moon. Modern authors treat transits as secondary to the natal chart and dasha: Frawley gives them about one-third weight in judging a period; Raman (HPA ch. 34) says the birth chart, dasha, ashtakavarga and vedha must be blended; Brihat Samhita 104.46 says benefic results scale with the running dasha and the person's station. Saturn's transit gives the 2.5-year (triennial) results (Raman).

transit/saturn/8.summary: Saturn in the 8th from the Moon (ashtama Shani, the 'big Dhaiya') is one of its worst transits in the classical texts: losses, illness, separation from family and friends, and hardship.
common_outcomes: losses of money and possessions
illness

by_area.career: Loss of position is among the dangers of Saturn in the 8th from the Moon (Phaladeepika 26.33).

by_area.health: Disease (Phaladeepika 26.22).

transit/saturn/8.lagna_or_context_notes: Classical gochara is counted from the natal Moon's sign; Phaladeepika 26.1 says only the Moon's lagna counts for transits. P.S. Sastri's note to Uttara Kalamrita ch. 6 (verse on annual results) records other views: count from the lagna up to age 33, from the Moon for the next 33 years and from the Sun after that, or from the stronger of lagna and Moon. Modern authors treat transits as secondary to the natal chart and dasha: Frawley gives them about one-third weight in judging a period; Raman (HPA ch. 34) says the birth chart, dasha, ashtakavarga and vedha must be blended; Brihat Samhita 104.46 says benefic results scale with the running dasha and the person's station. Saturn's transit gives the 2.5-year (triennial) results (Raman). Modern name: ashtama Shani, the 8th-house Dhaiya; see sade_sati/ashtama_dhaiya.

transit/saturn/11.lagna_or_context_notes: Classical gochara is counted from the natal Moon's sign; Phaladeepika 26.1 says only the Moon's lagna counts for transits. P.S. Sastri's note to Uttara Kalamrita ch. 6 (verse on annual results) records other views: count from the lagna up to age 33, from the Moon for the next 33 years and from the Sun after that, or from the stronger of lagna and Moon. Modern authors treat transits as secondary to the natal chart and dasha: Frawley gives them about one-third weight in judging a period; Raman (HPA ch. 34) says the birth chart, dasha, ashtakavarga and vedha must be blended; Brihat Samhita 104.46 says benefic results scale with the running dasha and the person's station. Saturn's transit gives the 2.5-year (triennial) results (Raman).

sade_sati/rising.summary: The rising (first) phase of Sade Sati: Saturn in the 12th sign from the natal Moon (vyaya Shani), about 2.5 years. The classical texts treat this house as bad (fruitless effort, losses, family illness, grief); modern authors describe the start of Saturn's pressure, awareness of losses and of where more responsibility is needed. Sade Sati as a named 7.5-year period is a later popular tradition, not in the classical texts read.

by_area.relationships: Trouble from enemies (Phaladeepika 26.23).

sade_sati/rising.lagna_or_context_notes: Classical status: none of the classical texts read for this entry (Phaladeepika ch. 26, Brihat Samhita ch. 104, Saravali ch. 53, Uttara Kalamrita ch. 6) names Sade Sati or Dhaiya; they judge each house from the Moon separately, and Phaladeepika 26.33 singles out Saturn in the 12th, 8th or 1st from the Moon as dangerous. Svoboda states that sade sati (Gujarati panoti) does not appear as such in the standard classical texts and that its origins are unclear; it is a later, popular tradition, very widely followed. Phase key: Saturn in the 12th sign from the natal Moon (whole signs; see transit/saturn/12 for the house-level classical results). Reckoning is from the Moon sign; Wikipedia reports a variant using 45 degrees either side of the natal Moon.

sade_sati/rising.phases: Each sign takes about 2.5 years; the three Sade Sati signs together about 7.5 years. Svoboda: the period starts 'as if a switch' when Saturn enters the sign before the Moon; a brief entry followed by retrogression gives 'advance notice' of effects that begin fully on the final entry. Classical rule: Saturn gives transit results mainly in the last part of a sign (Phaladeepika 26.25; Saravali 53.10).

sade_sati/peak.summary: The peak (second) phase of Sade Sati: Saturn over the natal Moon's own sign (janma Shani), about 2.5 years, usually called the most intense. The classical texts treat Saturn here as very bad (illness, losses, separation, humiliation, a bereavement); modern authors describe it as the phase where pressure and grief are processed and character is tested.

illness or low vitality
losses of money or position
separation from family or living away from home

rare_outcomes: danger from poison or fire, confinement (Brihat Samhita)

by_area.family: Loss of sons and a bereavement (Phaladeepika 26.22; Brihat Samhita 104.39).

sade_sati/peak.lagna_or_context_notes: Classical status: none of the classical texts read for this entry (Phaladeepika ch. 26, Brihat Samhita ch. 104, Saravali ch. 53, Uttara Kalamrita ch. 6) names Sade Sati or Dhaiya; they judge each house from the Moon separately, and Phaladeepika 26.33 singles out Saturn in the 12th, 8th or 1st from the Moon as dangerous. Svoboda states that sade sati (Gujarati panoti) does not appear as such in the standard classical texts and that its origins are unclear; it is a later, popular tradition, very widely followed. Reckoning is from the Moon sign; Wikipedia reports a variant using 45 degrees either side of the natal Moon.

sade_sati/peak.phrasing_guidance: Call it the most demanding stretch, a time to slow down, protect health and keep commitments realistic; stress that outcomes depend on the whole chart and dasha and that many people achieve a great deal in it. sade_sati/ashtama_dhaiya.disagreements: Popular accounts call the Dhaiyas less intense than Sade Sati, while Phaladeepika 26.33 groups the 8th with the 12th and 1st as the most dangerous places for Saturn. Modern authors differ on severity. Svoboda says the sade sati 'creates trouble for most everyone' and is gloomier than the Saturn return. Kurczak calls the fear-based framing 'folklore and myth' and now weighs mainly the 2.5 years over the Moon's own sign. Nirikhi Krishna Bhagavan lists severe effects but also good events (marriage, a child, promotion, property) and many exceptions. Raman treats a second Sade Sati as only moderately evil. K.N. Rao edited a group-research book titled 'Saadhe Saati: A Balanced View' (via summary: publisher's blurb only). Wikipedia (tertiary) reports a school holding it is less damaging than folk belief, and a variant reckoning of 45 degrees either side of the natal Moon instead of whole signs.
sade_sati/ashtama_dhaiya.phrasing_guidance: Describe a testing period for health, money and close ties that calls for caution, rest, avoiding risk and debt; never predict death or serious illness. Say plainly that Sade Sati and Dhaiya are popular traditions built on older house-by-house transit rules, and that modern authors disagree about how severe they are.

yogini/mangala.lagna_or_context_notes: Mansagari judges the period by the yogini's name (four benefic, four malefic) and by its planet's dignity. Chugh: results are modified by the strength and placement of the yogini's planet, including in divisional charts; apply the usual Vimshottari checks to it, and blend yogini and Vimshottari results before predicting; the end of one 36-year cycle and start of the next marks a turning point. Kursija instead says yogini periods should be predicted from the planets' natural results, not from house lordship. Goel (K.N. Rao's group) reads each period through the nakshatra that 'contributes' it: the sign holding that nakshatra is a progressed lagna, and the condition of that nakshatra's lord is judged in the natal and progressed charts. Jhanji: judge the period lord from the house in question and its significator, as alternative lagnas.

Rahu well placed and unafflicted (Chugh)
sub-period of a benefic yogini (Chugh: benefic-benefic very good; malefic main with benefic sub = good tending to neutral)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Rahu combust, debilitated or in an enemy sign (Mansagari: period becomes middling)
Rahu weak or afflicted (Chugh)
sub-period of a malefic yogini (Chugh: malefic-malefic very bad)
yogini/sankata.lagna_or_context_notes: Mansagari judges the period by the yogini's name (four benefic, four malefic) and by its planet's dignity. Chugh: results are modified by the strength and placement of the yogini's planet, including in divisional charts; apply the usual Vimshottari checks to it, and blend yogini and Vimshottari results before predicting; the end of one 36-year cycle and start of the next marks a turning point. Kursija instead says yogini periods should be predicted from the planets' natural results, not from house lordship. Goel (K.N. Rao's group) reads each period through the nakshatra that 'contributes' it: the sign holding that nakshatra is a progressed lagna, and the condition of that nakshatra's lord is judged in the natal and progressed charts. Jhanji: judge the period lord from the house in question and its significator, as alternative lagnas.

source_views.source: BPHS 46.196-198 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: names Sankata as the eighth yogini, from whom the shadow planet (tamas, glossed Rahu) arose

source_views.source: BPHS 46.199-200 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
source_views.view: start = (birth nakshatra number + 3) / 8, remainder gives the yogini; periods run 1 year rising by 1, so Sankata = 8 years; BPHS gives no results for the periods

source_views.source: Manasagari, Yogini-dasha section (Subodhini Hindi comm. Madhukanta Jha, Chowkhamba 1963, pp. 470-474), mahadasha-phala v.8
source_views.view: loss of position or kingdom; fear of fire in house, town, village and cattle-shed; thirst, disease, wasting of the body's tissues; separation from son and wife; delusion; fear of enemies; weakness of body; after birth, death does not happen without a dasha or antardasha of Sankata. v.9: if the Sankata antardasha falls in the dasha of Bhramari or Ulka, death follows (commentary: if in the life-span segment, otherwise suffering like death)

source_views.source: Manasagari, Yogini-dasha section (Subodhini Hindi comm. Madhukanta Jha, Chowkhamba 1963, pp. 470-474), v.4; Manasagari, Yogini-dasha-svamin verses (Subodhini ed. M. Jha, 1963, pp. 486-487), v.1
source_views.view: one of the four inauspicious yoginis (Pingala, Bhramari, Ulka, Sankata); results follow the name; malefic yoginis have malefic lords

source_views.source: Sumeet Chugh, Yogini and Kalachakra Dasas (Sagar), ch. 3 'Results of Yogini Dasa' (results based on Mansagari plus the author's experience)
source_views.view: can be extremely unfortunate: losses, death of near relations, disease, legal cases, imprisonment, dishonour, all-round difficulty; distress to the relative signified by Rahu's house

source_views.source: Dr. S.C. Kursija, A Practical Guide to Prediction through Dasha System (AIFAS), 'Prediction of Yogini Dasha'
source_views.view: ruin of the state; houses, villages and cities may catch fire; disease and loss of virility; separation from wife and sons; death takes place only in the period or sub-period of Sankata, certainly if Sankata's sub-period falls in Bhramari or Ulka

source_views.source: Rajeev Jhanji, An Introduction to the Yogini Dasha (vedicastro.com)
source_views.view: malefic yogini; Sankata ruled by Rahu, 8 years; results follow the yogini's meaning

source_views.source: Manasagari, Yogini-dasha-svamin verses (Subodhini ed. M. Jha, 1963, pp. 486-487), vv.3-4 (a variant 'of some')
source_views.view: Rahu arose from Sankata, and Ketu is likewise assigned at the end of this dasha; the commentary says Rahu and Ketu are treated as one in yogini reckoning

yogini/sankata.disagreements: Mapping: BPHS 46.197-198 and the main Mansagari verse give Rahu for Sankata; a variant cited in Mansagari ('of some') swaps Dhanya to Mercury and Bhadrika to Jupiter, and assigns Ketu at the end of Sankata (Jhanji: some give Sankata's first half to Rahu and second half to Ketu). Durations 1-8 years (36 total) agree across BPHS 46.200, Mansagari v.5 and all modern sources. Kursija's English for Pingala says 'free from' the diseases, contradicting the Mansagari Sanskrit and Hindi. Chugh lets the planet's placement modify results; Kursija says predict by natural results only.
yogini/sankata.phrasing_guidance: Describe the yogini as the tone of a period of 8 years and always say the planet's condition and the running Vimshottari dasha shape how it shows. Frame difficulties as a period calling for patience and care; never predict death, imprisonment, disability or the death of relatives, and mention remedies gently.

conditional_results.when: manual: if Rahu is well placed in combination with a yogakaraka in a kendra or trikona
effects: a raja yoga can arise, but in Sankata it seldom lasts and is a prelude to grave dangers or disgrace
conditional_results.source: Sumeet Chugh, Yogini and Kalachakra Dasas (Sagar), ch. 3 'Results of Yogini Dasa', Sankata

effects: can leave a lasting physical handicap
conditional_results.source: Sumeet Chugh, Yogini and Kalachakra Dasas (Sagar), ch. 3 'Results of Yogini Dasa', Sankata

effects: an unfortunate event concerning children (Chugh's example of distress to the relative of Rahu's house)
conditional_results.source: Sumeet Chugh, Yogini and Kalachakra Dasas (Sagar), ch. 3 'Results of Yogini Dasa', Sankata

conditional_results.when: manual: if the antardasha of Sankata falls within the mahadasha of Bhramari or Ulka
effects: [maraka: text predicts danger to life / death] (commentary: certain only within the life-span segment, otherwise suffering like death)
conditional_results.source: Manasagari, Yogini-dasha section (Subodhini Hindi comm. Madhukanta Jha, Chowkhamba 1963, pp. 470-474), Sankata-visheshata v.9; Dr. S.C. Kursija, A Practical Guide to Prediction through Dasha System (AIFAS), 'Prediction of Yogini Dasha'

effects: the whole yogini period gives happiness
conditional_results.source: Manasagari, Yogini-dasha-svamin verses (Subodhini ed. M. Jha, 1963, pp. 486-487), v.2

effects: the whole yogini period becomes middling (madhyama)
conditional_results.source: Manasagari, Yogini-dasha-svamin verses (Subodhini ed. M. Jha, 1963, pp. 486-487), v.2

conditional_results.when: manual: if the yogini's planet is 6th from the lord of the year (varshesha)
conditional_results.source: Manasagari, Yogini-dasha-svamin verses (Subodhini ed. M. Jha, 1963, pp. 486-487), v.2

remedies.remedy: adopt the remedies prescribed for the planet concerned (Rahu) to ward off the evil of an adverse yogini period
remedies.source: Dr. S.C. Kursija, A Practical Guide to Prediction through Dasha System (AIFAS), 'Prediction of Yogini Dasha'

yogini/sankata.phases: Mansagari (variant, vv.3-4): Ketu is assigned to the end of Sankata; Jhanji: some give the first half to Rahu and the second half to Ketu.

yoga/ruchaka.summary: One of the five Mahapurusha (great-person) yogas: Mars in its own sign (Aries, Scorpio) or exaltation (Capricorn) in a kendra (1, 4, 7, 10). It marks a forceful, martial, leadership-driven person, but only when Mars is genuinely strong.
common_outcomes: bold, enterprising and energetic temperament
success through daring effort and over rivals
leadership or command roles (army, police, management, sport)
strong physique and drive
rare_outcomes: ruler-like authority or high command when Mars is very strong and well supported
aggressive or domineering use of power when Mars is heavily afflicted (Raman's example of a destructive ruler)
knowledge of mantras and occult arts (BPHS, Saravali)

by_area.personality: Enthusiastic, brave, decisive and combative; can be harsh or arrogant (BPHS 75.3-7; Phaladeepika 6.2; Saravali 37.5-7).
by_area.career: Leadership, army or command posts, work that rewards daring; Raman: a great commander or leader of men (Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 22).
by_area.finance: Wealth gained through daring deeds (Phaladeepika 6.2); wealthy (Raman no. 22; Jataka Parijata 7.60).
by_area.health: Strong body and vitality (Raman no. 22; Jataka Parijata 7.60).
by_area.spirituality: Devoted to Brahmins and gods, versed in mantras and occult lore (BPHS 75.3-7; Saravali 37.5-7; Jataka Parijata 7.60).

strengtheners: Mars exalted rather than merely in own sign (Raman, by analogy with Hamsa)
placement in the 10th, the strongest kendra (Raman no. 19 remarks; Frawley)
yoga present from both the lagna and the Moon (Frawley; Phaladeepika 6.4 counts it from the Moon too)
Mars with friendly planets such as the Sun (Frawley)
Mars strong in shadbala and free of malefic aspect (Raman no. 22)
strong Sun and Moon (Saravali 38.22)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mars weak by debilitation in navamsa, association or aspect: the yoga then exists only in name (Raman no. 22)
weak Sun and Moon deny kingship; only children and wealth in the Mars period (Saravali 38.22)
heavy malefic influence on a strong Mars gives a destructive edge (Raman no. 22 example)
yoga/ruchaka.lagna_or_context_notes: Possible only for movable and fixed lagnas: Mars must be in Aries, Scorpio or Capricorn in a kendra, so Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn (Aries/Capricorn in kendras) and Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius (Scorpio in kendras) lagnas qualify (follows from the definition in BPHS 75.1-2). Results take on the house occupied; Raman stresses the 10th. Mars's lordship from the lagna (yogakaraka for Cancer and Leo, 8th lord for Aries, etc.) colours the results (Raman's lordship-unit method, Three Hundred Important Combinations, introduction).

source_views.source: BPHS 75.1-7 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
source_views.view: Mars strong in own or exaltation sign in a kendra from the lagna forms Ruchaka. The native has a long face, great enthusiasm and strength, loves battle, defeats enemies, is skilled in mantras, cruel-tempered, a leader of thieves, and rules a region. [maraka: text predicts death after age 70 by fire or weapons]

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.1-2, 6.4 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed. 1950)
source_views.view: Mars in a kendra in own or exaltation sign. Long face, wealth through daring deeds, brave, overcomes enemies, powerful, arrogant, army leader, victorious. The five yogas can also be counted from the Moon; one, two, three, four or five of them make one fortunate, king's equal, king, emperor or greater still.

source_views.source: Saravali 37.2, 37.5-7, 38.22 (Eng. tr., archive.org)
source_views.view: Same formation. Long face, great strength and valour, fond of war, mantra knowledge, conqueror of enemies, cruel; rules Vindhya and Sahya. [maraka: text predicts death at about 70 through weapons or fire] Even with Mars strong, weak luminaries deny kingship.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.59-60 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Mars with the greatest strength in a kendra in moolatrikona, own or exaltation sign. Physical strength, fortune, fame, learning in sciences and mantras, a king or king's equal, liberal, victorious, wealthy, lives 70 years in comfort commanding an army.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 22
source_views.view: Mars exalted or in own sign in a kendra. Strong, famous, versed in lore, king or equal, charitable, wealthy, long-lived, army leader. The Mahapurusha yogas exist in a real sense only when the planet is strong; a really powerful one is rare. A planet weakened by debilitation, association or aspect gives the yoga only de jure. Makes one martial, a commander, an aggressive but patriotic ruler.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.4.1
source_views.view: Mars in Aries, Scorpio or Capricorn in the 1st, 4th, 7th or 10th from the lagna; not applied from the Moon, mainly in the rasi chart. A great man of fiery nature: enthusiastic, a natural leader, victorious, versed in occult sciences, always successful.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, pp. 179-180
source_views.view: The 'radiant combination': courage, daring, will, independence, leadership; common in military leaders, politicians, lawyers, scientists, executives. Tamasic Mars traits (domination, violence) may surface; strong malefic Mahapurusha yogas can create tyrants.

yoga/ruchaka.disagreements: Reference point: BPHS 75.1-2 and Saravali 37.2 count the kendra from the lagna; Phaladeepika 6.4 and Frawley also allow it from the Moon; P.V.R. Narasimha Rao says it does not apply from the Moon. Dignity: BPHS, Phaladeepika, Saravali and Raman accept own or exaltation sign; Jataka Parijata 7.59 adds moolatrikona and requires the greatest strength. Tone: classical results mix kingship with cruelty; Raman and Frawley warn the martial nature can turn destructive under affliction.
yoga/ruchaka.phrasing_guidance: Present as a sign of drive, courage and leadership potential whose scale depends on Mars's actual strength. Avoid promises of rulership, never repeat the classical death-age or manner-of-death statements, and frame the 'aggressive' side as a tendency to channel well.

definitions.definition: Mars, strong, in its own sign or exaltation sign and in a kendra (1, 4, 7, 10) from the lagna.
Mars in a kendra that is its own sign or exaltation sign; the yoga is also recognised when the kendra is counted from the Moon.
Mars in own house or exaltation sign identical with a kendra.
Mars possessing the greatest strength, in a kendra, in its moolatrikona, own or exaltation sign.

definitions.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 22
definitions.definition: Mars exalted in a kendra or in a kendra that is its own sign; to count in practice Mars must be strong.
Mars in Aries, Scorpio or Capricorn in the 1st, 4th, 7th or 10th from the lagna; not from the Moon; mainly in the rasi chart.

cancellations.condition: Mars weak by debilitation (e.g. in navamsa), malefic association or aspect: the yoga exists only nominally (de jure) and does not operate in its real sense.
cancellations.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 22

cancellations.condition: Sun and Moon weak: no kingship, though the Mars period still gives children and wealth.

yoga/ruchaka.rarity_and_weight: Raman: an unblemished Mahapurusha yoga occurs only exceptionally; in most charts these yogas have little practical (political) value and a really powerful one is rare (nos. 20, 22). Frawley: Mahapurusha yogas are not uncommon and many charts have at least one, but they must be well placed to work. Classical texts rank it among the great-person (raja-type) yogas (BPHS 75; Phaladeepika 6.4).
yoga/ruchaka.timing: Mainly in the dasa of Mars (Saravali 38.22 speaks of the period of the concerned planet). Raman's general rule: the stronger yoga-forming planet fulfils the larger part of the yoga in its dasa, and sub-periods of that planet in other dasas give a share (Three Hundred Important Combinations, introduction). Jataka Parijata 7.66 (with notes): the powerful planet causing a yoga gives its results in its own dasa.

conditional_results.when: manual: Mars strong, unafflicted, ideally in the 10th
manual: Mars heavily joined or aspected by malefics while strong

yoga/bhadra.summary: Mahapurusha yoga of Mercury: Mercury in its own or exaltation sign (Gemini, Virgo) in a kendra. It marks intellect, eloquence, learning and commercial or communicative skill, provided Mercury is strong.
common_outcomes: sharp intellect and good speech
learning in many subjects and scriptures
success in writing, teaching, business or advisory work
supportive of relatives and friends
rare_outcomes: rulership or high rank (classical statements)
long life of 80-100 years (classical statements)

by_area.personality: Intelligent, articulate, independent in all undertakings, sattvic, systematic (BPHS 75.8-12; Phaladeepika 6.2; P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.4.2).
by_area.career: Clever speaker in assemblies, leader of men; intellectuals, teachers, writers and businessmen (Phaladeepika 6.2; Frawley p. 179).
by_area.finance: Very rich (Phaladeepika 6.2); friends share in his wealth (BPHS 75.11; Saravali 37.16-18).
by_area.health: Strong, well-built body with a lion-like or tiger-like face and broad chest (BPHS 75.8; Saravali 37.14-15; Raman no. 23).
by_area.relationships: Lives happily with wife and children (BPHS 75.12).
by_area.family: Protector of his family, helps relatives (BPHS 75.11; Raman no. 23; Jataka Parijata 7.62).
by_area.spirituality: Versed in yoga and the shastras (BPHS 75.9-10; Saravali 37.14-18).

strengtheners: Mercury free from malefic influence (Raman no. 23 example)
Mercury very powerful; otherwise the yoga is only de jure (Raman no. 23)
10th-house placement (Raman, Frawley)
present from both lagna and Moon (Frawley)
strong Sun and Moon (Saravali 38.22)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mercury weak: yoga only nominal (Raman no. 23)
weak luminaries deny kingship (Saravali 38.22)
poor aspects can spoil the planet's qualities (Frawley p. 180)
yoga/bhadra.lagna_or_context_notes: Mercury must be in Gemini or Virgo in a kendra, so only dual-sign lagnas (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces) can have it (follows from BPHS 75.1-2). Mercury in Virgo is both exalted and own sign. Mercury's own kendra lordship for these lagnas is a kendradhipatya concern that Raman, for Hamsa, says loses significance when a Mahapurusha yoga forms.

source_views.source: BPHS 75.1-2, 75.8-12 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
source_views.view: Mercury strong in own or exaltation sign in a kendra. Lion-like splendour, broad chest, elephant's gait, long arms, learned in all respects, versed in yoga, sattvic, fond of comforts, independent, protects his family, friends enjoy his wealth, happy with wife and children; rules the middle country and lives a hundred years.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.1-2 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Long life, keen intellect, cleanliness, praised by the learned, a leader, very rich, clever in addressing an assembly.

source_views.source: Saravali 37.14-18
source_views.view: Tiger-like face, elephant's gait, broad chest, learned, conversant with yoga, knows the shastras, righteous, independent, lets friends enjoy his wealth, rules the middle country, always happy; [maraka: text predicts death at 80].

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.59, 7.62
source_views.view: Mercury of greatest strength in a kendra in moolatrikona, own or exaltation sign. Tiger's face, elephant's gait, broad chest, a king devoted to befriending kinsmen, commanding genius, vast fame and wealth, reaches age 80.

source_views.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 23
source_views.view: Strong, lion-like face, well-proportioned, taciturn, helps relatives, lives to old age. Manifests per Mercury's intellectual nature; Mercury must be very powerful or the yoga is de jure. Example: Mercury unafflicted in own sign in the 10th showed intellect, learning, wealth and generosity.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.4.2
source_views.view: Mercury in Gemini or Virgo in a kendra from the lagna, not from the Moon. Great man of earthy nature, learned, deep voice, sattvic, knows yoga, surrounded by family and friends, clean, systematic, independent, religious.

source_views.source: Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, p. 179
source_views.view: The 'auspicious combination': speech, communication, commerce, intellect, wit, balanced psychology; common in intellectuals, teachers, writers and businessmen; can heighten Mercury's restless, acquisitive side.

yoga/bhadra.disagreements: Same reference-point and dignity splits as the other Mahapurusha yogas (lagna only in BPHS/Saravali/P.V.R. Narasimha Rao; Moon also in Phaladeepika/Frawley; moolatrikona added by Jataka Parijata). Raman calls the Bhadra native taciturn, whereas Phaladeepika stresses eloquence in assemblies.
yoga/bhadra.phrasing_guidance: Describe as a gift for thinking, speaking and practical skill whose scale depends on Mercury's strength; avoid rulership or lifespan promises.

definitions.definition: Mercury, strong, in own sign or exaltation sign in a kendra from the lagna.
Mercury in a kendra identical with its own or exaltation sign; also counted from the Moon.
Mercury in own house or exaltation sign identical with a kendra.
Mercury of greatest strength in a kendra in its moolatrikona, own or exaltation sign.
Mercury in a kendra identical with its own or exaltation sign, and very powerful.
Mercury in Gemini or Virgo in the 1st, 4th, 7th or 10th from the lagna; not from the Moon.

cancellations.condition: Mercury not very powerful: the combination is present only de jure.
Weak Sun and Moon: no kingship, only children and wealth in Mercury's period.

yoga/bhadra.rarity_and_weight: Restricted to dual-sign lagnas by definition. Raman: unblemished Mahapurusha yogas are exceptional and usually of limited practical value (no. 20 remarks). Frawley: Mahapurusha yogas are not uncommon, but must be well placed to work.
yoga/bhadra.timing: Mercury's dasa and bhuktis (Saravali 38.22; Raman's introduction on yoga timing; Jataka Parijata 7.66).

conditional_results.when: manual: Mercury strong and free from malefic influence
effects: intellectual eminence, learning, wealth and generosity

yoga/hamsa.summary: Mahapurusha yoga of Jupiter: Jupiter in its own sign (Sagittarius, Pisces) or exaltation (Cancer) in a kendra. It marks a righteous, respected, wise and comfortable person; Raman treats it as the most idealistic of the five.
common_outcomes: good character and moral standing
respect from others and from people in authority
comforts and good food
interest in learning, scripture or teaching
rare_outcomes: kingship or very high rank when Jupiter is exceptionally strong
a person of 'sterling character and immense moral fibre' (Raman)

by_area.personality: Righteous, pure-minded, liked by others, optimistic, ethical (Raman no. 19; Phaladeepika 6.3; Frawley p. 179). Classical texts also call him very passionate (BPHS 75.13-16).
by_area.career: Extolled by the good, a king or respected leader (Phaladeepika 6.3); religious people, teachers, liberal social and business leaders (Frawley p. 179).
by_area.finance: Eats sumptuous food, enjoys comforts (Phaladeepika 6.3; P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.4.5); prosperity and affluence (Frawley).
by_area.health: Handsome body (Phaladeepika 6.3; Raman no. 19); health (Frawley).
by_area.relationships: Blessed with a beautiful wife (Jataka Parijata 7.63).
by_area.spirituality: Spiritual strength and purity (P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.4.5); devoted to virtue and scripture (Jataka Parijata 7.63); Raman: Hamsa makes one idealistic, spiritual and selfless compared with Malavya.

strengtheners: Jupiter exalted (Cancer) rather than in own sign: removes even the trace of kendradhipatya fault (Raman no. 19)
placement in the 10th, the most powerful kendra (Raman no. 19)
Jupiter conjoined with lords of the lagna, 5th and 9th (Raman no. 19 example)
strong lagna and Jupiter (Raman no. 19)
present from both lagna and Moon (Frawley)
strong Sun and Moon (Saravali 38.22)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Jupiter powerfully aspected by malefics such as Saturn and Mars restricts the yoga (Raman no. 19 example)
the Moon forming Papadhi yoga (malefics 6/7/8 from it) dragged down a Hamsa chart (Raman no. 19 example)
weak luminaries deny kingship (Saravali 38.22)
yoga/hamsa.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman: possible for all dual lagnas and for Aries, Libra and Capricorn among movable lagnas (Jupiter in Cancer as a kendra); fixed lagnas cannot have Hamsa. Jupiter owning a kendra is normally a blemish for a benefic, but Raman says that principle loses significance when Hamsa is present.

source_views.source: BPHS 75.1-2, 75.13-16 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
source_views.view: Jupiter strong in own or exaltation sign in a kendra. Swan-like voice, handsome, prominent nose, a king, phlegmatic, sharp intelligence, marks of fish, goad, bow, conch and lotus on hands and feet, very passionate, fond of water sports, enjoys life fully; rules the land between the Ganga and Yamuna; [maraka: text predicts death after age 100].

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.3 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: A king praised by the good, marks of conch, lotus, fish and goad on hands and legs, beautiful body, sumptuous food, righteous disposition.

source_views.source: Saravali 37.11-13
source_views.view: Reddish face, high nose, great virility, fair complexion, swan-like voice, phlegmatic, fond of water sports and of women, rules Surasena, Gandharva and the land between Ganga and Yamuna, lives a hundred years.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.59, 7.63
source_views.view: Red mouth, prominent nose, swan's voice, fair limbs, beautiful wife, handsome, every comfort, studies scripture, acute, meritorious, beneficent, devoted to virtue, life of 82 years.

source_views.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 19
source_views.view: Jupiter in a kendra that is its own or exaltation sign. Handsome body, liked by others, righteous, pure in mind. Strength depends on the lagna, Jupiter and which kendra (10th strongest). Exaltation preferred over own sign. Should be interpreted carefully as it is meant to produce a person of sterling character. Examples show malefic aspects and a Papadhi Moon restricting it.

source_views.source: Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1 (chart illustrations)
source_views.view: Exalted Jupiter in the lagna conferring Hamsa is used in example charts to explain personal example, devotion to duty and high office, judged with the house it relates to.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.4.5
source_views.view: Jupiter in Sagittarius, Pisces or Cancer in a kendra from the lagna, not the Moon. Great man of ethereal nature: spiritual strength and purity, respected by all, passionate, a king, all comforts, a good conversationalist.

source_views.source: Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, p. 179
source_views.view: The 'swan combination': ethical, philosophical or religious nature, optimism, creativity, health, faith and affluence; common among religious people, teachers and liberal leaders; can give spirituality or merely self-promotion.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events (chart illustrations)
source_views.view: Calls Jupiter (with Venus) exalted in a Cancer lagna the most beneficial Hamsa Mahapurusha yoga, and reads such yogas inside the whole chart (arudha lagna, dasa sign) rather than in isolation.

yoga/hamsa.disagreements: Reference point: lagna only (BPHS, Saravali, P.V.R. Narasimha Rao) versus lagna or Moon (Phaladeepika 6.4, Frawley). Jataka Parijata adds moolatrikona. Classical texts call the Hamsa native very passionate or fond of women (BPHS, Saravali), while Raman and P.V.R. Narasimha Rao stress purity and spirituality. Raman prefers exaltation over own sign.
yoga/hamsa.phrasing_guidance: Frame as an indicator of integrity, wisdom and goodwill from others, scaled by Jupiter's strength. Do not promise kingship or quote lifespans.

definitions.definition: Jupiter, strong, in own sign or exaltation sign in a kendra from the lagna.
Jupiter in a kendra identical with its own or exaltation sign; also counted from the Moon.
Jupiter in own house or exaltation sign identical with a kendra.
Jupiter of greatest strength in a kendra in moolatrikona, own or exaltation sign.
Jupiter in a kendra that is his own sign or exaltation sign (lagna counted as a kendra).
Jupiter in Sagittarius, Pisces or Cancer in the 1st, 4th, 7th or 10th from the lagna; not from the Moon.

cancellations.condition: Jupiter subject to strong malefic aspects or associations restricts the yoga's effects.
Planet weak by debilitation, association or aspect: the Mahapurusha yoga is only nominal.
cancellations.source: Raman no. 22 remarks (applies to all five)

cancellations.condition: Weak Sun and Moon: no kingship, only children and wealth in Jupiter's period.

yoga/hamsa.rarity_and_weight: Not possible for fixed lagnas (Raman no. 19). Raman: of his example Mahapurusha charts only two had real strength; the rest were nominal (no. 22 remarks). Frawley: Mahapurusha yogas are not uncommon. Raman ranks Hamsa and Malavya as raja yogas.
yoga/hamsa.timing: Jupiter's dasa (Raman no. 19 example: Jupiter still gives Hamsa results to a good extent in his dasa; Saravali 38.22; Jataka Parijata 7.66).

conditional_results.when: manual: Jupiter exalted in the 10th and unafflicted
effects: yoga in full swing: high status, reputation, ethical leadership

conditional_results.when: manual: Jupiter aspected by malefics, or the Moon forming Papadhi yoga
effects: good personality and goodwill but no great elevation

yoga/malavya.summary: Mahapurusha yoga of Venus: Venus in its own sign (Taurus, Libra) or exaltation (Pisces) in a kendra. It marks comfort, wealth, vehicles, beauty, artistic taste and a happy married and family life.
common_outcomes: material comforts, vehicles and good food
attractive appearance and refined tastes
happiness from spouse and children
talent in arts, music or design
rare_outcomes: great riches and renown (Raman)
rulership of a region (classical statements)

by_area.personality: Resolute, strong-minded, refined, pleasure-loving; Raman: materialistic outlook in proportion to comforts (no. 20; Phaladeepika 6.3).
by_area.career: Artists, people of wealth or social influence, sometimes politicians (Frawley p. 179); famous and learned (Phaladeepika 6.3).
by_area.finance: Wealthy, prosperous, commands good vehicles (Phaladeepika 6.3; Raman no. 20).
by_area.health: Well-developed physique, clean or unperturbed senses (Phaladeepika 6.3; Raman no. 20); excellent health (P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.4.4).
by_area.relationships: Happiness from wife and children (Phaladeepika 6.3; Raman no. 20).
by_area.family: Endowed with wife, children and good fortune (Phaladeepika 6.3).
by_area.spirituality: Raman: spiritual advancement tends to run inversely to the material comforts it gives; Frawley: on a higher level Venus gives devotion.

strengtheners: Venus exalted in the 10th (Raman no. 20 example)
present from both lagna and Moon (Frawley)
Venus strong and well aspected (Raman no. 22 remarks; Frawley)
strong Sun and Moon (Saravali 38.22)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Venus weak by debilitation in navamsa, association or aspect: yoga only nominal (Raman no. 22 remarks)
poor aspects can ruin the planet's significations (Frawley p. 180)
weak luminaries deny kingship (Saravali 38.22)
yoga/malavya.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman gives the house in which Malavya can form by lagna: 1st for Taurus, Libra, Pisces; 7th for Aries, Scorpio, Virgo; 10th for Gemini, Leo, Capricorn; 4th for Sagittarius, Aquarius, Cancer. Results colour the matters of that house.

source_views.source: BPHS 75.1-2, 75.17-19 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
source_views.view: Venus strong in own or exaltation sign in a kendra. Beautiful lips, slender waist, moon-like lustre, fragrant body, medium stature, clean teeth, elephant-like voice, long arms; lives happily for seventy years as ruler of Sindhu and Malwa.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.3 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Strong limbs, resolute, wealthy, with wife, children and good fortune, prosperous, good meals, pleasures, good vehicles, famous and learned, unperturbed senses.

source_views.source: Saravali 37.2-4
source_views.view: Thin lips, even physique, moon-like splendour, majestic voice, pleasant body odour, piercing sight, arms to the knees, lives seventy years, rules Lata, Malwa and Sindhu.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.59, 7.64
source_views.view: Graceful build, handsome, powerful, blessed with children, wife, vehicles and wealth, knows scripture, learned, clever in the three regal powers, liberal, fond of other women, lives to 77.

source_views.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 20
source_views.view: Venus exalted or own sign in a kendra. Well-developed physique, strong-minded, wealthy, happy with wife and children, vehicles, clean senses, renowned and learned. Inclines one to Venusian pleasures; both Hamsa and Malavya are raja yogas, but Malavya is more materialistic and pleasure-loving. Unblemished Mahapurusha yogas are exceptional.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.4.4
source_views.view: Venus in Taurus, Libra or Pisces in a kendra from the lagna, not the Moon. Great man of watery nature: moon-like lustre, tasty food, luxuries, excellent health, well versed in arts.

source_views.source: Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, pp. 179-180
source_views.view: Comfort and prosperity, vehicles and resources, beauty, charm, artistic talent; common in artists and the wealthy; lower or higher Venus effects by placement, devotion at the higher level.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology (chart illustrations)
source_views.view: Uses Venus as 4th lord in the 4th (Malavya) and a Libra dasa sign housing Malavya to time a rajayoga period.

yoga/malavya.disagreements: Same reference-point split (lagna only vs lagna or Moon) and moolatrikona addition (Jataka Parijata) as the other Mahapurusha yogas. Classical texts describe it mainly through looks and rulership; Raman reads it as materialistic comfort as against Hamsa's idealism; Frawley allows devotional expression.
yoga/malavya.phrasing_guidance: Present as comfort, taste, charm and a good domestic life, scaled by Venus's strength; do not imply indulgence or infidelity as fixed traits; omit lifespans.

definitions.definition: Venus, strong, in own sign or exaltation sign in a kendra from the lagna.
Venus in a kendra identical with its own or exaltation sign; also counted from the Moon.
Venus in own house or exaltation sign identical with a kendra.
Venus of greatest strength in a kendra in moolatrikona, own or exaltation sign.
Venus in a kendra which is his own or exaltation sign.
Venus in Taurus, Libra or Pisces in the 1st, 4th, 7th or 10th from the lagna; not from the Moon.

cancellations.condition: Planet weak by debilitation, association or aspect: yoga exists only nominally.
Weak Sun and Moon: no kingship, only children and wealth in Venus's period.

yoga/malavya.rarity_and_weight: Possible for every lagna in some kendra (Raman's table). Raman: unblemished cases exceptional; in most charts of limited political value. Frawley: these yogas are not uncommon.
yoga/malavya.timing: Venus's dasa and bhuktis (Saravali 38.22; Raman introduction; Jataka Parijata 7.66). Rath times it through the dasa of the sign containing the yoga (Narayana/sign dasa usage).

yoga/sasa.summary: Mahapurusha yoga of Saturn: Saturn in its own sign (Capricorn, Aquarius) or exaltation (Libra) in a kendra. It gives authority over people and resources and capacity for sustained work, with classical warnings about ruthlessness that a strong Moon or Jupiter softens.
common_outcomes: positions of authority or management
