many servants or staff under one's command
capacity for hard, sustained work
control of land, property or industry
rare_outcomes: head of a town or kingdom (classical)
great industrial wealth (Raman example with Saturn exalted in the 4th)

by_area.personality: Valorous, shrewd, knows enemies' weak points, restless; classical texts add wickedness and coveting others' wealth (BPHS 75.20-22; Phaladeepika 6.4). Raman: these evils play only a restricted role if the Moon is unafflicted.
by_area.career: Head of a village, town or king; army chief; political and business leaders (Phaladeepika 6.4; Saravali 37.8-10; Frawley p. 180).
by_area.finance: Usurps or covets others' wealth (BPHS 75.21; Phaladeepika 6.4); Raman's example: earnings in lakhs as an industrialist.
by_area.health: Body not small, slender waist (BPHS 75.20).
by_area.relationships: Classical texts: fond of women and intrigues with others' wives (BPHS 75.21; Phaladeepika 6.4; Jataka Parijata 7.65).
by_area.family: Devoted to his mother (Saravali 37.8-10; Jataka Parijata 7.65).
by_area.spirituality: Benefically placed, gives detachment, spiritual insight and capacity for silence (Frawley p. 180).

strengtheners: Moon free from affliction: removes the coveting and unscrupulous side (Raman no. 21)
Jupiter exalted improving the Moon (Raman no. 21 example)
Moon or Jupiter strong (Frawley p. 180)
placement in the 4th (lands, houses) or 10th (Raman no. 21 example)
strong Sun and Moon (Saravali 38.22)
weakeners_or_cancellations: afflicted Moon brings out the unscrupulous, coveting tendencies (Raman no. 21)
weak Saturn: yoga only nominal (Raman no. 22 remarks)
Rath's example: a Sasa yoga became defunct in a chart dominated by the Kala Sarpa axis
yoga/sasa.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman: possible for movable and fixed lagnas; dual-sign lagnas cannot have Sasa. Saturn is yogakaraka for Taurus and Libra lagnas, which helps.

source_views.source: BPHS 75.1-2, 75.20-22 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 2)
source_views.view: Saturn strong in own or exaltation sign in a kendra. Small teeth and face, valorous, slender waist, wise, wanders in forests and mountains, knows enemies' weaknesses, lively, virile, fond of women, usurps others' wealth, rules several regions; [maraka: text predicts death at 70].

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.4 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Extolled by all, good servants, strong, headman of a village or king, wicked disposition, intrigues with others' wives, usurps others' wealth, happy.

source_views.source: Saravali 37.8-10
source_views.view: Small teeth and face, fast pace, crafty, very valorous, fond of forests, hills and forts, famous, army chief, skilful, a metallurgist, fickle, interested in women, enjoys others' wealth, devoted to his mother, intelligent; ruler of some place; [maraka: text predicts death at 70].

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.59, 7.65
source_views.view: A king, minister or general haunting woods and mountains, cruel-hearted, deceptive in pursuit of metallurgy, bountiful, wrathful eyes, brave, devoted to his mother, dark form, voluptuary, lives 70 years.

source_views.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 21
source_views.view: Saturn exalted or own sign in a kendra. Good servants, questionable character, head of a village, town or kingdom, covets others' riches. Results reflect Saturn's nature, but the Moon's state is decisive: an unafflicted Moon restricts the evil results. Example: Saturn exalted in the 4th with a good Moon made a great industrialist.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.4.3
source_views.view: Saturn in Capricorn, Aquarius or Libra in a kendra from the lagna, not the Moon. Great man of airy nature: hare-like, wise, enjoys wandering, valorous, slender, knows others' weaknesses, lively but vacillating, charitable.

source_views.source: Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, p. 180
source_views.view: Power over people, authority, control of material resources, strong work capacity; common in political and business leaders. Unless the Moon or Jupiter is strong, may be selfish or ruthless; well placed, it gives detachment.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology (chart illustrations)
source_views.view: Reads exalted Saturn in the 4th (Sasa) as steel/industry significations, and shows a Sasa yoga rendered ineffective by an overriding Kala Sarpa configuration.

yoga/sasa.disagreements: Same reference-point and moolatrikona splits as the other Mahapurusha yogas. Character: classical texts (BPHS, Phaladeepika, Jataka Parijata) describe moral flaws; P.V.R. Narasimha Rao gives a mostly neutral picture and calls the native charitable; Raman and Frawley make the flaws conditional on an afflicted Moon or weak Jupiter.
yoga/sasa.phrasing_guidance: Describe as organising power, endurance and authority. Do not state classical moral accusations (coveting wealth, adultery) as facts about the person; at most mention that the texts advise checking the Moon for how ethically this power is used.

definitions.definition: Saturn, strong, in own sign or exaltation sign in a kendra from the lagna.
Saturn in a kendra identical with its own or exaltation sign; also counted from the Moon.
Saturn in own house or exaltation sign identical with a kendra.
Saturn of greatest strength in a kendra in moolatrikona, own or exaltation sign.
Saturn in a kendra which is his own or exaltation sign.
Saturn in Capricorn, Aquarius or Libra in the 1st, 4th, 7th or 10th from the lagna; not from the Moon.

cancellations.condition: The Moon free from affliction: the evil results of Sasa (coveting, unscrupulousness) have only a restricted play.
Planet weak by debilitation, association or aspect: yoga only nominal.
Weak Sun and Moon: no kingship, only children and wealth in Saturn's period.

yoga/sasa.rarity_and_weight: Not possible for dual-sign lagnas (Raman no. 21). Raman: really powerful Mahapurusha yogas are rare. Frawley: Mahapurusha yogas are not uncommon; Saturn in an angle is usually viewed with some suspicion.
yoga/sasa.timing: Saturn's dasa and bhuktis (Saravali 38.22; Raman introduction; Jataka Parijata 7.66).

conditional_results.when: manual: the Moon unafflicted (or improved by a strong Jupiter)
effects: power and wealth without unscrupulous means
authority used selfishly; questionable means of gain

yoga/gajakesari.summary: Jupiter in a kendra (1, 4, 7, 10) from the Moon, in its commonest form; BPHS instead asks for Jupiter in a kendra from the lagna or the Moon, joined or aspected by a benefic, and not debilitated, combust or in an enemy sign. It promises reputation, intelligence, wealth and goodwill, but writers warn the bare form is common and weak.
common_outcomes: good name and respect
intelligence and good qualities
help from relatives and people in authority
moderate to good prosperity, depending on strength
rare_outcomes: lasting fame even after death
public office or civic leadership (Raman: municipal member, mayor if powerful)

by_area.personality: Splendorous, intelligent, virtuous (BPHS 36.3-4); polite and generous (Raman no. 1); energetic and meritorious (Jataka Parijata 7.117); lofty speaker, valorous (Phaladeepika 6.16).
by_area.career: Pleases or serves the ruler (BPHS 36.4; Jataka Parijata 7.117); builder of towns or magistrate, read in modern terms as civic or administrative posts (Raman no. 1); municipal commissioner or manager of a big corporation (Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XX).
by_area.finance: Wealthy (BPHS 36.4); much money and grain (Jataka Parijata 7.117). Raman (How to Judge a Horoscope): if Jupiter is linked to the 2nd house it makes one earn well, but the yoga may raise status without money or money without status.
by_area.health: Long-lived (Phaladeepika 6.16).
by_area.family: Many relations (Raman no. 1); respected by relations and friends (Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XX).
by_area.spirituality: Virtuous; P.V.R. Narasimha Rao calls it a key yoga for virtue and lasting fame.

strengtheners: Jupiter conjoined or aspected by a benefic (BPHS 36.3-4)
Jupiter and Moon in exaltation or good dignity (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope ch. V)
the Moon waxing (Kumaraswamiyam version cited by Santhanam)
the forming planets being benefic lords for the lagna (Raman no. 1 unit method)
Jupiter connected to the 2nd house for wealth (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope ch. V)
the yoga persisting in divisional charts such as D-4 (Rath example)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Jupiter debilitated, combust or in an enemy sign (BPHS 36.3-4)
yoga falling in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the lagna cannot advance the chart (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope ch. V)
Moon and Jupiter as lords of evil houses (e.g. 6th and 11th) reduce it (Raman no. 1)
malefic aspects/association and enemy signs give negative strength units; equal plus and minus units practically neutralise it (Raman no. 1, chart 3)
C.G. Rajan's Tamil BPHS: Mercury in the 5th from or aspecting the Moon annuls it (cited, and disputed, by Santhanam)
yoga/gajakesari.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman: results relate to the houses the Moon and Jupiter occupy and rule; e.g. Moon in the 4th and Jupiter in the 10th split the results between those houses. The yoga can show as reputation, career or wealth separately. K.N. Rao reads a retrograde Jupiter as also acting from the previous sign, so the yoga may be counted from there.

source_views.source: BPHS 36.3-4 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1)
source_views.view: Jupiter in a kendra from the lagna or the Moon, joined or aspected by a benefic, and free of debilitation, combustion and enemy sign. The native is splendorous, wealthy, intelligent, virtuous and pleases the king.

source_views.source: R. Santhanam, notes to BPHS 36.3-4
source_views.view: Bare Moon-Jupiter mutual angularity is merely Kesari and cannot yield supreme effects. Lists variants: Jataka Parijata's two kinds; Kumaraswamiyam (waxing Moon with Jupiter in the 4th or 10th from it, possible in only four placements); C.G. Rajan (Mercury not in the 5th from or aspecting the Moon, Moon not combust or debilitated); Bombay edition (Mercury aspecting/joining an undebilitated, uncombust Moon). Ranks Kumaraswamiyam's version strongest. Any version gives wealth and fame in the dasas of Jupiter, the Moon and related planets; one school says Kesari gives riches in Venus dasa.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.14, 6.16 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Calls it Kesari: the Moon in a kendra from Jupiter. Destroys enemies like a lion, speaks nobly in assemblies, passionate, long-lived, famous, very intelligent, conquers by his own valour.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.116-117 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Two forms: Jupiter in a kendra from the Moon; or the Moon aspected by Venus, Jupiter and Mercury that are not debilitated or combust. The native is energetic, rich in money and grain, intelligent, meritorious and pleases the king.

source_views.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 1 and introduction
source_views.view: Jupiter in a kendra from the Moon. Many relations, polite, generous, a builder or magistrate of towns, lasting reputation after death. Results must be adapted to modern life and vary hugely with the strength of the planets, houses and nakshatras; illustrates a plus/minus unit method by lordship, association, aspect and dignity, and shows one chart where the yoga is practically neutralised.

source_views.source: Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. V (Second House)
source_views.view: Moon and Jupiter in mutual kendras; strength depends on their dignity. In the 6th, 8th or 12th from the lagna it cannot advance the chart. It may raise reputation, career or wealth independently; with Jupiter linked to the 2nd, earnings are assured.

source_views.source: Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XX, no. 7
source_views.view: Kesari: Moon and Jupiter in mutual kendras; respected by relations and friends, municipal commissioner or manager of a big corporation, name goes to posterity, worldly enjoyments.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.6 (Other Popular Yogas)
source_views.view: Follows BPHS: Jupiter in a kendra from the Moon, with benefic conjunction/aspect, not debilitated, combust or in an enemy sign. Famous, wealthy, intelligent, of great character, liked by kings; key yoga for virtue and lasting fame. Some count it from the lagna too, and a strong Jupiter may form it without benefic aspect.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology (chart illustrations)
source_views.view: Weighs Gajakesari through its relation to the arudha lagna: joined with the AL lord it gave undying fame, and aspecting the 2nd from AL brought riches, timed by sign dasas. Also notes Moon and Jupiter as 1st and 9th lords forming it on the 4/10 axis.

source_views.source: K.N. Rao, Advanced Techniques of Astrological Prediction (education illustration)
source_views.view: A retrograde Jupiter is read as also acting from the previous sign, producing Gajakesari from that sign.

yoga/gajakesari.disagreements: Reference point: Moon only (Phaladeepika, Jataka Parijata first form, Raman, P.V.R. Narasimha Rao) versus lagna or Moon (BPHS 36.3). Conditions: BPHS adds benefic aspect/conjunction and freedom from debility, combustion and enemy sign; Raman and Phaladeepika do not. Jataka Parijata adds a second, aspect-based form. Name: Phaladeepika and Raman's Hindu Predictive Astrology call the bare form Kesari; Santhanam reserves 'Gajakesari' for the qualified forms. Kumaraswamiyam restricts it to a waxing Moon with Jupiter in the 4th/10th. Santhanam rejects C.G. Rajan's Mercury-in-5th cancellation as baseless. Results: BPHS stresses wealth; Raman says it may give status without money.
yoga/gajakesari.phrasing_guidance: Treat as a helpful sign for reputation, judgement and goodwill whose size depends on the Moon's and Jupiter's condition. Do not present the common bare form as a guarantee of wealth or fame; mention when the stricter BPHS conditions are not met.

definitions.definition: Jupiter in a kendra from the lagna or from the Moon, conjoined with or aspected by a benefic, and not debilitated, combust or in an enemy's sign.
The Moon in a kendra from Jupiter (equivalently Jupiter in a kendra from the Moon).
(1) Jupiter in a kendra from the Moon; or (2) the Moon aspected by Venus, Jupiter and Mercury that are neither debilitated nor combust.
Waxing Moon with Jupiter in the 4th or 10th from it, which only happens with Moon/Jupiter in Taurus/Aquarius or Sagittarius/Pisces.

definitions.source: C.G. Rajan, Tamil BPHS (via Santhanam's notes)
definitions.definition: Moon and Jupiter in mutual kendras, Mercury not in the 5th from or aspecting the Moon, the Moon not combust or debilitated.

definitions.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 1
definitions.definition: Jupiter in a kendra from the Moon.
Jupiter in a kendra from the Moon, conjoined or aspected by a benefic, not debilitated, combust or in an enemy sign; some also allow a kendra from the lagna.

cancellations.condition: Jupiter debilitated, combust or in an enemy's sign (the yoga does not form as BPHS defines it).
Yoga occurring in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the lagna cannot advance the chart.
cancellations.source: Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope ch. V

cancellations.condition: Moon and Jupiter as malefic lords, malefically aspected or in enemy signs: strength units cancel and the yoga is practically neutralised.
cancellations.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 1 (charts 1, 3)

cancellations.condition: Mercury in the 5th from or aspecting the Moon annuls it (C.G. Rajan's version; Santhanam disputes this).

yoga/gajakesari.rarity_and_weight: Santhanam: the bare Moon-Jupiter angularity deserves little importance and cannot give supreme effects; stricter versions rank higher. Raman: results vary greatly with strength and must be scaled down to modern life; it can be practically neutralised. P.V.R. Narasimha Rao calls it a key yoga for virtue and fame. Sources do not give a frequency figure.
yoga/gajakesari.timing: Dasas of Jupiter, the Moon and planets related to them; one school adds Venus dasa (Santhanam, notes to BPHS 36.3-4). Raman: the stronger of the Moon and Jupiter fulfils the larger part in its dasa; bhuktis of either in other dasas give a share (Three Hundred Important Combinations, introduction, chart 1). Rath times it through sign dasas aspecting or containing the yoga.

conditional_results.when: manual: Jupiter conjoined or aspected by a benefic and not debilitated, combust or in an enemy sign
effects: wealth, intelligence, virtue, favour of authorities

conditional_results.when: manual: the yoga falls in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the lagna
effects: yoga cannot advance the chart's indications
conditional_results.source: Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope ch. V

conditional_results.when: manual: Jupiter connected with the 2nd house
conditional_results.source: Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope ch. V

yoga/budhaditya.summary: Mercury conjoined with the Sun (Budha-Aditya, also called Nipuna yoga): intelligence, skill in work, reputation and comfort. Because Mercury is never far from the Sun it is very common, and modern writers require Mercury not to be combust for it to count.
common_outcomes: clever, capable and intelligent
good reputation and respect
work in service of government or authority (Saravali)
rare_outcomes: Kubera-like wealth and kingly status when in the 4th (Saravali 31.11)
danger, imprisonment and miserliness when in the 7th (Saravali 31.12)

by_area.personality: Clever, intelligent, famous and happy (Brihat Jataka 14.1; Phaladeepika 18.1); highly intelligent and skilful (Raman no. 24).
by_area.career: In service, dear to the king and good people (Saravali 15.4); skilful in all work (Raman no. 24; P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.2.4); strongest in the D-10 for career (P.V.R. Narasimha Rao).
by_area.finance: Unsteady wealth (Saravali 15.4); Sastri's note on Brihat Jataka 14.1: proficient and famous but not good for finance.
by_area.relationships: In the 7th: bereft of marital pleasures (Saravali 31.12).

strengtheners: Mercury not combust, i.e. more than about 10 degrees from the Sun (Raman no. 24; P.V.R. Narasimha Rao)
the yoga repeated in divisional charts such as D-10 or D-9 (P.V.R. Narasimha Rao)
placement in the 4th or lagna (Saravali 31.10-11)
Mercury vargottama or with good lordship (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope chart illustrations)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mercury combust (within about 10 degrees of the Sun) loses power to do good (Raman no. 24; P.V.R. Narasimha Rao)
conjunction in the 7th gives adverse results (Saravali 31.12)
yoga/budhaditya.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman's chart illustrations read Budha-Aditya through the houses Mercury rules (e.g. as 5th/8th lord, or the lagna lord Mercury with the Sun in the 7th). Saravali ch. 31 gives different results by kendra.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Sun with Mercury: clever, intelligent, famous and happy. Translator's note: proficient and famous but not good for finance; Varahamihira holds conjunctions generally poor for finance.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.1 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Repeats Brihat Jataka: Sun with Mercury makes one clever, intelligent, famous and happy.

Sun and Mercury in one house: in service, unsteady wealth, sweet speech, fame and money, noble, dear to king and good people, strength, beauty and learning. In the lagna: learned, talkative, adventurous, wise, long-lived; in the 4th: king's equal, famous, truthful, very rich; in the 7th: [maraka: text predicts death by murder or imprisonment], untruthful, miserly.

source_views.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 24
source_views.view: Mercury combining with the Sun. Highly intelligent, skilful, good reputation, respect, comforts. Planets with the Sun usually become combust; Mercury may be an exception, but the yoga should not be assumed regardless of distance: Mercury should not be within 10 degrees of the Sun. Not rare.

source_views.source: Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1 (glossary and chart illustrations)
source_views.view: Glossary: a combination for intelligence and learning. Chart readings tie it to integrity, learning and intellectual life, especially when Mercury is vargottama.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.2, 11.2.4
source_views.view: Sun and Mercury in one sign (Nipuna yoga): intelligent, skilful, well-known, respected, happy. Solar yogas are very common in the rasi chart because Mercury and Venus stay near the Sun; less common in divisional charts, so apply them in D-9 and D-10. Combust Mercury loses some power; in the rasi it gives results if Mercury is not combust. Periods of the Sun, Mercury and the sign holding them give the results.

yoga/budhaditya.disagreements: The classical texts read here (Brihat Jataka, Phaladeepika, Saravali) give Sun-Mercury conjunction results but do not use the name Budhaditya or a combustion rule; Raman and P.V.R. Narasimha Rao add the non-combustion requirement (Raman: more than 10 degrees apart). Finance: Saravali says unsteady wealth and Sastri says poor for finance, while Saravali 31.11 gives great wealth in the 4th. Raman suggests Mercury may be an exception to the combustion rule yet still requires the 10-degree separation.
yoga/budhaditya.phrasing_guidance: Present lightly, as a sign of intelligence and practical skill; note it is common. Give it extra weight only when Mercury is clear of combustion or the yoga repeats in D-9/D-10. Do not repeat the 7th-house danger statements.

definitions.definition: Sun and Mercury in the same sign (two-planet conjunction; not named Budhaditya).

definitions.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 24
definitions.definition: Mercury combined with the Sun, with Mercury not within 10 degrees of the Sun.
Sun and Mercury together in one sign (Nipuna yoga); gives results in the rasi if Mercury is not combust; most powerful in divisional charts like D-10.

cancellations.condition: Mercury within about 10 degrees of the Sun (combust): the yoga should not be taken as present.
Mercury combust: the yoga loses some power to do good.

yoga/budhaditya.rarity_and_weight: Very common in the rasi chart because Mercury never strays far from the Sun (P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.2); 'not, of course, rare' (Raman no. 24). Raman treats the solar yogas as indicating ego development, not comparable in eminence to raja yogas (no. 18 remarks on the solar yogas).
yoga/budhaditya.timing: Periods of the Sun, Mercury and the sign holding the conjunction; results also felt throughout life (P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.2.4).

conditional_results.when: manual: Sun and Mercury together with Mercury not combust
effects: intelligence, skill and reputation come forward in Mercury's period

conditional_results.when: manual: Sun and Mercury together in the 4th
manual: Sun and Mercury together in the 7th
effects: [maraka: text predicts death by murder or imprisonment]

yoga/chandra_mangala.summary: The Moon conjoined with Mars (Raman also accepts mutual aspect). Varahamihira gives harsh results (rough trades, disobedience to the mother), but Raman finds it a strong wealth yoga, especially with dignified Moon and Mars or in the 2nd, 9th, 10th or 11th.
common_outcomes: financial drive and earning capacity
worldly, enterprising and brave
tension with the mother or women (classical)
rare_outcomes: earnings by questionable means when the planets are badly placed
blood disorders (Saravali 15.8)
military wealth and bravery when in the 10th (Saravali 31.29)

by_area.personality: Valorous, brave in war (Saravali 15.8); worldly wise and materially successful (P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.3.5).
by_area.career: Dealer in hammers, ploughs, rough tools, drinks and earthen jars (Brihat Jataka 14.2; Phaladeepika 18.2); artisan, metallurgist, worker in mud and skin (Saravali 15.8); Raman: trades catering to baser needs unless the planets are well placed.
by_area.finance: Raman: a powerful factor in stabilising one's finances; bright financial results except when both are debilitated without cancellation (Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 6; How to Judge a Horoscope ch. V). Classical: earnings by unscrupulous means (Raman's summary of the ancients).
by_area.health: Blood disorders or bloody diseases (Saravali 15.8); in the lagna, defects of blood, digestion and bile (Saravali 31.26).
by_area.relationships: In the 7th: base, after others' money, untruthful, jealous (Saravali 31.28). Classical: trades in women (Brihat Jataka 14.2).
by_area.family: Disobedient to or harsh with the mother and relatives (Brihat Jataka 14.2; Raman no. 6). In the 4th: grief, loss of relatives (Saravali 31.27).

strengtheners: Moon exalted in Taurus with Mars in own Scorpio, or Moon in own Cancer with Mars exalted in Capricorn (Raman no. 6; How to Judge a Horoscope ch. V)
occurring in the 2nd, 9th, 10th or 11th house (Raman)
waxing Moon and Mars in own sign (Raman, chart 10 / How to Judge a Horoscope chart 47)
Mars as yogakaraka for the lagna (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope chart 46)
in the 10th: wealth and bravery (Saravali 31.29)
weakeners_or_cancellations: both planets debilitated without neecha-bhanga (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope ch. V)
falling in unfavourable houses spoils character and gives money by unholy means (Raman no. 6)
in the 4th or 7th: adverse results (Saravali 31.27-28)
yoga/chandra_mangala.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman: results follow the houses the Moon and Mars rule; for Libra lagna in Cancer it gives 2nd/11th-house results; for Cancer and Leo lagnas it is highly beneficial in Scorpio or Taurus. Mars is yogakaraka for Cancer and Leo lagnas.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.2 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Moon with Mars: a dealer in hammers, ploughs and rough tools, women, drinks and earthen jars; disobedient to his mother. Translator's note: here Varahamihira differs from Parasara, who is said to hold Sasimangala yoga good (Parasara's verse not located in this research).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.2 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Repeats Brihat Jataka 14.2.

Moon and Mars together: valorous, brave in war, a boxer, blood disorders, maker of articles of mud, skin and minerals, artisan, metallurgist. In the lagna: blood/bile defects, wealthy, harsh; 4th: grief, no wealth or happiness, defective limb; 7th: base, covets money, untruthful, jealous; 10th: wealth of an army, brave.

source_views.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 6
source_views.view: Mars conjoining the Moon. Ancient results are harsh (unscrupulous earnings, harshness to mother), but in Raman's view it powerfully stabilises finances; earnings come through baser trades unless the planets are well disposed. Also formed by mutual aspect (Taurus-Scorpio, Cancer-Capricorn are excellent). Good in the 2nd, 9th, 10th or 11th; in unfavourable houses it spoils character.

source_views.source: Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. V (Second House)
source_views.view: Has a great bearing on financial status. Dignified Moon and Mars give earnings through above-board means, provided it occurs in the 2nd, 9th, 10th or 11th. Needs conjunction or mutual aspect; mutual kendra gives something like it. Except when both are debilitated without cancellation, it generally gives bright financial results; nature follows the houses ruled. Glossary calls it the angular disposition of the Moon and Mars.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.3.5
source_views.view: Moon and Mars in one sign: worldly wise, materially successful, may earn by unscrupulous means, may treat mother or other women badly.

yoga/chandra_mangala.disagreements: Formation: conjunction only (Brihat Jataka, Saravali, P.V.R. Narasimha Rao) versus conjunction or mutual aspect (Raman), with mutual kendra as a lesser form (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope). Raman's own glossary calls it an 'angular disposition'. Results: Varahamihira and Phaladeepika give mostly negative results; Raman calls it a strong wealth yoga; Sastri reports that Parasara regards it as good, which was not confirmed in the BPHS text read.
yoga/chandra_mangala.phrasing_guidance: Frame as drive and earning ability, with emotional intensity that needs balance. Avoid the classical trade lists and statements about mistreating the mother or women; check dignity and house before calling it favourable.

definitions.definition: The Moon in the same sign as Mars (two-planet conjunction).

definitions.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 6
definitions.definition: Mars conjoining the Moon; Raman also accepts mutual aspect (7th from each other).

definitions.source: Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope ch. V
definitions.definition: Moon and Mars in conjunction or mutual aspect; mutual kendra gives something like the yoga.
Moon and Mars together in one sign.

cancellations.condition: Moon and Mars debilitated without neecha-bhanga: the bright financial results do not come.
cancellations.source: Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope ch. V

cancellations.condition: Occurring in unfavourable houses: character suffers and money comes by unholy means.

yoga/chandra_mangala.rarity_and_weight: Raman gives it significant weight for wealth (How to Judge a Horoscope ch. V); Varahamihira gives it little and mostly adverse significance (per Raman). No frequency figure in the sources.
yoga/chandra_mangala.timing: Raman's chart 47 / no. 6 example: the dasa of the better-placed planet (Mars there) was much better than the Moon's; general Raman rule that the stronger yoga planet gives most results in its dasa.

conditional_results.when: manual: Moon and Mars dignified (Taurus/Scorpio or Cancer/Capricorn) and the yoga in the 2nd, 9th, 10th or 11th
effects: earnings through fair means, financial stability
conditional_results.source: Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope ch. V; Raman no. 6

conditional_results.when: manual: both Moon and Mars debilitated without neecha-bhanga, or yoga in unfavourable houses
conditional_results.source: Raman no. 6; How to Judge a Horoscope ch. V

yoga/adhi.summary: Natural benefics (Mercury, Jupiter, Venus) in the 6th, 7th and 8th from the Moon (Chandradhi; some texts also count from the lagna). It promises leadership, wealth, health, long life and victory over enemies, scaled by how many benefics and how strong they are: army chief, minister or ruler.
common_outcomes: leadership or high office
prosperity and comfort
health and long life
overcoming opponents
rare_outcomes: rule or ministerial rank when all three benefics are strong
scholarly or saintly eminence (Uttara Kalamrita examples)

by_area.personality: Polite, trustworthy (Raman no. 7); high-souled, famous (Phaladeepika 6.42).
by_area.career: Commander, minister or ruler by the strength of the benefics (BPHS 37.5; Brihat Jataka 13.2; Phaladeepika 6.42); Raman: one strong benefic makes a leader, two a minister, three a more eminent position; almost a raja yoga.
by_area.finance: Wealthy throughout life, feeds many relatives (Phaladeepika 6.43); luxuries and affluence (Raman no. 7).
by_area.health: Exempt from diseases and dangers, long-lived (Brihat Jataka 13.2; Saravali 35.20-21; Raman no. 7).
by_area.relationships: Wife, children and friends (Uttara Kalamrita).
by_area.family: Feeds many relations (Phaladeepika 6.43).
by_area.spirituality: Learned (Uttara Kalamrita; Santhanam's notes).

strengtheners: benefics free of combustion and debilitation (Santhanam's notes to BPHS 36.37)
no malefic in or aspecting those houses (Saravali 35.20; Uttara Kalamrita)
the Sun not in those houses (Saravali 35.20)
the 4th from the reference point vacant (Santhanam's notes, citing several BPHS editions)
best arrangement: Mercury 6th, Jupiter 7th, Venus 8th (Santhanam's notes)
Jupiter in the 7th rather than the 6th or 8th from the Moon (Uttara Kalamrita notes)
number and strength of benefics (Raman no. 7; BPHS 37.5)
weakeners_or_cancellations: benefics devoid of strength: yoga present but feeble (Raman no. 7)
the Sun opposite the Moon lowers it a little (Sastri's notes to Brihat Jataka 13.2)
malefics in the 6/7/8 from the Moon form Papadhi, a negative version (Raman no. 7, citing Bhattotpala; Raman no. 19 example)
Jupiter in the 6th or 8th from the Moon creates Shakata-type trouble (Uttara Kalamrita notes; Phaladeepika 6.14 defines Shakata)
yoga/adhi.lagna_or_context_notes: Lagnadhi is the lagna-based variant: BPHS 36.37 uses only the 7th and 8th from the lagna (some editions add that the 4th be vacant); Saravali 34.13 and Jataka Parijata 7.114 use the 6th, 7th and 8th from the lagna without malefic contact. Phaladeepika 6.42 counts from the Moon or the lagna.

source_views.source: BPHS 37.5 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1)
source_views.view: Benefics in the 6th, 7th and 8th from the Moon form Adhi yoga; by their strength the native becomes a king, a minister or an army chief.

source_views.source: BPHS 36.37 with Santhanam's notes
source_views.view: Lagnadhi: benefics in the 7th and 8th from the lagna, free of malefic conjunction/aspect, make one great, learned and happy. Santhanam's synthesis: benefics in any of the 6th/7th/8th, no malefics there or aspecting, the 4th vacant, benefics not combust or debilitated; best with Mercury 6th, Jupiter 7th, Venus 8th.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 13.2 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri) with notes
source_views.view: Benefics in the 6th, 7th and 8th from the Moon: commander, minister or ruler; prosperity, victory over foes, long life free of disease and danger. Notes: lowered a little if the Sun opposes the Moon; two benefics give the middle results, one the lesser; Bhattotpala, citing Srutakirti, recognises seven sorts (benefics in one, two or all three houses); Badarayana and Parasara grade it by benefic strength; Kalyanavarma calls it a raja yoga when the benefics are not eclipsed or malefic-aspected.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.42-43 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Benefics in the 7th, 6th and 8th from the Moon or the lagna: a commander, minister or ruler; famous, prosperous, wealthy, long-lived, high-souled; lord of men, lifelong wealth, feeds relatives, overthrows enemies.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.113-115 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: 7.113 repeats Brihat Jataka 13.2 for the Moon (with the same notes). 7.114-115 Lagnadhi: benefics in the 6th, 7th and 8th from the lagna, unaspected and unjoined by malefics (other than in the 4th); scholar, army chief, generous, famous.

Chandradhi: all benefics in the 6th, 7th and 8th from the Moon, excluding the Sun and without malefic aspect; a king with vast realm, free of old age and disease, fearless, fortunate. Lagnadhi (34.13): exclusively benefics in the 6th-8th from the lagna give ministership, army leadership, kingship, long life. 13.33 classes Adhi among raja yogas.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita, Kanda IV, Adhi Yoga verse (tr. P.S. Sastri), with notes
source_views.view: Benefics in the 6th, 7th and 8th from the Moon with no malefics there: king or equal, great happiness, long life, victory, fame, learning, family and conveyances. Notes: one, two or three strong benefics give leader, minister, eminent position; Jupiter in the 6th or 8th from the Moon is undesirable, so Jupiter should be in the 7th. (Verse number not legible in the scan.)

source_views.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 7
source_views.view: Benefics in the 6th, 7th and 8th from the Moon: polite, trustworthy, happy, luxurious, defeats enemies, healthy, long-lived. Varahamihira specifies only benefics; Bhattotpala suggests a Papadhi (malefic) version. Benefics may be spread over one, two or three of these houses; one strong one makes a leader, two a minister, three more eminent; weak benefics make it feeble. Almost equivalent to a raja yoga.

source_views.source: Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XX, no. 8
source_views.view: Benefics in the 6th, 7th and 8th from the Moon: commander, minister or king, foeless, long-lived, free from disease.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.3.6
source_views.view: Natural benefics in the 6th, 7th and 8th from the Moon: king, minister or army chief by the strength of the planets involved.

source_views.source: K.N. Rao, Advanced Techniques of Astrological Prediction (education illustration)
source_views.view: Reads a retrograde Jupiter as also acting from the previous sign, giving Adhi yoga from there.

yoga/adhi.disagreements: Reference point: Moon (BPHS 37.5, Brihat Jataka, Saravali 35, Raman, P.V.R. Narasimha Rao) versus Moon or lagna (Phaladeepika 6.42); separate Lagnadhi rules differ (BPHS: 7th and 8th only; Saravali and Jataka Parijata: 6th-8th). Occupancy: some require all three houses filled, but Bhattotpala/Srutakirti and Raman accept benefics in any one or more. Extra conditions vary: Sun excluded (Saravali), 4th vacant (some BPHS editions), no malefic aspect (Saravali, Uttara Kalamrita). Raman reports Varahamihira allows only benefics, while Bhattotpala admits a Papadhi version. Uttara Kalamrita's notes and Santhanam both place Jupiter best in the 7th from the Moon.
yoga/adhi.phrasing_guidance: Present as support for standing, comfort and resilience, scaled by how many benefics are involved and how strong they are. Avoid promising ministerial or royal rank; give health and longevity statements only as general well-being.

definitions.definition: Benefics occupying the 6th, 7th and 8th counted from the Moon.
Benefics in the 7th and 8th from the lagna without malefic conjunction or aspect.
Benefics (Mercury, Jupiter, Venus) in the 6th, 7th and 8th from the Moon; per Bhattotpala they may occupy one, two or all three of these houses.
Benefics in the 7th, 6th and 8th from the Moon or from the lagna.
All benefics in the 6th, 7th and 8th from the Moon, those houses excluding the Sun and not aspected by malefics.
Benefics in the 6th, 7th and 8th from the Moon with no malefics in those houses.
Benefics in the 6th, 7th and 8th from the Moon, in one, two or all three of those houses.

cancellations.condition: Benefics devoid of strength: yoga present but feeble.
Sun in opposition to the Moon: effect lowered a little.
Malefic in or aspecting the 6th/7th/8th, or the Sun there: yoga not formed in Saravali's version.
Benefics combust or debilitated, or the 4th occupied: Santhanam's stricter synthesis is not met.

yoga/adhi.rarity_and_weight: Raman: one of the most important combinations, almost a raja yoga (no. 7); Saravali 13.33 and Kalyanavarma (per Sastri) class it as a raja yoga. The partial form with one benefic is far more common than the full form, and the texts grade results by count (Brihat Jataka notes; Raman).
yoga/adhi.timing: Jataka Parijata 7.66: in yogas like Adhi, the powerful yoga planet aspected by weaker ones gives the results in its dasa. Raman's examples: the dasa of the strongest participating benefic (Jupiter's or Venus's) was the peak period.

conditional_results.when: manual: all three benefics strong in the 6th/7th/8th from the Moon, free from malefic contact
effects: ruler-like or very eminent position, wealth, health, long life

conditional_results.when: manual: only one or two benefics, or benefics weak
effects: leadership or ministerial-level standing at a smaller scale; feeble if weak

conditional_results.when: manual: malefics occupy the 6th/7th/8th from the Moon (Papadhi)

yoga/amala.summary: A natural benefic in the 10th house from the lagna or from the Moon (BPHS and Santhanam: only benefics, no malefic there). 'Amala' means spotless: it gives lasting fame, clean character and honour, with wealth according to Phaladeepika.
common_outcomes: good, lasting reputation
honoured by employers or authorities
charitable and helpful to others
prosperity gained by fair means
rare_outcomes: fame lasting 'as long as the Moon and stars endure' (BPHS, Jataka Parijata)
ruling over the earth (Phaladeepika 6.20)

by_area.personality: Virtuous, pious, kind, gentle, affable in speech (Phaladeepika 6.12); spotless character (Raman no. 13).
by_area.career: Honoured by the king or authorities (BPHS 36.5-6; Jataka Parijata 7.120); P.V.R. Narasimha Rao: benefics in the 10th make one's conduct in society very pure.
by_area.finance: Wealthy (Phaladeepika 6.12, 6.20); prosperity unfailing to life's end (Jataka Parijata 7.118). Santhanam: the sage (BPHS) does not promise wealth.
by_area.family: Fond of relatives (BPHS 36.5-6); kind to relatives (Jataka Parijata 7.120); has sons (Phaladeepika 6.20).
by_area.spirituality: Pious, virtuous, charitable (BPHS 36.5-6; Phaladeepika 6.12).

strengtheners: the benefic unaccompanied and unaspected by malefics (Santhanam's notes and example)
strength of the occupying benefic and its aspects and associations (Raman no. 13)
the yoga present from both lagna and Moon (Raman's example chart 17)
weakeners_or_cancellations: a malefic also in the 10th voids the yoga's efficacy (Santhanam's notes to BPHS 36.5-6)
no benefic in the 10th: no Amala (Raman no. 13)
yoga/amala.lagna_or_context_notes: Santhanam: house positions for this yoga should be reckoned by the bhava chart, while the dignity of the planet depends on its sign. Raman: a malefic in the 10th also gives wealth in its dasa, but not fame or character, and the means may be questionable.

source_views.source: BPHS 36.5-6 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1) with notes
source_views.view: Exclusively a benefic in the 10th from the lagna or the Moon: fame lasting as long as the Moon and stars, honoured by the king, abundant pleasures, charitable, fond of relatives, helpful, pious and virtuous. Notes: a malefic joining the 10th makes the yoga void; the sage does not promise wealth; reckon by bhava chart.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.12, 6.19-20 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Benefics in the 10th from the lagna or the Moon. Virtuous, pious, kind, fortunate, amiable, revered by the ruler, gentle, wealthy; rules the earth, has sons, famous, prosperous and prudent.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.118-120 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: A benefic in the 10th from the Moon or lagna: fame unclouded and lasting as long as Moon and stars, unfailing prosperity till the end of life, revered by the sovereign, great enjoyments, liberal, kind to relatives, benevolent.

source_views.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 13
source_views.view: A benefic in the 10th from the Moon or lagna: lasting fame, spotless character, prosperity. Strength of the benefic and its aspects/associations matter. A malefic in the 10th still gives wealth in its dasa but not fame or character, and the means may be questionable; Amala makes one scrupulous about means.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.6 (Other Popular Yogas)
source_views.view: Only natural benefics in the 10th from the lagna or the Moon: everlasting fame, respected by kings, luxuries, virtuous, helps others; pure conduct in society.

yoga/amala.disagreements: Exclusivity: BPHS (as read by Santhanam) and P.V.R. Narasimha Rao require only benefics in the 10th, so a malefic there voids it; Phaladeepika, Jataka Parijata and Raman just require a benefic present. Wealth: Phaladeepika and Jataka Parijata promise it; Santhanam stresses that BPHS does not. Bhava chart versus sign-based houses: Santhanam prefers the bhava chart.
yoga/amala.phrasing_guidance: Present as a sign of good reputation and ethical conduct in public life. Do not promise permanent fame; mention that a malefic sharing the 10th weakens it.

definitions.definition: Exclusively a benefic in the 10th from the lagna or the Moon (no malefic sharing the house, per Santhanam's notes).
Benefics occupying the 10th house from the lagna or the Moon.
The 10th bhava from the rising sign or the Moon occupied by a benefic.
The 10th from the Moon or lagna occupied by a benefic planet.
Only natural benefics in the 10th from the lagna or the Moon.

cancellations.condition: A malefic joining the benefic in the 10th: the yoga's efficacy is void.
No benefic in the 10th: Amala is not caused (a malefic there gives wealth without fame or clean means).

yoga/amala.rarity_and_weight: Two reference points make the basic form fairly easy to meet; sources give no frequency figure. Santhanam: a pure Amala yoga gives name and fame for decades. Raman weighs it by the strength of the benefic.
yoga/amala.timing: Santhanam's example: results (a business start) came in the sub-period of the benefic forming it (Mercury in Venus dasa). Raman: any planet in the 10th from lagna or Moon gives wealth in its dasa.

conditional_results.when: manual: the 10th from the lagna or Moon holds only benefics, unaspected by malefics
effects: lasting good name, honour, prosperity through fair means
conditional_results.source: BPHS 36.5-6 with Santhanam's notes; Raman no. 13

conditional_results.when: manual: a malefic also in the 10th
effects: yoga void; wealth possible without fame or by questionable means

yoga/sunapha.summary: Sunapha forms when one or more planets other than the Sun occupy the 2nd sign from the Moon. The texts tie it mainly to self-earned wealth, intelligence and standing, coloured by whichever planet forms it.
common_outcomes: wealth and property gained by one's own effort (BPHS 37.7-10; Phaladeepika 6.6; Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 2)
intelligence, good reputation and a status 'equal to a king' in the classical idiom, meaning standing among one's own people (BPHS 37.7-10; Brihat Jataka 13.5)
learning in the sastras and a peaceable, virtuous disposition (Saravali 13.4)
rare_outcomes: Mars forming it: valour, wealth, harsh speech, command of soldiers, a fierce and proud nature (Saravali 13.10-11; Jataka Parijata 7.86 says a fierce, cruel, strong-minded ruler)
Mercury forming it: skill in Vedas, sastras, music and poetry, a brilliant physique (Saravali 13.10-11; Jataka Parijata 7.87)
Jupiter forming it: high learning, fame, a good family, plenty of wealth, favour of rulers (Saravali 13.12-14)
Venus forming it: wife, lands, wealth, cattle and honour from rulers (Saravali 13.12-14)
Saturn forming it: skill, respect in one's village or town, abundant wealth, devotion to work (Saravali 13.12-14)

by_area.personality: intelligent, virtuous, peaceable and well regarded (Saravali 13.4; BPHS 37.7-10)
by_area.career: rises by own effort to a position of authority; Saravali names king or minister in the classical idiom (Saravali 13.4)
by_area.finance: self-acquired property and wealth; Raman stresses that Sunapha has much influence on financial prosperity or adversity (Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 2, remarks)

strengtheners: benefic, well-placed or yogakaraka planets in the 2nd from the Moon (Raman no. 2: Venus as yogakaraka fortified finances in his chart 5)
several benefics in the 2nd from the Moon, e.g. Mercury, Jupiter and Venus together (Raman no. 2)
the 2nd from the Moon also falling in the 10th/11th from the lagna, which links the yoga to career and gains (Raman no. 2, Leo lagna illustration)
forming planets in exaltation, own or friendly signs or navamsas: then the full result is realised (Jataka Parijata 7.106)
a strong, bright Moon; the yoga works according to the Moon's state (Saravali 13.8-9)
the yoga operating in kendras: Saravali says one of royal birth then becomes a ruler (Saravali 35.176)
weakeners_or_cancellations: afflicted forming planets: Raman's chart 4 has five planets in the 2nd from the Moon with a debilitated Sun, Ketu and aspects of Saturn and Rahu, and he calls the yoga practically defunct (Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 2)
the Moon joined with Rahu or Ketu, Rahu in the 10th from the Moon, or a forming planet debilitated or combust: the results become mixed (Jataka Parijata 7.107)
yoga/sunapha.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman notes that the houses the 2nd from the Moon occupies from the lagna shape the results; with Leo lagna and Taurus Moon, planets in Gemini connect the yoga to the 10th and 11th houses (Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 2).

source_views.source: BPHS 37.7-10 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1, ch. 'Lunar Yogas')
source_views.view: A planet other than the Sun in the 2nd from the Moon gives Sunapha; the native is a king or like one, intelligent, wealthy, famous, with self-earned wealth.

source_views.source: BPHS 37.7-8 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com translation)
source_views.view: Same rule: a planet excluding the Sun in the 2nd from the Moon; the native becomes a king or equal to one.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.5-6 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Planets other than the Sun in the 2nd from the Moon give Sunapha; the native is a king or his equal, with self-acquired property, known for wisdom and wealth.

source_views.source: Saravali 13.1, 13.3-4, 13.8-14 (English tr., archive.org)
source_views.view: Excluding the Sun, any planet in the 2nd from the Moon; gives wealth, self-made position, learning, fame, rulership or ministry. Results depend on the Moon's phase, the forming planets' strength and the native's country and family. Separate results are given for Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 13.3-5, 13.7-8 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Planets other than the Sun in the 2nd from the Moon; the native is a king or equal, with self-acquired property and renowned for wisdom. Sastri's note says planets in the 2nd from the Moon give accumulation of wealth. Varahamihira gives the per-planet results without separating 2nd from 12th.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.72-73, 7.83-90, 7.106-107 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Same definition; per-planet Sunapha results; full results when forming planets are exalted, in own or friendly signs or navamsas; mixed when the Moon is with a node, Rahu is 10th from the Moon, or the forming planet is debilitated or combust.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 2 Sunapha Yoga
source_views.view: Planets excepting the Sun in the 2nd from the Moon; self-earned property, intelligence, wealth, reputation. The nature of the yoga depends on the planets forming it; results come in the dasas and bhuktis of those planets; strongly tied to finances; can be rendered defunct by affliction.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XX 'Some Special Yogas', no. 10
source_views.view: Planets in the 2nd from the Moon: a self-made man with self-acquired wealth, intelligent and reputed.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.3.1
source_views.view: Planets other than the Sun in the 2nd from the Moon; king or equal, intelligent, wealthy, famous, self-earned wealth.

yoga/sunapha.disagreements: Varahamihira (Brihat Jataka 13.3, Sastri's notes) reports two minority methods that he rejects: Srutakirti counted planets in the 4th from the Moon for Sunapha, and Devasarma counted from the sign of the Moon's navamsa. Sastri adds a footnote that Parasara recognised these two views. Saravali 13.3 counts 30 varieties of Sunapha, while Brihat Jataka 13.4 and Raman count 31.
yoga/sunapha.phrasing_guidance: Present this as a supportive yoga for earning by one's own effort. Name the planet forming it and its condition, since that changes the flavour a lot. Avoid promising wealth or rank; say it supports them when the forming planets are strong.

definitions.definition: A planet other than the Sun in the 2nd sign from the Moon.
Planets other than the Sun in the 2nd house from the Moon.
Excepting the Sun, any planet in the 2nd from the Moon.

Planets other than the Sun in the 2nd from the Moon; the commentary quoting Garga limits the planets to Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn, so Rahu and Ketu are not counted. Positions are by sign, not bhava (note to 13.5).
The 2nd from the Moon occupied by planets other than the Sun.

definitions.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 2
definitions.definition: Planets, excepting the Sun, in the 2nd house from the Moon: Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn, singly or together.

definitions.source: Brihat Jataka 13.3 (minority view of Srutakirti, rejected by Varahamihira)
definitions.definition: A planet other than the Sun in the 4th from the Moon.

cancellations.condition: Forming planet debilitated or combust, the Moon with Rahu or Ketu, or Rahu in the 10th from the Moon: results become mixed, not cancelled
Heavy affliction of the forming planets by malefics and nodes: the yoga is practically defunct
cancellations.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 2, chart 4

yoga/sunapha.rarity_and_weight: Varahamihira counts 31 combinations of the five planets for Sunapha (Brihat Jataka 13.4; Raman no. 4 remarks); Saravali 13.3 says 30. The yoga is common because any of five planets will do. Raman weighs it by the nature and strength of the occupying planets and says it strongly influences finances (no. 2).
yoga/sunapha.timing: Results show in the dasas and bhuktis of the planets that form the yoga (Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 2).

conditional_results.when: manual: if the planet in the 2nd from the Moon is exalted, in its own or a friendly sign, or in such a navamsa
manual: if the forming planet is debilitated or combust, or the Moon is with Rahu or Ketu, or Rahu is in the 10th from the Moon

yoga/anapha.summary: Anapha forms when one or more planets other than the Sun occupy the 12th sign from the Moon. The texts give good health and looks, character, fame and enjoyment, with spending rather than saving and, per Raman, detachment later in life.
common_outcomes: a healthy, well-formed body and a commanding appearance (BPHS 37.7-10; Raman no. 3)
virtue, fame and good manners (BPHS 37.7-10; Phaladeepika 6.6)
comforts, good dress, enjoyment of sense pleasures (Phaladeepika 6.6; Saravali 13.5)
rare_outcomes: renunciation and austerity in later life (Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 3; Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XX no. 9)
Mars forming it: leader of a band (Saravali says of thieves), arrogant, fond of war, honoured (Saravali 13.15-19)
Mercury forming it: skill in singing, dancing and writing, poet and orator, honoured by rulers (Saravali 13.15-19)
Jupiter forming it: majestic, intelligent, a poet, famous through a ruler (Saravali 13.15-19)
Venus forming it: strong liking for women, favour of rulers, abundant gold (Saravali 13.15-19)
Saturn forming it: broad-shouldered, a leader who keeps commitments, rich in cattle (Saravali 13.15-19)

by_area.personality: polite, generous, self-respecting, contented; eloquent per Saravali 13.5 (Raman no. 3; Phaladeepika 6.6)
by_area.finance: enjoyment and spending rather than accumulation; Sastri's note says planets in the 12th from the Moon give enjoyment without caring for accumulation (Brihat Jataka 13.5 note)
by_area.health: free from disease, well-formed limbs (BPHS 37.7-10; Phaladeepika 6.6; Raman no. 3)
by_area.spirituality: Raman links the 12th to moksha: the native cultivates detachment in later years (no. 3, chart 6)

strengtheners: strong, well-placed planets in the 12th from the Moon (Jataka Parijata 7.106)
a strong Moon (Saravali 13.8-9)
weakeners_or_cancellations: a debilitated forming planet weakens it; Raman calls the yoga 'feebly powerful' in chart 6 because Jupiter is debilitated, even with neecha bhanga (no. 3)
the Moon with Rahu or Ketu, Rahu in the 10th from the Moon, or a debilitated or combust forming planet: results mixed (Jataka Parijata 7.107)

source_views.source: BPHS 37.7-10 (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: A planet other than the Sun in the 12th from the Moon gives Anapha; the native is a king, free from disease, virtuous, famous, charming and happy.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.5-6 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Powerful, healthy, amiable, famous, comfortable, well dressed, contented and happy.

Excluding the Sun, a planet in the 12th from the Moon; eloquent, magnanimous, virtuous, enjoys food, drink, flowers, robes and women, famous, calm, beautiful body; separate results for each of the five planets.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 13.3, 13.5 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Strong, healthy, amiable, famous, comfortable, well dressed, contented. The note says the 12th gives enjoyment rather than accumulation.
Same definition; general and per-planet Anapha results.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 3 Anapha Yoga
source_views.view: Planets in the 12th from the Moon (Sun not counted); well-formed organs, majestic appearance, reputation, politeness, generosity, fondness for dress and pleasures, and renunciation in later life. The Sunapha remarks apply with slight variation; each planet's share shows in its own dasa.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XX no. 9
source_views.view: Commanding appearance, health, morality, freedom from mental sorrow, renown, sense pleasures and later renunciation.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.3.2
source_views.view: Planets other than the Sun in the 12th from the Moon; good looks, freedom from disease, character, reputation and comforts.

yoga/anapha.disagreements: Srutakirti (reported and rejected in Brihat Jataka 13.3 notes and Jataka Parijata 7.83 notes) took the 10th from the Moon for Anapha. Only Raman (and his Hindu Predictive Astrology) adds later-life renunciation; the classical verses read here do not mention it.
yoga/anapha.phrasing_guidance: Frame it as a yoga of health, presence and enjoyment, and note it leans toward spending. If Raman's detachment theme is used, offer it as a possible later-life inward turn, not a prediction of leaving home.

definitions.definition: A planet other than the Sun in the 12th sign from the Moon.
Planets other than the Sun in the 12th from the Moon.
Excepting the Sun, any planet in the 12th from the Moon.
Planets other than the Sun in the 12th from the Moon; per Garga only Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn count.
The 12th from the Moon occupied by planets other than the Sun.

definitions.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 3
definitions.definition: Planets in the 12th from the Moon; the Sun is not taken into account.
A planet other than the Sun in the 10th from the Moon.

cancellations.condition: Forming planet debilitated or combust, the Moon with Rahu or Ketu, or Rahu in the 10th from the Moon: results mixed

yoga/anapha.rarity_and_weight: 31 varieties (Brihat Jataka 13.4; Raman no. 4 remarks); 30 in Saravali 13.3. Common; weighed by the strength of the occupying planets (Raman no. 3).
yoga/anapha.timing: Each forming planet gives its share of the yoga in its own dasa (Raman no. 3, chart 6, where Saturn's quota is expected in Saturn's dasa). Raman places the renunciation theme in later life.

conditional_results.when: manual: if the planet in the 12th from the Moon is exalted, in its own or a friendly sign, or in such a navamsa
manual: if the forming planet is debilitated or combust, or the Moon is with Rahu or Ketu, or Rahu is in the 10th from the Moon

yoga/durudhara.summary: Durudhara (Dhurdhura) forms when planets other than the Sun occupy both the 2nd and the 12th signs from the Moon. It combines earning (2nd) with enjoying (12th): wealth, vehicles, generosity and comforts, coloured by the pair of planets involved.
common_outcomes: enjoyment of pleasures, wealth and vehicles (BPHS 37.7-10; Phaladeepika 6.7; Raman no. 4)
a charitable, bountiful nature (BPHS 37.7-10; Brihat Jataka 13.6; Raman no. 4)
faithful servants or attendants (BPHS 37.7-10; Phaladeepika 6.7)
rare_outcomes: grief from having to support family members (Saravali 13.6)
Mars and Mercury: untruthful, very wealthy, miserly, chief of his clan (Saravali 13.20)
Mars and Jupiter: famous for deeds, many enemies, protects his people, gathers money (Saravali 13.21)
Mars and Venus: a virtuous wife, fortunate, argumentative, fond of exercise, bold in war (Saravali 13.22)
Mars and Saturn: a difficult spouse, saves money, has vices, quick to anger, overcomes enemies (Saravali 13.23)
Jupiter and Mercury: learned, a poet, wealthy, famous (Saravali 13.24)
Mercury and Venus: sweet speech, fond of dance and music, a minister (Saravali 13.25)
Mercury and Saturn: travels from place to place to earn, little education, at odds with his own people (Saravali 13.26)
Jupiter and Venus: courageous, politically wise, owns gold and gems, in a ruler's service (Saravali 13.27)
Jupiter and Saturn: happy, politically knowledgeable, sweet-spoken, wealthy (Saravali 13.28)
Venus and Saturn: mature beyond his years, chief of his clan, dear to women, honoured, wealthy (Saravali 13.29; Jataka Parijata 7.105 gives a similar Venus-Saturn picture)

by_area.personality: liberal, generous, of good conduct; famed for speech, wisdom and valour (Saravali 13.6; Raman no. 4)
by_area.finance: both earns (planets in the 2nd) and spends or enjoys (planets in the 12th), per Sastri's note to Brihat Jataka 13.6; much wealth and conveyances (Raman no. 4)
by_area.relationships: spouse themes vary by pair: virtuous wife with Venus-Mars, a difficult one with Mars-Saturn (Saravali 13.22-23)
by_area.family: may come to grief through maintaining family members (Saravali 13.6)

strengtheners: well-dignified forming planets; Raman contrasts exalted Mars in the 2nd with Jupiter in the 12th against debilitated Jupiter in the 2nd with Mars in the 12th and says the permutations must be analysed (no. 4)
an exalted or strong Moon; Raman's chart 7 has the Moon exalted in Taurus with Saturn and Venus on either side (no. 4)
forming planets in exaltation, own or friendly signs or navamsas (Jataka Parijata 7.106)
weakeners_or_cancellations: the Moon with Rahu or Ketu, Rahu in the 10th from the Moon, or a debilitated or combust forming planet: mixed results (Jataka Parijata 7.107)
yoga/durudhara.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman's chart 7: Saturn, which is a yogakaraka counted from the Moon, flanks the Moon, so he expects the results mostly in Saturn dasa, especially the Venus bhukti (no. 4).

source_views.source: BPHS 37.7-10 (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Planets other than the Sun in both the 2nd and 12th from the Moon give Duradhara; the native enjoys pleasures, is charitable, has wealth, vehicles and good servants.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.5, 6.7 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Durudhara: takes life's joys as they come, has abundant wealth and vehicles, is bountiful and served by faithful attendants.

Planets other than the Sun in both the 2nd and 12th; famed for speech, wisdom, valour and virtue, enjoys freedom, comforts, wealth and vehicles, liberal, but suffers from supporting the family. Gives the results of each planet pair. Counts 180 varieties.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 13.3-4, 13.6 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Defined as above; 180 varieties, worked out in Sastri's notes (75+70+30+5). Bountiful, wealthy, with vehicles and faithful attendants. The note says the native both earns and spends.
Same definition; per-pair Durudhara results, e.g. Venus and Saturn on either side give a leading man in a traditional clan with much wealth and royal favour.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 4 Dhurdhura Yoga
source_views.view: Planets on either side of the Moon; bountiful, much wealth and conveyances. Each permutation of the five planets gives different results and must be analysed; about 180 varieties. Results in the dasa of the yoga-giving planet.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XX no. 11
source_views.view: Planets in the 2nd and 12th from the Moon: all pleasures, conveyances, liberal and generous, commanding, with dutiful children.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.3.3
source_views.view: Planets other than the Sun in the 2nd and 12th from the Moon; pleasures, charity, wealth, vehicles and good servants.

yoga/durudhara.disagreements: The texts agree on the definition. Saravali adds a cost (grief from supporting family) and gives pair results that are not uniformly good (Mars-Mercury, Mars-Saturn). Raman's Hindu Predictive Astrology adds dutiful children, which the classical verses read here do not give. Srutakirti's rejected variant used the 4th and 10th from the Moon (Brihat Jataka 13.3 notes).
yoga/durudhara.phrasing_guidance: Describe it as a supported, comfortable Moon: resources come in and go out freely. Name the two planets involved, because the pair changes the tone; avoid absolute claims about wealth.

definitions.definition: Planets other than the Sun in both the 2nd and the 12th from the Moon.
Planets other than the Sun in both the 2nd and 12th from the Moon.
Excepting the Sun, planets in both the 2nd and 12th from the Moon.
Planets other than the Sun in both the 2nd and 12th from the Moon; only the five planets Mars to Saturn are used in counting the varieties.

definitions.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 4
definitions.definition: Planets on either side of the Moon (2nd and 12th), drawn from Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn.
Planets in both the 4th and 10th from the Moon.

cancellations.condition: Forming planet debilitated or combust, the Moon with Rahu or Ketu, or Rahu in the 10th from the Moon: results mixed

yoga/durudhara.rarity_and_weight: 180 varieties (Brihat Jataka 13.4; Saravali 13.3; Raman no. 4). Raman says the general truth of these lunar yogas is money, power and reputation in varying degrees, and that each permutation produces different results (no. 4).
yoga/durudhara.timing: In the dasas and bhuktis of the flanking planets; in Raman's chart 7, Saturn dasa, especially Venus bhukti (no. 4).

conditional_results.when: manual: if the flanking planets are exalted, in their own or friendly signs, or in such navamsas
manual: if a flanking planet is debilitated or combust, or the Moon is with Rahu or Ketu, or Rahu is in the 10th from the Moon

yoga/kemadruma.summary: Kemadruma is the unsupported Moon: no planet other than the Sun in the 2nd or 12th from the Moon (and, in most versions, none with the Moon). It is the classic poverty-and-hardship yoga, but almost every text gives cancellations, chiefly planets in kendras from the lagna or the Moon.
common_outcomes: poverty, sorrow and dependence on others (Raman no. 5; Brihat Jataka 13.6; Phaladeepika 6.7)
loss of learning and intelligence, reproach from others, perils (BPHS 37.11-13)
obscurity even for those of a high-born family (Brihat Jataka 13.6; Phaladeepika 6.7; Saravali 13.7)
having to work hard and succeed through great effort (P.V.R. Narasimha Rao 11.3.4)
rare_outcomes: deprived of food, drink, home, clothing and friends; sickness and grime; living by hard labour (Saravali 13.7)
Raja yogas in the chart fail to work (Jataka Parijata 7.82; Saravali 39.19 when the Moon is also unaspected; enjoylearningsanskrit.com BPHS 37.13)
base or prohibited acts; Raman explains the word neecha in the original as acts against religious, moral and social codes (no. 5)

by_area.personality: sorrowful, mentally as well as physically, per Raman; Saravali says hostile to all (Raman no. 5; Saravali 13.7)
by_area.career: drudging as a menial in the classical idiom; must succeed through great effort (Brihat Jataka 13.6; Rao 11.3.4)
by_area.finance: poverty and penury (BPHS 37.11-13; Raman no. 5; Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XX no. 21: misery and poverty throughout life)
by_area.health: sickness and dirtiness (Saravali 13.7)
by_area.relationships: deprived of friends; at odds with others (Saravali 13.7)

strengtheners: the Moon unaspected by any planet makes it worse: Saravali counts no aspect as a formation condition and says Raja yogas then lose their existence (Saravali 13.2, 39.19)
Varahamihira: those of royal birth suffer the degradation even more (Raman no. 5 remarks; Brihat Jataka 13.6)
in the Jaimini reading, the Moon's aspect on the malefics makes the effects more severe (BPHS 33.94-99)
weakeners_or_cancellations: any of Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus or Saturn in a kendra from the lagna (Brihat Jataka 13.3 with Garga; Phaladeepika 6.5; BPHS 37.11 as rendered by Santhanam and enjoylearningsanskrit.com)
a planet in a kendra from the Moon (Phaladeepika 6.5; Saravali 13.2; Garga in Brihat Jataka 13.3 notes; Raman no. 5)
the Moon conjoined with a planet other than the Sun (Phaladeepika 6.5; Brihat Jataka 13.3; BPHS 37.11)
the Full Moon aspected by all the planets: long life and freedom from Kemadruma's evils (Saravali 35.47)
a Venus in the 8th destroys a Jaimini-style Kemadruma from the lagna (Rath, Crux, ch. V, chart 30)
yoga/kemadruma.lagna_or_context_notes: There are two separate traditions. (1) The lunar Kemadruma: no planet (Sun excluded) in the 2nd or 12th from the Moon. (2) A Jaimini Kemadruma: malefics in the 1st, 2nd and 8th from the Karakamsa, the Arudha lagna or the lagna (BPHS 33.94-99; Rath, Crux, ch. V and ch. XII). Jataka Parijata 7.71 and 7.78-79 also give other Kemadruma-like combinations: the Moon in the 1st or 7th without Jupiter's aspect, Saturn and Venus afflicted in mutual aspect or conjunction, and a weak, waning or debilitated Moon at night with certain aspects.

source_views.source: BPHS 37.11-13 (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Excluding the Sun, if no planet is with the Moon or in the 2nd or 12th from it, or in an angle from the ascendant, Kemadruma forms; the native is much reproached, without intelligence or learning, and reduced to poverty and perils.

source_views.source: BPHS 37.11-13 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com translation)
source_views.view: No planet, excluding the Sun, in the 2nd and 12th from the Moon; a kendra clause excludes the Moon when checking kendras from the lagna. Verse 13: this lunar yoga nullifies the results of other yogas.

source_views.source: BPHS 33.94-99 (tr. Santhanam, ch. 'Effects of Karakamsa')
source_views.view: Malefics in the Karakamsa, the Arudha lagna and the 2nd and 8th from them give Kemadruma, more severe with the Moon's aspect. It acts in the dasas of the signs or planets concerned, and also when malefics occupy the 2nd and 8th from the running dasa sign or from the chart cast for the start of a dasa.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.5, 6.7 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Kemadruma is the absence of Sunapha, Anapha and Durudhara. Some say it does not exist when a kendra or the Moon is associated with a planet, or when planets occupy a kendra from the Moon. Even those of princely birth become obscure, miserable, low, poor, menial and ill-inclined.

Kemadruma forms when none of the three yogas exists, or the Moon's kendras are empty, or the Moon is unaspected by all planets; extreme difficulty, loss of food, home, clothes and friends, poverty and sickness. A Full Moon aspected by all planets escapes it (35.47). Kemadruma with an unaspected Moon destroys Raja yogas (39.19).

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 13.3, 13.6 with Sastri's notes
source_views.view: The majority hold that Kemadruma is the absence of the three yogas; others deny it when a kendra from the lagna or the Moon is associated with a planet. Sastri, following Garga, says one of the five planets in any kendra (from the lagna or the Moon) or with the Moon annuls it. The Moon in a kendra with one of the five planets does not by itself destroy it. Effects as in Phaladeepika.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.71, 7.73, 7.78-83 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Gives several Kemadruma forms (Moon in the 1st or 7th without Jupiter's aspect; very low ashtakavarga points; afflicted Saturn-Venus; afflicted weak Moon at night). Gives exceptions to the related poverty yogas: the Moon or Venus in a kendra aspected by Jupiter; the Moon with a benefic or between two benefics aspected by Jupiter; the Full Moon in the lagna with a benefic. 7.82: Kemadruma makes Raja yogas vanish like elephants before a lion. 7.83 repeats Brihat Jataka 13.3.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 5 Kemadruma Yoga
source_views.view: No planets on either side of the Moon. Dirty, sorrowful, unrighteous, poor, dependent, a rogue. Some authors cancel it with planets in kendras from the lagna or the Moon or a planet with the Moon; in chart 8 Raman treats the yoga as clearly cancelled because kendras from both the Moon and the lagna are occupied.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XX no. 21
source_views.view: No planets in the 2nd and 12th from the Moon: misery and poverty throughout life; generally capable of neutralising all beneficial yogas.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.3.4
source_views.view: No planets other than the Sun in the 1st, 2nd and 12th from the Moon and no planets other than the Moon in kendras from the lagna. Unlucky, poor, troubled; kills the results of other good yogas, especially Chandra yogas; success comes through great effort.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. V (wealth, charts 29-30) and ch. XII (chart 106)
source_views.view: Uses the Jaimini Kemadruma: malefics including Rahu and Ketu in the 1st, 2nd and 8th from the lagna, Arudha lagna or navamsa lagna. From the lagna it gives lifelong poverty; from the Arudha lagna, a setback such as business collapse or loss of reputation. A benefic (Venus) in the 8th destroys it.

yoga/kemadruma.disagreements: The formation rule differs. (a) The bare rule is no planet in the 2nd or 12th from the Moon (Raman; Hindu Predictive Astrology; Phaladeepika and Brihat Jataka 'majority' view). (b) BPHS (Santhanam) and Rao also require no planet with the Moon and none in kendras from the lagna. (c) Saravali also lists empty kendras from the Moon or no aspect on the Moon. Which kendra cancels is also disputed: Brihat Jataka 13.3 says from the lagna; Phaladeepika 6.5 says from the lagna and from the Moon; Garga, cited by Sastri, says either. Sastri rejects reading 'the Moon in a kendra' as a cancellation. Brihat Jataka 13.3 also reports and rejects two variants (4th/10th from the Moon; counting from the Moon's navamsa sign), which Sastri says Parasara accepted. Rahu and Ketu are not counted in the classical lunar rule (Garga's five planets) but are counted as malefics in Rath's Jaimini form. Raman thinks the further kendra-and-navamsa versions are 'not generally acceptable', yet he applies the kendra cancellation in his own chart 8.
yoga/kemadruma.phrasing_guidance: Never present it as a sentence of poverty. Check the cancellations first, because most charts with the bare rule have a planet in a kendra. If it stands, describe periods of feeling unsupported and needing to build one's own resources, and pair it with the chart's strengths.

definitions.definition: Excluding the Sun: no planet with the Moon, none in the 2nd or 12th from the Moon, and none in an angle from the ascendant.
No planet (Sun excluded) in the 2nd and 12th from the Moon, with a clause on planets other than the Moon in kendras from the ascendant; the page does not make the link between the clauses explicit.
Absence of Sunapha, Anapha and Durudhara (no planet other than the Sun in the 2nd or 12th from the Moon).
None of the three yogas present, or the kendras from the Moon empty, or the Moon unaspected by all planets.
Absence of the three yogas; with Garga, only Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn are counted.
The Moon in the 1st or 7th without the aspect of Jupiter; also weak planets in places with very few ashtakavarga points give Kemadruma-like results.

Afflicted Saturn and Venus in mutual aspect or together; the Moon with a malefic in a malefic sign or navamsa at night aspected by a weak 10th lord; the Moon in its debilitation navamsa with a planet in khala state aspected by the 9th lord; the waning Moon debilitated in a night birth.
Malefics in the Karakamsa, the Arudha lagna and the 2nd and 8th from them.

definitions.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 5
definitions.definition: No planets on both sides of the Moon (2nd and 12th).
No planet other than the Sun in the 1st, 2nd or 12th from the Moon, and no planet other than the Moon in a kendra from the lagna.

definitions.source: Rath, Crux ch. V and ch. XII (Jaimini form)
definitions.definition: Malefics (Rahu and Ketu included) in the 1st, 2nd and 8th from the lagna, Arudha lagna or navamsa lagna.

cancellations.condition: A planet (Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus or Saturn) in a kendra from the lagna
cancellations.source: Brihat Jataka 13.3 with Sastri's notes (Garga, Kalyanavarma); Phaladeepika 6.5; Raman no. 5

cancellations.condition: A planet in a kendra from the Moon
cancellations.source: Phaladeepika 6.5; Garga as cited in Brihat Jataka 13.3 notes and Jataka Parijata 7.83 notes; Raman no. 5

cancellations.condition: The Moon conjoined with a planet other than the Sun
All planets aspecting the Moon (Saravali: a Full Moon aspected by all planets escapes Kemadruma's ill effects)
cancellations.source: Saravali 35.47; listed among exceptions in Brihat Jataka 13.3 notes

cancellations.condition: For the related poverty yogas: the Moon or Venus in a kendra aspected by Jupiter; the Moon with a benefic or between two benefics aspected by Jupiter; the Moon in a very friendly or exaltation navamsa aspected by Jupiter; the Full Moon in the lagna with a benefic; the exalted Moon in the 10th aspected by Jupiter
Jaimini form: a benefic in the 8th (Venus in Rath's example) destroys the yoga

yoga/kemadruma.rarity_and_weight: Weighed heavily when it stands: it is said to nullify Raja yogas and other good yogas (Jataka Parijata 7.82; Saravali 39.19; enjoylearningsanskrit.com BPHS 37.13; Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XX no. 21; Rao 11.3.4). The full uncancelled form is uncommon because the kendra and conjunction exceptions remove most cases; Raman's own illustration (chart 8) is a Kemadruma that is 'distinctly cancelled'.
yoga/kemadruma.timing: Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XX no. 21: misery throughout life. BPHS 33.94-99 (Jaimini form): in the dasas of the signs or planets concerned, and whenever malefics are in the 2nd and 8th from the running dasa sign. Rath (Crux ch. XII): from the lagna, lifelong; from the Arudha lagna, a setback in a period.

conditional_results.when: manual: if a planet other than the Sun occupies a kendra from the lagna or from the Moon, or joins the Moon
conditional_results.source: Phaladeepika 6.5; Brihat Jataka 13.3 notes; Raman no. 5

conditional_results.when: manual: if the Moon in Kemadruma is aspected by no planet
manual: if the Full Moon is aspected by all planets

yoga/shakata.summary: Shakata (Sakata, 'cart') is the Moon in the 6th, 8th or 12th from Jupiter (equivalently Jupiter in the 12th, 6th or 8th from the Moon). It gives fortune that rises and falls like a cart wheel: luck is lost and regained. Most texts cancel it when the Moon (or Jupiter) is in a kendra from the lagna. A separate Nabhasa Sakata (all planets in the 1st and 7th) shares the name.
common_outcomes: fortune lost and regained repeatedly (Phaladeepika 6.17; Raman no. 12)
being an ordinary, insignificant person in the world (Phaladeepika 6.17; Raman no. 12)
mental grief and unhappiness (Phaladeepika 6.17)
rare_outcomes: poverty, privation and misery; stubbornness; dislike from relatives (Raman no. 12 definition results)
even those of royal family become poor, worn out by trouble, and disliked by the ruler (Jataka Parijata 7.109)
