obstacles, turmoil and disease in the dasa of Jupiter when he forms it (Rath, Crux ch. XI)

Nabhasa Sakata (all planets in the 1st and 7th): disease, ugly nails, foolishness, living by pulling carts, poverty, no friends or relatives, a quarrelsome or bad wife (BPHS 35.24; Saravali ch. 21 v. 30; Brihat Jataka 12.13; Raman no. 86)

by_area.personality: stubborn (Raman no. 12)
by_area.career: fortune obstructed now and then (Raman no. 12, citing a Sukra Nadi)
by_area.finance: losses followed by recovery; Raman found the poverty usually nominal in practice (no. 12)
by_area.health: Rath ties it to disease in Jupiter's dasa (Crux ch. XI); the Nabhasa form gives sickness (BPHS 35.24)
by_area.relationships: Nabhasa form: a quarrelsome or bad wife (Raman no. 86; Saravali ch. 21 v. 30)
by_area.family: hated by relatives (Raman no. 12)

strengtheners: Rath counts it in the navamsa as well as the rasi; his example has Sakata in both (Crux ch. XI)
weakeners_or_cancellations: the Moon in a kendra from the lagna (Phaladeepika 6.14)
Jupiter, while 6th or 8th from the Moon, in a kendra from the lagna (Jataka Parijata 7.108, Sastri's note)
Raman's experience: the poverty is often only nominal (no. 12)
yoga/shakata.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman notes that when one planet is 8th from the other, the other is 6th from it, so the 6th/8th pair is symmetrical (no. 12). Raman no. 86 notes that the Nabhasa Sakata can merge with Rajju or Nala yogas for certain lagnas.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.14, 6.17 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: The Moon in the 12th, 8th or 6th from Jupiter causes Sakata, but there is no Sakata if the Moon is in a kendra from the lagna. The native often loses his luck and regains it, is ordinary and insignificant, and suffers unavoidable mental grief.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.108-109 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Sakata from the Moon-Jupiter relation. Sastri's note says the yoga loses its bad effects if Jupiter, while in the 6th or 8th from the Moon, is in a kendra from the lagna, and that this differs from Parasara's and Varahamihira's Sakata (all planets in the 1st and 7th). 7.109: even one of royal family becomes indigent, distressed and disliked by the king. The verse text of 7.108 is illegible in the scan; only the translator's note was read.

source_views.source: BPHS 35.9-11, 35.24, 35.50 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Only the Nabhasa Sakata: all planets in the ascendant and the 7th. Disease, ugly nails, foolishness, living by pulling carts, poverty, no friends or relatives. Nabhasa yogas act in all dasas (35.50). No Moon-Jupiter Sakata was found in the Santhanam chapters read.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 12.4, 12.13 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Nabhasa Sakata: all seven planets in the 1st and 7th. Livelihood by driving a cart, sickly, a bad wife. Sastri's note says the effect is bad because the planets are in opposition.

source_views.source: Saravali ch. 21 vv. 15, 30
source_views.view: Nabhasa Sakata: all planets only in the ascendant and the 7th. Diseases, a bad wife, dullness, living by pulling carts, poverty, no relatives or friends.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 12 Sakata Yoga
source_views.view: The Moon in the 12th, 6th or 8th from Jupiter. Loss and regaining of fortune, ordinariness, poverty, stubbornness, dislike from relatives. Raman notes that Parasara and Varahamihira define Sakata as all planets in the 1st and 7th. In many horoscopes he found the poverty only nominal. A Sukra Nadi says fortune is obstructed now and then, whenever the Moon transits the 6th, 8th or 12th from natal Jupiter.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 86 (Nabhasa)
source_views.view: All planets in the lagna and 7th: poverty and an unhappy domestic life, manual labour, sickness, a quarrelsome wife; evil because the 1st and 7th become the focus.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. XI (disease)
source_views.view: Jupiter in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the Moon causes Sakata (obstacles, turmoil, disease). His example has it in both the rasi and the navamsa, and knee trouble started with Jupiter dasa.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.5 (Nabhasa yogas)
source_views.view: Lists only the Nabhasa Sakata: all planets in the 1st and 7th from the lagna; disease, ugly nails, foolishness, no friends or family, living by pulling carts.

yoga/shakata.disagreements: Two different yogas share the name. BPHS, Brihat Jataka, Saravali and Rao give only the Nabhasa Sakata (all planets in the 1st and 7th). Phaladeepika, Jataka Parijata, Raman and Rath give the Moon-Jupiter Sakata. Within the Moon-Jupiter form: Phaladeepika and Raman use the Moon in the 6th, 8th or 12th from Jupiter. Jataka Parijata (per Sastri's note) speaks of Jupiter in the 6th or 8th from the Moon. Rath uses Jupiter in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the Moon. Jupiter 12th from the Moon is the same as the Moon 2nd from Jupiter, not 12th, so the '12th' clauses of Raman and Rath do not describe the same configuration. On cancellation, Phaladeepika uses the Moon in a kendra from the lagna; Jataka Parijata's note uses Jupiter in a kendra from the lagna. Raman doubts the severity in practice.
yoga/shakata.phrasing_guidance: Describe ups and downs in fortune that recover, not lasting poverty. Check the kendra cancellation first, and say which version (Moon-Jupiter or all planets in the 1st and 7th) the calculator found.

definitions.definition: The Moon in the 12th, 8th or 6th from Jupiter.

definitions.source: Jataka Parijata 7.108 (Sastri's note; verse illegible in scan)
definitions.definition: Jupiter in the 6th or 8th from the Moon.

definitions.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 12
definitions.definition: The Moon in the 12th, 6th or 8th from Jupiter.
Jupiter in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the Moon; applied in the navamsa too.

definitions.source: BPHS 35.11; Brihat Jataka 12.4; Saravali ch. 21 v. 15; Raman no. 86; Rao 11.5 (Nabhasa Sakata)
definitions.definition: All seven planets (nodes omitted, per Raman) in the lagna and the 7th.

cancellations.condition: The Moon in a kendra from the lagna
Jupiter (while 6th or 8th from the Moon) in a kendra from the lagna

yoga/shakata.rarity_and_weight: The Moon-Jupiter form is common, since it needs only a sign relation between two bodies. Raman gives it modest weight: in many charts the poverty was nominal and fortune was only obstructed at times (no. 12). The Nabhasa form, needing all planets in two signs, is rare. Nabhasa yogas act throughout life (BPHS 35.50).
yoga/shakata.timing: Raman, citing a Sukra Nadi: the effects come each time the Moon transits the 6th, 8th or 12th from natal Jupiter (no. 12). Rath: in Jupiter's dasa (Crux ch. XI). Nabhasa form: in all dasas (BPHS 35.50; Brihat Jataka ch. 12 notes).

conditional_results.when: manual: if the Moon is in a kendra from the lagna
manual: if Jupiter, being 6th or 8th from the Moon, is in a kendra from the lagna
manual: when the transiting Moon is in the 6th, 8th or 12th from natal Jupiter
conditional_results.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 12 (citing Sukra Nadi)

yoga/shubha_kartari.summary: Shubha Kartari forms when benefics occupy both the 12th and the 2nd from the lagna, 'hemming' the ascendant between benefics. The texts give long life, health, fearlessness, wealth and good character. The principle applies to any house or planet.
common_outcomes: long life, fearlessness, freedom from disease and enemies, happiness and wealth (Phaladeepika 6.11)
eloquence, charm and virtue (BPHS 36.1-2, Subha yoga)
superior lustre, wealth and strength (Jataka Parijata 7.127)
rare_outcomes: Santhanam's note adds a happy life, health, wealth, longevity and fame, saying the text does not state these (BPHS 36.1-2 notes)

by_area.personality: eloquent, charming, virtuous, fearless (BPHS 36.2; Phaladeepika 6.11; Rao 11.6)
by_area.finance: rich (Phaladeepika 6.11); wealth (Jataka Parijata 7.127)
by_area.health: long-lived and free from disease (Phaladeepika 6.11)
by_area.relationships: free from enemies (Phaladeepika 6.11)

strengtheners: a benefic in the lagna as well as in the 2nd and 12th: Santhanam calls it a Subha yoga of a very great order (BPHS 36.1-2 notes)
benefics unaspected by malefics (Phaladeepika 6.8, for the related Susubha yoga, a benefic in the 2nd)
weakeners_or_cancellations: functional malefice of the flanking benefics: Santhanam's example of Aquarius lagna with Mercury in the 2nd and Jupiter in the 12th, which he calls worse than a typical Asubha yoga (BPHS 36.1-2 notes)
the dignity, strength and associations of the planets can override the yoga (BPHS 36.1-2 notes)
yoga/shubha_kartari.lagna_or_context_notes: Santhanam warns against judging by natural benefic or malefic status alone: for Aquarius lagna, Mercury (lord of the 5th and 8th) in the 2nd and Jupiter (lord of the 2nd and 11th) in the 12th do not give a good result (BPHS 36.1-2 notes). Rao and Rath apply Kartari to any house, arudha or planet (Rao 11.6 footnote; Crux ch. VIII, X).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.8, 6.11, 6.13 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Benefics in the 12th and 2nd from the lagna give Subhakartari: long-lived, fearless, free from disease and enemies, happy and rich. Its effects follow those of benefic-made yogas like Sunapha (6.13).

source_views.source: BPHS 36.1-2 (tr. Santhanam, ch. 'Many Other Yogas')
source_views.view: A benefic in the ascendant, or benefics in both the 12th and 2nd, give Subha yoga: eloquent, charming and virtuous. Santhanam's notes say the double-flank form is superior and that dignity and house rulership must be weighed.

source_views.source: BPHS 36.1 (enjoylearningsanskrit.com translation)
source_views.view: Renders the clause as benefics in the 2nd or 12th house making the yoga auspicious.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.125, 7.127 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Benefics in the 12th and 2nd from the lagna give Soumyakartari (Subhakartari): superior lustre, wealth and strength. Sastri's note says the Sun and the Moon are not counted in these yogas.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.6 and footnote 31
source_views.view: Subha yoga: benefics in the lagna or subha kartari (benefics in the 12th and 2nd); eloquence, good looks and character. Kartari means scissors; subha kartari on any house helps its matters and can be seen for any house or planet.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI (Seventh House), chart 23
source_views.view: Applies subhakartari to a house: in chart 23 the 7th house (occupied by malefics) is subject to subhakartari caused by Mercury on one side and Venus and the Moon on the other, so Raman counts the Moon as a benefic for kartari.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. VIII (fifth house) and ch. X (seventh house)
source_views.view: Uses subhakartari on houses and arudhas; a house can be under both subha and papa kartari at once; the seventh house under subhakartari brings the yoga's effects into its matters.

yoga/shubha_kartari.disagreements: BPHS (Santhanam) and Phaladeepika require benefics in both the 2nd and 12th; the enjoylearningsanskrit.com rendering of BPHS 36.1 reads '2nd or 12th'. BPHS treats a benefic in the lagna itself as a Subha yoga as well. Jataka Parijata (Sastri's note) excludes the Sun and the Moon from the count, whereas Raman counts the Moon as one of the benefics forming subhakartari (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI, chart 23). Santhanam's notes say functional rulership can override natural benefic status.
yoga/shubha_kartari.phrasing_guidance: Describe it as a protected, supported self: health, poise and goodwill. Check the house rulership of the flanking benefics before calling it strong.

definitions.definition: The 12th and 2nd from the lagna occupied by benefics.
Benefics in both the 12th and 2nd (Subha yoga; a benefic in the lagna also forms Subha yoga).
Benefics in the 2nd or 12th house (Subha yoga).
Benefics in the 12th and 2nd from the lagna; the Sun and Moon are not reckoned.
Benefics in the 12th and 2nd from a house (here the lagna); applicable to any house or planet.

cancellations.condition: The flanking benefics are functional malefics for the lagna (e.g. Aquarius lagna with Mercury in the 2nd and Jupiter in the 12th): judged worse than a typical Asubha yoga
Dignity, strength and relations of the planets may nullify or limit the yoga

yoga/shubha_kartari.rarity_and_weight: Santhanam ranks the double-flank form above a single benefic in the lagna, and a benefic in all three houses as a Subha yoga of a very great order (BPHS 36.1-2 notes). He also says the extra benefits will not fully mature from a single ordinary benefic.

conditional_results.when: manual: if the benefics in the 2nd and 12th rule dusthanas or are otherwise functional malefics for the lagna
effects: the expected good results do not come

yoga/papa_kartari.summary: Papa Kartari forms when malefics occupy both the 12th and the 2nd from the lagna, hemming the ascendant between malefics like the blades of scissors. The texts give poverty, unhappiness, sinful tendencies, harm to health and longevity, and loss of spouse or children. The same principle is applied to any house, lord or significator.
common_outcomes: poverty, impurity, unhappiness, loss of wife and children, damage to a limb and short life (Phaladeepika 6.11)
sensuality, sinful acts and enjoying others' wealth (BPHS 36.1-2, Asubha yoga)
criminal tendencies, living on begged food, impurity (Jataka Parijata 7.127)
rare_outcomes: defeat, bondage and loss of reputation when Saturn and Rahu cause it on the lagna (Rath, Crux ch. IV)
applied to the 7th house and its lord without benefic influence: loss of husband (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI)
[maraka: Moon in the lagna hemmed between malefics without benefic aspect is listed among balarishta (infant death) combinations] (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII; Saravali 10.35-36)

by_area.personality: lustful, sinful, deceitful per the texts (BPHS 36.2; Jataka Parijata 7.126)
by_area.career: loss of reputation; defeat (Rath, Crux ch. IV)
by_area.finance: poor; living on others' wealth or begged food (Phaladeepika 6.11; BPHS 36.2; Jataka Parijata 7.127)
by_area.health: damage to a limb, short life (Phaladeepika 6.11); two or three malefics harm health and longevity (BPHS 36.1-2 notes)
by_area.relationships: bereft of wife (Phaladeepika 6.11); for the 7th house, loss of spouse (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI)
by_area.family: bereft of children (Phaladeepika 6.11)

strengtheners: more malefics make it worse: one malefic may not give such bad results, but two or three do (BPHS 36.1-2 notes)
no benefic influence on the hemmed house or planet (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI; Uttara Kalamrita, rule on hemmed bhava, lord and karaka)
weakeners_or_cancellations: well-dignified malefics: Santhanam's example of Virgo lagna with exalted Saturn in the 2nd and the Sun in Leo in the 12th need not be called Asubha (BPHS 36.1-2 notes)

the hemming malefics being the significators (lords) of the very house concerned: Raman says papakartari on Venus is toned down because the Sun and Saturn hemming it are the lords of the lagna and of the 7th from the Moon (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI)
yoga/papa_kartari.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman, Rao and Rath apply papakartari to any house, lord or karaka, not only the lagna (How to Judge a Horoscope vols. 1-2; Rao 11.6 footnote 31; Crux passim). Uttara Kalamrita says a bhava is destroyed when the bhava, its lord and its karaka are all hemmed between malefics, joined by weak malefics, and without benefic aspect or conjunction.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.8, 6.11, 6.13 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Malefics in the 12th and 2nd from the lagna give Papakartari: poor, impure, unhappy, without wife and children, deprived of some limb, short-lived. Malefic-made yogas give the opposite of Sunapha-type benefits (6.13).

source_views.source: BPHS 36.1-2 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: A malefic in the ascendant, or malefics in both the 12th and 2nd, cause Asubha yoga: sensuous, sinful, enjoys others' wealth. The notes say severity rises with the number of malefics, health and longevity suffer, and well-dignified malefics may prove favourable.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.125-127 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Malefics in the 12th and 2nd from the lagna give Papakartari: criminal, eating begged food, impure. The note says the Sun and the Moon are not counted.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita (tr. P.S. Sastri), rule on destruction of a bhava (ch. on effects of planets and houses)
source_views.view: When a bhava, its lord and its karaka are hemmed between malefics, joined by weak malefics and without benefic aspect or conjunction, the bhava is destroyed.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. 4 (First House, Cancer illustration); vol. 2, ch. XI (Seventh House)
source_views.view: Defines papakartari as hemmed in between malefic planets and applies it to the lagna lord (Moon between Saturn and Ketu) and to the 7th house and its lord: without benefic influence it shows loss of husband.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.6 and footnote 31
source_views.view: Asubha yoga: malefics in the lagna or paapa kartari on it; many desires, sinful, enjoys others' wealth. Paapa kartari harms the matters of any house it falls on.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. IV (ascendant, Nehru's chart) and passim
source_views.view: Saturn and Rahu causing papakartari on the lagna indicate defeat, bondage and loss of reputation. Rahu is counted as a malefic in forming it.

yoga/papa_kartari.disagreements: Which malefics count is not settled. Jataka Parijata's translator excludes the Sun and Moon. Raman counts Ketu (Saturn and Ketu hemming) and Rath counts Rahu, while the classical verses say only 'malefics'. BPHS includes a malefic in the lagna itself under Asubha yoga. Santhanam's notes say dignified malefics may help rather than harm. The enjoylearningsanskrit.com rendering of BPHS 36.1 has '2nd or 12th' for the benefic clause, while Santhanam has both.
yoga/papa_kartari.phrasing_guidance: Describe pressure or constraint on health, confidence and resources that needs care, not doom. Do not repeat short-life or spouse-loss lines; check the dignity of the malefics and any benefic aspect on the lagna first.

definitions.definition: The 12th and 2nd from the lagna occupied by malefics.
Malefics in both the 12th and 2nd (Asubha yoga; a malefic in the lagna also forms Asubha yoga).
Malefics in the 12th and 2nd from the lagna; the Sun and Moon are not reckoned.

definitions.source: Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI
definitions.definition: A house or planet hemmed in between malefic planets.
Malefics in the 12th and 2nd from a house; applies to any house or planet.

cancellations.condition: The flanking malefics are strong and well dignified (e.g. Virgo lagna, exalted Saturn in the 2nd, the Sun in own sign Leo in the 12th): need not be called Asubha
Benefic aspect on or association with the hemmed house or planet reduces it (the bhava is destroyed only when there is no benefic aspect or conjunction)
cancellations.source: Uttara Kalamrita (rule on destruction of a bhava); Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI (without any benefic influence)

cancellations.condition: The hemming malefics are themselves the lords or significators of the house concerned: papakartari is toned down
cancellations.source: Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI

yoga/papa_kartari.rarity_and_weight: Severity scales with the number of malefics: a single malefic may not give such bad results, but two or three do (BPHS 36.1-2 notes). Raman weighs it together with the other afflictions of the house (How to Judge a Horoscope).

conditional_results.when: manual: if the hemming malefics are exalted or in their own signs
effects: need not be treated as Asubha; may prove favourable

conditional_results.when: manual: if the lagna or its lord receives no benefic aspect or conjunction
effects: the full harm of the hemming
conditional_results.source: Uttara Kalamrita; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XI

yoga/grahan.summary: 'Grahan' (eclipse) yoga, the Sun or the Moon conjoined with Rahu or Ketu, is a later, popular name; the classical texts read here do not define a yoga by that name. They do treat birth at an actual eclipse as inauspicious and needing remedy. They also treat the Moon 'seized' by Rahu or Ketu as spoiling lunar yogas and pointing to poverty when malefics aspect it. Modern authors read the node-luminary conjunction as an eclipse of that light, with obstructed or transformed results.
themes: obstruction of Sun or Moon significations
common_outcomes: birth at a solar or lunar eclipse brings ailments, distress and poverty, and the text prescribes remedial rites (BPHS 91.1-14)
the Moon with Rahu or Ketu makes the results of the lunar yogas mixed (Jataka Parijata 7.107)
the Moon seized by Rahu or Ketu and aspected by a malefic: early poverty (Jataka Parijata 7.75)
the planet joined with a node is eclipsed: its energy is obstructed, negated or released (Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, 'The Lunar Nodes')
rare_outcomes: the Moon aspected by a benefic that has lost a planetary war, and seized by a node in an eclipse: the native is indigent (Jataka Parijata 7.76)
Rahu eclipsing the Sun (Sun in the 6th context): torment by disease; the evil is overcome if the Sun's longitude is higher than Rahu's and worse if lower (Rath, Crux ch. IX 9.2)
a close Sun-Rahu conjunction can show deep spirituality or renunciation, depending on the arudha lagna (Rath, Crux ch. XV)
the Sun-Rahu 'eclipse combination' can produce either a short-lived saint or a long-lived criminal (Rath, Crux ch. XII)

[maraka: text predicts danger to life / death] eclipsed Moon (or Sun at a solar eclipse) in the lagna with malefics and Mars in the 8th: death of mother and child (Saravali 10.37-38; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII balarishta no. 6, with Saturn)

[maraka: text predicts danger to life / death] birth during a solar or lunar eclipse: death of the father or the mother respectively (Uttara Kalamrita 8.8); BPHS 91.1-14 also names danger of death among the effects of eclipse birth
[maraka: text predicts danger to life / death] the Moon with Rahu and another malefic, Mars in the 8th: death of mother and child (Jataka Parijata 4.36)

by_area.personality: the Moon is the mind; Rath reads Moon with Ketu as an eclipse of the mind in a disease context (Crux ch. XI)
by_area.finance: poverty when the node-seized Moon is aspected by malefics (Jataka Parijata 7.75-76); poverty among the effects of eclipse birth (BPHS 91.1-14)
by_area.health: ailments (BPHS 91.1-14); torment by disease when Rahu eclipses the Sun (Rath, Crux ch. IX)
by_area.family: eclipse birth threatens the father (solar) or mother (lunar) in Uttara Kalamrita 8.8
by_area.spirituality: Sun-Rahu close conjunction may give renunciation or great spirituality (Rath, Crux ch. XV); Frawley calls eclipses points of energy transformation

strengtheners: a malefic aspect on the node-seized Moon (Jataka Parijata 7.75)
an actual eclipse at birth, not only a sign conjunction (BPHS ch. 91; Uttara Kalamrita 8.8)
the Sun at a lower longitude than Rahu (Rath, Crux ch. IX)
weakeners_or_cancellations: the Sun at a higher longitude than Rahu: the evil is overcome (Rath, Crux ch. IX)
remedial rites for eclipse birth are said to wipe off the evil effects (BPHS 91.1-14)
yoga/grahan.lagna_or_context_notes: Rath reads the Sun-Rahu result through the arudha lagna: in Aquarius the native is spiritual, in Leo the reverse (Crux ch. XV).

source_views.source: BPHS 91.1-14 (tr. Santhanam vol. 2, 'Remedies from Birth in Eclipses')
source_views.view: Birth at a solar or lunar eclipse brings ailments, distress, poverty and danger of death. The remedy is worship of the nakshatra deity, the Sun (solar) or Moon (lunar), and Rahu with specified images, offerings, havana and feeding of Brahmins, which wipes off the evil.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.75-76, 7.107 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: The Moon seized by Rahu or Ketu and aspected by a malefic gives poverty. The Moon aspected by a war-defeated benefic and seized by a node in an eclipse gives indigence. The Moon with Rahu or Ketu, or Rahu 10th from the Moon, makes lunar yoga results mixed. In his note to 4.36-37 (arishta) Sastri says the 'grasped Moon' (grasta Chandra) is read as the Moon in association with Rahu, not necessarily an actual eclipse; 4.36 itself says the Moon with Rahu and another malefic, with Mars in the 8th, kills mother and child [maraka].

source_views.source: Saravali 10.37-38 (ch. 'Balarishta')
source_views.view: Eclipsed Moon in the lagna with malefics and Mars in the 8th: the child dies with the mother; similarly for a solar eclipse with the Sun and malefics in the lagna. [maraka]

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita 8.8 (tr. P.S. Sastri)
source_views.view: If birth (or a girl's first menses) occurs during a solar or lunar eclipse, the father or the mother respectively dies. [maraka]

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, 'The Lunar Nodes'
source_views.view: The nodes are the eclipse points and mythically swallow the luminaries, so they can overpower the Sun and Moon. Any planet joined with a node is a kind of eclipse of that planet, its energy obstructed, negated or liberated. Eclipses are points of energy transformation.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. IX (9.2), ch. XII, ch. XV
source_views.view: Rahu eclipsing the Sun gives torment by disease, overcome if the Sun is ahead of Rahu in longitude. A Sun-Rahu eclipse combination can give a short-lived saint or a long-lived criminal. A close Sun-Rahu conjunction can show great spirituality and renunciation in Rahu dasa when the arudha lagna supports it.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII (Eighth House, Balarishta no. 6)
source_views.view: If the eclipsed Moon joins Saturn in the lagna and Mars is in the 8th, both mother and child die. [maraka]

yoga/grahan.disagreements: Provenance: none of the classical texts read (BPHS, Phaladeepika, Saravali, Brihat Jataka, Jataka Parijata, Uttara Kalamrita) names a 'Grahan yoga'. The term appears to be later or popular usage; its first appearance was not found. The classical material either requires an actual eclipse at birth (BPHS 91; Uttara Kalamrita 8.8; Saravali 10.37-38) or speaks of the Moon 'seized' by a node, which Sastri reads as simple association with Rahu (Jataka Parijata 4.36-37 notes). The calculator's rule (Sun or Moon with Rahu or Ketu in the same sign) is broader than an actual eclipse. Modern authors split on tone: Frawley and Rath allow spiritual or transformative results, while the classical lines are uniformly adverse.
yoga/grahan.phrasing_guidance: Say that this is a modern label, and that a same-sign conjunction is not an actual eclipse at birth. Describe it as pressure or intensity on the Sun's or Moon's matters (vitality, father, mind, mother) that can also turn inward or spiritual. Never repeat the parent-death or infant-death lines to a user.

definitions.source: Calculator / popular usage (no classical source found)
definitions.definition: The Sun or the Moon in the same sign as Rahu or Ketu.
Birth during an actual solar or lunar eclipse (not a yoga by name).
The Moon 'seized by' or in conjunction with Rahu or Ketu.
Any planet conjoined with a lunar node is a kind of eclipse of that planet.
The 'grasped Moon' read as the Moon in association with Rahu, not necessarily an actual eclipse.

cancellations.condition: The Sun has a higher longitude than Rahu: the evil (disease) is overcome
Remedial rites for eclipse birth remove the evil effects

yoga/grahan.rarity_and_weight: The sign-conjunction form is fairly common. The texts give heavy weight only to an actual eclipse at birth (BPHS ch. 91; Uttara Kalamrita 8.8; Saravali 10.37-38). For the conjunction, Jataka Parijata 7.107 treats it as a modifier that mixes the lunar yogas rather than as a yoga by itself.
yoga/grahan.timing: Rath: in Rahu dasa (renunciation in his ch. XV example; the mother's sudden death in a Rahu dasa in his ch. XII example).

remedies.remedy: for birth at an eclipse: install images of the eclipse nakshatra's deity (gold), the Sun (gold) for a solar or the Moon (silver) for a lunar eclipse, and Rahu (lead); worship them with the matching mantras, flowers and cloth; perform havana with arka wood for the Sun, palasa for the Moon, durva grass for Rahu and pipal for the nakshatra deity; sprinkle the child and parents with kalasha water, honour the priest and feed Brahmins
remedies.source: BPHS 91.1-14 (tr. Santhanam)

conditional_results.when: manual: if the Moon joined by Rahu or Ketu is aspected by a malefic
manual: if the Moon is with Rahu or Ketu while a lunar yoga (Sunapha, Anapha, Durudhara) is present
effects: the lunar yoga gives mixed results

conditional_results.when: manual: if Rahu is conjoined with the Sun and the Sun's longitude is lower than Rahu's
manual: if Rahu is conjoined with the Sun and the Sun's longitude is higher than Rahu's

yoga/raja_kendra_trikona.summary: A link (conjunction, exchange, mutual aspect, or one placed in the other's kind of house) between the lord of an angle (1, 4, 7, 10) and the lord of a trine (1, 5, 9) is the basic Parashari Raja Yoga for status, power and prosperity. Modern writers stress that some such link exists in many charts, so the result depends on the strength, closeness and freedom from affliction of the two planets.
common_outcomes: rise in status, authority or public standing in the periods of the linked planets
prosperity and comfort (texts say 'becomes a king or equal to one'; modern writers read this as high position rather than literal kingship)
fame and honour
rare_outcomes: rulership or emperor-like standing when both lords attain high divisional dignity (Simhasanamsa or above in BPHS 41.29-34)
political power when the yoga planets are linked to the Sun, Moon or the 10th house (Raman); military command when linked to Mars (Raman)

by_area.personality: Famous, honoured, with qualities of a leader (BPHS 34.11-12).
by_area.career: Status, authority, high position or administrative power; the 10th-lord links count most (Laghu Parashari; Raman HJH).
by_area.finance: Trine lords are called wealth-givers (BPHS 34.2-7; 41.16), so the yoga usually brings prosperity along with status.
by_area.spirituality: BPHS 41.28 calls the angles houses of Vishnu and the trines houses of Lakshmi; their union is read as lasting well-being.

strengtheners: The lords are strong by sign (exalted, own, moolatrikona) and by divisional dignity (Parijatamsa and higher: BPHS 41.29-34; PVR 11.7.2).
The link is close in degrees: Raman (HJH) says within 12 degrees; PVR says full results need roughly 5-6 degrees.
The link involves the 10th lord (strongest angle) or the 9th lord (strongest trine) (Laghu Parashari sl. 17; Raman HJH).
The link is conjunction, exchange or mutual aspect rather than mere mutual angular/trinal placement (Santhanam's note to BPHS 41.28).
Lagna lord also strong (Santhanam, note on BPHS 39).
weakeners_or_cancellations: One of the lords also owns a dusthana or 3rd/11th: BPHS 34.15 says such a lord does not produce Raja Yoga by mere relation.
Both lords blemished by other lordships: no yoga (Laghu Parashari sl. 15 as explained by Verma).
The 9th/10th lords also owning the 8th/11th (Laghu Parashari sl. 22).
Combustion, debilitation, enemy sign, bad avasthas, affliction by functional malefics (PVR 11.7.2; Raman HJH).
General Raja Yoga obstructions listed in Saravali ch. 39 (see cancellations).
yoga/raja_kendra_trikona.lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS 34.19-44 names, for each lagna, which pairs do or do not give yoga. For example, for Aries the Jupiter (9/12) + Saturn (10/11) conjunction does not give a good result (34.19-22; also Bhavartha Ratnakara ch. 1 st. 4), and for Leo the Jupiter + Venus conjunction does not either (34.29-30). Bhavartha Ratnakara ch. 1 st. 1 says the 4th and 5th lords (Moon and Sun) give Raja Yoga for Aries. Raman (HJH) says to measure yogas from the lagna or the Moon, whichever is stronger.

source_views.source: BPHS 34.11-12 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1)
source_views.view: Exchange between an angular and a trinal lord, the two together in an angle or a trine, a trinal lord in an angle or an angular lord in a trine, or full mutual aspect gives yoga; the native becomes a king and famous. Santhanam lists six variants.

source_views.source: BPHS 34.15 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: An angular or trinal lord that also owns an evil house does not cause Raja Yoga by the mere relations of 34.11-12. Santhanam adds that the moolatrikona sign decides which lordship dominates.

source_views.source: BPHS 39.33-38 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: The 9th lord and especially the 5th lord act as ministers. Their mutual aspect or conjunction gives kingship. The 4th or 10th lord joining the 5th or 9th lord gives kingdom (39.37). So does the 5th lord in the 1st, 4th or 10th with the 9th or lagna lord (39.38).

source_views.source: BPHS 41.28-34 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Angles are Vishnu-sthanas and trines Lakshmi-sthanas; a relation between their lords gives Raja Yoga. Its grade rises with the pair's divisional dignity, from Parijatamsa (king) to Simhasanamsa (emperor) and beyond. Santhanam ranks the relations as exchange, mutual aspect and conjunction, then the weaker mutual angles or trines.

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari (Jataka Chandrika), Raja Yoga chapter sl. 14-17, 22 (tr. O.P. Verma)
source_views.view: Related kendra and trikona lords that own no other bad house give auspiciousness par excellence (14). If one of them is blemished they still give good results, but if both are blemished they do not (15). The best case links the 10th lord with a trine lord or the 9th lord with a kendra lord (17). The yoga is extinguished when the 9th/10th lords also own the 8th/11th (22).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.37-38 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Lords of a kendra and a kona conjoined in an auspicious bhava form Sankha yoga, which brings comfort and pleasures. The 9th-10th special case is named Raja yoga.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7, notes to sl. 21 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: The translator's note cites the classical rule that the association of kendra and kona lords produces Raja Yogas and lists four kinds of relationship (exchange, mutual aspect, conjunction, and a fourth not legible in the scan).

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, 'Considerations in Judging a House' pp. 9-11
source_views.view: An angular lord associated with a trinal lord causes Raja Yoga. Of the two, the one unblemished by other ownership or by association with the 3rd/6th/8th lords acts as the yogakaraka. The yoga has substantial effect only when the planets are within 12 degrees, and its extent depends on ownership, association, occupation and aspect.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, General Introduction and yogas 245-263
source_views.view: Raman's yoga method first classes each planet as a benefic, malefic or neutral lord for the lagna. He warns that the theoretical presence of a Raja Yoga is of no consequence without inherent vitality, and that results must be adapted to modern conditions: high position rather than kingship.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.7.1-11.7.2
source_views.view: Counts conjunction, mutual graha drishti and parivartana as associations, with lagna counting as both angle and trine. Notes that this association is found in many charts, so magnitude depends on freedom from functional-malefic affliction, an orb of about 6 degrees, no combustion, debilitation or bad avastha, and the dasa-varga amsa count.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, house-rulership section p. 162
source_views.view: Combinations of trine and quadrant lords, especially the 9th with the 10th, create Raja Yoga when well placed and usually only when the planet does not rule other bad houses.

yoga/raja_kendra_trikona.disagreements: BPHS 34.11-12 counts placement alone (a trine lord in an angle or vice versa) as yoga. Laghu Parashari, Raman and PVR require an actual relation (conjunction, exchange or aspect) and grade the mutual-angle and mutual-trine kinds as weaker. On blemished lords, BPHS 34.15 says an angle or trine lord that also owns an evil house gives no yoga by mere relation. Laghu Parashari sl. 15 allows the yoga if only one of the pair is blemished. Raman (HJH) says the strong pairs overcome 'slight' blemish. On orb, Raman allows 12 degrees and PVR about 5-6 degrees; the classics give none.
yoga/raja_kendra_trikona.phrasing_guidance: Present it as potential for rising responsibility and recognition, not guaranteed power or wealth. Because many charts have some kendra-trikona link, mention it only when the planets are strong and close, and tie it to the dashas of those planets.

definitions.definition: Kendra lord and trikona lord in exchange, or both in a kendra or a trikona, or the trikona lord in a kendra or the kendra lord in a trikona, or in full mutual aspect.
Any relationship between an angular lord and a trinal lord. Santhanam lists exchange, mutual aspect, conjunction, mutual angles and mutual trines.
4th or 10th lord joined with the 5th or 9th lord. Or the 5th lord in the 1st, 4th or 10th together with the 9th or lagna lord.

definitions.source: Laghu Parashari Raja Yoga ch. sl. 14-17 (Verma)
definitions.definition: Relationship between kendra and trikona lords, unblemished by other evil lordships, or with only one of them blemished. Best when the 10th lord or 9th lord is involved.
Lords of a kendra and a kona conjoined in an auspicious bhava (named Sankha; the 9th+10th case is named Raja yoga).
Kendradhipati associated with Trikonadhipati. The 9th-10th, 4th-5th, 7th-5th, 10th-5th, 4th-9th and 7th-9th pairs are singled out as powerful.
Lord of a quadrant and lord of a trine conjoined, in mutual graha drishti, or in parivartana. Lagna may count as either.

cancellations.condition: An angular or trinal lord that also owns an evil house gives no yoga by mere relation (Santhanam's note: the moolatrikona lordship decides).
9th and 10th lords also owning the 8th or 11th: the person does not enjoy the yoga (Verma extends this to all kendra/trikona lords owning the 8th/11th).
cancellations.source: Laghu Parashari Raja Yoga ch. sl. 22 (Verma)

cancellations.condition: Arudha Lagna and Dara Pada in mutual 6/8 or 2/12: poverty, with the horoscope's Raja Yogas not giving their effects.

Two or more of Mars, Saturn, Jupiter or Sun debilitated with one in lagna while the Moon is in Scorpio; weak Moon in certain gandanta navamsas unaspected; all malefics in angles in debility or enemy signs with benefics in 6/8/12; Vargottama lagna unaspected; Aquarius rising with three planets debilitated; four planets debilitated, combust or in enemy signs with no benefic in an angle or with the Moon.
Five planets debilitated; three or more debilitated (even an emperor's son begs); five planets in enemy signs or combust while neither luminary is exalted.

Yoga planets in planetary war, losing lustre or strength; weak Moon in deep debilitation; Sun in deep fall (10th degree of Libra) or Sun singly in deep fall; Kemadruma with Moon unaspected; Venus in debilitation navamsa.
Saravali says the stronger of the Raja Yoga and its obstruction prevails.
Leo lagna with Saturn exalted but in a debilitated navamsa or aspected by benefics; Sun at deep debilitation. Raman doubts the Sun's fall alone destroys all Raja Yogas.
Raja Yoga works only when stronger than the Raja-bhanga yogas present; lords of Arudha Lagna and Arudha of the 12th conjoined gives a fall from position (Rajabhrashta).
A Kemadruma yoga nullifies a Raja yoga.
cancellations.source: Jataka Parijata 7.82 (via the translator's table of contents only)

yoga/raja_kendra_trikona.rarity_and_weight: Common. PVR (11.7.2) says the conjunction of a quadrant lord and a trine lord is found in many charts and its magnitude depends on strength and closeness. Raman (HJH) gives it substantial effect only within 12 degrees. In 300 Combinations, Raman says a merely theoretical Raja Yoga is of no consequence. Laghu Parashari and BPHS 41.29-34 grade it by the planets' strength and divisional dignity. Weight: moderate by default; high only when the lords are strong, close, unblemished and involve the 9th/10th lords.
yoga/raja_kendra_trikona.timing: Laghu Parashari (Verma sl. 18-19, 34): greatly auspicious results come in the dasa and bhukti of the yogakaraka planets. Related inauspicious planets give mixed results in their bhuktis. Results start in the dasa of one yoga lord and the bhukti of a related planet; if the yoga starts in a maraka's bhukti, it brings recognition more than real gain. Phaladeepika 20.54: in a yogakaraka's dasa, Raja Yoga begins in the bhuktis of the karaka planets and is increased by malefic bhuktis that follow. Raman (300 Combinations, Introduction): the stronger of the two yoga planets fulfils most of the yoga in its own dasa and the weaker as sub-lord. Jataka Parijata 7.66 note: Raja Yogas fructify in the dasa/antardasa of the lord or occupant of the lagna or 10th.
yoga/raja_kendra_trikona.phases: Laghu Parashari (Verma, sl. 34 note): when a planet is both yogakaraka and maraka, its dasa gives the yoga in the auspicious bhuktis first and the maraka evils later, at the end of the maraka bhukti.

yoga/yogakaraka.summary: A yogakaraka is a single planet that rules both an angle and a trine from the lagna. It is a Raja Yoga in itself: Venus for Capricorn and Aquarius, Saturn for Taurus and Libra, Mars for Cancer and Leo. Its strength and placement decide how much status and prosperity its periods bring.
common_outcomes: fame, honour, financial prosperity and success in the periods of the yogakaraka when it is strong (Raman HJH)
the planet acts as the chart's most reliable functional benefic
rare_outcomes: kingly status when the yogakaraka is also linked to another trine lord (Laghu Parashari sl. 20: 'what better yoga than this')

by_area.career: Status and recognition through the houses the yogakaraka rules (Raman HJH p. 9-10).
by_area.finance: Financial prosperity (Raman HJH); BPHS 34 Taurus note: Saturn 'will bestow kingly status'.

strengtheners: Strength by Shadbala, association, aspect and occupation (Raman HJH).
Relation to another trine lord (Laghu Parashari sl. 20).
Placement in an angle or trine (BPHS 34.13 counts this as 'specially' yogakaraka).
Raman's unit method (300 Combinations Introduction): one positive unit each for being a benefic lord, joined by a benefic lord, aspected by a benefic lord, and being in exaltation or a friendly sign.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Debilitation, combustion and similar states leave a planet 'dispossessed of strength' and unable to confer auspiciousness (Verma, Laghu Parashari sl. 20 note).
Raman's negative units: joined or aspected by malefic lords, in debilitation or an enemy sign.
BPHS 34.19-22 (Aries): Jupiter's good is lost if he is 'at the disposal of a malefic'. This principle is applied there to trine lords generally.
yoga/yogakaraka.lagna_or_context_notes: From what BPHS 34 says for the lagnas read in Santhanam's edition: Taurus, Saturn causes Raja Yoga (34.23-24). Cancer, Mars confers a full-fledged yoga (34.27-28). Virgo, Venus with Mercury produces yoga (34.31-32). Libra, Saturn and Mercury are auspicious (the Raja Yoga pair is partly illegible in the scan; 34.33-34). Scorpio, the Sun and Moon are yogakarakas (34.35-36). Sagittarius, the Sun and Mercury confer yoga (34.37-38). Capricorn, only Venus gives a superior yoga (34.39-40). Aquarius, Venus is the only Raja Yoga planet (34.41-42). Pisces, Mars and Jupiter cause yoga (34.43-44). Raman HJH lists the single-planet yogakarakas: Mars for Cancer and Leo, Saturn for Taurus and Libra, Venus for Capricorn and Aquarius.

source_views.source: BPHS 34.13 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: A planet that owns both a trine and an angle, or one that is placed in an angle or a trine, becomes specially a yogakaraka.

source_views.source: BPHS 34.14, 34.2-7 notes (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: A malefic owning an angle becomes auspicious only if it also owns a trine. Santhanam calls Saturn for Libra the 'unsullied yogakaraka'. He says the luminaries, owning one sign each, are exempt from this rule.

source_views.source: BPHS 34.17 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Rahu or Ketu in an angle associated with or aspected by a trinal lord, or in a trine associated with an angular lord, becomes a yogakaraka.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.52-54 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Rahu and Ketu in a kendra or trikona connected with the lord of one of these become yogakarakas. In a yogakaraka's dasa, the Raja Yoga begins with the bhuktis of the karaka planets.

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari Raja Yoga ch. sl. 18-21 (tr. Verma)
source_views.view: Yogakaraka dasas and bhuktis give great auspiciousness. A planet owning a kendra and a trikona is a yogakaraka; related to another trikona lord it gives the highest yoga, related to a further kendra lord less so. A yogakaraka's strength can override the blemish of a related trine lord that also owns the 8th. Rahu and Ketu can act as yogakarakas.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1 pp. 9-10
source_views.view: Yogakarakas confer fame, honour, dignity, financial prosperity, political success and reputation. Only Mars, Saturn and Venus can own both a kendra and a trikona. The extent depends on Shadbala, association, aspect and occupation.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Bhavartha Ratnakara (tr.) ch. 1
source_views.view: Gives lagna-by-lagna yogas. For example, for Aries the 4th and 5th lords (Moon, Sun) give Raja Yoga, while Jupiter and Saturn (9th, 10th) do not.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 13.2
source_views.view: The planet owning a quadrant and a trine becomes a yogakaraka; a table per lagna is given.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers p. 162
source_views.view: For some ascendants one planet alone produces Raja Yoga: Saturn for Gemini and Libra, Venus for Capricorn and Aquarius, Mars for Cancer and Leo. For Aries and Scorpio the Sun and Moon combine to do so.

yoga/yogakaraka.disagreements: Frawley lists Saturn as the single yogakaraka for Gemini, but for Gemini Saturn rules the 8th and 9th, not an angle. BPHS 34.25-26 names only Venus as auspicious for Gemini, and Raman's HJH list omits Gemini. BPHS 34.13 also counts any planet merely placed in an angle or trine as specially yogakaraka, which is much broader than the ownership definition of Raman and PVR. For Taurus, BPHS classes Venus (lagna and 6th lord) as a malefic; Santhanam notes that Susloka Sataka disagrees.
yoga/yogakaraka.phrasing_guidance: Describe the yogakaraka as the chart's most supportive planet, whose periods tend to bring growth and recognition in proportion to its strength. Do not promise wealth or power, and say plainly when the planet is weak or afflicted.

definitions.definition: One planet ruling both a trine and an angle, or a planet placed in an angle or trine (specially yogakaraka).
Rahu/Ketu in an angle related to a trinal lord or in a trine related to an angular lord.
A planet owning both a kendra and a trikona: Mars (Cancer, Leo), Saturn (Taurus, Libra), Venus (Capricorn, Aquarius).
The same planet owning a kendra and a trikona.
Planet owning a quadrant and a trine.

cancellations.condition: Debilitated, combust or otherwise weak: cannot confer auspiciousness.

Raman says that when negative units (malefic lord, malefic association or aspect, debilitation or enemy sign) predominate, the planet gives no evil but also less good. Equal positive and negative units practically neutralise the yoga.

yoga/yogakaraka.rarity_and_weight: Structural: half the lagnas have a single-planet yogakaraka (Cancer, Leo, Taurus, Libra, Capricorn, Aquarius per Raman HJH), so its presence is fixed by the lagna and says nothing by itself. Its weight comes from its strength and placement (Raman HJH; Laghu Parashari).
yoga/yogakaraka.timing: Dasas and bhuktis of the yogakaraka (Laghu Parashari sl. 18). Phaladeepika 20.54 says that within the yogakaraka's dasa, results begin in the bhuktis of the karaka planets. Laghu Parashari sl. 34 says a yogakaraka does not give its yoga results in its own bhukti of its own dasa (Verma's note).

conditional_results.when: manual: the yogakaraka is debilitated, combust or in an enemy sign
conditional_results.source: Laghu Parashari sl. 20 note (Verma); Raman 300 Combinations Introduction

yoga/dharma_karmadhipati.summary: The link between the 9th lord (dharma, fortune) and the 10th lord (karma, action) is the best of the kendra-trikona Raja Yogas. They may be joined, exchange signs, aspect each other, or occupy the 9th/10th. It brings righteous success, fortune and status, provided neither planet also owns the 8th or 11th.
common_outcomes: wealth, happiness and prosperity (Uttara Kalamrita 4.3)
high position and recognition (Uttara Kalamrita 4.4; Raman HJH)
sincere, devoted, righteous and fortunate nature (PVR)
rare_outcomes: kingship 'extolled by his people' when the 9th and 10th lords exchange (Phaladeepika 7.9)
a ruler amassing great wealth when the 9th-10th pair is strong and related (Uttara Kalamrita 4.4)

by_area.personality: Sincere, devoted and righteous (PVR 11.7.1).
by_area.career: Rise through one's own work and dharma; the 10th is the strongest kendra and the 9th the strongest kona (P.S. Sastri, note on UK).
by_area.finance: Wealth and prosperity (UK 4.3). With the 2nd lord also joined, much wealth and many vehicles (Jataka Parijata 7.21).
by_area.spirituality: Righteous conduct (PVR); the 9th as dharma (P.S. Sastri note).

strengtheners: Both lords strong. Uttara Kalamrita 4.4 requires them to 'possess strength'.
Also associated with the lords of the 1st, 4th, 5th or 7th, or placed in those houses (Uttara Kalamrita 4.3).
Also associated with the 2nd lord, which adds wealth (Jataka Parijata 7.21).
Close conjunction or aspect (PVR 11.7.2).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Either lord also owning the 8th or 11th (UK 4.3; Laghu Parashari sl. 22).
Combustion: in the UK translator's example chart, lords set within 5-6 degrees of the Sun reduce the result (Sareen, ex. 7).
yoga/dharma_karmadhipati.lagna_or_context_notes: For Aries, Jupiter (9th/12th) and Saturn (10th/11th) do not form this yoga in practice (BPHS 34.19-22; Bhavartha Ratnakara ch. 1 st. 4; Laghu Parashari sl. 22 per Vinayaka Sastri as quoted by Verma). BPHS 34.25-26 says the same Jupiter-Saturn conjunction for Gemini behaves as for Aries. For Taurus, Saturn alone owns both houses and is the yogakaraka. Uttara Kalamrita 4.4 also reckons the 9th/10th lords from the 9th and 10th houses, giving middling and lower grades.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita 4.3 (tr. S.S. Sareen; also P.S. Sastri)
source_views.view: Raja Yoga forms when the 9th and 10th lords are in their own houses, conjoined in either house, exchanged, or in mutual aspect. Associated with the lords of the 5th, 7th, 1st or 4th, or occupying those houses, they give wealth, happiness and prosperity. Neither may also own the 8th or 11th.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita 4.4 (tr. Sareen)
source_views.view: The 9th/10th lords reckoned from the lagna, from the 9th, and from the 10th give, in order, high, ordinary and below-average position. When related by conjunction, exchange or aspect and strong, or in mutual kendras, the native amasses wealth and rules.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.37-38 and 7.9 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: The 9th and 10th lords conjoined in an auspicious bhava constitute Raja Yoga: a king with elephants, conveyances and royal honours. The 10th lord in the 9th and the 9th lord in the 10th gives a king extolled by his people.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.21 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: The 10th and 9th lords conjoined with the 2nd lord make one wealthy. The same pairs reckoned from the 9th and 10th, in exchange or mutual-aspecting kendras with the 2nd lord, do too. If the 4th lord or karaka is also connected, much wealth and many vehicles follow.

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari sl. 16, 22 (tr. Verma)
source_views.view: The 9th and 10th lords in each other's houses, together in one of them, or one in the other's house aspected by its dispositor gives great auspiciousness. The yoga is lost if they also own the 8th/11th.

source_views.source: BPHS 39.37 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: The 10th lord joining the 9th lord gives kingdom (one of four kendra-trikona joinings listed).

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, HJH vol. 1 p. 10
source_views.view: The most powerful Raja Yoga comes from the 9th and 10th lords associating. Their exchange makes each a Rajayogakaraka, as does the 9th lord in the 10th or the 10th lord in the 9th, or their full mutual aspect.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach 11.7.1
source_views.view: Names it Dharma-Karmadhipati Yoga, a special case of the basic Raja Yoga between the strongest trine and the strongest quadrant. The native is sincere, devoted, righteous and fortunate.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology (PDF p. 95)
source_views.view: Rath uses the name for the 9th-lord-10th-lord link even in a divisional chart (D-24), reading it as excellent for higher education there.

yoga/dharma_karmadhipati.disagreements: On which relations count: Uttara Kalamrita and Raman include own-house placement and mutual aspect. Phaladeepika 6.37 requires conjunction in a good bhava. Laghu Parashari sl. 16 includes the case of one lord in the other's house aspected by its dispositor. Uttara Kalamrita alone adds the reckoning from the 9th and 10th houses as lesser grades.
yoga/dharma_karmadhipati.phrasing_guidance: Frame as alignment between one's sense of purpose and one's work, which tends to bring steady recognition. Avoid predicting fame or office; mention the dashas of the 9th and 10th lords as the likely windows.

definitions.definition: 9th and 10th lords in own houses, or conjoined in the 9th or 10th, or exchanged, or in mutual aspect; neither owning the 8th or 11th.
9th and 10th lords conjoined in an auspicious bhava.
10th lord in the 9th and 9th lord in the 10th (exchange).
9th and 10th lords in the 10th and 9th, or together in one of these, or one in the other's house aspected by its dispositor.
9th and 10th lords associated, exchanged, one in the other's house, or in full mutual aspect.
9th and 10th lords conjoined, in mutual graha drishti, or in parivartana.

cancellations.condition: Either lord also owns the 8th or 11th house.
Aries lagna: the Jupiter-Saturn conjunction does not produce yoga.

yoga/dharma_karmadhipati.rarity_and_weight: Less common than kendra-trikona links in general, since it needs the two specific lords related. Raman (HJH) calls it the most powerful Raja Yoga, and Laghu Parashari sl. 17 calls it the best combination. Uttara Kalamrita 4.4 grades it by reference point and strength.
yoga/dharma_karmadhipati.timing: Dashas and bhuktis of the 9th and 10th lords (Laghu Parashari sl. 18 as for yogakarakas). The UK example chart shows a Mercury-Saturn period giving difficulty when the lords are combust (Sareen).

yoga/parivartana.summary: Parivartana is a mutual exchange of signs: planet A sits in a sign of planet B while B sits in a sign of A. Phaladeepika counts 66 possible exchanges between house lords. It divides them into Maha (28, good houses), Khala (8, involving the 3rd lord) and Dainya (30, involving the 6th, 8th or 12th lords), whose results range from wealth and authority to misfortune.
common_outcomes: Maha: prosperity, authority, gifts from rulers, vehicles, wealth and children (Phaladeepika 6.34)
Khala: fluctuating fortune, sometimes prosperous and sometimes in distress (Phaladeepika 6.33)
Dainya: foolishness, enemies, harsh speech, obstacles in undertakings (Phaladeepika 6.33)
rare_outcomes: rulership from an exchange of the 4th and 10th lords when both are very strong and in Gopuramsa (Raman HJH 4th house)
Maha Raja Yoga from exchange of the lagna and 5th lords (BPHS 39.6-7)

by_area.personality: Dainya: unsteady mind and harsh speech (PD 6.33). Khala: alternately astray and gentle (PD 6.33).
by_area.career: Maha: authority conferred by the sovereign (PD 6.34). An exchange of the 10th and lagna lords gives close association with rulers (BPHS 40.13).
by_area.finance: Maha: wealth, gold ornaments and gifts (PD 6.34). An exchange of the 2nd with the 5th or 11th lord brings financial prosperity in those dashas (Raman HJH 2nd house). The 2nd-11th exchange is a very powerful Dhana yoga (BPHS vol. 2, translator's note to ch. 48).

strengtheners: Both planets strong; Raman (HJH) mentions Gopuramsa for the 4th-10th exchange.
Exchange between kendra and trikona lords counts as Raja Yoga (BPHS 34.11-12; 41.28; PVR 11.7.1).
Frawley (p. 181) says an exchange can integrate the planets' power more than each simply being in its own sign.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Involvement of the 6th, 8th or 12th lord (Dainya) or the 3rd lord (Khala) (Phaladeepika 6.32-33).
Exchange of the 2nd and 12th lords is a yoga for poverty (Frawley p. 181).
yoga/parivartana.lagna_or_context_notes: Which kind forms is a property of the two houses involved, counted from the lagna. Rath (Crux) notes that in an exchange each planet gives the results of the other: in his chart 38, Saturn gives Mars's results. Rath also shows an exchange protecting a house (the lagna lord in the 6th exchanging with the 6th lord, chart 14).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.32 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Two bhava lords occupying each other's houses is Parivartana. There are 66 such exchanges: 30 involve the 6th, 8th and 12th lords (Dainya), 8 the 3rd lord (Khala), and the remaining 28 are Maha. Sastri enumerates each set.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.33-34 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Dainya natives are foolish, revile others, are tormented by enemies, wounding in speech, unsteady, with interrupted undertakings. Khala natives alternate between going astray and gentleness, prosperity and distress. Maha natives are blessed by Sri, wealthy, given authority, gifts, vehicles and children.

source_views.source: BPHS 39.6-7 and 40.13 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Exchange of the lagna and 5th lords is a Maha Raja Yoga, making one famous and happy. Exchange of the 10th and lagna lords associates the native greatly with the king.

source_views.source: BPHS 34.11-12 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: An exchange between an angular and a trinal lord is the first of the Raja Yoga forms.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7, notes to sl. 21 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: The note lists 12 named yogas from relationships between the lords of successive houses (1st-2nd through 12th-1st). It counts sign exchange as one of the four kinds of relationship.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, HJH vol. 1, Fourth House p. 161 and Second House p. 95
source_views.view: Parivartana between the 4th and 10th lords gives lands, or even rulership if they are very strong (Gopuramsa). Exchange of the 4th and 6th lords gives lands from enemies. Exchange of the 2nd and 5th or 2nd and 11th lords gives financial prosperity in their periods.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology (PDF pp. 41, 79, 113)
source_views.view: An exchange makes each planet give the other's results. An exchange between the lagna lord in the 6th and the 6th lord in the lagna causes Raja Yoga and removes the bad effects of the lagna lord in the 6th. Rath also uses exchange to alter counting direction in the Saptamsa.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers pp. 173, 181
source_views.view: Sign exchange is a complete connection (sambandha) like a mutual full aspect, akin to Western mutual reception, and among the most powerful connections. Planets exchanging signs can produce stronger effects than the same planets in their own signs. Many yogas require exchange.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach 11.7.1
source_views.view: Parivartana is one of the three associations (with conjunction and graha drishti) that link a kendra and a trikona lord into Raja Yoga.

yoga/parivartana.disagreements: Phaladeepika labels every exchange touching the 6th, 8th or 12th lord as Dainya, with bad results. Rath reads a lagna-6th exchange as a Raja Yoga that removes the 6th-house harm (chart 14). Frawley treats exchange as generally strengthening. Raman's 4th-6th exchange gives lands from enemies rather than misery.
yoga/parivartana.phrasing_guidance: Explain an exchange as two areas of life becoming closely tied, each planet acting for the other. Say which kind (Maha, Khala or Dainya) it is from the houses involved. Avoid harsh language for Dainya; say it points to effort and obstacles around the dusthana matters.

definitions.definition: Two bhava lords each occupying the other's house; 66 possible pairs.
Exchange between any two of the lords of 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10, 11 (28 pairs).
Exchange of the 3rd lord with the lord of 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10 or 11 (8 pairs).
Any exchange involving the lord of the 6th, 8th or 12th (30 pairs).
Two planets each in a sign ruled by the other (e.g. Jupiter in Aries, Mars in Pisces).

yoga/parivartana.rarity_and_weight: Phaladeepika's count: 28 of the 66 possible exchanges are Maha, 8 Khala and 30 Dainya. Frawley rates exchange among the most powerful connections. Weight depends on the houses involved and the planets' strength (Raman HJH).
yoga/parivartana.timing: Raman (HJH) times the 2nd-5th and 2nd-11th exchanges to the periods and sub-periods of those lords. Rath reads results through the exchanged planets' periods and dasas (e.g. Mars-Venus exchange in the D-16, Crux PDF p. 87).

yoga/dhana.summary: Dhana yogas are links among the wealth houses: the 2nd (wealth), 11th (gains), 5th and 9th (fortune) and the lagna. The classic form joins the 2nd and 11th lords with the 5th and 9th lords. These yogas promise wealth in proportion to the strength of the planets involved.
common_outcomes: earning and accumulating wealth (Bhavartha Ratnakara ch. 2)
financial prosperity in the periods of the linked lords (Raman HJH)
rare_outcomes: great affluence when the 5th and 11th lords are in their own houses in specific lagna-wise forms (BPHS 41.2-8; Raman 300 nos. 118-122)
immense wealth when the lagna lord in its own sign in the lagna is joined or aspected by certain planets (BPHS 41.9-15; Raman 300 nos. 123-128)

by_area.finance: The core area: earnings, savings and gains. Uttara Kalamrita 4.5 links the 2nd and 11th lord pair to affluence and wealth.

strengtheners: The 2nd and 11th lords combined with the 5th and 9th lords rather than with other lords (Bhavartha Ratnakara ch. 2 st. 3-4).
Lords in own, friendly or exaltation signs (Uttara Kalamrita 4.5).
Strength and favourable disposition of the participating planets (BPHS 41.17; PVR 11.9).
A strong 11th house (PVR 11.9).
weakeners_or_cancellations: 2nd and 11th lords combined with the 12th lord: much wealth is not acquired (Bhavartha Ratnakara ch. 2 st. 5).
2nd lord with the 12th lord gives only ordinary prosperity in the 2nd lord's dasa (Raman HJH 2nd house).
Lords of the lagna, 4th and 9th in the 8th, or the 5th lord in the 8th, give financial losses in their periods (Raman HJH 2nd house).
yoga/dhana.lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS 41.2-15 gives lagna-specific forms: the 5th lord in the 5th with the 11th lord or specific planets in the 11th, and the lagna lord in the lagna joined or aspected by specific planets. Raman (300 nos. 118-128) and PVR (11.9) list them per lagna. Raman notes the same form gives the same degree of wealth but from different sources depending on which lords are involved (no. 119).

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara ch. 2 st. 1-8 (tr. B.V. Raman)
source_views.view: Lists the wealth combinations: exchange of the 2nd and 5th or 2nd and 11th lords; the 5th lord in the 5th and the 9th lord in the 9th; the 2nd and 11th lords combined with the 5th and 9th lords. If the 2nd and 11th lords join lords other than the 5th and 9th, only modest wealth follows. Combined with the 12th lord, much wealth does not come. Jupiter with the 2nd lord and Mercury, the lords of the 11th, 1st and 2nd in their own houses, and the 2nd and 11th lords in the lagna are also listed. Raman notes that the majority of horoscopes fall in the modest-wealth category.

source_views.source: BPHS 41.16-17 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: The 9th and 5th lords, and planets conjunct them, bestow wealth in their dasas. All wealth yogas must be weighed by the strength and disposition of the planets involved.

source_views.source: BPHS 41.2-15 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Specific combinations: the 5th lord in its own sign in the 5th with the 11th lord or other named planets in the 11th gives great riches (2-8). The lagna lord in its own sign in the lagna, joined or aspected by named planets, makes one wealthy (9-15).

source_views.source: BPHS 39.18 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: One of the Moon, Jupiter, Venus or Mercury exalted in the 2nd makes one wealthy.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita 4.5 (tr. Sareen)
source_views.view: Among four pairs of lords, the 2nd and 11th lords, related by conjunction, exchange or mutual aspect and in friendly, own or exaltation signs, give affluence and wealth.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.21 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: The 10th and 9th lords conjoined and associated with the 2nd lord (and the same pairs counted from the 9th and 10th) make one wealthy.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, HJH vol. 1, Second House pp. 94-95
source_views.view: Wealth should be predicted only when other strong Dhana yogas exist. Financial prosperity comes in the periods of the 2nd and 5th or 2nd and 11th lords in exchange, or of the 5th and 9th lords in their own houses. The 2nd lord with the 12th gives ordinary prosperity.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations nos. 118-128
source_views.view: Raman reproduces the BPHS 5th/11th and lagna-lord wealth forms, noting that all fortify the 5th and 11th houses and that their strength varies by lagna.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach 11.9
source_views.view: Basic principle: the 5th and 9th lords and planets joining them give money in their dasas. The 11th and 2nd houses are also important. Strength of the participating planets decides the magnitude.

yoga/dhana.disagreements: The calculator's '1/2/5/9/11 lords' rule matches no single classical verse exactly. Bhavartha Ratnakara st. 3 centres the 2nd and 11th lords with the 5th and 9th. BPHS 41 centres the 5th and 9th lords and adds lagna-specific forms. Uttara Kalamrita 4.5 pairs the 2nd and 11th lords alone. Jataka Parijata 7.21 ties wealth to the 9th-10th lords plus the 2nd lord. Inclusion of the lagna lord comes from BR st. 7 (lords of 11, 1 and 2 in their own houses) and BPHS 41.9-15.
yoga/dhana.phrasing_guidance: Speak of capacity to earn and build resources, which shows most in the periods of the lords involved. Never promise riches; Bhavartha Ratnakara itself says most charts get modest rather than great wealth.

definitions.definition: Lords of the 2nd and 11th combined with the lords of the 5th and 9th.
2nd-5th or 2nd-11th lord exchange; 5th lord in the 5th and 9th lord in the 9th; lords of 11, 1 and 2 in their own houses; 2nd and 11th lords in the lagna.
The 5th and 9th lords and planets conjunct them give wealth.
2nd and 11th lords together, exchanged or in mutual aspect, in a friendly, own or exaltation sign.
9th and 10th lords conjoined with the 2nd lord.
5th and 9th lords and planets joining them; with a strong 11th and 2nd.

cancellations.condition: 2nd and 11th lords combined with lords other than the 5th and 9th: only modest wealth.
2nd and 11th lords combined with the 12th lord.
Planets involved unfavourably disposed or weak.

yoga/dhana.rarity_and_weight: Common in some form. Raman's note to Bhavartha Ratnakara ch. 2 st. 4 says the majority of horoscopes have the weaker form that gives humble wealth. Raman (HJH) warns not to predict wealth unless other strong Dhana yogas exist. The lagna-specific BPHS forms are much rarer and stronger.
yoga/dhana.timing: Dasas of the 5th and 9th lords and planets conjunct them (BPHS 41.16; PVR 11.9). Periods and sub-periods of the 2nd-5th or 2nd-11th exchanging lords, and of the 5th and 9th lords in their own houses (Raman HJH).

yoga/lakshmi.summary: Lakshmi Yoga (named after the goddess of wealth) needs a strong 9th lord in its own, moolatrikona or exaltation sign in an angle (or a trine in some texts) and a strong lagna lord. Phaladeepika gives a variant requiring the 9th lord and Venus in such signs. It promises wealth, virtue, good looks, reputation and high standing.
common_outcomes: wealth and comforts (Raman 300 no. 27)
good character, reputation and attractive appearance (BPHS 36.27-28)
rare_outcomes: 'a king of kings' ruling many lands (Jataka Parijata 7.153)
immense wealth when the 9th lord and Venus are both in own or exaltation signs in kendras or trikonas (Raman's grading of the Phaladeepika form)

by_area.personality: Charming, virtuous, of high moral merit (BPHS 36.27-28); learned and of high integrity (Raman).
by_area.career: Kingly status, a good ruler (BPHS; Raman); protects his people (Phaladeepika 6.24).
by_area.finance: Abundant wealth (BPHS); 'predominantly to do with wealth' (Raman).
by_area.health: Free from disease (Phaladeepika 6.24).
by_area.relationships: Phaladeepika 6.24 pictures him ever sporting with an amiable damsel. Jataka Parijata 7.153 gives numerous wives and sons.
by_area.family: Many sons (BPHS 36.27-28; Jataka Parijata 7.153).
by_area.spirituality: Blessed by the goddess of wealth (Phaladeepika 6.24).

strengtheners: Strength of the lagna lord, Venus and the 9th lord (Raman).
Other Dhana yogas present (Raman).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Raman: the lagna and 9th lords associated in the 3rd, 6th or 8th do not form even the ordinary type.
yoga/lakshmi.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman says the strong form is rare, but in almost every horoscope with any claim to wealth some form of Lakshmi Yoga is found.

source_views.source: BPHS 36.27-28 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: The 9th lord is in an angle identical with its moolatrikona, own or exaltation sign, and the lagna lord is strong. The native is charming, virtuous, kingly, with many sons, abundant wealth, fame and high moral merit.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.21, 6.24 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: The 9th lord and Venus are in their own or exaltation houses identical with a trikona or kendra. The native is healthy, wealthy and brilliant, protects his people, is blessed by the goddess of wealth, rides in palanquins, and is the best of kings and liberal.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.152-153 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: The 9th lord is in a kendra identical with its moolatrikona, and the lagna lord is in exaltation with abundant strength. The native is a king of kings, virtuous, ruling many lands, learned and handsome, with many wives and sons.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 27
source_views.view: Definition: a powerful lagna lord with the 9th lord in own or exaltation sign in a kendra or trikona. Raman lists variants and grades the 9th lord plus Venus form as the most powerful. The lagna and 9th lords associated or in mutual aspect outside the 3rd, 6th and 8th gives an ordinary type. Strong forms are rare, but some form is common in wealthy charts.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach 11.6
source_views.view: The 9th lord in own or exaltation sign in a quadrant and a strong lagna lord: becomes a king, good-looking, of good character, wealthy, with many children, principled and famous.

yoga/lakshmi.disagreements: On the 9th lord's dignity: BPHS accepts moolatrikona, own or exaltation; Jataka Parijata requires moolatrikona; Phaladeepika accepts own or exaltation. On location: BPHS and JP require a kendra, while Phaladeepika and Raman accept a kendra or trikona. On the second factor: BPHS and PVR need a strong lagna lord, JP needs the lagna lord exalted, and Phaladeepika needs Venus in its own or exaltation sign instead. Raman's ordinary type (mere lagna-9th lord association) is his own grading.
yoga/lakshmi.phrasing_guidance: Speak of good fortune, resources and a graceful life that tend to grow when the 9th lord's period runs. Avoid promising riches or many children.

definitions.definition: 9th lord in a kendra identical with its moolatrikona, own or exaltation sign, and lagna lord strong.
9th lord and Venus in their own or exaltation signs identical with a kendra or trikona.
9th lord in a kendra identical with its moolatrikona, and lagna lord exalted and very strong.
Lagna lord powerful and 9th lord in own or exaltation sign in a kendra or trikona.
9th lord in own or exaltation sign in a quadrant, and lagna lord strong.

cancellations.condition: Raman's ordinary type fails if the lagna and 9th lords are associated in the 3rd, 6th or 8th.

yoga/lakshmi.rarity_and_weight: Raman says a really strong Lakshmi Yoga is rare and then gives full results, but some weaker form is found in almost every horoscope with any claim to wealth. Weight: high if the strict BPHS/JP form holds.
yoga/lakshmi.timing: Raman's example (Chart 27): the 9th lord's (Mars) dasa brought wealth and reputation. Generally the 9th lord's and lagna lord's periods (Raman's Introduction method).

yoga/saraswati.summary: Saraswati Yoga (named after the goddess of learning) forms when Jupiter, Venus and Mercury occupy angles, trines or the 2nd house, with Jupiter in its own, exaltation or friendly sign. It promises learning, eloquence, literary or artistic skill, fame and wealth.
common_outcomes: high intelligence and learning (Phaladeepika 6.27)
skill in composition, poetry, accounts or exposition of texts (Phaladeepika 6.27)
fame and wealth (Raman 300 no. 161)
rare_outcomes: fame 'over the three worlds' and respect from the best of kings (Phaladeepika 6.27)

by_area.personality: Highly intelligent and clever (PD 6.27); praised by all (Raman).
by_area.career: Poet, writer or scholar, skilled in prose, verse, drama and accounts, respected by rulers (PD 6.27; Raman).
by_area.finance: Exceedingly wealthy (PD 6.27); rich (Raman).
by_area.relationships: Endowed with wife and children (PD 6.27); a good wife and children (Raman).
by_area.family: Good children (Raman).
by_area.spirituality: Skilled in exposition of sacred texts (PD 6.27).

strengtheners: Jupiter strong: own, exaltation or friendly sign and 'possessing strength' (PD 6.26).
All three planets strong (Raman).
weakeners_or_cancellations: If the planets are weak, the yoga merges with other, more powerful yogas (Raman).
yoga/saraswati.lagna_or_context_notes: Because Mercury and Venus stay close to the Sun, the three often fall in the allowed houses together. Raman calls the yoga not rare.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.26-27 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Venus, Jupiter and Mercury occupy a kendra, a trikona or the 2nd, with Jupiter strong in its exaltation, own or a friendly sign. The native is highly intelligent; skilled in drama, prose, verse, accounts, poetics and exposition of sacred texts; famous, very wealthy, with wife and children, fortunate and respected by kings.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 161
source_views.view: Jupiter, Venus and Mercury occupy the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 5th, 7th, 9th or 10th, jointly or severally, with Jupiter in own, exaltation or friendly sign. The native is a poet, famous, learned, skilled, rich and praised, with a good wife and children. Not rare; if the planets are strong it is prominent, otherwise it merges with stronger yogas.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach 11.6
source_views.view: Each of Mercury, Jupiter and Venus is in a quadrant, a trine or the 2nd (not necessarily together), with Jupiter in an own, friendly or exaltation sign. The native is very learned, skilful, intelligent, rich, famous and praised.

yoga/saraswati.disagreements: Only small differences: Raman lists the houses explicitly (1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10), which matches kendra + trikona + 2nd. Phaladeepika adds that Jupiter must 'possess strength'. Not found in Santhanam's BPHS yoga chapters, in Saravali, or in Jataka Parijata ch. 7 (as read), so classical support here rests on Phaladeepika.
yoga/saraswati.phrasing_guidance: Describe an aptitude for learning, expression and the arts that rewards study. Avoid promising fame; Raman notes the yoga is common and depends on strength.

definitions.definition: Venus, Jupiter and Mercury in a kendra, trikona or the 2nd, with Jupiter in exaltation, own or friendly sign and strong.
Jupiter, Venus and Mercury in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 5th, 7th, 9th or 10th, jointly or severally, with Jupiter in own, exaltation or friendly sign.
Each of Mercury, Jupiter, Venus in a quadrant, trine or the 2nd, with Jupiter in own, friendly or exaltation sign.

yoga/saraswati.rarity_and_weight: Raman: 'not a rare one'. It is prominent only when the planets are strong and otherwise merges with more powerful yogas.

yoga/vasumati.summary: Vasumati Yoga forms when benefics occupy the upachaya houses (3, 6, 10, 11) from the lagna or the Moon. It is a yoga of independence and steady wealth: more benefics there means more wealth.
common_outcomes: commands plenty of money (Phaladeepika 6.20)
not dependent on others (Raman 300 no. 9)
rare_outcomes: very great wealth when all benefics are in upachayas (BPHS 37.6; Saravali 13.32)

by_area.personality: Independent, not a dependent (Raman). 'Always keeps to his house' (Phaladeepika 6.20).
by_area.finance: Plenty of wealth. All three benefics give much, two give medium and one gives little (BPHS 37.6; Saravali 13.32).

strengtheners: More benefics in upachayas (BPHS 37.6; Saravali 13.32).
Upachayas that are the benefics' exaltation signs (Raman).
Counting from the lagna rather than the Moon (Raman: the lagna form seems more influential).
Strong benefics with no malefics in the upachayas (PVR).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Upachayas that are the benefics' debilitation signs (Raman).
Benefics there associated with or aspected by malefics (Raman).
Malefics occupying upachayas (PVR).
yoga/vasumati.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman notes that counted from the Moon, all four upachayas cannot hold benefics because only three benefics remain. He also says Varahamihira held that Vasumati predictions do not fail.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 6.19-20 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: All the benefics occupy upachaya houses reckoned from the lagna or the Moon. The native keeps to his house and commands plenty of money.
