rising_sign/gemini.summary: Gemini rising is classically read as a quick, sociable, talkative and pleasure-loving person, good at reading others, fond of music and learning, but restless and changeable. Venus (5th lord) is the one clearly good planet; Mars, Jupiter and the Sun are counted as difficult; there is no single-planet yogakaraka.
common_outcomes: Clever, quick-witted, fond of reading, writing and talk (HJH; Frawley).
Liking for music and dance (PD 9.3); voluptuous and fond of relatives (JP 9.105).
Skilled at reading others' thoughts (PD 9.3).
Nervous, restless and changeable; can exhaust itself (HJH; Frawley).
rare_outcomes: Jataka Parijata 9.105: exceedingly prosperous, contemplative and philosophical, but ailing.
Bhavartha Ratnakara (Mithuna st. 10): Mercury in the 11th brings misunderstandings with the eldest brother.
Frawley p. 118: tends to marry more than once.

by_area.personality: Dark eyes, curly hair, raised nose, home-keeping, playful (PD 9.3); compassionate, worthy, contemplative, liked by the good (JP 9.105); wavering mind, ingenious, vivacious, inconsistent (HJH); restless, adaptable, articulate, can be unreliable or tricky (Frawley p. 118).
by_area.career: Experts in mechanical sciences, conversation and literature, best in active work (HJH); writers, journalists, secretaries, programmers, scientists (Frawley p. 118).
by_area.finance: Venus, Mars and the Moon in the 2nd give wealth in Venus dasa (BR Mithuna st. 2); the Moon and Mars in the 11th with Saturn in the 9th give strong Dhana Yoga (st. 8); Mars and Saturn in the 2nd with the Moon in the 8th lose wealth in their periods (st. 5-6).
by_area.health: Ailing (JP 9.105); prone to sudden nervous breakdown (HJH); weak but active, can be hypersensitive (HJH; Frawley).
by_area.relationships: Sporting with women (PD 9.3); voluptuous (JP 9.105); should be careful with the opposite sex (HJH); mobile in relationships, may marry more than once (Frawley p. 118).
by_area.family: Fond of relatives (JP 9.105); home-keeping (PD 9.3); misunderstanding with the eldest brother if Mercury is in the 11th (BR Mithuna st. 10).
by_area.spirituality: Knows the real nature of the world and spirit, contemplative (JP 9.105); can become quite spiritual once seeking inner knowledge (Frawley p. 119).

strengtheners: Venus with Mercury gives Raja Yoga (LP Gemini notes; HPA); Venus with Saturn in good signs gives a distinguished career (HPA).
The Sun and Mercury in the 3rd make Mercury give yoga in its period (BR Mithuna st. 1).
Saturn's 9th lordship (moolatrikona) outweighs its 8th lordship (Santhanam's notes on BPHS 34.2-7); Saturn-Mercury links give Raja Yoga (Verma).
Santhanam suggests a Saturn-Jupiter exchange between the 9th and 10th could be favourable for Gemini (his own view, note on BPHS 34.25-26).
The lagna is strong when occupied or aspected by its own lord, Jupiter or Mercury, and not by other planets (Brihat Jataka 1.19).
Whatever a sign gives as lagna is also given, in a lesser way, when the Moon occupies it (Phaladeepika 9.13); the lagna and Moon should be read together.
Raman: the sign delineations hold for an empty lagna; planets in the 1st, the strength of the lagna lord and aspects on the lagna modify them (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Jupiter and Saturn together give the same poor result as for Aries (BPHS 34.25-26; LP; HPA).
Mars, 6th and 11th lord, is the most malefic (HJH; Santhanam).
Jupiter as owner of two kendras (7th and 10th) carries kendradhipatya dosha and maraka status (Verma's LP notes).
Raman: when the Sun, Moon and lagna are afflicted by more than one malefic, proneness to accidents is indicated (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25-26).
BPHS 34.45-46 (Santhanam): lordship-based roles are only a frame; a planet that forms a strong yoga (e.g. a Nabhasa yoga) gives that yoga's results despite its role for the lagna.
rising_sign/gemini.lagna_or_context_notes: Gemini is a biped (human) sign, which Brihat Jataka 1.17 counts as strong when it is the lagna. For Gemini, Jupiter owns two angles, so the classical 'benefic owning angles' blemish falls heavily on it.

rising_sign/cancer.summary: Cancer rising is classically read as sensitive, home- and family-centred, fond of good food, clothes and comfort, intelligent and frugal, with strong emotions. Mars (5th and 10th lord) is the yogakaraka; Jupiter and the Moon are also good; Venus and Mercury are counted as difficult.
common_outcomes: Sensitive, emotional, intuitive and receptive (HJH; Frawley).
Attached to home, family and friends; many houses or dwells in others' homes (PD 9.4; JP 9.105; HJH; Frawley).
Intelligent, industrious and frugal, sometimes to miserliness (PD 9.4; HJH).
Fond of water and of good food, clothes and ornaments (PD 9.4; JP 9.105).
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika 9.4: henpecked; short; crooked in views.
Bhavartha Ratnakara (Karkataka st. 6-7): Mercury, Venus and the Moon in the 11th, Jupiter in the lagna and Saturn in the 10th gives a kingly Maharaja Yoga.
Raman: often disappointed in love (HJH ch. IV).

by_area.personality: Intelligent, quick-walking, crooked in views (PD 9.4); soft voice, a mind inclined to fraud yet virtuous (JP 9.105); extremely sensitive, inquisitive, restless, frugal, honest and unbending, loves justice (HJH); friendly, caring, nurturing, may be shy or dependent (Frawley p. 119).
by_area.career: Suits occupations of a fluctuating nature (HJH); can gain social or political influence through sensitivity to the masses (Frawley p. 119).
by_area.finance: Rich, with many houses (PD 9.4); Mars, Jupiter and the Moon in the 2nd with Sun and Venus in the 5th give wealth (BR Karkataka st. 4); Sun and Mars in the 10th make one rich (st. 8).
by_area.health: Fleshy neck, short stature, bulky (PD 9.4; JP 9.105).
by_area.relationships: Henpecked (PD 9.4); disappointments in love affairs (HJH); values intimate exchange of feeling (Frawley).
by_area.family: Surrounded by friends, few sons (PD 9.4); deeply attached to family and children (HJH); loves home and family, sometimes narrowly (Frawley p. 119).
by_area.spirituality: Psychic tendencies (HJH); devotional bent when opening to the spiritual life (Frawley p. 119).

strengtheners: Mars, owner of the 5th and 10th, gives full yoga (BPHS 34.27-28; LP; HJH; HPA; PVR; BR Karkataka st. 2).
Mars with Jupiter gives Raja Yoga (LP; HPA); Mars with the Moon or Jupiter in houses 1, 5, 9 or 10 gives reputation (HPA).
The Moon in the lagna with Jupiter, or with Mars in Capricorn, Saturn in Libra or the Sun in Aries gives Raja Yoga (BR Karkataka st. 10-13).
Venus in the 12th or 2nd gives yoga (BR Karkataka st. 3); Mercury and Venus in the 12th give Raja Yoga in Venus dasa (st. 9); Mercury and Venus in the 5th make Mercury give yoga (st. 5).
The lagna is strong when occupied or aspected by its own lord, Jupiter or Mercury, and not by other planets (Brihat Jataka 1.19).
Whatever a sign gives as lagna is also given, in a lesser way, when the Moon occupies it (Phaladeepika 9.13); the lagna and Moon should be read together.
Raman: the sign delineations hold for an empty lagna; planets in the 1st, the strength of the lagna lord and aspects on the lagna modify them (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Jupiter, though 9th lord, gives no special yoga; Raman says its period mixes career gains with debts, disease and enemies (BR Karkataka st. 1 and notes).
The Sun's dasa brings loss of wealth if the Moon and Mars are in the lagna, the Sun and Mercury in the 4th and Venus in the 11th (BR Karkataka st. 14-15).
Jupiter with Venus, or Jupiter with Saturn, are spoilt combinations (Verma).
Raman: when the Sun, Moon and lagna are afflicted by more than one malefic, proneness to accidents is indicated (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25-26).
BPHS 34.45-46 (Santhanam): lordship-based roles are only a frame; a planet that forms a strong yoga (e.g. a Nabhasa yoga) gives that yoga's results despite its role for the lagna.
rising_sign/cancer.lagna_or_context_notes: For movable lagnas the 11th lord is a strong malefic: Venus for Cancer (Santhanam's note on BPHS 34.27-28). The Moon as lagna lord is the least of the three benefics (Mars, Jupiter, Moon) in Santhanam's ranking.

rising_sign/leo.summary: Leo rising is classically read as proud, brave and commanding, quick to anger, drawn to forests, hills and travel, and able to overcome enemies and charm rulers. Mars (4th and 9th lord) is the yogakaraka and the best planet; the Sun and Jupiter are also good; Mercury, Venus and Saturn are counted as difficult.

by_area.family: Few sons (JP 9.106); obedient to the mother (PD 9.5); may hold children too tightly (Frawley p. 120).

strengtheners: Mars, owning the 4th and 9th, is the best planet (BPHS 34.29-30; LP; HJH; HPA; PVR; Frawley).

Whatever a sign gives as lagna is also given, in a lesser way, when the Moon occupies it (Phaladeepika 9.13); the lagna and Moon should be read together.

weakeners_or_cancellations: Jupiter with Venus does not give good results and can destroy yoga (BPHS 34.29-30; LP; HPA; BR Simha st. 4).

Saturn, 6th and 7th lord and enemy of the Sun, is adverse (Santhanam; Verma).
Raman: when the Sun, Moon and lagna are afflicted by more than one malefic, proneness to accidents is indicated (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25-26).
BPHS 34.45-46 (Santhanam): lordship-based roles are only a frame; a planet that forms a strong yoga (e.g. a Nabhasa yoga) gives that yoga's results despite its role for the lagna.

rising_sign/virgo.summary: Virgo rising is classically read as modest, truthful, kind-spoken and learned, skilled in many kinds of work, discriminating and prudent, with few children. Mercury and Venus are the good planets and together give yoga; Mars, Jupiter and the Moon are counted as difficult; there is no single-planet yogakaraka.
common_outcomes: Learned and skilled in various works, interprets scriptures (PD 9.6; JP 9.106).
Truthful and kind in speech, modest (PD 9.6; JP 9.106).

Few children (PD 9.6).

Bhavartha Ratnakara (Kanya st. 3-4): the Moon and Venus in the 7th, Jupiter in the 11th and the Sun in Aries give several wives in the periods of Jupiter and Venus (Raman: read today as a romantic life).

by_area.personality: Truthful, kind-spoken, modest look (PD 9.6); skilled, prosperous, talented, sound judgment, fond of relations, sincere (JP 9.106); impulsive, emotional, fond of learning and the arts, lacking self-confidence, methodical, shrewd (HJH); discriminating, exacting, orderly, service-minded (Frawley pp. 120-121).

by_area.finance: Respectability through others' houses and wealth (PD 9.6); prosperous (JP 9.106); the Sun linked to Venus or the Moon gives wealth in Sun dasa, followed by loss in Venus dasa (BR Kanya st. 1-2); Saturn in the 11th gives good results in its period (st. 6).
by_area.health: Nervous breakdown or paralysis if afflicted (HJH); weakest physically of the signs, nervous digestion, chronic disorders (Frawley p. 121; Virgo shares sixth-house traits, p. 162).
by_area.relationships: Fond of sexual enjoyment (PD 9.6); delights in the company of women (JP 9.106); shy when young (Frawley p. 121).
by_area.family: Very few children (PD 9.6); fond of relations (JP 9.106).
by_area.spirituality: Knows the meaning of the shastras (PD 9.6); suited to philosophies of purity and detachment such as Vedanta (Frawley p. 121).

The Sun does well when joined to good planets in good houses, e.g. with Mercury in the 10th (Santhanam's note).
The lagna is strong when occupied or aspected by its own lord, Jupiter or Mercury, and not by other planets (Brihat Jataka 1.19).

weakeners_or_cancellations: Jupiter rules two angles (4th and 7th) and is a strong maraka in the 7th (Verma's LP note).
Saturn's 6th lordship (moolatrikona) makes it less reliable despite owning the 5th (Santhanam; Frawley p. 160).
Venus loses its good results if linked with the Sun (BR Kanya st. 2 and Raman's note).
Raman: when the Sun, Moon and lagna are afflicted by more than one malefic, proneness to accidents is indicated (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25-26).
BPHS 34.45-46 (Santhanam): lordship-based roles are only a frame; a planet that forms a strong yoga (e.g. a Nabhasa yoga) gives that yoga's results despite its role for the lagna.
rising_sign/virgo.lagna_or_context_notes: Virgo is a biped sign, strong as lagna (Brihat Jataka 1.17). Mercury rules both the lagna and the 10th, so its strength matters doubly.

rising_sign/libra.summary: Libra rising is classically read as good-looking, refined and fond of pleasure, clever in trade and argument, honoured by rulers, yet sometimes timid or irresolute; Raman and Frawley stress idealism, love of justice and influence over people. Saturn (4th and 5th lord) is the yogakaraka; Mercury is also good; Jupiter, the Sun and Mars are counted as difficult; Venus is neutral.
common_outcomes: Handsome, with a lovely face and eyes (JP 9.107; HJH).
Clever in trade, impartial in argument (PD 9.7).
Honoured by rulers; learned (JP 9.107).
Idealistic, loves justice and order, can sway masses (HJH; Frawley).
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika 9.7: has two names.
Jataka Parijata 9.107: front teeth set apart; irresolute and very timid.
Bhavartha Ratnakara (Thula st. 15): Saturn, Jupiter, Mercury and Mars in Aquarius with Rahu in the 10th give pilgrimages in Rahu dasa.

by_area.personality: Lean, tall, wandering, brave yet merciless, impartial in argument (PD 9.7); calm and pensive but irresolute and timid (JP 9.107); idealistic, quick-witted, forceful, keen observer, not easily moved by reason, loves truth (HJH); sense of harmony and justice, reformer, idealist, charismatic (Frawley p. 121).
by_area.career: Clever in trading (PD 9.7); political leaders and religious reformers with great influence over masses (HJH); leaders, generals, administrators, artists working for social change (Frawley p. 121).
by_area.finance: Possesses women, wealth and lands (JP 9.107); the Sun, Venus and Mercury in the lagna give fortune and wealth (BR Thula st. 8); Mercury, Saturn and Venus in the lagna, or the Moon and Mars in the 7th, give riches in Mercury dasa (st. 9-10).
by_area.health: Lean and frail body (PD 9.7); Jupiter linked with Venus (or both in Saturn's or Mars' signs or aspected by them) brings pox, wounds or similar troubles in their joint periods (BR Thula st. 3-4).
by_area.relationships: Fond of love's pleasures (JP 9.107); sensual disposition (HJH); charismatic, values beauty around them, less concerned with home and family (Frawley p. 121).
by_area.family: Limited number of children (PD 9.7). The Sun and Mercury in the 12th aspected by Saturn: father fortunate but lives to middle age (BR Thula st. 5).
by_area.spirituality: Worships gods and Brahmins (PD 9.7); can transcend the world through love of truth (Frawley p. 121).

strengtheners: Saturn, lord of the 4th and 5th, gives Raja Yoga (BPHS 34.33-34; LP; HJH; HPA; PVR; BR Thula st. 1; Frawley).
The Moon with Mercury gives Raja Yoga (BPHS 34.33-34; LP variant; HPA).
Saturn in the lagna with the Moon in Cancer gives Raja Yoga (BR Thula st. 14); Jupiter in the 8th, Saturn in the 9th, Mars and Mercury in the 10th give a strong Raja Yoga (st. 11).
Mars or the Sun linked to Saturn, Mercury or Venus can turn helpful (Santhanam's note; BR Thula st. 6-7).
Venus is good only in the lagna or the 8th (Verma, citing Pt. Rama Yatna Ojha).
The lagna is strong when occupied or aspected by its own lord, Jupiter or Mercury, and not by other planets (Brihat Jataka 1.19).
Whatever a sign gives as lagna is also given, in a lesser way, when the Moon occupies it (Phaladeepika 9.13); the lagna and Moon should be read together.
Raman: the sign delineations hold for an empty lagna; planets in the 1st, the strength of the lagna lord and aspects on the lagna modify them (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Jupiter, lord of the 3rd and 6th, is the dire malefic (Santhanam; HJH; PVR).
Jupiter, Mars and the Sun linked together but not to Saturn, Mercury or the Moon are more malefic (Santhanam).
Venus in the lagna can act as a maraka (BR Thula st. 13) [maraka: text predicts danger to life / death].
Raman: when the Sun, Moon and lagna are afflicted by more than one malefic, proneness to accidents is indicated (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25-26).
BPHS 34.45-46 (Santhanam): lordship-based roles are only a frame; a planet that forms a strong yoga (e.g. a Nabhasa yoga) gives that yoga's results despite its role for the lagna.
rising_sign/libra.lagna_or_context_notes: Libra is a movable sign: the 11th lord (the Sun) is a strong malefic for movable lagnas (Santhanam). Frawley notes Libra is sometimes called the best ascendant for worldly influence, because Saturn becomes a Raja Yoga planet and the main malefic is Jupiter (p. 161). Libra is a biped sign, strong as lagna (Brihat Jataka 1.17).

Jupiter: dire malefic in most, but Bhavartha Ratnakara and some cited by Frawley allow it to give good results. Moon: Raja Yoga partner with Mercury (BPHS, LP, HPA) vs malefic (HJH).
rising_sign/libra.phrasing_guidance: Describe the rising sign as a tendency, not a fixed fate; blend it with planets in the 1st house, the lagna lord and the Moon sign. Name functional roles plainly (e.g. 'Saturn tends to work in your favour') and never turn maraka lore into a death or illness prediction; skip old caste, gender and fidelity stereotypes from the classical lists.

rising_sign/scorpio.summary: Scorpio rising is classically read as intense, proud, sharp-eyed and forceful, able to endure, often meeting early illness or separation from parents and teachers, and capable of harsh action yet honoured by rulers. The Sun and Moon (10th and 9th lords) are the yogakarakas and Jupiter is good; Mercury, Venus and Saturn are counted as difficult; Mars is neutral.
common_outcomes: Forceful, proud and fiercely willed (JP 9.108; HJH; Frawley).
Broad eyes and chest, round thighs and knees (PD 9.8).
Early-life illness and separation from parents or teachers (PD 9.8).
Interest in the occult and hidden things (HJH; Frawley).
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika 9.8: lotus marks on hands and feet; honoured by the sovereign.
Jataka Parijata 9.108: long-lived and wealthy.
Raman: liable to piles (HJH).

by_area.personality: Cruel looks, very fickle, proud, learned, hostile to good men, pensive (JP 9.108); does cruel acts but honoured by the ruler (PD 9.8); sarcastic, impulsive, subtle mind hard to influence, generous, fond of excitement and contest (HJH); intense, secretive, perceptive, passionate (Frawley p. 122).
by_area.career: Soldiers, police, athletes, chemists, surgeons, researchers (Frawley p. 122); enterprising, good writers, conversationalists, can master music and fine arts (HJH).
by_area.finance: Wealthy (JP 9.108); Jupiter and Mercury joined or in mutual aspect give much wealth (BR Vrischika st. 1); Jupiter and Mercury in the 5th with the Moon in the 11th give great fortune (st. 4).
by_area.health: Illness early in life (PD 9.8); long-lived (JP 9.108); hot constitution, piles (HJH).
by_area.relationships: Passionate and attached (Frawley p. 122); a woman born under Scorpio is described as masculine in nature (HJH).
by_area.family: Separated from parents and teachers (PD 9.8).
by_area.spirituality: Drawn to occult study (HJH); depth psychology, Tantra and Yoga, can develop profound insight (Frawley p. 122). Jupiter in the 3rd gives a charitable disposition (BR Vrischika st. 2).

strengtheners: The Sun (10th lord) and the Moon (9th lord) are yogakarakas, especially in exchange or joined in the 9th or 10th (BPHS 34.35-36; LP; HPA; Verma; Frawley p. 161).
Jupiter and Mercury joined or in mutual aspect give wealth (BR Vrischika st. 1).
The Sun, Mercury and Venus in the 7th give fame and power in Mercury dasa (BR Vrischika st. 2-3); Jupiter, the Moon and Ketu in the 9th give power in Jupiter dasa (st. 5).
Saturn becomes practically auspicious in the 5th or 9th (Santhanam's note).
The lagna is strong when occupied or aspected by its own lord, Jupiter or Mercury, and not by other planets (Brihat Jataka 1.19).
Whatever a sign gives as lagna is also given, in a lesser way, when the Moon occupies it (Phaladeepika 9.13); the lagna and Moon should be read together.
Raman: the sign delineations hold for an empty lagna; planets in the 1st, the strength of the lagna lord and aspects on the lagna modify them (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mercury, 8th and 11th lord, is wholly evil (Verma); Venus, 7th and 12th lord, carries kendradhipatya dosha and maraka status (Verma).
Mars with Jupiter is a spoilt combination per Verma, as Jupiter takes on the 6th lord's blemish.
Raman: when the Sun, Moon and lagna are afflicted by more than one malefic, proneness to accidents is indicated (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25-26).
BPHS 34.45-46 (Santhanam): lordship-based roles are only a frame; a planet that forms a strong yoga (e.g. a Nabhasa yoga) gives that yoga's results despite its role for the lagna.
rising_sign/scorpio.lagna_or_context_notes: Scorpio as lagna carries some eighth-house tendencies (Frawley p. 162). Santhanam cites Susloka Sataka that the 6th lordship does not taint Mars for Scorpio.

rising_sign/sagittarius.summary: Sagittarius rising is classically read as eloquent, generous, favoured by rulers and strong against enemies, the best of the family, with fame and wealth; moderns add a principled, religious and philosophical bent. The Sun and Mars are the good planets and the Sun with Mercury gives yoga; Venus is the chief malefic.
common_outcomes: Wise, eloquent and liberal in giving (PD 9.9; JP 9.108).
Favoured by rulers; overcomes enemies (PD 9.9).
Best of the family, prosperous, famous (JP 9.108).
Religious, philosophical, honest and principled (HJH; Frawley).
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika 9.9: long face and neck, large ears and nose, short stature; won over only by kindness.
Bhavartha Ratnakara (Dhanus st. 4): Mars and Sun in Aquarius with Rahu in Leo give a sea-bath in Rahu dasa.
Raman: in later years careful about lungs and rheumatic pains (HJH).

by_area.personality: Intent on his work, eloquent, generous, strong, won by kindness (PD 9.9); wise, best of the family (JP 9.108); philosophical, humane, impulsive, enterprising, conventional, honest, hates show (HJH); positive, generous, principled, can be dogmatic or self-righteous (Frawley pp. 122-123).
by_area.career: Favourite of the king (PD 9.9); business-like and prompt (HJH); lawyers, religious leaders, businessmen (Frawley p. 123).
by_area.finance: Possessing fame and wealth (JP 9.108); Saturn in the 5th or 11th gives yoga in its period, the 11th only for this lagna (BR Dhanus st. 1-2); Sun and Venus in the 9th with Saturn in the 3rd give fame and wealth in Saturn dasa (st. 3).
by_area.health: Tends to corpulence; lungs and rheumatic pains in later years (HJH).
by_area.relationships: Strict control over relations with the opposite sex (HJH); finds it hard to settle down (Frawley p. 123).
by_area.family: The best of the family (JP 9.108); can inherit from father or family (Frawley p. 123).
by_area.spirituality: Inclined to philosophy and occult study, God-fearing (HJH); keeps a higher aspiration, attracted to religion (Frawley p. 123).

strengtheners: The Sun (9th lord) with Mercury (10th lord) gives yoga (BPHS 34.37-38; LP); Santhanam: still better if they join.
Mars with Jupiter is greatly auspicious (Verma; HPA); Mars gives mainly 5th house results (Santhanam).
The Moon with Jupiter can give an excellent yoga (Santhanam's note).
Saturn in the 5th or 11th gives yoga (BR Dhanus st. 1-2).
The lagna is strong when occupied or aspected by its own lord, Jupiter or Mercury, and not by other planets (Brihat Jataka 1.19).
Whatever a sign gives as lagna is also given, in a lesser way, when the Moon occupies it (Phaladeepika 9.13); the lagna and Moon should be read together.
Raman: the sign delineations hold for an empty lagna; planets in the 1st, the strength of the lagna lord and aspects on the lagna modify them (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Venus, 6th and 11th lord, is the chief malefic (BPHS; LP; HJH; HPA; PVR).
Mars with Mercury is a spoilt combination (Verma).
The Moon as 8th lord cannot be a strong yogakaraka unless well linked to Mercury, the Sun or Mars (Santhanam).
Raman: when the Sun, Moon and lagna are afflicted by more than one malefic, proneness to accidents is indicated (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25-26).
BPHS 34.45-46 (Santhanam): lordship-based roles are only a frame; a planet that forms a strong yoga (e.g. a Nabhasa yoga) gives that yoga's results despite its role for the lagna.
rising_sign/sagittarius.lagna_or_context_notes: Mercury owns two angles here (7th and 10th) yet BPHS counts it capable of yoga with the Sun; Santhanam explains this by the 10th being Mercury's moolatrikona sign. Sagittarius' first half is a biped sign, strong as lagna (Brihat Jataka 1.17).

rising_sign/capricorn.summary: Capricorn rising is classically read as hard-working, persistent and strong-willed, finishing what it starts, practical and ambitious, though sometimes lazy, shameless or prone to wind complaints. Venus (5th and 10th lord) is the yogakaraka and Mercury is good; Mars, Jupiter and the Moon are counted as difficult.
common_outcomes: Carries through what he undertakes; great strength or courage (PD 9.10).
Persevering, industrious, ambitious, starts slowly and succeeds over time (HJH; Frawley).
Weak lower limbs, prone to wind disorders (PD 9.10).
Fortunate (PD 9.10).
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika 9.10: a religious hypocrite; attached to older women; devoid of shame.
Jataka Parijata 9.108: perfidious, speaks dejectedly.
Bhavartha Ratnakara (Makara st. 4-5): Venus and Mercury in the lagna with the Moon in the 5th aspected by Jupiter gives an emperor-like Maharaja Yoga.

by_area.personality: Courageous, completes tasks, indolent, fortunate, always on the move (PD 9.10); speaks dejectedly (JP 9.108); stoical, sympathetic, generous, strong in purpose, secretive, vindictive when Saturn is afflicted, talkative (HJH); hard-working, tenacious, ambitious, shrewd, traditional (Frawley p. 123).
by_area.career: Capable of great endeavour, industrious (HJH); business, science, technology, mathematics (Frawley p. 123).
by_area.finance: Access to conveyances (BR Makara st. 7, which Raman calls vague); Saturn and Mercury in the 9th give fortune (st. 9); Jupiter in the lagna with Venus and Mars in the 11th gives money through brothers in Jupiter dasa (st. 6); cannot economise, likes show (HJH).

by_area.relationships: Fond of women (PD 9.10; JP 9.108); perfectionist at home, may not get on with the spouse (HJH).

strengtheners: Venus, owner of the 5th and 10th, is the only planet capable of a superior yoga (BPHS 34.39-40; LP; HJH; HPA; PVR; Frawley).
Venus with Mercury gives special yoga (LP; HPA); Mercury in the 10th with Venus in the 9th is a Dharma-Karmadhipati yoga (Verma).
Venus in the 5th is good (BR Makara st. 3); the Moon in Cancer with Mars in Capricorn gives Raja Yoga (st. 10); Rahu in the 12th with Jupiter becomes a yogakaraka (st. 9).
Mercury (6th and 9th lord) gives yoga for Capricorn because its 9th lordship is joined with its exaltation (BR Karkataka st. 1 and Raman's note).
The lagna is strong when occupied or aspected by its own lord, Jupiter or Mercury, and not by other planets (Brihat Jataka 1.19).
Whatever a sign gives as lagna is also given, in a lesser way, when the Moon occupies it (Phaladeepika 9.13); the lagna and Moon should be read together.
Raman: the sign delineations hold for an empty lagna; planets in the 1st, the strength of the lagna lord and aspects on the lagna modify them (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Venus in the 10th gives no yoga because of kendra lordship by a benefic (BR Makara st. 3 and Raman's note).
Mars, 4th and 11th lord, is the worst malefic (HJH; Santhanam).
Mars with Mercury, and the Moon with Mercury, are spoilt combinations (Verma).
Raman: when the Sun, Moon and lagna are afflicted by more than one malefic, proneness to accidents is indicated (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25-26).
BPHS 34.45-46 (Santhanam): lordship-based roles are only a frame; a planet that forms a strong yoga (e.g. a Nabhasa yoga) gives that yoga's results despite its role for the lagna.
rising_sign/capricorn.lagna_or_context_notes: For movable lagnas the 11th lord (Mars for Capricorn) is a strong malefic (Santhanam). Saturn as lagna lord also owns the 2nd but is said not to kill on its own (BPHS; LP).

rising_sign/capricorn.phrasing_guidance: Describe the rising sign as a tendency, not a fixed fate; blend it with planets in the 1st house, the lagna lord and the Moon sign. rising_sign/aquarius.summary: Aquarius rising is classically read harshly - secretive, covetous, careful with money, with fluctuating gains and losses - while Raman and Frawley describe a reserved, humanitarian, intelligent person suited to teaching, writing and service. Venus (4th and 9th lord) is the yogakaraka and Saturn is good; Jupiter, the Moon and Mars are counted as difficult.
common_outcomes: Reserved, sympathetic and helpful to others (HJH; Frawley).
Fluctuating gains and losses; careful or miserly with money (PD 9.11; JP 9.109).
Endures long journeys (PD 9.11).
Shines as teacher, writer, speaker (HJH).
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika 9.11: body shaped like a water-pot; fond of perfumes and flowers.
Raman: setbacks that can affect reputation unless other factors help (HJH).
Bhavartha Ratnakara (Kumbha st. 6): the Sun, Mercury and Jupiter in the 3rd give political power through the Sun.

by_area.personality: Secretly does wrong, covetous, uses others' wealth (PD 9.11); crafty, miserly (JP 9.109); reserved, peevish when provoked but quick to calm, generous, very sympathetic, intelligent, good memory, sometimes timid (HJH); self-effacing, humanitarian, may be eccentric (Frawley p. 124).
by_area.career: Teachers, writers, lecturers, astrology, upholders of causes (HJH); religious leaders and teachers rather than political leaders (Frawley p. 124); Frawley notes Aquarius is sometimes called the worst ascendant for fame and charisma (p. 162).
by_area.finance: Limited means, gains and losses (PD 9.11); master of much wealth (JP 9.109). Venus and Saturn in the 11th give yoga in Venus dasa (BR Kumbha st. 5).
by_area.health: Colic and chest pain (HJH); a weak chest if Saturn is in the 4th (HJH).
by_area.relationships: Fond of other men's wives (JP 9.109); devoted to the spouse, needs a happy home or health suffers, family happiness not sufficient (HJH).
by_area.family: Insufficient happiness in family life (HJH).
by_area.spirituality: Frawley: often called the best sign for spiritual growth, capable of surrender to the Divine (pp. 124, 162).

strengtheners: Venus, owner of the 4th and 9th, is the only Raja Yoga planet (BPHS 34.41-42; LP; HJH; HPA; PVR; Frawley).
Venus with Mars (9th and 10th lords) gives Raja Yoga (LP; HPA); best if Venus is in the 10th and Mars in the 9th (Verma). Raman holds the 9-10 combination works in practice (BR notes).
Venus in the lagna, the Sun in the 10th and Rahu in Aquarius give yoga in Rahu and Jupiter dasas (BR Kumbha st. 2).
Jupiter aspecting the 2nd and Saturn aspecting the lagna (each its own house) help finances in both periods (Raman's note on BR Kumbha st. 4).
The lagna is strong when occupied or aspected by its own lord, Jupiter or Mercury, and not by other planets (Brihat Jataka 1.19).
Whatever a sign gives as lagna is also given, in a lesser way, when the Moon occupies it (Phaladeepika 9.13); the lagna and Moon should be read together.
Raman: the sign delineations hold for an empty lagna; planets in the 1st, the strength of the lagna lord and aspects on the lagna modify them (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Bhavartha Ratnakara (Kumbha st. 1): the mere combination of the 9th and 10th lords gives no particular yoga.
The Sun and Mars in the 8th bring sorrow in their periods (BR Kumbha st. 3); Jupiter in the lagna with Saturn in the 2nd gives mixed results in Jupiter dasa and none in Saturn's (st. 4).
Saturn as lagna lord also owns the 12th, so it is weaker in the 12th (Verma; Frawley p. 162).
Raman: when the Sun, Moon and lagna are afflicted by more than one malefic, proneness to accidents is indicated (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25-26).
BPHS 34.45-46 (Santhanam): lordship-based roles are only a frame; a planet that forms a strong yoga (e.g. a Nabhasa yoga) gives that yoga's results despite its role for the lagna.
rising_sign/aquarius.lagna_or_context_notes: Aquarius is a biped sign, strong as lagna (Brihat Jataka 1.17). Frawley calls Aquarius sometimes the worst ascendant for worldly fame because the lagna lord also owns the 12th, yet the best for spiritual growth (p. 162).

rising_sign/pisces.summary: Pisces rising is classically read as learned, grateful, kind to friends, fond of the spouse, fortunate and able to overcome enemies, with a well-proportioned body and good eyes; moderns add emotion, imagination, devotion and dependence on others. The Moon (5th lord) and Mars (2nd and 9th lord) are the good planets and Mars with Jupiter gives yoga; Saturn, Venus, the Sun and Mercury are counted as difficult.
common_outcomes: Learned, grateful, overcomes enemies, fortunate (PD 9.12; JP 9.109).
Well-proportioned shining body and very good eyes (PD 9.12).
Kind to friends and fond of the spouse (PD 9.12; JP 9.109).
Religious, devotional and sensitive (HJH; Frawley).
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika 9.12: gains by trading pearls and sea products; drinks much water.
Bhavartha Ratnakara (Meena st. 4): Jupiter in the 5th gives more daughters than sons.
Bhavartha Ratnakara (Meena st. 12-14): the Sun, Mercury, Venus, Jupiter and Saturn in their own signs and the Moon and Mars exalted form a great yoga, even if one or two are missing.

by_area.personality: Learned, grateful, kind to friends, spirited and strong (PD 9.12; JP 9.109); stubborn, psychically receptive, highly religious, stoical, reserved, just, lacking self-confidence (HJH); emotional, imaginative, impressionable, compassionate, may lack boundaries (Frawley pp. 124-125).
by_area.career: Gains from pearls and sea produce (PD 9.12); ambitious to rule over others but rarely realises it (HJH); good followers and promoters, musicians (Frawley p. 125). Jupiter, lord of the lagna and 10th, in the 10th gives Raja Yoga (BR Meena st. 11).
by_area.finance: Possesses much corn and wealth (JP 9.109); frugal (HJH); the Moon in the 2nd with Mars in the 5th gives wealth in Moon dasa (BR Meena st. 5); the Moon in the 12th loses wealth (st. 2).
by_area.health: Drinks water excessively (PD 9.12); sensitive digestion and nerves, emotional disorders, can depend on sugar or alcohol (Frawley p. 125).
by_area.relationships: Fond of his wife (PD 9.12); can become dependent or make others dependent (Frawley p. 125).
by_area.family: More daughters and few sons if Jupiter is in the 5th (BR Meena st. 4); generally dependent on others through life yet independent in spirit (HJH).
by_area.spirituality: Highly religious, God-fearing, rigid in observance (HJH); loves ceremony, ritual and devotion (Frawley p. 125).

strengtheners: Mars with Jupiter gives yoga (BPHS 34.43-44; LP); Mars with the Moon or Jupiter gives Raja Yoga (HPA).
Mars and Jupiter in exchange (9th and 10th) form a very powerful Raja Yoga; the Moon in the 10th with Jupiter exalted in the 5th is also powerful (Verma).
Saturn in the 12th is good (BR Meena st. 2); Mercury, Jupiter, the Moon and Mars in the 4th give kingly fame in their periods (st. 9-10).
The lagna is strong when occupied or aspected by its own lord, Jupiter or Mercury, and not by other planets (Brihat Jataka 1.19).
Whatever a sign gives as lagna is also given, in a lesser way, when the Moon occupies it (Phaladeepika 9.13); the lagna and Moon should be read together.
Raman: the sign delineations hold for an empty lagna; planets in the 1st, the strength of the lagna lord and aspects on the lagna modify them (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saturn, 11th and 12th lord, is the most harmful (Santhanam; Frawley p. 160).
Venus in the 12th gives no yoga for Pisces or Aquarius (BR Meena st. 1).
The yoga of Saturn in the 12th is reduced in the Moon's sub-period of Jupiter dasa (BR Meena st. 3).
Mars with Mercury, and Mercury with Jupiter, are spoilt combinations (Verma).
Raman: when the Sun, Moon and lagna are afflicted by more than one malefic, proneness to accidents is indicated (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IV, p. 25-26).
BPHS 34.45-46 (Santhanam): lordship-based roles are only a frame; a planet that forms a strong yoga (e.g. a Nabhasa yoga) gives that yoga's results despite its role for the lagna.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka ch. 1 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri) vv. 4-5, 10, 20
source_views.view: Pisces governs the feet; two fishes head to tail; rises both ways; counted among diurnal signs; white.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 9 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri) v. 12
source_views.view: Drinks much water, fine body, fond of wife, gains from sea produce, learned, grateful, conquers foes, fine eyes, fortunate.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 9 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri) v. 109
source_views.view: Learned, moderate in pleasures, kind to friends, spirited, rich in corn and wealth.

source_views.source: Laghu Parashari / Jataka Chandrika ch. 5 (tr. and notes O.P. Verma), Pisces vv. 71-72
source_views.view: Saturn, Venus, Sun and Mercury inauspicious; Mars and Moon auspicious; Mars and Jupiter together give yoga; Mars is a maraka who does not kill; Saturn and Mercury are marakas.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara ch. 1 (tr. and notes B.V. Raman, 2nd ed. 1947), Meena st. 1-14
source_views.view: Venus in the 12th gives no yoga; Saturn in the 12th is good; Moon in the 12th loses wealth; Jupiter in the 5th gives more daughters; Jupiter in the 10th gives Raja Yoga; planets in own and exaltation signs give a great yoga.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. II p. 13 and ch. IV p. 29
source_views.view: Moon and Mars benefic; Saturn, Sun, Venus, Mercury malefic; Jupiter neutral. Pisces rising: religious, reserved, frugal, just.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XVII (Key-Planets for Each Sign), pp. 134-137
source_views.view: The Moon and Mars auspicious, Mars most powerful; Mars with the Moon or Jupiter gives Raja Yoga; Saturn, Venus, Sun, Mercury evil; Mars does not kill as maraka.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, pp. 124-125, 160
source_views.view: Pisces types are emotional, devotional and impressionable; Saturn as 11th and 12th lord is very inauspicious for Pisces.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, sec. 13.2, Table 30
source_views.view: No yogakaraka; benefics Moon, Mars; neutral Jupiter; malefics Sun, Mercury, Venus, Saturn.

rising_sign/pisces.disagreements: Jupiter as lagna and 10th lord: very favourable in Santhanam's reading of BPHS but neutral in HJH and PVR. Mars as maraka: does not kill independently (BPHS, LP) or does not kill at all (HPA). Day/night strength: BPHS calls Pisces night-strong; Brihat Jataka counts it among diurnal signs.
rising_sign/pisces.phrasing_guidance: Describe the rising sign as a tendency, not a fixed fate; blend it with planets in the 1st house, the lagna lord and the Moon sign. Name functional roles plainly (e.g. 'Saturn tends to work in your favour') and never turn maraka lore into a death or illness prediction; skip old caste, gender and fidelity stereotypes from the classical lists.

karaka/atmakaraka.summary: The Atmakaraka is the planet with the highest degree within its sign; it stands for the self or soul and is the 'king' of the chart, whose condition colours the whole horoscope and governs bondage and liberation.
karaka/atmakaraka.determination: Rank the seven planets Sun to Saturn by degrees travelled within their own sign (sign ignored; ties broken by minutes, then seconds); highest = Atmakaraka, then Amatya, Bhratri, Matri, Putra, Gnati and lowest = Darakaraka (7-karaka scheme, the one the calculator uses). In the 8-karaka scheme Rahu is added (its degrees counted back from the end of its sign) and a Pitrikaraka (father) is inserted after the Matrikaraka, so every role below Matrikaraka can fall on a different planet. Sources: 7-karaka with Rahu only as a tie-filler - BPHS 32.1-2 first view, B. Suryanarain Rao, B.V. Raman, Prabhakara Murthy, K.N. Rao (via summary); 8-karaka - BPHS 32.1-2 second view and Santhanam's worked example, Abhyankar's text of Jaimini 1.1.10-18, P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Sanjay Rath (8 for living beings, 7 for mundane charts). The Atmakaraka is the highest-degree planet. Under the 7-karaka scheme it is always one of Sun to Saturn; under the 8-karaka scheme Rahu can be Atmakaraka when it is near the start of its sign.
significations: the native's self and soul (Jaimini 1.1.10-11 Abhyankar numbering; BPHS 32.3-8)
bondage and release - misery and happiness (Jaimini 1.1.11 Abhyankar / 1.1.12 B.S. Rao)
the main reference point for the karakamsa (its navamsa sign) and for raja yogas, sustenance and spiritual progress
common_outcomes: A strong, well-placed Atmakaraka lifts the whole chart; a weak one limits it (Raman art. 8; Murthy ch. 2).
If the Atmakaraka is favourable, the other karakas cannot impose their bad effects fully; if it is adverse, they cannot give their good effects fully (BPHS 32.9-12).
The planet's own nature describes the native's inner drive and the lesson the soul works on (Rath).
rare_outcomes: Rahu as Atmakaraka (8-karaka scheme only): Rath cites it in the charts of Srila Prabhupada and Ramakrishna; P.V.R. Narasimha Rao (8.2) says it can show a saint on one side or a revolutionary or outcast on the other.
Exalted Atmakaraka with only benefic influence is read by B. Suryanarain Rao as pointing to final liberation (moksha).

by_area.personality: Murthy ch. 2: Sun as AK - courageous and enduring; Moon - bright and adaptable; Mars - bold, adventurous; Mercury - intelligent, drawn to material gain; Jupiter - self-confident, ambitious; Venus - gentle, fond of comforts; Saturn - principled, hard-working, prospers later. Rath: Sun must overcome ego; Moon be caring; Mars avoid violence; Mercury keep speech truthful; Jupiter respect teachers and care for children; Venus keep clean character; Saturn share others' sorrows; Rahu stay guileless though often deceived.
by_area.career: Uttara Kalamrita ch. 4: the most-advanced planet joined by the Sun gives an adviser at court; by full Moon and Venus a wealthy scholar; by Mars a soldier, commander or metal-worker; by Mercury a sculptor or trader; by Jupiter one skilled in Vedic rites; by Saturn many activities; by Rahu/Ketu work with poisons or metals. PVR 11.8: AK and Amatyakaraka together make one a minister; AK in own or exaltation sign in a kendra or trikona aspecting the 9th lord is a further royal yoga. Abhyankar intro: Sun as AK makes one fit for government service.
by_area.health: Raman art. 129: the native is generally healthy if the AK is free of malefic conjunction and aspect; afflictions to the 6th from the AK's sign and from the karakamsa count more than those to the 6th from the lagna.
by_area.relationships: Murthy ch. 10: the elemental nature and mutual friendship of the Atmakaraka and Darakaraka show harmony between the spouses.
by_area.spirituality: Jaimini 1.1.11: the AK rules bondage and liberation. B.S. Rao: exalted or benefic-joined AK gives release, residence in holy places and moksha; debilitated or malefic-joined AK gives confinement and denies moksha unless benefics aspect. Rath: a malefic AK suggests a more advanced soul than a benefic one; a combust AK gives spiritual insight; a retrograde AK shows a deep-rooted desire behind the birth. PVR 14.3: the lord of the 8th from the AK (Maheswara) shows the channels through which the soul seeks liberation.

strengtheners: exaltation, moolatrikona, own or friendly sign (Murthy ch. 2; B.S. Rao on 1.1.12)
benefic conjunction or aspect (B.S. Rao on 1.1.12)
conjunction with the Putrakaraka or Amatyakaraka for raja yoga (PVR 11.7.3, 11.8; Murthy ch. 7)
benefics with the AK or in trines from it increase longevity class (kaksha vriddhi) (Raman art. 115)
weakeners_or_cancellations: debilitation, combustion or an inimical sign (Murthy ch. 2) - though Rath reads combustion of the AK as giving spiritual insight
malefic conjunction or aspect (B.S. Rao on 1.1.12; Raman art. 129)
karaka/atmakaraka.lagna_or_context_notes: Rath counts the sign of the AK from the navamsa lagna: 1st - noble standing, rise from humble birth if the navamsa lagna lord joins the AK; 2nd - deeply spiritual; 3rd - wealth and powerful friends; 4th - a karma yogi; 5th - dharmic and protected by the father's blessings; 6th - disease and trouble; 7th - clean heart and many joys; 8th - many troubles; 9th - pious and fortunate; 10th - a pillar of family; 11th - brave and successful; 12th - very rich. Raman art. 127: the 5th lord aspecting the AK gives high intelligence; the 4th lord aspecting it a happy life; the 12th lord aspecting it a spendthrift.
timing: Rath: the Vimshottari dasa of the AK often brings hardship, especially when the AK is a malefic, but can be helpful to spiritually inclined natives; the Narayana dasa of the AK's sign, or of signs aspecting it, brings major achievement.
Raman art. 112: Jaimini's third longevity method uses the stronger of the 8th lord from the AK and the 8th lord from the 7th from the AK; AK in the 9th from lagna swaps short and full life.
PVR 16.5.1: the Vimshottari period of an exalted planet in the 12th from the AK in the navamsa can bring serious thoughts of liberation.
PVR 14.3 / Raman art. 38: Maheswara, the 8th lord from the AK (with exceptions when Rahu or Ketu join it), is used in longevity and liberation analysis.
karaka/atmakaraka.karakamsa: The navamsa sign holding the Atmakaraka is the karakamsa (BPHS 33.1 note; Jaimini 1.2.1); see karaka/karakamsha_<sign>.

source_views.source: BPHS (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1) 32.1-2, 32.13-17
source_views.view: Karakas are taken from the seven planets Sun to Saturn; some add Rahu only when two planets share the same longitude, others always count eight including Rahu. The eight in order are Atma, Amatya, Bhratri, Matri, Pitri, Putra, Gnati and Stree (Dara) karaka; some treat Matri and Putra karaka as one. If two planets tie, one role is left short and the constant significator is used for it. These are chara (variable) karakas.

source_views.source: BPHS (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1) 32.3-8
source_views.view: Among Sun etc., the one that has crossed the most degrees in its sign is the Atmakaraka; ties go by minutes, then seconds; Rahu's degrees are counted from 30. The AK is the most important karaka and rules the native as a king rules his country, able to bind and release.

source_views.source: BPHS (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1) 32.9-12
source_views.view: As a minister cannot oppose the king, the other karakas cannot override the AK: an adverse AK blocks the others' good effects and a favourable AK blocks their evil.

source_views.source: Jaimini Upadesa Sutras (tr. K.V. Abhyankar) 1.1.10-11
source_views.view: The planet most advanced in degrees is the chief significator; it rules a person's bondage and liberation (misery and happiness).

source_views.source: Jaimini Sutras (tr. B. Suryanarain Rao, 1955 ed.) 1.1.11-12
source_views.view: Of seven planets Sun to Saturn, or eight Sun to Rahu, the one with the highest degrees is AK; it gives good or bad results through its dignity and associations.

source_views.source: B. Suryanarain Rao, notes to his Jaimini Sutras (1955 ed.) on 1.1.12
source_views.view: Exalted or benefic-joined AK: release even if confined, life in holy places and moksha; debilitated or malefic-joined AK: confinement and no moksha unless benefic aspect relieves it.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita ch. 4 (tr. P.S. Sastri)
source_views.view: The planet that has crossed the most degrees in a sign is the 'advanced' planet; with the Sun - royal adviser; full Moon and Venus - wealthy scholar; Mars - soldier or metal-worker; Mercury - sculptor or trader; Jupiter - Vedic ritualist; Venus - long life and affairs; Saturn - varied activity; Rahu/Ketu - poisons and metal works. Malefic in the 3rd from it gives courage, benefic timidity. (Verse numbers not legible in the scan.)

source_views.source: P.S. Sastri, notes to Uttara Kalamrita ch. 4
source_views.view: Sastri identifies this as Jaimini's Atmakaraka and objects that Kalidasa reads it from the rasi only, whereas Jaimini judges it from its navamsa (the karakamsa).

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Studies in Jaimini Astrology art. 8, 15-16
source_views.view: The highest-degree planet is AK; its strength reflects the strength of the whole chart; the natural AK is the Sun. Raman follows seven karakas with Rahu only as a gap-filler when planets tie, calling it the view supported by Parasara.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach 8.1-8.2
source_views.view: Eight chara karakas (seven planets plus Rahu, Ketu excluded as he signifies moksha); they show people and matters affecting sustenance, achievement and spiritual progress, and how karma carries between lives. The AK throws light on the inner self.

source_views.source: Prabhakara Murthy, Introduction to Jaimini Astrology ch. 2
source_views.view: Seven karakas; Rahu only fills a vacancy when planets tie, never as AK in the 7-karaka scheme. Strength of AK decides strength of chart; strong in exaltation, moolatrikona, own and friendly signs; weak in debility, combustion and enemy signs. Gives the traits of each planet as AK.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, 'Atmakaraka & Karakamsa' (srath.com)
source_views.view: The AK's nature shows the soul's nature; a malefic AK indicates higher spiritual development; retrograde AK shows a deep desire behind the birth; combust AK gives spiritual insight; gives a lesson for each planet as AK and results of the AK counted from the navamsa lagna; AK's Vimshottari dasa often brings suffering, its Narayana dasa achievement.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, 'Atmakaraka II: Bhagavat Gita' (srath.com)
source_views.view: Seven planets Sun to Saturn suffice for mundane charts; living, procreating beings use eight with Rahu (Ketu excluded).

source_views.source: K.N. Rao (via summary: Sri Harsha Indrasena, 'Chara Karaka Scheme - No longer A Mystery', Saptarishis Astrology, 2009)
source_views.view: K.N. Rao is reported to use seven karakas always, with no Pitrikaraka.

karaka/atmakaraka.disagreements: 7- vs 8-karaka: BPHS 32.1-2 records both views without choosing; Jaimini 1.1.19 says some authorities merge mother and son karakas. Abhyankar's text lists eight (with Pitrikaraka) and reads 1.1.19 as the seven-planet alternative; B. Suryanarain Rao's text has no Pitrikaraka sutra at all and uses Rahu only to fill gaps when planets tie; Raman, Murthy and K.N. Rao (via summary) use seven; P.V.R. Narasimha Rao and Sanjay Rath use eight (Rath: eight for living beings, seven for mundane charts). The choice changes which planet holds the middle and lower roles. Rahu as AK: possible only in the 8-karaka scheme (PVR, Rath); Murthy rules it out for the 7-karaka scheme. Natural AK: Raman names the Sun. Malefic AK: Rath reads it as spiritually more advanced, while B.S. Rao reads malefic influence on the AK as bondage. Uttara Kalamrita reads the AK's results from the rasi; Jaimini and Sastri from the navamsa.
karaka/atmakaraka.phrasing_guidance: Describe the Atmakaraka as the planet that shows the person's core drive and life lessons. Do not call a malefic or weak AK bad luck; frame it as the area of growth. Avoid predictions of imprisonment, death or moksha as certainties.

karaka/amatyakaraka.summary: The Amatyakaraka is the planet with the second-highest degree; as the 'minister' to the Atmakaraka it shows counsel, career and the means by which the native rises.
karaka/amatyakaraka.determination: Rank the seven planets Sun to Saturn by degrees travelled within their own sign (sign ignored; ties broken by minutes, then seconds); highest = Atmakaraka, then Amatya, Bhratri, Matri, Putra, Gnati and lowest = Darakaraka (7-karaka scheme, the one the calculator uses). In the 8-karaka scheme Rahu is added (its degrees counted back from the end of its sign) and a Pitrikaraka (father) is inserted after the Matrikaraka, so every role below Matrikaraka can fall on a different planet. Sources: 7-karaka with Rahu only as a tie-filler - BPHS 32.1-2 first view, B. Suryanarain Rao, B.V. Raman, Prabhakara Murthy, K.N. Rao (via summary); 8-karaka - BPHS 32.1-2 second view and Santhanam's worked example, Abhyankar's text of Jaimini 1.1.10-18, P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Sanjay Rath (8 for living beings, 7 for mundane charts). The Amatyakaraka is second in degrees. Adding Rahu (8-karaka) can change it when Rahu's counted-back degrees fall above the 7-karaka Amatyakaraka.
significations: ministers and advisers (Jaimini 1.1.12 Abhyankar / 1.1.13 B.S. Rao; PVR 8.2)
profession (P.S. Sastri on Uttara Kalamrita ch. 4)
career elevation and social status (Murthy ch. 10)
common_outcomes: A strong, well-aspected Amatyakaraka can make one a counsellor or minister; a weak, afflicted one an adviser who brings disgrace (B.S. Rao on 1.1.13).
Links between the Amatyakaraka and the 10th lord or Atmakaraka are read as yogas for high position (PVR 11.8).
rare_outcomes: Devotion: BPHS ch. 33 (12th-from-karakamsa section) and Jaimini 1.2.82 say the deity rules can also be read from the 6th from the Amatyakaraka's navamsa (B.S. Rao: the 6th planet from it in weekday order); Raman art. 142 says similar results follow if the Amatyakaraka is in the karakamsa.

by_area.career: PVR 11.8: 10th lord conjoined or aspected by the AmK or its dispositor - an important person at court; AK with AmK - very intelligent, a minister; AmK very strong in own or exaltation sign - a minister; AmK in a trine from lagna - a famous minister; AmK in a kendra or trine from the AK - an associate liked by the ruler. P.S. Sastri: Kalidasa's rule that the planet next to the most advanced decides profession matches Jaimini's Amatyakaraka. Murthy ch. 10: important for elevation in employment and social status.
by_area.relationships: Murthy ch. 10: the Amatyakaraka plays an important role in marriage.
by_area.family: Murthy ch. 10: the Amatyakaraka plays a role in childbirth.
by_area.spirituality: BPHS ch. 33 and Jaimini 1.2.82: rules for the deity worshipped can also be applied from the 6th from the Amatyakaraka's navamsa.

strengtheners: own or exaltation sign (PVR 11.8)
conjunction with the Atmakaraka (PVR 11.8)
trine from lagna, or kendra/trine from the AK (PVR 11.8)
good combination and aspect (B.S. Rao on 1.1.13)
weakeners_or_cancellations: debility, evil combination and malefic aspect - an adviser who brings disgrace (B.S. Rao on 1.1.13)
karaka/amatyakaraka.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman art. 9: there is no natural (naisargika) Amatyakaraka, but Mercury may be taken as such.
timing: Murthy ch. 10: important in timing marriage, childbirth and job elevation (no specific dasa rule given).
karaka/amatyakaraka.karakamsa: Raman art. 142: if the Amatyakaraka is in the karakamsa, the deity-worship results of the karakamsa apply similarly.

source_views.source: BPHS (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1) 32.1-2, 32.13-17
source_views.view: Karakas are taken from the seven planets Sun to Saturn; some add Rahu only when two planets share the same longitude, others always count eight including Rahu. The eight in order are Atma, Amatya, Bhratri, Matri, Pitri, Putra, Gnati and Stree (Dara) karaka; some treat Matri and Putra karaka as one. If two planets tie, one role is left short and the constant significator is used for it. These are chara (variable) karakas.

source_views.source: Jaimini Upadesa Sutras (tr. K.V. Abhyankar) 1.1.12
source_views.view: The planet next to the chief significator is the minister significator (Amatyakaraka).

source_views.source: Jaimini Sutras (tr. B. Suryanarain Rao, 1955 ed.) 1.1.13 (with notes)
source_views.view: Next in degrees to the AK is the Amatyakaraka; when powerful and well aspected the person becomes a great minister or councillor, when debilitated and afflicted an evil adviser who disgraces himself and those he advises.

source_views.source: Jaimini Sutras (tr. B. Suryanarain Rao, 1955 ed.) 1.2.82 (with notes)
source_views.view: Read as 'likewise from the Amatyakaraka': B.S. Rao takes the 6th planet from the AmK (weekday order) in an evil karakamsa as devotion to lower spirits.

source_views.source: Jaimini Upadesa Sutras (tr. K.V. Abhyankar) 1.2.82
source_views.view: Abhyankar instead reads this sutra as applying the deity rules to the 6th house from the Atmakaraka's division.

source_views.source: BPHS (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1) ch. 33 (vv. 63-74 section)
source_views.view: Ends the deity rules for the 12th from the karakamsa by saying similar inferences come from the 6th navamsa counted from the Amatyakaraka's navamsa.

source_views.source: P.S. Sastri, notes to Uttara Kalamrita ch. 4
source_views.view: Kalidasa's planet next below the most advanced one, which he says decides profession, is Jaimini's Amatyakaraka.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Studies in Jaimini Astrology art. 9, 142
source_views.view: The planet with the next highest degrees is the sub-lord; no natural AmK but Mercury may serve; AmK in karakamsa repeats the deity results.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach 8.2, 11.8
source_views.view: AmK shows advisers and counsellors: intellectuals when strong, indecisive people when weak; gives the court/minister yogas listed above.

source_views.source: Prabhakara Murthy, Introduction to Jaimini Astrology ch. 2, ch. 10
source_views.view: Second-highest planet; plays an important role in marriage, child birth, elevation in employment and social status.

karaka/amatyakaraka.disagreements: 7- vs 8-karaka: BPHS 32.1-2 records both views without choosing; Jaimini 1.1.19 says some authorities merge mother and son karakas. Abhyankar's text lists eight (with Pitrikaraka) and reads 1.1.19 as the seven-planet alternative; B. Suryanarain Rao's text has no Pitrikaraka sutra at all and uses Rahu only to fill gaps when planets tie; Raman, Murthy and K.N. Rao (via summary) use seven; P.V.R. Narasimha Rao and Sanjay Rath use eight (Rath: eight for living beings, seven for mundane charts). The choice changes which planet holds the middle and lower roles. Jaimini 1.2.82 is read by B.S. Rao as 'from the Amatyakaraka' and by Abhyankar as 'from the 6th house'; BPHS ch. 33 supports the Amatyakaraka reading.
karaka/amatyakaraka.phrasing_guidance: Present the Amatyakaraka as the planet describing the kind of work and support that helps the person rise. Avoid promising ministerial office; speak of leadership, advisory or service roles.

karaka/bhratrikaraka.summary: The Bhratrikaraka is the third-highest planet by degree and signifies brothers and sisters; some read it also for courage and manliness.
karaka/bhratrikaraka.determination: Rank the seven planets Sun to Saturn by degrees travelled within their own sign (sign ignored; ties broken by minutes, then seconds); highest = Atmakaraka, then Amatya, Bhratri, Matri, Putra, Gnati and lowest = Darakaraka (7-karaka scheme, the one the calculator uses). In the 8-karaka scheme Rahu is added (its degrees counted back from the end of its sign) and a Pitrikaraka (father) is inserted after the Matrikaraka, so every role below Matrikaraka can fall on a different planet. Sources: 7-karaka with Rahu only as a tie-filler - BPHS 32.1-2 first view, B. Suryanarain Rao, B.V. Raman, Prabhakara Murthy, K.N. Rao (via summary); 8-karaka - BPHS 32.1-2 second view and Santhanam's worked example, Abhyankar's text of Jaimini 1.1.10-18, P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Sanjay Rath (8 for living beings, 7 for mundane charts). The Bhratrikaraka is third in degrees.
significations: brothers and sisters (Jaimini 1.1.13 Abhyankar / 1.1.14 B.S. Rao; Raman art. 10; PVR 8.2)
valour and manliness (P.S. Sastri on Uttara Kalamrita ch. 4)
common_outcomes: Exalted, well-joined and well-aspected Bhratrikaraka: many brothers who prosper (B.S. Rao on 1.1.14).
Debilitated, malefic-joined or badly aspected Bhratrikaraka: harm to brothers - none, or ones who suffer (B.S. Rao on 1.1.14).

by_area.personality: P.S. Sastri: Kalidasa's planet next below the Amatyakaraka decides valour and manliness.
by_area.family: Raman art. 10: all events concerning brothers and sisters are read from the Bhratrikaraka; art. 132: the number of siblings may be judged from the navamsas gained by the 3rd and 11th houses or by the Bhratrikaraka.

strengtheners: exaltation, good combination and benefic aspect (B.S. Rao on 1.1.14)
weakeners_or_cancellations: debility, conjunction with malefics, malefic aspect (B.S. Rao on 1.1.14)
karaka/bhratrikaraka.lagna_or_context_notes: Natural significator of siblings is Mars (Raman art. 10); Jaimini 1.1.20 assigns sisters, brothers-in-law, younger brothers (and mother) to Mars; Raman art. 132 reads younger and elder siblings from the 3rd and 11th from the Upapada.

source_views.source: BPHS (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1) 32.1-2, 32.13-17
source_views.view: Karakas are taken from the seven planets Sun to Saturn; some add Rahu only when two planets share the same longitude, others always count eight including Rahu. The eight in order are Atma, Amatya, Bhratri, Matri, Pitri, Putra, Gnati and Stree (Dara) karaka; some treat Matri and Putra karaka as one. If two planets tie, one role is left short and the constant significator is used for it. These are chara (variable) karakas.

source_views.source: Jaimini Upadesa Sutras (tr. K.V. Abhyankar) 1.1.13
source_views.view: The planet next to the Amatyakaraka is the significator of the brother.

source_views.source: Jaimini Sutras (tr. B. Suryanarain Rao, 1955 ed.) 1.1.14 (with notes)
source_views.view: Next in degrees after the AmK; debilitated, malefic-joined BK ruins brothers, exalted and well-aspected BK gives many prosperous brothers.

source_views.source: P.S. Sastri, notes to Uttara Kalamrita ch. 4
source_views.view: The planet next lower than the Amatyakaraka is said by Kalidasa to decide valour and manliness.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Studies in Jaimini Astrology art. 10, 132
source_views.view: BK becomes lord of brothers; all events about brothers and sisters are read from it; Mars is the natural significator.

karaka/matrikaraka.summary: The Matrikaraka is the fourth-highest planet by degree and signifies the mother; in the 7-karaka tradition it may also stand for children.

karaka/matrikaraka.phrasing_guidance: Speak of the bond with and support from the mother; never predict a mother's illness or death from the karaka alone.

karaka/putrakaraka.summary: The Putrakaraka is the fifth planet by degree in the 7-karaka scheme (sixth in the 8-karaka) and signifies children; with the Atmakaraka it forms a key raja yoga.
karaka/putrakaraka.determination: Rank the seven planets Sun to Saturn by degrees travelled within their own sign (sign ignored; ties broken by minutes, then seconds); highest = Atmakaraka, then Amatya, Bhratri, Matri, Putra, Gnati and lowest = Darakaraka (7-karaka scheme, the one the calculator uses). In the 8-karaka scheme Rahu is added (its degrees counted back from the end of its sign) and a Pitrikaraka (father) is inserted after the Matrikaraka, so every role below Matrikaraka can fall on a different planet. Rao (via summary); 8-karaka - BPHS 32.1-2 second view and Santhanam's worked example, Abhyankar's text of Jaimini 1.1.10-18, P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Sanjay Rath (8 for living beings, 7 for mundane charts). In the 7-karaka scheme the Putrakaraka follows the Matrikaraka directly; in the 8-karaka scheme a Pitrikaraka (father) comes between them.
common_outcomes: A well-placed, exalted Putrakaraka in good vargas with benefic associations gives children who are virtuous, happy and dutiful (B.S. Rao on 1.1.16).

Atmakaraka with Putrakaraka, together with lagna and 5th lords conjoining, gives a raja yoga of power and prosperity (PVR 11.7.3); Murthy ch. 7 calls the AK-PK association the most powerful karaka yoga, stronger in the lagna, 5th or karakamsa.
rare_outcomes: AK and PK in the lagna or 5th, in own sign, exaltation or with benefic aspect, with lagna and 5th lords exchanged, gives a 'great king' yoga (PVR 11.7.3).

by_area.career: PVR 11.7.3 and Murthy ch. 7: AK-PK association is a raja yoga for power and status.
by_area.family: PVR 8.4: troubles or achievements around children that touch the soul are read from the Putrakaraka, while the plain birth of children is read from the 5th from Jupiter. Murthy ch. 10: children are judged from the Upapada and its 7th, the Putra arudha (A5), and the Putrakaraka.

strengtheners: exaltation, good shadvargas, benefic conjunction and aspect (B.S. Rao on 1.1.16)
conjunction with the Atmakaraka (PVR 11.7.3; Murthy ch. 7)

karaka/putrakaraka.phrasing_guidance: Speak of children, students or followers and creative output. Never predict childlessness or a child's misfortune from the karaka alone.

karaka/gnatikaraka.summary: The Gnatikaraka is the sixth planet by degree in the 7-karaka scheme (seventh in the 8-karaka) and signifies cousins and kinsfolk; it is widely used for rivals and obstacles.
karaka/gnatikaraka.determination: Rank the seven planets Sun to Saturn by degrees travelled within their own sign (sign ignored; ties broken by minutes, then seconds); highest = Atmakaraka, then Amatya, Bhratri, Matri, Putra, Gnati and lowest = Darakaraka (7-karaka scheme, the one the calculator uses). Rao (via summary); 8-karaka - BPHS 32.1-2 second view and Santhanam's worked example, Abhyankar's text of Jaimini 1.1.10-18, P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Sanjay Rath (8 for living beings, 7 for mundane charts). The Gnatikaraka is second-lowest in degrees.

by_area.family: Cousins and relatives (B.S. Rao on 1.1.17; Raman art. 13).

karaka/gnatikaraka.phrasing_guidance: Frame as competition, disputes with relatives or rivals that build resilience; avoid naming specific enemies or predicting conflict as certain.

karaka/darakaraka.summary: The Darakaraka is the planet with the lowest degree in its sign and signifies the spouse; the planet itself (not the 7th from it) describes the partner.
karaka/darakaraka.determination: Rank the seven planets Sun to Saturn by degrees travelled within their own sign (sign ignored; ties broken by minutes, then seconds); highest = Atmakaraka, then Amatya, Bhratri, Matri, Putra, Gnati and lowest = Darakaraka (7-karaka scheme, the one the calculator uses). In the 8-karaka scheme Rahu is added (its degrees counted back from the end of its sign) and a Pitrikaraka (father) is inserted after the Matrikaraka, so every role below Matrikaraka can fall on a different planet. Sources: 7-karaka with Rahu only as a tie-filler - BPHS 32.1-2 first view, B. Suryanarain Rao, B.V. Raman, Prabhakara Murthy, K.N. Rao (via summary); 8-karaka - BPHS 32.1-2 second view and Santhanam's worked example, Abhyankar's text of Jaimini 1.1.10-18, P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Sanjay Rath (8 for living beings, 7 for mundane charts). The Darakaraka is the lowest in degrees. In the 8-karaka scheme Rahu becomes Darakaraka when it is near the end of its sign (lowest counted-back degrees).
significations: wife or husband (Jaimini 1.1.18; BPHS 32.13-17 'Streekaraka'; Raman art. 14)
common_outcomes: PVR 8.3: the Darakaraka itself represents the spouse; one does not take the 7th from it.
Murthy ch. 10: marriage is likely in the dasa or antardasa of a sign occupied or aspected by the Darakaraka (Jaimini sign dasas).
rare_outcomes: Raman art. 133 worked example: a Darakaraka in a benefic sign aspected by benefics is credited with protecting the spouse despite other affliction.

Rao on 1.1.18: the word 'cha' in the sutra means the spouse must also be judged from the houses counted from the lagna, Arudha Lagna and Upapada, not from the karaka alone. Murthy ch. 10: the nature and friendship of the Atmakaraka and Darakaraka show the couple's harmony.

strengtheners: benefic sign and benefic aspect (Raman art. 133 example)
karaka/darakaraka.lagna_or_context_notes: Natural significator of spouse is Venus (Raman art. 14; PVR 8.3 for marriage timing); BPHS 32.13-17 (Santhanam note): if planets tie and no planet is left for the Dara role, use Venus for marriage matters.
timing: Murthy ch. 10: dasa or antardasa of the sign occupied or aspected by the Darakaraka can bring marriage, along with Upapada-based signs and Jupiter's transit of the 2nd from the Upapada.
PVR 12.6: for marriage one may want transiting Jupiter to be benefic (in prastaara ashtakavarga) from references such as Venus or the Darakaraka.

karaka/karakamsha_aries.summary: With the Atmakaraka in Aries navamsa, Jaimini and Parasara speak of trouble from rats, cats and similar small animals.
common_outcomes: Nuisance or bites from rats, cats and similar creatures (Jaimini 1.2.2; BPHS 33.2-8; Raman art. 129).
rare_outcomes: Murthy ch. 6 adds possible involvement in trading animals.
B.S. Rao's first reading of Jaimini 1.2.70 and Raman art. 142: karakamsha in Aries with Ketu (B.S. Rao: with a benefic) points to moksha.

by_area.health: Raman art. 129: fear from cats, rats and similar creatures.
by_area.spirituality: Jaimini 1.2.70 as read by B.S. Rao and Raman art. 142: Aries karakamsha with Ketu (or benefics) gives final liberation.

strengtheners: benefic aspect on the karakamsha removes the evil (BPHS 33.2-8)
weakeners_or_cancellations: a malefic joining increases the nuisance (BPHS 33.2-8)
BPHS 33.12: Atmakaraka in a division of Mars (Aries is Mars-ruled) is said to incline one to others' spouses
karaka/karakamsha_aries.lagna_or_context_notes: The karakamsha is the navamsa sign of the Atmakaraka (7-karaka scheme in the calculator). Results are modified by the planets in and aspecting it and by the houses counted from it (BPHS ch. 33; Jaimini 1.2). Murthy ch. 6 also reads the same sign in the rasi chart.
sign_specific_rules: BPHS 33.12: AK in divisions of the Moon, Mars or Venus inclines one towards others' spouses, otherwise the contrary.
BPHS 33.19-22: Rahu and Sun in the karakamsha in a malefic's sign aspected by Jupiter - fire to a neighbouring house (Jaimini 1.2.28 via Abhyankar: fire reaches but does not burn one's own house).
Abhyankar's reading of Jaimini 1.2.70: Ketu in the 12th from the karakamsha, that 12th being Pisces, definitely gives salvation - this applies to an Aries karakamsha.

planets_in_or_aspecting.rule: Sun in the karakamsha: royal or government work (Jaimini 1.2.14; BPHS 33.13-18); Raman art. 136: political leadership or state service.
Full Moon (BPHS: more so with Venus' aspect) in the karakamsha: enjoyment and living by learning (Jaimini 1.2.15; BPHS 33.13-18).
Strong Mars: weapons, fire, alchemy or metallurgy (Jaimini 1.2.16; BPHS 33.13-18).
Strong Mercury: trade, weaving, crafts, arts; intelligent and educated (Jaimini 1.2.17; BPHS 33.13-18).
Jupiter: religious rites, spiritual and Vedic learning (Jaimini 1.2.18; BPHS 33.13-18).
Venus: state affairs or government service, sensuous, long-lived (Jaimini 1.2.19; BPHS 33.13-18).
Saturn: livelihood by a well-known or family profession (Jaimini 1.2.20; BPHS 33.13-18).
Rahu: archer, machinery or metal work, poison-cure; also a thief (Jaimini 1.2.21; BPHS 33.13-18).

Ketu: dealing in elephants; also a thief (Jaimini 1.2.22; BPHS 33.13-18); with Venus' aspect a performer of sacrifices, with Saturn's an ascetic or servant, with malefic aspect ear trouble (Jaimini 1.2.32-37; BPHS 33.25-29).
Sun and Rahu together: danger from snakes, averted by benefic aspect; in benefic vargas a poison-healer; Mars' aspect links it to fire (Jaimini 1.2.23-28; BPHS 33.19-22).
Moon in the karakamsha aspected by Venus: alchemist; by Mercury: physician (Jaimini 1.2.86-87; BPHS 33.77-84).
Benefics only in the karakamsha and the navamsa lagna, aspected by benefics: royal status; benefics in kendras/trines from it: wealth and learning; mixed influence gives mixed results (BPHS 33.9-11).
Sun and/or Venus aspecting the karakamsha: royal servant or ambassador (Jaimini 1.2.38; Raman art. 136).
Jupiter or Moon in the karakamsha or its 5th: an author or scholar; Venus a lesser writer, Mercury lesser still (BPHS 33.41-45, 33.85-86; Raman art. 136).

source_views.view: After the karakas, Jaimini takes up the division occupied by the chief significator and gives a result for each of the twelve divisions counted from Aries.

source_views.source: Jaimini Sutras (tr. B. Suryanarain Rao, 1955 ed.) 1.2.1-13
source_views.view: Having found the Atmakaraka, judge the results of his navamsa position; one sutra per navamsa sign, decoded by katapayadi numbers.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach 7.3.6
source_views.view: The sign occupied by the Atmakaraka in the navamsa chart is the karakamsa; the navamsa can be read with it as lagna; the 12th from it shows liberation and Ketu there helps moksha.

karaka/karakamsha_aries.disagreements: Which sign: BPHS, B.S. Rao, Raman, PVR and Murthy take the Atmakaraka's navamsa sign; Murthy also uses the same sign in the rasi chart ('karakamsa rasi') and notes that some read 'swamsa' as the navamsa lagna; Abhyankar's translation speaks only of the 'division occupied by' the significator, counted from Aries; Kalidasa (Uttara Kalamrita ch. 4) reads the Atmakaraka's rasi position, which P.S. Sastri rejects. Jaimini 1.2.70 (kriya-chapa): B.S. Rao and Raman read it as the karakamsha itself in Aries or Sagittarius; B.S. Rao's second reading and BPHS 33.63-74 make it the 12th from the karakamsha in Aries/Sagittarius (karakamsha Taurus or Capricorn); Abhyankar reads the 12th as Pisces or Cancer.
karaka/karakamsha_aries.phrasing_guidance: The sign results are old, often literal (animals, water, falls); present them as areas to be careful with or symbolic themes, never as predicted accidents or diseases. Lead with supportive themes where sources give them, and do not state illegitimacy, adultery or criminality claims to a user.

karaka/karakamsha_taurus.summary: With the Atmakaraka in Taurus navamsa, the texts link the native's fortunes to four-footed animals - happiness from them in Parasara, gain or trouble in the commentators.
common_outcomes: Happiness or gain from quadrupeds such as cattle and horses (BPHS 33.2-8; B.S. Rao on 1.2.3; Murthy ch. 6).
rare_outcomes: Trouble from quadrupeds when the Atmakaraka is weak or afflicted (B.S. Rao on 1.2.3; Raman art. 129 lists bulls and horses under dangers).

by_area.finance: BPHS 33.2-8 and Murthy ch. 6: benefit through quadrupeds.
by_area.health: Raman art. 129: dangers from bulls, horses and similar animals.
by_area.spirituality: The 12th from a Taurus karakamsha is Aries: BPHS 33.63-74 and B.S. Rao's second reading of Jaimini 1.2.70 say Ketu there, aspected by a benefic, gives final liberation.

strengtheners: benefic aspect (BPHS 33.2-8)
strong, unafflicted Atmakaraka turns the result towards gain (B.S. Rao on 1.2.3)
weakeners_or_cancellations: weak or afflicted Atmakaraka turns it towards trouble (B.S. Rao on 1.2.3)
BPHS 33.12: Venus-ruled division - inclination to others' spouses
karaka/karakamsha_taurus.lagna_or_context_notes: The karakamsha is the navamsa sign of the Atmakaraka (7-karaka scheme in the calculator). Results are modified by the planets in and aspecting it and by the houses counted from it (BPHS ch. 33; Jaimini 1.2). Murthy ch. 6 also reads the same sign in the rasi chart.
sign_specific_rules: BPHS 33.12: AK in divisions of the Moon, Mars or Venus inclines one towards others' spouses.
12th from karakamsha = Aries: Ketu there with benefic aspect gives moksha (BPHS 33.63-74; Jaimini 1.2.70, B.S. Rao second reading).

planets_in_or_aspecting.rule: Sun in the karakamsha: royal or government work (Jaimini 1.2.14; BPHS 33.13-18); Raman art. 136: political leadership or state service.
Full Moon (BPHS: more so with Venus' aspect) in the karakamsha: enjoyment and living by learning (Jaimini 1.2.15; BPHS 33.13-18).
Strong Mars: weapons, fire, alchemy or metallurgy (Jaimini 1.2.16; BPHS 33.13-18).
Strong Mercury: trade, weaving, crafts, arts; intelligent and educated (Jaimini 1.2.17; BPHS 33.13-18).
Jupiter: religious rites, spiritual and Vedic learning (Jaimini 1.2.18; BPHS 33.13-18).
Venus: state affairs or government service, sensuous, long-lived (Jaimini 1.2.19; BPHS 33.13-18).
Saturn: livelihood by a well-known or family profession (Jaimini 1.2.20; BPHS 33.13-18).
Rahu: archer, machinery or metal work, poison-cure; also a thief (Jaimini 1.2.21; BPHS 33.13-18).

Ketu: dealing in elephants; also a thief (Jaimini 1.2.22; BPHS 33.13-18); with Venus' aspect a performer of sacrifices, with Saturn's an ascetic or servant, with malefic aspect ear trouble (Jaimini 1.2.32-37; BPHS 33.25-29).
Sun and Rahu together: danger from snakes, averted by benefic aspect; in benefic vargas a poison-healer; Mars' aspect links it to fire (Jaimini 1.2.23-28; BPHS 33.19-22).
Moon in the karakamsha aspected by Venus: alchemist; by Mercury: physician (Jaimini 1.2.86-87; BPHS 33.77-84).
Benefics only in the karakamsha and the navamsa lagna, aspected by benefics: royal status; benefics in kendras/trines from it: wealth and learning; mixed influence gives mixed results (BPHS 33.9-11).
Sun and/or Venus aspecting the karakamsha: royal servant or ambassador (Jaimini 1.2.38; Raman art. 136).
Jupiter or Moon in the karakamsha or its 5th: an author or scholar; Venus a lesser writer, Mercury lesser still (BPHS 33.41-45, 33.85-86; Raman art. 136).

karaka/karakamsha_capricorn.summary: With the Atmakaraka in Capricorn navamsa, Parasara promises gain from water creatures and sea products (conch, pearl, coral), while Jaimini's sutra speaks of trouble from aquatic creatures, birds and skin growths.
common_outcomes: Parasara: gains from water creatures and conch, pearl, coral (BPHS 33.2-8; Murthy ch. 6: gain from marine products).
Jaimini: trouble from aquatic creatures, birds or wild animals, itches and stubborn swellings (Jaimini 1.2.11; Raman art. 129).
rare_outcomes: Raman art. 129 adds troubles from women and spirits; B.S. Rao notes 'khechara' (sky-goers) may mean evil spirits or be read 'bhuchara' (land beasts).
The 12th from a Capricorn karakamsha is Sagittarius: Ketu there with benefic aspect gives moksha (BPHS 33.63-74; Jaimini 1.2.70, B.S. Rao second reading).

by_area.spirituality: Ketu in the 12th (Sagittarius) with benefic aspect: moksha (BPHS 33.63-74).

12th from karakamsha = Sagittarius: Ketu there with benefic aspect - moksha (BPHS 33.63-74).

Strong Mercury: trade, weaving, crafts, arts; intelligent and educated (Jaimini 1.2.17; BPHS 33.13-18).

Saturn: livelihood by a well-known or family profession (Jaimini 1.2.20; BPHS 33.13-18).
