varga/what_d10_shows.summary: The dashamsa (D10, each sign split into ten parts of 3 degrees) is Parashara's chart for power and position ('great results'); modern authors use it as the chart of career, work and achievements in society.
common_outcomes: Read career questions in D10 after checking the D1 10th house, its lord and the 10th from the Moon.
Treat D10 as showing how work actually unfolds and the standing it brings, not only the job title.
rare_outcomes: Rath also calls D10 'karmamsa' or 'swarga chakra' and uses it for the work a spiritual person does in the world (e.g. heads of religious institutions).

by_area.career: Core use (BPHS 7.1-8; PVR 6.3; Rath ch. XIII; Raman HPA ch. X).
by_area.spirituality: Rath ch. XII: the work one does to further spiritual aims is also seen in D10.

varga/what_d10_shows.lagna_or_context_notes: D10 counting: from the sign itself for an odd sign, from the 9th sign for an even sign (BPHS 6.13-14; Phaladeepika 3.6). PVR gives the seed house of D10 as the 10th, hence 'karma or action in society'.

source_views.source: BPHS 7.1-8 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1)
source_views.view: Power and position are to be judged from the dasamsa.

source_views.view: In deciding one's career the dasamsa positions of the planets are of supreme importance.
Defines the ten 3-degree dasamsas, counted from the sign itself in odd signs and from the 9th in even signs.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 6.3 Table 11, 6.5 and 18.5
source_views.view: D10 shows career, activities and achievements in society; to study career one should analyse the dasamsa; its seed is the 10th house, so it shows karma in society.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. II sec. 7 and ch. XIII 13.2
source_views.view: D10 is also called karmamsa or swarga chakra; the focus is the 10th house in that chart; power or rise due to karma is seen in D10.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. X
source_views.view: Among Parashara's sixteen divisions the dasamsa is used for profession; a beginner need not use these finer divisions yet.

varga/what_d10_shows.disagreements: Parashara's word is 'great results' / power and position (Santhanam: power and position); career-as-profession is the modern reading. Raman treats D10 as an advanced tool rather than a default one.
varga/what_d10_shows.phrasing_guidance: Present D10 as describing the shape of one's working life and recognition; avoid naming a single fixed job.

varga/d10_weight_vs_d1.summary: Classical weighting gives the dasamsa little general weight (one quarter of the rasi effect in Phaladeepika; 1.5 of 20 vimshopaka points in the ten-division scheme), so D10 refines career judgement but does not replace D1.
common_outcomes: Judge career first from D1 (10th house, 10th lord, 10th from Moon) and use D10 to confirm and specify.
For overall planetary strength the dasamsa counts only in the ten- and sixteen-division schemes.

by_area.career: Main sphere where D10 gets more than background weight (PVR 6.5; Rath 13.2.1).

varga/d10_weight_vs_d1.lagna_or_context_notes: The dasamsa is not part of the six- or seven-division schemes (BPHS 7.17-20; Phaladeepika 3.2).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 3.2-3.3 (tr. Sastri, 1950)
source_views.view: Removing the dasamsa, shashtyamsa and kalamsa from the ten vargas gives the saptavarga; effects are full in the rasi, half in other vargas and only a quarter in the shodasamsa, dasamsa and shashtyamsa.

source_views.source: BPHS 7.20-25 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: In the dasavarga scheme the rasi gets 3, the shashtiamsa 5 and each other division (dasamsa included) 1.5 points; in the shodasavarga scheme the dasamsa is among the divisions getting half a point.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 6.5 and 13.4.1
source_views.view: Choose the divisional chart by the matter of interest: for career and achievements in society D10 is the correct chart.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. XIII 13.2.1
source_views.view: The dasamsa should be analysed in detail independently, like the rasi chart.

varga/d10_weight_vs_d1.disagreements: Classical weights give D10 little general force; PVR and Rath give it primary weight for career questions specifically.
varga/d10_weight_vs_d1.phrasing_guidance: Say D10 adds detail to the career picture already in the birth chart.

varga/d10_lagna_and_lord.summary: The D10 lagna and its lord represent the person in their working life; the lord's house in D10 shows working style (in the 9th: independent, own boss; in the 5th: prefers service), and planets linked to it drive the career.
common_outcomes: D10 lagna lord in the 9th: independent, suited to business or self-directed work (Rath).
D10 lagna lord in the 5th: tends to work as a subordinate or in service (Rath).
D10 lagna lord in a dusthana (e.g. 8th) weakens the career chart; in a trine it strengthens it (PVR 32.2.1 example).
rare_outcomes: Rath: heads of the Kanchi math seem to have a watery D10 lagna with a strong Jupiter-Mars combination.

by_area.career: Core use.

strengtheners: D10 lagna lord in a kendra or trikona
benefics in or aspecting the D10 lagna
weakeners_or_cancellations: D10 lagna lord in the 8th (PVR example)
8th lord joining the D10 lagna or its lord (Rath ch. XI)
varga/d10_lagna_and_lord.lagna_or_context_notes: The D10 lagna changes sign about every 12 minutes of birth time (PVR 32.2.1); see birth_time_sensitivity.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. II sec. 7 and ch. XIII 13.2.4
source_views.view: In the divisional chart the ninth house is the boss and the fifth the subordinates; the lagna lord in the 9th makes one independent (business suits), in the 5th one prefers to be a subordinate or in service.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 32.2.1
source_views.view: Example: a D10 with the lagna lord in the 8th is weak, while the same lord in the 9th strengthens it.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. XII (spiritual heads)
source_views.view: Notes a recurring watery D10 lagna with a strong Jupiter-Mars yoga in charts of heads of the Kanchi Kamakoti Peetham.

source_views.source: BPHS 7.1-8 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: General method: houses and lords are judged within the relevant division; Santhanam's example is the 2nd and 4th lords in the chaturvimsamsa for education.

varga/d10_lagna_and_lord.phrasing_guidance: Describe preferred working style, not a fixed destiny of 'boss' or 'employee'.

conditional_results.when: manual: D10 lagna lord in the 9th house of D10
effects: independent work; business or self-directed roles suit

conditional_results.when: manual: D10 lagna lord in the 5th house of D10
effects: prefers service or a subordinate role

conditional_results.when: manual: D10 lagna lord in the 8th house of D10

varga/d10_tenth_house_and_lord.summary: The 10th house of D10 shows the true nature of one's work and conduct in society; any planet there can independently give rise and success, and the planet's nature points to the field.
common_outcomes: Planets in the D10 10th (and the other artha houses 2 and 6) colour the field: Sun politics or public service, Mars police/army, Jupiter law/teaching/priesthood/astrology, Mercury business/writing/trade, Venus entertainment and beauty, Saturn heavy or menial work, Rahu imports, Ketu exports (Rath 13.2.1).
Also study the 7th of D10, the arudha (pada) of the 10th (Rath).
The 10th from the arudha lagna in D10 shows perceived status in career, as opposed to the 10th from the D10 lagna (PVR 9.3).

by_area.career: Core use.

strengtheners: strong planet in the D10 10th
10th lord of D10 well placed

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. XIII 13.2.1
source_views.view: The artha trikona (2, 6, 10) of D10 governs functioning; any planet in the D10 10th can give power, rise and success; the 7th, as pada to the 10th, should also be studied; lists fields by planet dominating these houses.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. II sec. 7
source_views.view: In D10 the focus is the 10th house; the artha trikonas (2, 6, 10) normally decide the choice of profession.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 9.3
source_views.view: The 10th from lagna in D10 shows true conduct in society and the true nature of one's work; the 10th from the arudha lagna in D10 shows how that conduct is perceived and one's status in career; A10 in D10 shows the workplace.

source_views.source: Saravali 33.2-6 (Santhanam tr.)
source_views.view: Classically, the 10th from the stronger of lagna and Moon is the house of karma; if its lord is strong karma prospers; occupants of the 10th from the Moon or lagna shape livelihood by their nature (D1 rule, the basis D10 refines).

varga/d10_tenth_house_and_lord.disagreements: Saravali works from the D1 10th (from lagna or Moon); Rath and PVR transfer the analysis into D10.
varga/d10_tenth_house_and_lord.phrasing_guidance: Offer fields as broad families of work; avoid stigmatising labels like 'menial'.

conditional_results.when: manual: the Sun dominates the 2nd, 6th or 10th of D10
manual: Mars dominates the 2nd, 6th or 10th of D10
manual: Jupiter dominates the 2nd, 6th or 10th of D10
manual: Mercury dominates the 2nd, 6th or 10th of D10
manual: Venus dominates the 2nd, 6th or 10th of D10
manual: Saturn dominates the 2nd, 6th or 10th of D10
manual: any planet occupies the 10th house of D10
effects: can independently give power, rise and success in career

varga/planets_strong_in_d10.summary: A planet in its exaltation, moolatrikona or own sign in D10 is strong for career; its periods bring career gains, especially if linked to the D10 lagna or power points; debilitated malefics in key D10 houses damage the matters of those houses.
common_outcomes: Expect career progress in the periods of planets strong in D10, particularly if they relate to the D10 lagna, 10th or their lords.
A debilitated malefic in the D10 7th damages business and pushes towards service (Rath).
rare_outcomes: PVR: a planet exalted in the ghati lagna of D10 can give power and authority in its period.

by_area.career: Core use.

weakeners_or_cancellations: debility or combustion in D10
varga/planets_strong_in_d10.lagna_or_context_notes: The calculator's D9 dignity facts do not cover D10; D10 dignity must be judged manually.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 6.6 and 16.5.1
source_views.view: Exaltation, moolatrikona or own sign in a divisional chart makes a planet very strong in that chart; a planet gives the results promised by its divisional positions, e.g. a planet exalted in ghati lagna in D10 can give power and authority.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. XIII 13.2.2 and ch. XI (chart example)
source_views.view: A debilitated malefic in the 7th of D10 encourages service and damages business; in the example it destroyed the business.

source_views.source: BPHS 7.1-8 (tr. Santhanam, with notes)
source_views.view: A dasha lord dignified in the relevant division gives that division's results (Santhanam's example: dignified in the chaturvimsamsa, wide learning); a bhava flourishes when its lord is in a benefic shodasamsa.

source_views.source: Saravali 45.22 (applied by analogy)
source_views.view: Gives graded results by navamsa dignity (exaltation full, own moderate-good, enemy/debilitation little); no equivalent dasamsa rule is stated in Saravali.

varga/planets_strong_in_d10.disagreements: Classical texts state dignity-by-division rules mainly for the navamsa; applying them to D10 is the modern practice (PVR, Rath) following BPHS 7's instruction to judge each matter in its division.
varga/planets_strong_in_d10.phrasing_guidance: Speak of periods that favour professional growth rather than guaranteed promotions.

conditional_results.when: manual: dasha lord is exalted, moolatrikona or own sign in D10
manual: a debilitated malefic in the 7th house of D10

varga/service_vs_business_in_d10.summary: In D10 the 6th house shows service (employment) and the 7th business; whichever is stronger or more occupied indicates the path; the 9th is the boss, the 5th subordinates, the 8th retirement.
common_outcomes: Stronger or more occupied D10 6th: service; stronger D10 7th: own business (Rath 13.2.2).
Benefic influence on the D10 9th: helpful boss; malefic obstruction on it: trouble from the boss in that planet's period (Rath 13.2.3).
The 3rd, 8th and 12th of D10 (3rd from the 1st, 6th and 10th) cause problems; 8th shows retirement, 3rd short leave, 12th long leave (Rath 13.2.3).
rare_outcomes: Rath: the 7th lord's period can unsettle a job, since the 7th (business) is the maraka of the 6th (service).

by_area.career: Core use.
by_area.finance: The 2nd of D10 (8th from the 7th) governs the finance to start a business (Rath 13.2.4).

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. XIII 13.2.2-13.2.4
source_views.view: 6th rules service, 7th business; more planets or strength in one decides; 7th lord's period may destabilise service; boss from the 9th, subordinates from the 5th; 3rd, 8th and 12th cause problems; the 2nd governs business finance.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. II sec. 7
source_views.view: In D10 the 7th is business and the maraka of the 6th (service); the 8th, being 11th from the 10th, is retirement and inherited business; the 4th is the premises; the 9th the boss.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 9.3 and 13.4.1
source_views.view: A10 in D10 shows the workplace; choose the house in the divisional chart for the matter (e.g. the 7th for dealings with others in that sphere).

varga/service_vs_business_in_d10.phrasing_guidance: Offer as leanings, not instructions to quit a job or start a business.

conditional_results.when: manual: the 6th house of D10 is stronger or more occupied than the 7th
manual: the 7th house of D10 is stronger than the 6th
manual: running period lord has malefic argala on the 9th of D10

varga/d10_eighth_house.summary: The 8th house and lord of D10 can bring career trouble (loss of job, lawsuits, debt) or, if linked to the D10 lagna lord, inheritance of an enterprise or headship; it also marks retirement.
common_outcomes: 8th lord or 8th-house planets of D10 can bring loss of service, lawsuits, even imprisonment in their periods, depending on nature and strength (Rath).
If well connected to the D10 lagna lord, the 8th can give inheritance of factories, institutions or party leadership (Rath).
A benefic in the D10 8th favours business; a malefic there favours service (Rath).
rare_outcomes: Rath: the 8th lord in the D10 lagna shows chronic debt.

by_area.career: Core use.
by_area.finance: Debt or large loans for enterprise (Rath).

strengtheners: 8th lord with benefic argala on the D10 lagna lord
weakeners_or_cancellations: 8th lord in the D10 lagna

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. XI (8th house)
source_views.view: The D10 8th lord or 8th-house planets can cause loss of service, lawsuits and imprisonment; well connected to the D10 lagna lord they give inheritance of enterprises or headship; a benefic in the 8th favours business, a malefic service; the 8th lord in the D10 lagna shows chronic debt.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. XIII 13.2
source_views.view: The 8th, as 11th from the 10th, is retirement or end of career; beneficially disposed it gives big loans for enterprise, ill-disposed endless debt.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 12.5 (Example 39, ashtakavarga of D-10)
source_views.view: Strong sarvashtakavarga points in the D10 8th explained struggles in a politician's career despite a strong D10 lagna.

varga/d10_eighth_house.phrasing_guidance: Never predict imprisonment or lawsuits; speak of periods needing care with obligations and contracts.

conditional_results.when: manual: running period is of the D10 8th lord or a planet in the D10 8th, and it is weak or afflicted
manual: D10 8th lord well connected to the D10 lagna lord

varga/amatyakaraka_and_career.summary: The amatyakaraka (second-highest degree chara karaka, the 'minister') is linked to profession and advisory or official roles; sources state the rules in D1 (and karakamsa) and modern authors read it alongside D10, but no source read gives a D10-specific amatyakaraka rule.
common_outcomes: 10th lord joined or aspected by the amatyakaraka or its dispositor: an important position with authority (BPHS 40.1; PVR 11.8).
Amatyakaraka strong in own or exaltation sign, in a trine from the lagna, or conjunct the atmakaraka: ministerial or senior advisory roles (PVR 11.8).
Check the amatyakaraka's D10 placement as supporting evidence for career direction (Rath's examples).
rare_outcomes: BPHS 33 (via Santhanam): deity of worship can also be read from the 6th navamsa from the amatyakaraka's navamsa.

by_area.career: Core use.
by_area.spirituality: Rath ch. XII and BPHS 33: 6th from the amatyakaraka in D9 for places/deity of worship.

strengtheners: amatyakaraka in a kendra or trikona from the atmakaraka (PVR 11.8)
varga/amatyakaraka_and_career.lagna_or_context_notes: Seven vs eight karaka schemes can change which planet is amatyakaraka (BPHS 32.1-2). See karaka/amatyakaraka for significations.

source_views.source: BPHS 40.1 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: If the 10th lord is joined or aspected by the amatyakaraka's dispositor, or the amatyakaraka itself, the native is a chief in the king's court.
The amatyakaraka is the planet next after the atmakaraka in degrees.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 11.8 (Raaja sambandha yogas)
source_views.view: 10th lord with AmK or its dispositor; AK and AmK conjoined; AmK strong in own or exaltation; AmK in a trine from lagna; AmK in kendra/trine from AK: all give association with rulers and ministerial roles.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. XIII (example charts)
source_views.view: The amatyakaraka plays an important role in determining profession; in examples he reads its rasi, navamsa and dasamsa placements together.

varga/amatyakaraka_and_career.disagreements: No source read states a rule for the amatyakaraka in D10 as such; the D10 use is inferred from Rath's worked examples.
varga/amatyakaraka_and_career.phrasing_guidance: Use as supporting colour for advisory, managerial or official roles.

conditional_results.when: manual: D1 10th lord conjunct or aspected by the amatyakaraka or its dispositor
effects: position of authority or high office

conditional_results.when: manual: amatyakaraka in own or exaltation sign, or in a trine from the lagna

varga/d10_yogas.summary: Yogas can be read inside D10; raja yogas of D1 should be confirmed there (and in D5), and solar yogas like Budha-Aditya are most powerful in divisional charts such as D10.
common_outcomes: Confirm a D1 raja yoga by checking whether the same planets are strong and linked in D10 (Rath 13.2).
Sun and Mercury together in D10 (not too close): strong Budha-Aditya yoga in career, felt in the periods of Sun, Mercury and that sign (PVR 11.2.4).
rare_outcomes: Rath (example): a five-planet malika yoga in D10 coincided with the real raja yoga period.

by_area.career: Core use.

weakeners_or_cancellations: combust Mercury weakens Budha-Aditya (PVR 11.2.4)

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. XIII 13.2
source_views.view: Raja yogas need to be confirmed in the panchamamsa (D5) and the dasamsa (D10).

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 11.2 and 11.2.4
source_views.view: Solar yogas can be applied in D9 and D10; Budha-Aditya yoga is most powerful in divisional charts like D10 and gives career results throughout life, especially in the periods of Sun, Mercury and the sign involved.

source_views.source: BPHS 6.42-53 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Good vargas are counted across schemes and the resulting grades are used in raja yogas; divisions of combust or weak planets are ignored because they destroy good yogas.

varga/d10_yogas.phrasing_guidance: Present as confirmation of potential already in the birth chart.

conditional_results.when: manual: a D1 raja yoga's planets are also strong and connected in D10
manual: Sun and Mercury in the same sign in D10 and Mercury not combust
effects: skill and recognition in career; active in Sun/Mercury periods

varga/classical_profession_via_navamsa.summary: Before D10 became standard, classical texts read the kind of profession from the lord of the navamsa occupied by the 10th lord (from lagna, Moon or Sun, whichever is strongest); this rule complements a D10 reading.
common_outcomes: Find the 10th lord (from the strongest of lagna, Moon, Sun), note its D9 sign and that sign's lord; the lord's nature gives the means of livelihood (Phaladeepika 5.1-5.8).

Sun's navamsa: medicine, wool, metals, government service; Moon's: water products, agriculture, cattle, clothes; Mars's: metals, fighting, cooking, land, weapons; Mercury's: writing, scriptures, clerical work, astrology (Phaladeepika 5.2-5.5).

by_area.career: Core use.
by_area.finance: Phaladeepika 5.1: the source of wealth (father, mother, enemy, friend, sibling, spouse, servant) follows the planet in the 10th from the stronger of lagna and Moon.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 5.1-5.5 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Profession is that of the lord of the navamsa occupied by the 10th lord counted from the lagna, Moon or Sun, whichever is strongest; gives the trades for the Sun's, Moon's, Mars's and Mercury's navamsas and onwards.

source_views.source: Saravali 33.2-6
source_views.view: The 10th from the stronger of lagna and Moon is karmasthana; a strong 10th lord makes karma prosper; occupants of the 10th from Moon or lagna shape livelihood by their nature.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. VIII 8.1
source_views.view: Skill and intelligence, which shape the profession, are seen from the 5th from the navamsa lagna or karakamsa.

varga/classical_profession_via_navamsa.disagreements: Classical texts derive profession from D9 (navamsa of the 10th lord); modern authors (PVR, Rath) use D10. They can be read together.
varga/classical_profession_via_navamsa.phrasing_guidance: Translate old trade lists into modern families of work.

conditional_results.when: manual: lord of the D9 sign occupied by the 10th lord is the Sun
effects: work with medicine, metals, wool, government or respected patrons

conditional_results.when: manual: lord of the D9 sign occupied by the 10th lord is the Moon
effects: water products, agriculture, cattle, clothing trade, service under a woman

conditional_results.when: manual: lord of the D9 sign occupied by the 10th lord is Mars
effects: metals, land, weapons, cooking, adventurous or combative work

conditional_results.when: manual: lord of the D9 sign occupied by the 10th lord is Mercury
effects: writing, clerical work, scriptures, astrology, priestly work

varga/birth_time_sensitivity.summary: The D10 lagna changes sign roughly every 12 minutes of birth time (the D1 lagna moves about 1 degree in 4 minutes and each dasamsa is 3 degrees), and planets near a 3-degree boundary can also flip sign; so D10 is only as reliable as the birth time.
common_outcomes: If the reported birth time could be off by more than a few minutes, treat the D10 lagna and house positions as uncertain.
Check whether the ascendant degree is within about 1 degree (4 minutes) of a 3-degree boundary, or the Moon within a few arc-minutes of one: then two D10 versions are possible.
rare_outcomes: PVR: the Moon moves about 1 arc-minute in 1.8 minutes, so even a 2-minute error can move it across a D10 boundary when it is right at the edge.

by_area.career: Reliability of all D10 career judgements depends on this.

varga/birth_time_sensitivity.lagna_or_context_notes: Slow planets rarely change D10 sign within a few minutes (the Sun changes D10 sign about every 3 days, the Moon about every 6 hours), so planet signs are usually safe unless near a boundary.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 32.1-32.2.1
source_views.view: Twins born minutes apart differ because divisional lagnas change fast; the lagna moves 1 degree in about 4 minutes and changes sign in D10 in 12 minutes (D24 in 5); check planets at varga borders and consider both positions.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. II sec. 8
source_views.view: For proper use of divisional charts the birth time should first be rectified using the navamsa, dwadasamsa and other key divisions, then fine-tuned.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XI
source_views.view: The exact moment of birth is rarely recorded; rectification is for experienced astrologers using pronounced life events.
Each dasamsa spans 3 degrees, the basis of the sensitivity.

varga/birth_time_sensitivity.phrasing_guidance: Be open that fine career detail depends on an accurate birth time; never present D10 specifics as certain when the time is approximate.

conditional_results.when: manual: D1 ascendant degree is within about 1 degree of a multiple of 3 degrees in its sign
effects: D10 lagna uncertain; consider both candidate D10 lagnas

varga/uncertain_d10_handling.summary: When D10 is uncertain, sources say to rectify from known life events (fix D9 or D10 lagna from marriage and career history, then refine), consider both candidate positions, and otherwise fall back on D1 and D9 rather than averaging.
common_outcomes: If career history is known, test each candidate D10 lagna against it and keep the one that explains the past (PVR 32.1, 32.3).
Do not use an averaged time: a 6-minute window covers people with different D10 charts (PVR 32.1).

Without verification, lean on the D1 10th house/lord, 10th from the Moon and the classical navamsa-of-10th-lord rule, and mark D10-only conclusions as tentative (Raman ch. X advises beginners to rest on rasi and navamsa).
rare_outcomes: PVR warns most textbook rectification formulas (e.g. Pranapada in navamsa, kunda) fail the test of twins; only event-based rectification works.

by_area.career: Core use.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 32.1 and 32.3
source_views.view: Reported birth times are seldom accurate; the only correct rectification finds a nearby time that explains the person's nature and known events; do not average a range; first fix the D9 or D10 lagna, then go to higher charts, revisiting if stuck.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. II sec. 8
source_views.view: Rectify first using the navamsa, dwadasamsa and other important divisions before relying on divisional charts.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. X-XI
source_views.view: Beginners should judge from rasi and navamsa; birth times can be rectified only by experienced astrologers from pronounced life events.

varga/uncertain_d10_handling.disagreements: PVR treats D1-only prediction as unscientific and insists on rectification; Raman accepts rasi-plus-navamsa judgement as the practical baseline.
varga/uncertain_d10_handling.phrasing_guidance: State plainly when a career statement rests on an unverified D10 and offer it as a possibility.

varga/d10_and_dasha.summary: Career events are timed by the periods of planets well or badly placed in D10 and linked to its lagna, 10th and power points; Narayana dasa can be run on D10 itself.
common_outcomes: Promotion: planets or signs connected to the ghati lagna and to the arudha lagna (or its 5th/10th) in D10; e.g. the AL lord in the 10th from AL aspecting GL (PVR 6.5).
Job start: the period of the 5th lord from the D10 lagna (Rath, ch. X example; and 13.2: joining a new job is timed from the 5th house).
A well-disposed planet aspecting A3 in D10 can bring writing or publishing (PVR 16.5.1).
rare_outcomes: PVR runs Narayana dasa of D10 to time career changes (18.5).

by_area.career: Core use.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 6.5, 16.5.1 and 18.5
source_views.view: Promotions are linked to ghati lagna and arudha lagna in D10; a planet exalted in GL in D10 can give authority in its period; Narayana dasa of D10 times career events.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. XIII 13.2 and ch. X example (5th lord in D10)
source_views.view: The timing of joining a new job is done from the 5th house; in an example the D10 5th lord's sub-sub period gave the appointment.

source_views.source: BPHS 7.30-32 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Dasha results are to be declared according to the planet's vimshopaka grade across the divisions (eight grades from full to very little).

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV
source_views.view: A dasha lord's results are modified by its divisional (navamsa) strength; e.g. full political success from the Sun in the 10th only if equally strong in the navamsa.

varga/d10_and_dasha.phrasing_guidance: Give timing as favourable windows, not dates.

conditional_results.when: manual: running period lord is strong in D10 and linked to the D10 lagna, 10th house or their lords
manual: running sub-period or sub-sub-period lord is the 5th lord from the D10 lagna
conditional_results.source: Rath, Crux 13.2 and ch. X example

varga/d10_deities.summary: Parashara assigns a presiding deity of the ten directions to each dasamsa (Indra, Agni, Yama, Rakshasa, Varuna, Vayu, Kubera, Isana, Brahma, Ananta; reversed in even signs), but gives no rule for how they modify results.
common_outcomes: Record the deity only as descriptive colour; no interpretive rule is sourced.

source_views.source: BPHS 6.13-14 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: The ten dasamsas of an odd sign are presided over by Indra, Agni, Yama, Rakshasa, Varuna, Vayu, Kubera, Isana, Brahma and Ananta; in reverse order for an even sign.

varga/d10_deities.phrasing_guidance: Do not draw predictions from the deity alone.

varga/what_d9_shows.summary: The navamsa (D9, each sign split into nine parts of 3 deg 20 min) is the chart Parashara assigns to the spouse; modern authors widen it to marriage, dharma (one's duty and values), the inner self and the real strength of the planets.
common_outcomes: Use D9 first for questions about marriage and the spouse, after reading the D1 promise.
Use D9 dignity as a test of how well a planet can deliver what its D1 placement promises.
Read D9 for values, sense of duty, basic skills and how the person deals with others (PVR), not only for marriage.
rare_outcomes: PVR notes that where marriage is not treated as a duty but only as living together, the D1 chart may describe the relationship better than D9.
Rath also reads love and affection from Venus and D9, and skill or intelligence (which shapes profession) from the 5th from the navamsa lagna or karakamsa.

by_area.personality: Inner nature, values and sense of duty (PVR 6.3; Rath ch. IV 4.1).
by_area.career: Indirectly: classical texts read the profession from the navamsa sign of the 10th lord (see dashamsa file).
by_area.relationships: Spouse and married life: the main use of D9 (BPHS 7.1-8; PVR 6.3, 13.4.1; Raman HPA ch. X).
by_area.family: Spouse's family can be read from D9 (PVR 13.4.2).
by_area.spirituality: Dharma; the karakamsa and the 12th from it in D9 are read for liberation (PVR 7.3.6; BPHS ch. 33).

varga/what_d9_shows.lagna_or_context_notes: PVR calls the navamsa the 'dharmamsa' because its seed house is the 9th (dharma): marrying and living with a spouse are treated as duties.

source_views.source: BPHS 7.1-8 (tr. R. Santhanam, vol. 1)
source_views.view: Lists the use of each of the 16 divisions: the spouse is to be judged from the navamsa, power and position from the dasamsa.

source_views.source: BPHS 6.12 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Defines the navamsa: counted from the sign itself for a movable sign, from the 9th for a fixed sign and from the 5th for a dual sign.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 6.3 Table 11 and 18.5
source_views.view: D9 covers marriage and everything about the spouse, dharma, interaction with others, basic skills and the inner self; it is also called dharmamsa because its seed is the 9th house.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. X (The Shadvargas)
source_views.view: Each of Parashara's divisions is used for one area, e.g. the navamsa for the wife; navamsa is the most important division and most astrologers judge from rasi and navamsa together.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. II sec. 7 and ch. VIII 8.1
source_views.view: D9 is the spouse chart in the physical-plane group (D1-D12) and holds first place among the divisions after the rasi chart; love and affection are also seen from Venus and the navamsa.

varga/what_d9_shows.disagreements: Parashara names only the spouse for D9; PVR and Rath extend it to dharma, inner self and skills. PVR adds that in cultures where marriage is not a duty the D1 may describe relationships better than D9.
varga/what_d9_shows.phrasing_guidance: Describe D9 as the chart of partnership and inner values; avoid saying it decides whether someone will or will not marry.

varga/d9_weight_vs_d1.summary: D1 is the main chart and D9 the most important division after it; texts differ on how far D9 can override D1, from 'half the effect' (Phaladeepika) to 'the navamsa effects prevail when its lord is stronger' (Saravali).
common_outcomes: Read D1 for what is promised; use D9 to confirm, strengthen or weaken it.

When a planet's D1 and D9 positions disagree, weigh the dispositors: Saravali and Phaladeepika say that if the navamsa lord is stronger than the sign lord, the navamsa result takes over (stated for the Moon).
In the vimshopaka (20-point) scheme the navamsa carries the second-largest weight after the rasi in the six- and seven-division schemes.
rare_outcomes: In the 16-division scheme the navamsa (3 points) is close to the rasi (3.5) and below the shashtiamsa (4).

by_area.personality: Rath: the nature of the person blends the rasi and navamsa lagna signs, with the navamsa lagna predominating.

varga/d9_weight_vs_d1.lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS vimshopaka weights for the navamsa: 5 of 20 in the six-division scheme, 4.5 in the seven-division scheme, 1.5 in the ten-division scheme, 3 in the sixteen-division scheme.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 3.2-3.3 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 1950)
source_views.view: Effects are full in the rasi and half in the other divisions (one quarter in the shodasamsa, dasamsa and shashtyamsa); some authors hold that the navamsa gives effects equal to the rasi and bhava.

source_views.source: BPHS 7.17-25 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Gives the 20-point vimshopaka weights: navamsa 5 in shadvarga (rasi 6), 4.5 in saptavarga (rasi 5), 1.5 in dasavarga (rasi 3, shashtiamsa 5), 3 in shodasavarga (rasi 3.5, shashtiamsa 4).

source_views.source: Saravali 24.22-24 (Santhanam tr.)
source_views.view: If the navamsa lord is stronger than the sign lord, only the navamsa effects of the Moon come to pass, as against her sign position (attributed to the Vriddha Yavanas).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.17
source_views.view: If the lord of the Moon's navamsa is strong, the results given for the Moon's sign and aspects are nullified and the navamsa results take over.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. II sec. 7 and ch. IV (after 4.3.12)
source_views.view: After the rasi chart the navamsa holds first place; sign results are a blend of rasi and navamsa lagna with the navamsa in predominance.

source_views.source: C.S. Patel, Navamsa in Astrology, ch. 1
source_views.view: Some astrologers give the navamsa more value than the rasi; calls the rasi the tree and the navamsa the fruit, and notes that the nakshatra quarter coincides exactly with a navamsa.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. X
source_views.view: Navamsa is the most important division; begin by judging from rasi and navamsa together.

varga/d9_weight_vs_d1.disagreements: Phaladeepika 3.3 gives divisions half the force of the rasi but reports others who make the navamsa equal; Saravali/Phaladeepika (Moon) let a stronger navamsa lord override the rasi; Patel and Rath lean towards the navamsa predominating; PVR assigns each chart its own sphere instead of ranking them.
varga/d9_weight_vs_d1.phrasing_guidance: Present D9 as a refinement of D1, not a replacement; when they conflict, say results are mixed rather than choosing one silently.

conditional_results.when: manual: the lord of the Moon's navamsa is stronger than the lord of the Moon's sign
effects: the Moon's navamsa results prevail over her sign results

varga/vargottama.summary: A planet is vargottama when it occupies the same sign in D1 and D9 (the first navamsa of a movable sign, the middle of a fixed sign, the last of a dual sign); texts treat it as a source of strength and good results.
common_outcomes: Treat a vargottama planet as stronger and more reliable in giving its D1 results.
Its dasha tends to be favourable (Phaladeepika 20.22).
Combine with sign dignity: vargottama in own or exaltation sign is doubly strong; vargottama in the debilitation sign doubles the debility (Patel).
rare_outcomes: Patel warns that several vargottama planets did not give good results in a chart where they had low sarvashtakavarga points; he reads a vargottama planet as amplifying the house it is in, good or bad by bindus.
Raman: a strong, well-aspected Jupiter in vargottama makes a great lecturer or orator.
strengtheners: own sign or exaltation in D1 together with vargottama (Patel ch. 3)
benefic aspect
weakeners_or_cancellations: vargottama in the debilitation sign (Patel calls it neecha-vargottama)
combustion or eclipse (Phaladeepika 20.22 says results are then mixed)
low sarvashtakavarga bindus in that house (Patel ch. 3)
varga/vargottama.lagna_or_context_notes: Vargottama degree ranges: movable signs 0-3 deg 20 min, fixed signs 13 deg 20 min-16 deg 40 min, dual signs 26 deg 40 min-30 deg.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 3.1 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Vargottama is the navamsa in a sign that bears the same name as the sign itself.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 1.34 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, vol. I)
source_views.view: The vargottama navamsa is the first in a movable sign, the middle one in a fixed sign and the last in a dual sign; Sastri's note adds that planets in vargottama are said to produce much good.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.22
source_views.view: The dasha of a planet in vargottama gives favourable results; mixed if that planet is eclipsed or debilitated.

source_views.source: Saravali 24.22-24
source_views.view: The Moon's good effects are full in a vargottama navamsa, medium in her own navamsa and minor in others' navamsas; for bad effects it is the reverse.

source_views.source: C.S. Patel, Navamsa in Astrology, ch. 3
source_views.view: Distinguishes own-sign, exalted and debilitated vargottama; lists results of each vargottama planet; links strength to sarvashtakavarga bindus.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XX (education)
source_views.view: Jupiter powerful, well aspected and vargottama makes the person a great lecturer and orator.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 11.7.3 (More Raja Yogas, item 15 and footnote 40)
source_views.view: Defines vargottamamsa as the same sign in rasi and navamsa; uses a strong Moon in vargottama aspected by four or more planets as a raja yoga.

varga/vargottama.disagreements: Classical texts call vargottama simply auspicious; Patel qualifies it by sign dignity (debilitated vargottama is doubly weak) and by ashtakavarga bindus.
varga/vargottama.phrasing_guidance: Say the planet acts with extra consistency and steadiness; do not promise specific events from vargottama alone.

conditional_results.when: md_vargottama == true and (md_combust == true or md_dignity == 'debilitated')
effects: results mixed rather than wholly good

conditional_results.source: C.S. Patel, Navamsa in Astrology ch. 3
C.S. Patel, Navamsa in Astrology ch. 3

varga/vargottama_lagna_and_moon.summary: A vargottama lagna or Moon is singled out: aspected by four or more planets it is a royal yoga, though Saravali also says a vargottama lagna with no aspect at all makes raja yogas fail.
common_outcomes: A vargottama lagna or Moon strengthens the whole chart and the person's standing in their group (Brihat Jataka via Patel: head of their class).
Check how many planets aspect it: four or more (other than the Moon) is a classic raja yoga.
rare_outcomes: Saravali 39.5: a vargottama lagna that receives no aspect from any planet makes raja yogas fail.

by_area.personality: Leader within one's circle (Brihat Jataka 21.7 via Patel).
by_area.career: Rise above birth circumstances when the yoga is full (Phaladeepika 7.5; JP 7.5).

strengtheners: four or more planets aspecting (Phaladeepika 7.5; Jataka Parijata 7.5)
weakeners_or_cancellations: vargottama lagna with no planetary aspect (Saravali 39.5)
varga/vargottama_lagna_and_moon.lagna_or_context_notes: Jataka Parijata 7.5 restricts the aspecting planets to those in the 4th, 7th and 10th (Sastri's note), so that they fully aspect the lagna or Moon.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 7.5-7.6
source_views.view: A rising vargottama navamsa or a vargottama Moon, with the lagna aspected by four planets other than the Moon, makes even a person of low birth a king; lagna lord in a kendra or the 9th in vargottama with the 9th lord exalted or in own sign in a similar amsa gives royal status.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.5 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Moon or lagna in vargottama aspected by planets in the 4th, 10th and 7th makes a leader of men; Sastri's note cites Saravali and Brihat Jataka for four or more aspecting planets.

source_views.source: Saravali 35.6 and 39.5
source_views.view: Lagna or Moon in vargottama aspected by 5 or 6 planets makes a king even from a mean family; but a vargottama lagna not aspected by any planet makes the raja yogas a failure.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 21.7 (via C.S. Patel, Navamsa in Astrology ch. 3)
source_views.view: When the rising navamsa is vargottama the person becomes head of the class described for that navamsa.

source_views.source: C.S. Patel, Navamsa in Astrology, ch. 3
source_views.view: A vargottama ascendant makes the chart inherently strong; lagna and Moon vargottama get the most importance.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. IV example (chart 16)
source_views.view: Uses a vargottama Taurus lagna to describe stature, complexion and intelligence.

varga/vargottama_lagna_and_moon.disagreements: Number of aspecting planets: four (Phaladeepika, JP) vs five or six (Saravali 35.6). Saravali 39.5 adds a negative rule (unaspected vargottama lagna spoils raja yogas) not found in the others.
varga/vargottama_lagna_and_moon.phrasing_guidance: Speak of natural steadiness and leadership potential; 'king' yogas should be translated into ordinary standing and influence.

conditional_results.when: manual: lagna or Moon is vargottama and aspected by four or more planets (other than the Moon)
effects: rise to high status even from humble birth

conditional_results.when: manual: lagna is vargottama and aspected by no planet
effects: raja yogas in the chart fail to deliver

varga/exalted_in_d9.summary: A planet in its exaltation sign in D9 gives its good effects in full (Saravali 45.22); it can lift a weak or debilitated D1 placement.
common_outcomes: Upgrade the planet's delivery: its D1 significations come through more fully.
Especially notable when the planet is debilitated in D1 (see d1_d9_dignity_reversal and neecha_bhanga_via_d9).
rare_outcomes: Rath: a debilitated planet in an exalted navamsa gives sudden elevation; if also retrograde the rise is short-lived.
strengtheners: also vargottama or exalted in D1
benefic association
weakeners_or_cancellations: retrograde (Rath, for a D1-debilitated planet)

source_views.source: Saravali 45.22
source_views.view: In its exaltation navamsa a planet's good effects are full; in its own navamsa they equal those of its own sign; friendly navamsa gives moderate results; enemy or debilitation navamsa gives little good.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.144 (tr. Sastri, vol. II)
source_views.view: Mercury debilitated but in its exaltation navamsa brings prosperity at the end of its dasha though the start is barren.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. IX 9.2
source_views.view: A debilitated planet placed in an exalted navamsa gives neechabhanga raja yoga with sudden elevation; if retrograde the elevation is short.

source_views.source: C.S. Patel, Navamsa in Astrology, ch. 1 and ch. 13 (Deva Keralam verse)
source_views.view: A planet debilitated in rasi but exalted in navamsa makes the person happy.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 6.6
source_views.view: A planet in moolatrikona, own or exaltation sign in a divisional chart is very strong in that chart; counting such charts gives its amsa strength.

varga/exalted_in_d9.phrasing_guidance: Say the planet has strong inner backing that helps its promise come through; avoid guaranteeing outcomes.

effects: good effects of the planet come in full
good effects of the sub-period lord come in full

varga/debilitated_in_d9.summary: A planet in its debilitation (or an enemy's) sign in D9 gives little of its good effects and its dasha is described as untoward, even if D1 looks good.
common_outcomes: Discount the planet's D1 promise; expect results that start well but do not hold, or come with struggle.
For Venus specifically, Saravali says a debilitation navamsa can take away even a large kingdom (raja yogas spoiled).
rare_outcomes: Rath reads Jupiter debilitated in D9 as 'rajbhanga' (fall from fortune) and uses debilitated D9 planets as signs of marital trouble.

by_area.relationships: Rath links debilitated D9 Jupiter (for a woman) or the D9 7th lord's weakness to marital difficulty.

weakeners_or_cancellations: also debilitated in D1 (Patel cites Deva Keralam: lagna lord debilitated in both, aspected by a malefic, gives an inwardly angry, somewhat miserly nature)

source_views.source: Saravali 45.22
source_views.view: In an enemy's or the debilitation navamsa the planet's good effects are quite little.

source_views.source: Saravali 39.22
source_views.view: Venus in its debilitation navamsa deprives the native even of a vast kingdom.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.170 (from Brihat Jataka, per Sastri's note)
source_views.view: The dasha of a planet in a debilitation or inimical navamsa is untoward.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.143
source_views.view: Mercury in its exaltation sign but debilitation navamsa makes the person unfit for work and poor during its dasha.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. X (charts 69-71)
source_views.view: Jupiter debilitated in the navamsa indicates rajbhanga (misfortune) and spoiled marriage despite good D1 promise.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV
source_views.view: Dasha results are modified by the favourable or unfavourable situation of the dasha lord in the navamsa; e.g. political success from the Sun in Aries in the 10th is full only if he is equally strong in the navamsa.

varga/debilitated_in_d9.phrasing_guidance: Say the planet's gifts need more effort to hold on to; never predict loss of marriage or fortune from this one factor.

effects: little of the planet's good effects
raja yogas undermined; loss of position
incompetence for work and poverty during the dasha

varga/own_sign_in_d9.summary: A planet in its own sign in D9 gives results like a planet in its own sign in D1: steady and good; all planets in own navamsas is a royal combination in Yavana texts.
common_outcomes: Read the planet as dependable and self-supported in its significations.
rare_outcomes: Brihat Yavana Jataka (via Patel): all planets in their own navamsas makes a splendid ruler.
strengtheners: vargottama in own sign (Deva Keralam via Patel: pleasures and raja yoga)
varga/own_sign_in_d9.lagna_or_context_notes: PVR's navamsa bala (Tajaka): own sign in D9 = 5 units, friend 2.5, enemy 1.25.

source_views.source: Saravali 45.22
source_views.view: In its own navamsa a planet gives results applicable to its own-sign placement.

source_views.source: Saravali 24.22-24
source_views.view: The Moon in her own navamsa gives medium (between vargottama and others') good results.

source_views.source: C.S. Patel, Navamsa in Astrology, ch. 13 (Deva Keralam 2 p.78 v.29; Brihat Yavana Jataka v.25)
source_views.view: A planet vargottama in its own sign gives pleasures and raja yoga; all planets in own navamsas make a powerful ruler.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 28.4.5
source_views.view: Navamsa bala: 5 units in own D9 sign, 2.5 in a friend's, 1.25 in an enemy's.

varga/own_sign_in_d9.phrasing_guidance: Say the planet acts from a secure base.

effects: results like the planet in its own sign

conditional_results.source: Deva Keralam via C.S. Patel ch. 13

varga/d1_d9_dignity_reversal.summary: When D1 and D9 dignity point opposite ways, the navamsa is often given the deciding vote: exalted in D1 but debilitated in D9 brings sorrow; debilitated in D1 but exalted in D9 brings happiness.
common_outcomes: Do not read an exalted D1 planet as wholly good if it is debilitated in D9; expect its promise to fall short.
Do not read a debilitated D1 planet as wholly bad if it is exalted in D9; expect late or eventual success.
rare_outcomes: Jataka Parijata (Mercury) times it: the reversed planet's dasha is barren at first and prosperous at the end.

source_views.source: Deva Keralam 2 p.78 v.29 (via C.S. Patel, Navamsa in Astrology ch. 13)
source_views.view: Exalted in sign but in debilitation navamsa gives grief; debilitated in sign with exaltation navamsa gives happiness.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.143-144
source_views.view: Mercury exalted in sign but in debilitation navamsa makes one unfit for work and poor in its dasha; Mercury debilitated but in exaltation navamsa brings prosperity at the end of its dasha.

source_views.source: Saravali 45.22
source_views.view: Good effects are full in the exaltation navamsa and little in the debilitation navamsa, independent of the rasi.

source_views.source: C.S. Patel, Navamsa in Astrology, ch. 1
source_views.view: The Sun in Aries (exalted) in Libra navamsa is of no avail; the Sun in Libra in Aries navamsa gives very good results.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. IX 9.2
source_views.view: A debilitated planet in an exalted navamsa gives sudden elevation (neechabhanga raja yoga).

varga/d1_d9_dignity_reversal.disagreements: Jataka Parijata states the rule for Mercury only; Patel (via Deva Keralam) and Rath state it generally.
varga/d1_d9_dignity_reversal.phrasing_guidance: Frame as 'promise vs delivery': a strong-looking placement may need care, a weak-looking one may mature well.

effects: promise of the exaltation not delivered; sorrow or setbacks in the period
conditional_results.source: Deva Keralam via Patel ch. 13; Jataka Parijata 18.143

effects: happiness and rise; results improve towards the end of the dasha
conditional_results.source: Deva Keralam via Patel ch. 13; Jataka Parijata 18.144; Rath ch. IX 9.2

conditional_results.when: md_dignity == 'debilitated' and md_d9_dignity == 'exalted' and md_retro == true
conditional_results.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology ch. IX 9.2

varga/neecha_bhanga_via_d9.summary: D9 can cancel a D1 debilitation: classically when the lord of the navamsa occupied by the debilitated planet is in a kendra or trikona (Jataka Parijata 7.14); modern authors add the debilitated planet itself being exalted in D9.
common_outcomes: For a debilitated D1 planet, find its D9 sign lord and check whether that lord sits in a kendra or trikona.
Also check whether the debilitated planet is exalted in D9 (Rath, Patel).
rare_outcomes: Jataka Parijata 7.14 adds an alternative: a movable lagna, or the lagna lord in a movable-sign navamsa.

by_area.career: Rise to power or high position (JP 7.14; Rath).

weakeners_or_cancellations: retrograde debilitated planet in exalted navamsa: rise is brief (Rath)
varga/neecha_bhanga_via_d9.lagna_or_context_notes: The calculator's own neecha_bhanga yoga uses D1 rules; this entry covers only the D9 routes. See yoga/neecha_bhanga for the D1 definitions.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.14 (tr. Sastri, vol. I)
source_views.view: If the lord of the navamsa occupied by a debilitated planet is in a kendra or trikona, and the birth lagna is a movable sign or the lagna lord is in a movable-sign navamsa, the person becomes a king or very powerful.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 7.26-29
source_views.view: Gives the D1 routes to cancellation (lord of the debilitation sign or of the exaltation sign in a kendra from lagna or Moon, mutual kendras, aspect of the sign lord); no D9 route is legible in the OCR of this edition.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. IX 9.2
source_views.view: A debilitated planet in an exalted navamsa gives neechabhanga raja yoga with sudden promotion.

source_views.source: C.S. Patel, Navamsa in Astrology, ch. 1
source_views.view: A planet debilitated in rasi but exalted in navamsa makes the person happy.

varga/neecha_bhanga_via_d9.disagreements: JP 7.14 cancels through the navamsa dispositor; Rath and Patel cancel through the planet's own D9 exaltation. Phaladeepika's legible slokas use only D1 conditions.
varga/neecha_bhanga_via_d9.phrasing_guidance: Present as 'an early weakness that can turn into strength'; avoid promising fame or power.

effects: debility cancelled; sudden elevation in the period
conditional_results.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux ch. IX 9.2; Patel ch. 1

conditional_results.when: manual: the planet is debilitated in D1 and the lord of its D9 sign is in a kendra or trikona, with a movable lagna or the lagna lord in a movable-sign navamsa

varga/d9_lagna_and_lord.summary: The navamsa lagna (the D9 sign of the ascendant degree) and its lord describe the inner person, appearance and disposition; texts weigh it alongside, or above, the D1 lagna.
common_outcomes: Blend the D1 and D9 lagna signs when describing temperament, giving extra weight to the D9 lagna (Rath).
Judge physique and disposition from the navamsa lagna or the strongest planet; or from the lord of the Moon's navamsa (Saravali 9.45-46, 51.1).
Read the navamsa lagna as the self in marriage and dharma (PVR); its dasha can bring marriage.
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 21.7 (via Patel) assigns a social character to each non-vargottama rising navamsa (e.g. Leo navamsa a ruler, Gemini navamsa learned).
Saravali ch. 51 gives a description for each of the 108 rising navamsas.

by_area.personality: Main use: temperament and appearance.
by_area.relationships: PVR: lagna in navamsa is the self as spouse and partner.

strengtheners: navamsa lagna lord well placed in D1, or benefics in the navamsa lagna (Patel ch. 3)
vargottama lagna
weakeners_or_cancellations: lords of the navamsa lagna, Moon sign and natal lagna all combust: Saravali lists this among short-life combinations [maraka: text predicts short life]
varga/d9_lagna_and_lord.lagna_or_context_notes: The navamsa lagna moves through nine signs while the D1 lagna crosses one sign (about 2 hours), so it needs a reliable birth time; PVR advises fixing the D9 lagna first when rectifying (PVR 32.1-32.3).

source_views.source: Saravali 9.45-46 and 51.1
source_views.view: Physical appearance follows the navamsa lagna or the strongest planet, or the lord of the Moon's navamsa; complexion and disposition are judged from the rising navamsa, using the stronger of the Moon's navamsa lord and the navamsa lagna lord.

source_views.source: Saravali 10.16-17 (evils at birth)
source_views.view: If the lords of the navamsa lagna, Moon sign and natal lagna are combust, life is short [maraka: text predicts short life].

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 21.7 (via C.S. Patel ch. 3)
source_views.view: Each rising navamsa gives a type of person; when vargottama the person heads that class.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. IV 4.1 and after 4.3.12
source_views.view: The ascendant represents the native in all divisions, especially the navamsa; sign results blend rasi and navamsa lagna with the navamsa predominating.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 18.5 (Example 72) and 32.3
source_views.view: Lagna in navamsa shows the self from the point of view of dharma and married life, so its dasha favours marriage; fix the D9 lagna first when rectifying birth time.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XVIII
source_views.view: Before predicting from the rising sign, consider the lagna and its lord in both rasi and navamsa.

varga/d9_lagna_and_lord.disagreements: Saravali uses the stronger of navamsa-lagna lord and Moon's navamsa lord; Rath gives the navamsa lagna predominance outright; Raman simply asks that both charts be considered.
varga/d9_lagna_and_lord.phrasing_guidance: Describe inner temperament gently; do not make appearance claims from the navamsa lagna alone.

conditional_results.when: manual: lords of the navamsa lagna, the Moon sign and the natal lagna are all combust

varga/d9_seventh_house_and_lord.summary: For marriage, read the 7th house of D9, its lord and planets in it (and, classically, the navamsa falling on the 7th cusp); its sign lord's nature colours the spouse, and the D9 7th lord's period can bring marriage.
common_outcomes: Benefic sign or benefic navamsa on the 7th: a well-favoured, fortunate spouse; Saturn's or Mars's: harder qualities (Saravali 46.20-24; Phaladeepika 11.3).
Describe the spouse from the ruler of the 7th sign or 7th navamsa: Jupiter virtuous and restrained, Venus handsome and fortunate, Mercury skilled, Saturn older (Saravali 46.21-24).
Time marriage by the period of the D9 7th lord or planets linked to the D9 lagna and 7th (PVR 16.5.1; Rath 10.5.2).
rare_outcomes: Saravali 34.47: number of spouses from the number of navamsas passed in the 7th or planets aspecting it; one spouse if Leo, Aries or Scorpio rises in navamsa.
Rath: the 8th house of D9 can show the spouse's death or affairs [maraka: text links D9 8th house to danger to the spouse].

by_area.relationships: Core use.

strengtheners: benefic sign or navamsa on the 7th
D9 7th lord in a kendra or trikona, own or exalted
weakeners_or_cancellations: 7th sign or navamsa of Mars with Mars there: Phaladeepika 11.3 predicts widowhood for a woman [maraka: text predicts the husband's death]
malefic, weak, combust planets in the 7th aspected by malefics (Saravali 46.15-17)
varga/d9_seventh_house_and_lord.lagna_or_context_notes: Classical rules about the '7th navamsa' (the navamsa on the 7th cusp, 'setting navamsa') are not identical to the 7th house of the D9 chart; modern authors (PVR, Rath) use the D9 chart's 7th house and lord.

source_views.source: Saravali 46.20-24 (female horoscopy)
source_views.view: The husband's nature follows the ruler of the 7th house or its navamsa (Saturn old and foolish, Mars irascible, Venus handsome and fortunate, Mercury skilled, Moon soft, Jupiter virtuous); the text says the same applies to males.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 11.3-11.5
source_views.view: If the 7th house or setting navamsa belongs to a benefic, the husband is bright, learned and wealthy; otherwise deformed or wasteful; Mars's sign and amsa on the 7th with Mars there predicts widowhood [maraka: text predicts the husband's death].

source_views.source: Saravali 34.47
source_views.view: Number of wives from planets aspecting the 7th or navamsas passed in it; a single wife if Leo, Aries or Scorpio rises in navamsa.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXX (Female horoscopy) rule 4
source_views.view: If the 7th bhava falls in a benefic navamsa she will love her husband; in Mars's navamsa aspected by Saturn it shows trouble.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 16.5.1
source_views.view: The period of the 7th lord in D9 can give marriage.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. X 10.5.2-10.5.3 and ch. XI
source_views.view: The dasha lord should associate with the navamsa lagna or its lord, the antardasha lord with the D9 7th lord, the pratyantar lord be in trines to the D9 7th; the 8th house of D9 can bring the spouse's death or affairs.

varga/d9_seventh_house_and_lord.disagreements: Classical texts work with the navamsa on the 7th cusp and often state rules for women's charts; modern authors use the D9 chart's 7th house for both sexes.
varga/d9_seventh_house_and_lord.phrasing_guidance: Describe partner qualities and relationship themes; never predict widowhood, death of a spouse or divorce; keep timing as windows, not dates.

conditional_results.when: manual: the 7th house of D9 (or the navamsa on the 7th cusp) is a benefic's sign
manual: the 7th house or its navamsa belongs to Mars and Mars occupies the 7th
effects: [maraka: text predicts widowhood for a woman]

conditional_results.when: manual: the running period lord is the D9 7th lord or is linked to the D9 lagna/7th

varga/d1_seventh_lord_in_d9.summary: The D1 7th lord's navamsa placement and dignity show how well the marriage promise is supported; the D9 sign it occupies is also used to time marriage by transit.
common_outcomes: D1 7th lord well placed in D9 (kendra/trikona, own or exalted): supportive marriage (PVR note to Chart 96; Rath chart 72).
Marriage may come when Jupiter, Venus or the 7th lord transits a sign trine to the D1 7th lord's rasi or navamsa (Phaladeepika 10.12, 10.14; Rath 10.5.3).
Lagna lord's navamsa in its own debilitation sign or an enemy's sign: Jataka Parijata warns of losing the spouse or no spouse.
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika 10.11: the spouse's Moon sign may be trine to the sign or navamsa of the 1st or 7th lord.

by_area.relationships: Core use.

strengtheners: 7th lord in benefic navamsa (Jataka Parijata 14.22)
weakeners_or_cancellations: 7th lord in enemy or debilitation sign or eclipsed (Phaladeepika 10.15)

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 10.11-10.15
source_views.view: Spouse's Moon sign trine to the rasi or navamsa of the 1st and 7th lords; marriage when Venus or the 7th lord transits a trine to the lagna lord's rasi or navamsa, or when Jupiter transits a trine to the 7th lord's rasi or navamsa in the period of the stronger of the 7th lord's rasi and navamsa lords.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 14.22 and 14.46 (tr. Sastri, vol. II)
source_views.view: 7th lord in a kendra aspected by a benefic or in a benefic navamsa gives a devout wife; marriage comes when Jupiter transits a sign of the lord of the lagna lord's navamsa, but if that navamsa is the lagna lord's debilitation or enemy sign the person may lose the wife or have none.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, Part 6 (note to Chart 96) and 25.4
source_views.view: If the D1 7th lord is well placed in navamsa it is good; the 7th lord in rasi is the partner in physical life, navamsa the inner self; transits over the natal navamsa sign of the 7th lord or Venus can time marriage.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. X 10.5.3 and chart 72
source_views.view: Jupiter transiting the 7th lord's navamsa can give marriage; the 7th lord exalted in a kendra of D9 promises a long married life.

varga/d1_seventh_lord_in_d9.phrasing_guidance: Use as supporting evidence and timing windows; avoid predicting 'no spouse'.

conditional_results.when: manual: D1 7th lord is in a kendra or trikona of D9, or own/exalted in D9
manual: lagna lord's navamsa sign is its debilitation or an enemy's sign
effects: difficulty in marriage; possible loss of spouse or no spouse

varga/venus_jupiter_in_d9.summary: Venus (natural spouse significator, and for men the wife) and Jupiter (for women the husband, and dharma) are read in D9 by sign and dignity; Venus in Jupiter's or the 1st/9th lord's sign in rasi or navamsa gives a loving spouse, Mars/Saturn divisions colour sexuality.
common_outcomes: Venus in a sign of Jupiter or of the 1st or 9th lord, in rasi or navamsa: chaste, loving, happy spouse (Raman).
Venus in a navamsa of Mars or Saturn adds strong or unusual sexual tastes (BPHS 18; Saravali 46).
Jupiter in a sign or navamsa of Saturn or Mars: risk of affairs (JP 14.17); Jupiter debilitated in D9 in a woman's chart: marital misfortune (Rath).
rare_outcomes: Raman: in a woman's chart the Moon in Jupiter's navamsa supports loyalty; in Saturn's or Mars's navamsa it does not.

by_area.relationships: Core use.
by_area.spirituality: Jupiter in D9 as dharma (Rath, PVR).

strengtheners: Venus or Jupiter own or exalted in D9
Venus aspected by Jupiter (Rath 10.4.7)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Venus debilitated in D9 (Saravali 39.22)
Jupiter debilitated in D9 (Rath)

source_views.source: BPHS 18.10-13 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Venus in a sign or navamsa of Mars, or conjunct/aspected by Mars, gives unusual sexual habits; similarly related to Saturn, relations with the same sex.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 14.17
source_views.view: Jupiter in a rasi or navamsa owned by Saturn or Mars gives intrigues with other women.

source_views.source: Saravali 46.18 and 39.22
source_views.view: Venus and Mars exchanging divisions makes a woman go after other men; Venus in its debilitation navamsa ruins status.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XVI
source_views.view: Venus in the house of Jupiter or of the 1st or 9th lord, in rasi or navamsa, gives a chaste, loving, happy wife; in a woman's chart the Moon should be in Jupiter's navamsa, not Saturn's or Mars's.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. X 10.4.7, 10.5.2 and charts 69-71
source_views.view: Venus governs sexual happiness; Jupiter in trines to the navamsa lagna promotes chastity; planets with Venus in rasi and navamsa give marriage; Jupiter debilitated in navamsa gives rajbhanga in marriage.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 25.4 (Example 105)
source_views.view: Uses Venus's natal navamsa position and the D9 9th lord (dharma) when timing a wedding.

varga/venus_jupiter_in_d9.phrasing_guidance: Sexual and fidelity statements in these texts must not be repeated as predictions; translate into general warmth/compatibility themes.

conditional_results.when: manual: Venus in a sign of Jupiter or of the 1st or 9th lord in D1 or D9

varga/darakaraka_in_d9.summary: The darakaraka (planet with the lowest degree among the chara karakas) signifies the spouse; Jaimini-leaning authors read its navamsa sign and links to the D9 lagna and 7th, alongside the natural significator Venus.
common_outcomes: Note which planet is darakaraka and its D9 dignity and house; use it with Venus, not instead of it.
If two planets tie for a karaka role, Venus stands in as darakaraka (BPHS 32).
rare_outcomes: Rath reads the chara darakaraka's position relative to the 7th to describe first vs later spouses.

by_area.relationships: Core use.

varga/darakaraka_in_d9.lagna_or_context_notes: The 7-karaka and 8-karaka schemes give different darakarakas (BPHS 32.1-2, 13-17); the calculator's scheme decides which applies. See karaka/darakaraka for significations.

source_views.source: BPHS 32.13-17 (tr. Santhanam) with Santhanam's notes
source_views.view: Defines the chara karakas in descending order of degrees, ending with the stree/dara karaka; if two planets share a longitude, use the constant significator (Venus for the spouse).

Planets in the 7th from the karakamsa (the atmakaraka's navamsa sign) describe the wife: Moon and Jupiter a beautiful wife, Venus sensuous, Mercury skilled in arts, Saturn older or pious/sick, Rahu a widow.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 8.2 Table 13
source_views.view: Lists the darakaraka as the karaka for the spouse.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. III (chart 7) and ch. X (charts 41ff.)
source_views.view: Uses the chara darakaraka (e.g. its 12th-from-7th position) and the natural dara-karaka Venus together to judge spouses.

varga/darakaraka_in_d9.disagreements: Seven vs eight chara karaka schemes give different darakarakas; Parashara records both.
varga/darakaraka_in_d9.phrasing_guidance: Treat darakaraka readings as supporting colour only.

conditional_results.when: manual: darakaraka is own/exalted in D9 or in a kendra/trikona from the D9 lagna
conditional_results.source: Rath ch. X (applied examples); no single rule stated

varga/pushkara_navamsa.summary: Pushkara navamsas are two especially auspicious navamsas in each sign (24 in all, all owned by benefics); a planet in one is said to give higher status; the idea is rare in standard texts and comes mainly from Vidyamadhaviyam and Nadi works.
common_outcomes: Treat a planet (especially Jupiter) or the rising navamsa in a pushkara navamsa as a mild plus for standing and comfort.
Distinguish pushkara navamsa (a 3 deg 20 min span) from pushkara bhaga/pushkaramsa (a single degree per sign used in muhurta).
rare_outcomes: Deva Keralam (via Patel): Jupiter in a kendra or trikona in pushkara navamsa makes one lucky, but if that navamsa sign is the 6th, 8th or 12th from the D1 lagna it adds weak health or grief over a child.

by_area.career: Patel: people with the rising navamsa in vargottama or pushkara navamsa are outstanding in their careers.
by_area.finance: Deva Keralam (via Patel): all seven planets in pushkara navamsas gives wealth and comforts.

strengtheners: Jupiter in pushkara navamsa joined by Mars and the Moon (Jataka Parijata 7.25 via Patel)
weakeners_or_cancellations: pushkara navamsa sign falling in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the D1 lagna (Deva Keralam via Patel)
varga/pushkara_navamsa.lagna_or_context_notes: Pushkara navamsas per Vidyamadhaviyam (via Patel): Aries/Leo/Sagittarius the 7th (Libra) and 9th (Sagittarius); Taurus/Virgo/Capricorn the 3rd (Pisces) and 5th (Taurus); Gemini/Libra/Aquarius the 6th (Pisces) and 8th (Taurus); Cancer/Scorpio/Pisces the 1st (Cancer) and 3rd (Virgo).

source_views.source: C.S. Patel, Navamsa in Astrology, ch. 4 (citing Vidyamadhaviyam pt. I pp.30-31)
source_views.view: Defines the 24 pushkara navamsas, separates them from the one-degree pushkaramsas of muhurta texts, says standard books rarely use them while Nadi texts use them freely, and gives Deva Keralam results.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 7.25 (via Patel ch. 4; the sloka is illegible in the archive.org OCR of Sastri's edition, whose index lists 'Pushkaramsa ... ushers a King, vii, 25')
source_views.view: Jupiter joined by Mars and the Moon in a vargottama or pushkara navamsa makes a king.

varga/pushkara_navamsa.disagreements: Patel notes that no standard text defines pushkara navamsa; only Vidyamadhaviyam does. BPHS, Phaladeepika and Saravali (as read) do not mention it.
varga/pushkara_navamsa.phrasing_guidance: Mention only as a small positive; do not build a reading on it.

conditional_results.when: manual: Jupiter with Mars and the Moon in a vargottama or pushkara navamsa
manual: all seven planets in pushkara navamsas

varga/varga_dignity_count.summary: A planet's overall varga strength is the count of divisions (D9 included) in which it is in exaltation, moolatrikona or own sign, and its 20-point vimshopaka score; low scores mean it cannot give good results.
common_outcomes: Vimshopaka below 5 of 20: the planet cannot give auspicious results; 5-10 some good; 10-15 medium; above 15 wholly favourable (BPHS 7.26-27).
Named counts of good vargas (e.g. Parijata = 2, Gopura = 4, Simhasana = 5 in the ten-division scheme) mark strong planets.
rare_outcomes: PVR: the lagna lord in simhasanamsa (5 good charts in dasavarga) makes one very famous.
weakeners_or_cancellations: divisions of a combust, defeated, weak planet or one in a bad avastha are not counted as good (BPHS 6.42-53)
varga/varga_dignity_count.lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS also counts as good the divisions owned by the lords of kendras from the Arudha lagna; Santhanam notes this makes too many signs qualify and prefers exaltation, moolatrikona and own sign.

source_views.source: BPHS 6.42-53 (tr. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Names the grades by number of good vargas in the 6-, 7-, 10- and 16-division schemes; good vargas are exaltation, moolatrikona, own sign and signs of kendra lords from the Arudha lagna; ignore those of combust, defeated, weak or badly placed planets.
Vimshopaka score thresholds (below 5 no good, 5-10 some, 10-15 medium, above 15 full) and grading dasha results by vimshopaka.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 3.6-3.7
source_views.view: Vaiseshikamsas arise from trikona, moolatrikona, own sign, exaltation, kendra and vargottama across the vargas; names Parijata (2) through Airavata (9).

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 1.44
source_views.view: Vaiseshikamsas start with uttama, produced by moolatrikona, own sign, exaltation and vargottama across the ten vargas.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 6.6
source_views.view: Counts only moolatrikona, own and exaltation signs; the dasavarga grouping is the important one; a kendra lord with good amsa bala in dasavarga brings success.

varga/varga_dignity_count.disagreements: Which placements count as 'good': BPHS includes Arudha-kendra lords' signs; Phaladeepika includes kendra and vargottama; PVR and Santhanam restrict to exaltation, moolatrikona and own sign.
varga/varga_dignity_count.phrasing_guidance: Use as background weighting, not as a stand-alone claim.

conditional_results.when: manual: planet's vimshopaka score is below 5 of 20
manual: planet's vimshopaka score is above 15 of 20

varga/d9_and_dasha.summary: A dasha lord's D9 condition modifies its period: vargottama or exalted in D9 helps, debilitated or inimical D9 spoils; and D9 houses tell what the period does for marriage and dharma.
common_outcomes: Check the dasha and antardasha lords' D9 dignity before finalising a period's tone (Raman; Phaladeepika 20.22; JP 18.170).
Periods of the D9 7th lord or planets tied to the D9 lagna can bring marriage (PVR; Rath).
Period of an exalted planet in the 12th from the atmakaraka in D9 can turn the mind to liberation (PVR).
rare_outcomes: PVR runs Narayana dasa on D9 (starting from the D1 9th lord's D9 sign) to time marriage events.

by_area.relationships: Marriage timing.
by_area.spirituality: 12th from AK in D9.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 20.22
source_views.view: The dasha of a vargottama planet is favourable; mixed if that planet is eclipsed or debilitated.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.170
source_views.view: The dasha of a planet in a debilitation or inimical navamsa is untoward.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology, ch. XXIV
source_views.view: The dasha lord's results are modified by its favourable or unfavourable navamsa position among other factors.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Integrated Approach, 16.5.1 and 18.5
source_views.view: A planet gives results promised by its positions in the divisional charts, e.g. the D9 7th lord's period can give marriage; Narayana dasa of D9 times marital events.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, ch. X 10.5.2
source_views.view: Timing of marriage can be done accurately from the navamsa via the dasha lord's link to the navamsa lagna and the antardasha lord's link to the D9 7th lord.

varga/d9_and_dasha.phrasing_guidance: Use D9 condition to soften or strengthen period descriptions, not to flip them completely.

aspect/jupiter/1.summary: Jupiter aspecting the lagna gives religious and virtuous habits, honour from authorities, fame and good company, and protects and fills out the body; it is one of the strongest supports a lagna can have.
common_outcomes: interest in religious observances, honoured by rulers, famous, keeps the company of the virtuous, elders and guests (Saravali 34.1-7)
the lagna is strong when aspected by Jupiter, Mercury or its lord (Phaladeepika 4.6)
stout body if Jupiter aspects the lagna from a watery sign (Raman HJH vol. 1 ch. 4)
fair complexion, large eyes and dignified bearing; tendency to corpulence (Raman HJH vol. 1 ch. 4, chart notes)
rare_outcomes: Aspects on the natal Moon (the Moon as second lagna, BPHS ch. 12): Phaladeepika 18.6-11 gives Jupiter's aspect on the Moon as kingly status in Aries, Scorpio, Capricorn and Pisces; respect in Taurus; learning in Gemini; wisdom in Cancer; wealth in Leo; command of an army in Virgo; goldsmith's work in Libra; rule in Sagittarius; leadership in Aquarius. Raman HPA ch. XIII: the Jupiter-Moon opposition is extremely good.

Saturn, Mars and Venus in the lagna without Jupiter's aspect, with a waning Moon in the 7th: [maraka: text predicts the child's death in the 7th year] (Raman HJH vol. 2 ch. XII) - Jupiter's aspect is the protective factor.
Jupiter aspecting the lagna and Mercury trinally gave an analytical, legal intellect in a Raman case (HJH vol. 2 ch. XIV).

by_area.personality: Principled, religious, dignified, respected (Saravali 34.1-7).
by_area.career: Honour from those in power (Saravali 34.1-7).
by_area.health: Good constitution and fuller build (Raman HJH vol. 1 ch. 4).
by_area.spirituality: Devotion and religious practice (Saravali 34.1-7).

strengtheners: Saravali 34.8: Sagittarius or Pisces lagna aspected by its own lord gives happiness, wealth and closeness to rulers.
Phaladeepika 4.11: Jupiter is the most powerful planet for warding off evil.
Raman HJH vol. 1 ch. 4: aspect from a watery sign adds bodily stoutness.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Jupiter vitiated by association with Ketu or Rahu gives less benefit (Raman HJH vol. 1 ch. 6 chart notes).
aspect/jupiter/1.lagna_or_context_notes: Jupiter aspects house 1 fully from the 7th (7th aspect), the 9th (5th aspect) and the 5th (9th aspect); BPHS 26.4 makes the 5th and 9th aspects full for Jupiter; Brihat Jataka 2.13 calls Jupiter auspicious in them.

source_views.source: Saravali (tr. R. Santhanam) 34.1-7
source_views.view: Jupiter aspecting the ascendant: religious observances, honoured by the king, famous, in the company of the virtuous, elders and guests.

source_views.source: Saravali (tr. R. Santhanam) 34.8, 34.10-11
source_views.view: Own-sign aspect on the lagna gives happiness and wealth; even one benefic aspecting the lagna is auspicious.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 1950) 4.6
source_views.view: Lagna is strong when occupied or aspected by its lord, Jupiter or Mercury.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 1950) 4.11
source_views.view: In completely warding off evil and promoting prosperity Jupiter is the most powerful planet; Mercury and Venus have smaller shares of that power (fractions illegible in the scan).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 1950) 18.6-11
source_views.view: Moon in each sign aspected by Jupiter (third in the list).
