aspect/sun/9.summary: The Sun's aspect on the 9th (from the 3rd) on Jupiter there makes one equal to a king; when the Sun owns the 9th (Aries lagna) its aspect keeps fortune in one's own country.
common_outcomes: Jupiter in the 9th aspected by the Sun: equal to a king (Saravali 32.6-7)
rare_outcomes: Jupiter in the 9th aspected by the Sun together with: Mars - sovereignty, gems, gold, courage and vehicles; the Moon - plenty, devotion to parents, fame, kingly status, more than one wife; Mercury - grace, fortune, a fine spouse and skill in poetry and arts; Venus - a festive, social nature and cattle wealth; Saturn - headship of a country, town or group, learning and a habit of accumulating (Saravali 32.8-12). These hold only when no other planet aspects (Saravali 32.23).

by_area.career: Royal or high status when Jupiter in the 9th receives the Sun's aspect (Saravali 32.6-7).

strengtheners: Saravali 32.4: the 9th aspected by its own lord (the Sun for Sagittarius lagna) gives fortune in one's own country.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saravali 32.4: aspect by planets other than the 9th lord makes fortune dawn elsewhere (away from home).
Frawley: the Sun's heat tends to limit or burn up the matters of the house it aspects.
aspect/sun/9.lagna_or_context_notes: The Sun aspects the 9th from the 3rd house.

source_views.source: Saravali (tr. R. Santhanam) 32.4
source_views.view: If the 9th is aspected or occupied by its own lord, fortune is made in one's own country; if other planets aspect or join it, fortune dawns elsewhere.

aspect/venus/1.summary: Venus aspecting the lagna (from the 7th) is classically linked with good looks, pleasure, comfort and wealth, and with strong attraction to the opposite sex; texts also warn of indulgence.
common_outcomes: handsome or attractive appearance and magnetism to the opposite sex (Saravali 34.1-7; Braha)
enjoyment of wealth and pleasures (Saravali 34.1-7; Jataka Parijata 11.43-44)
bodily well-being, as the lagna is aspected by a benefic (BPHS 12.3-4; Saravali 34.10-11)
rare_outcomes: Saravali 34.1-7 and Jataka Parijata 11.43-44 add attachment to courtesans or women of ill fame and a voluptuous nature
Raman (HJH vol. 2, longevity rules): when the lagna lord receives the aspect of Venus and Jupiter and is itself in a kendra, the native is long-lived (an aspect on the lagna lord, not the house)
Raman (HJH vol. 1, Sixth House, pp. 249-250): if Venus is in the lagna with the 6th lord and is aspected by Saturn, Rahu or Mars, relatives cause trouble (Venus as the aspected planet)

by_area.personality: youthful, pleasure-loving, charming and attractive (Saravali 34.1-7; Braha)
by_area.finance: happiness from wealth; opulence (Saravali 34.1-7; Jataka Parijata 11.43-44)
by_area.health: a benefic aspect on the lagna favours bodily felicity (BPHS 12.3-4)
by_area.relationships: strong appeal to the opposite sex; texts warn of indulgence in many relationships (Saravali 34.1-7; Jataka Parijata 11.43-44; Braha)

strengtheners: Venus owning the lagna (Taurus or Libra rising): an aspect on its own sign confers happiness, wealth and royal favour (Saravali 34.8)
two or more planets aspecting the lagna bring happiness and wealth (Saravali 34.10-11)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Venus debilitated, combust or in an enemy sign (Phaladeepika 15.1)
malefic aspects on the lagna at the same time give mixed results (Phaladeepika 15.2)
aspect/venus/1.lagna_or_context_notes: Venus has only the full 7th-house aspect, so it aspects house 1 fully when placed in house 7. Classical partial aspects (BPHS 26.2-5, Brihat Jataka 2.13, Phaladeepika 2.23): one-quarter from houses 11 and 4, one-half from houses 9 and 5, three-quarters from houses 10 and 6; Braha says practising astrologers ignore these partial aspects and the calculator uses only the full 7th. As a natural benefic, Venus's aspect is classed as helpful (Phaladeepika 15.1, BPHS 11.14-16), but its functional role for the lagna changes this (Raman, Braha).

effects: Venus aspects its own sign: the house is protected and its matters flourish
conditional_results.source: BPHS 11.14-16 (tr. Santhanam: a house aspected by its own lord prospers); Saravali 34.8 (for the lagna)

effects: the good results of a benefic aspect are not assured
an aspect from the 8th or 12th lord brings loss, destruction and misery to the house
an aspect from the 9th lord gives strongly positive and spiritual energy to the house

conditional_results.when: manual: the aspected sign is Venus's exaltation sign (Pisces)
manual: the aspected sign is Venus's debilitation sign (Virgo)
effects: the aspect can do harm instead of good

source_views.view: If Venus aspects the lagna, the native is addicted to women of ill fame, opulent and voluptuous.

source_views.view: Bodily felicity if the ascendant is aspected by or joined with a benefic; poor health if aspected by malefics without benefic aspect.

source_views.view: Because Venus in the 7th aspects the 1st, the person is beautiful and magnetic to the opposite sex.

source_views.view: Effects of the 10th reveal beneficially if benefics aspect the 10th from the Moon; malefic aspects spoil them. Malefics in the 10th from the Moon aspected by benefics: doctor, purohit, astrologer or cheat.

aspect/venus/10.disagreements: Saravali's rule is stated from the Moon, not the lagna.
aspect/venus/10.phrasing_guidance: Keep general: a pleasant, cooperative working environment.

aspect/venus/11.summary: Venus connected with the 11th (by aspect, ownership or divisions) gives gains through Venusian things - travel, pearls, silver, and in the text courtesans; benefic aspect increases gains.
common_outcomes: gains through travel, pearls and silver (Saravali 34.63)
benefic aspect on the 11th increases its gains (Saravali 34.65)
rare_outcomes: Saravali 34.63: gains through connections with courtesans
Saravali 34.66: if all planets aspect the 11th, wealth comes in many ways

by_area.finance: income through Venus-ruled trades and goods (Saravali 34.63, 34.65)

strengtheners: Venus exalted: full results (Saravali 34.67)
Venus owning the 11th (BPHS 11.14-16 principle)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Venus in own or friendly sign gives half, inimical sign a quarter, combust very little (Saravali 34.67)
malefic influence on the 11th reduces the results (Saravali 34.65)
aspect/venus/11.lagna_or_context_notes: Venus has only the full 7th-house aspect, so it aspects house 11 fully when placed in house 5. Classical partial aspects (BPHS 26.2-5, Brihat Jataka 2.13, Phaladeepika 2.23): one-quarter from houses 9 and 2, one-half from houses 7 and 3, three-quarters from houses 8 and 4; Braha says practising astrologers ignore these partial aspects and the calculator uses only the full 7th. As a natural benefic, Venus's aspect is classed as helpful (Phaladeepika 15.1, BPHS 11.14-16), but its functional role for the lagna changes this (Raman, Braha).

effects: Venus aspects its own sign: the house is protected and its matters flourish
conditional_results.source: BPHS 11.14-16 (tr. Santhanam: a house aspected by its own lord prospers); Saravali 34.8 (for the lagna)

effects: the good results of a benefic aspect are not assured
an aspect from the 8th or 12th lord brings loss, destruction and misery to the house
an aspect from the 9th lord gives strongly positive and spiritual energy to the house

conditional_results.when: manual: the aspected sign is Venus's exaltation sign (Pisces)
manual: the aspected sign is Venus's debilitation sign (Virgo)
effects: the aspect can do harm instead of good

source_views.source: Saravali 34.58, 34.63, 34.65-67 (Eng. tr., retyped edition)
source_views.view: A planet in, aspecting or owning the 11th (or its divisions so connected) gives gains of its nature; Venus: prostitutes, travels, pearls, silver. Benefic aspect increases, malefic decreases; dignity scales results.

aspect/venus/11.phrasing_guidance: Speak of income from creative, luxury or travel-related work; leave out the courtesan reading.

aspect/venus/12.summary: No source read gives a specific result for Venus aspecting the 12th; only the general rule that a benefic's aspect helps a house applies.
common_outcomes: general rule only: a house aspected by a benefic, free of malefic aspect, gives good results (Phaladeepika 15.1; BPHS 11.14-16)
strengtheners: Venus owning the 12th (BPHS 11.14-16 principle)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Venus debilitated or combust (Phaladeepika 15.1)
aspect/venus/12.lagna_or_context_notes: Venus has only the full 7th-house aspect, so it aspects house 12 fully when placed in house 6. Classical partial aspects (BPHS 26.2-5, Brihat Jataka 2.13, Phaladeepika 2.23): one-quarter from houses 10 and 3, one-half from houses 8 and 4, three-quarters from houses 9 and 5; Braha says practising astrologers ignore these partial aspects and the calculator uses only the full 7th. As a natural benefic, Venus's aspect is classed as helpful (Phaladeepika 15.1, BPHS 11.14-16), but its functional role for the lagna changes this (Raman, Braha).

effects: Venus aspects its own sign: the house is protected and its matters flourish
conditional_results.source: BPHS 11.14-16 (tr. Santhanam: a house aspected by its own lord prospers); Saravali 34.8 (for the lagna)

effects: the good results of a benefic aspect are not assured
an aspect from the 8th or 12th lord brings loss, destruction and misery to the house
an aspect from the 9th lord gives strongly positive and spiritual energy to the house

manual: the aspected sign is Venus's debilitation sign (Virgo)

source_views.view: All planets aspect the 7th fully; partial aspects grow by quarters (3rd/10th 1/4, 5th/9th 1/2, 4th/8th 3/4); results are in proportion to the aspect.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 15.1-2 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: A house occupied or aspected by benefics or its own lord, free of malefic aspect, gives full good results, provided the planets are not debilitated, combust or in enemy signs; mixed influences give mixed results.

aspect/venus/12.phrasing_guidance: Keep it general; do not invent specific results.

conjunction/sun_moon.summary: Sun and Moon in one sign (a new-Moon birth) is read classically as practical, technical skill (machinery, stone, metal work) and cleverness in work, with a tendency to be guided by one's spouse. The Moon is weak here because it is close to the Sun.
common_outcomes: skill with machines, stone or metal work
clever and capable in whatever work is taken up
strongly guided by or devoted to the spouse
rare_outcomes: trade in intoxicants (Saravali)
immodest or able to deceive (Saravali; the translator gives 'metallurgist' with 'able to deceive' as an alternative reading)

by_area.personality: Clever and capable in work (Jataka Parijata 8.1); Saravali 15.2 adds a less modest, possibly calculating side.
by_area.career: Machinery and stone work (Brihat Jataka 14.1; Phaladeepika 18.1); metal work or trade in intoxicants (Saravali 15.2).
by_area.finance: Saravali 15.2 says quite wealthy; V. Subrahmanya Sastri's note on Brihat Jataka 14 treats the new-Moon conjunction as the one Sun conjunction that is not bad for money.
by_area.relationships: Under the influence of the wife or of women (Saravali 15.2); submissive to the wife (Jataka Parijata 8.1).

strengtheners: Saravali 15.23: results increase when both planets occupy good vargas (divisions).
weakeners_or_cancellations: The Moon is combust (astangata) within 12 degrees of the Sun (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII); Frawley gives a 15-degree orb for the Moon.
Frawley: the Moon is weakest as it approaches the Sun and strongest when full.
Saravali 5.27: a combust planet loses its power to give good results and can give bad results in full.
Saravali 15.23: results decrease when the planets occupy bad vargas.
conjunction/sun_moon.lagna_or_context_notes: The classical two-planet results are general and apply in any house; Jataka Parijata (note to Adhyaya 8) says house-by-house results for each pair are given in other works (Horaratna), which were not read here.

named_yogas.name: Amavasya (new-Moon) birth
named_yogas.source: V. Subrahmanya Sastri, note on Brihat Jataka 14.1

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 (tr. M. Neely, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: One who makes things of stone and builds machines.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed.)
source_views.view: Skilled in machinery and stone work; the note calls it a creative combination and the one Sun conjunction that is not bad for finance (the new-Moon conjunction).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.1 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Skilled in machinery and stone work (same as Brihat Jataka).

source_views.source: Saravali 15.2 (English tr., archive.org 'Kalyana Varmas Saravali'; translator not named)
source_views.view: Under the control of his wife or women, immodest, a metal worker (or deceptive), quite wealthy, expert in selling intoxicants.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.1 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 1932)
source_views.view: Submissive to his wife and clever in every task.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII (Eighth House, Astangata Harana)
source_views.view: The Moon within 12 degrees of the Sun is astangata (combust).

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, Planetary Aspects and Combinations (pp. 175-176)
source_views.view: The Moon's combustion orb is 15 degrees; it weakens as it nears the Sun; planetary-war rules do not apply to the Sun or Moon.

conjunction/sun_moon.disagreements: Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika stress technical skill; Saravali adds immodesty, wealth and trade in intoxicants; Jataka Parijata stresses being clever and submissive to the wife. On combustion, Raman gives 12 degrees for the Moon and Frawley 15.
conjunction/sun_moon.phrasing_guidance: Present it as a practical, hands-on, capable nature and a close bond with the partner. Mention that the Moon is faint near the Sun as a reason feelings may be kept inside, not as a defect. Leave out the intoxicants and deception readings unless strongly supported elsewhere.

conjunction/sun_mars.summary: Sun with Mars gives strength, energy and a fiery, forceful temperament; the classical texts warn that the same force can turn harsh, untruthful or destructive.
common_outcomes: strong, energetic and valorous
fiery, forceful temperament
risk of harsh or unscrupulous conduct
rare_outcomes: inclined to cruelty or violence (Saravali)
dull-witted despite strength (Saravali)

by_area.personality: Splendid, brave, strong and fierce but quick to lie and harsh (Saravali 15.3); illustrious and energetic but untruthful (Jataka Parijata 8.1); fiery (Frawley).
by_area.health: Frawley: Mars with the Sun often makes the constitution fiery.
by_area.spirituality: Inclined to wrongdoing (Brihat Jataka 14.1; Phaladeepika 18.1).

strengtheners: Saravali 15.23: results improve when both occupy good vargas.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mars is combust within 17 degrees of the Sun (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII); Frawley gives 8 degrees 30 minutes.
Saravali 5.27: a combust planet loses its power for good.
Frawley: a planet in a favourable sign or house can largely offset combustion.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 (tr. M. Neely, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: One who takes pleasure in wrongdoing.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Intent on sinful deeds; the note calls it a destructive combination.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.1 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Inclined to sinful deeds.

source_views.source: Saravali 15.3 (archive.org English tr.)
source_views.view: Splendid, brave, strong but slow-witted; untruthful, sinful, inclined to harm and fierce.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.1 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Illustrious, strong and energetic, but untruthful and wicked.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, Medical Astrology (p. 217)
source_views.view: Mars conjunct the Sun often makes a person fiery.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII
source_views.view: Mars is combust within 17 degrees of the Sun.

conjunction/sun_mars.disagreements: All texts read agree on strength and harshness; Saravali and Jataka Parijata add splendour and fame, Brihat Jataka gives only the negative. Combustion orb: Raman 17 degrees, Frawley 8.5 degrees.
conjunction/sun_mars.phrasing_guidance: Describe drive, courage and a strong will, and suggest directing it into constructive challenges. Do not call the person sinful or violent; frame the classical warning as a need to watch temper and bluntness.

conjunction/sun_mercury.summary: Sun with Mercury forms Budha-Aditya yoga: intelligence, skill, learning and a good name. Most authorities rate it well; its strength depends on Mercury not being too deeply combust.
common_outcomes: clever, intelligent and skilful in work
good reputation and respect
learning and pleasant speech
favour of superiors or authorities
rare_outcomes: fluctuating wealth (Saravali)
fickle-mindedness (Jataka Parijata)
work in service (Saravali)

by_area.personality: Clever, intelligent, sweet-spoken, noble (Brihat Jataka 14.1; Saravali 15.4); learned but somewhat fickle (Jataka Parijata 8.1).
by_area.career: In service, dear to the king and good people (Saravali 15.4); skilful in all work (Raman, PVR).
by_area.finance: Fame and money but unsteady wealth (Saravali 15.4); Sastri's note says it is not good for finance.

strengtheners: Raman (Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 24): Mercury should be more than 10 degrees from the Sun for the yoga to work.
PVR Narasimha Rao: strongest in divisional charts such as the D-10; works in the rasi chart when Mercury is not combust.
Raman (How to Judge a Horoscope, chart 202): Jupiter's aspect on a combust Mercury largely removes the harm of combustion.
Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mercury is combust within 14 degrees of the Sun, 12 when retrograde (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII); Frawley gives 2 degrees.
Raman (How to Judge a Horoscope, chart 202): combust Mercury is said to make one superficial and short of judgement.
PVR: yogas formed by combust planets lose some of their power to do good.
conjunction/sun_mercury.lagna_or_context_notes: PVR: the yoga gives its results in the periods of the Sun and Mercury (and of the sign holding them).

named_yogas.name: Budha-Aditya yoga (Nipuna yoga)
named_yogas.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 24; PVR Narasimha Rao 11.2.4

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 (tr. M. Neely, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Clever and intelligent, gains reputation and comfort (Neely's rendering adds a harsh streak).

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Clever, intelligent, famous and happy; the note says it gives proficiency and a good name but is not good for finance.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.1 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Clever, intelligent, famous and happy.

source_views.source: Saravali 15.4 (archive.org English tr.)
source_views.view: In service, unsteady wealth, sweet speech, fame and money, noble, liked by the king and good people, with strength, beauty and learning.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.1 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Learning, beauty and strength, but fickle-minded.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 24 Budha-Aditya Yoga
source_views.view: Highly intelligent, skilful, well regarded and comfortable; Mercury is usually an exception to the harm of combustion but should be more than 10 degrees from the Sun; not rare.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XIV (chart 202)
source_views.view: Almost all standard works call the Sun-Mercury combination auspicious; combust Mercury can make one superficial, but Jupiter's aspect largely cancels this.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.2.4
source_views.view: Intelligent, skilful, well known, respected and happy; combustion reduces it; most powerful in the D-10.

conjunction/sun_mercury.disagreements: Saravali and Sastri's note say wealth is unsteady or weak while Raman and PVR give comfort and happiness. Combustion orb for Mercury: Raman 14 degrees (12 retrograde) in How to Judge a Horoscope, 10 degrees for the yoga in Three Hundred Important Combinations; Frawley 2 degrees.
conjunction/sun_mercury.phrasing_guidance: Present as a sharp, capable, articulate mind and a good reputation. If Mercury is very close to the Sun, say the gift may need focus and patience to show fully rather than calling it cancelled.

conjunction/sun_jupiter.summary: Sun with Jupiter is read as a person devoted to work for others, often in an advisory, ministerial or teaching role; texts disagree on whether the nature is kind or stern.
common_outcomes: works on behalf of others
favour of rulers or superiors
virtuous or faithful nature
rare_outcomes: a stern or cruel streak (Sastri's translation of Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika)
minister of a king or preceptor (Saravali)

by_area.personality: Virtuous, good-minded (Saravali 15.5); full of faith and active (Jataka Parijata 8.1); Sastri's Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika also call him cruel.
by_area.career: Minister or preceptor (Saravali 15.5); pleases the king through his work (Jataka Parijata 8.1); devoted to other people's work (Brihat Jataka 14.1).
by_area.finance: Wealthy (Jataka Parijata 8.1); gains through friends (Saravali 15.5).
by_area.relationships: Gains through friends (Saravali 15.5).
by_area.spirituality: Faith and virtue (Jataka Parijata 8.1; Saravali 15.5).

strengtheners: Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Jupiter is combust within 11 degrees of the Sun (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII); Frawley gives 8 degrees 30 minutes.
Saravali 5.27: a combust planet loses its power for good.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 (tr. M. Neely, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Devotes himself to the work of others.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Cruel and engaged in other people's work; the note says cruel-hearted and benefits others at his own cost.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.1 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Cruel, yet interested in helping others.

source_views.source: Saravali 15.5 (archive.org English tr.)
source_views.view: Virtuous, a king's minister, gains through friends, good-minded, a preceptor.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.1 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Full of faith, active, pleases the king through his work, wealthy.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII
source_views.view: Jupiter is combust within 11 degrees of the Sun.

conjunction/sun_jupiter.disagreements: The 'cruel' reading appears in Sastri's translations of Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika but not in Neely's Brihat Jataka, Saravali or Jataka Parijata, which are positive (virtue, faith, ministerial role). Combustion orb: Raman 11 degrees, Frawley 8.5.
conjunction/sun_jupiter.phrasing_guidance: Lead with service, guidance and principled work for others. Do not call the person cruel; at most mention a firm, strict side.

conjunction/sun_venus.summary: Sun with Venus is linked classically to earning through performance or arms, public entertainment, and money or connections through women or the spouse; Venus is weakened by combustion.
common_outcomes: earns through performing, acting or entertaining the public
skill with weapons
gains or ties through women or the spouse's family
rare_outcomes: weak eyesight in old age (Saravali)

by_area.personality: Mighty and able to amuse people (Saravali 15.6); intelligent (Jataka Parijata 8.2); Sastri's note calls it an imitative spirit.
by_area.career: Earns as an actor or through weapons (Brihat Jataka 14.1; Phaladeepika 18.1); skilled with weapons and entertains the public (Saravali 15.6).
by_area.finance: Much money earned through women (Saravali 15.6).
by_area.health: Weak sight in old age (Saravali 15.6).
by_area.relationships: Gains through women (Saravali 15.6).
by_area.family: Respects and attends to the relatives gained through his wife (Jataka Parijata 8.2).

strengtheners: Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Venus is combust within 10 degrees of the Sun, 8 when retrograde (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII); Frawley gives 4 degrees.
Frawley: Venus, like Mercury and the Moon, is weaker the closer it is to the Sun.
conjunction/sun_venus.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman notes that Venus is exempt from the combustion reduction in the longevity (ayurdaya) calculation; this is specific to that calculation.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 (tr. M. Neely, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Profits through weapons and warfare.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Earns as an actor or by weapons; note: an imitative spirit.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.1 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Earns as an actor or through weapons.

source_views.source: Saravali 15.6 (archive.org English tr.)
source_views.view: Skilled with weapons, mighty, weak-sighted in old age, entertains the public, much money through women.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.2 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Intelligent and attentive to the relatives acquired through his wife.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII
source_views.view: Venus combust within 10 degrees (8 retrograde).

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, Planetary Aspects and Combinations (p. 175)
source_views.view: Venus combust within 4 degrees; inner planets are weaker near the Sun.

conjunction/sun_venus.disagreements: Brihat Jataka, Phaladeepika and Saravali stress performance and weapons; Jataka Parijata gives only intelligence and attention to in-laws. Combustion orb: Raman 10 degrees, Frawley 4.
conjunction/sun_venus.phrasing_guidance: Frame as charisma, a flair for performance or public life, and strong ties through the partner. Mention eyesight only as a general care point, never as a prediction.

conjunction/sun_saturn.summary: Sun with Saturn joins two enemies: classically it gives hard work and skill with metals or crafts, dutifulness, but strain with family or superiors and a sense of being held back.
common_outcomes: skilled in metal work or crafts
hardworking and dutiful
difficulties with superiors, opponents or the father
rare_outcomes: loss or separation concerning spouse and children (Saravali)
under the power of enemies (Jataka Parijata)

by_area.personality: Virtuous, mindful of duty, pure but not wholly straightforward (Saravali 15.7); somewhat slow-witted (Jataka Parijata 8.2); hardworking (Sastri's note).
by_area.career: Metal work or vessel-making (Brihat Jataka 14.1; Phaladeepika 18.1; Saravali 15.7).
by_area.finance: Sastri's note on Brihat Jataka 14 groups Sun conjunctions as bad for finance.
by_area.health: Raman: Sun in the 6th afflicted by Saturn points to heart trouble or chest pain unless Jupiter aspects.
by_area.relationships: Saravali 15.7 speaks of losing wife and son.
by_area.family: Rath: Saturn joining the Sun in the 6th shows enmity with the father.

strengtheners: Rath (Crux 9.2): if the Sun has a higher longitude than Saturn, the trouble is overcome.
Raman (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX): Jupiter's aspect relieves the Sun-Saturn affliction in the 6th.
Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Rath (Crux 9.2): if the Sun has a lower longitude than Saturn, the evil is more evident.

Saturn becomes combust near the Sun (Raman lists Saturn with the other planets; the scan reads 5 degrees, unverified); Frawley gives 8 degrees 30 minutes. Raman notes Saturn is exempt from the combustion reduction in the longevity calculation.
conjunction/sun_saturn.lagna_or_context_notes: House-specific notes read: in the 6th house (Raman; Rath).

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 (tr. M. Neely, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Skilled in metal work, makes various kinds of vessels.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Clever in metal work; note: one who works hard.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.1 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Skilled in metal work or pottery.

source_views.source: Saravali 15.7 (archive.org English tr.)
source_views.view: Metal worker, virtuous and dutiful, loses wife and son, true to his family's ways, pure but not fully upright.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.2 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Somewhat dull-witted and in the power of his enemies.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX (Sixth House)
source_views.view: Sun in the 6th afflicted by Saturn shows heart trouble or chest pain unless Jupiter aspects.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology 9.2 (in the same archive.org item)
source_views.view: Saturn conjoining the Sun in the 6th shows enmity with the father; the Sun at a higher longitude overcomes it, a lower longitude makes it worse.

conjunction/sun_saturn.disagreements: Saravali gives virtue and duty with family loss; Jataka Parijata gives dullness and enemies; Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika give only craft. The Saturn combustion orb in Raman's scan (5 degrees) differs from Frawley's 8.5 degrees.
conjunction/sun_saturn.phrasing_guidance: Frame as discipline, endurance and achievement through steady effort, with lessons around authority and the father. Never predict loss of spouse or children; mention heart care only as general wellbeing.

conjunction/sun_rahu.summary: Sun with Rahu is an 'eclipse' combination in modern readings: the Sun's significations (self, father, vitality) are obstructed or transformed, and the result can lean either to worldly trouble or to spiritual renunciation. The classical two-planet chapters read do not cover the nodes.
common_outcomes: Sun's matters (self-confidence, father, authority) obstructed or unusual
possible pull towards spirituality or renunciation
rare_outcomes: Rath: this eclipse combination can produce either a saint or a criminal type, depending on other factors

by_area.personality: Rath: Rahu brings spirituality or renunciation while the Sun may turn negative; with lagna or arudha lagna in Aquarius the native is spiritual, in Leo the reverse.
by_area.health: Rath (Crux 9.2): Rahu eclipsing the Sun in the 6th shows torment by disease.
by_area.spirituality: Rath: Rahu with the Sun can show great spirituality or renunciation.

strengtheners: Rath (Crux 9.2): if the Sun has a higher longitude than Rahu, the evil is overcome.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Rath (Crux 9.2): if the Sun has a lower longitude than Rahu, the evil is more evident.
Frawley: closer conjunctions are stronger; a node conjoined with a planet acts as an eclipse of that planet.
conjunction/sun_rahu.lagna_or_context_notes: Rath: results depend on whether lagna or arudha lagna is Aquarius (spiritual) or Leo (worldly or negative).

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology 15.16 (chart 155) and 9.2
source_views.view: A close Sun-Rahu conjunction is an eclipse; Rahu shows great spirituality or renunciation while the Sun can be negative; in the 6th it shows disease, overcome when the Sun has the higher longitude.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology 12.13
source_views.view: An eclipse combination of the Sun can produce either a short-lived saint (Sun) or a long-lived criminal (Rahu).

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, The Planets (pp. 102-103)
source_views.view: A planet conjoined with either node is eclipsed: its energy is obstructed, negated or released; the nodes take on and magnify the planets they join.

conjunction/sun_rahu.disagreements: Brihat Jataka 14, Saravali 15, Jataka Parijata 8 and Phaladeepika 18 cover only the seven visible planets and say nothing on this pair. Rath's spiritual-versus-negative split is not found in Frawley, who stresses obstruction.
conjunction/sun_rahu.phrasing_guidance: Describe it as an intense, unusual relationship with authority, ego and the father, with a strong pull towards meaning or ambition. Avoid 'curse' or 'dosha' language; never predict illness.

conjunction/sun_ketu.summary: Sun with Ketu is treated in modern sources as an eclipse of the Sun: the Sun's significations are obstructed or turned inward. Frawley adds that Ketu can boost a planet that is strong in its own or exaltation sign. The classical two-planet chapters read do not cover the nodes.
common_outcomes: Sun's matters (self-confidence, father, status) obstructed or unusual
rare_outcomes: with a strong Sun, Ketu may boost its power (Frawley's general rule for Ketu)
strengtheners: Frawley: a planet in its own sign or exalted gains considerable power when conjoined with Ketu.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: conjunction with a node eclipses the planet, obstructing or negating its energy.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, The Planets (pp. 103, 105)
source_views.view: Node conjunctions eclipse a planet; Ketu boosts strong planets it joins (own sign or exalted); its results are sudden and unexpected, for good or ill.

conjunction/sun_ketu.disagreements: No classical two-planet chapter read covers this pair; only one modern source speaks to it.
conjunction/sun_ketu.phrasing_guidance: Keep it gentle: a reflective, less ego-driven expression of the self that may grow into inner strength. Do not predict harm to the father or health.

conjunction/moon_mars.summary: Moon with Mars forms Chandra-Mangala yoga: a brave, energetic, emotionally intense nature and drive to earn. Classical texts warn of rough trades and friction with the mother; Raman and PVR stress material success.
common_outcomes: material success and earning power
brave and energetic
intense, quick emotions
friction with the mother or women
rare_outcomes: trade in liquor, tools or women (Brihat Jataka; Phaladeepika)
blood disorders (Saravali)
high birth and virtue (Jataka Parijata)

by_area.personality: Valorous and brave (Saravali 15.8; Jataka Parijata 8.2); Raman: emotional, high-strung and hard to control in mind when Mars closely contacts the Moon.
by_area.career: Rough trades such as tools, liquor and earthenware (Brihat Jataka 14.2); artisan, metal or leather work (Saravali 15.8); Raman: earning through trades that cater to baser needs when afflicted, approved means when well placed.
by_area.finance: Raman: a powerful factor for stabilising finances; rich (Jataka Parijata 8.2); PVR: materially successful, possibly by unscrupulous means.
by_area.health: Blood disorders (Saravali 15.8).
by_area.relationships: May treat women badly (PVR).
by_area.family: Disobedient to or harsh with the mother (Brihat Jataka 14.2 in Sastri's tr.; Phaladeepika 18.2; PVR; Raman citing the ancients).

strengtheners: Raman: most productive of good in the 2nd, 9th, 10th or 11th house.
Raman: when the Moon and Mars are well disposed, earnings come through approved means.
Saravali 5.40: a planet joined with the Moon is able to give happiness.
Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Raman (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX): Moon in the 6th afflicted by Mars and Saturn gives obscure, hard-to-cure illness and revengeful enemies.
conjunction/moon_mars.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman holds the yoga also forms by mutual aspect (e.g. Moon in Taurus with Mars in Scorpio, Moon in Cancer with Mars in Capricorn) and calls those excellent; the conjunction-only definition is PVR's and the classical one.

named_yogas.name: Chandra-Mangala yoga (Sasi-Mangala)
named_yogas.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 6; PVR Narasimha Rao 11.3.5

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.2 (tr. M. Neely, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Trades in liquor and is involved in schemes with deceitful women; an inauspicious combination.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.2 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Dealer in rough tools, women, drinks and earthen jars, disobedient to his mother; note: Varahamihira differs here from Parashara, who holds the yoga good.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.2 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Deals in tools, women, liquor or earthen jars; disobedient to his mother.

source_views.source: Saravali 15.8 (archive.org English tr.)
source_views.view: Valorous, brave in war, a boxer, prone to blood disorders, makes things of clay, skin and minerals; an artisan and metal worker.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.2 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Brave, of high birth, virtuous, rich and worthy.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 6 Chandra Mangala Yoga
source_views.view: Gives the ancient results (unscrupulous earnings, harshness to mother), then argues the yoga strongly stabilises finances; good in the 2nd, 9th, 10th, 11th; also forms by mutual aspect.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX (Sixth House)
source_views.view: Mars in close contact with the Moon shows a high-strung, emotional, erratic temperament with little control over the mind.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.3.5
source_views.view: Worldly wise and materially successful; may earn by unscrupulous means; may treat mother or women badly.

conjunction/moon_mars.disagreements: Varahamihira (and Phaladeepika) read it negatively; Jataka Parijata and, per Sastri's note, Parashara read it as good; Raman sides with the good reading for finance. Raman counts mutual aspect as forming the yoga; PVR and the classical texts require the same sign.
conjunction/moon_mars.phrasing_guidance: Lead with drive, courage and earning ability, and note that strong feelings need a healthy outlet. Mention the mother relationship as an area for patience, not as conflict foretold; omit trades in women or liquor.

conjunction/moon_mercury.summary: Moon with Mercury, two benefics, gives pleasant, skilful speech, literary or interpretive talent, good fortune and reputation, and a charming manner.
common_outcomes: sweet, courteous speech
skill in interpreting, poetry or stories
good luck and reputation
many good qualities
rare_outcomes: devotion to the sciences and piety (Jataka Parijata)

by_area.personality: Courteous, resourceful, smiling and attractive (Brihat Jataka 14.2; Saravali 15.9); pious with varied merits (Jataka Parijata 8.2).
by_area.career: Clever at interpreting (Brihat Jataka 14.2 in Sastri's tr.); skilled in poetry and stories (Saravali 15.9).
by_area.finance: Wealthy (Saravali 15.9); Sastri's note says even this benefic pair is not good for finance.
by_area.relationships: Affectionate to the wife (Saravali 15.9).
by_area.spirituality: Pious (Jataka Parijata 8.2).

strengtheners: Saravali 5.40: a planet joined with the Moon can give happiness.
Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saravali 15.23: bad vargas reduce the results.
Raman (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX): a harmonious Moon-Mercury relationship is a great asset to the mind; affliction of either harms it.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.2 (tr. M. Neely, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Courteous speech, resourceful in reaching goals, reputation and good luck.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.2 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Sweet-tongued, clever in interpreting, lucky and famous; note: two benefics give good results, though not for finance.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.2 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Sweet speech, skilled at interpreting, good luck and fame.

source_views.source: Saravali 15.9 (archive.org English tr.)
source_views.view: Skilled in poems and stories, wealthy, kind to his wife, handsome, smiling, with distinct virtues.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.2 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Pious, devoted to the sciences, with many merits.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX (Sixth House)
source_views.view: The Moon and Mercury are the two determinants of mental qualities; harmony between them is a great asset.

conjunction/moon_mercury.disagreements: Saravali calls the native wealthy; Sastri's note on Brihat Jataka says the pair is not good for finance.
conjunction/moon_mercury.phrasing_guidance: Present as a warm, witty communicator with a feel for words and stories. Keep wealth claims modest.

conjunction/moon_jupiter.summary: Moon with Jupiter is one of the best two-planet combinations classically: intelligence, loyalty, respect for elders and the wise, family leadership and wealth, with Brihat Jataka adding a restless mind.
common_outcomes: wealthy
head or protector of the family or a group
virtuous, respectful of the wise and the divine
intelligent and protective of good people
rare_outcomes: fickle or restless mind (Brihat Jataka; Phaladeepika)
overpowers enemies (Sastri's tr.)

by_area.personality: Bold but restless (Brihat Jataka 14.2); firm in friendship and modest (Saravali 15.10); very intelligent (Jataka Parijata 8.3).
by_area.career: Leader of a group (Brihat Jataka 14.2).
by_area.finance: Wealthy (Brihat Jataka 14.2; Saravali 15.10); Sastri's note calls it an exception to conjunctions being bad for finance, and elsewhere says it gives good wealth and constitution.
by_area.health: Good constitution (Sastri's note to Brihat Jataka ch. 18).
by_area.relationships: Firm in friendship (Saravali 15.10).
by_area.family: Chief of the family (Brihat Jataka 14.2 in Sastri's tr.); respectful to relatives (Saravali 15.10).
by_area.spirituality: Regards the gods and the wise (Saravali 15.10); protects good people (Jataka Parijata 8.3).

strengtheners: Saravali 5.40: a planet joined with the Moon can give happiness.
Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saravali 15.23: bad vargas reduce the results.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.2 (tr. M. Neely, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Bold, leads a group, restless mind, holds wealth.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.2 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Overpowers enemies, fickle, head of the family, wealthy; note: an exception, good for finance.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.2 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Overpowers enemies but fickle; family chief and wealthy.

source_views.source: Saravali 15.10 (archive.org English tr.)
source_views.view: Firm in friendship, modest, respectful to relatives, wealthy, virtuous, honours gods and the learned.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.3 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Very intelligent and a protector of good people.

conjunction/moon_jupiter.disagreements: Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika add a restless or fickle mind; Saravali and Jataka Parijata do not.
conjunction/moon_jupiter.phrasing_guidance: Speak of generosity, wisdom and a protective, family-minded nature, with a lively mind that benefits from routine.

conjunction/moon_venus.summary: Moon with Venus is linked classically to cloth, fragrance and fine goods, skill in trade, and a pleasure-loving, easygoing nature.
common_outcomes: skill with cloth, weaving, tailoring or dyeing
clever in buying and selling
fond of flowers, scents and fine clothes
rare_outcomes: very lazy (Saravali)
evil-minded (Jataka Parijata)

by_area.personality: Dear to his family but very lazy (Saravali 15.11); Jataka Parijata 8.3 calls him evil-minded.
by_area.career: Weaving, tailoring and dyeing (Brihat Jataka 14.2; Phaladeepika 18.2); trade (Saravali 15.11; Jataka Parijata 8.3).
by_area.finance: Sastri's note: no financial success is indicated.
by_area.family: Dear to his family (Saravali 15.11).
by_area.spirituality: Knows how to perform rites (Saravali 15.11; 'kriya' read as duties or rites).

strengtheners: Saravali 5.40: a planet joined with the Moon can give happiness.
Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saravali 15.23: bad vargas reduce the results.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.2 (tr. M. Neely, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Skilled in the clothing trade and similar work.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.2 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Adept in weaving, tailoring and dyeing; note: no financial success indicated.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.2 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Skilled in weaving, tailoring and dyeing.

source_views.source: Saravali 15.11 (archive.org English tr.)
source_views.view: Has flowers, incense and clothes, knows his duties, dear to his family, very lazy, skilled in buying and selling.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.3 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Evil-minded and clever in bargaining.

conjunction/moon_venus.disagreements: Jataka Parijata gives a negative character reading that the others do not; Saravali alone gives laziness and family affection.
conjunction/moon_venus.phrasing_guidance: Speak of taste, a love of beauty and comfort, and a knack for trade or design. Leave out 'evil-minded'; mention a relaxed pace kindly.

conjunction/moon_saturn.summary: Moon with Saturn is a difficult classical pair: limited wealth, dependence on others and family or marital burdens, and (Raman) a serious, slow, melancholy cast of mind unless benefics relieve it.
common_outcomes: limited or slow-growing wealth
serious, stubborn or melancholy mood
dependence on or service under others
strains in marriage or with parents
rare_outcomes: born of a remarried widow (Brihat Jataka; Phaladeepika)
breeds elephants and horses, liked by the public (Saravali)

by_area.personality: Stubborn, slow, prone to melancholy without benefic relief (Raman); lacking virtues, controlled by others (Saravali 15.12).
by_area.career: Under the control of others; keeper of elephants and horses (Saravali 15.12).
by_area.finance: Without wealth (Saravali 15.12; Jataka Parijata 8.3); Sastri's note: bad for finance.
by_area.health: Raman: Moon in the 6th afflicted by Mars and Saturn gives obscure, hard-to-cure illness; Saturn afflicting the Moon gives chronic complaints.
by_area.relationships: An aged or worn wife (Saravali 15.12); a bad wife (Jataka Parijata 8.3).
by_area.family: Abuses parents (Jataka Parijata 8.3); unusual birth circumstances (Brihat Jataka 14.2).

strengtheners: Raman: Adhi yoga or Gajakesari yoga, or a benefic aspect, relieves the mind and gives balance and memory.
Saravali 5.40: a planet joined with the Moon can give happiness.
Saravali 15.23: good vargas improve the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Raman: with Rahu also involved, especially in Scorpio or the 6th, there is risk of mental disturbance.
Saravali 15.23: bad vargas worsen the results.
conjunction/moon_saturn.lagna_or_context_notes: Sastri's note to Brihat Jataka ch. 19 says Saturn's influence on the Moon is bad except when the Moon is in Taurus or Capricorn (stated for aspects; the note links it to this conjunction).

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.2 (tr. M. Neely, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Child of a remarried widow (punarbhu).

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.2 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Son of a remarried widow; note: bad for finance.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.2 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Son of a remarried widow.

source_views.source: Saravali 15.12 (archive.org English tr.)
source_views.view: An aged wife, liked by the public, keeps elephants and horses, lacking virtue, dependent, without wealth and defeated.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.3 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: A bad wife, abuses his parents, without wealth.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX (Sixth House)
source_views.view: Moon with Saturn and no benefic relief makes the mind stubborn, slow and given to melancholy; Adhi or Gajakesari yoga gives balance.

conjunction/moon_saturn.disagreements: Saravali allows popularity with the public; the other texts are wholly negative. Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika speak only of birth circumstances, the others of wealth and family.
conjunction/moon_saturn.phrasing_guidance: Frame as a serious, responsible, deep-feeling nature that matures with time, and advise rest and support during low moods. Never mention the birth-circumstance reading; do not diagnose depression.

conjunction/moon_rahu.summary: Moon with Rahu (Raman's Chandra-Chandala yoga) is read in modern sources as a highly sensitive, restless mind prone to obsession, unusual psychic experience or excess; how it shows depends on sign, house and relief from benefics. The classical two-planet chapters read do not cover it.
common_outcomes: heightened emotional and psychic sensitivity
restless, easily excited mind
pull towards unusual interests, mediumship or the occult
rare_outcomes: severe mental disturbance when heavily afflicted (Raman; Frawley)
temptation towards black magic, especially with the Moon in Scorpio (Raman)

by_area.personality: Raman: inclined to unhealthy or unusual mental states, obsession, religious mania, mediumship, drugs or vices, varying with sign and house. Frawley: heightened astral sensitivity.
by_area.health: Raman: Moon afflicted by Rahu shows skin troubles, and by Rahu or Ketu mental disturbance, hysteria or peculiar psychic states. Raman also says severe affliction can give suicidal tendencies through extreme sensitiveness [maraka: text predicts danger to life].
by_area.spirituality: Raman lists mediumship and religious mania among the tendencies; Frawley: astral sensitivity.

strengtheners: Frawley: Rahu's effect may be countered by other forces in the chart.
Raman: benefic association or aspect relieves the combination.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Raman: Moon in Scorpio afflicted by Rahu or Saturn is worse.
Raman: Rahu with the Moon and Saturn together, especially in the 6th, can make the native a 'psychological misfit' unless relieved by benefics.
conjunction/moon_rahu.lagna_or_context_notes: Raman: how the tendencies express themselves depends on the houses and signs.

named_yogas.name: Chandra-Chandala yoga
named_yogas.source: Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX (Sixth House, p. 138 of scan)
source_views.view: Chandra-Chandala yoga (Moon with Rahu) inclines the mind to unhealthy conditions, obsession, religious mania, mediumship, drugs and vices; severe affliction by Rahu or Saturn can give hysteria and suicidal tendencies.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX (Planets in the Sixth House)
source_views.view: Moon afflicted by Rahu: skin troubles; by Rahu or Ketu: mental derangement or peculiar psychic conditions; Rahu with Moon and Saturn is to be dreaded unless relieved.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, The Planets (pp. 103-104)
source_views.view: Rahu is the main factor behind neurosis and nervous disorders, especially when conjunct the Moon; he observed many Moon-Rahu conjunctions in such charts, though the effect is not always severe.

conjunction/moon_rahu.disagreements: No classical two-planet chapter read covers the pair. Raman and Frawley agree on the mental-sensitivity theme; neither gives a positive reading beyond sensitivity.
conjunction/moon_rahu.phrasing_guidance: Speak of a sensitive, intuitive, imaginative mind that does best with grounding routines and calm surroundings. Never mention insanity, suicide or black magic; do not diagnose.

conjunction/moon_ketu.summary: Moon with Ketu is an eclipse of the Moon in modern readings: emotional detachment or sensitivity and unusual psychic states. Sources are thin; the classical two-planet chapters read do not cover it.
common_outcomes: inward or detached emotional life
heightened psychic sensitivity
rare_outcomes: mental disturbance when heavily afflicted (Raman)

by_area.health: Raman: Moon afflicted by Rahu or Ketu shows mental disturbance, hysteria or peculiar psychic conditions.

weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: a node conjoined with a planet eclipses it, obstructing or negating its energy.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX (Planets in the Sixth House)
source_views.view: Moon afflicted by Rahu or Ketu: mental derangement, hysteria or peculiar psychic conditions.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, The Planets (p. 103)
source_views.view: Conjunction with either node eclipses a planet.

conjunction/moon_ketu.phrasing_guidance: Describe a quiet, inward, intuitive emotional nature that benefits from reflection and spiritual practice. Avoid any mental-health claims.

conjunction/mars_mercury.summary: Mars with Mercury points classically to medicine, herbs, oils and drugs, metal and building trades, and combative skill; Jataka Parijata adds eloquence. Wealth and marriage are often described as weak.
common_outcomes: work with medicines, herbs, oils or drugs
skill in wrestling or boxing
sharp, eloquent speech
rare_outcomes: work with gold and iron or as a builder (Saravali)
an unlucky marriage (Saravali)

by_area.personality: Eloquent (Jataka Parijata 8.3).
by_area.career: Trader in roots, oils and drugs, or a wrestler (Brihat Jataka 14.3); medicine-making, metal work, architecture (Saravali 15.13); medicine and fine arts (Jataka Parijata 8.3).
by_area.finance: Little wealth (Saravali 15.13); Sastri's note: bad for finance.
by_area.relationships: Unlucky wife and an improper liaison (Saravali 15.13).

strengtheners: Planetary war: if the two are within about a degree, the winner gains and the loser weakens; a planet that wins is strong and auspicious (Saravali 4.36, 5.40).
Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Planetary war: the planet that is southern, dim or small loses (Brihat Samhita 17.9); Frawley instead says the planet with the lower longitude wins. A defeated planet loses its auspiciousness and can give bad results in full (Saravali 5.2-4, 5.27).
Saravali 15.23: bad vargas reduce the results.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.3 (tr. M. Neely, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Trader in roots, oils and similar goods, or a wrestler.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.3 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Dealer in herbs, barks, oils and drugs, clever at boxing; note: condemned trades per Manu, bad for finance.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.3 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Deals in herbs, barks, oils and drugs; skilled at boxing.

source_views.source: Saravali 15.13 (archive.org English tr.)
source_views.view: Unlucky wife, little wealth, works with gold and iron, an architect, keeps a bad widow, expert in making medicines.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.3 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Eloquent and clever in medicine and fine arts.

source_views.source: Brihat Samhita 17.7, 17.9 (siva.sh)
source_views.view: In a planetary meeting the defeated planet harms what it governs and the victor brings prosperity; the southern, dim, harsh-looking or small planet is defeated.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, Planetary Aspects and Combinations (pp. 175-176)
source_views.view: Planets within one degree are at war; the lower longitude wins; a benefic losing to a malefic is badly weakened; a retrograde loser suffers less.

conjunction/mars_mercury.disagreements: All texts read share the medicine/drugs theme; Jataka Parijata is positive (eloquence, arts) where Saravali is negative on wife and wealth. Planetary-war winner: Brihat Samhita (northern and brighter wins) versus Frawley (lower longitude wins).
conjunction/mars_mercury.phrasing_guidance: Present as a quick, practical, debating mind with aptitude for medicine, technical or hands-on trades. Do not predict marital misfortune.

conjunction/mars_jupiter.summary: Mars with Jupiter is a favourable classical pair: leadership, standing in the community, learning and wealth earned through one's own effort.
common_outcomes: leader of a town, group or people
learned, intelligent and articulate
wealth through own effort
respected and worthy
rare_outcomes: skill in mathematics or computation (Jataka Parijata)
fond of weapons (Saravali)

by_area.personality: Loving, revered and worthy (Jataka Parijata 8.4); intelligent, eloquent and wise (Saravali 15.14).
by_area.career: Head of a city or ruler (Brihat Jataka 14.3); artisan or Vedic scholar (Saravali 15.14).
by_area.finance: Gains wealth (Brihat Jataka 14.3); Sastri's note: earns by own exertion, an exception to conjunctions being bad for finance.
by_area.spirituality: Learned in sacred lore (Saravali 15.14; Brihat Jataka 14.3 'a Brahmin').

strengtheners: Planetary war: a winning planet is strong and auspicious (Saravali 4.36, 5.40).
Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Planetary war: the loser (southern, dim or small per Brihat Samhita 17.9; lower longitude wins per Frawley) is weakened (Saravali 5.2-4, 5.27).
Saravali 15.23: bad vargas reduce the results.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.3 (tr. M. Neely, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: City administrator, ruler, gains wealth, or a Brahmin.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.3 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Leader of a city, king or wealthy Brahmin; note: a good position, earns by his own exertion.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.3 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: City leader, king or wealthy Brahmin.

conjunction/mars_jupiter.disagreements: Saravali stresses learning and weapons rather than rulership; otherwise the texts agree it is favourable.
conjunction/mars_jupiter.phrasing_guidance: Present as principled courage, leadership and learning that earns respect and resources.

conjunction/mars_venus.summary: Mars with Venus gives strong passions, physical vigour and cleverness; classical texts warn of gambling, deceit and affairs, though Saravali also gives leadership and calculating skill.
common_outcomes: passionate and physically active
clever, capable, sometimes cunning
liking for games of chance or risk
rare_outcomes: chief among his people, honoured (Saravali)
mathematician or astrologer (Saravali)
interest in metallurgy (Jataka Parijata)

by_area.personality: Capable but cunning and fond of tricks (Brihat Jataka 14.3; Jataka Parijata 8.4); Sastri's note calls it a moral wreck.
by_area.career: Herdsman, athlete or wrestler (Brihat Jataka 14.3); mathematician or astrologer and leader (Saravali 15.15); metallurgy (Jataka Parijata 8.4).
by_area.finance: Fond of gambling (Brihat Jataka 14.3; Saravali 15.15).
by_area.relationships: Pursues others' spouses (Brihat Jataka 14.3; Phaladeepika 18.3).

strengtheners: Planetary war: a winning planet is strong and auspicious (Saravali 4.36, 5.40); Frawley: a benefic that wins against a malefic becomes much stronger.
Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Planetary war: Frawley says a benefic (Venus) that loses to a malefic (Mars) may be rendered very weak; Brihat Samhita 17.9 names the southern, dim or small planet as the loser.
Saravali 15.23: bad vargas reduce the results.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.3 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Shepherd, wrestler, adulterous or gambler.

source_views.view: Fond of metallurgy, delights in tricks, cunning.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (p. 176)
source_views.view: A benefic defeated in planetary war by a malefic may be very weak; one that wins becomes much stronger.

conjunction/mars_venus.disagreements: Varahamihira condemns the pair; Sastri's note says Parashara and others favour it, and Saravali gives honour and leadership alongside gambling.
conjunction/mars_venus.phrasing_guidance: Describe passion, charm, energy and a competitive streak, and suggest channels like sport or creative work. Do not predict infidelity or gambling.

conjunction/mars_saturn.summary: Mars with Saturn, two malefics, is read classically as hardship, quarrelsomeness and unreliability, with skill in metals or mechanical tricks; Raman links it to accidents, operations and disputes with siblings.
common_outcomes: hardship or struggle
quarrelsome or disputatious
work with metals or mechanical skill
reputation suffers through unreliability
rare_outcomes: interest in music (Jataka Parijata)
trouble from weapons or poison (Saravali)

by_area.personality: Untruthful and held in low regard (Brihat Jataka 14.3); deceitful and quarrelsome (Saravali 15.16); disputatious and slow-witted (Jataka Parijata 8.4).
by_area.career: Metal work, jugglery (Saravali 15.16).
by_area.finance: Miserable, beset by hardship (Brihat Jataka 14.3).
by_area.health: Troubled by weapons and poison (Saravali 15.16). Raman: Mars in the 6th afflicted by Saturn, death may come through an operation or injury by animals [maraka: text predicts danger to life / death]; Saturn in the 6th afflicted by Mars gives dangerous illness and operations.
by_area.family: Raman: Saturn afflicting Mars favours litigation with brothers and cousins.

strengtheners: Planetary war: the winner is strong (Saravali 4.36, 5.40).
Saravali 15.23: good vargas improve the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Planetary war: the southern, dim or small planet loses (Brihat Samhita 17.9); Frawley: the lower longitude wins. The loser gives bad results (Saravali 5.27).
Sastri's note: a conjunction of two malefics, bad.
Saravali 15.23: bad vargas worsen the results.
conjunction/mars_saturn.lagna_or_context_notes: House-specific notes read: the 6th house (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX).

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.3 (tr. M. Neely, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Beset by hardship, unreliable in promises, held in low regard.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.3 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Miserable, untruthful, despised; note: two malefics, bad.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.3 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Miserable, untruthful and despised.

source_views.source: Saravali 15.16 (archive.org English tr.)
source_views.view: Metal worker, skilled in jugglery, deceitful, clever at theft, troubled by weapons and poison, fond of quarrels.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.4 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Disputatious, given to music, dull-witted.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX (Planets in the Sixth House)
source_views.view: In the 6th: Saturn afflicting Mars points to death by operation or animals, and to litigation with brothers and cousins; Mars afflicting Saturn to dangerous illness and operations.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers (pp. 175-176)
source_views.view: Planetary war within one degree; the lower longitude wins.

conjunction/mars_saturn.disagreements: All texts read are negative; Jataka Parijata alone adds music. Planetary-war winner rules differ between Brihat Samhita and Frawley.
conjunction/mars_saturn.phrasing_guidance: Frame as determination and endurance under pressure, with a need for patience, safety and calm handling of disputes. Never predict accidents, surgery or death; suggest care with machinery and conflict.

conjunction/mars_rahu.summary: Mars with Rahu intensifies Mars: modern sources link it to impulsive force and, when afflicted, risk of accidents or self-harm. The classical two-planet chapters read do not cover it.
common_outcomes: amplified drive and aggression
rare_outcomes: danger of self-harm when severely afflicted (Raman)

by_area.personality: Frawley: the nodes take on and magnify the planets they join.
by_area.health: Raman: Mars in the 6th afflicted by Rahu, death may be by suicide [maraka: text predicts danger to life / death]; Mars afflicted by Rahu or Ketu shows a tendency to suicide or death by poisoning.

strengtheners: Raman: Mars well disposed is an asset.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: a node conjoined with a planet eclipses it.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX (Planets in the Sixth House)
source_views.view: Mars in the 6th afflicted by Rahu: death may be due to suicide; Mars afflicted by Rahu or Ketu: tendency to suicide or poisoning.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, The Planets (pp. 103-106)
source_views.view: Nodes eclipse and magnify the planets they join; Rahu can also boost a strong planet, to a lesser degree than Ketu.

conjunction/mars_rahu.disagreements: Raman's reading is limited to the 6th house and affliction; Frawley gives only general node rules.
conjunction/mars_rahu.phrasing_guidance: Speak of intense drive that needs discipline and safe outlets such as sport. Never mention suicide, poisoning or death.

conjunction/mars_ketu.summary: Mars with Ketu: Frawley treats Ketu as Mars-like and says it boosts a strong Mars (e.g. great military prowess); Raman warns of danger when Mars is afflicted by Ketu in the 6th. The classical two-planet chapters read do not cover it.
common_outcomes: sharp, sudden energy
rare_outcomes: great martial or military prowess with a strong Mars (Frawley)
danger of poisoning when afflicted (Raman)

by_area.career: Frawley: Mars in Scorpio in the 3rd with Ketu can give great military prowess.
by_area.health: Raman: Mars in the 6th afflicted by Ketu, death may be by poisoning [maraka: text predicts danger to life / death].

strengtheners: Frawley: Ketu gives considerable power to a planet in its own sign or exalted (Mars in Aries, Scorpio or Capricorn).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Raman: affliction of Mars by Ketu is unfavourable.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, The Planets (pp. 103, 105-106)
source_views.view: Ketu is like Mars; it boosts strong planets it joins; Mars in Scorpio in the 3rd with Ketu can give great military prowess.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX (Planets in the Sixth House)
source_views.view: Mars in the 6th afflicted by Ketu: death by poisoning; Mars afflicted by Rahu or Ketu: tendency to suicide or poisoning.

conjunction/mars_ketu.disagreements: Frawley allows a strongly positive result with a dignified Mars; Raman, speaking of the 6th house and affliction, is negative.
conjunction/mars_ketu.phrasing_guidance: Describe focused, sudden bursts of courage and a need for caution with impulsive action. Never mention poisoning or death.

conjunction/mercury_jupiter.summary: Mercury with Jupiter is linked to the performing arts (music, dance, drama), scholarship and eloquence, with a wise, happy nature.
common_outcomes: talent for music, dance or acting
learned and wise
eloquent and amiable
rare_outcomes: statesman (Sastri's alternative reading of 'rangachara')
exceedingly wealthy (Jataka Parijata)

by_area.personality: Wise and happy (Saravali 15.17); eloquent, handsome and amiable (Jataka Parijata 8.4).
by_area.career: Actor, musician, dancer (Brihat Jataka 14.4; Phaladeepika 18.4); dancer, scholar, singer, instrumentalist (Saravali 15.17).
by_area.finance: Exceedingly wealthy (Jataka Parijata 8.4); Sastri's note: not good for finance unless these planets rule the house of wealth.
by_area.spirituality: Raman: Mercury joined by Jupiter in the 6th points to spiritual gains.

strengtheners: Planetary war: the winner is strong (Saravali 4.36, 5.40).
Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Planetary war: the loser (southern, dim or small per Brihat Samhita 17.9; lower longitude wins per Frawley) is weakened (Saravali 5.27).
Saravali 15.23: bad vargas reduce the results.

conjunction/mercury_venus.summary: Mercury with Venus gives eloquence, persuasion, artistic and musical taste, learning and social influence, often with property or wealth.

fond of music, art, humour and fine things
learning in sacred or classical texts
leadership in an assembly or group

politician (Saravali)

by_area.career: Head of an assembly or of landholders (Brihat Jataka 14.4); politician or artisan (Saravali 15.18).
by_area.finance: Abundantly rich (Saravali 15.18); possesses land (Brihat Jataka 14.4 in Sastri's tr.); Sastri's note: not good for finance.
by_area.spirituality: Versed in sacred books (Jataka Parijata 8.5); studies the Vedas (Saravali 15.18).

skill with words or verse

much travel (Saravali)

conjunction/mercury_rahu.summary: Mercury with Rahu: modern sources say Rahu amplifies and unsettles Mercury, the mind and nerves; Raman warns of excitability and nervous strain when afflicted. The classical two-planet chapters read do not cover it.
common_outcomes: restless, quick, unconventional mind
rare_outcomes: nervous strain or mental excitability when afflicted (Raman)

by_area.personality: Frawley: Rahu acting on mind factors such as Mercury heightens sensitivity.
by_area.health: Raman: Mercury afflicted by Rahu, Ketu or Saturn gives despondency and excitability; in the 6th, affliction by Mars and Rahu or by Saturn and Rahu risks breakdown through excitement.

weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: a node conjoined with a planet eclipses it.

source_views.view: Rahu is a key factor in nervous and neurological disorders, especially when it influences the Moon, Mercury or the 4th house.

conjunction/mercury_rahu.phrasing_guidance: Describe an inventive, fast, unconventional mind that benefits from rest and focus. Never mention insanity.

conjunction/mercury_ketu.summary: Mercury with Ketu has little sourced material: Raman groups Ketu with Rahu and Saturn as afflictions of Mercury that can bring despondency or excitability, and Frawley's node rules apply. The classical two-planet chapters read do not cover it.
rare_outcomes: despondency or excitability when afflicted (Raman)

strengtheners: Frawley: Ketu boosts a planet in its own sign or exalted (Mercury in Gemini or Virgo).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: a node conjoined with a planet eclipses it.

conjunction/mercury_ketu.phrasing_guidance: Describe intuitive, non-linear thinking that benefits from structure. Avoid mental-health claims.

conjunction/jupiter_venus.summary: Jupiter with Venus, the two great benefics, gives learning, wealth, a good spouse and many virtues; Varahamihira's commentator calls it the exception to conjunctions being bad for finance.
common_outcomes: learned and well read
prosperous
a good spouse and happy marriage
many good qualities
rare_outcomes: royal favour (Jataka Parijata)
earns through teaching or debate (Saravali)

by_area.career: Lives by learning and debate (Saravali 15.20); in the king's favour (Jataka Parijata 8.5).
by_area.finance: Prosperous (Brihat Jataka 14.4); Sastri's note: good for finance.
by_area.relationships: Married, an excellent wife (Brihat Jataka 14.4; Saravali 15.20).
by_area.spirituality: Follows a highly virtuous path (Saravali 15.20).

source_views.view: Energetic, in royal favour, very intelligent.

conjunction/jupiter_venus.phrasing_guidance: Present as wisdom, grace, prosperity and a supportive partnership.

conjunction/jupiter_saturn.summary: Jupiter with Saturn is the most disputed classical pair: Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika give humble crafts (barber, potter, cook), Jataka Parijata an artist, while Saravali gives heroism, wealth and civic leadership.
common_outcomes: practical or artistic craft
steady, structured work
rare_outcomes: head of a town, assembly or association, famous and wealthy (Saravali)

by_area.personality: Heroic and famous (Saravali 15.21).
by_area.career: Barber, potter or cook (Brihat Jataka 14.4; Phaladeepika 18.4); an artist (Jataka Parijata 8.5); head of a city, village or association (Saravali 15.21).
by_area.finance: Plenty of wealth (Saravali 15.21).

conjunction/jupiter_saturn.disagreements: Saravali's leadership-and-wealth reading is the opposite of Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika's humble crafts; Jataka Parijata's 'artist' sits between. In Sastri's Brihat Jataka notes, the eyesight and marriage-brings-wealth remarks printed under 'Jupiter conjunction Saturn' match the Venus-Saturn verse (14.5) and are not used here.
conjunction/jupiter_saturn.phrasing_guidance: Present as patient, structured, practical skill that can grow into responsibility in the community. Avoid naming specific humble trades.

conjunction/jupiter_rahu.summary: Jupiter with Rahu is called Guru-Chandala yoga in modern usage (Sanjay Rath uses the name for this conjunction); Frawley's rules say Rahu eclipses and magnifies the planet it joins. The classical two-planet chapters read do not cover it, and no source read gives a general result for it.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: a node conjoined with a planet eclipses it, obstructing, negating or releasing its energy.
conjunction/jupiter_rahu.lagna_or_context_notes: Rath applies the yoga to the houses Jupiter rules (e.g. Guru-chandala of the 4th lord affecting mother's side and family business) in chart examples; no general rule is stated.

named_yogas.name: Guru-Chandala yoga
named_yogas.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology ch. VII (chart example)

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology ch. VII, with a further use of the term in ch. IV (4.4) (in the same archive.org item)
source_views.view: In ch. VII, calls the 4th lord Jupiter's conjunction with Rahu the Guru-chandala yoga and reads it through the houses Jupiter rules; in ch. IV the yoga works alongside a strong raja yoga and brings division and upheaval (whether that example is a conjunction was not checked).

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, The Planets (pp. 103-106)
