conjunction/jupiter_rahu.disagreements: No classical two-planet chapter read covers the pair. The general results for this dosha belong in the dosha/guru_chandal entry.
conjunction/jupiter_rahu.phrasing_guidance: Describe it as unconventional thinking about belief, teachers and ethics, best balanced by trusted guidance. Avoid 'chandala' or other caste-loaded labels when speaking to users.

conjunction/jupiter_ketu.summary: Jupiter with Ketu has only general node rules in the sources read: Ketu eclipses a planet but also boosts one that is strong in its own or exaltation sign (Frawley). The classical two-planet chapters read do not cover it.
rare_outcomes: a strong Jupiter boosted by Ketu (Frawley's general rule)
strengtheners: Frawley: Ketu gives considerable power to a planet in its own sign or exalted (Jupiter in Sagittarius, Pisces or Cancer).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: a node conjoined with a planet eclipses it.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, The Planets (pp. 103, 105)
source_views.view: Node conjunctions eclipse a planet; Ketu boosts a planet in its own sign or exalted; Ketu's results are sudden.

conjunction/jupiter_ketu.phrasing_guidance: Describe an inward, spiritually inclined wisdom. Do not predict loss of teachers or children.

conjunction/venus_saturn.summary: Venus with Saturn gives artistic, craft and writing skill (painting, drawing, books, sculpture), with Brihat Jataka linking wealth to a young woman or marriage and adding weak eyesight.
common_outcomes: skill in painting, drawing, writing or sculpture
wealth that grows through a woman or the marriage
rare_outcomes: short-sighted (Brihat Jataka; Phaladeepika)
owns cattle or quadrupeds (Saravali; Jataka Parijata)
athlete or boxer (Saravali; Jataka Parijata)
barber or woodcutter (Saravali)

by_area.personality: Fond of wandering (Saravali 15.22).
by_area.career: Writing, painting, books (Brihat Jataka 14.5); painter or sculptor, woodwork, barber, boxer (Saravali 15.22); athlete (Jataka Parijata 8.5).
by_area.finance: Wealth increased through a young woman (Brihat Jataka 14.5); Sastri: marriage is the key to financial success; large herds of cattle (Jataka Parijata 8.5).
by_area.health: Short-sighted (Brihat Jataka 14.5; Phaladeepika 18.5).
by_area.relationships: Sastri: marriage and the start of earning come together.

strengtheners: Planetary war: the winner is strong (Saravali 4.36, 5.40).
Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Planetary war: the loser is weakened (Brihat Samhita 17.9; Frawley; Saravali 5.27); Frawley: a benefic (Venus) losing to a malefic may be very weak.
Saravali 15.23: bad vargas reduce the results.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.5 (tr. M. Neely, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Poor eyesight, wealth growing through young women, expertise in drawing, writing and books; other combinations to be judged from those already given.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.5 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Short-sighted, wealth through a young woman (marriage the key to financial success), skilled in writing and painting; the note on eyesight and earning beginning with marriage is printed under the Jupiter-Saturn heading.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 18.5 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Short-sighted, wealth grows through a young woman, skilled in writing and painting.

source_views.source: Saravali 15.22 (archive.org English tr.)
source_views.view: Skilled in cutting wood, a barber, painter or sculptor, boxer, fond of wandering, owns quadrupeds.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 8.5 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Owns large herds of cattle and is an athlete.

conjunction/venus_saturn.disagreements: Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika stress arts, writing and wealth through marriage; Saravali stresses crafts and wandering; Jataka Parijata gives cattle and athletics.
conjunction/venus_saturn.phrasing_guidance: Present as patient artistic or craft talent and a partnership that supports material growth. Mention eyesight only as general care.

conjunction/venus_rahu.summary: Venus with Rahu has only general node rules in the sources read: Rahu eclipses and magnifies the planet it joins, and can boost a strong planet to a lesser degree than Ketu (Frawley). The classical two-planet chapters read do not cover it.
strengtheners: Frawley: Rahu can boost a planet in its own sign or exalted (Venus in Taurus, Libra or Pisces), less than Ketu does.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: a node conjoined with a planet eclipses it.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, The Planets (pp. 103-106)
source_views.view: Nodes eclipse and magnify the planets they join; a strong Rahu gives worldly success and fulfilment of desires but usually not inner fulfilment.

conjunction/venus_rahu.phrasing_guidance: Describe strong attraction to beauty, pleasure and the unusual, best balanced by clear values. Do not predict scandal.

conjunction/venus_ketu.summary: Venus with Ketu: Frawley says Ketu gives considerable power to a strong Venus, citing Venus in Libra in the 2nd with Ketu as giving wealth; otherwise only general node rules are sourced. The classical two-planet chapters read do not cover it.
rare_outcomes: wealth when Venus is in its own sign, e.g. Libra in the 2nd (Frawley)

by_area.finance: Frawley: Venus in Libra in the 2nd house with Ketu will give wealth.

strengtheners: Frawley: Ketu gives considerable power to a planet in its own sign or exalted.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: a node conjoined with a planet eclipses it.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, The Planets (pp. 103, 105)
source_views.view: Ketu boosts strong planets; Venus in Libra in the 2nd conjoined with Ketu gives wealth.

conjunction/venus_ketu.phrasing_guidance: Describe refined, perhaps unconventional taste and a quieter, inward approach to love; mention material gains only when Venus is strong.

conjunction/saturn_rahu.summary: Saturn with Rahu joins two heavy malefics (Frawley: Rahu acts like Saturn); Raman links Rahu's affliction of Saturn to nervous or hysterical states, especially in the 6th. The classical two-planet chapters read do not cover it.
rare_outcomes: hysteria or nervous strain when afflicted in the 6th (Raman)

by_area.health: Raman: Saturn in the 6th afflicted by Rahu: hysteria; Rahu in the 6th with the Moon and Saturn: liability to mental derangement.

strengtheners: Raman: benefic associations or aspects relieve the combination (stated for Rahu with Saturn and the Moon).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: a node conjoined with a planet eclipses it.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX (Planets in the Sixth House)
source_views.view: Saturn in the 6th afflicted by Rahu: hysteria; Rahu with the Moon and Saturn: mental derangement unless relieved by benefics.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, The Planets (pp. 102-103)
source_views.view: Rahu is like Saturn, the greater malefic, but subtler and harder to neutralise; it magnifies the planets it joins.

conjunction/saturn_rahu.phrasing_guidance: Describe long-term challenges that build resilience and the value of steady routines. Avoid 'curse' language; never diagnose.

conjunction/saturn_ketu.summary: Saturn with Ketu has only general node rules in the sources read: Ketu eclipses a planet but boosts one in its own or exaltation sign (Frawley). The classical two-planet chapters read do not cover it.
strengtheners: Frawley: Ketu gives considerable power to a planet in its own sign or exalted (Saturn in Capricorn, Aquarius or Libra).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: a node conjoined with a planet eclipses it.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, The Planets (pp. 103, 105)
source_views.view: Node conjunctions eclipse a planet; Ketu boosts strong planets; its results are sudden, for good or ill.

conjunction/saturn_ketu.phrasing_guidance: Describe a serious, detached, introspective streak that can support discipline and spiritual practice.

conjunction/rahu_ketu.summary: Rahu and Ketu never conjoin: they are the two opposite lunar nodes, always 180 degrees (seven signs) apart, so there is no conjunction to interpret.
conjunction/rahu_ketu.phrasing_guidance: If asked, explain that the nodes are always opposite each other, so this pair never occurs in a chart.

source_views.view: Deva gana birth: eats sparingly; oriented to the other world; appreciates virtue; a fine speaker; said to stand apart from worldly qualities; the text also says short of stature.

source_views.source: Muhurta Chintamani of Rama Daivajna (with Hindi commentary; Source Library AI translation, unreviewed), ch. 6 (vivaha / marriage) v.29-30, 33 (p.97-98)
source_views.view: Gana is fixed by the birth nakshatra (Deva: Ashwini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Hasta, Swati, Anuradha, Shravana, Revati; Manushya: Bharani, Rohini, Ardra, Purva Phalguni, Uttara Phalguni, Purva Ashadha, Uttara Ashadha, Purva Bhadrapada, Uttara Bhadrapada; Rakshasa: Krittika, Ashlesha, Magha, Chitra, Vishakha, Jyeshtha, Mula, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha). Same gana: great affection (6 points); Deva-Manushya: middling (5); Rakshasa with Manushya: [maraka: text predicts danger to life / death]; Rakshasa with Deva: enmity (0). The commentary adds directional variants (a Manushya groom with a Rakshasa bride is the worst case). v.33: if the Moon-sign lords or navamsha lords of the couple are friends, the gana fault does not apply.

panchang/gana/deva.disagreements: The Jataka Bharanam verse is unusually ascetic (short stature, little food) compared with the usual reading of Deva gana as simply virtuous; the AI translator also flags this.
panchang/gana/deva.phrasing_guidance: Describe gana as a temperament style, not moral worth; never call anyone 'demonic'. For Rakshasa, say 'forceful, independent temperament'. In matching, mention cancellations before any warning, and never repeat a death prediction.

cancellations.condition: the lords of the couple's Moon signs, or of their navamshas, are friends

panchang/nadi/adi.summary: Adi (first) nadi: one of three nakshatra groups used in nadi-kuta, the heaviest-weighted matching factor.
common_outcomes: used only in compatibility: both partners in the same nadi is a fault; different nadis earn the full 8 points

by_area.relationships: nadi-kuta: 8 of 36 points; same nadi is the classic 'nadi dosha'

weakeners_or_cancellations: Same nadi for both partners is a matching fault (nadi dosha).
panchang/nadi/adi.lagna_or_context_notes: Nadi comes from the Moon's nakshatra at birth and says nothing about the person alone in the sources read; it is a matching factor.

source_views.source: Muhurta Chintamani of Rama Daivajna (with Hindi commentary; Source Library AI translation, unreviewed), ch. 6 (vivaha / marriage) v.34 (p.98-99)
source_views.view: Nadi is set by the birth nakshatra (Adi: Ashwini, Ardra, Punarvasu, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Jyeshtha, Mula, Shatabhisha, Purva Bhadrapada; Madhya: Bharani, Mrigashira, Pushya, Purva Phalguni, Chitra, Anuradha, Purva Ashadha, Dhanishta, Uttara Bhadrapada; Antya: Krittika, Rohini, Ashlesha, Magha, Swati, Vishakha, Uttara Ashadha, Shravana, Revati). Bride and groom in the same nadi is inauspicious; both in Madhya nadi: [maraka: text predicts danger to life / death]. Other views quoted: the side nadis' fault does not apply south of the Godavari or for Kshatriyas; Adi harms the groom, Antya the bride, Madhya both. If only the nakshatra (not the pada) nadi matches, the fault is minor. Remedies: Mahamrityunjaya japa and the gift of a golden nadi. Nadi purity is required even when other kuta faults are cancelled (v.32 commentary).

panchang/nadi/adi.disagreements: Muhurta Chintamani records several views: regional exemptions for the side nadis (Adi, Antya), which partner each nadi harms, and four- and five-nadi schemes used in some regions instead of the three-nadi scheme.
panchang/nadi/adi.phrasing_guidance: Do not describe nadi as a personal trait. In matching, state nadi dosha calmly, mention the exemptions and remedies, and never repeat a prediction of death or childlessness.

cancellations.condition: the nadi matches by nakshatra but not by pada: fault is minor
regional view: side-nadi (Adi/Antya) fault not applied south of the Godavari or for Kshatriyas

remedies.remedy: Mahamrityunjaya japa; gift of a golden nadi

panchang/yoni.summary: Yoni assigns each birth nakshatra an animal (14 animals, two nakshatras each with Abhijit); in marriage matching it measures instinctive and physical compatibility and scores 4 of 36 points.
common_outcomes: same yoni: excellent; friendly yonis: good; neutral: average; enemy yonis: inauspicious
natural enemy pairs: cow-tiger, elephant-lion, horse-buffalo, dog-deer, mongoose-serpent, monkey-sheep, cat-rat

by_area.relationships: yoni-kuta, 4 points

weakeners_or_cancellations: Enemy yonis (e.g. cow-tiger) are to be avoided in a match (Muhurta Chintamani ch. 6 v.26).
panchang/yoni.lagna_or_context_notes: From the Moon's nakshatra. Animals per Muhurta Chintamani: horse (Ashwini, Shatabhisha), elephant (Bharani, Revati), sheep (Krittika, Pushya), serpent (Rohini, Mrigashira), dog (Ardra, Mula), cat (Punarvasu, Ashlesha), rat (Magha, Purva Phalguni), cow (Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Bhadrapada), buffalo (Hasta, Swati), tiger (Chitra, Vishakha), deer (Anuradha, Jyeshtha), monkey (Purva Ashadha, Shravana), mongoose (Uttara Ashadha, Abhijit), lion (Dhanishta, Purva Bhadrapada).

panchang/yoni.disagreements: The AI-translated verse has slips (Purva Ashadha under both monkey and dog; Magha and Purva Phalguni under cat); the commentary on the next page gives the usual scheme (Ardra = dog, Magha and Purva Phalguni = rat), used here.
panchang/yoni.phrasing_guidance: Speak of yoni as one small compatibility factor; avoid sexual or animal-character language about the person.

panchang/varna.summary: Varna ranks the Moon signs into four classes for marriage matching (1 of 36 points); it is the lowest-weighted factor and says little about the person.
common_outcomes: Brahmin: Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces; Kshatriya: Aries, Leo, Sagittarius; Vaishya: Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn; Shudra: Gemini, Libra, Aquarius
the point is given when the groom's varna is equal to or higher than the bride's

panchang/varna.lagna_or_context_notes: From the Moon sign. It is a matching rule only; the sources read give no personal reading for it.

panchang/vashya.summary: Vashya groups the Moon signs (human, quadruped, water, wild, insect) to judge which partner's sign 'is controlled by' the other's; it scores 2 of 36 points in marriage matching.
common_outcomes: human signs hold all others under their control except Leo; water signs are 'food' of the human signs
all signs are under Leo except Scorpio
the points are given when the bride's sign is under the groom's sign

by_area.relationships: vashya-kuta, 2 points; read as mutual attraction or influence

panchang/vashya.lagna_or_context_notes: From the Moon sign. Human signs per the commentary: Gemini, Virgo, Libra, first half of Sagittarius, Aquarius. Muhurta Chintamani says other relations of control are to be judged 'from worldly behaviour', and its table gives half or partial points for mixed pairs.

panchang/tithi/1.phrasing_guidance: Present as a minor colouring of temperament, never as fate. Mention the tithi deity as a devotional focus. If a dosha is noted (gandanta, Rikta, Amavasya, Krishna Chaturdashi), mention it gently as a traditional concern with a traditional remedy; do not repeat any prediction about death or harm to parents.

remedy/sun.summary: Remedies for Sun are indicated when it is weak, afflicted or badly placed, and especially while it runs a hard dasha or antardasha or an adverse transit (Phaladeepika 26.49; BPHS 84.26). The classical means are worship, its mantra, homa, feeding and gifts; modern authors add bija mantras, conduct and lifestyle changes, and optional gemstones only when Sun is functionally helpful in the chart.
common_outcomes: Classical texts present planetary worship as bringing peace, prosperity, health and long life (BPHS 84.2-3).
Navagraha Stotra phalashruti: obstacles pacified, bad dreams removed, troubles from planets and stars calmed.
PVR: remedies change the details of a period, not its basic pattern.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: debilitated (Libra), in an enemy sign such as Saturn's, in the 6th/8th/12th, or under Saturn, Rahu or Ketu (Ketu's close conjunction especially). Shows as low self-worth, weak will, dependence; the father may fare poorly.
remedy/sun.lagna_or_context_notes: Which remedy fits depends on the planet's functional role from the lagna: modern authors (PVR 34.2; Frawley, Astrology of the Seers Part III ch. 4 and Ayurvedic Astrology ch. 9) reserve gems for functional benefics and use mantra, worship and charity for malefics. BPHS 84.26 says to worship whichever planet is badly placed at the time.

remedies.remedy: Recite the planet's Vedic mantra beginning 'Akrishnena rajasa...' after worshipping Sun; prescribed count 7,000 repetitions.
remedies.source: BPHS ch. 84 (tr. G.S. Kapoor, Ranjan 1992, vol. 2 of the Santhanam set; = ch. 86 in G.C. Sharma) vv. 17-20; https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl

remedies.remedy: Recite verse 1 of the Navagraha Stotra (to the Sun as bright as the japa (hibiscus) flower, son of Kashyapa, enemy of darkness, remover of sins), or the whole hymn; the closing verses say that whoever recites it with a collected mind, day or night, has obstacles pacified and troubles from planets and stars calmed.
remedies.source: Navagraha Stotra attributed to Vyasa (sanskritdocuments.org text, tr. V. Rao & S. Kalyanaraman), v. 1 and phalashruti; https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/navanew.html

remedies.remedy: Name and seed mantras: name mantra OM SURYAYA NAMAHA (also Savitre, Adityaya, Ravaye); bija OM SUM; RAM also suggested; at least 108 times a week, preferably Sunday at dawn, noon or sunset.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley

remedies.remedy: Read the planet's introductory verse a few times, then repeat its basic mantra about 6,000 times, ideally on its weekday; PVR also suggests the planet's 108 names, kavacha or stotra, recited with devotion and correct pronunciation.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.4; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: Graha puja: make an image of Sun in copper (or draw it on cloth in its colour) and contemplate it as two-armed, seated on a lotus holding a lotus, red like a lotus, on a chariot of seven horses (84.6); offer flowers and cloth of its colour, sandal paste, lamp, incense (guggulu) and the food it likes.
remedies.source: BPHS ch. 84 (tr. G.S. Kapoor, Ranjan 1992, vol. 2 of the Santhanam set; = ch. 86 in G.C. Sharma) vv. 3-16; https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl; same content in G.C. Sharma ch. 86, https://archive.org/details/brihatparasarahorasastrawithenglishtranslationgirishchandsharmavolume2_433_w

remedies.remedy: Homa: offer arka (aak) as the sacrificial fuel for Sun, dipped in honey, ghee, curd or milk, 108 or 28 times.
remedies.source: BPHS ch. 84 (tr. G.S. Kapoor, Ranjan 1992, vol. 2 of the Santhanam set; = ch. 86 in G.C. Sharma) vv. 21-22; https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl

remedies.remedy: Graha-yajna as taught by Yajnavalkya: worship with flowers and items of the planet's colour (red), recite its mantra, and give the prescribed food and gift; recommended for anyone troubled by a hostile planet or wanting peace and prosperity.
remedies.source: Garuda Purana 1.101 'Propitiation of malignant planets' (tr. M.N. Dutt, wisdomlib); https://www.wisdomlib.org/hinduism/book/the-garuda-purana-dutt/d/doc122581.html

remedies.remedy: Worship of the Sun is prescribed for troubled Sun sub-periods in several mahadashas (e.g. Sun in Mars, Rahu, Saturn, Mercury and Venus dashas, chs. 54, 55, 57, 58, 60); recitation of the Aditya Hridaya is prescribed for the Sun sub-period in Jupiter's dasha when the Sun rules the 2nd or 7th (ch. 56 vv. 56-57).
remedies.source: BPHS antardasha chapters 52-60 (Kapoor/Ranjan numbering; verse numbers not recorded unless given); https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl

remedies.remedy: Worship a deity linked to Sun: Shiva, Rama; PVR advises choosing the form that best fits the planet's combinations in the chart.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.5 Table 78; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: Deity: Shiva as the Divine Father; Vishnu as the benefic side of solar light; ruling deity Agni, over-ruler Shiva (ch. 5 table).
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets' and David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 5 'Worship and Meditation on the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley

remedies.remedy: Feed Brahmins rice cooked with jaggery and give a milch cow (with calf) as the gift (dakshina), according to one's means and with respect.
remedies.source: BPHS ch. 84 (tr. G.S. Kapoor, Ranjan 1992, vol. 2 of the Santhanam set; = ch. 86 in G.C. Sharma) vv. 23-25; https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl; the gift list matches Garuda Purana 1.101 'Propitiation of malignant planets' (tr. M.N. Dutt, wisdomlib), https://www.wisdomlib.org/hinduism/book/the-garuda-purana-dutt/d/doc122581.html

remedies.remedy: Do a good deed in Sun's area: go to a temple, donate to a temple or help run one. Give away wheat, the grain ruled by Sun.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.3; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: Place a small bowl of wheat on the altar to represent Sun in worship; Frawley adds these are good foods when the planet is weak.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 5 'Worship and Meditation on the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley

remedies.remedy: Fasting on the weekday of the relevant planet (Sunday for Sun). PVR's own examples tie the day to the planet that rules the troubled area (e.g. the upapada lord's day for marriage), not to a fixed list.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.3 (fasting); weekday attribution from 34.2/34.4 and Komilla Sutton, 'Astrology and Gemmology' (Skyscript, 2005; from Astrology and Medicine Newsletter 40, 2004); https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: Conduct and lifestyle: cultivate independence and courage, face fears, take initiative and leadership, spend time in the sun, rise early and greet the Sun with a prayer at dawn, noon and sunset.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley

remedies.remedy: Planets are always favourable to one who harms no one, keeps self-control, earns wealth by righteous means and keeps a steady religious discipline; when a planet is adverse in dasha, bhukti, ashtakavarga or transit, pacify it with prayers and mantras suited to it, virtuous acts, vows, gifts and worship.
remedies.source: Phaladeepika (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed. 1950) ch. 26 vv. 49-50; https://archive.org/details/Phaladeepika2ndEd.1950ByVSubrahmanyaSastri

remedies.remedy: Common-sense precautions in a difficult period (e.g. drive carefully if accidents are indicated, restrain oneself if conflict with authority is indicated); good deeds in the planet's area of life.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.1.1 and 34.3; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. Gem traditionally assigned to Sun: ruby (substitutes: garnet (larger size)). Frawley: ruby (min. ~2 carats) in gold, ring finger of the right hand, first worn on a Sunday at sunrise when the Sun is strong. Avoid when the Sun rules malefic houses (3rd, 6th, 11th), when it combusts or opposes benefics one wants to strengthen, or with high-Pitta conditions or a domineering, proud temperament.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley; gem list also David Frawley, Ayurvedic Astrology, ch. 9 'Vedic Gem Therapy', https://archive.org/details/david-frawley-ayurvedic-astrology-self-healing-through-the-stars_202305

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. PVR: wear the gem only if Sun is a functional benefic in the chart (useful even if that benefic is weak or badly placed); avoid gems of functional malefics, and of marakas during maraka periods; first wear it on the planet's weekday when the planet is strong.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.2 and Table 77; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. Sutton: prefer the gems of strong planets (especially the lagna lord and trine lords) over weak ones; gems help only alongside a real change of attitude; wearing the planet's colour, its oils or seeds can stand in for an unaffordable gem.
remedies.source: Komilla Sutton, 'Astrology and Gemmology' (Skyscript, 2005; from Astrology and Medicine Newsletter 40, 2004); https://skyscript.co.uk/gems.html

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. Phaladeepika lists ruby as Sun's gem among the planets' correspondences; the verse assigns gems but does not prescribe wearing them as a remedy.
remedies.source: Phaladeepika (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed. 1950) ch. 2 v. 29; https://archive.org/details/Phaladeepika2ndEd.1950ByVSubrahmanyaSastri

source_views.source: BPHS ch. 84 (tr. G.S. Kapoor, Ranjan 1992, vol. 2 of the Santhanam set; = ch. 86 in G.C. Sharma)
source_views.view: Joys and sorrows depend on the planets, so those wanting peace, wealth, health or long life should worship them; whichever planet is badly placed at a given time should be worshipped with special care, because Brahma granted the planets the boon of honouring those who honour them (vv. 2-3, 26-27). For Sun: image in copper, mantra 'Akrishnena rajasa...' x 7,000, fuel arka (aak), food rice cooked with jaggery, gift a milch cow (with calf).

source_views.view: Remedy is indicated whenever a planet is badly placed in dasha, bhukti, ashtakavarga or transit; the means are prayer and planet-specific mantra, propitiatory rites, virtuous acts, vows, gifts and worship. Non-harming, self-control, honestly earned wealth and discipline keep the planets favourable.

source_views.view: Verse 1 praises the Sun as bright as the japa (hibiscus) flower, son of Kashyapa, enemy of darkness, remover of sins; the closing verses promise pacification of obstacles, bad dreams and planet-caused troubles.

source_views.view: Yajnavalkya's graha-yajna: anyone under a hostile planet, or wanting prosperity and peace, should perform it; colour for Sun red; gifts follow the same order as BPHS.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures'
source_views.view: Remedies adjust the details of a karmic pattern, not the pattern; four ways to please a planet: gem (only for functional benefics), good deeds, mantra/stotra, deity worship. For Sun: deed - go to a temple, donate to a temple or help run one; deity - Shiva, Rama; mantra count ~6,000.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'
source_views.view: Strengthen a planet chiefly when it is weak, and be careful strengthening natural malefics; mantra and meditation are safer than gems or herbs, and are used to ward off an over-strong malefic. Signs of a weak Sun: Frawley: debilitated (Libra), in an enemy sign such as Saturn's, in the 6th/8th/12th, or under Saturn, Rahu or Ketu (Ketu's close conjunction especially). Shows as low self-worth, weak will, dependence; the father may fare poorly.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Ayurvedic Astrology, ch. 9 'Vedic Gem Therapy'
source_views.view: Gems are called the main remedial measure in Vedic astrology, but wrongly prescribed gems can cause imbalances; two schools exist (strengthen weak benefics - the 'safe school' Frawley follows - versus propitiate the troublesome malefic), and Frawley advises against wearing malefics' gems unless backed by serious mantra and meditation practice.

source_views.source: Komilla Sutton, 'Astrology and Gemmology' (Skyscript, 2005; from Astrology and Medicine Newsletter 40, 2004)
source_views.view: Wear gems of strong, not weak, planets; criticises wearing many gems as a shortcut and astrologers who profit by selling costly stones; gems work only with a change of attitude; node gems best avoided.

remedy/sun.disagreements: Mantra counts: BPHS 84.19-20 gives 7,000 for Sun; PVR gives about 6,000 (his counts follow a different scheme). Mantra type: the classical texts read here prescribe Vedic verses and hymns; the short bija and name mantras come from modern authors (Frawley, PVR), and their classical mantra-text source (e.g. Mantra Maharnava) was not verified. Gemstones: the graha-shanti chapters read (BPHS ch. 84, Garuda Purana 1.101) prescribe worship, japa, homa, feeding and gifts, not wearing a planet's gem (Garuda mentions wearing metals); Phaladeepika 2.29 only lists the gems as correspondences. Among moderns: PVR and Frawley's 'safe school' give gems only for functional benefics (even weak ones) and avoid gems of functional malefics; a second school Frawley reports gives the gem of the troublesome malefic itself; Sutton prefers gems of strong planets over weak ones. Frawley and Sutton warn about side effects (blue sapphire, cat's eye, ruby, node gems) and Sutton criticises commercial gem-selling. Translation: in BPHS ch. 84 the Kapoor translation differs from the Sanskrit on some details (e.g. Rahu's image metal lead vs glass, the vehicles of Saturn and Ketu, Mars's count 10,000 vs 11,000).
remedy/sun.phrasing_guidance: Offer these as optional devotional or lifestyle practices, never as a requirement or a fix. Do not frame the planet as something to fear. Do not promise that any remedy will change events, health or money. Mention gemstones only as an optional tradition that sources disagree on, recommend consulting a qualified, independent astrologer before buying one, and never tie a reading to a purchase. Prefer free practices first: prayer or mantra on the planet's day, simple charity, and the conduct changes. Classical gifts of animals (cows, bulls, goats, horses) can be described as the tradition's form of charity; a modern reader can give in kind or to a cause instead. No medical claims: herbs or gems are not treatment.

remedy/moon.summary: Remedies for Moon are indicated when it is weak, afflicted or badly placed, and especially while it runs a hard dasha or antardasha or an adverse transit (Phaladeepika 26.49; BPHS 84.26). The classical means are worship, its mantra, homa, feeding and gifts; modern authors add bija mantras, conduct and lifestyle changes, and optional gemstones only when Moon is functionally helpful in the chart.
common_outcomes: Classical texts present planetary worship as bringing peace, prosperity, health and long life (BPHS 84.2-3).
Navagraha Stotra phalashruti: obstacles pacified, bad dreams removed, troubles from planets and stars calmed.
PVR: remedies change the details of a period, not its basic pattern.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: waning (especially near new Moon), debilitated (Scorpio), aspected by Saturn, Rahu, Ketu or Mars (Rahu and Saturn worst unless Jupiter helps), or in the 6th/8th/12th. Shows as emotional instability, anxiety, moodiness; the mother may suffer.
remedy/moon.lagna_or_context_notes: Which remedy fits depends on the planet's functional role from the lagna: modern authors (PVR 34.2; Frawley, Astrology of the Seers Part III ch. 4 and Ayurvedic Astrology ch. 9) reserve gems for functional benefics and use mantra, worship and charity for malefics. BPHS 84.26 says to worship whichever planet is badly placed at the time.

remedies.remedy: Recite the planet's Vedic mantra beginning 'Imam deva asapatnam...' after worshipping Moon; prescribed count 11,000 repetitions.

remedies.remedy: Recite verse 2 of the Navagraha Stotra (to the Moon, white as curd, conch and frost, born from the ocean of milk, ornament on Shiva's crown), or the whole hymn; the closing verses say that whoever recites it with a collected mind, day or night, has obstacles pacified and troubles from planets and stars calmed.
remedies.source: Navagraha Stotra attributed to Vyasa (sanskritdocuments.org text, tr. V. Rao & S. Kalyanaraman), v. 2 and phalashruti; https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/navanew.html

remedies.remedy: Name and seed mantras: name mantras OM SOMAYA NAMAHA / OM CHANDRAYA NAMAHA; bija SOM, also CHAM and SHRIM; on Mondays, in the evening, especially near the full Moon.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley

remedies.remedy: Read the planet's introductory verse a few times, then repeat its basic mantra about 10,000 times, ideally on its weekday; PVR also suggests the planet's 108 names, kavacha or stotra, recited with devotion and correct pronunciation.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.4; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: Graha puja: make an image of Moon in crystal (sphatika) (or draw it on cloth in its colour) and contemplate it as white, in white garments and white ornaments, two arms (mace and boon-giving gesture), on a chariot of ten horses (84.7); offer flowers and cloth of its colour, sandal paste, lamp, incense (guggulu) and the food it likes.
remedies.source: BPHS ch. 84 (tr. G.S. Kapoor, Ranjan 1992, vol. 2 of the Santhanam set; = ch. 86 in G.C. Sharma) vv. 3-16; https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl; same content in G.C. Sharma ch. 86, https://archive.org/details/brihatparasarahorasastrawithenglishtranslationgirishchandsharmavolume2_433_w

remedies.remedy: Homa: offer palasha as the sacrificial fuel for Moon, dipped in honey, ghee, curd or milk, 108 or 28 times.
remedies.source: BPHS ch. 84 (tr. G.S. Kapoor, Ranjan 1992, vol. 2 of the Santhanam set; = ch. 86 in G.C. Sharma) vv. 21-22; https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl

remedies.remedy: Graha-yajna as taught by Yajnavalkya: worship with flowers and items of the planet's colour (white), recite its mantra, and give the prescribed food and gift; recommended for anyone troubled by a hostile planet or wanting peace and prosperity.
remedies.source: Garuda Purana 1.101 'Propitiation of malignant planets' (tr. M.N. Dutt, wisdomlib); https://www.wisdomlib.org/hinduism/book/the-garuda-purana-dutt/d/doc122581.html

remedies.remedy: Gift of a white cow and/or a female buffalo is prescribed for troubled Moon sub-periods (e.g. Moon in the Sun's dasha, ch. 52; Moon in Rahu's dasha, ch. 55); Durga Saptashati recitation for the Moon sub-period in Jupiter's dasha (ch. 56).
remedies.source: BPHS antardasha chapters 52-60 (Kapoor/Ranjan numbering; verse numbers not recorded unless given); https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl

remedies.remedy: Worship a deity linked to Moon: Gauri, Lalita, Saraswati, Krishna; PVR advises choosing the form that best fits the planet's combinations in the chart.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.5 Table 78; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: Deity: the Divine Mother (Parvati, Lakshmi, Tara and other forms), meditated in the full Moon; ruling deity Apas (waters), over-ruler Parvati (ch. 5 table).
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets' and David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 5 'Worship and Meditation on the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley

remedies.remedy: Feed Brahmins rice cooked in milk (payasa) and give a conch as the gift (dakshina), according to one's means and with respect.
remedies.source: BPHS ch. 84 (tr. G.S. Kapoor, Ranjan 1992, vol. 2 of the Santhanam set; = ch. 86 in G.C. Sharma) vv. 23-25; https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl; the gift list matches Garuda Purana 1.101 'Propitiation of malignant planets' (tr. remedies.remedy: Do a good deed in Moon's area: donate to a music institution or help a woman in need ('a fair lady' in the text). Give away rice, the grain ruled by Moon.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.3; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: Place a small bowl of white rice on the altar to represent Moon in worship; Frawley adds these are good foods when the planet is weak.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 5 'Worship and Meditation on the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley

remedies.remedy: Fasting on the weekday of the relevant planet (Monday for Moon). PVR's own examples tie the day to the planet that rules the troubled area (e.g. the upapada lord's day for marriage), not to a fixed list.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.3 (fasting); weekday attribution from 34.2/34.4 and Komilla Sutton, 'Astrology and Gemmology' (Skyscript, 2005; from Astrology and Medicine Newsletter 40, 2004); https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: Conduct and lifestyle: seek an atmosphere of peace, faith and caring; do service work; stay in a supportive family or community and nurture others; devotional (bhakti) practice.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley

remedies.remedy: Planets are always favourable to one who harms no one, keeps self-control, earns wealth by righteous means and keeps a steady religious discipline; when a planet is adverse in dasha, bhukti, ashtakavarga or transit, pacify it with prayers and mantras suited to it, virtuous acts, vows, gifts and worship.

remedies.remedy: Common-sense precautions in a difficult period (e.g. drive carefully if accidents are indicated, restrain oneself if conflict with authority is indicated); good deeds in the planet's area of life.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.1.1 and 34.3; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. Gem traditionally assigned to Moon: pearl (substitutes: cultured pearl or moonstone (larger size)). Frawley: natural pearl (min. ~2 carats) in silver, ring finger, first worn on a Monday in the waxing Moon. Avoid when the Moon rules malefic houses (e.g. for Taurus, Sagittarius, Aquarius lagnas), or with Kapha excess (congestion, overweight) or strong emotional attachment.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley; gem list also David Frawley, Ayurvedic Astrology, ch. 9 'Vedic Gem Therapy', https://archive.org/details/david-frawley-ayurvedic-astrology-self-healing-through-the-stars_202305

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. Sutton: prefer the gems of strong planets (especially the lagna lord and trine lords) over weak ones; gems help only alongside a real change of attitude; wearing the planet's colour, its oils or seeds can stand in for an unaffordable gem.

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. Phaladeepika lists pearl as Moon's gem among the planets' correspondences; the verse assigns gems but does not prescribe wearing them as a remedy.

source_views.view: Joys and sorrows depend on the planets, so those wanting peace, wealth, health or long life should worship them; whichever planet is badly placed at a given time should be worshipped with special care, because Brahma granted the planets the boon of honouring those who honour them (vv. 2-3, 26-27). For Mars: image in red sandalwood, mantra 'Agnir murdha divah kakut...' x 10,000 by the Sanskrit numeral word ('disho' = 10); the Kapoor table prints 11,000, fuel khadira (khair), food havishya (simple sacrificial rice), gift a bull/ox.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures'
source_views.view: Remedies adjust the details of a karmic pattern, not the pattern; four ways to please a planet: gem (only for functional benefics), good deeds, mantra/stotra, deity worship. For Mars: deed - take up physical exercise or donate to a school gym; deity - Hanuman, Rudra, Kartikeya (Subrahmanya), Narasimha; mantra count ~7,000.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'
source_views.view: Strengthen a planet chiefly when it is weak, and be careful strengthening natural malefics; mantra and meditation are safer than gems or herbs, and are used to ward off an over-strong malefic. Signs of a weak Mars: Frawley: debilitated (Cancer), aspected by Saturn or Rahu, combust, or in the 5th, 8th, 9th or 12th. Shows as low energy and motivation, difficulty standing up for oneself.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Ayurvedic Astrology, ch. 9 'Vedic Gem Therapy'
source_views.view: Gems are called the main remedial measure in Vedic astrology, but wrongly prescribed gems can cause imbalances; two schools exist (strengthen weak benefics - the 'safe school' Frawley follows - versus propitiate the troublesome malefic), and Frawley advises against wearing malefics' gems unless backed by serious mantra and meditation practice.

source_views.source: Komilla Sutton, 'Astrology and Gemmology' (Skyscript, 2005; from Astrology and Medicine Newsletter 40, 2004)
source_views.view: Wear gems of strong, not weak, planets; criticises wearing many gems as a shortcut and astrologers who profit by selling costly stones; gems work only with a change of attitude; node gems best avoided.

source_views.view: Ancient texts suggest mantra-based remedies for afflictions (arishta yogas) shown in the chart (ch. XI); karma and free will coexist, so astrology should not be used fatalistically (ch. VIII). Raman gives no planet-by-planet list here.

remedy/mars.disagreements: Mantra counts: BPHS 84.19-20 gives 10,000 by the Sanskrit numeral word ('disho' = 10); the Kapoor table prints 11,000 for Mars; PVR gives about 7,000 (his counts follow a different scheme). Mantra type: the classical texts read here prescribe Vedic verses and hymns; the short bija and name mantras come from modern authors (Frawley, PVR), and their classical mantra-text source (e.g. Mantra Maharnava) was not verified. Gemstones: the graha-shanti chapters read (BPHS ch. 84, Garuda Purana 1.101) prescribe worship, japa, homa, feeding and gifts, not wearing a planet's gem (Garuda mentions wearing metals); Phaladeepika 2.29 only lists the gems as correspondences. Among moderns: PVR and Frawley's 'safe school' give gems only for functional benefics (even weak ones) and avoid gems of functional malefics; a second school Frawley reports gives the gem of the troublesome malefic itself; Sutton prefers gems of strong planets over weak ones. Frawley and Sutton warn about side effects (blue sapphire, cat's eye, ruby, node gems) and Sutton criticises commercial gem-selling. Translation: in BPHS ch. 84 the Kapoor translation differs from the Sanskrit on some details (e.g. Rahu's image metal lead vs glass, the vehicles of Saturn and Ketu, Mars's count 10,000 vs 11,000).
remedy/mars.phrasing_guidance: Offer these as optional devotional or lifestyle practices, never as a requirement or a fix. Do not frame the planet as something to fear. Do not promise that any remedy will change events, health or money. Mention gemstones only as an optional tradition that sources disagree on, recommend consulting a qualified, independent astrologer before buying one, and never tie a reading to a purchase. Prefer free practices first: prayer or mantra on the planet's day, simple charity, and the conduct changes. Classical gifts of animals (cows, bulls, goats, horses) can be described as the tradition's form of charity; a modern reader can give in kind or to a cause instead. No medical claims: herbs or gems are not treatment.

remedy/mercury.summary: Remedies for Mercury are indicated when it is weak, afflicted or badly placed, and especially while it runs a hard dasha or antardasha or an adverse transit (Phaladeepika 26.49; BPHS 84.26). The classical means are worship, its mantra, homa, feeding and gifts; modern authors add bija mantras, conduct and lifestyle changes, and optional gemstones only when Mercury is functionally helpful in the chart.
common_outcomes: Classical texts present planetary worship as bringing peace, prosperity, health and long life (BPHS 84.2-3).
Navagraha Stotra phalashruti: obstacles pacified, bad dreams removed, troubles from planets and stars calmed.
PVR: remedies change the details of a period, not its basic pattern.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: aspected by malefics (Saturn, Rahu, Ketu, Sun, Mars), debilitated (Pisces), or in the 6th/8th/12th. Shows as poor communication, weak memory, nervousness.
remedy/mercury.lagna_or_context_notes: Which remedy fits depends on the planet's functional role from the lagna: modern authors (PVR 34.2; Frawley, Astrology of the Seers Part III ch. 4 and Ayurvedic Astrology ch. 9) reserve gems for functional benefics and use mantra, worship and charity for malefics. BPHS 84.26 says to worship whichever planet is badly placed at the time.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'
source_views.view: Strengthen a planet chiefly when it is weak, and be careful strengthening natural malefics; mantra and meditation are safer than gems or herbs, and are used to ward off an over-strong malefic. Signs of a weak Mercury: Frawley: aspected by malefics (Saturn, Rahu, Ketu, Sun, Mars), debilitated (Pisces), or in the 6th/8th/12th. Shows as poor communication, weak memory, nervousness.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Ayurvedic Astrology, ch. 9 'Vedic Gem Therapy'
source_views.view: Gems are called the main remedial measure in Vedic astrology, but wrongly prescribed gems can cause imbalances; two schools exist (strengthen weak benefics - the 'safe school' Frawley follows - versus propitiate the troublesome malefic), and Frawley advises against wearing malefics' gems unless backed by serious mantra and meditation practice.

source_views.source: Komilla Sutton, 'Astrology and Gemmology' (Skyscript, 2005; from Astrology and Medicine Newsletter 40, 2004)
source_views.view: Wear gems of strong, not weak, planets; criticises wearing many gems as a shortcut and astrologers who profit by selling costly stones; gems work only with a change of attitude; node gems best avoided.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Planetary Influences on Human Affairs, ch. XI 'Astrology as an Aid to Medical Science' and ch. VIII
source_views.view: Ancient texts suggest mantra-based remedies for afflictions (arishta yogas) shown in the chart (ch. XI); karma and free will coexist, so astrology should not be used fatalistically (ch. VIII). Raman gives no planet-by-planet list here.

remedy/mercury.disagreements: Mantra counts: BPHS 84.19-20 gives 9,000 for Mercury; PVR gives about 17,000 (his counts follow a different scheme). Mantra type: the classical texts read here prescribe Vedic verses and hymns; the short bija and name mantras come from modern authors (Frawley, PVR), and their classical mantra-text source (e.g. Mantra Maharnava) was not verified. Gemstones: the graha-shanti chapters read (BPHS ch. 84, Garuda Purana 1.101) prescribe worship, japa, homa, feeding and gifts, not wearing a planet's gem (Garuda mentions wearing metals); Phaladeepika 2.29 only lists the gems as correspondences. Among moderns: PVR and Frawley's 'safe school' give gems only for functional benefics (even weak ones) and avoid gems of functional malefics; a second school Frawley reports gives the gem of the troublesome malefic itself; Sutton prefers gems of strong planets over weak ones. Frawley and Sutton warn about side effects (blue sapphire, cat's eye, ruby, node gems) and Sutton criticises commercial gem-selling. Translation: in BPHS ch. 84 the Kapoor translation differs from the Sanskrit on some details (e.g. Rahu's image metal lead vs glass, the vehicles of Saturn and Ketu, Mars's count 10,000 vs 11,000).
remedy/mercury.phrasing_guidance: Offer these as optional devotional or lifestyle practices, never as a requirement or a fix. Do not frame the planet as something to fear. Do not promise that any remedy will change events, health or money. Mention gemstones only as an optional tradition that sources disagree on, recommend consulting a qualified, independent astrologer before buying one, and never tie a reading to a purchase. Prefer free practices first: prayer or mantra on the planet's day, simple charity, and the conduct changes. Classical gifts of animals (cows, bulls, goats, horses) can be described as the tradition's form of charity; a modern reader can give in kind or to a cause instead. No medical claims: herbs or gems are not treatment.

remedy/jupiter.summary: Remedies for Jupiter are indicated when it is weak, afflicted or badly placed, and especially while it runs a hard dasha or antardasha or an adverse transit (Phaladeepika 26.49; BPHS 84.26). The classical means are worship, its mantra, homa, feeding and gifts; modern authors add bija mantras, conduct and lifestyle changes, and optional gemstones only when Jupiter is functionally helpful in the chart.
common_outcomes: Classical texts present planetary worship as bringing peace, prosperity, health and long life (BPHS 84.2-3).
Navagraha Stotra phalashruti: obstacles pacified, bad dreams removed, troubles from planets and stars calmed.
PVR: remedies change the details of a period, not its basic pattern.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: debilitated (Capricorn), aspected by Saturn, Rahu, Ketu or Mars, or in the 6th/8th/12th. Shows as low faith and joy, pessimism, money troubles; children (or a woman's husband) may suffer.
remedy/jupiter.lagna_or_context_notes: Which remedy fits depends on the planet's functional role from the lagna: modern authors (PVR 34.2; Frawley, Astrology of the Seers Part III ch. 4 and Ayurvedic Astrology ch. 9) reserve gems for functional benefics and use mantra, worship and charity for malefics. BPHS 84.26 says to worship whichever planet is badly placed at the time.

remedies.remedy: Recite the planet's Vedic mantra beginning 'Brihaspate ati yad aryo...' after worshipping Jupiter; prescribed count 19,000 repetitions.

remedies.remedy: Recite verse 5 of the Navagraha Stotra (to Jupiter, teacher of gods and sages, golden in hue, wisdom itself, lord of the three worlds), or the whole hymn; the closing verses say that whoever recites it with a collected mind, day or night, has obstacles pacified and troubles from planets and stars calmed.
remedies.source: Navagraha Stotra attributed to Vyasa (sanskritdocuments.org text, tr. V. Rao & S. Kalyanaraman), v. 5 and phalashruti; https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/navanew.html

remedies.remedy: Name and seed mantras: name mantra OM BRIHASPATAYE NAMAHA; bija OM BRAHM; also SHRIM, OM, and Ganesha's OM GAM GANESHAYA NAMAHA.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley

remedies.remedy: Read the planet's introductory verse a few times, then repeat its basic mantra about 16,000 times, ideally on its weekday; PVR also suggests the planet's 108 names, kavacha or stotra, recited with devotion and correct pronunciation.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.4; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: Graha puja: make an image of Jupiter in gold (or draw it on cloth in its colour) and contemplate it as yellow complexion, four arms holding staff, rosary and water-pot with a boon-giving hand (84.10); offer flowers and cloth of its colour, sandal paste, lamp, incense (guggulu) and the food it likes.
remedies.source: BPHS ch. 84 (tr. G.S. Kapoor, Ranjan 1992, vol. 2 of the Santhanam set; = ch. 86 in G.C. Sharma) vv. 3-16; https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl; same content in G.C. Sharma ch. 86, https://archive.org/details/brihatparasarahorasastrawithenglishtranslationgirishchandsharmavolume2_433_w

remedies.remedy: Homa: offer pippala (peepal) as the sacrificial fuel for Jupiter, dipped in honey, ghee, curd or milk, 108 or 28 times.
remedies.source: BPHS ch. 84 (tr. G.S. Kapoor, Ranjan 1992, vol. 2 of the Santhanam set; = ch. 86 in G.C. Sharma) vv. 21-22; https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl

remedies.remedy: Graha-yajna as taught by Yajnavalkya: worship with flowers and items of the planet's colour (yellowish), recite its mantra, and give the prescribed food and gift; recommended for anyone troubled by a hostile planet or wanting peace and prosperity.
remedies.source: Garuda Purana 1.101 'Propitiation of malignant planets' (tr. M.N. Dutt, wisdomlib); https://www.wisdomlib.org/hinduism/book/the-garuda-purana-dutt/d/doc122581.html

remedies.remedy: Shiva Sahasranama and/or Rudra japa are prescribed for troubled Jupiter sub-periods (e.g. Jupiter in the dashas of Mars, Jupiter, Saturn and Mercury; chs. 54, 56-58), with a gift of gold in Saturn's dasha (ch. 57); Mrityunjaya japa for Jupiter in the dashas of Ketu and Venus (chs. 59-60); worship of the ishta devata for Jupiter in the Sun's dasha (ch. 52).
remedies.source: BPHS antardasha chapters 52-60 (Kapoor/Ranjan numbering; verse numbers not recorded unless given); https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl

remedies.remedy: Worship a deity linked to Jupiter: Hayagriva, Vishnu, Parameshvara, Dattatreya, any guru; PVR advises choosing the form that best fits the planet's combinations in the chart.

remedies.remedy: Deity: Brihaspati; Ganesha; ruling deity Indra, over-ruler Brahma (ch. 5 table).

remedies.remedy: Feed Brahmins curd with rice and give cloth/garments as the gift (dakshina), according to one's means and with respect.
remedies.source: BPHS ch. 84 (tr. G.S. Kapoor, Ranjan 1992, vol. 2 of the Santhanam set; = ch. 86 in G.C. Sharma) vv. 23-25; https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl; the gift list matches Garuda Purana 1.101 'Propitiation of malignant planets' (tr. remedies.remedy: Do a good deed in Jupiter's area: respect and donate to a learned Brahmin or priest, or donate cows to a priest. Give away chickpeas (e.g. a bowl given away on a Thursday morning), the grain ruled by Jupiter.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.3; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: Place a small bowl of chickpeas on the altar to represent Jupiter in worship; Frawley adds these are good foods when the planet is weak.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 5 'Worship and Meditation on the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley

remedies.remedy: Fasting on the weekday of the relevant planet (Thursday for Jupiter). PVR's own examples tie the day to the planet that rules the troubled area (e.g. the upapada lord's day for marriage), not to a fixed list.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.3 (fasting); weekday attribution from 34.2/34.4 and Komilla Sutton, 'Astrology and Gemmology' (Skyscript, 2005; from Astrology and Medicine Newsletter 40, 2004); https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: Conduct and lifestyle: cultivate optimism and faith, live by principle, perform rituals and good deeds, be friendly and sociable, align with the forces of good.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley

remedies.remedy: Planets are always favourable to one who harms no one, keeps self-control, earns wealth by righteous means and keeps a steady religious discipline; when a planet is adverse in dasha, bhukti, ashtakavarga or transit, pacify it with prayers and mantras suited to it, virtuous acts, vows, gifts and worship.

remedies.remedy: Common-sense precautions in a difficult period (e.g. drive carefully if accidents are indicated, restrain oneself if conflict with authority is indicated); good deeds in the planet's area of life.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.1.1 and 34.3; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. Gem traditionally assigned to Jupiter: yellow sapphire (substitutes: yellow topaz, citrine, yellow zircon). Frawley: yellow sapphire (min. ~2 carats) in gold, index finger of the right hand, first worn on a Thursday in the waxing Moon. Among the safest gems; avoid when Jupiter rules malefic houses (Taurus, Libra lagnas) unless exalted or in its own sign.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley; gem list also David Frawley, Ayurvedic Astrology, ch. 9 'Vedic Gem Therapy', https://archive.org/details/david-frawley-ayurvedic-astrology-self-healing-through-the-stars_202305

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. Sutton: prefer the gems of strong planets (especially the lagna lord and trine lords) over weak ones; gems help only alongside a real change of attitude; wearing the planet's colour, its oils or seeds can stand in for an unaffordable gem.

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. Phaladeepika lists topaz (Jupiter) as Jupiter's gem among the planets' correspondences; the verse assigns gems but does not prescribe wearing them as a remedy.

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. Gem traditionally assigned to Venus: diamond (substitutes: white sapphire, clear zircon, quartz crystal). Frawley: diamond (min. ~1 carat) in gold or white gold, middle finger, first worn on a Friday in the waxing Moon, with Venus not close to the Sun. Avoid when Venus rules malefic houses (Sagittarius, Pisces lagnas), when Venus is strongly sensual (fixed signs, Mars aspect, 5th/7th/12th), or when the person already has a strong drive for pleasure and luxury.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley; gem list also David Frawley, Ayurvedic Astrology, ch. 9 'Vedic Gem Therapy', https://archive.org/details/david-frawley-ayurvedic-astrology-self-healing-through-the-stars_202305

source_views.source: BPHS ch. 84 (tr. G.S. Kapoor, Ranjan 1992, vol. 2 of the Santhanam set; = ch. 86 in G.C. Sharma)
source_views.view: Joys and sorrows depend on the planets, so those wanting peace, wealth, health or long life should worship them; whichever planet is badly placed at a given time should be worshipped with special care, because Brahma granted the planets the boon of honouring those who honour them (vv. 2-3, 26-27). For Venus: image in silver, mantra 'Annat parisruto rasam...' x 16,000, fuel udumbara (goolar), food rice with ghee, gift a horse.

source_views.source: BPHS antardasha chapters 52-60 (Kapoor/Ranjan numbering; verse numbers not recorded unless given)
source_views.view: Worship of Durga and Lakshmi, often with a gift of a (tawny) cow or female buffalo, is prescribed for troubled Venus sub-periods (e.g. Venus in the dashas of Rahu, Saturn, Mercury, Ketu and Venus; chs. 55, 57-60); Rudra japa with a gift for Venus in the Moon's dasha (ch. 53); Mrityunjaya and Rudra japa with a tawny cow or female buffalo when Venus rules the 6th or 8th in the Sun's dasha (ch. 52).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed. 1950) ch. 26 vv. 49-50
source_views.view: Remedy is indicated whenever a planet is badly placed in dasha, bhukti, ashtakavarga or transit; the means are prayer and planet-specific mantra, propitiatory rites, virtuous acts, vows, gifts and worship. Non-harming, self-control, honestly earned wealth and discipline keep the planets favourable.

source_views.source: Navagraha Stotra attributed to Vyasa (sanskritdocuments.org text, tr. V. Rao & S. Kalyanaraman)
source_views.view: Verse 6 praises Venus, white as snow, jasmine and lotus fibre, supreme teacher of the daityas, expounder of all shastras; the closing verses promise pacification of obstacles, bad dreams and planet-caused troubles.

source_views.source: Garuda Purana 1.101 'Propitiation of malignant planets' (tr. M.N. Dutt, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Yajnavalkya's graha-yajna: anyone under a hostile planet, or wanting prosperity and peace, should perform it; colour for Venus white; gifts follow the same order as BPHS.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures'
source_views.view: Remedies adjust the details of a karmic pattern, not the pattern; four ways to please a planet: gem (only for functional benefics), good deeds, mantra/stotra, deity worship. For Venus: deed - read poetry or help a poet; deity - Lakshmi, Parvati; mantra count ~20,000.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'
source_views.view: Strengthen a planet chiefly when it is weak, and be careful strengthening natural malefics; mantra and meditation are safer than gems or herbs, and are used to ward off an over-strong malefic. Signs of a weak Venus: Frawley: debilitated (Virgo), aspected by malefics (Sun, Mars, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu), or in the 6th/8th. Shows as difficulty with affection and romance; for men, the wife may suffer.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Ayurvedic Astrology, ch. 9 'Vedic Gem Therapy'
source_views.view: Gems are called the main remedial measure in Vedic astrology, but wrongly prescribed gems can cause imbalances; two schools exist (strengthen weak benefics - the 'safe school' Frawley follows - versus propitiate the troublesome malefic), and Frawley advises against wearing malefics' gems unless backed by serious mantra and meditation practice.

source_views.source: Komilla Sutton, 'Astrology and Gemmology' (Skyscript, 2005; from Astrology and Medicine Newsletter 40, 2004)
source_views.view: Wear gems of strong, not weak, planets; criticises wearing many gems as a shortcut and astrologers who profit by selling costly stones; gems work only with a change of attitude; node gems best avoided.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Planetary Influences on Human Affairs, ch. XI 'Astrology as an Aid to Medical Science' and ch. VIII
source_views.view: Ancient texts suggest mantra-based remedies for afflictions (arishta yogas) shown in the chart (ch. XI); karma and free will coexist, so astrology should not be used fatalistically (ch. VIII). Raman gives no planet-by-planet list here.

remedy/venus.disagreements: Mantra counts: BPHS 84.19-20 gives 16,000 for Venus; PVR gives about 20,000 (his counts follow a different scheme). Mantra type: the classical texts read here prescribe Vedic verses and hymns; the short bija and name mantras come from modern authors (Frawley, PVR), and their classical mantra-text source (e.g. Mantra Maharnava) was not verified. Gemstones: the graha-shanti chapters read (BPHS ch. 84, Garuda Purana 1.101) prescribe worship, japa, homa, feeding and gifts, not wearing a planet's gem (Garuda mentions wearing metals); Phaladeepika 2.29 only lists the gems as correspondences. Among moderns: PVR and Frawley's 'safe school' give gems only for functional benefics (even weak ones) and avoid gems of functional malefics; a second school Frawley reports gives the gem of the troublesome malefic itself; Sutton prefers gems of strong planets over weak ones. Frawley and Sutton warn about side effects (blue sapphire, cat's eye, ruby, node gems) and Sutton criticises commercial gem-selling. Translation: in BPHS ch. 84 the Kapoor translation differs from the Sanskrit on some details (e.g. Rahu's image metal lead vs glass, the vehicles of Saturn and Ketu, Mars's count 10,000 vs 11,000).
remedy/venus.phrasing_guidance: Offer these as optional devotional or lifestyle practices, never as a requirement or a fix. Do not frame the planet as something to fear. Do not promise that any remedy will change events, health or money. Mention gemstones only as an optional tradition that sources disagree on, recommend consulting a qualified, independent astrologer before buying one, and never tie a reading to a purchase. Prefer free practices first: prayer or mantra on the planet's day, simple charity, and the conduct changes. Classical gifts of animals (cows, bulls, goats, horses) can be described as the tradition's form of charity; a modern reader can give in kind or to a cause instead. No medical claims: herbs or gems are not treatment.

remedy/saturn.summary: Remedies for Saturn are indicated when it is weak, afflicted or badly placed, and especially while it runs a hard dasha or antardasha or an adverse transit (Phaladeepika 26.49; BPHS 84.26). The classical means are worship, its mantra, homa, feeding and gifts; modern authors add bija mantras, conduct and lifestyle changes, and optional gemstones only when Saturn is functionally helpful in the chart.
common_outcomes: Classical texts present planetary worship as bringing peace, prosperity, health and long life (BPHS 84.2-3).
Navagraha Stotra phalashruti: obstacles pacified, bad dreams removed, troubles from planets and stars calmed.
PVR: remedies change the details of a period, not its basic pattern.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: debilitated (Aries), aspected by Sun, Mars, Rahu or Ketu, or in the 5th, 6th, 8th or 12th. Shows as agitation, poor endurance, trouble with institutions and money.
remedy/saturn.lagna_or_context_notes: Which remedy fits depends on the planet's functional role from the lagna: modern authors (PVR 34.2; Frawley, Astrology of the Seers Part III ch. 4 and Ayurvedic Astrology ch. 9) reserve gems for functional benefics and use mantra, worship and charity for malefics. BPHS 84.26 says to worship whichever planet is badly placed at the time.
