source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'
source_views.view: Strengthen a planet chiefly when it is weak, and be careful strengthening natural malefics; mantra and meditation are safer than gems or herbs, and are used to ward off an over-strong malefic. Signs of a weak Saturn: Frawley: debilitated (Aries), aspected by Sun, Mars, Rahu or Ketu, or in the 5th, 6th, 8th or 12th. Shows as agitation, poor endurance, trouble with institutions and money.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Ayurvedic Astrology, ch. 9 'Vedic Gem Therapy'
source_views.view: Gems are called the main remedial measure in Vedic astrology, but wrongly prescribed gems can cause imbalances; two schools exist (strengthen weak benefics - the 'safe school' Frawley follows - versus propitiate the troublesome malefic), and Frawley advises against wearing malefics' gems unless backed by serious mantra and meditation practice.

source_views.source: Komilla Sutton, 'Astrology and Gemmology' (Skyscript, 2005; from Astrology and Medicine Newsletter 40, 2004)
source_views.view: Wear gems of strong, not weak, planets; criticises wearing many gems as a shortcut and astrologers who profit by selling costly stones; gems work only with a change of attitude; node gems best avoided.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Planetary Influences on Human Affairs, ch. XI 'Astrology as an Aid to Medical Science' and ch. VIII
source_views.view: Ancient texts suggest mantra-based remedies for afflictions (arishta yogas) shown in the chart (ch. XI); karma and free will coexist, so astrology should not be used fatalistically (ch. VIII). Raman gives no planet-by-planet list here.

remedy/saturn.disagreements: Mantra counts: BPHS 84.19-20 gives 23,000 for Saturn; PVR gives about 19,000 (his counts follow a different scheme). Mantra type: the classical texts read here prescribe Vedic verses and hymns; the short bija and name mantras come from modern authors (Frawley, PVR), and their classical mantra-text source (e.g. Mantra Maharnava) was not verified. Gemstones: the graha-shanti chapters read (BPHS ch. 84, Garuda Purana 1.101) prescribe worship, japa, homa, feeding and gifts, not wearing a planet's gem (Garuda mentions wearing metals); Phaladeepika 2.29 only lists the gems as correspondences. Among moderns: PVR and Frawley's 'safe school' give gems only for functional benefics (even weak ones) and avoid gems of functional malefics; a second school Frawley reports gives the gem of the troublesome malefic itself; Sutton prefers gems of strong planets over weak ones. Frawley and Sutton warn about side effects (blue sapphire, cat's eye, ruby, node gems) and Sutton criticises commercial gem-selling. Translation: in BPHS ch. 84 the Kapoor translation differs from the Sanskrit on some details (e.g. Rahu's image metal lead vs glass, the vehicles of Saturn and Ketu, Mars's count 10,000 vs 11,000).
remedy/saturn.phrasing_guidance: Offer these as optional devotional or lifestyle practices, never as a requirement or a fix. Do not frame the planet as something to fear. Do not promise that any remedy will change events, health or money. Mention gemstones only as an optional tradition that sources disagree on, recommend consulting a qualified, independent astrologer before buying one, and never tie a reading to a purchase. Prefer free practices first: prayer or mantra on the planet's day, simple charity, and the conduct changes. Classical gifts of animals (cows, bulls, goats, horses) can be described as the tradition's form of charity; a modern reader can give in kind or to a cause instead. No medical claims: herbs or gems are not treatment.

remedy/rahu.summary: Remedies for Rahu are indicated when it is weak, afflicted or badly placed, and especially while it runs a hard dasha or antardasha or an adverse transit (Phaladeepika 26.49; BPHS 84.26). The classical means are worship, its mantra, homa, feeding and gifts; modern authors add bija mantras, conduct and lifestyle changes, and optional gemstones only when Rahu is functionally helpful in the chart.
common_outcomes: Classical texts present planetary worship as bringing peace, prosperity, health and long life (BPHS 84.2-3).
Navagraha Stotra phalashruti: obstacles pacified, bad dreams removed, troubles from planets and stars calmed.
PVR: remedies change the details of a period, not its basic pattern.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: in the 5th, 6th, 8th or 12th, with a weak, debilitated or combust dispositor, or aspected by Saturn, Sun or Mars. Shows as anxiety, impressionability, confusion, unwholesome habits.
remedy/rahu.lagna_or_context_notes: Which remedy fits depends on the planet's functional role from the lagna: modern authors (PVR 34.2; Frawley, Astrology of the Seers Part III ch. 4 and Ayurvedic Astrology ch. 9) reserve gems for functional benefics and use mantra, worship and charity for malefics. BPHS 84.26 says to worship whichever planet is badly placed at the time.

remedies.remedy: Recite the planet's Vedic mantra beginning 'Kaya nas chitra a bhuvat...' after worshipping Rahu; prescribed count 18,000 repetitions.
remedies.source: BPHS ch. 84 (tr. G.S. Kapoor, Ranjan 1992, vol. 2 of the Santhanam set; = ch. 86 in G.C. Sharma) vv. 17-20; https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl

remedies.remedy: Recite verse 8 of the Navagraha Stotra (to Rahu, half-bodied, of great valour, afflicter of the Sun and Moon, born of Simhika), or the whole hymn; the closing verses say that whoever recites it with a collected mind, day or night, has obstacles pacified and troubles from planets and stars calmed.
remedies.source: Navagraha Stotra attributed to Vyasa (sanskritdocuments.org text, tr. V. Rao & S. Kalyanaraman), v. 8 and phalashruti; https://sanskritdocuments.org/doc_z_misc_navagraha/navanew.html

remedies.remedy: Name and seed mantras: name mantra OM RAHAVE NAMAHA; bija OM RAM (as Frawley gives it); also Shiva's HUM and Durga's DUM.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley

remedies.remedy: Read the planet's introductory verse a few times, then repeat its basic mantra about 18,000 times, ideally on its weekday; PVR also suggests the planet's 108 names, kavacha or stotra, recited with devotion and correct pronunciation.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.4; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: Graha puja: make an image of Rahu in lead ('sisa' in the Sanskrit; the Kapoor translation renders it glass) (or draw it on cloth in its colour) and contemplate it as fearsome face, four arms holding sword, shield and trident with a boon-giving hand, blue, riding a lion (84.12); offer flowers and cloth of its colour, sandal paste, lamp, incense (guggulu) and the food it likes.
remedies.source: BPHS ch. 84 (tr. G.S. Kapoor, Ranjan 1992, vol. 2 of the Santhanam set; = ch. 86 in G.C. Sharma) vv. 3-16; https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl; same content in G.C. Sharma ch. 86, https://archive.org/details/brihatparasarahorasastrawithenglishtranslationgirishchandsharmavolume2_433_w

remedies.remedy: Homa: offer durva grass as the sacrificial fuel for Rahu, dipped in honey, ghee, curd or milk, 108 or 28 times.
remedies.source: BPHS ch. 84 (tr. G.S. Kapoor, Ranjan 1992, vol. 2 of the Santhanam set; = ch. 86 in G.C. Sharma) vv. 21-22; https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl

remedies.remedy: Graha-yajna as taught by Yajnavalkya: worship with flowers and items of the planet's colour (black), recite its mantra, and give the prescribed food and gift; recommended for anyone troubled by a hostile planet or wanting peace and prosperity.
remedies.source: Garuda Purana 1.101 'Propitiation of malignant planets' (tr. M.N. Dutt, wisdomlib); https://www.wisdomlib.org/hinduism/book/the-garuda-purana-dutt/d/doc122581.html

remedies.remedy: Mrityunjaya japa with gift of a goat is prescribed for troubled Rahu sub-periods (e.g. Rahu in the dashas of Jupiter and Saturn, chs. 56-57; Mrityunjaya japa in Venus's dasha, ch. 60); Naga puja, feeding Brahmins and Mrityunjaya japa in Mars's dasha (ch. 54); Durga and Lakshmi mantras with a tawny cow or female buffalo in Mercury's dasha (ch. 58); Durga Saptashati in Ketu's dasha (ch. 59).
remedies.source: BPHS antardasha chapters 52-60 (Kapoor/Ranjan numbering; verse numbers not recorded unless given); https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl

remedies.remedy: Worship a deity linked to Rahu: Durga, Narasimha; PVR advises choosing the form that best fits the planet's combinations in the chart.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.5 Table 78; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: Deity: Durga as the demon-slayer; also Rama; ruling deity Durga, over-ruler Sarpa (serpent deity) (ch. 5 table).
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets' and David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 5 'Worship and Meditation on the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley

remedies.remedy: Feed Brahmins rice cooked with meat (mamsa) and give iron (Kapoor: weapons of iron) as the gift (dakshina), according to one's means and with respect.
remedies.source: BPHS ch. 84 (tr. G.S. Kapoor, Ranjan 1992, vol. 2 of the Santhanam set; = ch. 86 in G.C. Sharma) vv. 23-25; https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl; the gift list matches Garuda Purana 1.101 'Propitiation of malignant planets' (tr. M.N. Dutt, wisdomlib), https://www.wisdomlib.org/hinduism/book/the-garuda-purana-dutt/d/doc122581.html

remedies.remedy: Do a good deed in Rahu's area: donate to a research organisation or go on a pilgrimage. Give away black gram (urad), the grain ruled by Rahu.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.3; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: Place a small bowl of black gram on the altar to represent Rahu in worship; Frawley adds these are good foods when the planet is weak.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 5 'Worship and Meditation on the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley

remedies.remedy: Fasting on the weekday of the relevant planet (Saturday (Sutton; Frawley also allows the day of Rahu's sign lord) for Rahu). PVR's own examples tie the day to the planet that rules the troubled area (e.g. the upapada lord's day for marriage), not to a fixed list.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.3 (fasting); weekday attribution from 34.2/34.4 and Komilla Sutton, 'Astrology and Gemmology' (Skyscript, 2005; from Astrology and Medicine Newsletter 40, 2004); https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: Conduct and lifestyle: avoid powerful sensations, mass media, drugs, excess sex, talk and fantasy, junk food and artificial environments; cultivate peace, quiet, rest and a protective setting; devotion and a clear tradition rather than astral or visualisation practices.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley

remedies.remedy: Planets are always favourable to one who harms no one, keeps self-control, earns wealth by righteous means and keeps a steady religious discipline; when a planet is adverse in dasha, bhukti, ashtakavarga or transit, pacify it with prayers and mantras suited to it, virtuous acts, vows, gifts and worship.
remedies.source: Phaladeepika (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed. 1950) ch. 26 vv. 49-50; https://archive.org/details/Phaladeepika2ndEd.1950ByVSubrahmanyaSastri

remedies.remedy: Common-sense precautions in a difficult period (e.g. drive carefully if accidents are indicated, restrain oneself if conflict with authority is indicated); good deeds in the planet's area of life.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.1.1 and 34.3; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. Gem traditionally assigned to Rahu: hessonite garnet (gomeda) (substitutes: golden grossularite garnet). Frawley: hessonite (min. ~3 carats) in gold or silver, middle finger (or the finger of Rahu's sign lord), first worn in the waxing Moon on a Saturday or the sign lord's day; suggested mainly when Rahu is in strong houses like the 10th with a strong benefic lord. Avoid dark garnets, and avoid when Rahu is in trines or angles under strong malefic aspects unless its lord is benefic. Sutton advises that node gems are best avoided unless one can handle their energy.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley; gem list also David Frawley, Ayurvedic Astrology, ch. 9 'Vedic Gem Therapy', https://archive.org/details/david-frawley-ayurvedic-astrology-self-healing-through-the-stars_202305

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. PVR: wear the gem only if Rahu is a functional benefic in the chart (useful even if that benefic is weak or badly placed); avoid gems of functional malefics, and of marakas during maraka periods; first wear it on the planet's weekday when the planet is strong.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.2 and Table 77; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. Sutton: prefer the gems of strong planets (especially the lagna lord and trine lords) over weak ones; gems help only alongside a real change of attitude; wearing the planet's colour, its oils or seeds can stand in for an unaffordable gem.
remedies.source: Komilla Sutton, 'Astrology and Gemmology' (Skyscript, 2005; from Astrology and Medicine Newsletter 40, 2004); https://skyscript.co.uk/gems.html

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. Phaladeepika lists 'agate' in Sastri's rendering (Rahu) as Rahu's gem among the planets' correspondences; the verse assigns gems but does not prescribe wearing them as a remedy.
remedies.source: Phaladeepika (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed. 1950) ch. 2 v. 29; https://archive.org/details/Phaladeepika2ndEd.1950ByVSubrahmanyaSastri

remedies.remedy: Gift of a goat is prescribed for troubled Ketu sub-periods (e.g. Ketu in the dashas of Rahu, Saturn and Mercury; chs. 55, 57, 58); Mrityunjaya japa in Jupiter's dasha (ch. 56); Durga Saptashati and Mrityunjaya japa in Ketu's own dasha (ch. 59); Mrityunjaya japa and a goat in Venus's dasha (ch. 60). For Ketu in Mars's dasha the translator notes no remedy is given (ch. 54).
remedies.source: BPHS antardasha chapters 52-60 (Kapoor/Ranjan numbering; verse numbers not recorded unless given); https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl

remedies.remedy: Worship a deity linked to Ketu: Ganesha; PVR advises choosing the form that best fits the planet's combinations in the chart.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.5 Table 78; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: Deity: Rudra, the fierce form of Shiva; Brahma as knowledge; ruling deity Chitragupta, over-ruler Brahma (ch. 5 table).
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets' and David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 5 'Worship and Meditation on the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley

remedies.remedy: Feed Brahmins mixed rice (chitranna; Kapoor: khichdi) and give a goat as the gift (dakshina), according to one's means and with respect.
remedies.source: BPHS ch. 84 (tr. G.S. Kapoor, Ranjan 1992, vol. 2 of the Santhanam set; = ch. 86 in G.C. Sharma) vv. 23-25; https://archive.org/details/pcis_brihat-parasara-hora-sastra-volume-2-by-maharshi-parasara-sanskrit-and-engl; the gift list matches Garuda Purana 1.101 'Propitiation of malignant planets' (tr. M.N. Dutt, wisdomlib), https://www.wisdomlib.org/hinduism/book/the-garuda-purana-dutt/d/doc122581.html

remedies.remedy: Do a good deed in Ketu's area: do meditation.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.3; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: Place a small bowl of horse gram (kulattha) on the altar to represent Ketu in worship; Frawley adds these are good foods when the planet is weak.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 5 'Worship and Meditation on the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley

remedies.remedy: Fasting on the weekday of the relevant planet (Tuesday (Sutton); Frawley gives Saturday or the day of Ketu's sign lord for Ketu). PVR's own examples tie the day to the planet that rules the troubled area (e.g. the upapada lord's day for marriage), not to a fixed list.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.3 (fasting); weekday attribution from 34.2/34.4 and Komilla Sutton, 'Astrology and Gemmology' (Skyscript, 2005; from Astrology and Medicine Newsletter 40, 2004); https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: Conduct and lifestyle: trust one's own perceptions; take up spiritual study (Frawley suggests astrology) under a teacher or tradition; keep a discipline that joins will with compassion.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley

remedies.remedy: Planets are always favourable to one who harms no one, keeps self-control, earns wealth by righteous means and keeps a steady religious discipline; when a planet is adverse in dasha, bhukti, ashtakavarga or transit, pacify it with prayers and mantras suited to it, virtuous acts, vows, gifts and worship.
remedies.source: Phaladeepika (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed. 1950) ch. 26 vv. 49-50; https://archive.org/details/Phaladeepika2ndEd.1950ByVSubrahmanyaSastri

remedies.remedy: Common-sense precautions in a difficult period (e.g. drive carefully if accidents are indicated, restrain oneself if conflict with authority is indicated); good deeds in the planet's area of life.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.1.1 and 34.3; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. Gem traditionally assigned to Ketu: cat's eye (chrysoberyl) (substitutes: quartz cat's eye). Frawley: cat's eye (min. ~3 carats), preferably in gold, middle finger (or the finger of Ketu's sign lord), first worn in the waxing Moon on a Saturday or the sign lord's day; suggested when Ketu is strong (with a benefic in its own or exalted sign, or unafflicted in the 12th). Avoid when Ketu conjoins planets (unless they are exalted or own-sign), when its lord rules the 6th or 11th, or with high-Pitta conditions. Ayurvedic Astrology ch. 9 lists cat's eye among gems with possible side effects; Sutton advises node gems are best avoided.
remedies.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'; https://archive.org/details/astrology-of-the-seers-david-frawley; gem list also David Frawley, Ayurvedic Astrology, ch. 9 'Vedic Gem Therapy', https://archive.org/details/david-frawley-ayurvedic-astrology-self-healing-through-the-stars_202305

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. PVR: wear the gem only if Ketu is a functional benefic in the chart (useful even if that benefic is weak or badly placed); avoid gems of functional malefics, and of marakas during maraka periods; first wear it on the planet's weekday when the planet is strong.
remedies.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures', 34.2 and Table 77; https://archive.org/details/vedic-astrology-integrated-approach-1

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. Sutton: prefer the gems of strong planets (especially the lagna lord and trine lords) over weak ones; gems help only alongside a real change of attitude; wearing the planet's colour, its oils or seeds can stand in for an unaffordable gem.
remedies.source: Komilla Sutton, 'Astrology and Gemmology' (Skyscript, 2005; from Astrology and Medicine Newsletter 40, 2004); https://skyscript.co.uk/gems.html

remedies.remedy: OPTIONAL. Phaladeepika lists 'lapis lazuli or turquoise' in Sastri's rendering (Ketu) as Ketu's gem among the planets' correspondences; the verse assigns gems but does not prescribe wearing them as a remedy.
remedies.source: Phaladeepika (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed. 1950) ch. 2 v. 29; https://archive.org/details/Phaladeepika2ndEd.1950ByVSubrahmanyaSastri

source_views.source: BPHS ch. 84 (tr. G.S. Kapoor, Ranjan 1992, vol. 2 of the Santhanam set; = ch. 86 in G.C. Sharma)
source_views.view: Joys and sorrows depend on the planets, so those wanting peace, wealth, health or long life should worship them; whichever planet is badly placed at a given time should be worshipped with special care, because Brahma granted the planets the boon of honouring those who honour them (vv. 2-3, 26-27). For Ketu: image in bell-metal (kamsya), mantra 'Ketum krinvann aketave...' x 17,000, fuel kusha grass, food mixed rice (chitranna; Kapoor: khichdi), gift a goat.

source_views.source: BPHS antardasha chapters 52-60 (Kapoor/Ranjan numbering; verse numbers not recorded unless given)
source_views.view: Gift of a goat is prescribed for troubled Ketu sub-periods (e.g. Ketu in the dashas of Rahu, Saturn and Mercury; chs. 55, 57, 58); Mrityunjaya japa in Jupiter's dasha (ch. 56); Durga Saptashati and Mrityunjaya japa in Ketu's own dasha (ch. 59); Mrityunjaya japa and a goat in Venus's dasha (ch. 60). For Ketu in Mars's dasha the translator notes no remedy is given (ch. 54).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed. 1950) ch. 26 vv. 49-50
source_views.view: Remedy is indicated whenever a planet is badly placed in dasha, bhukti, ashtakavarga or transit; the means are prayer and planet-specific mantra, propitiatory rites, virtuous acts, vows, gifts and worship. Non-harming, self-control, honestly earned wealth and discipline keep the planets favourable.

source_views.source: Navagraha Stotra attributed to Vyasa (sanskritdocuments.org text, tr. V. Rao & S. Kalyanaraman)
source_views.view: Verse 9 praises Ketu, like the palasha flower, head of the stars and planets, fierce and terrible; the closing verses promise pacification of obstacles, bad dreams and planet-caused troubles.

source_views.source: Garuda Purana 1.101 'Propitiation of malignant planets' (tr. M.N. Dutt, wisdomlib)
source_views.view: Yajnavalkya's graha-yajna: anyone under a hostile planet, or wanting prosperity and peace, should perform it; colour for Ketu black; gifts follow the same order as BPHS.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 34 'Remedial Measures'
source_views.view: Remedies adjust the details of a karmic pattern, not the pattern; four ways to please a planet: gem (only for functional benefics), good deeds, mantra/stotra, deity worship. For Ketu: deed - do meditation; deity - Ganesha; mantra count ~7,000.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers, Part III ch. 4 'Treatment Methods: Balancing Influences of the Planets'
source_views.view: Strengthen a planet chiefly when it is weak, and be careful strengthening natural malefics; mantra and meditation are safer than gems or herbs, and are used to ward off an over-strong malefic. Signs of a weak Ketu: Frawley: weak dispositor, in the 3rd, 6th or 8th, or aspected by Saturn and Mars. Shows as self-doubt, poor concentration, feeling constricted.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Ayurvedic Astrology, ch. 9 'Vedic Gem Therapy'
source_views.view: Gems are called the main remedial measure in Vedic astrology, but wrongly prescribed gems can cause imbalances; two schools exist (strengthen weak benefics - the 'safe school' Frawley follows - versus propitiate the troublesome malefic), and Frawley advises against wearing malefics' gems unless backed by serious mantra and meditation practice.

source_views.source: Komilla Sutton, 'Astrology and Gemmology' (Skyscript, 2005; from Astrology and Medicine Newsletter 40, 2004)
source_views.view: Wear gems of strong, not weak, planets; criticises wearing many gems as a shortcut and astrologers who profit by selling costly stones; gems work only with a change of attitude; node gems best avoided.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Planetary Influences on Human Affairs, ch. XI 'Astrology as an Aid to Medical Science' and ch. VIII
source_views.view: Ancient texts suggest mantra-based remedies for afflictions (arishta yogas) shown in the chart (ch. XI); karma and free will coexist, so astrology should not be used fatalistically (ch. VIII). Raman gives no planet-by-planet list here.

remedy/ketu.disagreements: Mantra counts: BPHS 84.19-20 gives 17,000 for Ketu; PVR gives about 7,000 (his counts follow a different scheme). Mantra type: the classical texts read here prescribe Vedic verses and hymns; the short bija and name mantras come from modern authors (Frawley, PVR), and their classical mantra-text source (e.g. Mantra Maharnava) was not verified. Gemstones: the graha-shanti chapters read (BPHS ch. 84, Garuda Purana 1.101) prescribe worship, japa, homa, feeding and gifts, not wearing a planet's gem (Garuda mentions wearing metals); Phaladeepika 2.29 only lists the gems as correspondences. Among moderns: PVR and Frawley's 'safe school' give gems only for functional benefics (even weak ones) and avoid gems of functional malefics; a second school Frawley reports gives the gem of the troublesome malefic itself; Sutton prefers gems of strong planets over weak ones. Frawley and Sutton warn about side effects (blue sapphire, cat's eye, ruby, node gems) and Sutton criticises commercial gem-selling. Translation: in BPHS ch. 84 the Kapoor translation differs from the Sanskrit on some details (e.g. Rahu's image metal lead vs glass, the vehicles of Saturn and Ketu, Mars's count 10,000 vs 11,000).
remedy/ketu.phrasing_guidance: Offer these as optional devotional or lifestyle practices, never as a requirement or a fix. Do not frame the planet as something to fear. Do not promise that any remedy will change events, health or money. Mention gemstones only as an optional tradition that sources disagree on, recommend consulting a qualified, independent astrologer before buying one, and never tie a reading to a purchase. Prefer free practices first: prayer or mantra on the planet's day, simple charity, and the conduct changes. Classical gifts of animals (cows, bulls, goats, horses) can be described as the tradition's form of charity; a modern reader can give in kind or to a cause instead. No medical claims: herbs or gems are not treatment.

profession/rule.summary: Classical rule for the kind of work that suits a person: take the lord of the 10th house (counted from the lagna, the Moon and the Sun, using the strongest of the three), see which navamsa (D9) sign it occupies, and the lord of that sign is the indicator planet whose nature points to the field of livelihood (Phaladeepika 5.1; Brihat Jataka 10.1). It shows a leaning, not a fixed job.
common_outcomes: Step 1: find the 10th house from the lagna, from the Moon and from the Sun, and the lord of each (Phaladeepika 5.1; Brihat Jataka 10.1 with Sastri's notes).
Step 2: pick the strongest of these reference points (or of these 10th lords); Sastri's worked example on Brihat Jataka 10.1 takes the strongest of the navamsa lords reached this way.

Step 3: note the navamsa sign that 10th lord occupies; its lord is the indicator planet, and the work 'prescribed for' that planet describes the livelihood (Phaladeepika 5.2-5.8; Brihat Jataka 10.2-10.3).
Strength of the indicator decides how easily wealth comes: strong gives gains without much strain, weak gives modest gains (Phaladeepika 5.9).

Place of earning: judged from the 10th sign or the navamsa sign of the 10th lord; if that sign holds or is aspected by its own lord, or is a fixed sign, the person earns in their own country; if other planets occupy or aspect it, earnings come from elsewhere (Phaladeepika 5.9).
rare_outcomes: Source of wealth (a separate rule in the same verses): the planet occupying the 10th from the stronger of lagna and Moon shows who wealth comes through: Sun father, Moon mother, Mars opponents, Mercury friends, Jupiter brothers, Venus spouse or women, Saturn servants or subordinates (Phaladeepika 5.1; Brihat Jataka 10.1; Saravali 33.81).
Rath: a fixed navamsa for the 10th lord suggests a settled, desk-based job; a movable one, moving around for one's living; a dual one, a mix (Crux of Vedic Astrology 13.7).

by_area.career: Core use: the indicator planet names the family of work; Raman adds that the 10th lord, any occupant of the 10th, and this navamsa lord should be weighed together, the strongest leading (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2 ch. XIV).
by_area.finance: Phaladeepika 5.9: a strong indicator brings wealth without much exertion, a weak one only a little. Brihat Jataka 10.4: strong benefics in the 1st, 2nd and 11th give income from many sources.

strengtheners: Indicator planet strong (Phaladeepika 5.9).
Rath: the navamsa dispositor of the 10th lord well placed and friendly to the lagna lord and the 10th lord (Crux 13.7).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Indicator planet weak: little wealth from the work (Phaladeepika 5.9).
Rath: if the navamsa dispositor is a malefic and strongly hostile to the 10th lord, the 10th lord's dasha, especially its sub-period, can be hard for career (Crux 13.7).
Raman: a 10th lord in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the navamsa lagna makes the career routine or slow to rise (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2 ch. XIV).
profession/rule.lagna_or_context_notes: Three reference points (lagna, Moon, Sun) can give three different indicator planets. Varahamihira and Mantreswara say use the strongest; Bhattotpala (quoted by Sastri under Brihat Jataka 10.1) says every one of them should be considered. Rahu and Ketu own no signs in this scheme, so they can never be the indicator planet; neither Phaladeepika 5 nor Brihat Jataka 10 assigns them a livelihood (Raman only groups both under routine work in general).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 5.1 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed. 1950)
source_views.view: Wealth is judged from the stronger of the lagna and the Moon; the planet in the 10th from it names the source (father, mother, foe, friend, brother, wife, servant for Sun to Saturn). The profession is that of the lord of the navamsa occupied by the 10th lord counted from the lagna, the Moon and the Sun, whichever is strongest.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 5.9 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: A strong navamsa lord gives wealth without exertion, a weak one little wealth. The country of earning follows the 10th sign or the 10th lord's navamsa sign: own country if that sign holds or is aspected by its lord, or if the navamsa is a fixed sign; elsewhere if other planets occupy or aspect it.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 10.1 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Wealth comes, first, from the person signified by the planet in the 10th from lagna or Moon; second, through the profession of the ruler of the 10th house or of the ruler of the navamsa occupied by the 10th lord from the lagna, Moon or Sun. Sastri's note: take the strongest of the three 10th lords and read its navamsa lord; he cites Bhattotpala, who holds that all of them, not only the strongest, should be considered.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 10.3-10.4 with notes (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: The person succeeds in the work of the planet owning the navamsa of the 10th lord. Wealth sources are also read from planets in friendly, enemy or own signs; strong benefics in the 11th, 1st and 2nd give income in many ways. A quoted note adds that the profession is judged from planets in the 10th, else from those in the 1st and those aspecting the Sun and Moon, and from planets close to the Sun or the 10th cusp.

source_views.source: Saravali 33.2-6, 33.65-81 (tr. R. Santhanam)
source_views.view: Karma is read from the 10th of the stronger of lagna and Moon; a strong 10th lord makes work prosper. Livelihood follows the occupant of the 10th, the stronger of the two 10th lords, and the sign on the 10th (with a list of trades per sign). Saravali here gives no navamsa-lord rule.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XIV 'Concerning the Tenth House' (archive.org file of vols 1-2)
source_views.view: Astrology shows tendencies and aptitudes, not a fixed job, and no factor can be fixed for each vocation. In his study of over 50 charts the 10th lord and 10th house clearly decided the profession in only 15. With an empty 10th, weigh the 10th lord against the navamsa lord of the 10th lord and take the stronger; with an occupant, take the strongest of lord, occupant and navamsa lord; with several, blend. Reckon from lagna, Moon and Sun and prefer the strongest. The strongest planet in the whole chart also bears on profession.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology, 13.7 (archive.org file in the same item)
source_views.view: The navamsa dispositor of the 10th lord can make or mar the career depending on its placement and its relationship with the lagna lord and 10th lord; fixed, movable and dual navamsas of the 10th lord suggest settled, mobile and mixed work.

source_views.source: Barbara Pijan Lama, commentary on Phaladeepika 5 (Kapoor translation)
source_views.view: Reads the planet trade lists as broad modern associations (for example Venus as music, design, finance and deal-making) and widens 'earning in another country' to crossing any regional, language or cultural boundary. Rahu and Ketu do not appear in the rule.

profession/rule.disagreements: Which reference point: Phaladeepika 5.1 and Brihat Jataka 10.1 count from the lagna, Moon and Sun and take the strongest; Saravali 33 uses only the stronger of lagna and Moon and reads the sign and lord of the 10th, without the navamsa step. Strongest only or all: Bhattotpala (via Sastri on BJ 10.1) says to consider every 10th lord's navamsa lord, not only the strongest. 10th lord itself: Brihat Jataka 10.1 lets the ruler of the 10th house or the ruler of its navamsa decide; Phaladeepika names only the navamsa lord; Raman weighs both and any occupant, taking the strongest. Trade lists: Varahamihira's lists are short (e.g. Sun: grass, gold, wool, medicine); Mantreswara's are longer and add other items (e.g. Sun: fruit trees, mantras, service under a ruler). Modern authors (Raman, Rath) add the D10 and stress tendencies over fixed outcomes.
profession/rule.phrasing_guidance: Present the indicator planet as pointing to a family of work or a style of earning, never a single job title or a verdict. Translate old trade lists into modern fields. Mention that the method is one classical view among several (with the D10 and the planets in the 10th) and that effort and choice shape the career.

profession/sun.summary: Sun as the indicator: work linked with government, authority or respected institutions, leadership roles, medicine and health products, and trades in gold or metals.
common_outcomes: Service under a ruler or a respected person; working with metals; medicine (Phaladeepika 5.2).
Dealing in grass, gold, wool, medicine and similar goods (Brihat Jataka 10.2).
Sastri's modern note: honourable posts under the state or a public body, titled appointments, jewellers and goldsmiths, wool-mill work, mint work (Brihat Jataka 10.2 notes).
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika 5.2 also lists fruit trees, reciting mantras, wool, and less honest means (fraud, gambling, falsehood).

by_area.career: Raman groups the Sun with the Moon and Mars under economic occupations; Sun or Mars influence on an intellectual planet points to state service (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2 ch. XIV).

strengtheners: Indicator strong: gains come with less effort (Phaladeepika 5.9).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Indicator weak: modest gains (Phaladeepika 5.9).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 5.2 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: 10th lord in the Sun's navamsa: livelihood through fruit trees, mantra recitation, wool, medicine, metal work or service under a king or respectable person; also through fraud, gambling or falsehood.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 10.2 with notes (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Sun as navamsa lord: living by dealing in grass, gold, wool, medicine and the like. Notes: honourable state or public employment, royal and titled posts, jewellers, goldsmiths, wool mills, mints.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XIV
source_views.view: Sun, Moon and Mars refer generally to economic occupations; Sun or Mars added to an intellectual signature indicates service under the state.

source_views.source: Barbara Pijan Lama, commentary on Phaladeepika 5
source_views.view: Modern associations for the Sun: politics, public visibility and celebrity, creative literature, drama and showmanship.

profession/sun.disagreements: Brihat Jataka gives a short list (grass, gold, wool, medicine); Phaladeepika adds fruit trees, mantras, metal work, royal service and dishonest means. Sastri's notes stress state and titled posts.
profession/sun.phrasing_guidance: Say: drawn to roles with responsibility, public standing or institutional backing; leave out the 'fraud, gambling' items in a consumer report.

profession/moon.summary: Moon as the indicator: work connected with water and liquids, food and farming, textiles and clothing, travel or pilgrimage, caring roles and serving the public, often with women as clients or employers.
common_outcomes: Trade in water products (pearls, corals), agriculture and cattle farming, pilgrimage, service under a woman, trade in clothes (Phaladeepika 5.3).
Agriculture, things from water (conches, pearls, fish), or through women (Brihat Jataka 10.2).
Sastri's modern note: sailors, navigators, fishermen, watermen, midwives, nurses (Brihat Jataka 10.2 notes).

by_area.career: Raman groups the Moon with the Sun and Mars under economic occupations (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2 ch. XIV).

strengtheners: Indicator strong: gains come with less effort (Phaladeepika 5.9).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Indicator weak: modest gains (Phaladeepika 5.9).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 5.3 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: 10th lord in the Moon's navamsa: income through water products, agriculture and cattle, pilgrimage to shrines, service under a young woman, or the cloth trade.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 10.2 with notes (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Moon as navamsa lord: living by agriculture, things from water, or through women. Notes: sailors, mariners, fishermen, midwives, nurses.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XIV
source_views.view: The Moon is among the planets of economic occupations.

source_views.source: Barbara Pijan Lama, commentary on Phaladeepika 5
source_views.view: Modern associations for the Moon: housing, agriculture, fishing and ocean work, schooling, and working under mother-like or nurturing figures; 'service under a woman' widened to service industries catering to women.

profession/moon.disagreements: Phaladeepika adds cattle, pilgrimage and the cloth trade to Brihat Jataka's agriculture, water products and women.
profession/moon.phrasing_guidance: Say: suited to nurturing, public-facing or hospitality work and fields tied to food, water, travel or textiles; avoid gendered wording.

profession/mars.summary: Mars as the indicator: work that takes courage and technical skill, such as defence, police or security, engineering, metals and machinery, land and property, cooking or work with fire, and surgery or medicine.
common_outcomes: Metals, fighting, cooking, land, gold, weapons and adventurous work (Phaladeepika 5.4).
Metallurgy and forceful work such as fighting (Brihat Jataka 10.2).
Sastri's modern note: military ranks, doctors, physicians, chemists, engine drivers, and workers in iron, steel or fire (Brihat Jataka 10.2 notes).
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika 5.4 also lists troubling others, association with wicked people, spying and theft.

by_area.career: Raman groups Mars with the Sun and Moon under economic occupations; Sun or Mars influence points to state service, and his chart 115 reads a Mars navamsa lord as a military profession (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2 ch. XIV).

strengtheners: Indicator strong: gains come with less effort (Phaladeepika 5.9).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Indicator weak: modest gains (Phaladeepika 5.9).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 5.4 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: 10th lord in a Mars navamsa: income through metals, battle, cooking, land, gold, weapons, daring acts; also by harming others, bad company, spying or theft.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 10.2 with notes (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Mars as navamsa lord: livelihood by metallurgy and violent acts like fighting. Notes: soldiers and officers, doctors, physicians, chemists, butchers, barbers, engine drivers, workers in iron, steel or fire.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XIV (chart 115)
source_views.view: Mars is among the planets of economic occupations; with the 10th lord in a strong Mars navamsa from the strongest reference point, Raman reads a military profession.

profession/mars.disagreements: Sastri's notes include medicine (doctors, chemists) under Mars, while Phaladeepika 5.2 lists medicine under the Sun.
profession/mars.phrasing_guidance: Say: energy for hands-on, technical or protective work; leave out 'theft, spying, harming others' in a consumer report.

profession/mercury.summary: Mercury as the indicator: work with words, numbers and ideas, such as writing, accounting, mathematics, teaching, clerical or office work, trade, astrology and the arts.
common_outcomes: Composing poetry, study of scriptures, work as a scribe or clerk, astrology, Vedic study on others' behalf, mantra recitation, priestly roles (Phaladeepika 5.5).
Earning as a writer, through mathematics, poetry or the arts (Brihat Jataka 10.2).
Sastri's modern note: authors, translators, accountants, astrologers, school teachers, mathematicians, lawyers, booksellers, printers, postmen (Brihat Jataka 10.2 notes).
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika 5.5 also mentions earning through some trick or pretext.

by_area.career: Raman: Mercury (with Jupiter) refers to intellectual work and Mercury also to traders; Mercury is key for creative writing (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2 ch. XIV).

strengtheners: Indicator strong: gains come with less effort (Phaladeepika 5.9).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Indicator weak: modest gains (Phaladeepika 5.9).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 5.5 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: 10th lord in a Mercury navamsa: earning by composing poems, scripture study, as a scribe or clerk, through astrology, Vedic study for others, mantra recitation, acting as a priest, or by some trick or pretext.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 10.2 with notes (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Mercury as navamsa lord: livelihood as a writer, by mathematics, poetry or the arts. Notes: authors, translators, accountants, astrologers, teachers, mathematicians, poets, lawyers, booksellers, printers, postmen.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XIV
source_views.view: Jupiter and Mercury refer to intellectual avocations and Mercury also to traders; a scientist shows Mercury prominent, a philosopher Jupiter.

profession/mercury.disagreements: Phaladeepika puts priestly and Vedic work under Mercury as well as Jupiter; Brihat Jataka keeps Mercury to writing, mathematics, poetry and arts.
profession/mercury.phrasing_guidance: Say: suited to communication, analysis, writing, teaching or commerce; skip 'trick or pretext'.

profession/jupiter.summary: Jupiter as the indicator: work in teaching, advising, law and religion, scholarship, counselling or guidance, and finance or banking, often with the support of learned people or institutions.
common_outcomes: Living through the help of learned people, temples or royal favour, by reciting Puranas, study of the Shastras, teaching morality, religious instruction, or money-lending (Phaladeepika 5.6).
Earning through Brahmins, deities, learned men, mines and the like, or by religious acts (Brihat Jataka 10.3).
Sastri's modern note: judges, priests, scholars, preachers, ministers, bankers (Brihat Jataka 10.3 notes).

by_area.career: Raman: Jupiter (with Mercury) refers to intellectual work; a philosopher's chart shows Jupiter prominent (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2 ch. XIV).
by_area.finance: Phaladeepika 5.6 includes lending money (usury); Sastri's notes include bankers.
by_area.spirituality: Religious instruction and scriptural learning are named as livelihoods (Phaladeepika 5.6; Brihat Jataka 10.3).

strengtheners: Indicator strong: gains come with less effort (Phaladeepika 5.9).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Indicator weak: modest gains (Phaladeepika 5.9).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 5.6 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: 10th lord in a Jupiter navamsa: maintained through Brahmins, gods or royal favour, reciting Puranas, studying Shastras, preaching morality, religious teaching, or money-lending.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 10.3 with notes (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Jupiter as navamsa lord: money through Brahmins, deities, learned men, mines and the like, or by religious acts. Notes: judges, priests, learned men, preachers, ministers, bankers.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XIV
source_views.view: Jupiter and Mercury signify intellectual avocations; Jupiter prominent for philosophers.

profession/jupiter.disagreements: Brihat Jataka (Sastri) lists mines under Jupiter, which Phaladeepika does not; Phaladeepika adds money-lending and recitation of Puranas.
profession/jupiter.phrasing_guidance: Say: suited to roles of trust, teaching, guidance, law or finance; keep religious wording optional and inclusive.

profession/venus.summary: Venus as the indicator: work in the arts, music, dance and design, beauty, fashion, jewellery and luxury goods, hospitality and food, and work that involves women or partnerships.
common_outcomes: Earning through women, cattle, horses, music with dance, silver, perfumes, milk, ornaments, silk, as a companion to a ruler, or by poetic talent (Phaladeepika 5.7).
Dealing in rubies, silver and the like, and rearing cows and buffaloes (Brihat Jataka 10.3).
Sastri's modern note: dealers in gold, gems or horses, hotel-keepers, confectioners, musicians, painters, drapers, jewellers, actors, embroiderers, perfume dealers (Brihat Jataka 10.3 notes).

by_area.career: Raman: Venus refers to aesthetic professions such as music, acting, dance and other arts (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2 ch. XIV).

strengtheners: Indicator strong: gains come with less effort (Phaladeepika 5.9).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Indicator weak: modest gains (Phaladeepika 5.9).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 5.7 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: 10th lord in a Venus navamsa: earnings through a woman, cows, buffaloes, elephants, horses, music and dance, silver, scents, milk, ornaments, silks, as a companion to a king, or through poetry.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 10.3 with notes (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Venus as navamsa lord: dealing in rubies, silver and the like, and rearing cows and buffaloes. Notes: dealers in gold, rubies, horses; hotel-keepers, confectioners, musicians, painters, drapers, jewellers, players, embroiderers, scent dealers.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XIV
source_views.view: Venus refers to aesthetic professions (musicians, actors, singers, dancers, artists).

source_views.source: Barbara Pijan Lama, commentary on Phaladeepika 5
source_views.view: Modern associations for Venus: music, women's concerns, finance and banking, design, deal-making, alliance-building and contract work.

profession/venus.disagreements: Brihat Jataka's list is short (gems, silver, cattle); Phaladeepika adds music, scents, ornaments, silk and poetry. Pijan Lama adds finance and contracts, which the classical lists do not name.
profession/venus.phrasing_guidance: Say: drawn to creative, aesthetic, hospitality or relationship-based work; avoid gendered framing.

profession/saturn.summary: Saturn as the indicator: steady work that rewards patience and effort, such as labour-intensive or service roles, construction, wood, mining, farming of roots and produce, craft and sculpture, and in modern readings large organisations and public systems.
common_outcomes: Dealing in roots and fruits, physical labour, through servants, carrying loads, sculpture and wooden goods (Phaladeepika 5.8).
Living by tiring work, carrying burdens, or enforcing punishments (Brihat Jataka 10.3).
Sastri's modern note: gardeners, miners and bricklayers among others (Brihat Jataka 10.3 notes).
rare_outcomes: Phaladeepika 5.8 and Brihat Jataka 10.3 also list base or low pursuits, dealing in poor grain, and work as an executioner or butcher; Sastri's notes add shoemakers, scavengers, grave-diggers and undertakers.

by_area.career: Raman: Saturn refers to hard-working jobs; elsewhere in the same chapter Saturn in the 10th can give a ruler, judge or agriculturist working for the masses (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2 ch. XIV).

strengtheners: Indicator strong: gains come with less effort (Phaladeepika 5.9).
weakeners_or_cancellations: Indicator weak: modest gains (Phaladeepika 5.9).

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 5.8 (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: 10th lord in a Saturn navamsa: living by roots and fruits, physical exertion, through servants and low people, poor grains, carrying loads, base work, sculpture, wooden goods, or as an executioner or butcher.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 10.3 with notes (tr. Sastri)
source_views.view: Saturn as navamsa lord: living by wearisome work, carrying out punishments, bearing burdens, or some low pursuit. Notes: shoemakers, scavengers, grave-diggers, undertakers; also gardeners, miners, bricklayers.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XIV
source_views.view: Saturn refers to hard-working jobs.

source_views.source: Barbara Pijan Lama, commentary on Phaladeepika 5
source_views.view: Modern associations for Saturn: large corporations, bureaucracy, institutional systems and large rule-governed technical systems.

profession/saturn.disagreements: Classical lists stress hard manual or low-status work; Raman elsewhere gives Saturn in the 10th high posts (ruler, judge), and Pijan Lama reads Saturn as large organisations and systems. The classical lists reflect an old social order.
profession/saturn.phrasing_guidance: Say: success through discipline, persistence and structured or long-term work; never use 'low', 'base', 'executioner' or 'butcher' in a consumer report.
